text_en: Should Damielliot remain unconscious, his body will soon atrophy─making recovery even more difficult, if not impossible.
The formula I gave you is the result of our best attempt to devise a treatment. All our hopes rest on its effectiveness.
You will be able to procure one of the rarer reagents from the merchant Nomomo. She is known to frequent Camp Black Brush, near Ul'dah.
We are doing all we can to help Damielliot. We have already exhausted every conventional treatment known to us.
We have barely left the Phrontistery of late, but it will be a small price to pay to see him well again.
They say the wise man keeps only three friends close─a doctor, a moneylender, and a gravedigger.
There are plenty of the first to be befriended around here. As for the second and third, you'd best look elsewhere.
You adventurers tend to be more of a hindrance than a help...but you're nothing if not cheap!
The reagents we need for our medicines are costly enough on their own. We must save what coin we can, where we can.
From the Phrontistery, ain't you? Aye, you stink of the place. What is it this time, then? That younglin' take ill again?

You won't see me puttin' none of them bloody concoctions in my body. But I s'pose seein' yer son sick an' dyin'll drive a father to do damn near anythin'... <sigh> Here, take this. All you need now's [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,10009011,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,10009011,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].
Bloody alchemists and healers'd bottle and sell life if they could. When I'm lyin' on my deathbed, you'll not see me quaffin' their pisses to keep alive. Give me a clean end.
But I s'pose seein' yer son sick an' dyin'll drive a father to do damn near anythin'.
You're returned! And you have the medicine? Excellent! That treatment was devised by Master Faustigeant himself. It will serve to nourish the body, even in an unconscious state.
Please, take it to Damielliot's sickroom at once. There isn't a moment to lose.
Despite his condition, he still shows signs that he is dimly aware of his surroundings. Perhaps your mere presence will evoke a response.
Take the corridor which leads to the children's ward. Healer S'lyhhia by the door there will guide you.
Damielliot's room lies in the children's ward.
The corridor that leads there is just through those doors. Healer S'lyhhia will guide you.
Our search for curative reagents to use in new medicines encompasses the whole of Eorzea─including those parts one might not think to look.
Many from the lands of Ala Mhigo, for example, show great promise...which makes the Garleans' decision to occupy the region all the more regrettable.
In all my years, I've never seen a sickness like that which grips Damielliot. Nothing we do seems to ease his affliction.
I'd swear the mere presence of you adventurers does him more good than any potion or tonic. He has always warmed to your kind.
The climate is ill at ease of late. Have you not noticed? I fear it may be taxing for the young ones.
Gods know, it takes its toll on us. Healer S'lyhhia seems to be at her wits' end. Do be kind to her.
I will see you to Damielliot's room. Please, may I have the medicine?
Allow Healer S'lyhhia to guide you?
Allow Healer S'lyhhia to guide you?

Word spreads quickly in the Phrontistery. [@IF($E4($E8(1),1),They are saying Damielliot recognized you. Have you met him before?,They are saying Damielliot claimed to feel a strange power when he stirred from his sleep.)]

[@IF($E4($E8(1),1),If the two of you share some past that Damielliot remembers, that,I suppose everything must seem a strange power to one so heavily medicated. That)] [@1A(1)]could[@1A(0)] explain why he was roused from his slumber.
I would like to be optimistic, but a lifetime spent studying the healing arts has made me a realist. Do not expect such dramatic results next time.
The body is a thing of resilience, and to live is to build tolerances. The efficacy of new medicines and the stimulation of new faces will only diminish with time.
It seems the Phrontistery was right to take you on.
I pray that when Damielliot next wakes, there is time enough for you to tell him tales of the outside world. It would do him well to hear them.
As it seems my time on you...

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Why won't Damielliot wake up and tell us more stories? Doesn't he know we haven't had a story in ages?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: It grieves all at the Phrontistery to see Damielliot in such pain...

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: As I told you before, we mean to affect any stimulation we can. I wonder, would you not do us the kindness of visiting him? Your presence may trigger some new reaction.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: All of the young ones admitted at the Phrontistery hold a place in their heart for Damielliot.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: When he was well, he would spend hours on end with them─playing with them and telling them stories when there were none else to do so.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: The Phrontistery keeps a vast collection of alchemical tomes and treatises.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Of all in our order, Damielliot alone can boast having read every one of them. He may well be as knowledgeable as Master Faustigeant himself. Like father, like son.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: We are known to all as Eorzea's foremost house of healing─but what we do is costly, and our numbers are not great. As it is, only families of privilege can afford to send their children here.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: The thought of denying the poor equal treatment does not sit well with many─myself included. If you feel the same, then I urge you to learn our ways, and then spread them on your travels.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Did you come to see Damielliot? Me too. I hope he wakes up soon. I want him to tell us more stories.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: How come I never want to go to sleep, but the grown-ups never want to wake up?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: I picked some wildflowers and put them by Damielliot's bedside. The healers told me they would bring him pretty dreams.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: I wish I could sleep that long...but I can't. My insides hurt too much.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Ugggh... Dr-Dragons... No...

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Dragons!? Damielliot's dreaming about dragons! I'm sure he'll tell us all about it when he wakes up.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: I knew he wouldn't forget to finish his story. He was telling us about dragons last time. Before he fell asleep.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: There was a child, just like us, who lived in the forest. And then, one day, some bad people came down from the mountains and took him away. And they were going to try and ransom him back to his mother and father.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: They put him on a chocobo and rode north and north and ever farther─all the way back to the mountains. But before they got back to the bandits' hideout, a dragon appeared in the sky!

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: It was so big that when it beat its wings it made a wind that blew all over Eorzea!

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: And Damielliot said the wind was [@1A(1)]so[@1A(0)] strong it blew all the bandits off their chocobos! And it blew the little boy from the forest off his chocobo too, and then─

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: That's where Damielliot ended the story that day. We're all waiting for him to wake up so we can hear the rest!

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: <rasp>

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: I wish I knew what happened to the boy and the dragon after that. Damielliot will wake up and finish the story, won't he?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I am loath to trouble you at a time like this, but an urgent matter has arisen.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: We have learned of a new reagent known as starfall grass. It may prove helpful in treating Damielliot's condition. The plant in question is native to Gridania.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: The Phrontistery has already arranged for the purchase of what could be found at market─but it is not much. We would like to procure a great deal more.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Please, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], travel north to Gridania and learn what you can of this reagent. Specifically, we need to know from whence it might be obtained.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Should you come across someone who has purchased any, do whatever you must to obtain it. Parley if necessary─we simply must have it.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: You need do no more than follow the road north out of Ul'dah. Before long, it will give way to the Timberline, which will lead you straight into the heart of Gridania.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Make what preparations you must. But remember─time is of the essence. May the gods go with you.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], you must make for Gridania and find more starfall grass. Its medicinal properties may prove to be the key to curing Damielliot's ailment.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: You might think about consulting any adventurers you happen upon along the way. There may be more useful information to be had─who can say? Just make sure you procure as much of the stuff as you can.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: And should you find any who have bought up whatever starfall grass there is, do whatever you must to obtain it. Even parley if need be.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Gridania lies within the forests to the north, deep within the Black Shroud. The trade routes will see you there.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Take care not to stray too far east once in the wood. The last place you want to get lost is in sylph territory.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Traveling merchants often bring us word of the goings-on in Gridania.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Many of Ul'dah's own traders wish to establish a foothold there─close as it is. But if their stories are to be believed, the Gridanians are invariably hard of head and tight of purse.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: The journey to the north can be an arduous one. Many do not take well to the sudden changes in climate.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Do be well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Your trip is an important one. The fate of the Phrontistery may well hang in the balance.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Starfall grass? I don't believe I've ever─wait, perhaps I have heard that name somewhere before.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Yes, yes, I'm sure of it. I was just making the rounds here at the Canopy, and overheard some traveler or another commenting on its use as a powerful healing agent.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: And what is it that brings you to fair Gridania, friend? Starfall grass?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: I'm afraid I'm not familiar with that particular species. But I've two questions for you all the same─is it valuable? And if so, where can I find it?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: From the Phrontistery of Frondale, are you? And come all this way to Gridania seeking starfall grass, no less. Aye, I know the stuff. For in legend and lore, there are fabled blades of grass, and there are fabled blades of steel, and the true bard sings of both.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: That said, 'tis known well enough to be a right rare herb, that one. Scarce makes it to market afore being straightways bought up.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Why is it that people always seem to forget what we traveling bards spend most of our time doing? No, not “barding.” Traveling! I've come here to hear what tales there are to be heard in Gridania, and once I have, I'll be off in search of the next.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Now, seeing as Eorzea's roads are long, and her sanctuaries few and far between, I lug a wee cartload of remedies about to treat those ailments me prayers can't cure─remedies including a certain rare grass. Of course, I wouldn't bother lugging them about if I didn't need them─and I've no intention of parting with me own stash.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: What can I tell you of the bard Penelope? Hehehe, looking for some leverage, are you? It'll do you no good. She's as clever as any, that one─and more than most.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Sweeten the deal with a sack of Frondale's funds?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: You must be quite motivated! Very well, let me have a little think...

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Not much is known of the passing bards. As a rule, they prefer singing of others to speaking of themselves. But I do know from whence your bard hails, if that'll help.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: <sigh> Please, spare me your games. I've a guild to run, for gods' sakes.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Sweeten the deal with a sack of Frondale's funds?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: So, she has some herbs that you need, does she? Why not try and parley with her? Not many bards can refuse a good parley─they pride themselves on the skill of their tongues far too much for that.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Penelope? Yes, of course I know of her. Near all Gridanians do.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: But it is simply not proper for a lady to discuss the affairs of another. Perhaps you would care to hear me speak of my own?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Let me see... Ah, but of course! I will speak of our fine establishment! You see, I've long had a mind to renovate the place, but our coffers simply do not seem to replenish themselves as readily as once they did.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Sweeten the deal with a sack of Frondale's funds?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: A pleasure doing business with you. Hahaha!

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: <hiss> I ought to burrry my teeth in your stinking flesh!

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Sweeten the deal with a sack of Frondale's funds?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Thank you for coming to the Roost. We hope to see you again soon.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
The Boy and the Dragon Gay
The Boy and the Dragon Gay
The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Lower your voice! Aye, I've heard the tale of the Boy and the Dragon Gay, and more times than one. But the archbishop in Ishgard has declared it a heretic's tale. Best not to recount it here, so close to the mountains.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: I've come to hear what less [@1A(1)]controversial[@1A(0)] tales there are to be heard in Gridania, and once I have, I'll be off to Ishgard in search of the next. If the gods are good, we shall meet again, adventurer.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: I've been to Gridania myself. Tell me, what was it about the forest that most struck you?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: For me, it was the quiet. There's nothing like it in Ul'dah. Many of the city's wealthier residents sojourn in Gridania simply to escape the din of the city. It's not something that's oft considered─the value of silence.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: So, you [@1A(1)]didn't[@1A(0)] find the Gridanians to be hard-headed? Aye, well, I don't suppose that's too much of a surprise. You're an adventurer, after all. Parleying can take your kind a long way.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: When I said folks called them a stubborn lot, I meant in trade. Ul'dahn merchants liken bartering with forestborn to chewing sand.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: I've heard stories that the Black Shroud is home to as yet unknown beasts and beings. Did you hear any such talk in your time there?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Living in Eorzea's most prosperous nation, it's hard to imagine such remote and wild regions still exist. Tell me, did you find the natives...barbaric?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Ah, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], you have returned. I trust that your labors bore fruit? Most excellent. The Phrontistery stores can never have too much starfall grass. It is an [@1A(1)]extremely[@1A(0)] potent reagent─too potent for ingestion as is, in fact. Only an alchemist who truly takes the time to understand its potential can then coax it into its fullest healing expression.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: No doubt you are weary from your travels, but there is one more task I would ask of you. Healer S'lyhhia has been eagerly anticipating your return. You had...best speak to her directly.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: I have seen the children in low spirits before, but now...well, they are utterly despondent. Healer S'lyhhia hardly has the time to be amusing them with faerie tales and legends.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Please, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], entertain the children with talk of your recent travels to Gridania. It always lifts their spirits to hear of the world beyond the Phrontistery walls.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: It is good to see you returned, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I know it was not asked of you, but I wonder, did you hear any tales on your journey?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: The young ones have been up in arms, crying out for a story, but my duties keep me from obliging them. Would you mind giving them the pleasure of your company─if only for a short while?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
The Boy and the Dragon Gay
The Boy and the Dragon Gay
The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: So good of you to come, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Please, make your way to Damielliot's sickroom. You will find the way open to you.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: You must look in on Damielliot at once. As I said, we are gathering together any he might know in an attempt to stimulate his dormant senses. You will do this small thing, won't you?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: You may come across some of the other young ones at play in the children's ward. They are here in the same capacity as you. See to it you don't scare them off.

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay
text_en: Perhaps you should reconsider what it is that brought you to us. The suffering of Damielliot is felt by all here. Would you truly stand by and do nothing?

quest_names: The Boy and the Dragon Gay

text_en: P-Please...help...me...
Master Damielliot was whispering in his sleep just a bit ago. Did you hear it? He was, I swear he was! If you don't believe me, just go and listen!
Help... Help...me...
You are too kind to us. I shall fetch some of the children's toys. Perhaps they will prove to be of use.
So, you have heard about Damielliot's worsening condition?
His sleep is punctuated with feverish fits and moans of pain. It is simply too much for the eyes of children.
None of our poppies or nightshades do aught to ease Damielliot's pain. His body has developed a resistance to them.
Just keep an eye to the halls, here. Healers are oft running to his room with hopeful faces, having happened upon some possible new treatment. But all return downcast and defeated.
Frondale's Phrontistery boasts the finest healers and alchemists in all Eorzea─true masters of their craft.
We are renowned for shrinking from neither grotesque wound nor acute suffering. But Damielliot's pain is... His groans, they... I-I cannot bring myself to look upon him.
The young ones no doubt sense that something terrible will soon come to pass. I believe that is why they refuse to leave Damielliot's side.
They are doing only that which they hope others would do for them.
Is something bad going to happen to Master Damielliot? He isn't going to die, is he? ...Is he?
He's very poorly, isn't he? I think it must really hurt. Can't somebody do something? I don't want to see him like this anymore. Please make him better...
I [@1A(1)]suppose[@1A(0)] I'll go back to my room. But if I fall asleep...I could wake up dead tomorrow.
Do you think he is in pain? Maybe he is just sleeping because if he wakes up it will hurt more. We can't leave him alone, we just can't!
Help... Help...me...
Help... P-Please...
The dragon... It was the dragon. It came from above, and...I...I fell. Yes...that's why I fell.
Here... Take this...
I-I can't move. Somebody... <grunt> Help... Is anybody there?
Thank you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]... Thank you...
You... You saved me.
After the dragon... After the fall...
Were you dreaming of dragons, Damielliot? Like the dragons in the story you told us?
Did you fall off a cliff, too? Just like the little boy did?
Did you meet a little dragon? A little dragon like in the story? Did you!?
What do you think hurts more? Being sick like Damielliot or falling off a cliff like the boy in the story? I think they'd both hurt a [@1A(1)]lot[@1A(0)].
Thank you for helping Damielliot get better! Now that he's awake, he can tell us stories again!
Did I hear some sort of commotion coming from the children's ward? Oh gods... He hasn't...has he?
[@1A(1)]Awake!?[@1A(0)] Twelve be praised! I had feared the worst!
There is no need for us to go through with the treatment now that Damielliot has regained consciousness.
Such drastic measures are only considered for the comatose, and only then as a last resort. The gods are good to have returned him to us in time to avoid it.

The word going around the Phrontistery is that Damielliot was dreaming of dragons all that time. It's strange─such creatures are the stuff of faerie tales here in the desert. In reality, dragons keep to the mountains of the far north and the lands of Ishgard.
Actually...now that I think on it, I did hear in passing once that Damielliot had spent some time there...though I may be mistaken.

I confess, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I have a reason for asking you here. Since Damielliot's condition has worsened, the children refuse to leave his bedside. But the healers have resolved to administer a treatment we do not wish for them to see.
The children have come to admire you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and would heed your words before those of any other. Please, speak to them for us. For Damielliot...
You are too kind to us. I shall fetch some of the children's toys. Perhaps they will prove to be of use.
I have no desire to resort to brute force, but I shall, should the children leave me no other recourse.
But it is trying enough that they are sick and away from home. I do not wish for them to endure further trauma at my hand.
Don't go equating the Gods' Quiver with them polearm-wielding Wood Wailers, now. They put down evils born within the forest. We repel evils come from without.
And there's no greater evil out there than the Ixal. We'll need you fighting them as soon as you're able. Now go and speak with Keelty. She'll see to your training.
Well met, friend. I myself am newly come to the Gods' Quiver. I pray we may serve the wood together for many moons hence.
The value of archery lies in its lethality at range. But range doesn't amount to a pot of piss if you lack the skill to hit your target.
And unless you pinpoint your enemies' vitals, you'll give them a chance to close and counter.
Every arrow loosed requires intense focus. So intense, in fact, that we're practically defenseless when taking aim.
That's why the leaders insist we range in pairs. We have to watch each other's backs, especially when there are no Wailers or conjurers around to do it for us.
To think that even the slightest errant step could incur the greenwrath... Be careful out there. I'd rather fight a hungry Ixal than an angry elemental any day!
They say that if you waken an elemental's fury, it banishes you to a hellish prison where time stands still. Don't know if it's true or not, but I'm in no hurry to find out.
Have you been paired yet? It's strange... Before joining the Quiver I had always looked after myself. But to suddenly have my life thrown into the hands of another was very...humbling.
We've yet to see an Ixal enter the Twelveswood and not defile it in some way. Even the elementals recognize them as enemies. Don't think twice before emptying your quiver at any you come across.
Do not take your patrols lightly. They are essential to protecting lives─both of the beasts themselves, and the leatherworkers who depend on them.
The watch is yours, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I imagine Keelty has already set out for Camp Emerald Moss.
A ranging into the Twelveswood already!? It must be nice to be an adventurer... I still can't even draw my bowstring.
To properly guard the Twelveswood, one must first know and respect the circle of life. The forest's balance is fragile. We cannot allow it to be disturbed by evils from without.
You've been paired with Keelty? Ah...I've heard she can be very... My prayers are with you.
A pairing is a profound thing. It cannot exist without trust and ability─the trust to place your life in the hands of another, and the ability to guard the life placed in your own.
You heard a scream and she was gone?
Then what the bloody hells are you doing back here!? Get out there and find her!
You really saw an Ixal? Well, they rarely hunt alone. I hope the one you saw wasn't simply distracting you while his flock ambushed Keelty.
Abandoning your partner in the face of danger is punishable by exile! You'd best go and find her. Now!
I'm relieved to see you both returned safe. Scares like that remind me why I took a clerical post.
At least one conjurer is assigned to each guild in Gridania. They function as mediums of sorts, conveying the will of the elementals to those who cannot hear them.

Brother Morys and Sister M'koliwe are the two conjurers assigned to the Gods' Quiver. Sister M'koliwe joined us quite recently, with orders to keep an eye on a certain archer known for her...spontaneity.
I hope Keelty is all right. She's as nice a lass as they come.
I don't know how it is that she's always coming to harm. Most of the others fault her for being clumsy and a bit oblivious.
Welcome back from your first patrol. We'll make an archer out of you yet, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]!

Keelty assures me you show great promise. We need many more like you if we are to continue our fight against the Ixal. Nevertheless, there is an important lesson to be learned from your experiences, is there not? You know of what I speak, yes?
Do you know of what Nonolato speaks?
Good! You fell under attack and allowed your partner to come to harm. Remember, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], we derive our safety from trust and ability. Without them, we are nothing.
No!? Gods, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)], you fell under attack and allowed your partner to come to harm! Never forget, we derive our safety from trust and ability. Without them, we are nothing.
What? Keelty sent you off on your own!?

Why that godsdamned─I've lost count of the number of times she's done this. And scolding her does naught save sore my throat. It's only a matter of time before her actions meet with the direst of consequences.
<sigh> What's done is done. Here, take your reward. The Quiver will have work for you again soon enough.
We are the Gods' Quiver, and our will is that of the elementals─to punish all who would visit harm upon the wood.
Join our ranks, adventurer. In return for your service, you shall learn the ways of the bow. What say you?
Enlist in the Archers' Guild?
Very good. But be forewarned─the Twelveswood can be a fickle mistress. She demands respect. You must never cross her borders with malice or deception in your heart.

Any dolt with hands can nock an arrow, but it takes an archer's eye to see one to its target. And targets are in no short supply, friend. The greatest threats facing us now are those foul Ixal buzzards and the damned imperials pouring out of Garlemald. Enemies in kind, but as different as night and day.

Our war with the Ixal has been waged since the time of our fathers' fathers, and theirs before them. Since before the elementals granted our kind entry into the wood, even. When the only refuge to be found was deep below the ground.
The Ixal must be stopped, no matter the cost. We'll not abide them to run unchecked through the Twelveswood, defiling the elementals' work. Will you pledge yourself to this cause?

So be it. All that remains is for you to form your bond. We require all archers to range in pairs outside the city. You'll find your partner within. Midlander lass by the name of Keelty. You two play nice, now.
No stomach for it, eh? You're certainly not the first adventurer to turn tail at the mere mention of Ixal.
That is most unfortunate. Perhaps I was foolish to believe an outsider could comprehend the importance of our mission.
Go and speak with Keelty. You must make for Owl's Nest with all haste.
See those papers safe to the hands of the Knights of Ishgard, and no other. Go now, and Twelve be with you.
Our sole purpose is to protect the forest. What business could Nonolato possibly have with the Knights of Ishgard?
So it's to be Ishgard, is it? Well, you need only head west out of the Twelveswood, and make for the mountains. The way is simple, but long.
The region is fraught with its own dangers, which is why we seldom trade with them. In fact, last I heard, their gates were barred to outsiders.
You may come across armored knights on chocoboback once in Coerthas. Should that happen, I suggest you mind your manners.

Do not confuse the Knights of Ishgard with those of Limsa. If you ask me, it's a crime to let those Barracudas style themselves knights. Knights of a bloody fish? Laughable. No, it is the Ishgardians who are the true knights─they who value honor and respect above all else.
Gridania and Ishgard have raised their banners against one another several times in the past. The Battle of Dragonfall, in particular, was...tragic.
I've heard it said the Gods' Quiver has been in close contact with the Knights of Ishgard. I'm sure it is no cause for concern.
Still, it begs the question─with [@1A(1)]which[@1A(0)] order of knights are we in treaty?
I'll never understand the people of Owl's Nest. Who would choose to live in such a perilous place?
Not that I would rather they take refuge in the Twelveswood, mind you. That would only worsen the problems we now face.
You are speaking of the ranging into Coerthas, yes?
Nonolato has briefed me, but with my wounds I'll only slow you down. Go ahead without me and I'll meet you at Owl's Nest.
Stick to the roads and you should be able to avoid any trouble.
Victory in our endless battle with the dragons is the dearest wish of all true Ishgardians.
It is an honor and a privilege to join the ranks of the Dragonsbane. To earn that privilege, you must first prove your worth.
You're far from the safety of the trees, adventurer. The elementals will not save you here.
This hamlet lies within the jurisdiction of Ishgard. Observe her law, or suffer her justice.
Aye? And who'll tend yer crops when their dragonfire sends ye home charred to a crisp? Fightin' ain't our way, never has been. Leave the fightin' to the adventurers, like this'un here.

Them knights have the right of it. Us farmers ought to be fightin' the heretics ourselves when we can. Ain't no cause for bein' afeared. Prick 'em an' they bleed, same as any. An' if they bleed, we can kill 'em.
Y'ask me, it's the patrols what need bolsterin'. Any soul seen abroad without cause should be caught an' questioned!
Were you granted audience with the Knights of Ishgard garrisoned at Owl's Nest? Very good.
Ser Vairemont? Your timing was fortunate. No doubt he will see to our dilemma at once.
And what of Keelty? I see you've somehow managed to return on your own, yet again.
The letters contained news of heretics? Hmmm... I have heard such stories from Ishgard, but what concern is it of the Gods' Quiver?
I traveled to Ishgard myself, not long ago.
The Knights of Ishgard made me swear before gods and man not to speak of anything I'd seen or heard during my time there. Things being what they were, I'm half grateful they did.
I heard you made it all the way to Owl's Nest.
The people of that poor hamlet have been at war with the dragons for longer than most can remember─not unlike ourselves and the Ixal.
It was Keelty's wish to be paired with an adventurer. Didn't want to get too attached, I suppose.
She had another partner before you. He forsook the Quiver and the Twelveswood long ago. None think he'll return, but she claims she'll wait as long as it takes.

These lands are to be purged of all who would take a life in violation of the law, no matter their history─that is the archbishop's word. It is but a matter of time before this fiend is apprehended or killed.
I still haven't found answers to the questions that brought me here, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. And I will not leave until I have them.
I'm sorry, but you will have to return without me. I promise I won't be far behind. I'll catch up to you on the road─somewhere near Camp Emerald Moss.
I still haven't found answers to the questions that brought me here, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. And I will not leave until I have them.
I'm sorry, but you will have to return without me. I promise I won't be far behind. I'll catch up to you on the road─somewhere near Camp Emerald Moss.
There are those who oppose the Conclave─condemned by Ishgard for their crimes. Such sinners cannot escape the eyes of the conjurers.
If Siward were to return to the forest, he too would face a similar fate.
Of course, how could I have been so blind? Nonolato called upon the might of Ishgard to flush out the heretics hiding in the wood.
Those taken prisoner are heretics, plain and simple. They decry the faith of Ishgard, and are eternally condemned for it.
That is why they fled and sought refuge in the Twelveswood.
The Battle of Dragonfall is still a tender scar. Neither Gridania nor Ishgard is likely to soon forget.

Hopefully, incidents like this latest one will serve to improve relations. With the Garleans and the beast tribes at our borders, the prospect of being flanked by the mounted strength of Ishgard does not bear thinking about.
The conjurers saw Lord Yuhelmeric and his men safely out of the forest.
The elementals have no love for the Ishgardians. Without an escort, they would not have made it out of the wood alive.
I trust your last ranging taught you something of the harmful changes being wrought on the Twelveswood by the outside world.
Between the Garleans and the Ixal, our resources are spread too thin. Still, we must do what we can.
The Wood Wailers have begun to solidify Gridania's bonds with the other nations. But the conjurers inform us that not all we do sits well with the elementals. Where we see alliances, they see evils.
We must do more to prove our loyalty and sincerity to the elementals. We must put their minds at ease by restoring tranquility to the wood.
You are to travel west, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], to the nation of Ishgard. You will be carrying important papers which must be delivered to the Knights of Ishgard, and none other.
I knew I could count on you. Take this, then, and make for Owl's Nest together with Keelty.
You surprise me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I had not thought you the kind to be cowed by reputation, as formidable as the Knights may be.
You must find Keelty before she comes to harm. Someone or something is hunting her, I'm sure of it.
I regret I have no spare archers to send with you. Heed these words─the Twelveswood is no friend of yours. You must be on constant vigil at all times.
Searching for Keelty, are you? Haven't seen her. Heard she's been paying visits to Ishgard of late, though. Maybe try your luck there.
According to the conjurers, there are far worse things in the wood than heretics from Ishgard. The elementals are agitated of late.
Orders for a ranging will come down soon enough. It is only a matter of time.
Keelty? I spoke with her briefly. Some nonsense about having a favor to ask of the elementals.

Not bloody likely without a moogle or a conjurer around, though. Hells if I know what she was on about. Maybe she was planning a trip to Everschade, near Sorrel Haven. Or perhaps─ Actually, just forget I said anything.
Young Gridanians rarely leave the forest for the other cities. There may be the odd exception, but for the most part, to hail from the forest is to know its safety.
Yes, I've heard about Keelty. You shouldn't worry so much. She is a far greater archer than you imagine.

Still, I see your concern is genuine... Look, I don't know if this helps, but I've seen her wandering alone just south of here on a couple of occasions. Some say a tree with the power to grant wishes grows in the forest depths. Perhaps she has gone seeking it.
Keelty was born and raised here, and everyone knows her for a saint. Who or what could possibly have reason to hunt her?
I can't think of a single person who would wish her ill. But she's wounded so often, it's difficult to believe that it's the work of Ixal alone.
What is that wide-eyed look for? Did you find something?

You found Keelty...and yet you've returned without her [@1A(1)]again[@1A(0)]? I truly cannot fathom whether your chief failing is a lack of bravery or a lack of brains. For Keelty's sake, I hope it's the latter. Now get back out there and save her!
I've never seen Keelty so sullen. This better not be your doing!
The conjurers claim an outsider was driven from the wood. Some sort of assassin from what I heard, and a wanted man in Ishgard.
Have you ever heard of the Faces of Mercy? If not, I envy you your innocence. Some evils in this world are best not known.
Pray all you like to the elementals, they're not like to listen. It's the same as any Eorzean praying to the Twelve, is it not?
The elementals protect us, as we protect the forest. Knowing this gives Gridanians a sense of happiness that others cannot possibly fathom.
You're carrying a great weight, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I can sense it.

Confiding secrets in another will strengthen the bond between you. But each is a weight, and should that bond grow too heavy, it will only serve to drag you both down. If you would spare yourselves that anguish, choose your secrets wisely.
Keelty's injuries were caused by arrows, that much is clear. Yet they were not made by the likes of any arrow I've ever seen.
Siward?
There's a name I have not heard for a long while. He was a fine archer, paired with Keelty some years ago. One day, without so much as a word, he quit the Quiver and left the wood.
I do not know all of what has happened, but I am glad to have Keelty back safely. You should go and speak with her, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Keelty has yet to return. But I haven't the manpower to conduct a search, now least of all.

You have a right to know... We suspect that Keelty is being pursued. By whom or what we cannot say, but there is no other explanation for her frequent accidents and odd behavior. She denies it, of course.
I realize that she may not always be completely forthcoming with you, but perhaps you may be able to discover something. Please, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], find Keelty!
I swear you were sent by the Twelve themselves, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Your tireless service honors us all.

Years ago, Keelty was paired with a truly gifted young Midlander. One of the best rangers the guild's ever had, and the finest damned archer I've ever seen. The day he turned his back on the wood, we lost more than a man. We lost a part of Keelty, as well. She hasn't trusted another since─and I fear it may yet prove her downfall.
I cannot say where she has gone, but others claim to have seen her in the forest. You would do well to ask any you come across.
I regret I have no spare archers to send with you. Heed these words─the Twelveswood is no friend of yours. You must be on constant vigil at all times.
Forgive me, it seems I have asked too much. I would not have troubled you...but I believe her life to be in the gravest danger.

It is tragic. That woman wishes to serve Nald'thal, yet is deaf to Master's words.
You have seen the deed done? Good. Go, then. I will make it known to the others that the time is near.

The beasts you must slay are the guano gnats near the entrance to the Copperbell Mines. Might you be [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]?
Oh, how embarrassing. I do apologize. Gods, I knew that old fool was spouting nonsense!
I've been waiting for you─in a way. Please, let me explain. Do you know of the Marasaja Pit? It is a prison, here in Ul'dah.

In prison, a man will do most anything to keep his mind occupied. Indeed, of late one of the inmates claims to hear the voice of Nald'thal. No doubt he has lost his mind after serving one hundred years of his life sentence.

He claims the Traders revealed to him that an adventurer bearing your name would come to hunt down foul beasts to procure what he calls [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000556,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000556,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. And with this gem would come the prisoner's freedom.
I've never seen anything quite like it. Of course, I make it for nothing more than the maniacal ravings of a cell[@1F]crazed, sweaty[@1F]toothed madman.
His name is Ququruka, and as if his story were not proof enough of his lunacy, he also styles himself a black mage.
But such magic was lost to Eorzea centuries ago. Who does this senile charlatan think he will fool with such rubbish?
<sigh> Nevertheless, some among the Order believe it ill-advised to ignore his words. And though I am still no believer, you have come, as he said you would.
So let us get to the bottom of this, shall we? It may be that you are an agent of fate, or perhaps you are merely a crooked old man's accomplice.
In either case, I ask that you travel to the Copperbell Mines, just as our deluded friend foretold. Near the entrance lurk beasts known as guano gnats.

According to our mummer, it is one of these gnats that carries this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000556,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000556,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].
It is no more than a pretty stone oft mentioned in bedtime stories and the tales of faeries. It certainly isn't something prized from the carcasses of shite-eating gnats.
I am embarrassed even to ask, but will you humor us all a bit through this foolishness?
You have my thanks. The sooner this ends, the better.
I'm sorry to send you on this wild dodo chase. Indeed, I pray Nald'thal [@1A(1)]has[@1A(0)] summoned you─but only to end this foolishness, rather than to prolong it.
Hah! It seems the old bugger's prophecy didn't take the free will of adventurers into account. Ohhh, this is rich!
If only that were the end of it... Sadly, the guild has charged me with seeing this idiocy through to its conclusion. <sigh>

I am pleased to see that you do not fear your newfound powers. But then, you adventurers were ever wont to embrace the new.
You are now ready to set forth on your journey─to find the keys required to seal the Voidgate. Hear me well, for mine are Master's own words.
“The next key requires the blood of sacrifice.
“Travel to western Thanalan. West beyond Nophica's Wells. There find the yarzon beast known as Daddy Longlegs, and by its blood slake the thirst of the land.
“Once drunk, its essence shall be borne away upon the aethereal currents of the earth, and thence serve to notify our friends in the wastelands that the time has come.

“Complete the task put to you, and the black mage testimony you carry will shine full with a new light. Light to envelop and absorb evil. Light to show you destruction and guide you to righteousness. This light is the key. Take it into you, and it will forever burn bright.”
...That is all. Do you understand and accept what you must do?
Master foretold as much. Here, take this linkpearl with you.
Contact us when the deed is done. Master will have further instructions for you. Go now, black mage, and may Nald'thal watch over you.
You are unfit for Master's words, so weak is your devotion. Leave now, and return only when you are truly prepared to walk the path of the black mage.

Upon hearing the truths spoken by Master, the Order has acknowledged his gifts. They have allowed him to retire within to meditate. I speak for him in his absence, yet I see you are not ready to hear his words. Return to me when you and the black magic are one.
The next black mage quest will be available from Lalai upon reaching level 35.
Recall Master's words.
“In western Thanalan, farther west still than Camp Horizon, is a cave recorded on no map of men. In its depths, Kazagg Chah awaits.”
Go forth then, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], for the Voidgate shall not seal itself!
Squaaawk! Perhaps you. See it, Dozol does.
Yes, I sense it. You are the one we seek─look, search, seek.

We meet again, [@SWITCH($E8(1),Hyur,Elezen,Lalafell,Miqo'te,Roegadyn)]─chosen of [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000556,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000556,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].
Its power brings us together again. At last the time has come. And yet I know nothing of [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] who would guide us. Come, tell me your name.
[@STRING($EB(1))]. I am Kazagg Chah, a thaumaturge, as were my forebears. I am the fourth of my line to walk this path, and it has brought me now to this land.

You have fed the aethereal currents with the blood of fiends. The [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000556,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000556,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] is proof of what you have done, and a sign of what you must yet do. Know that you must face death before your purpose can be fulfilled. Your next task will take you to the south of Camp Bald Knoll in western La Noscea. It is the blood of a beast known as Whitetalon for which the earth now thirsts.
Your foe is cunning. Formidable, yet cautious. She will not show herself at first, but rather set her minions upon you to test your mettle.

Slay them, and her, and the [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000556,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000556,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] will shine ever more brilliant. Great power, you have. But enough, is it? Squaaawk!

[@STRING($EB(1))] of the black, you return to me victorious.

[@2B([@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000556,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000556,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)])] burns bright. You are indeed the [@IF($E9(4),heiress,heir)] to a dark and ancient power, as Ququruka foretold.

Long ago, my great-grandfather uttered a prophecy:[@CR]“When four magi meet in a barren land,[@CR]Black powers of eld woven by their hand,[@CR]Shall see the fate of wickedness made stark,[@CR]And the path to light shall be lit by dark.”
The [@1A(1)]black powers of eld[@1A(0)] require no explanation. And know that [@1A(1)]wickedness[@1A(0)] refers to the evil birthed by the void.
That the seal holding the Voidgate shut will falter and fail is beyond doubt. Yet your deeds speak of determination and ability, and in them I spy hope. I have learned all of you that I must.
I have bestowed upon you the knowledge kept by my line. Here and now, I speak an oath to discard old grudges. By our power combined, the Voidgate will be sealed anew.

You have brought this old Amalj'aa much happiness. Few believed the words of my great-grandfather. He was mocked and ridiculed, and worse, ignored. Yet your coming has fulfilled the prophecy he spoke.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], the dark magic coursing through you shares a deep bond with the Voidgate. Should that portal be cast open, you will come to great peril.
Temper yourself, in both mind and body. When you are ready, seek out Dozol Meloc, and he will speak to you of your next task.
Growing stronger, you are. Squaaawk! Kazagg Chah awaits. You go!
I pray you are unhurt─uninjured, unwounded, unhurt. Kazagg Chah awaits you. Yes, yes, go now.

There are few who know of our existence, even among those versed in the ways of magic. Nor will you find mention of us in all but the most esoteric of texts.
Yet within the forbidden library of this Sacrarium, the secrets of our dark art lie encrypted.

It was Master himself who deciphered and read the texts, some one hundred years past. It is said the first of our kind were the favored of Nald'thal, and it was He who entrusted them with the duty of sealing the Voidgate.
But as you well know, the power of black magic lies in its great potential for destruction. The slightest errancy in its use may give way to the most tragic of disasters.
Of the disappearance of the black mages from Eorzea, Master says only, “We must not repeat the errors of the past.”
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], Master has made known to me what it is you must now do. Listen now, with all your being...

“In the hands of one who will usher our return, [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000556,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000556,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], testimony of our creed, will shine with a new light. And by its light, the three keepers will become your allies.
“In western Thanalan, farther west still than Camp Horizon, is a cave recorded on no map of men. In its depths, Kazagg Chah awaits.”

...That is all. Do you understand and accept what you must do? Dwell not on the fact that the Amalj'aa are the sworn enemies of Ul'dah. It is not your place to question Master's will─for it is the will of Nald'thal Himself.
Master foretold as much. Go forth then, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], for the Voidgate shall not seal itself!
You are unfit for Master's words, so weak is your devotion. Leave now, and return only when you are truly prepared to walk the path of the black mage.
You are not yet ready to take the next step of your journey. Return to me when you are more practiced in the ways of black magic. Then, and only then, will I impart to you Master's words.
The next black mage quest will be available from Lalai upon reaching level 40.
You travel for the Shroud, yes? Yes, yes, it is a mysterious place. Home to timeless elementals, and all manner of strange creatures─uncanny, bizarre, strange.
A secret waits in the wood, too. Waits there, hidden─forgotten, unseen, hidden! Yes, yes, laid to rest there by a black mage of old, it was. But will you find it?
Gloom senses [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Senses keeper of key. Repel it, you must. Repel with hidden black magic.

Deep in Black Shroud. West Shroud. Northwest of Turning Leaf. Mossy stone stela. Raise [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000556,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000556,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] there, you must. Raise high! Squaaawk!
Gem guides black mage. Chosen black mage. Unlock hidden magic, it will.
Go now! Fly! Go, fly means. Squaaawk!
A powerful black magic has awakened within you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. It has not gone unnoticed. Gloom seeps forth from the Voidgate. Darkness gathers. The way before us will not be easy.
Dozol Meloc's words are steeped in truth. Though he speaks as one touched by the gods, and is prone to caprice, his motives are pure. By his guidance, you will find the black magic that awaits you.
You need not report your every coming and going to us. Master sees all through the eyes of Nald'thal. A task stands before you. See it done.
A stone stela covered in moss rises here.
Your Gem of Shatotto shines bright, revealing an inscription in the stone.

To close Voidgate, strong black magic you need. Ready for test, are you?
Ready, are you?
Very good. Squaaawk! You have sharp sense, like Dozol. Noticed, have you? Your aura. Strangeness, it has.
Fool! Squaaawk! But no matter. Sharp sense, Dozol has. Your aura. Strangeness, it has.
Now, the Voidgate. Gloom, it makes. Like black breath. Gloom drawn to black magic. Drawn to you. Like moth to flame. Black magic, it seeks, to corrupt and make own.
Losing strength, seal is. Black magic and Voidgate share bond. Very deep. But must not leave be too long. Else other side maybe take you! Squaw-aw-awk.
No fear yet! Still weak, Gloom is. Time, you have. Strong [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)] find next key!
Teach you, Dozol will, what must do.
Many black mages, there were. Long ago. One more powerful than rest. Very powerful. Epic, even. Epic black mage.
Black magic too powerful. Too dangerous. Wrong hands must not have. Know this, he did. Enciphered spells. Hid secrets. Dark way passed to few. Very few.
Teaching, writing, spread over realm. Lost to time, they were. Forgotten. One carved in stone. Still in stone. Stone in wood. Wood of Black Shroud. Squaaawk!
Chosen [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)] is chosen! Unleash power of this black magic, you can. Key, it is! Key to end of Gloom!
Knowledge of my line, this is. Passed to Dozol from mother. From mother mother. From mother mother mother. Four hatchings past. Strong mage, she was. Epic, even. Epic mage!
Great love for dark art. More than anything. Joined with lizardmen to learn all. Name betrayer, she was. Chased from village. Squaaawk!

Her words, Dozol keeps. Teach to strong [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)] now.[@CR]“Four magi meet, in barren land,[@CR]Old black powers, have they, in hand[@CR]Fate of all wicked, be made stark[@CR]Path to light then be lit by squaaawk!”[@CR]That her squaaawk. Not Dozol squaaawk. Should be [@1A(1)]dark[@1A(0)], Dozol thinks.
Good words. Deep words. Bring Dozol here, they did. To pass on. Not Dozol alone. Others come too. Other mages.
Birdman. Lizardman. No matter. All wait for strong [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. True grit, you have. Help you, Dozol will.
Deep in Black Shroud. West Shroud. Near stone stela of Turning Leaf. Lurking beast, there is. Slay it, you must. No need fear beast. Strong [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)] is strong!
Go now! Fly! Go, fly means. Squaaawk!
Scared of beast, you are? Disappoint, Dozol is. [@1A(1)]Very[@1A(0)] disappoint.
Black mage, you are. Dozol hear all from lizardman. You come back when ready. Next task, I give. Squaaawk!
The next black mage quest will be available from Dozol Meloc upon reaching level 45.

The tablet seems to say one who would close the Voidgate must first find this sacred garb─gear, loot, garb! Yes, yes, only then can the Voidgate be closed.

I know the first four places written on the tablet. Yes, yes, these four I know. I will mark them on your map. This fifth, I... [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)]? I have never heard of such a place. No, no, never.
One does not simply walk into these four places. There is evil there that does not sleep─slumber, rest, sleep. Oh, do be careful. Very, very careful.
You have reclaimed the key from the depths of the Shroud─wood, forest, Shroud. Yes, you have done well. Very, very well. Indeed, you are the one foretold of in our words─prophecy, legend, words.
I am Da Za, Da Za I am. Yes, yes, a thaumaturge of the kobolds, Two Hundred and Sixty-Ninth Order Mendicant Da Za. A legend of my people brought me to this Thanalan. Such is what legends do.

“When four magi meet in a barren land,[@CR]Black powers of eld woven by their hand,[@CR]Shall see the fate of wickedness made stark,[@CR]And the path to light shall be lit by dark.” Black, shadow, dark.
You have heard these words before. Yes, yes, here I found Kazagg Chah and Dozol Meloc. The words that brought us all to Thanalan are the same─equal, identical, same.

It was one hundred years ago that a kobold first deciphered the legend─decrypted, decoded, deciphered. The great mage who did it was my own ancestor, First Order Patriarch Da Gu. Yes, yes, my very own.

But he broke kobold law. The First Patriarch must never leave O'Ghomoro. No, no, never. But leave he did. He set out from La Noscea to pursue this legend. And for that he was named traitor─betrayer, turncloak, traitor.

He wanted to know more of the legend. To know all of it. Yes, yes, he wanted this more than any other. Such was not my feeling. No, no, not at all. When I first heard this legend, I felt strange─peculiar, odd, strange.
I felt I must do something. I could not simply be idle. I, too, left La Noscea, just as Da Gu before me. Yes, and I have come here to Thanalan.
Now I see the legend is real. Yes, the words kept by Kazagg Chah, Dozol Meloc, and Da Za are true. [@1A(1)]You[@1A(0)] have appeared. That is no coincidence. No, no, none at all.
I may not know as much as the others in the ways of magic, but I am a kobold! Yes, yes, I am. And we kobolds are good at finding things─treasures, trinkets, things. I will give you what help I can.

Da Gu left behind many things when he left. Yes, many, many things. I was given a stone tablet. The others in my family thought it rubbish─dross, refuse, rubbish. Its surface has many scratches, you see. Yes, many, many. But I sense in it a great power.
Here, it may give some─ Your gem! The light! It is illuminating the tablet. The scratches are...growing!? Gods, they are no scratches! No, no, not scratches at all. They are carvings! Words!
“Know thee, brave keeper of Shatotto's light,[@CR]As these very words wax plain to thy sight,[@CR]The seal what was cast doth shudder and sigh,[@CR]And the Voidgate's dread sundering draws nigh.”
“To ward against the creeping of the Gloom,[@CR]Thou needeth great garb to stay any doom,[@CR]To this sacred wear thy thoughts must now tend,[@CR]Unto thy black command darkness shall bend.”
This tablet was more important than I imagined. Yes, yes, much more. It seems to say one who would close the Voidgate must first find this sacred garb─gear, armor, garb!

And the names of places are written here as well. Yes, yes, these four I know. I will mark them on your map. This fifth, I... [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)]? I have never heard of such a place. No, no, never.
These words are meant for the [@1A(1)]keeper of Shatotto's light[@1A(0)]. Yes, yes, the gem will be needed to find this garb, I think. In this I cannot help─aid, assist, help.

I cannot go with you. No, no, I cannot. But I will look into this [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)]. You must travel to these other four places, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Yes, you must. You will very much need this [@1A(1)]garb[@1A(0)], I think.
One does not simply walk into these four places. There is evil there that does not sleep─slumber, rest, sleep. Oh, do be careful. Very, very careful.
I see, I see. You are just returned from the Shroud─wood, forest, Shroud. You must be tired. Yes, yes, very tired. Come see me again when you are ready.
Garb to guard against Gloom? Never heard this, has Dozol. How works? How!? Squaaawk!
I see. So the one who would close the Voidgate must be possessed of sacred garb...
There were many mages of the black in days of old. Mayhap these artifacts are the legacy they have left to us.
There is little time left. You have been told what you must do. Now do it.

It seems Da Gu set out for the [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)] to seek the artifact hidden there. Yes, yes, he did. But he made his journey one hundred years ago, and no record of it remains.
Perhaps Dozol Meloc or Kazagg Chah can tell you something more. They are both very wise─learned, knowing, wise. Visit them and ask if they have discovered anything new.
Dozol Meloc's great-grandmother also set out from her home one hundred years ago? That is curious. Yes, yes, most curious. It cannot be mere coincidence─chance, happenstance, coincidence.
Kazagg Chah's ancestor as well─also, too, as well? Are you certain it was one hundred years ago─a century, five score, one hundred?
The power of destruction. Yes, yes, the black magic. [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)]... Awakening? Most curious.
Is it true─absolute, certain, true? Was it all lies to free this Barbatos? To [@1A(1)]destroy[@1A(0)] Eorzea?
Disturbing. Yes, yes, most disturbing.
The legend... Yes, yes, the words of my ancestor. I believed in them. They brought me to this land.
We must put things right, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. We must use our black magic to defend the realm─not destroy it. Yes, yes, we must.
Back from journey, you are. Dozol too. Returned to great nest in north. Ask about [@1A(1)]Solace[@1A(0)].
Learn nothing, Dozol did! Squaaawk!
Try hard, Dozol did. Asked many, many Ixal. When talk of black magic, grow quiet, they do.
Blood from four hatchings past, Dozol has. Ixal don't like. Think go over to Amalj'aa, Dozol will. Like mother mother mother before.
Always same, it is. Since long ago. Dozol and family hated by Ixal. Cast out. Squaaawk!
Small minds, Ixal have. Hold long grudge. Time of mother mother mother far past. One hundred years ago, it was.
Da Gu? Ancestor of Da Za? Left home? Search for [@1A(1)]Solace[@1A(0)], he did? One hundred years ago!?
Same as mother mother mother, it is! squaaawk! Both disappear one hundred years ago, they did! Maybe die! What means!? Squaaawk!
Bad feeling, Dozol has. Speak to Kazagg, you must!
Da Gu search for [@1A(1)]Solace[@1A(0)], he did. One hundred years ago. Same as mother mother mother, it is! Squaaawk!
Mean something, it does! Not chance. Go! Fly! Speak with Kazagg, you must! Squaaawk!
Ancestor of Kazagg Chah too? Left home? One hundred years ago? Search for [@1A(1)]Solace[@1A(0)], he did? Squaaawk!
Power of destruction. Magic to close Voidgate, it is! Black magic. Maybe mother mother mother knew, too? Knew of Voidgate, she did. Squaaawk!
Black magic? [@1A(1)]Open[@1A(0)] the Voidgate, it does? Squaaawk!
Stop him, you will? Dozol go with strong [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Squaaawk!
Welcome back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Yours has been a long and perilous quest. Dozol Meloc? He parted just before your coming.
He has gone to ask if any among his people know of the [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)]. I fear he has been sullen of late. I must remember to have words with him.
You have gathered the first of the four artifacts, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. That is no small feat.

Yet I fear little time remains. If the tablet of Da Za's great ancestor is to be believed, there are yet four more. Drawing near the Voidgate before you have found them all would be the height of folly.
I, too, have been searching for some clue as to where this [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)] lies. I have gone through all of the records left me by my great-grandfather, yet have discovered little.

The only seemingly relevant passage I found was his last. He put it to paper one hundred years ago, just before he bid farewell to his home. “The true power of destruction will be awoken in that most sacred of places.”
The power of destruction is black magic, of course. But as to what is meant by this “awakening”...I fear I am at a loss.
The ancestors of Da Za and Dozol Meloc? They too left their homes one hundred years ago? And damned for traitors, no less?
It could be mere coincidence... But I do not think it likely.
I fear this foreshadows our doom. Should you find aught else, I beseech you to tell me at once. I too will continue the search for answers.

My great-grandfather was among the foremost magi of his day. As were the ancestors of Da Za and Dozol Meloc of the same generation. And now it seems they all met with the same fate. A coincidence, perhaps, but I think not.
I fear this foreshadows our doom. Should you find aught else, I beseech you to tell me at once. I too will continue the search for answers.
Could it be? Could my great-grandfather have played some part in so vile a deed?
If my blood had some hand in this, then I too am responsible. Come, together let us put an end to this madness.
Not much time remains to you. Again, you have been told what it is you must do. Do it─see the Voidgate sealed.
Ququruka has disappeared! You must find him!
That man is no messenger of Nald'thal. He is a miscreant and a charlatan. Nothing more. One guilty of the most heinous of crimes.
None have seen him for days. I became worried, fearful. I decided to enter his chambers, though he prohibited any from doing so. It was there I found evidence of his deception.
The records he had hidden were damning. I now know why he was condemned as the greatest criminal of his day.
One hundred years past, he conspired with magi from the beast tribes to create a monstrosity that would destroy all of Eorzea─a monstrosity known as Barbatos.
On the verge of success, their plot was discovered by the Order of Nald'thal, and the Voidgate was forced closed before Barbatos could emerge.
For his heinous crime, Ququruka was cast into the Marasaja Pit, where he was to rot until his last breath.

The Order was loath to allow knowledge of this to spread, fearing others might seek to summon Barbatos forth. They therefore left no record of the plot, save for a few inscrutable documents, intelligible only to those to whom the secret had already been made known.
These were the last words I found among the bastard's scribblings.
“The answer lies in the number four. Four spells of the black. Four artifacts of eld. The blood of four races. By four alone shall the final power of destruction be awakened from the Voidgate.”

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]... Black magic is not the key to sealing the Voidgate. It is the key to [@1A(1)]opening[@1A(0)] it! Ququruka used us to revive this ancient dark art, and now means to finish what he began one hundred years ago.
We have all fallen victim to his lies. You as well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You are as culpable as myself and the others.
We must see this maniac stopped! There is no time! Hurry to Nald's Reflection, west of Camp Broken Water in southern Thanalan.

The Voidgate was used to hold back the monstrosity created by Ququruka and his beastmen companions. So the bastard bode his time, and now, a full century later, he has used us all in an attempt to force it open.
If nothing is done, Barbatos will soon be unleashed upon Eorzea!
There is no time! Hurry to Nald's Reflection, west of Camp Broken Water in southern Thanalan. Ququruka [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)] be stopped!
You have gathered the first four artifacts! Yes, yes, you have. Excellent!
I returned to La Noscea while you were away to ask about the [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)]. None of the kobolds learned in geography have ever heard of it. No, no, not a one.
I was not able to find a single hint─clue, inkling, hint. But I [@1A(1)]did[@1A(0)] hear that when Da Gu left O'Ghomoro, he was heard to say he was making for the [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)]!
We have seen the tablet's text. Yes, yes, we have. The tablet which belonged to Da Gu. Mayhap he too set out searching for this [@1A(1)]garb[@1A(0)].
But one hundred years have passed since his journey. There are few records, and those that do remain are vague─unclear, incomplete, vague.
Forgive me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I am no help. No, no, none at all.
What of Dozol Meloc and the others? Perhaps something has happened since you saw them last. Yes, yes, something.
Very good! I will continue my search for answers. Yes, yes, I will. I feel all of this is connected in some way.
Your journey has left you weary─tired, spent, weary. Rest now. Yes, yes, rest. Shhhhhh, sh, sh, sh. Come see me when you have regained your strength.
Forgive me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Yes, yes, I am so very sorry. I do not yet know where this [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)] is.
Please give me more time. Yes, just a bit. Come back when you have the power of the first four artifacts─garb, gear, artifacts.
The next black mage quest will be available from Da Za upon reaching level 50.

A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Ah, another guest. You are kind to pay me visit, young one.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Naught gives us elderly folk more pleasure than the company of the young. Add to that a steaming pot of tea and the beauty of the Twelveswood, and we could want for little more!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Ah. But the curl of your lip tells me that tea and scenery are not what you desire. You seek knowledge of archery, I take it? In which case, I'm afraid I must disappoint you...[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], was it?

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Yes, yes, I am Jehantel, the one they called the Godsbow─but that was in another life. I have long cast aside my bow, taking instead a harp to my breast. For years I have lived as a bard, going wherever the wind blows, exulting in the beauty of creation through song.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: To be sure, I still have the eyes to recognize a promising archer when I see one. And you, young one, have promise. Keep your nose to the grindstone, and one day you may count yourself a virtuoso of the bow.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Yet know that virtuosity is worthless without virtue. Aye, the words of the Ballad of the Vainglorious Fool tell us this much.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: ...You truly wish to remain and learn poetry and verse? Well, well, well...I must admit to being rather taken aback.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: In uncertain times such as these, there are few indeed who would devote their time to song as opposed to more “tangible” endeavors.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: You intrigue me, young one. I find myself growing curious as to how the melodies of old might find expression through you.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: I do believe a certain friend of mine would be of the selfsame opinion. Aye, that would be as good a place as any for us to begin.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Listen well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. There is a moogle named Pukno Poki, who resides within a cave situated east of here. I would have you present yourself to him.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Pukno Poki is possessed of a discerning eye for talent. If he sees potential in you, I should be well satisfied that you indeed have the makings of a bard.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Heed me, O Puissant Althyk! Turn Thee over the hourglass of time, that we might gaze upon the battles of yore!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Jehantel the Godsbow has made his camp somewhere north of Camp Tranquil. Being an agreeable sort of fellow, he should be willing enough to meet with you.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Kupoarrrgh! How could this have happened? It's just so...embarrassing! A blunder for the ages, kupo!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Hm? You understand what I'm saying, don't you?

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: That's a rare talent, I'll allow, but you've caught me at a bad time, kupo. Now, be a good adventurer and show yourself out─

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Jehantel sent you!? You should have said so sooner, kupo!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: You [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] know that Jehantel is no ordinary bard? His songs can salve your heart and strengthen your resolve. They can banish your fears and fill you with hope...and that's not even scratching the surface!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Why, to hear him perform is like bathing in sunbeams, kupo!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: I've asked, begged, and pled more times than I care to count for Jehantel to stay and sing in the forest. Only now has he deigned to set foot here again...but he's refusing to sing for us. That's a blatant breach of promise, kupo!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: ...But what's this? Why, your being resonates with a chord similar to Jehantel's! Perhaps even identical, kupo!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: By the Twelve, this means that things may yet turn out as planned! Why, you might even have it in you to surpass the man, and that's saying a [@1A(1)]lot[@1A(0)], kupo!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Egads! Your coming had so excited me, my predicament nigh escaped my mind!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: There's a charm that I had meant to give to Jehantel, you see, but it was stolen as I napped, kupo! I roused just in time to espy the thief─a Qiqirn shirrer─and attempted to give chase. Alas, drowsiness robbed me of my balance and I...was [@1A(1)]delayed[@1A(0)] by a nearby tree.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Last I saw of the thief, it was scurrying east, kupo. Now, I realize we've only just met, but would you mind recovering the charm and delivering it to Jehantel in my stead?

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: I'll take that surprised expression as a yes, kupo! Oh, and when you see Jehantel, tell him that Pukno Poki thinks him a cunning rogue, but is excited nonetheless! So excited, in fact, that he cannot help but sing![@CR]Kupololololo～♪

text_en: The charm I had promised Jehantel was stolen by a Qiqirn shirrer! The creature snatched it as I napped, and then fled east.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: You must liberate the charm by whatever means necessary and see it delivered to Jehantel, kupo! Oh, and when you see Jehantel, tell him that Pukno Poki thinks him a cunning rogue, but is excited nonetheless! So excited, in fact, that he cannot help but sing![@CR]Kupololololo～♪

text_en: Welcome back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I take it your meeting with Pukno Poki went well. Hm? A message, you say?

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: A cunning rogue, am I? Hah hah hah!

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: I suppose I must explain. Pukno Poki and I go back a long way, to when first I took up the harp. I made a promise to him then, one that I have yet to make good upon.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Pukno Poki desires that I remain here and sing, you see. Regrettably, I have been ill able to oblige him.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Duty called, you see─I had battlefields to stand upon and comrades to protect. Moreover, an event came to pass that rendered my being in the Twelveswood...problematic.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: I thought that by taking eager souls such as you under my wing, mayhap it would suffice to appease Pukno Poki.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Of course, he saw straight through my little ruse. What the moogles lack in grace, they amply make up for in wit.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: The creatures are great lovers of song. That you return with [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000557,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000557,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] is proof positive of his high regard for your potential as bard and archer both.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: The charm is a crystal known as the Soul of the Bard. Pukno Poki asked that you bring it to me, aye, but he meant for you to have it. It is a gift from the moogles, bestowed upon those they deem worthy of walking the path of the true bard.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: The Soul of the Bard harbors memories of the past─verses and refrains sung by the bards of old.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: As you gain in worldly experience, more of these memories will find expression through your being, imbuing your song with powers untold.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Now, it may surprise you to hear that bowmen and bards are as next of kin. By the same token, mastery of song is dependent upon one's prowess as an archer.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: The sense in this will be lost upon you at first, but in time the realization will dawn that bow and harp are but stringed instruments played by the same hand.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: Go now, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and let your body and soul drink deep of the melodies of old.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: When next we meet, I hope to see a fully fledged bard standing before me...one who exceeds even Pukno Poki's wildest expectations.

quest_names: A Song of Bards and Bowmen
text_en: The next bard quest will be available from Jehantel upon reaching level 35.
