Arthur is awake, and suffered me long enough to answer my questions. He is a good man, and a brave soul. He spoke of rapid fortifications being made in Ala Mhigo, and of Ala Mhigans being driven by lash and brand to make them.

He painted a godless picture, and I fear the reality of it even worse. A spy must needs smother his own feelings─to deny all that defines him. He had to stand by and watch Ala Mhigans beaten and worked and starved to death. It is enough to drive any man mad...

We are not godless machines, after all. The heart does not always accept what the mind knows. Mayhap it is all the more true for Gridanians. Nowhere have I seen an air of such love and brotherhood amongst a people.
...We must talk of other matters. This fortification of Ala Mhigo, it seems to be the initiative of a legatus newly come to the Eorzean front.

Heavily armored units, new magitek weaponry, extensive drilling of the troops─the Empire is in full motion. Unfortunately, Arthur knew nothing of this destructive force the elementals claim was sent into the skies.
Something big is happening, and not knowing what makes it feel all the more dire.
I know little and less of this new legatus─this Nael van Darnus...
What the bloody hells is he up to?
What is this bloody legatus up to?
I know little and less of this new legatus... Who is this Nael van Darnus? And what of Gaius van Baelsar? What the bloody hells is the Empire playing at?
What is this bloody legatus up to?
Those questions will have to wait. For now, I wish to thank you. Arthur would be dead were it not for your efforts.
I have told those at the Adders' Nest of all you have done.

Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna is appealing to the other two nations to stand together. Even so, many within the Twin Adder are moving to ensure they bring as many capable Serpents to their own banner as possible. I'd wager you'll be offered enlistment sooner than late.

I offer only this by way of advice─think well before swearing yourself to a cause, even one that for all appearances is good. I'll not spout any bloody nonsense about following your heart, but you'll know when it feels right.

Why not travel to the other nations and see what it is they have to offer you? I'm sure you'll land on your feet wherever you chance to go. In fact, I'm counting on it. Soon, you adventurers will decide the future of Eorzea, and I, for one, can't wait to see it.
The Order of the Twin Adder has need of every man and woman. Please, find your courage, and serve well.
Things have taken a dreadful turn... Gods, this is all such serious business!
Ah, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], it is you. I trust you were able to attend the address of Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna? Her words and those of the great ones have touched the hearts of all Gridanians.
Word has reached us of the leaders of the Grand Companies of Ul'dah and Limsa Lominsa giving like speeches.
I pray they, too, will serve to unify the people of their nations, that we might fight together against the Garleans.

Our nations must strive to understand one another. To comprehend not only those things we share, but all things, with sympathy and compassion. That is the key to Eorzea's future. Forgive me. We Gridanians are prone to speak so─flowery and full of hope.

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I urge you to travel to the other nations, and hear what the leaders of the Maelstrom and the Immortal Flames have to say. Let your understanding begin there, and then let that guide the decisions you must make.
Bowlord Lewin speaks for us all. Mark well his words.
You've seen the deed done, though no celebrations are in order. Still, you should be proud.
So you are the adventurer. The one to whom the Twin Adder has seen fit to entrust this task.
So you are the one they call [@STRING($EB(1))]. Well met. I am Lewin, Bowlord of the Gods' Quiver.

You will have seen many of my archers hereabouts, as well as lancers of the Wood Wailers, and engineers of the Garlond Ironworks. All have gathered here at the Elder Seedseer's request, to learn what we might of Dalamud.
We have yet to learn why the lesser moon has taken on its red stain. But we have uncovered one truth that may prove vital.
We were led to it by the whispers of the elementals. They tell us that some moons ago, a great destructive force was sent into the skies.

What is the nature of this terrible power? By what means was it sent? By whom, and to what end? When put these questions, the elementals become terrified, and their whispers turn to silence. And so we have taken another path to seek our answers.
Arthur is one of mine own men─as able as any I have. At my bidding, he has stolen into Ala Mhigo, and placed himself amongst the Garleans.
Why? Because this unknown power, this destructive force, whatever it might be...may very well prove to be the Empire's doing.
We have invited the master of the Ironworks himself, Cid Garlond, to aid us in our investigation. There was some risk in this, but we thought it best he hear the reports of Arthur for himself.
Which brings me to the task we would ask of you.
Meet with Arthur in the clearing to the west of Camp Nine Ivies. Such is as close as we dare draw near the Empire's domain, lest we jeopardize all we have worked for─and Arthur's life besides.
Travel there, and secure the area. There may be beasts, or worse things, but this deed must needs be done.
You've done well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You needn't worry about Arthur. He has woken, and even spoke with Cid at some length.
It seems Cid now wishes to have words with you. Best not keep him waiting.

Did you hear the address of Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna? Yes? Then I envy you. Mine own duties held me at the airship landing, seeing to repairs. It wouldn't be so bad, but every man, woman and child who [@1A(1)]did[@1A(0)] attend has been singing her praises ever since.
Master Cid visited Arthur after he woke. He returned not long ago, in fact. I...I confess, I found his expression troubling. I can only wonder what Arthur must have told him...

Come, you are most welcome, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I have heard all you have done in the service of the Twin Adder. You have proven yourself both capable and loyal, and so it is to you that we have turned this day.

We seek a union between Gridania and the Garlond Ironworks. Aye, an unlikely union, I grant you. But it is our very differences that might be made to serve both parties should such an alliance be formed.

The tragedies to which Arthur bore witness have scarred him. A sad fate, but one shared all too often by those who selflessly serve a greater good. Thanks to his sacrifice, all will now know the atrocities visited upon Ala Mhigo by the Garleans, and that is the most important thing of all.

Well met. I am Suzari Sorezari. I have come here in good faith, as an honest man of the Garlond Ironworks, but ever since arriving, I've felt as if I were being watched─[@1A(1)]and not by the people[@1A(0)], if you take my meaning.
Never... Never would I have thought things would come to this.

Ah, I've been awaiting your return, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. We received word that the speeches of General Raubahn Aldynn and Chief Admiral Merlwyb Bloefhiswyn were given. Were you present? Come, tell me all there is to know.

I see... That is good. The people of each nation must be brought together before the nations themselves can unite. I only pray that day comes sooner rather than later. In the meantime, you may rely upon me to apprise the Elder Seedseer of that which you have told me.
I thank you for all you have done, both in Gridania and elsewhere. I trust, though, that your time in the other nations has not...lured you from the path of the Twin Adder.
Recall the words of the great elementals─we must hold to our righteousness and trust to our bravery. So long as we protect our forest, Nophica will never abandon us to the darkness.

And yet...I mark in my fellow Gridanians' eyes the same fear that would take the heart of me. These times see great changes in the Twelveswood, and the red of Dalamud grows deeper with each day's passing.

None can say with certainty what is taking place. We know only that it was when Dalamud's visage first took on its bloody hue that the foulness in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak stirred─a sign most ill.
Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna believes Dalamud to be at the center of all that is happening, and has ordered that thorough studies be made.

The conjurers have taken to the wood, listening for the whispers of the elementals. Men and women of the Wood Wailers, Gods' Quiver, and Garlond Ironworks have begun surveys as well, both within the forest and without.
Ah, but there is more that you must know...yet it is not my place to tell you.
We have dire need of you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─now more than ever. Please, you must visit Stillglade Fane.
Many of the archers, lancers, and engineers have already assembled there. Seek out Bowlord Lewin. He will explain all.
Then go, now. And may the Twelve and the elementals both watch over you.
That is...most unfortunate. Know that our need is real, and pressing. We will welcome you with open arms should you experience a change of heart.
There is more that you must know...but it is not my place to tell you.
Many of the archers, lancers, and engineers have already assembled at Stillglade Fane. Travel there and seek out Bowlord Lewin. He will explain all.

The Order of the Twin Adder welcomes you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You have been asked to come concerning a task of great secrecy. But few among the Wood Wailers and Gods' Quiver have knowledge of what we aim to do.
The rest has done Arthur well. He is himself again. Still, he will never return to Ala Mhigo. Not after this.
The Adders' Nest welcomes you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
By now you will have seen and heard much in each of the nations of Eorzea. Yet I trust you would agree our Gridania is most virtuous among them.
A [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of your talent and resolve belongs with the Twin Adder. Come, tarry no longer in the role of recruit. Let us greet you as a true Serpent of the Order.
But first, there is something you must know.
To pledge yourself to our cause, you must forsake any bonds you have forged with the Maelstrom and the Immortal Flames.
Officially enlisting in the Order of the Twin Adder will delete any recruit status you have with the other Grand Companies.
Duties from the Maelstrom and the Immortal Flames will become unavailable.
You may keep whatever Storm and Flame Seals you have, as they were earned by your own toil. We will not deny you those.
Yet keeping them will yield little benefit. The sutlers in the Hall of Flames and Maelstrom Command will not honor the seals of a sworn Serpent.
Naught will change with regard to your Serpent Seals, of course. You have my word on that.
There is one more thing...
The vows of the Twin Adder are for life. Once made, the bond cannot be unmade, nor will you be able to join the Grand Companies of the other nations.
But believe me when I say that you will have no need of them. The Order of the Twin Adder rewards its leal Serpents, and through service here you will come to know great glories.
Join the Order of the Twin Adder?
Then I greet you as a [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]! The annals of our time shall read that from this day forth, [@STRING($EB(1))] was reborn a Serpent of the Order of the Twin Adder!
The elementals favor you, that much is clear. You will climb our ranks quickly, and your name will one day be spoken throughout the realm. Of that I am sure.

But I speak of things to come. In the here and now, learn what you can from your fellow Serpents. Follow their example, observe and uphold our code, and carry out our tasks to the best of your ability.
Now, I shall teach you the salute of our Order. Come, do as I do.
The Order of the Twin Adder salute can be performed by selecting Serpent Salute from the emote list, or by inputting the /gcsalute text command.

As you are now one of us, you will find our sutlers have more items to offer you. Your Serpent Seals can now buy you the likes of [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,2001005,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,2001005,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], and more.

With a [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,2001005,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,2001005,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], you will be able to pick a chocobo from the stables. It will serve as your mount, to name as you wish.
We have many and more duties for you to choose from. If you'll allow me, I would be more than happy to detail them.

The Order of the Twin Adder is not alone in its use of chocobo caravans. They are essential to the movement of goods across the region. Our birds serve us as well as any man or woman, and so we do not compromise when it comes to their safety. Should you volunteer for caravan security duty, you will be charged with seeing our chocobos safe to their destination, with precious cargo intact.

Surely you now know much and more of the Adventurers' Guild and its guildleves. The Grand Companies have adopted a similar means of delegating tasks, though ours tend more towards direct confrontation with beast and foe.

Supply missions involve the synthesis and delivery of the items required for the Order's operations. We have great need of able crafters. Without the instruments of war, we could wage few battles, and win less.

Provisioning missions involve the procurement and delivery of the raw materials required for the Order's operations. The war effort demands that prodigious amounts of resources be ever ready, of course, but we must needs take care not to tax the forest too heavily.
Very well, then let me speak lastly of our Grand Company currency, the Serpent Seal.

As befits your current rank and station, you are limited to having [@FORMAT([@SHEET(gcRank,11,1)],,)] on your person at any given time. As you perform more duties and distinguish yourself with service, this limit will be raised.
The most rapid way to accomplish this is by ascending the ranks, though bear in mind that a promotion can only be gained after a payment of dues in the form of seals has been made.
The dues vary with rank, of course, but I can say your next promotion will cost you [@FORMAT([@SHEET(gcRank,11,2)],,)] Serpent Seals.
And that, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], is all I have time to tell you. If you would have more, you won't have it from me. I suggest you talk to Lieutenant Sondraix over there.
So go forth, Private [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You are a Serpent now, and the Order of the Twin Adder expects nothing short of greatness from you.
You mean to put in with one of the other nations, then? Weaker [@IF($E9(4),women,men)] than you have succumbed to the siren calls of Ul'dah and Limsa. I only pray that you reconsider.
You mean to put in with one of the other nations, then? Weaker [@IF($E9(4),women,men)] than you have succumbed to the siren calls of Ul'dah and Limsa. I only pray that you reconsider.
Hm? How did you get in? Maelstrom Command is not to open to miscreants, ne'er-do-wells, and the like! To the brig with you, trespasser! Guards! Arrest this [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]!

No...wait. Belay that last order![@CR]Perhaps there is a better way to go about this. You [@1A(1)]did[@1A(0)] manage to find your way here, proving you are both determined and resourceful─two qualities the Admiral is looking for in her recruits.
Very well. I assume you have heard rumors of the Maelstrom upon the lips of Limsa's garrulous citizenry, much of it exaggerated, no doubt.

Let me dispel any misapprehensions you may have regarding the organization by explaining exactly who we are. The Maelstrom is a provisional armada established by Chief Admiral Merlwyb Bloefhiswyn. It is empowered to command not only the existing thalassocratic navy, but public vessels as well, in order to bolster the city[@1F]state's defenses against external aggression.

Now as for recruitment policy, Limsa Lominsa has always been a city[@1F]state that prides itself on the diversity of its citizenry. The thalassocracy was built on this diversity, and therein lies its strength. The Maelstrom will be no different.

Now, if you do not have any questions, I would like to ask of you a favor. Consider it a precursory assessment of your worth to us. Do well, and I can see you having no difficulty earning a place in our ranks once formal admissions have commenced.

There is a certain...rabble-rouser, to put it politely, who has made it his mission to blacken the Admiral's name by writing outrageous articles slandering her character and policies. If allowed to continue, his lies could incite unwanted anger and fear in the public, ultimately weakening the city[@1F]state in critical areas such as defense and trade.

We would have you travel to Wineport and speak with this individual, who is known to go by the name Walcher. Convince him that it is in his [@1A(1)]best interests[@1A(0)] to forbear from writing any more on the Admiral.
Excellent. Now, do not return until you have persuaded the reporter to choose a different subject for his scribblings. How you accomplish this is...well, let us consider that a part of your test.
A [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] who can say “no.” Interesting. There are not many here who can claim that distinction. 'Tis a pity, though. Someone of your character would do well in the Maelstrom.

Walcher is known to frequent Wineport. I suggest starting your search for him there. You need not return until you have persuaded the reporter never to write of the Admiral again. How you accomplish this is...well, let us consider that a part of your test.
Now let me see if I have this straight. You've been sent by the Knights of the Barracuda with an order telling me to desist from any further criticism of the Admiral or her policies?

Hah! I would expect naught less from that tyrant and her host of mindless myrmidons. Well, you can tell her that her idle threats will do little to hide the truth from the eyes of the public. My words are merely a reflection of what lies in the hearts of proud Lominsans across the region.

If anything, the Admiral should be [@1A(1)]thanking[@1A(0)] me for the service I provide. My articles have prompted discourse where before there was none─a means by which Lominsans can release all that they have kept bottled up inside.

Yes, there are those who disapprove of Merlwyb and her lofty ambitions, but for every naysayer who is moved to speak his mind, there is a supporter ready to argue the counterpoint. That being so, what manner of message does stifling the voice of the detractors send, if not one of fear? Fear of the truth behind their words. Silence me if you must...but do so in the knowledge that you will only be strengthening my cause.

Which is not to say, however, that I cannot be swayed from...how shall I put it, taking my articles in a different direction. Everything has its price...my integrity included. With a little persuasion, I might feel moved to abandon my criticism of the Admiral in favor of a different story. One the public is certain to devour.
You being an adventurer, I can assume you've heard of the suspicious character who is oft seen in the aetheryte camps ranting about the Seventh Umbral Era and the end of the world.
Well, I have my own theory about his true identity.

Perhaps you, too, have heard the legend of the Sixth Umbral Era, and how the great deluge that ushered in the dark age was in fact conjured forth by a band of immortal mages who forged a blood pact with the demon lords of the seven hells to deliver a thousand thousand souls in exchange for sole dominion over Eorzea.
I believe that the false prophet Urianger is one of those mages, awoken from fifteen centuries of slumber to complete the fell pact left unfinished so long ago.

Now, if one were to facilitate a meeting between me and this man, the resulting story would take the realm by storm. Better yet, I might not even need to pen an article. There are those who would pay good coin to see this man in chains...

What say you, friend? Help me capture Urianger, and I promise you I shall lay down my quill, just as your Admiral asks. Rumor has it that the mage keeps camp along the coast somewhere to the east of here. I am in no hurry, but I [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] continue my commentary on the thalassocracy in the meantime. Ah hah hah hah hah.
Your Admiral does not think much of her citizens nor their ability to see the world as it truly is. Simply stopping me from reporting the facts will not serve to change them.

But I suspect that the officer who sent you here will not accept that as an answer, which is why I present you with the opportunity to make us all happy. Find me Urianger, and I get my story, your Admiral gets her piece of mind, and you get your reward. I would start my search to the east of here, where the false prophet is said to have made camp.

Well, then─I glean from the sight of you standing here before me that you did not meet an untimely end at the hands of our false prophet. Might it be that you were successful in capturing the preening prognosticator?
He summoned a familiar? Then my sources were correct. This man is much more than he would have us believe.
And you say you spoke with a Miqo'te after dispatching the demon? Hmmm...given the remoteness of the region, it would strain credulity to call this meeting a chance occurrence...
You failed to bring me Urianger, but the information you [@1A(1)]did[@1A(0)] bring me may prove just as valuable. I suppose, then, I should make good on my end of the contract.

Tell your precious Admiral that my days of laying out her sullied smallclothes for all the world to see are officially over. I will be moving on to sweeter-smelling pastures. Here, I have even put it in writing.
You have my word. My future publications will be free of all mention of the Admiral.
Back, are you? Then I can assume your assignment was a success?
No, no, no. I do not want to know how it is you [@1A(1)]convinced[@1A(0)] Walcher to sign this statement, only that it is done, and that we can put this episode behind us.

You have done well, adventurer. The Admiral will be pleased. If you have any interest in serving the city[@1F]state as a member of the Maelstrom, speak with me again. You would be doing Limsa Lominsa a great service.
Interested in joining the Maelstrom, are we?
Even as we speak, similar organizations in Ul'dah and Gridania have cropped up like foul weeds in a newly tilled field.

To prevent eager adventurers such as yourself from being siphoned off into their ranks, Chief Admiral Bloefhiswyn has instructed us to immediately begin a provisional recruitment program which will allow its members to experience all that the Maelstrom has to offer.

We shall even accept those who have already joined another city[@1F]state's company, in the hope that you will ultimately see sense and pledge your allegiance to ours when the time comes...as well as spy on─er, report to us regularly on our neighbors' activities.

Both Gridania and Ul'dah will most certainly attempt to lure you with honey-sweetened words of peace and honor, but the fact remains─neither city[@1F]state has historically had much in the way of success when tested on the fields of battle. Only Limsa Lominsa can claim victories over foreign invaders, pirates, and beast tribes. Only Limsa Lominsa can claim sole dominion over the five seas of Eorzea.

Whereas Gridania and Ul'dah's armies are limited to where their legs can carry them, Limsa Lominsa's forces straddle both land and water. Whereas Gridania is ruled by a litter of untested whelps and Ul'dah by a bickering brood of privileged peacocks, our Admiral actually [@1A(1)]earned[@1A(0)] her seat on the Bridge. So, what say you, adventurer? Take your place in Lominsan legend, or remain an insignificant footnote in the annals of time?
Join the Maelstrom as an interim recruit?

You have made a wise and noble decision─exactly what I would expect of a member of the Maelstrom. Wear the title with pride, knowing that you are now a representative of something greater than anything the realm has seen in fifteen centuries.
Remember, though: your actions will not only speak for you, but for the company, as well. Disgrace yourself, and you disgrace us all.
Which is why, before you step out into the world as the newest bearer of our standard, you will need to make the proper preparations. One way to go about this is with “company seals.”
What are these seals, you ask? Well, you might call them a special type of currency that is earned by completing tasks for the Maelstrom.
They can be used to purchase various items that will aid you in your company-related endeavors─specially crafted items unavailable to Limsa Lominsa's civilian population.

Ah, but that is not all. We provide benefits beyond the mere procurement of items, for not all success can be measured in material gain─a fact to which most battle-hardened warriors will readily attest.

There is, however, one thing you must not forget─the company seals you earn while in the employ of the Maelstrom can only be redeemed here in Limsa Lominsa, so do not think you can make use of them in Gridania or Ul'dah. Likewise, seals earned from the Order of the Twin Adder or the Immortal Flames have no value within these walls.
The amount of Maelstrom company seals (Storm Seals) you have accumulated can be viewed on the Grand Companies tab under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)].
Now, I suppose you are wondering how you might fill your purse with Storm Seals.
Very well. Consider this an incentive to consider remaining with our company for the duration of the coming conflict. No strings attached.
Grizzly Gnat─the good man standing next to me─can instruct you on how you might put the seals you've earned to use.

A footnote it is, then... Unfortunate, for I believe you could have made a name for yourself in our ranks. My offer stays open, however. Have a change of heart, and you may come back here at any time.
Join the Maelstrom as an interim recruit?
Congratulations, recruit, and welcome to the Maelstrom. I am Storm Sergeant First Class Grizzly Gnat, in charge of company seal distribution and exchange.
The first lieutenant has asked me to brief you on the various items we have made available for purchase. Shall I proceed?
Learn more about available items?

Every item available for exchange has been fashioned here in Limsa Lominsa by skilled craftsmen adhering to the strictest of quality standards. As you are still a recruit, I cannot grant you access to our full inventory. I can, however, show you a few options.
The remainder will be revealed to you only upon your official enlistment into the Maelstrom.

In addition to items, company seals can also be exchanged for promotions within our ranks. As you increase in rank, missions of greater import will be assigned to you. It goes without saying that said missions will carry considerably more risk.
And now I suppose you are wondering how one might achieve official enlistment.
Well, as the first lieutenant is sure to have implied, you must first prove your loyalty to our cause before a promotion shall be considered.
As a newly inducted recruit, you still have a long road ahead of you. That, however, does not mean that the journey will be impossible.
Continue to perform tasks for the Maelstrom, and you will gradually earn the company seals required for official enlistment.

As for the present, might I suggest you exchange the seals you just earned for this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3020202,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,3020202,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]? I can see it being of great use to you on your first mission as a Maelstrom member.
Learn more about available items?
Then I cannot help you.
Learn more about available items?

It must have been a wearisome journey from Limsa Lominsa to Millers' Glade. I trust you did not encounter any trouble on the road? I, too, have traveled many malms to be here, yet I am in the privileged position of having an airship at my disposal. I cannot begin to imagine how you adventurers endure all the walking.
Of late, our leader has nearly all of us at the Ironworks out in the field taking readings of soil, rock, air, aether...which is odd, for I am a specialist in the field of imperial weaponry...
I suppose he has his reasons, and I am not one to question his wisdom, but I would feel much more in my element were I sitting at a desk poring over design schematics.
I see you have had more than your fill of rules and regulations, and are ready to prove your worth to the Maelstrom. Good, because I have just the mission to help you do precisely that.

The frequency of Garlean attacks on Vylbrand has been increasing by the day. The Empire appears to have adopted a multi-pronged approach, striking the region's outlying areas in precisely timed waves in an attempt to overwhelm our defenses and force us to fall back to the coastline.

So far, our lines have held, but we are not foolish enough to imagine that the Empire is using even a fraction of its firepower. No, the Admiral believes that this is merely a single element of a much larger plan already in motion, and that their true objective lies in upper La Noscea, near the volcano, O'Ghomoro.

According to intelligence gathered by a reconnaissance party dispatched to the area, the kobolds have recently completed the construction of a pair of new encampments. No sooner had the final stakes been hammered in, however, than the Empire launched a coordinated assault on both locations.

Normally, Limsa Lominsa would welcome attacks on the filthy beastmen, but this time things are different. If the Empire were to take control of the kobold encampments, it would give them a solid foothold in the region. With the impenetrable O'Ghomoro at their back, and the camps' commanding elevation, we would be at a grave disadvantage should we choose to mount an offensive.
In short, once that foothold is established, there will be nothing to stop them from setting their sights on Limsa Lominsa...

To prevent the Garleans from ever making it that far, the Admiral has already ordered a party of elite warriors to engage the imperial troops en route to the kobold encampment. They will work quickly and efficiently, but there is always the chance that some of the targets will escape. That is where you come in. We would have you journey to upper La Noscea via a narrow canyon linking the highlands to eastern La Noscea, and wait there in ambush. If you encounter any imperial soldiers attempting to traverse the canyon, you are to slay them.
Well said. Your enthusiasm will prove a fine example for the other recruits.

Now take care in making the proper preparations for this mission. The imperial soldiers will be well equipped and may outnumber you. Fortunately, they are also like to be fatigued from their flight, [@1A(1)]and[@1A(0)] you will have the element of surprise to your advantage. Good luck, and may the Navigator guide you to victory.

How quickly the enthusiasm drains from a young adventurer when danger looms. I cannot force you to accept this mission any more than I can force you to give your life for a greater good─but I do [@1A(1)]strongly[@1A(0)] suggest you reconsider. We can only overcome the Empire if we stand together.
So you're the Maelstrom's messenger [@IF($E9(4),girl,boy)]. Small world, ain't it?
You the one the Maelstrom sent to deliver the magitek transceiver? Well met. I'm Nymiene of the Garlond Ironworks.

The forge has us out here surveyin' the landscape for a future assignment. What it is, I ain't at liberty to say, mind you. But what I [@1A(1)]can[@1A(0)] tell you is that the readin's are most definitely disturbin'.

What does it all mean? Buggered if I know. I just write down the numbers. The chief back at the forge does all the brain work. My own personal opinion, though, is that it ain't all sunsets and sweetmeats, if you get my meanin'.
Somethin' sinister's loomin' on the horizon, and I'm not sure I want to be anywhere near this place when it rears its ugly mug.

The Empire cannot be allowed to gain a foothold in the region. To see that they do not, the Maelstrom has dispatched a party of our best men and women to engage the Garleans before they invade and occupy the kobold encampments in upper La Noscea.

The party will handle the bulk of the fighting, but there will doubtless be some who fly the killing field and attempt to fall back to the imperial landing points along the eastern La Noscean coastline. You are to travel to the narrow canyon connecting upper and eastern La Noscea, near the kobold encampment, and wait in ambush for any retreating troops.

As I said before, the imperial soldiers will be well equipped and may outnumber you, but they are like to be fatigued from their flight. Be sure to use this and the element of surprise to your advantage. You have your orders, recruit. Good luck, and may the Navigator guide you to victory.

Early reports state that you saw some action in the canyon. Well done, recruit. Your bravery has seen our realm secure for another day. The Empire will think twice before attempting to set foot in that area again.
Hm? You say you found something of interest on one of the imperials you slew? Let me see that.

Why...this is a magitek transceiver...and it is intact! The Empire uses these metal boxes to communicate with each other, much like we do with linkpearls. Little else is known of them, however, the reason being that they are designed to explode when taken too far from their owners. This one must be defective... At any rate, I must inform the Garlond Ironworks immediately!

The Ironworks contact I spoke with expressed a profound interest in the transceiver. He believes that they may be able to use it in deciphering the code the Empire employs in all of their communications.

Unfortunately, the engineer in charge of linguistic research has just left the city[@1F]state to attend to pressing matters, and there are no others here with the requisite skill in cryptology. Under normal circumstances, we would wait until his return to present him with the transceiver; however, our circumstances are anything but normal.

Your next assignment is to deliver this imperial machina to Ebrelnaux in the Coerthas eastern lowlands. He is said to be conducting his current experiments at a windmill in a small settlement called Millers' Glade on the shores of Briar Lake.
But take care. The Empire is bound to know that one of their transceivers is missing, and they will be intent on recovering it.

There are few in Eorzea who have ever seen the inner workings of the Empire's machina, and of those few, only the engineers of Garlond Ironworks are privy to the knowledge of how to manipulate them. It is said that the company's leader stole that knowledge from the great Garlean library in the imperial capital. Ebrelnaux is his right-hand man.
Take the magitek transceiver you found to Ebrelnaux so he may begin his deciphering of the Garlean code.
He is thought to be conducting experiments at a windmill in Millers' Glade, a small settlement in the eastern lowlands of Coerthas, far to the northeast, on the continent of Aldenard.
A messenger sent on behalf of the Maelstrom? Well, well, aren't we far from home?
My fellow colleagues in Limsa Lominsa have already informed me of the task you were sent to complete. They say you come bearing gifts.

...A magitek transceiver! Do you know how long we have tried to obtain one of these? Years! [@1A(1)]Hundreds[@1A(0)] of covert missions into imperial territory, raids on Garlean camps, kidnappings and assassinations─all of them foiled by a failsafe device designed to deny access to the Empire's secrets. And then, quite by chance, an adventurer-for-hire stumbles across one on a mission to ambush imperial deserters!? Dear me.

Oh, I did not mean to belittle your efforts, but you must forgive me if I seem a little miffed by our own ill fortune. Ill fortune until now, that is. I shall begin deciphering the imperial code immediately and will inform the Admiral upon completion.

I was wondering when you would arrive, recruit. The Garlond Ironworks have already sent a report on their findings and the Admiral is busy using that information to orchestrate the thalassocracy's next move.

By deciphering a series of encoded exchanges between imperial operatives, we have learned that the Empire has begun establishing temporary bases of operation in two abandoned underground complexes known as the Dzemael Darkhold and the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak─located in Coerthas and the Black Shroud, respectively.

We have also confirmed what we already knew─that the multi-pronged assault on several areas around La Noscea was nothing but a feint, conducted to divert our attention away from the Empire's true objective─the establishment of a fortified stronghold within thalassocratic borders.

Luckily─for the time being, at least─the kobolds' cunning has proven to be a match for the Garleans' machina, and they have yet to give a single ilm of ground. As long as the beast tribe continues to resist the Empire, we will refrain from any interference. As I believe the saying goes: “The enemy of one's enemy can oft be a friend.”

You have done well, recruit, though I find it troubling that you insist on maintaining your allegiances with...other parties. The talents you possess would be wasted in the ranks of those preening fools. I ask you, under whose flag do you want to be standing when the Empire is toppled and it falls to the thalassocratic navy to guide Eorzea into a new era?

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: You have come on a most glorious day, recruit. A ceremony to officially inaugurate the Maelstrom armada is scheduled to take place [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),later this evening,later today)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),this evening,later this evening)])], and is to be conducted by none other than the Admiral herself.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: There is, however, one small problem. You see, the Admiral is...well...she is...how would you say...[@1A(1)]in absentia[@1A(0)]. Alright, she's missing. She left the city several bells past, saying that she needed to meet with representatives of Limsa's most prestigious pirate crews in order to settle the remaining details of their peace accord.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: So as not to betray their trust, she insisted on traveling to the meeting place unarmed and, ahem, without escort... This, unfortunately, has left us all in the dark as to her safety.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Worse, we cannot dispatch a party of Barracuda Knights to search for her for fear of inviting the ire of the pirates and thereby undermining all that the Admiral has worked so hard to achieve. No, our only option is to send a suitably inconspicuous third party in our stead. A third party who would rouse little suspicion if spotted... A third party, in point of fact, like you. What better disguise than a common adventurer chasing chigoes on some levequest or other?

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: The Admiral's attendants overheard her mention a clearing southwest of Camp Bloodshore. We believe it to be the location of the moot. Would you consent to go there on our behalf?

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: You have my thanks, recruit. Now, I must ask that you work quickly. The longer the Admiral is away from the city, the greater the chance her absence will be noted, and the likelier it is that one of the more ambitious pirate crews will endeavor to turn the situation to their advantage.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Have you no sense of loyalty? No ambition? I thought you forged of sterner stuff. Perhaps I was mistaken...

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: It is believed the Admiral left, unarmed and unattended, for a clearing to the southwest of Camp Bloodshore. You are to travel to the clearing and confirm her whereabouts and well-being.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Halt. Come not a step closer till you have made yourself known.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Guincum sent you, did he? Well, you may report to the overstrung officer that he should put away his timeworn tenterhooks─his beloved Admiral is quite unscathed. Well, her person is, at least─her wits have been dealt something of a blow. I came here to trade words with the Archon, you see, but learned rather more than I had hoped to know...

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: <sigh> And now I suppose courtesy dictates I explain myself. My advisors would most certainly advise against it, of course...but they are not here, and I rarely heed their cautioning cries when they are. So then, I have heard the whisperings concerning the Archon and know that there are many who would brand him an enemy of the realm. I, for my part, would not have you believe that I was conspiring with a criminal, and spread rumors to that effect, as is doubtless your wont.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: No, you shall have it plain. Let it be seeds of truth and not hearsay that you scatter amongst those who still harbor doubts as to my intentions.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: First, a confession: it was not I who devised the plan to re-establish the Maelstrom. That I owe to Urianger─to the Archons. Had I made this fact known in the beginning, few would have credited it, and those who did would have demanded my resignation, or─in the case of the pirates─my head.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Hence the secrecy, and hence my traveling here alone...though little good that did. I caught wind of a band of overly inquisitive ruffians tracking me on my way to this clearing. I did my best to cover my trail in hopes that I would have enough time to conduct my business with Urianger and void the area before they arrived.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: What's this? You met with the band upon the road and summarily slew the brigands? ...Well, you adventurers are seldom afraid to take the initiative. Would that the Maelstrom had more [@IF($E9(4),women,men)] like you.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: You have served the thalassocracy well today. As a token of my gratitude, I invite you to join me at the Grand Company inauguration ceremony.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: The ceremony was to be held on the Bridge later this evening, but it appears my little outing has taken rather longer than anticipated... I [@1A(1)]would[@1A(0)] warn you that proceedings are like to be delayed, but I have little doubt that you will arrive at precisely the right moment in any event─you adventurers being uncannily gifted where timing is concerned.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: I will inform the guard Zanthael that you are to be allowed access to the Bridge via the lift on the bottommost level of the Mizzenmast. Until then, I ask that you keep the details of our conversation a secret.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: The Twelve have willed that our paths cross once more, and for this I give thanks.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: For that which came to pass when last we met, I do beg thy pardon. Though I called upon my familiar, I swear I meant thee no lasting hurt.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Upon these once taintless shores lurk Garlean devils, dizened in darkness─their object, to bestrew venomous falsehoods anent my person and purpose.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: They claim me one of a cabal of malign mages whom erst summoned forth a terrible doom unto Eorzea. They covet my knowledge of the Seventh Moon, deeming it a threat to peace, and have ventured so far as to call for my death, luring would-be abettors with the luster of false riches.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: I have pled mine innocence to them that would hear it, but what is one voice of truth amidst a chorus of calumnies? So, that my message might be delivered, I was compelled to brave a less trodden path. I had need of them that could discern good from evil, though each be clad in the cloth of the other.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: And it was with this in mind that I did test thee, knowing that when thou hadst overcome adversity, thou wouldst awaken anew to the light of truth.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: From thy feats that day, I know I have found one of them I seek. Thou art blessed with the fortitude to endure the blight that will descend upon Eorzea anon. Aye, thou shalt prove a boon in the battle to come, and any of the Grand Companies of Eorzea would be fortunate to count thee in their number.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Yet...though thou hast hitherto endured much, thou must needs apprehend all this as but the beginning. The fate of the realm rests upon thy shoulders and the shoulders of thy compeers. Shirk not this burden, for if thou dost, Eorzea will perish ere the first flame falleth from the heavens.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: I have traveled far this day. Permit me a moment's respite, I prithee, that I might rest my weary bones before betaking me to my journey once more.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Offer her body and blood to the Navigator, indeed? I suppose that [@1A(1)]might[@1A(0)] stir the drowsy deity from her hitherto ceaseless slumber...but I suspect her sacrifice would benefit Limsa's carrion crabs rather more than her people.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: And we could not have that, for I fear the mighty Maelstrom would fare rather poorly without Merlwyb at its helm. There is no other in this city with a voice as resounding as hers.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Now, I had an opportunity to exchange pleasantries with the Admiral before the day's display of pomp and circumstance. She spoke highly of you, commending your courage and cunning; even going so far as asking me to present you with that token of her appreciation. Indeed, it seems both she [@1A(1)]and[@1A(0)] Urianger have fallen for your charms.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Yes, I know of the Archon, for he and I are colleagues, sent from a land far to the north to study what some call the “Divine Chronicles.”

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: You seem...unconvinced. Mayhap you recall our rather timely meeting in eastern La Noscea? Well, it just so happens that I traveled there that day in order to discuss how best to persuade the Admiral to reinstate the Maelstrom. Can you guess with whom I spoke?

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: And here we are. Would that I could say things are all well and good, but as you can imagine, they are far from it.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Based on the information that my brothers and I have gathered, it would seem the Garlean Empire has chosen to tread the same vainglorious path that other civilizations trod in ages past─a course which may succinctly be described as the shortest road to ruin.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: But all is not yet lost. Sensing the gravity of the situation, our master─the Allseer─has arrived to begin his search for Daybreak─one of the valliant blades mentioned in the Divine Chronicles.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: So you see, though we are beset on all sides by death, there is still hope. Hope in Merlwyb, hope in the Maelstrom, and hope in those who follow them.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: And then there is you. In the coming moons, you shall face a despair darker than any you have ever known. But the light of hope burns bright in your soul─a light which none may quench save you yourself.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: You have come to the end of one journey, but a new one awaits. A journey to pass that light on to others, so that they, too, may carry on when the hammer of judgment falls.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: You must let that flame guide you to the furthest reaches of Eorzea─to the burning sands of Ul'dah and the dewy groves of Gridania.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Heed the words of the maiden who speaks with the trees, embrace the resolve of the warrior who stands alone against many, and let each add to your flame.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: A path must be chosen, a decision made. Open your mind and your senses to all that is around you, and answers will come. My companions await you.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Now go, but forget not that of which I spake. Hope is what you are, and [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] are what we seek.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Me cap'n always says we be free to do as we please. 'Tis the way o' the pirates, he says, and always has been. I'm wonderin', though...does that makes us free to join the Admiral?

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: That bloody saltwife's stubborn as a sea lion, and twice as ugly...but her love o' Limsa runs deeper than the abyss itself, and there ain't many as can say that.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: When Merlwyb failed to appear in time for the originally scheduled ceremony, I immediately assumed the worst. This [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] Limsa Lominsa, you know. We've had more than a few Admirals turn up in the gutter over the years, whether drink-sodden...or dead.

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: What a speech! Never have I been more inspired in all my years as a Knight of the Barracuda! I'm more than ready to play my part!

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Even if it [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] cleaning up after the ceremony... <sigh>

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: [@STRING($EB(1))]? The Admiral has informed me of your arrival. Do you wish to proceed to the Bridge?

quest_names: An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: Access the lift?

An Officer and a Wise Man
text_en: You [@1A(1)]are[@1A(0)] aware this is the only means of access to the Bridge, are you not? The Crow's Lift will take you no further than the airship landing.
