Assemble a party of [@IF($E5(2,0),[@IF($E2(2,10),[@SWITCH(2,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(2)])],[@VALUE(2)])] to [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] members and then you can enter as you please.

If you're hells-bent on chasing after your friends, I'll not stop you. But neither will I give you leave to enter the Maws alone. Assemble a party of [@IF($E5(2,0),[@IF($E2(2,10),[@SWITCH(2,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(2)])],[@VALUE(2)])] to [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] members and then you can enter as you please.

Only parties consisting of between [@IF($E5(2,0),[@IF($E2(2,10),[@SWITCH(2,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(2)])],[@VALUE(2)])] and [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE($E8(4))] or above will be granted entry to the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak.
'Course, you'd best make sure they actually entered the Maws before you go in after them. The guards stationed at the dungeon entrance will know.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], is it? We had word from Nuala you would be coming. You mean to find the Ul'dahns who came ahead of you, yes?
Neither I nor Nuala granted them leave to enter the Maws. After I refused their demands, they sunk so low as to attempt a bribe, but Gridanian honor cannot be bought─least of all with Ul'dahn gil.

The Maws are a labyrinth of twisting tunnels and shafts, and break the surface in more places than one. Our eyes cannot be everywhere at once. It is possible they found another way in. It would not be the first time, nor the last, I venture.
There is even talk of moogles leading folk to secret entrances, though what possesses the furry little bastards is a mystery to me.

Whatever came of the Ul'dahns, I can't bloody well say if they are even in the Maws. You seem confident that they are. It might be you are privy to some knowledge I am not. But I don't much care in any event. You'll have to brave the Maws yourself if you wish to search for them.
The beasts within are in a frenzy the likes of which we've never seen in the Twelveswood. I will not refuse you entry, but I must insist on certain conditions.
Once you set foot in the Maws, I cannot permit you to re-enter until your body has had time to rid itself of the noxious residues of woodsin and aether which permeate the place.

After completing an expedition in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak, you will not be allowed to return immediately to the dungeon. To confirm how long you must wait before re-entering, view the Timers tab located under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)].

As another measure to prevent the untimely loss of life to the beasts lurking below, I shall be performing a special incantation prepared by the Conjurers' Guild to draw you and your party out of the dungeon after a set amount of time has passed.
You can remain in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak for a maximum of [@VALUE($E8(2))] minutes (Earth time) per visit.
In addition to my spell, you may leave at any time by returning to the entrance on foot.

There are also rumors of an imperial magitek device located in the farthest reaches of the dungeon. It is said the infernal machine can instantly return a man to this spot, but I am not sure I would trust anything constructed by the Empire. Who knows what sort of havoc the contraption might play on one's humours.

Finally, if you find yourself knocked unconscious by one of the creatures, our scouts have confirmed that using a Return spell will transport you back to the dungeon's entrance, so you may continue your mission, if you so wish.
All items in a player's loot list will automatically be transferred to that player's inventory upon leaving the dungeon. Items unable to be obtained will be lost.

That is all I can tell you for now. The truth is that we, too, are not fully apprised of the situation─including the role of the moogles in all this. We will provide you with what support we can, but you'd be wise not to let your guard down once inside.
Go and make what preparations you must. Speak to me again when you wish to enter.
It seems you are as ready as you will ever be. Very well. Enter now, and may the Twelve watch over you.
Enter the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak?
It is an admirable thing, wishing to help one's brethren. But if you are unsure of your mettle, perhaps it is best you not enter.
Enter the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak?
Goodness gracious me! You look almost exactly like an adventurer I once met, adventurer. I wonder, kupo...can you understand me? Are you hearing more than just incomprehensible kupo noises right now?
You are an adventurer, yes? I wonder, kupo...can you understand me? Are you hearing more than just incomprehensible kupo noises right now?
You are looking for your friends? How touching! You adventurers are all best friends forever, kupo!
Oooh, maybe this belongs to one of your friends, kupo? I found it deep, deep in the dungeon. But you mustn't go there! I saw Garleans! Garleans and more Garleans!
Your friends... I think perhaps they are... Well, they're dead, kupo.

I don't know what happened. One moment we were dancing in our flower fields, and the next we were here. That's when I noticed your friends, kupo. They must have seen the hidden entrance we used in the forest and followed us!

Anyway, it was then that I heard a strange voice, kupo. It sent a shiver right down my spine. Not long after that, we found this contraption here. Your friends started poking and picking at it, kupo. Maybe it was this strange device that brought us here... That called to us...
I pulled this bit off it, but now I've got a very, very bad feeling, kupo. Here, please take it far away from here. Far, far away!
Now, I'll just have a little nap and then be on my way. No need to worry about me, kupo.
I'll just have a little nap and be on my way. No need to worry about me, kupo. I'm feeling a bit better now, thanks to A[@1F]Ruhn.
He saved us! A[@1F]Ruhn saved us!
It was the voice. We couldn't resist it, kupo! A[@1F]Ruhn told us it was the crystals crying out.
Just what is this horrible contraption doing to the crystals?
So you have escaped the Maws with your life─no small feat, that. Tell me, what did you discover within?
I see... At the hands of imperials, you say? I am sorry. That is...most tragic.
Garleans... I see. And your missing friends? Ah. It is as I feared. I am sorry for Ul'dah's loss.

But their death was not in vain. Both they and you have learned much of great value. This magitek device that appears to be of Garlean making, and its influence over the moogles... But what is the connection?

We must carry out further investigations if we are to understand all of this. Until we do, I must ask that you not let word of this spread to the masses. We cannot afford the panic. I will send word to Nuala myself.

There is much to consider. The power of this mysterious voice, for example. For it to summon beasts is one thing─but moogles? And this magitek device...if it is indeed of Garlean making... What does it all mean? We must investigate further.

I will see that Nuala is informed of everything. I ask that you refrain from speaking of this to any of my countrymen. We must not let unconfirmed information disseminate amongst the people. That will only lead to panic.
On behalf of Gridania, I thank you. The information you have provided may prove crucial to understanding the Empire's plans for my nation, and Ul'dah as well.

I will see that Nuala is informed of everything that has happened. I ask that you refrain from speaking of this to any of my countrymen. We must not let unconfirmed information disseminate amongst the people. That will only lead to panic.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! It is good to see you in the Hall of Flames once more. Tell me, were you able to find our soldiers?
This bracer belongs to... No. Dead? All of them? But they were some of our most battle-hardened warriors! What evil could have done such a thing?
Garleans!?
Limsa Lominsa, too, must be informed of this. The three nations must devise a strategy together.

I would not have thought the Gridanians capable of concealing information of such import. And now it has cost us the lives of many good men. Had we known, we may have pursued another course of action.
We will keep this bracer, in memory of our fallen. At least you have returned to us with your life. Thank the gods for that.

As for this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000262,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000262,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], you claim it to be part of a magitek device placed within the Maws by the Garleans? If so, then we must see it to the engineers of the Garlond Ironworks for inspection.
This bodes ill...all of it. Hordes of feral beasts, Garlean soldiers, a strange voice that unmans even moogles... Just what in the bloody hells is going on in that damnable dungeon!?

The Immortal Flames will not stand idly by. This is a time for action. And to act we must have information─such as the kind you have brought us this day. You have done well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and shall be rewarded.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], again you honor us with your visit. And again I have a task for you.

Many years ago, the Ishgardians undertook to build a mountain fortress in the central highlands of Coerthas. They called it the Dzemael Darkhold. Regretfully, we have learned that it has fallen under Garlean control.
As if that were not troubling enough, our scouts report seeing a high-ranking officer amongst the imperial forces stationed there─a man we believe to be the Legatus of the VIIth Legion.
In case you are unaware, the hold takes its name from House Dzemael, one of the four high houses of Ishgard. It was they who were responsible for its construction and subsequent defense...

Clearly, they were no match for the might of the Empire. But then who alone could claim to be? Perhaps it was this realization that drove them to put away their pride and take up arms with the other high houses. Together, they were able to retake the Darkhold's main gate.

But the structure is vast, and built around naturally occurring caves and tunnels. There are not men enough to secure all points of entry. And so another of the high houses, House Fortemps, has appealed to the knights of Ishgard's outer regions to join the fight.
Those come from the city are at Owl's Nest in the eastern lowlands of Coerthas. From there, they have sent messengers into the high mountains to deliver the call to arms.

When the call is answered, the army of House Fortemps will be flooded with unknown faces. Think of it─none will contest the presence of complete strangers. If ever there were a time to plant a spy to the north, that time is [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)]! We must learn what we can of the Darkhold, and of Garlean operations in the area.

The Flames would send you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Travel to Ishgard and take part in the attempt to reclaim Dzemael Darkhold. The commanding officer of House Fortemps's army is Ser Artoirel. You will first need to present yourself to him for duty.

Excellent. Then head north until you are among the knights, and look for the unicorn─the sigil of House Fortemps. Seek out this Ser Artoirel, and present him with this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000265,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000265,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].

For years now, Ishgard's gates have been closed to outsiders. Never have we seen such an opportunity to place one of our own in their midst, and we do not intend to let it pass by. If you will not serve us, we will find another who will.
Travel to Ishgard and take part in the attempt to reclaim Dzemael Darkhold. Learn whatever you can of what lies within, and of the Garleans who have seized control.

Knights of House Fortemps have been dispatched to Owl's Nest. Travel there and deliver this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000265,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000265,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] to Ser Artoirel, their commanding officer.
You seek Ser Artoirel? On what business?

So you bear a [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000265,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000265,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. Are you the [@IF($E9(4),daughter,son)] of a swineherd, then? <sigh> It would seem our desperation knows no bounds. Well met, country bumpkin. You have the honor of speaking to Ser Vairemont of House Fortemps.
I cannot present you to Ser Artoirel because he is not here. He has ridden for the front with the main body of our force.
He departed the instant we received word that Nael van Darnus, Legatus of the VIIth Legion, had been sighted amongst the Garleans' ranks.

If you wish to distinguish yourself with service, hurry to the Darkhold in the central highlands. Show that [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000265,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000265,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] of yours to the knights at the main gate. They will grant you entry.

But know this─the latest reports show that it is not only Garleans infesting the Darkhold. There are all manner of beasts and monsters roaming those halls, as well. The kind that take bumpkin sers for tasty morsels, hahaha!

The guard will not grant you entry should you go alone, so gather a party of between [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] and [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] members. That should not prove difficult, especially for the [@IF($E9(4),daughter,son)] of a [@1A(1)]swineherd[@1A(0)]. Ahahaha!

Ahem. Storm the Darkhold with your brethren, and put down whatever imperials you encounter within. Return with proof of their demise, and you shall be generously rewarded─with more than you're like to see in a lifetime in Norwick, I should imagine.

To enter the Dzemael Darkhold, you must be in a party consisting of between [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE($E8(4))] or higher.

The sigil of a Norwick knight. House Fortemps welcomes you. Ser Artoirel and his force have stormed the Darkhold in pursuit of Nael van Darnus. The last reports we received were grim, however. An enemy pincer action had seen our men surrounded, and they were able neither to press forward nor retreat.

We had heard that Nael van Darnus was a cunning leader in battle, and a gifted tactician. Should you find him, I warn you not to confront him directly. Such recklessness will only serve to make the Darkhold your tomb.

If you truly value your life, then listen carefully to my words. The depths of the Darkhold are said to contain a rift through which the creatures of the void gain entrance to this realm. And they are not all that passes through.

Foul miasmas seep into the caverns, clogging the lungs and poisoning the minds of any who linger too long. Those who have entered the hold are therefore advised to wait for a period of several suns to allow the taint to quit the body before attempting another foray.

After completing an expedition in the Dzemael Darkhold, you will not be permitted to return to the area immediately. To confirm how long you must wait before re-entering, view the Timers tab located under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)].

To ensure that the noisome mists are not allowed the opportunity to tighten their grip, I shall be casting a spell upon you that will teleport you back here to my side after the passing of several bells.
You can remain in the Dzemael Darkhold for a maximum of [@VALUE($E8(2))] minutes (Earth time) per visit.
In addition to the spell, you may leave the Darkhold at your leisure by returning to the entrance on foot.

Previous expedition parties reported finding what they called a magitek terminal deep in the farthest reaches of the lower chambers. It is said the device can instantly return a man to this spot, but I have found it best to take such tales with a grain of salt.

Oh, and should you come to grief down there, former visitors have confirmed that using a Return spell will transport you back to the Darkhold's entrance, so you may continue your mission, if you so wish.
All items in a player's loot list will automatically be transferred to that player's inventory upon leaving the dungeon. Items unable to be obtained will be lost.
And that is all the information I can give you. If I may offer an opinion, though─this is an evil place, forsaken by the Twelve and embraced by devils. Leave while you still can, and don't look back.
But seeing as you will not, the least I can do is offer you one last opportunity to make your final preparations. Speak to me once more when you are ready.
I see you could not be swayed. Very well.
Enter the Dzemael Darkhold?
Time is of the essence. Make whatever preparations you must, but do it quickly!
Enter the Dzemael Darkhold?
Your deeds have brought great honor to House Fortemps. Go now, Vairemont awaits your report at Owl's Nest.
It seems I underestimated you. Your bravery in the Darkhold brought many of our men back alive. Ser Artoirel himself saw fit to praise your deeds.
Still, Nael van Darnus escaped us. It seems the Legatus is as crafty when retreating as he is when attacking.

Hm? This helmet... This is [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000266,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000266,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]! The helm of a legatus! Its design is unmistakable. But that would mean...
Y-You... Twelve be good, could it be? You've slayed Nael van Darnus!

...Is no doubt what you wanted to hear. Am I not right, Ser Bumpkin? The truth of it is that scores of men have brought me countless of these false helms upon their return from the Darkhold. So many, in fact, that I am heartily sick of seeing them!

You fools from the country have much to learn. The Garleans often employ this tactic. The corpse you prized this helm from was but one of many decoys─men clad to resemble the Legatus in order to protect him. A crowd for that craven to cower behind.

Ser Artoirel, too, was vexed by this. He pursued van Darnus and his men into the Darkhold, only to be flanked by another force led by another van Darnus! Gods know how many doppelgangers the bastard has!
Decoys, the whole bloody lot! And we ran headlong into their trap, as the fox after the hen! Van Darnus has made fools of us all!

We have spies who have infiltrated the Empire. From their reports, we know that the Legatus is a man of great intellect, but also great cruelty and savagery. We know that he is feared among the Garleans. And yet we do not even know if he was among those we pursued into the Darkhold.

It may well be that van Darnus was simply toying with us, laughing all the while from behind the safety of Garlean lines. Yet the knights of Ishgard do not make excuses. We were bested this time around.

But we will not let ourselves be fooled again. Not by the likes of van Darnus, nor by the likes of you. Aye, Ser Bumpkin, your lies have been exposed. Another among our ranks hails from Norwick. After hearing you in passing, he claims you do not speak the region's dialect.

If it were left to me, I'd have you chained to a stone in the mountains as dragon bait. But none can deny the merit of your deeds in the Darkhold. Whatever lies you've told, you saved the lives of many of our men. It is for Ser Artoirel to decide your fate, anyway, and he has ordered you be set free. Now be gone from my sight, false knight.

I take it the deed is done? You see, we received a parcel not long ago, addressed to you care of the Flames. It contained a gold nugget and a note complimenting your incomparable valor and distinguished service...marked with no less than the seal of House Fortemps.

Traveling from one end of Eorzea to the other and speaking with the same accent... You must have taken leave of your bloody senses! Did you honestly think you wouldn't be discovered!? Lucky for you, your deeds spoke louder than your distinctly unconvincing words. Ser Artoirel has ordered that your crime of impersonating a knight of Ishgard be pardoned.

And lucky for us, as well. This could easily have ignited tensions between our nations. A narrow escape, indeed. Oh, I should probably mention that we've taken the liberty of exchanging your nugget for Flame Seals. Now, tell me all that you have learned.

Then it is just as we thought. The Garleans have deployed a magitek device within the Darkhold, yes, but what we must ask is why [@1A(1)]there[@1A(0)]? Of all the places in all the realm, why did they choose [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] precise location?

It seems to me now that the answer lies with the crystals. Dzemael Darkhold lies atop lands once prized by all the nations for their high crystal content and mining potential. The Empire must covet them for the same reasons.
Yet I cannot fathom why they should... Ceruleum is the fuel needed to drive their magitek. To what end would they crave crystals?
And if our reports are to be believed, the Legatus of the XIVth Legion has now been seen at the Darkhold as well. It appears the Empire has no intentions of losing control of it.

We will have to continue our investigations at the Darkhold to determine precisely what it is the Garleans are after. No doubt we will call on you again, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. For now, though, your duty is fulfilled. Well done.

Being a chef on a ship can truly dampen one's spirits... Why, a few big waves and half the food you serve reappears on the deck. One of these days, I hope to invent a dish so delicious, it will taste better going down the second time.
Out of the way, scullion! Popoto peeler extraordinaire, Aentfoet Tuberbane coming through!
O Byregot, mighty maker of all things good, see me safe through the blazing inferno of the ovens, and guide my hand to those ingredients most fresh, that I, too, might make as Thou dost.
The more I stand over the flames of these ovens, the more my stomach cries out to me in agony, “Why dost thou torment me so!? But one bite, I prithee! That is all I ask!”

I never wanted to be a chef... I wanted to be a pirate! But my mother and father would have none of it─insisted I took up a [@1A(1)]proper[@1A(0)] trade. The fact they made me do it here, in a city [@1A(1)]full[@1A(0)] of pirates, just rubs salt, pepper, and sundry bloody spices in the wound!
Just because you are clueless does not mean you have to look it. The last thing we need is for our clientele to suppose that the rabble has invaded our ranks.
Now run along to our two top chefs, Pulmia and Prudentia, and listen closely to the knowledge they provide. They are just over there.
Ahhh, I see you have chosen to lend your hand to [@IF($E1($E8(1),0),Prudentia,Pulmia)]'s noble cause. I do hope you remembered to write down the recipe...

Oh, I know, I know. It may not seem like the culinary challenge you were seeking when you first entered the guild, but a master chef is not made in a day. It takes many suns and many moons of boiling, seasoning, curing... Mmm... All this talk about food has made me hungry. Now off with you! You do not want to keep [@IF($E1($E8(1),0),Prudentia,Pulmia)] waiting!

You have a keen eye for talent if you chose to assist me over Pulmia! Here, I need you to whip me up [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000069,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000069,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].
Lend Prudentia a hand?
Haha! Here's the recipe! Chop-chop, now!
Refusing aid to a damsel in distress!? And you call yourself an adventurer!
Lend Prudentia a hand?

What are you waiting for!? Make [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000069,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000069,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] I requested, now!
I shall see to it that both you and Prudentia eat your words!
Speak with me all you like! The more time you spend chatting away, the further behind Pulmia falls! Hah hah hah hah!

I appreciate your promise of assistance, but words will not fill that order. Might you begin work on [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000070,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000070,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] I requested?

I require [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000070,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000070,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], and would be truly grateful if you would agree to assist me in making some.
Lend Pulmia a hand?
You have my thanks! Here is the recipe. Now make haste, for there is little time!
Well, if you have no intention of assisting me in my endeavors, I ask that you stand aside while I toil away on my own.
Lend Pulmia a hand?
Frequent an establishment like this one and it won't be long before you know precisely which cook's cuisine best whets your appetite.
Lately, I find myself coming more and more often for the entertainment... The battle between those two beauties is far tastier than any dish.
I must admit, the food was as spectacular as I had heard...and the view, well...you need only look yourself to see there is little else in Eorzea that could match [@1A(1)]those[@1A(0)] masterpieces.
And yet, one thing does trouble me─the fate of that downtrodden lass who was denied her opportunity to shine. I hope nothing ill has befallen her.

Lives on the streets of Limsa, I does, [@IF($E9(4),milady,sir)]. I knows all there is t' know, and if there's one thing worth knowin', it's that Pulmia makes the best slop in town. An' that ain't no lie!
Prudentia? Well, she 'as 'er place, o' course. Like what the sailors always say, you comes for Prudentia's legs, but you stays for Pulmia's wings!

The biggest drawback of a long sea voyage is the lack of a good meal. But, then again, one could argue that drawback is actually a blessing in disguise, for when the journey is complete, everything tastes ten times better than you remember it!

Of course, that's not the only reason Limsa's cooks always seem to deliver. Being in a port city, they have access to every exotic ingredient under the sun...assuming said delicacies can make it past Mealvaan's Gate, that is.
Might I ask that you step aside? I'm quite busy with this order. If you wish to chat, speak with Prudentia.
She will be brooding somewhere behind the restaurant, as she always does when she believes she has been slighted in some way.
We have quite a number of regulars here, and each has a favorite chef.
We encourage our chefs to maintain a close relationship with their individual patrons, and that is why you will see many speaking with those who purchased their culinary masterpieces.

The culinary world is dog-eat-dog. (No, you won't find dog on the menu...that is, unless you truly want a tasty leg of...er, ahem!) Even those who find fame cannot grow lax, for there will always be an ambitious young chef looking to out-season their savoriest sauce!
You need not worry about Prudentia. She'll survive this episode, as she has all those in the past.
As long as the fire burns hot in her heart, her tears will soon dry.

O Menphina, divine Lover and shepherd of the stars, Thy celestial light ever shines upon Pulmia and Prudentia, drawing the eyes of the masses from all others who would grace the kitchen's stage! How much longer must I dwell in their shadows?
Leave me be. I have no time for your pleasantries. I must concentrate.

Day after day after day...battling with the other cooks to entice the taste buds of each and every last customer... The pressure is unbearable! My heart is ready to burst! If I could only trade this skillet for a scimitar, these eggs for an eyepatch, this parsnip for a parrot!

Hmph! Presentation may be an important part of the culinary experience, but one cannot rely on appearances alone. The cruel hands of Time will peel away all those two have to offer, and toss it with the rest of the kitchen scraps. Then and only then will we see what they are truly made of.
I think I need some time to myself.
Haha! And now our quotas can be met. Are you ready to begin?

Though, just because you're now working [@1A(1)]for[@1A(0)] the Bismarck, doesn't mean you'll necessarily be working [@1A(1)]in[@1A(0)] the Bismarck. We provide the finest cuisine for every trade ship, fishing ship, naval ship, and pirate ship for a fifty-malm radius.

Put in your time here, and you'll never have to worry about...well, going hungry again. Why, there are even jobs such as galley cook that provide you the opportunity to sail to the far corners of the globe!

But the realm of the culinary arts spreads far and wide, and there are many out there just like you, looking to make a name for themselves. You must work hard to find customers, but even harder to keep them.
Ah, you seem somewhat overwhelmed. I do apologize for that.
But you need not fret! Everything shall be sweetmeats and strawberries! Go and speak with the two chefs there for your first assignment.
Very well! Do you see those two buxom beauties beyond the central counter? They shall tell you all you need to know.
Why, what sort of general retreats before even taking the field? Your lack of enthusiasm disappoints me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
<sigh> What ever will become of our quotas...?

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: I've tried asking Prudentia to tell me just what it is that is troubling her...but it seems every time I do...I merely end up pushing her further away.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: I believe she is more at ease speaking with adventurers and travelers because she feels they do not put excess pressure on her to succeed.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: If I am correct, you will have better luck at lifting Prudentia's foul mood than I, or any of her fellow culinarians would. And you may just get some cooking practice in the process.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: All you need do is talk to her, listen to her, comfort her, and everything else will fall into place.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Prudentia in a sour mood? Isn't she always? But then again, aren't we all? Chefs are ceaselessly searching for the perfect flavor, the perfect aroma, the perfect blend of eleven herbs and spices... They say no one is perfect, but then everyone expects us to be just that!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: How dare that man treat her with such disdain! Prudentia may be fifteen summers my junior, but she is one of my dearest friends. I shall not sit idly by as addle-brained imbeciles besmirch her name!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: O Llymlaen, benevolent Navigator! Hast Thou forsaken me!? Thy light did steer me to the secrets of Prudentia's scrumptious stew... Oh, but it was cursed! Cursed, I say!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Beware what you seek, adventurer. A grim fate awaits all those who learn Prudentia's secrets...

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: <sigh> Prudentia is an exceptional chef. Try as I might, it will be nigh on impossible to ever match her skill, her beauty, her...well, everything. I might as well just pack up and return to my mother and father's popoto farm.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: The transformation of a chef from ordinary to extraordinary is possible so long as the scullion wielding the skillet can put all of her skills to the test without succumbing to doubt. Prudentia's current state proves only that she still has much room to grow.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: I cannot help but to wonder if that kind merchant from Ul'dah truly did enjoy my cooking...or if he was only forcing it down out of pity...

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: If my meals are indeed unpalatable, then I must know, and I must know soon...while there is still time for me to find a path more forgiving of my inadequacies... <sigh>

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Well, what did you discern from your colloquy with our disconcerted cook?

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Ah, the merchant from Ul'dah. Yes, I do recall that his disappearance was...unusually abrupt.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: From what you say, it would seem for the time being that Prudentia wishes to be left alone to wallow in her sorrows. But just because [@1A(1)]we[@1A(0)] cannot tackle the symptom, it does not mean [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] cannot tackle the cause! Might I be so bold as to suggest you travel to Ul'dah, locate this fickle trader, and see what the fellow has to say for himself?

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: I seem to recall him saying in passing that he worked for Sunsilk Tapestries, a respectable clothier which also serves as the realm's Weavers' Guild. One of their reception staff should be able to tell you where he may be found.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: <sigh> All this over the whim of a single customer... If only Prudentia could see this man is but one fish in the sea. She would be wise to concentrate on the school, not the straggler.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Now you, on the other hand, could help bring her to her senses by tracking down this minnow of a merchant and discovering what compelled him to shun our chef. I believe he said he worked for the Weavers' Guild in Ul'dah. It would be “fitting” if you started your search there.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: An adventurer? What business might you have with the Weavers' Guild?

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: You're here from Limsa Lominsa? Well, that must have been quite a journey! One of our traders returned from there yesterday morning. He brought back a number of wonderful tales about the city, her people, and the sumptuous cuisine he dined upon.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Why, he's just over there, in the brown shirt and tinted spectacles.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: I'm sure he'd be delighted to regale you with tales of his journey, should you be interested.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: [@STRING($EB(1))]? A pleasure, but I don't believe you were summoned. What business might you have with us today?

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: You're here from Limsa Lominsa? Well, that must have been quite a journey! One of our traders returned from there yesterday morning. He brought back a number of wonderful tales about the city, her people, and the sumptuous cuisine he dined upon.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Why, he's just over there, in the brown shirt and tinted spectacles.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Did I not make myself clear? The one you seek is the fellow in the brown shirt and tinted spectacles just over [@1A(1)]there[@1A(0)].

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: ...It occurs to me that he must have been quite a customer to bring you all the way across the sea. Might I inquire as to how much of our coffers' contents he poured into your establishment to warrant such service? No? Well then...

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: From Limsa Lominsa, you say? You're a long way from home, [@IF($E9(4),my lady,my good sir)]. How might I be of service?

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: You came all this way simply to learn why I stopped frequenting the Bismarck? I see they take their business seriously!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: However, it pains me to say I cannot reveal to you my motives, for there is the matter of my honor at stake. If your mission requires that you return with a reason, then simply tell your employers that I fell ill and was forced to foreshorten my stay in Limsa Lominsa, as I have little faith in the leeches of that filthy city.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: <sigh> I see you are a persistent one. Very well, I shall play your little game.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Ahahahaha. You thought a full belly might prompt me to divulge that which you hunger for? You have much to learn, [@IF($E9(4),milady,sir)]. I am a well-traveled merchant, and have dealt with far wilier hagglers than you in my time.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Perhaps you should rethink your approach in the shade of one of the sultanate's floating gardens.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Flavor has nothing to do with my decision. Your chef fed me food fit for a rat, and insulted me in the process.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: So I will tell you this―if you wish to keep your custom, tell your guildmaster to either release the offending chef from his employ, or get her to make something that is somewhat less pleasing to a rat's tongue.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Welcome back from your long journey, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I hope it proved fruitful.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: I see... So the rumors have begun to spread. That is unfortunate...[@CR]As a port city, Limsa Lominsa has become a melting pot for people of all races and creeds. Here, you are judged on your skill at your chosen craft, and little else. While the Qiqirn may look different from most of us, they are nevertheless accepted in this city, for they work hard and rarely complain. However, I can see how someone who hails from a closed city like Ul'dah might see them in a less forgiving light.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: There have been times when the creatures gather in the alley behind the restaurant looking for scraps, but for the most part, they are harmless. If it were left up to me, I would put this whole issue behind us.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: However, it is not a decision I have the authority to make. I must take what you have told me to Master Lyngsath and wait for him to pass his judgment. How far he is willing to go to cater to the tastes of our foreign guests, it is not for me to say.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: In Ul'dah, you will find there are many sympathetic to the Empire. As a result, the Garleans' hatred of the beast tribes is not as frowned upon as it is in other city[@1F]states...though we Lominsans reserve a share of ire for the fishbacks.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Still, I cannot say I approve of anyone, Qiqirn or not, loitering in our back alleys scrounging for scraps. Our establishment must maintain some semblance of decorum.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: That merchant stopped coming because some Qiqirn enjoy Prudentia's mushroom stew!? How absurd!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: As much as I wish to expose him for the narrow-minded fool he is, it might be wiser if we were to keep this one small truth to ourselves. Prudentia cares dearly for her friends...what few she has. And in her current state, if she were to learn that those friends were the cause of her losing a customer...who knows how she might react?

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Traveled all the way to the burning deserts of the east for poor Prudentia, did you? A fine [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)], you are. Not many would cross sand and sea for another. She is fortunate to have a friend such as you.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Rat food!? Pah! You need not lend your ear to the rattlings of a desert snake! Let the halfman dine on camel dung and marmot piss. I'll take a piping bowl of Prudentia's mushroom stew any day!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: O merciful Matron! Wrap me in Thy motherly embrace and protect me from the wrath of the foul beast tribes and their terrible eikons so that I may live another day to sup on Prudentia's scrumptious stews!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: You had best not speak of that which you see in the shadows of the alleys...

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Should I offer Prudentia comfort, or a reprimand? Forgive me, my dear Pulmia, for I have the nerve to do neither!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: As of late, Prudentia spends much of her time in the alleys behind the restaurant. She claims she is out there thinking, but I doubt that is all she is up to.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: I'm sorry that I caused you so much worry. Sometimes I get so caught up in my own failings that I fail to see how my mood affects those around me.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: But you need no longer worry. Both you and my furry companions have done a fine job in lifting my spirits. I won't question my talents again...I promise!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: I see that Prudentia has returned to her rightful spot here in the kitchens. You have my deepest thanks for that, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Now hopefully things can revert to normal...and I can return to being the top chef...not that I permitted her absence to affect my work, mind you.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Prudentia has returned!? Oh this is... And I...I had just convinced a few of her customers to order from me... And now...! <groan>

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: You see!? I told you! I TOLD you! The customer is always wrong! Unless the customer happens to agree with you, and that would make him right... But until then, he's wrong!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: O Navigator! Guide me on my path to culinary greatness. Give me strength to bear the trials and tribulations every chef must face, that I might bring joy to my customers.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Stay your tongue, friend. Naught will come of sowing the seeds of hearsay.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: If I had consoled Prudentia...then Pulmia would have... <sigh> Will I [@1A(1)]ever[@1A(0)] have the courage to tell her my true feelings?

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Looks like you've helped solve another of our problems, adventurer. I would thank you, but I was just starting to get used to the peace and quiet in here...

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: It seems your conversation with Prudentia had quite an effect.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Or perhaps it was your actions which spoke for you in place of words─and loudly, too. Few would deny that your act of traveling to Ul'dah spoke more loudly than all but the lustiest of larynges.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Or perhaps she was simply glad to know she had a friend willing to travel across the realm in her name. As you might have noticed, she enjoys the attention. Ah ha ha!

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: Welcome! I have bad news...and then I have worse news. Not moments ago, I spoke to Pulmia about taking you under her wing for a spell. However, it pains me to inform you that she refused the offer on account of the fact that she finds herself swamped with her normal duties, so much so that she would have little time to properly instruct you.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: So, I went to Prudentia to ask of her the same favor, and...well, that too did not go as planned. You see, as of late, the kittle kitten has been of a dour disposition. While difficult enough to handle when in high spirits, she is practically untouchable when in one of her saturnine states.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: But you need not frown, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], for it was then I was touched by inspiration. You see, it seems Prudentia fancies your company, so I believe you, more than any of us, may be well-placed to return the spring to her step. And everyone shall benefit─Prudentia gets back on her feet, you are granted the opportunity to work with one of our most talented chefs, and the rest of us are no longer forced to endure her incessant whining and repining.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: You have my thanks, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. This task should not prove any more difficult than slaying a few wharf rats, as long as you are willing to listen. Lend your ear to Prudentia's plight and the path to her renewed happiness should become apparent.

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home
text_en: What is this? Do you mean to tell me that you do not feel even the merest iota of pity for poor, poor Prudentia? Your blood must be as cold as serpent's. Perhaps we were wrong about you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]...

quest_names: Mystery of the Gastronome Gone Home

text_en: Why hello there, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! If it is Prudentia you seek, you shall find her at her station near the ovens.
Well, what masterpiece of masticability did our good Prudentia call you down here to help make?

You say she simply stopped speaking upon spying a certain someone at my station? Now, whoever could that be? Many of our customers come to me wishing to express their personal thanks to the chefs who oversaw the making of their meals. I cannot be expected to remember the face of every man and woman who happens to approach me.
I wish Pulmia and her suitor all the best! May their days together be as bright as the fires of an oven...and their nights as warm! Ah hah hah hah!
Leave Pulmia be. Naught but ill will come of your meddling.

Look close enough and you will see Prudentia has a right keen interest in Pulmia's suitor. And who [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] this suitor, you ask? Why, a strapping young sailor, fresh off the sea; the scent of salt still on his wind-swept hair; free to roam the Navigator's realm...while I'm stuck here peeling popotoes. <sigh>
Let the young lads and lasses laze amidst their love stories while youth still smiles upon them. A few more strokes from the hands of Time, and they'll be as alone as I.
If Prudentia only had the strength to put the past behind her... Yet she insists on dragging it about like a babe with a threadbare blanket.

If she is not behind the restaurant tending to her...pets, it may be she has gone down to the sea to watch the [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),sunset,sunrise)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),ships come in,sunset)])]. Not anywhere too far off, mind you. Not for a moment would I believe even [@1A(1)]she[@1A(0)] had the courage to leave the protective walls of the city.

Even as the hardest of bones can be boiled to the softest of jellies; and even as the largest of merbeasts can be ground and minced into the tiniest of fishballs, so too can the coldest of shoulders ignite the hottest of flames in a young maiden's heart...there to burn red till naught is left but the ashes of sorrow.
While Prudentia's away, able Aentfoet of the Laughing Leek is king of the kitchens! Kneel before my chopping board and I shall dub thee Knight of Napkins!
P-P-P-P-Pulmia has a s-s-s-s-suitor!? O Menphina the merciful! Why must Thou forsake poor Kikichua!? Yes, I have sinned many a grievous sin, but naught that was not in the name of Love!
It would be better not to [@1A(1)]drag[@1A(0)] Prudentia's dirty laundry out into the open...

It was ultimately Prudentia's decision to work at the Bismarck that doomed her relationship...and more like than not, all those to follow, as well. I suppose I could attempt to brighten her spirits...but no, no, no. That wouldn't be right. No, not at all. Oh, dearest mother, dearest father! Forgive me for fostering such unsavory urges!
Former suitors? Pshaw! If I had a popoto for every man who once suited me, I could make enough mash to feed all the bloody pirates in Limsa!
Oh, what did I do to deserve this cruel fate?
Oh, what did I do to deserve this cruel fate?
When I learned who it [@1A(1)]truly[@1A(0)] was who robbed me of my love, I expressed my anger in the only way I could!
But...now I wish I could take it all back... I didn't mean to...[@1A(1)]p-p-p-poison their food![@1A(0)]

I must find them and stop them from eating any of the soup![@CR]<gasp> But what if they already have!? I-I need someone to make [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000071,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000071,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] in my stead. I'm so sorry to drag you into this, but might you be willing to do that for me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]?
The poison won't do them any permanent harm...but it [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] have them hugging their privies for the next fortnight...or two...I think.
You found Prudentia? And what is this you say? She's here?
That is odd. I cannot say that I have seen her. Perhaps she thought it unsightly to show her tears to the rest of us.

As you can see, I am far too busy to pay any mind to the comings and goings of each and every customer and kitchen colleague. Though, now that you mention it, I [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] recall a suspicious character lurking about the soup pots...

Looking to make [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000071,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000071,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]? Ask a fishback. Now if it's [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000074,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000074,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you need... Heh heh heh.

Prudentia? Yes, I saw her earlier wandering about without the restaurant. She had a solemn look on her face...as if she were deeply troubled about something or somewhat. I know that look all too well... It greets me every time I stare into the pots of soup I stir for bells on end... <sigh>

She looked as if she had, oh, I don't know, [@1A(1)]poisoned someone's stew in a fit of passion only to have second thoughts about how she could ever even have contemplated committing such a craven and contemptible crime[@1A(0)]. Well, either that or she had a touch of the wind.

We don't receive many orders for [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000071,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000071,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] around here, it being a Sahagin speciality and all. Most of our patrons prefer the less pungent [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000073,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000073,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. That said, I shouldn't imagine you'd need to modify the recipe for the latter too much if you wanted to make a batch of the former.
I-I-I...I saw everything! O, benignant Nald'thal, hear my humble plea! There is naught I would not give to trade away these sullied eyes!

Though the flames of passion can oft be as hot as those of the hottest oven, they may yet sate themselves in the space of a moment. But when the flames of indigestion burn bright, they can only be cooled by the soothing kiss of this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000075,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000075,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. Add it to any dish to extinguish the intestinal inferno that might otherwise be ignited in the unsuspecting diner.
I will not ask that you lie for me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], but, if possible, would you at least keep quiet about my...secret?
If customers were to stop frequenting the restaurant because they knew the truth, the head chef would serve me for supper!
Adventurers and travelers from all across the realm visit these halls each day, but only a few know Prudentia's true identity.
And now that [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] know, you can truly be called one of us. Welcome to our family, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]!
With all the ovens blazing and the soups boiling, the kitchens can become a veritable furnace. I can see why a man might want to wear a wispy skirt instead of a sticky pair of leather leggings.
While Prudentia's away, I'm king...er, queen...er, king of the kitchen!

O Thaliak, wilt Thou not lead Thy lost lamb to the Forbidden Fruit of Knowledge, that I might consume its secrets? (Its [@1A(1)]culinary[@1A(0)] secrets, that is. I need know no more of Prudentia's impure past!)
Feel like a fool, don't you?
We all knew about Prudentia's p─uh, [@1A(1)]past[@1A(0)], but the guildmaster made us take an oath of silence. You have my humblest apologies, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

I don't care what delights may be lurking in your undergarments─if your soup tastes like plague rat piss, you won't last long in my kitchens. Now, if you've the time to be talking to me, you've the time to be practicing...so get at it!
My friend Rycharde is one of the best cooks in Lominsa. However,Delmonteto taste, the wanderer took one look and refused to even smell it!

I wonder if any of the cooks here at the Bismarck were lucky enough to have been taught by [Delmonte]. If the wanderer would give me even one lesson, I'd trade in my adventurer's garb for an apron and never look back.
[en]
[en]
[en]
Oh,Delmonte
And oh,Delmonteroams the land, I'll never be the greatest chef in Eorzea...
Stand down! Stand down! Anyone who comes too close to the magnificent [Delmonte] will have their head peeled by none other than me, potato peeler extraordinaire!
Have you heard him speak of his adventures? No matter what kind of trouble he faces, he always finds a way out...using solely his culinary skills!
Quiet down! I cannot hear what the wanderer is saying!
Hmph... So this is the magnificent wanderer? Looks little more than a dried up old vagrant to me.
[en]
[xxxxx] contacted you as well, eh? So, what did you bring?
Nothing? What are you thinking? A chance to have one of your creations tasted by the greatest chef this side of the Garlean Empire and you waltz in here empty handed?
Why not tell [Delmonte] some of your adventuring stories? I'm sure he'd listen...well, that is if it isn't something I've already told him...and I've pretty much told him everything I know.
I expect it will be quite difficlut for our students to provide the wanderer with something he desires to consume...since he's eaten almost everything worth eating...everywhere.
I'll try your dish...as long as it's something different from what they serve here.
Hm... That does look decent...but nothing I haven't seen before.
[en]
[en]
Look who's back! And look what he's brought!

Let me see this... Amazing! They may be rutheless barbarians, but this recipe makes them look like gourmands! Let me work on this in the kitchen. You make one as well, and bring it to me when you are done.
So you decided to come? Well, there he is, right over there. And don't think about asking to shake his hand. The wanderer refuses to touch anything other than the utensils he wields.

You laugh? Hah! Only because you've never seen first hand the magic he weaves. Whenever he arrives in a town, the local chefs flock to his side, hoping to catch a glimpse of his techniques, to taste a morsel of his masterpieces.Why, steal even one of his tricks, and you'd be set for life!
What do you say? Have I piqued your interest? I might be able to get you an exclusive meeting!
[en]
Well, he's right over there. Try talking to him all you like, but I can't guarantee he'll listen.
Oho! [He/She] denies the chance at fame and fortune? Perhaps she drowns in the illusion that [his/her] skills measure up to even a mere onze of what the wanderer possesses.
[en]
A number of ancient-looking tomes and treatises adorn the shelf.

text_en: Penned by Lewphon of Sharlayan, master theologian and astrologist, in the Year 233 of the Sixth Astral Era, to weave together the disparate histories of the nations of Eorzea with a common thread─the thread of time.
For through its inevitable march the hours turn into Suns, and they into Moons, and they into Years. And from the Years come the Ages of Man. And ever eclipsing those is the eternity of Gods.

By the unit of a sole Sun we mean that period which lasts for the duration of four cycles of the six elemental hours─those of Ice, Water, Wind, Lightning, Fire, and Earth. And so is the Sun twenty hours and four, and so shall it ever be.
The life of a single Moon spans four cycles of eight Suns, and is thus the sum of thirty and two.
The eight deriveth from the elements six, Ice, Water, Wind, Lightning, Fire, and Earth, and the polarities two, Astral and Umbral.
The Year is made when the Moons go round the two Astral and Umbral poles, fluctuating between the six elements, and that in turn. In this, the Year can be said to be the length of twelve Moons.

The first and second Moons of the Year are the first Astral and first Umbral, and together they share an affinity with Ice. On their watch, all is frozen, and breath of life sloweth to near silence beneath.

The second Astral and second Umbral Moons come third and fourth in turn, and they are the Water of the melting Ice, and with their flowing slaketh the thirst of life again. Fifth and sixth are the third Astral and third Umbral Moons, and the Wind bloweth over the Water, carrying its heavenly boons near and far.

The fourth pairing of Astral and Umbral Moons come seven and eight, when the heavens rageth with the furies of Lightning, and sendeth them below with godly terror to test the faith of men.[@CR]The ninth and tenth Moons are the fifth Astral and Umbral, as the Lightning turns to Fire, and it charreth growing life with the colors of its flames, bleeding blade and leaf with brilliant hues of crimson and scarlet.[@CR]Year's end cometh in the eleventh and twelfth Moons, the sixth Astral and sixth Umbral, in which Earth consumes all, for out of the ground we are taken for the dust we are, and to the dust we shall return.

The wisdom of the Twelve saw fit to grant man with the cycle of years, and in turn the reverence of man bound them to his gods─the Year of the Navigator, of the Wanderer, of the Builder, of the Destroyer, of the Warden, of the Traders, of the Matron, of the Keeper, of the Fury, of the Lover, of the Scholar, and of the Spinner.
The turning of these Years twelve is a sacred thing, and together they comprise one epoch of man, by which the histories of his endeavor are measured.
The constancy and eternity of time derive from the pulse and breath of the Twelve.

And by their divine will the brilliance of the Astral Eras which see man flourish and prosper, and the shadows of the Umbral Eras which see man falter and doubt, are visited upon him in equal, and neither the greatest good nor the greatest evil may escape their purview.

Since the peace among the Twelve was broken and life was created to wage their wars, six cycles of the Eras have come to pass in keeping with the elemental order. The Sixth Umbral Era belonged to the waters, as heavy rains fell and the seas rose high, submerging and cleansing all in a great deluge. With time the waters receded, ushering in the present Sixth Astral Era, during which man has again rebuilt his halls and tilled his lands.

Naught save the ken of the Twelve themselves knoweth when the Seventh Umbral Era shall come and end our days. The sole certainty what resides within man is the selfsame as it has ever been─ours is the power to make of our Era what we might.
A cursory examination reveals that the volume is comprised of four chapters dealing with the elements and creation.
