text_en: The spark of Lightning ignites when it strikes, and thus Fire is born.[@CR]The heat of Fire renders to ash all that it touches, and thus Earth is born.[@CR]The density of Earth shuns Sun and harbors cold, and thus Ice is born.[@CR]The armor of Ice melts away, and thus Water is born.[@CR]The moistness of Water mists and rises, and thus Wind is born.[@CR]The gusts and sighs of Wind gather the clouds, and thus Lightning is born.
Earth grounds Lightning.[@CR]Water erodes Earth.[@CR]Lightning boils Water.
Fire is extinguished by Wind.[@CR]Ice is melted by Fire.[@CR]Wind is obstructed by Ice.
The six elements are manifest in all things great and small, and their polarity deriveth from the Astral heavens above and the Umbral depths below.
Many botanists from Greatloam Growery have enlisted in the Order of the Twin Adder. Even those who do not fight are welcome in units such as the Blue Badgers.
All things happen for a reason, yet it is the responsibility of the individual to find meaning in that which comes to pass.
Behold with the clarity of a still pond. Hearken with the tranquility of a virgin grove. Take but these words to heart, and no truth shall ever elude you.

I have the proud honor of being Aubrenard the Verbose, a merchant who deals in the currency of words as well as coin. Should you seek to learn more of the arts of parley, I should be more than happy to lend my services, good [@IF($E9(4),lady,sir)].
Damn it, woman, twist! Show that Ixali bastard his own guts when you yank 'em out of him!
I sometimes wonder if the forestborn have not become so concerned with the will of the Twelveswood that they fail to notice other truly important things going on around them.
Garleans continue to pour into the Twelveswood... None can now doubt that the imperial threat is real.
But faith keeps fear at bay, and makes life possible. The elementals, the conjurers, the Wood Wailers, the Gods' Quiver―these are the pillars of Gridanian faith.
Even the slightest errant cut or etch can destroy the overall aesthetic of the most complex and beautiful piece. Odd, isn't it?
Most outsiders are oblivious to the true power of the Twelveswood. It gives form to life, and nurtures it from birth to death. It purifies the air we breathe, and protects our very city.

For this we love her, and take care never to waste her gifts. Every necessary thing you see here, from weapons and tools to furnishings and playthings, was made from that which she freely gave. Welcome to the Oak Atrium.
Did you see the stars falling from the sky? Did you, did you!?
I heard that everyone in the area where they fell got turned into sludge! Some are saying it's the work of the elementals―that they are punishing us.
It's a credible enough theory, of course, but I, for one, can't help wondering if Dalamud might not have something to do with it.
It's always a pleasure to meet a fellow pugilist. We're few enough around these parts.
In the south, I fought alongside others. Then I traveled here unaccompanied, to learn the ways of the lone fighter. A complete pugilist must be a master of both styles.
Do come and see me again when you're a bit stronger.
Few places in Eorzea are as perilous as the Twelveswood. There is much to learn here of the ways of combat. Still, I think the time has come for me to move on to stronger quarry.
Of course, the greatest pugilists end up in Ul'dah. They say you only need a pair of fists to make a fortune there.
The guild has established itself at the Platinum Mirage. Any aspiring pugilist should make it a point to visit. Just try not to get too distracted by all the glitter.
Might you be a gamblin' [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]? Naught like the thrill of beating the Spinner at Her own game, eh?

Well, then what say you make the ultimate wager? There's a place in Coerthas known as the Aurum Vale where gold seeps forth from the rock and the walls are lined with mythril─all ripe for the taking. But only if you survive the poisonous mists, the ravenous creatures, and the Garlean grunts, that is.
Best take heed where you step in these parts, friend. The Hedge that protects Gridania runs not far from here.
The conjurers and Wood Wailers make regular patrols near the hedgetrees. You'll oft see them hereabouts, resting their weary legs between shifts.

And where are [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] going? All sorts of living things are gathering here, you know. Some are being led here, others come as if answering a call. But all of them are searching─searching for an answer.
[en]
I want to play in the forest. I'm not afraid of any stupid Ixal!
The Black Shroud... Forestborn call it the Twelveswood. And that Hedge of theirs borders it all.
I heard it said the conjurers make them hedgetrees with their magic. Up close, they [@1A(1)]shine[@1A(0)]―shine like no natural tree got any right to.
Ain't nothing stopping you looking at 'em, o' course. Cutting and burning 'em, though... Well, every adventurer worth his spit knows better than to mark [@1A(1)]them[@1A(0)] trees up.
Blacksmiths are right national treasures 'round here. Caught wind of that, did you? That what brought you?
Odd thing about Gridanians is they enjoy repairing things more than making 'em. If I had a gil for every hammered-out dent, I could buy this wood twice over.

How about a little bit of advice, then? Have you gotten your hands on any secondary tools? If not, you'd best do so. Might be Ahldiyrn's blacksmith shop over at the markets has got something you could use.
Repairing is all well and good, but there's only so much one can do with what's available here.
I reckon I'm past due a visit back to the guild in Limsa. I'd give my good arm for a chance to work a forge at Naldiq & Vymelli's again.
It's just such a damned long way―far to the south and west of here, 'cross the Rhotano Sea. There's a ferry point west of Ul'dah. The ships there'll see you across.
A journey and then some, to be sure, but one every true smith must make. The masters at the Blacksmiths' Guild can teach you better than any.
There have long been reports of imperial airships encroaching over Eorzean territory, but in recent days such sightings have increased tenfold!
Is there nothing the Order of the Twin Adder can do!? If this invasion is not dealt with, we shall lose our trade routes for certain!
I'd give anything to have the power of the moogles―to be able to call upon the elementals within things to restore them.
Gods, don't tell anyone I've said that. Most in these parts think it near heresy to want the powers of nature for oneself.
The will of the elementals is the only will served beyond these gates. To pass is to accept this, under punishment of exile.

Have you ever been in a place where you could hear yourself draw breath? We Gridanians like to say it is so quiet here that you can hear another's thoughts. So be careful what you think in that head of yours! Hehehe!
...Hm? Unless I'm mistaken, you've become flustered all of a sudden. <gasp> Surely the lesser moon isn't playing havoc with your humours!?
I'm afraid I can't let you pass. Orders are orders, and I've no intention of breaking them.
The Twelveswood protects Gridania. Without her we are nothing. This has ever been the way of things, and must continue to be so.
Any imperial soldiers that seek to threaten this sacred bond shall suffer for their intrusion. I pray that you will aid our cause, friend.
My orders are to let none pass beyond this point. Hie thee hence!
Gods damn it! My nocking is still far too slow. An Ixal would bury its beak in my face before I ever loosed an arrow. I... I am not fit for the Quiver.
Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna has returned to us from the depths of the Twelveswood.
She has made known to all her intention to lead Gridania in the fight against the Garleans. To do so, she has refounded the Grand Company of Gridania!
Have you been to Atelier Fen[@1F]Yll yet? The leatherworkers there are second to none.
Our timber is the finest around, and our pieces last years longer than most, but that leather damn near [@1A(1)]never[@1A(0)] wears out. I've seen things of theirs that have lasted for generations.
Protocol is everything, and without it nothing can be begun. Now listen...
First comes the greeting―sharp and crisp. Greet all you happen upon on the road or elsewhere, friends as well as enemies.
Still a great deal to be done, but yes, it's coming along quite nicely. Don't you think?
Well met and well come, adventurer. You have reached Buscarron's Fold, Gridania's humble bastion in the south. We've no luxuries to offer, but you are free to stay as long as you wish.
Garuda has wreaked havoc upon us yet again! How many humiliating defeats must we suffer before her reign of destruction is ended!?
If only we could turn primal against primal by some ruse... Ah, but that is wishful thinking indeed. Victory must needs come by our own hands if it is to come at all.
There is no end to what the moogles teach us. It is they who show us which trees may be logged, which grasses cut, which fruits and flowers picked.
I haven't the slightest idea what those adorable little devils are saying, but you can tell their mood by the bouncing of the globes above their heads.

As of this moment, the globes tell me that the moogles are under great strain, doubtless from the ongoing turmoil that has befallen the Twelveswood. I wonder whether there's aught we might do to ease their burden...
Hyrstmill was once a haven for wounded warriors, mostly archers of the Quiver fighting against the Ixal.
Now? The camp is a battlefield more oft than not. If things don't improve soon, we'll have no choice but to send our injured back to Gridania...
Please, do not sully me with your presence. The stench of the woodsin is all about you.
Each step I am forced to watch you take makes my stomach roil.
Think of it. Someday I might happen across the soul who comes to own this bag. That is the crafter's greatest joy.
You'll not pass as long as I draw breath. Best just go back the way you came.
Not now! If this hole is half an ilm off, the entire piece will be ruined. Waaait for it...
To put a weapon as long as the polearm to best use in dense forest requires many moons of practice [@1A(1)]in[@1A(0)] the wood.
But there is value in practicing here as well. The Wailers are a symbol―a symbol which stirs the hearts of our people, and strikes fear into the hearts of our enemies.
It seems the Grand Company of old has been restored to its former glory. They've already established a base of operations in the Lotus Gardens.
The Order of the Twin Adder's banner flies once more. If you've a mind to lend your strength to the fight against the Garleans, you'd do well to pledge your allegiance.
A fishing rod is no sword, but if the Garleans bring their war to Gridania, we fisherfolk will do what we can.
If they gave me half a chance, I'd break my pole over their general's pate and throttle his lieutenants with my line!
But never mind about that. Do be sure and carry some secondary tools with you. You never know when you'll happen upon some shallow waters ripe for spearfishing.
I hope what I have told you proves to be of some use. Remember, friend―not all we fight are fish.
It pains me to say that not everyone at the Fishermen's Guild back in Limsa Lominsa shares my sense of duty.
Any lout with eyes could glean as much from a visit to Fisherman's Bottom. That's where you'll find most pullers and casters these days.

Actually, if you've a mind to contribute, why not head there yourself? After all, if it comes to war with the Garleans, not even the fishers will be spared. Oh, but don't go repeating what I said about duty―they can be quite...hotheaded.
I ain't never seen none go traipsin' 'round the wood so merry-like. You adventurers are either the bravest souls I ever heard of, or the foolest.
Now, since you're plainly a good sort, I'm gonna let you in on a little secret: it's the greenwrath what's given Dalamud his bloody hue and made Garuda stronger besides. Quite a revelation, eh?
Cobbling's my trade. See more repairs than I do new makes, but that's to be expected, I suppose. Who doesn't love a good, old boot?
Most Gridanians keep footwear from decades, even centuries ago. They just repair it over and over as it passes from generation to generation.
Them ruins in the deep forest are sacred to all us Gridanians─the cornerstone of our very history. Fell whatever beasts ye must, but don't so much as put a scratch on those ancient stones.
How in the bloody hells do these weeds get so damned hardy, anyhow!? Where are all the weedy weeds? That's what I want to pull up!
Your kind certainly has an insatiable appetite for tidings. Whatever would you do without the Adventurers' Guild?

Oh, that dumbfounded look is so unbecoming. You needn't worry, there are many and more thaumaturges like myself, if only you know where to look. Why, the Order of Nald'thal is its own guild, you know.

Gridania has guilds of its own, to be sure. Those militant types with their pointy spears and arrows, and those adorable little conjurers, and...oh, whatever else it is they do here. If what you seek isn't here, I imagine it can be found elsewhere.
Your kind certainly has an insatiable appetite for tidings. Whatever would you do without the Adventurers' Guild?
Very well, I will oblige you this once. But as a thaumaturge, you should be aware that what little news I have pertains to the Order.

If all the magic you weave aims merely to inflict harm, you are no different from a conjurer. A skilled thaumaturge saps the essence of [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] foe, thereby strengthening [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] allies.
Twelve be good, you're of the Order! You are a welcome sight indeed. What brings you to Gridania?

Oh, you simply [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)] pay a visit to the guild. You do know of it, yes? Ah...I remember the day I first set foot in the Arrzaneth Ossuary... I never dreamt there were so many like-minded souls in Ul'dah!
You need do no more than take the Lumberline beyond the forest and across the desert until you reach the city. The Ossuary is our true home, and the seat of untold power!
How much pocket money do you get? Is it more than us?
Those godsdamned Ixal... I swear they only strike when our back is turned. A pox on the cowards and a pox on their wretched primal!
The Twelveswood could not be rid of their foul ilk soon enough. Should you come upon any suspicious activity in the wood, be sure to report it to the Wailers without delay.
Come now, tell me true, have you ever seen such beautiful fruits? The most delicious in all Eorzea, you have my word!
The wind elementals gather here at Quarrymill. Their presence livens the wings of the small creatures carrying pollen, and our gardens and orchards are the end result.

Alas, the appearance of Garuda threatens my fruits─my very livelihood. The primal is said to hold dominion over the winds, you see, and the elementals cannot help but disperse at her coming. Ah, would that some brave souls could send that winged plague back whence she came!
It seems Proscen is intent on leaving us, but I fear for her safety.
The Ixal raids come more frequently than ever─it is no time to be wandering the wilds alone. If only the water elementals would give us some sort of sign, it would help set my mind at ease.
You show me an adventurer and I'll show you someone who wants to rent a chocobo. There is nothing to be done about it. We simply cannot supply enough birds.
I trust you've heard as much, but between the forest and the mountains of Ishgard to the north lie the homelands of the Ixal.
Twelve curse them and their foul eikon! They plague our people at every turn, wantonly killing and sounding their mocking caws as they flee from a fair fight.
Just once I would like to look one in the eye... But then, my mother always said my curiosity would be the end of me.
So, you're an armorer, come to learn what there is to be learned, eh? Aye, you've the right of it. A good armorer must learn the foe to be fought before the armor can be wrought.
If there is one piece of wisdom I might impart, let it be this...
You've two hands―make use of them both. There's secondary tools to be had at Matheonien's armorer shop in the markets.
How have you fared, friend? Made many an ally, and unmade many an enemy, I daresay. But tell me, is your hammer screaming for an anvil yet?
Then travel with me to Ishgard! Together we― What? You've yet to join the guild? Bloody hells, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]!

There is more to our craft than hammering out plate! Get your arse to Limsa, and learn from the best armorers in all the realm. You need only take the Lumberline south to Ul'dah, then head west to the ferries of Vesper Bay.
The conjury of the sylphs is far beyond the base magic we command. A good conjurer knows it when [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] sees it, but cannot make it [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] own.
The sylphs live within the Twelveswood, as well. Quite nearby, actually. You've never noticed, have you? Yes, such is their way.
This here's the Hawthorne Hut, named after the legendary Hawthorne, scourge of the mountains, from whom our master Rolfe is descended.
You needn't let a thing like that scare you, though. His days of banditry are long behind him now. The hospitality of the Hut is yours, traveler, such as it is.
I see you've taken your oath. Be welcome, Wailer. It will be an honor to fight at your side.
So you wish to be a Wailer, do you? To be hero to all the younglings?

Not just any adventurer is given leave to join our ranks. We've a conjurer among us─as all guilds in Gridania do. We trust in Sister Challinie to separate the wheat from the chaff when it comes to your kind.
The red moon is certainly an arresting sight. One can see it clearly even through the canopy! It is terrible and breathtaking all at once...
The soldiers claim there is naught to fear, yet I cannot help but wonder what will become of us...

The forces of the Empire have grown restless this past moon. And now there is talk of some great-mawed beast roaming the wilds. Keep your hand on your sword hilt should you plan to venture outside of town.
Have you come to take up the bow, as well? We Elezen are unmatched at the butts. Prowess with the bow is mind over matter, friend. Remember that.
With both the Garlean Empire and the Ixal bearing down upon us, it is all too easy to lose focus. Yet maintain it we must, for the sake of all who abide in the Twelveswood.
How fares your training? Prowess with the bow is mind over matter, friend. Remember that.
With both the Garlean Empire and the Ixal bearing down upon us, it is all too easy to lose focus. Yet maintain it we must, for the sake of all who abide in the Twelveswood.

The primal Garuda is said to be the wind given form. Those who have beheld her tell of an immense creature possessed of great wings, whose beating serves to raise her far beyond the reach of our conjury.
Louisoix of the Circle of Learning has been deliberating with our nation's leaders on how best to neutralize this wind-borne foe. For all our sakes, I pray that their efforts bear fruit.
Maisenta of Black Rabbit Traders, at your service.
Hate to disappoint, but I'm a wholesale merchant. Can't be bothered with trifling volumes. Best try your luck elsewhere.
Sun's sweet smile and wind's cool breath,♪[@CR]Both of these I send thee,♪[@CR]To ripe thy fruit and spread thy seed,♪[@CR]And nourish those that tend thee.♪

Well, good [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),eve,morn)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),day,eve)])] to you, friend. Do you not know that hymn of Nophica? It's an old favorite among farmers and harvesters.
My name is Eugenaire, of the Trappers' League―the greatest huntsman in these parts.
<sigh> Or so I was long ago... Now, it seems I spend more of my days hunting poachers than game.
Be wary of the ruins should you ever venture near them. There is great evil deep within the forest, to which no life is sacred.
Beware also the birdlike beastmen known as the Ixal. They lurk in the depths of the Twelveswood, preying upon the hapless wayfarer.
If you make a chair just right, people will have no choice but to take notice of the chap who sits in it.

This one time we put the Ixal to rout, their commander fled, but not before dropping a rather peculiar ornament. Upon it was carved the likeness of Garuda. To simply behold it sent a shiver down my spine.

Sad to say, even a place as peaceful as Gridania is not without its crime...and crime has been on the rise of late. Some claim that Dalamud is driving law-abiding citizens to stray from the straight and narrow.
Still, I cannot help but feel for those imprisoned here. The gaols of Gridania are a far worse fate than those of the other nations.
Halt, there! Very well, I see you are no sylph. Be on your way with these words of warning: the Ixal have taken to summoning Garuda to wreak havoc upon Gridania.

Our hamlets in particular are regular targets for the primal's wrath. Practice due caution on your travels, lest you stumble into the midst of the chaos, and add your name to the lists of the fallen in so doing.
Taken an interest in the leather trade, have you? Come to learn what it's like to work with skin and hide?
Leatherworkin's a gods-given privilege. It's a metaphor for life itself. And it'll teach you what it means to be alive.
Hetzkin doesn't like this sky one bit. It is ill at ease, and the elementals' voices have abandoned us in their fear. We are truly lost.
The airships are still in their testing stages. Gridania asks for your patience and understanding.
You―tell me, did you come across a great conjurer within the forest? You're not like to forget her if you did.
My skin turns all to goose flesh and I go weak in the knees just remembering the gaze she fixed me with. Such is the awesomeness of the Seedseers.
You... You're a weaver?
Bah, what does a lickspittle from beyond the seas know of clothcraft!?
Best head over to Foinine's weaver shop in the markets and get yourself a decent secondary tool or two.
Mend your skills if my words do not sit well with you. I will be here.
I admit, you are not altogether inept.
But you still know so little of our ways. I wonder, do you even know where our guild lies?
It is to the south, in great Ul'dah, where the sun beats on your back with fiery fists, and the sins and sands are both hot and golden and everywhere at once.
Making your way to Gridania? I've just come from there, myself. It's always a pleasure doing business with them woodfolk.
Welcome back to the Roost, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. How can I help you?
Have a pleasant stay!
I can honestly say the Roost provides the best night's sleep in all Gridania. Perfect for the adventure-weary traveler!

Entering an inn room grants a [@COLOR(#ffff7b1a)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]resting[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] status. This indicates that you are gradually accumulating a [@1A(1)]rested bonus[@1A(0)]. This continues even while offline if you logged out from inside an inn room.
While rested, experience points earned through combat, synthesis, and gathering are increased by 50%. How rested you are is shown in green on your experience bar.
If your experience point bar is highlighted in red, then this indicates that your rested bonus will continue beyond your current level.
There are rules, of course. We must must maintain a peaceful environment for our patrons, after all.
Synthesis, repairs, and materia melding cannot be performed inside inn rooms.
We hope you choose the Roost as your return destination!
It is possible to set an inn room in the Roost as a secondary home point. Doing so will ensure that you are teleported there when using the Return command.
I apologize, but orders have been given. None are to pass beyond this point.
You heard the rumors of that monster with the great big mouth? They say it conjures up some other kind of beast that glows with a terrible light. Best keep your distance, I say.
Had word of a shady bloke seen wanderin' about. Best keep an eye out, eh?
Althyk, the Keeper, is the surveyor of time and space. Holding dominion over gravity, He manipulates the sands of time at will, and can thus see all that has been and all that will be.
Before singing of past battles, it is customary that we bards give prayer to Althyk.

Since I began overseeing drills at the Quiver's Hold, a change has come over my song─it has become richer in timbre, and clearer in purpose. And this after so many years. A fitting reminder that one should ever strive for greater mastery over one's art.
The masks we wear are part of our war garb. But there is nothing we seek to conceal. We value truth and virtue as much as any, and more than most.
If you ever find your hide in need of saving in the wood, it will be the Wailers who come.
Hyaaah!
Nothing worth doing can be done without a good set of boots. And every boot starts with a sole. My first mentor told me that, and only now am I beginning to grasp what he meant.
Some of the folk around here believe that when strange shadows follow you in the forest, it is your own death drawing near.
Others think it's just sylphs playing a trick on us. One easy way to find out―chuck some water at it. If it giggles, it's a sylph. If it don't... Well, best make your peace with the Twelve.

'Course, strange shadows and mischievous sylphs aren't exactly the biggest of our problems these days─hells, they almost seem comforting. I'd sooner run into one of those than a horde of bloodthirsty Ixal and their primal.
Beyond here lies Stillglade Fane. It is sacred ground, marked by the Skyserpent's Egg, the stone cast to Eorzea from the heavens by Nophica the Matron.
It may well be that, likewise, Dalamud comes to us at the Matron's behest. I urge one and all to remain calm, lest panic spread like poison throughout the populace.
The materials left behind by the things that live are evidence of their having been. By reworking those traces into new creations, we honor that which they were.
If you are come here, then the elementals must favor you. Know the people here. Know the land. But most importantly, know the elementals.
The Elder Seedseer has returned to the city! Returned to lead Gridania to peace once more!
Should the day ever come that you have chance to meet the great Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna, see to it you pay her the greatest respect.
You are but a mere adventurer, but should the day ever come that you have chance to meet the great Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna, see to it you pay her the greatest respect.
I daresay you've a hankering to open up a little shop of your own at the Ebony Stalls at some point in time, eh? Gods know I do.
For now, I'll work here and save the coin, but someday I'll manage it─just you wait. Dalamud can come crashing down on Eorzea if he fancies, but I [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] have my shop!
Gods, I've been dry as a bone for the past six bells. M-Mead... Jus' give me enough mead to wet me lips...
Oho, ain't we lookin' valiant today! Jhal Tristram himself would approve!
Oho, ain't we lookin' every ilm the predator today! Must feel fine bein' at the top of the food chain, eh!?
Oho, ain't we lookin' menacin' today! Makin' a killin' lettin' blood with that dirty great axe of yers, I'll wager.
Oho, ain't we dressed to kill today─dragons, that is! Ye ken what they say about a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] with a big polearm? Aye, well, neither do I...but I reckon it's probably a good sign.
Oho, look who's dressed to entertain today! How about a little ditty to help me along with me hammerin', then? I don't care what it is, so long as it's bawdy! Hra hra hra!
An' who's this picture of benevolence who stands before me!? Slap a pair of horns on ye, an' ye'd fair pass for a Padjal!
Oho, looks like someone's got an appetite for destruction! Promise me ye won't go droppin' any stars on me head, eh!?
Ye're... Ye're still alive! Why the hells do you adventurers have to be so godsdamned sturdy!?

A fell breath seeps from the Thousand Maws... Just standing here is enough to set my hairrrs on end. I've nothing but the utmost respect for the brave souls fighting whatever evil lurks in that accursed place.
I'm afraid the airship is currently unavailable. Local flight activity is limited to testing at present.
We've seen your kind before. What brings you here? Have you come to fight for the wood or against it?
For it, you say? I pray you speak the truth, for your sake. Hyrstmill welcomes her allies.
Do not be frightened by the Wailers at the gate. Their warning words are meant for the meek of heart, and their polearms for enemies of Gridania.
You'll find an establishment by the name of the Carline Canopy at the top of this incline. It might be worth your while to pay it a visit―most adventurers do.

I've been charged with dyeing these skins to hide their wearers in the wood. You'd be amazed what a difference a bit of pigment can make. If you get it just right, the results are akin to invisibility!
We built our little hamlet here with the consent of the elementals.

Among the different kinds of elementals, none are more intimate with men than those who abide in the trees. In their benevolence, they have veiled the reddening Dalamud from our sight, sparing us the constant reminder that dark days lie ahead.
So, you wish to know which of this region's beasties pose the greatest threat to your continued good health?

Well, given that I cannot say with any degree of certainty how capably you handle yourself, I shall offer only this―do try and avoid the ghosts. Bogies or revenants or whatever else you may stumble upon.

Of course, should things take a turn for the worse, you can always make haste for the safety of Camp Bentbranch. Barring that, I advise you to carry damn near your body's weight in salves and potables.
Few value the work we alchemists do more than the conjurers―but we must still secure their prior consent when we wish to venture into the forest's farthest recesses.
I see you are something of an alchemist yourself. Heed this―though good-natured, the Gridanians can be quite stubborn in their ways. They are not as reliable as they may seem in all things.
By the by, you would do well to acquire some secondary tools from Mumuko's alchemy shop. They [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] have their uses.
There you have it. We alchemists must watch after one another, yes?
Tidings have arrived from Ul'dah. Things south are as lively as ever, it would seem.
<sigh> I long to return at times. You have been to Frondale's Phrontistery, yes? The libraries there always leave me in rapture. So many volumes, so much knowledge!
If you wish to further your alchemical studies, I highly urge you to visit the Phrontistery and enlist with the guild.
I'm afraid I've never been much of one for giving directions. But a good map and a southern bearing should see you there with little trouble.
You can beg till you go hoarse, but orders for my signature belts are stacked for the next twelve moons.
Come to learn the trade? If you wish to see the work of a master, just take notice of the belts of our good citizens. You'll find none finer.
Folks 'round here put a lot of trust in us Wailers, and no mistake. Makes us what we are, it does. And any Wailer who forgets that...well, he ain't like to be one much longer─nor much else neither.
Our lances barely leave our hands these days, now that the bloody Ixal are stirrin' again. Between protectin' hamlets an' vanquishin' primals, a Wailer scarce has the time to make water.
Our clientele is as diverse as one could imagine. People from all creeds and all corners of Eorzea come seeking items bearing the Fen[@1F]Yll name.
Yet no matter how much money they offer or how high their standing might be, all are equal in the eyes of our guild.
I am terribly busy recording my findings. Please, if you have nothing to contribute, be so kind as to leave me to my work.
Need you guidance through the Lotus Gardens? I shall see you wherever you mean to go.
It is the moogles who first taught the language of the elementals to man.
It was thanks to their efforts that some learned to hear the elementals, and understand them, as we do now. Even so, it requires arduous training to nurture the gift.
Don't imagine we'll save your hide when the Ixal come cawing, outsider. You'll get no pity from us, and less from the elementals.
If there is something you seek in the wood, I suggest you do not range far. Your search may well prove the end of you.
Airships are [@1A(1)]fun[@1A(0)]! ...Are we there yet? Are we there yet? Are we there yet? Are we there yet? Are we [@1A(1)]not[@1A(0)] there yet?[@CR]...Awww! You were supposed to say no!
We are honored that you have taken an interest in the Growery's gardens. Under normal circumstances, only forestborn Gridanians may enter.
No matter how much we admonish our guests, there are always those who pluck whatever flowers they like. Ul'dahns mostly, as if [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] were a surprise.
You must notify the Wailers at once if you see any Ixal within the forest.
The Garleans make them for one of the so-called “beast tribes.” But to us they are mere beasts, and should be dealt with as such.

For some years, the Ixal had done little of note to trouble the peace, but their summoning of Garuda emboldens them anew. Thence do they resume their war against Gridania, making their presence in the Twelveswood sorely felt at every turn.
Well don't just stand there looking sorry for yourself. I'll not have it said the Carline Canopy failed to welcome an adventurer.

Close your eyes and open your ears. Do you hear it? Just like being up in the real canopy. The chirping birds, the whispering breeze... What better way to put the mind at ease in uncertain times such as these.
Of course, I'm only too aware how restless you people are wont to get, so I've fitted the place with all of the adventuring amenities you could wish for, as well.
Be on your guard! The great-mawed creature that appeared in Coerthas has been spotted in this very region!
There are more and more strange characters appearing about here as of late. Stay safe, friend.
As Gridanians, everything we do is done in service to the elementals. These gates are open to all who would honor this creed during their time here.
We're saved, kupo! Saved! I thought I was doomed for sure.
What is this, kupo? What's happening here? I have a bad feeling. A very, very bad feeling, kupo!
Kupopo... Raya[@1F]O told us off again... Apparently, we should be making ourselves useful rather than flapping about after her. Would it kill her to show a little appreciation, kupo?
It must be reassuring to have Oha[@1F]Sok and her kindred with you constantly, kupo! Aye, nearly as good as having us moogles about!
Raya[@1F]O has the stuff of great leaders. When she speaks, people listen...elsewise they'll never hear the end of it, kupo.
Raya[@1F]O is in high spirits again, kupo! Was it something you said, adventurer?
You outsiders may call it the Black Shroud, but to us Gridanians it is the Twelveswood―and it is home.
The name may seem appropriate enough from here, I grant you, but it's born of ignorance nonetheless. The forest punishes the profane, and protects the pure.
But now [@1A(1)]we[@1A(0)] are the ones who must protect the forest─aye, from the wicked Ixal and their primal, Garuda. Neither must be suffered to defile the sanctity of the Twelveswood.
There are those among us who reside within the wood, but are not of the wood.
Those fled from the ash and ruins of Ala Mhigo seek refuge here, though it is the elementals who determine who may stay and who must go.
Size is nothing to a carpenter of skill. Be it a mask, a waterwheel, a house, or a ship, the true woodworker is undaunted by scale.
We must pour ourselves wholly into all we make, else we slight the elementals within. For it is from them that the power and beauty of things emanate.
Let one of the filthy Ixal show so much as a tail feather within my sight─I shall see the vile beast's head adorn the tip of my spear.
You are an adventurer, are you not? Know that none but the conjurers can help those tainted by the woodsin. You have been warned. Do not plead ignorance should the greenwrath find you.
Come ooon, let's look for a moogle!
I worry this might be a slight case of overacting... It pains every artistic bone in my body, but for whatever reason the masses seem to enjoy this tripe.
Gridania's guilds share a comradery unlike any I have seen elsewhere. The manner in which they aid one another is truly inspiring.

It goes beyond mere unity on the battlefield. They provide for one another in times of peace, as well―giving whatever they can, and taking only what they need. All of Eorzea could learn much from their example.
You needn't take my word for it. Ask any carpenter or leatherworker or botanist you happen to meet.
An adventurer would do well to strengthen [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] ties here. Your journeys will be the better for it.
If you craft yourself, then surely you've made some like-minded acquaintances by now. But what of warriors? What of mages?
I advise you not to neglect any of these on your travels. Your journeys will be the better for it.
A goldsmith! Why, this is a treat indeed.
Sadly, our friends in Gridania do not value all that glitters. So it falls to us to convince them of it with our work!
If I might make a suggestion―pay a visit to Gagaulu's goldsmith shop over in the markets. They've an assortment of the secondary tools of our trade.
It is an honor to meet such an accomplished goldsmith. Tell me, has the forest yielded any inspiration?
If so, I suggest you join the Goldsmiths' Guild, lest your ideas be stolen the instant you make them known. The moneyed organizations can be quite ruthless like that.
Eshtaime's Lapidaries is where the guild resides, in the city of Ul'dah to the south. No doubt you have heard the name.
We are the Gods' Quiver, and our will is that of the elementals―to punish all who would visit harm upon the Twelveswood.
Both the Garlean interlopers and the Ixal, with their primal Garuda, shall know the wrath of the forest─depend on it.
Join our ranks, adventurer. In return for your service, you shall learn the ways of the bow. What say you?
The Twelveswood is a vast forest set aside just for the elementals by the Matron, Nophica. It was here long before we came, and will remain long after we are gone.
You are their guest, and may tread only where allowed. Adventurers are not permitted beyond the hunting grounds. See to it your feet do not stray.
The Gods' Quiver has been hurling its strength against the Ixal. It pleases me to see that you adventurers have not been idle either.

Owing to your efforts in the name of the Twin Adder, we've managed to conduct a number of successful forays into enemy territory, up in the ranges. Alas, our numbers are but few, and we've been unable to gain little and less ground beyond that.
Oh, now there's a face for the ages. Nothing spells misery quite like the weathered mug of an adventurer. What is it, dear? No gil for repairs?
You just take a whiff of ol' Odilie, here. Smell that? That's gil. Gil got by gathering and crafting, looting and bazaaring, and levequesting besides.

It's like a sword fight―stick to the basics and you'll come out on top nine times out of ten. By the by, have you visited the market dens in the west of the city? Adventurers run their own stands down there, you know.
Well I'll be damned! You're a culinarian?

Well, there's no place like Gridania for fine ingredients. Only trouble is, people here are so fixated on using every last scrap that they barely seem to notice the taste. Must be why there's so few gourmets.
That's no excuse for not trying, though. Get yourself some secondary tools if you haven't already, and learn to use them. Should be some for sale at Stanilde's culinarian shop over at market.
Finally had a bellyful of the wood's bounty?
Aye, it gets bland after a while, I admit. If its flavors you're after, best travel to the Culinarians' Guild in Limsa Lominsa.
Oh, the varieties... Fishes no Gridanian's ever dreamt of, spices from every corner of Eorzea. One meal at the Bismarck, and you'll never want to leave.
It's a fair old trip from here, but you can always cover your expenses by cooking along the way. You need only head south to Ul'dah, and then west to the ferry point.
The skies bless us with rain, and the rains nurture all that they wet. That is the way of things.
Come in, come in. And welcome to the Greatloam Growery―the very roots of this Gridania.

Gathering is our trade, in all its splendor. From the lumber used to craft bucklers and bedposts, to the ingredients used to cook up Eorzea's breakfasts, lunches, and dinners. Without us botanists, the economy would be in quite a pinch.
Tell me, have you seen one of these so-called Archons? You know, the strange figures appearing throughout the realm wherever aetheryte are found.

Some claim to have seen imperials in armor of silver roaming the region in search of them, but as to what end, I couldn't say. All I can say is this─if any of the lot are bold enough to show their faces around here, Garlean and Archon alike, we'll take them. Dead or alive.
What news from beyond the wood, friend?
Tell me all that you know. What is the world, after all, if it is not worth knowing?
There was a strange fellow here not long ago, preaching to any who would listen. Dark words, they were, about the coming of the Seventh Umbral Era. Perhaps it has already begun...
There was a strange fellow here not long ago, preaching to any who would listen. Dark words, about the coming of the Seventh Umbral Era...
Despite bein' away from her parents, this wee one's copin' pretty well with all the travelin'─a little [@1A(1)]too[@1A(0)] well, even. Has the makin's of an adventurer, she does.

Still, someone has to look after her, 'specially here in the Black Shroud. I hear them elementals'll fly into a rage if you so much as hiccup too loud─and it don't make a whit of difference if you're a younglin' who knows no better. Anyroad, I'll see to it she comes to no harm.
This is a splendid curve. Yes, this will serve quite well. Give your bow the same attention you would a lover, lest it betray you when needed most.
The wood is enraged, kupo. And when it's enraged, [@1A(1)]dreadful[@1A(0)] things happen. The flower fields are sounding more inviting by the minute...
The best spot in Gridania? Well, that's a fool question. Ain't no place any worse or better than any other. Go on and ask any Gridanian. They'll tell you as much.
Were I you, I'd want to know the safest place to be. The thrice-damned Ixals've been makin' a right nuisance of themselves of late, see.
They've taken to summonin' their primal Garuda, in point of fact, and she in her turn has taken to layin' waste to our hamlets. The elementals take them!
So you want to know whereabouts in this bloody forest that pickaxe might find a rock to lay into, eh?
Sorry, friend. Miner or no, I can't go givin' out secrets like that willy-nilly. S'pose I could part with a hint, though.
Reckon you've seen some outcrops in your time, am I right? Type that won't have nothing to do with a pickaxe? Aye, you'll need yourself some secondary tools to get at them.
Wrap your noggin 'round that, and you'll know all you need to know.
Might not think it, but there's rocks to be had 'mongst all them trees out there. Found any yet?
'Course, ain't nothin' more borin' than diggin' up the same old shite time and again. Ever think of headin' south? Ain't no minin' in Eorzea like they got down in Ul'dah.
Place down there by the name of Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern. Got their very own mountain, Twelve as my witness. More miners down there than trees up here.
Why not head down to that there Concern and put in at the Miners' Guild? There's a pretty gil in it, that's for sure.
Twist...twine...addle... Gods, I'm never going to get this right!
I saw this river in a dream... This little river I have known for so long. Its waters were stained red, like blood, and flowed fast and thick.
Only, I cannot know if it is my terror of the Ixal, or the wisdom of the elementals that sent this dream to me.

Does it foretell my death at the hands of the Ixal and their primal Garuda? Or is it a vision of the gore-stained Dalamud looming overhead? I suspect the truth shall remain veiled to me until the very hour of my demise.
Ah, would that more bards like Jehantel sang in the Twelveswood! Then my kinsmoogles and I could bathe in sunbeams all day long, kupo!
Jehantel now sings for us daily, and we owe it all to you! Promise me you'll ever do your part to bathe folk the world over in sunbeams, kupo!

Beyond lies sacred moogle ground, where enchanted keystones have been erected. For your own safety, you'll want to tread [@1A(1)]warily[@1A(0)] when guardians of the grove are near─sudden movements are like to rouse their anger, kupo.
Kupopopo... This is terrible...a veritable dilemma and a half! We have to act, and soon, kupo!
Where in the name of the elementals did everyone disappear to, kupo? It's so unbearably lonely here. How long am I expected to wait? <sniff>

I put this to you, friend: does man truly need airships? Can't we leave the skies to the birds and the bees, and be content with our place on the land, with the gentle caress of the grass between our toes?
How will you respond?
Ah, a kindred spirit who appreciates what it means to be as one with nature! I [@1A(1)]knew[@1A(0)] I was not alone in my sentiments!

Wh-What do you mean by that!? I most certainly am [@1A(1)]not[@1A(0)] afraid of heights, if that's what you're thinking! I'm perfectly comfortable with vertiginous, t-towering...h-hei... <shudder> Oh...oh...dear.
What's your quarry, friend? Mostly free rein for huntin' game 'round here. Them conjurers cleared it with the elementals and everythin'.
Gods, you're a bloody adventurer? Ain't no huntin' here for you. Your kind ain't never satisfied, no matter how much killin' you does. Now bugger off!
When in the Twelveswood, one must ever be mindful of the elementals. They suffer none who disregard their laws.
I shall personally deal with those who defile the sanctity of the forest. That is, if the elementals haven't already seen to them. Theirs is a swift and brutal justice.
In striving to realize the ideal Eorzea envisioned by Oha[@1F]Sok, we do right by elementals and men both─I have come to see this now.
So long as I draw breath, I shall give my all to ensure that peace ever reigns within the Twelveswood. I have no doubt that you will strive to do the same.

We Gridanians have a penchant for festivities you'll not find elsewhere. We hold ceremonies to praise the elementals, and other rites to give them our thanks. We even dance to appease them when they are angered.

If the annals are to be believed, there was actually a ceremony intended to [@1A(1)]arouse[@1A(0)] their anger at one time. What in the hells was the point of that, I wonder!? And who in their right minds would think to take part!?
If it were up to me, I would let you pass. But my orders are to let none through. Please go, before there's trouble.

Muaha, muahahaha! You could read all the literature in Eorzea, friend─every last treatise and tome─and still you would know nothing of [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,10012013,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,10012013,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. [@1A(1)]Nothing![@1A(0)]

But even if books [@1A(1)]could[@1A(0)] help you, you'd have no need of them. Nooo, not a single page. Ronan Kognan knows all! For the Ashcrown Consortium is his employer, and crystals his employment, muahahaha!

Yeees, my precious little beauties are hard to come by of late. Every clan and creed south of the Bloodbrine is after them, each for their own ends. You see, the fate of Eorzea is tied to the crystals, my friend.
Should the crystals die, so too shall the realm. And so we must study whatever dead crystals we can, as best we can. We must find out why their light has left them.

So bring me any [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,10012013,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,10012013,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you come across, adventurer. I shall cut them to pieces and grind them to powder, muaha! Touch them, smell them, taste them, muahahaha! I shall do whatever I must and [@1A(1)]more[@1A(0)] to discover the cause of their death! Muahahaha!
No, no, no. I've already given you the unimaginable treasure I promised. I couldn't possibly endow a single soul with [@1A(1)]two[@1A(0)] of them!

Ooone, muaha, twooo, muahaha, thr─ Huh!? What in the hells do you take me for!? There's nowhere [@1A(1)]near[@1A(0)] enough here! You'll have no [@SWITCH($E8(1),[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,1000003,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,1000003,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,1000008,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,1000008,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,1000007,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,1000007,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,1000006,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,1000006,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,1000005,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,1000005,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,1000004,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,1000004,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,8012102,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,8012102,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)])] from me for this sorry haul.
But I must have them. I [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)]! If I fail to meet my quota, the Consortium will have my godsdamned fingers!
Yeees, so brilliant! So [@1A(1)]lustrous[@1A(0)]! Errr, that is... I meant to say, these sorry specimens will barely suffice for my studies! Yeees, [@1A(1)]barely[@1A(0)]! Muahahaha!
Most curious... It seems the crystals share some bond with the moon. Yeees, the lunar phases seem to influence the flavor─errr, the rate at which the crystals lose their aspect.

Ever since the lesser moon Dalamud was stained red, it feels as though the power of the crystals is weakening. Ahhh, but I must know the truth... Bring me more. Mooore! I shall unravel this mystery! Muahahaha!
No doubt about it, the aspects of these crystals have been utterly obliterated. Muahahaha!

I've seen blindingly brilliant crystals, darkened dead crystals, and crystals with only a hint of their aspect still glimmering within. That is how I know these deadened crystals were not always so, but once shone as magnificently as any. But [@1A(1)]why[@1A(0)] has their light gone out? [@1A(1)]Why?[@1A(0)]“

<sigh> If only we had the knowledge of the crystals of Sharlayan... Though, I have heard the Archons have left there and come to Eorzea. They are pious souls who devote themselves to studying the prophesies of the Divine Chronicles. Perhaps they could shed some light on these mysteries.
Many thanks, adventurer. Yeees, many thanks indeed. These will prove invaluable to my studies. Invaluable! Muahahaha! Tore them from the corpse of a foul beast, did you?
Many of the crystals I collect are formed faaar below the earth, where aether flows in abundance. Yeees, but aether flows through living things, as well.

And so it is with us, muahahaha! Even now, as we speak, that [@IF($E9(4),svelte,strapping)] adventurer's body of yours is coursing with the stuff! Yeees, you too have an aspect! Perhaps there is even a colorless, deaspected Lalafell running about somewhere in Eorzea...
Muaha! Many, many thanks, adventurer, muahaha! Yeees, you have brought me a rare thing indeed. Muahahaha!

The Ashcrown Consortium has dealings with many peoples and tribes─beastmen among them. Yeees, we trade crystals with even the Amalj'aa and Ixal. That is how we came to learn that they, too, are attempting to solve the mystery of this deaspecting phenomenon.

They claim this Ifrit of theirs─the flame deity conjured by their vile rituals─consumes crystals. I thought perhaps the dead ones were all that remained after the foul god's feasting─crumbs after a meal. But they told me I was wrong in this.
Yeees! More! Mooore! Muahahaha! Hm? What will I do with them after my studies are complete, you ask?

Why, I shall restore their lost power, of course! Yeees, certain corners of this realm are awash with aether. You need only bury a deaspected crystal there, and what once was dead will soon be alive again! Alive, do you hear!? [@1A(1)]Aliiive![@1A(0)] Muahahaha!

Yet many will never know such joyous rebirth. My studies take their toll on the crystals, you see. It's all the [@1A(1)]probing[@1A(0)]. Often, I am left with mere fragments. Even the tiniest of these seem to interest the moogles, though. Might you know why? They're rather [@1A(1)]odd[@1A(0)], if you ask me.
Y-You should be careful, 'cause the wood c-can be a bit scary sometimes.
None is more versed in the language of flowers than I. Did you know that the lavender says, “I will give you the world, one flower at a time”?
And the carnation, “I roll about on the ground, taken with fits of laughter.” I confess, the younglings came up with that last one.
Look, look! It's an adventurer!
In my time here, more than one of my friends has gone missing. Taken by the elementals, the others say, for their sins against the wood.
Aye, it would seem this Black Shroud was not named without reason―its perils rival even its beauty, or so most think.
But me? I make their vanishing the work of the Garleans, or perhaps the Ixal. Not that it makes much matter.

It does me well to see a [@IF($E9(4),sister of the sword,fellow brother of the blade)]. Come, I will impart to you what knowledge I can, that you might avoid the wrath of the elementals during your sojourn here.
None are as versatile in battle as we gladiators. Our techniques are many, but you must make sure your choices are the right ones.
To attack an enemy, find its weaknesses. To defend against one, know its strengths. If you mean to protect your companions, you'll need a solid shield, as well.
Your sword will set you apart here. Most forestborn take up the polearm or bow, influenced by the local guilds. Now then, surely that advice was worth a few measly gil?
Come and hear what Seikfrae has to tell you, friend. I may be poor as a pauper, but playing at words with me will serve you better than playing at swords with most.
The Coliseum in Ul'dah welcomes all who wish to walk the path of the warrior. For those with strength and skill, greatness awaits.
The Gladiators' Guild will take you in as one of their own. Go there, and learn what you can.
And while you're there, tell my guildbrothers and sisters that their Seikfrae has fallen upon hard times in the forest, and to send what gil they can.
The abominations seen lurking in the Maws are nothing like even the direst of the Twelveswood's beasts.
The citizens of Gridania pay visit to Stillglade Fane more often of late, seeking reassurance in the midst of uncertainty.
They come to us with their apprehensions and fears, and we offer them such comfort as we are able.

Theirs is an affliction that does not make itself known to the eye directly, yet it is no less real than a wound of the flesh. Left untreated, it will fester and give rise to what is perhaps the greatest enemy to the souls of men: despair.
The watch over Gridania's airship landing has been doubled, and her defenses bolstered. Such caution serves best in times so troubled as these.
We all have a part to play, friend. Should you see anything at all out of the ordinary, get word to any crew at the landing, or a Serpent of the Twin Adder.
You are an inspiration to us all, truly.

My word is that of the great Warden, Azeyma herself, for unto me has she spoken! The way of those who honor the Twelve with purity in their hearts shall be lit by her guiding brilliance─yet upon those who harbor doubt shall she rain down cleansing fire!
There is talk of adapting our aetherial technologies for martial use. Some think it could aid us in our battles against the Ixal and Garleans. I, however, find the mere thought troubling.
Have you heard of the magical tree stump within the Twelveswood? One need only place a broken item upon it─be it toy, tool, or weapon─and it will be mended shortly after.
It is the work of the moogles, who speak to the elementals within. Or so the Gridanians would have you believe.
A marauder such as yourself could do well here. I'm an axeman myself. In fact, I'll let you in on a little secret...
With some decent gear and a little skill, you can be the core of any battle group. Unlike too many others, we marauders are tough enough to take a beating from the enemy and stay on our feet.
But you must take care never to harm an elemental. If the bloody things even exist, that is.
The forest isn't kind to us. You need open space to make an axe sing, not trees closing in on all sides.
I suggest you make for Limsa Lominsa. The sight of one of her brine-soaked brutes in full swing is all the proof you'll need that you've gone to the right place.
The Marauders' Guild has set up shop there as well, aboard a docked vessel called the Astalicia. But you didn't hear none of that from me, savvy?
It's no easy trek, mind you. You could do worse than to put in at Ul'dah along the way.
When my life, such as it is, comes to an end, I pray the Twelve let it be here in Hyrstmill.

Me younglin's keep yatterin' on at me about how safe Gridania is, and beggin' me to move there. Even went and squeezed me out some grandchildren, the sly buggers. But this is me home, and not even an army of those birdmen could force me to leave.
I've made my living as a cobbler, but not for love of shoes. I just love feet. Tell me true, is there any beauty in this world greater than that of a woman's foot?
Aye, I've shoed chocobos. Hells, I could shoe a flubbering flan if I had a mind to. But a woman's foot... Gods, give me a woman's foot!
I've been listening to these damn trees for more summers than you've seen. No one else can make sense of them, which I suppose is why they suffer me to stay.

I always wanted to hear the elementals in steel and iron and bronze─[@1A(1)]metals[@1A(0)], you know? Maybe earn myself a ride on one of them fancy Garlean airships. But nothing ever seems to work out the way we plan it.

Ah, but to be able to commune with rock and stone─now [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] would be something. Mayhap I could have myself a nice little heart-to-heart with Dalamud up above. You know, get his perspective on matters Eorzean. He must have a fine view from up there.

Have you heard the rumors, adventurer? It's said all manner of fiendish beasts are lurking about the Thousand Maws of Toto-Rak in the Twelveswood. Perrrhaps that is why the forest is ill at ease of late.

Worry not. The elementals will protect us from all evils─Garlean or otherwise. Should the gods abandon us and the elementals suffer defeat, however... Save your worry for [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] day, friend.

Solicitation and all other activities deemed a public nuisance are prohibited within the landing grounds. We ask that you promptly report any infractions to the landing crew or Serpents of the Twin Adder present.
The changes in the red moon have disrupted our operations greatly. We apologize for any inconvenience, and ask for your patient understanding.
There have been widespread sightings of vessels believed to be imperial airships.
Should we encounter any enemy craft, I urge you to stay calm and follow the instructions of the crew.
I owe all that I am today to the captain of the Wood Wailers.
He found me in the forest one day, near death, and carried me here to safety. All of the others I was with had been slaughtered by imperials.
We mustn't let any false rumors reach the smallfolk. The evil in the Maws has all of Gridania on edge as it is. Best not to fan the flames of panic.
The Oak Atrium here is a part of Gridanian history.
The sum of the knowledge and love left us by those who came before resides within these walls. And we will see it passed to those who come after.
Upon all the powers that be, I swear that I shall know no rest until I claim Garuda's head and avenge─

...Hm!? I would thank you not to eavesdrop, adventurer! You'd do well to disregard my earlier words and heed these instead:[@CR]Those who have stained themselves with woodsin must stand before the conjurers. The city will not suffer the greenwrath of outsiders.
Why, hello therrre. And welcome to our humble inn, the Roost. I hope your stay is a memorable one.
Have you seen the wildflowers? They are awfully beautiful this time of year.
I like to bed down among them and let the elementals bring me sweet, sweet dreams.

Everyone is always [@1A(1)]sooo[@1A(0)] excited to hear I'm a spy. They assume I have a thousand tales to tell, each more amazing than the last. Bloody nonsense! Being a spy is waiting, waiting, waiting... You thought adventuring a grind? Hah! You know nothing of the word.

I-I have a confession to make. I've been growing these mushrooms day in day out, for years and, um...I'm not sure how to say this, but...they've come to seem...[@1A(1)]attractive[@1A(0)] to me. I'm not well, am I?
What business have you with the Wood Wailers? If it concerns the lesser moon Dalamud, it is the Order of the Twin Adder that you should seek.
For all other matters, know that we are sworn to serve trueborn Gridanians alone. If it is enlistment you seek, say so now or begone.
What business have you with the Wood Wailers?
Should you catch sight of an Ixali dirigible mid-flight, you are to alert the captain posthaste. Under no circumstances are you to attempt to engage them.

Nay, don't even imagine what it would feel like to throw a small stone in its general direction. The last thing we need is for the Ixal to get it inside their feathered heads to unleash the wrath of Garuda upon us.
Poachers, bandits, fugitives... We get all manner of ne'er-do-wells encroaching from beyond the trees.

The Gods' Quiver toils to keep such villains from stealing into the Twelveswood. It falls to the Wood Wailers to oust those already within. Our two groups ordinarily act in concert with the conjurers of Stillglade Fane, an arrangement born of custom and necessity both.
Yet, time-trusted though this alliance may be, it avails us naught against Garuda─neither arrows nor spells seem to have any effect upon the primal.
These skins won't do... They won't do at all! Gods, isn't there better game to be had out there?
Lost your way, have you? Surely a traveler such as yourself knows how to unfurl a map. Best start soon, else you'll take a wrong turn into trouble before long.
This magic they speak of down in Ul'dah, this “thaumaturgy”―it is not a natural thing. I make it for evil, if not pure artifice.
What of ours, you ask? Our conjury is a magic born of the elements. We do not dabble in death, nor seek power over life.
Hohoho, quite the feat, making it all the way here on your own.
And what of the eyes fixed upon you? Not those of the townspeople. I speak of the eyes that sit in no socket nor hold no light. Do you feel their cold stare, or their benevolent gaze?

We Wailers are not alone in our service to Gridania. The archers of the Quiver and the conjurers of Stillglade Fane stand alongside us. This partnership grows ever more vital in the face of the combined threat of the Empire and the Ixal.
There is strength in numbers, friend. Rushing to battle in denial of that fact is folly, be it born of bravery or rank madness.

The Carpenters' Guild cares for the city's young ones. The parents of most lack the time to attend upon offspring and duties both, while the rest simply don't have any parents, having lost them to the war―or even the wood.
But here they have the company of one another, and seem to enjoy their studies well enough. I daresay we learn as much from them as they from us.
Follow this path up its incline to reach the Lotus Gardens. You'll find it split into two areas─the residential Peasants Ward and the mercantile market dens.

For the most part, the Gardens are taken up with the homes of the forestborn. Time was naught but farmers lived there, but with the burgeoning trade to the north and south, there's more merchants and crafters now.
Aye, it's become quite a bustling little area─though whether for better or worse, I couldn't say.
The market dens are just that─Gridania's marketplace. It can be a bit confusing at first, but the den names should help you find your way about.
And more than like some fellow adventurers will be glad to share what they know.
So you've heard already, have you? Aye, it's true, the Order of the Twin Adder has established a base of command in the Lotus Gardens.
The Adders' Nest, it's called. If you wish to serve Gridania, I urge you to pay a visit.
The Heartstream is the ward where you find yourself now. It is Gridania's core, where the three gates meet.
There are workshops aplenty as well, in and amongst all the running waters and waterwheels.
You'll find the way to the Lily Hills through here as well, where Gridania's wealthiest folk live. I suggest you take a jaunt that way, should you find the time.
But know that the guards there are ever watchful, and may see fit to deny you entry.

If you mean to part with your coin, you'll find no quicker way than by taking in all the shops and stands in the market. Odds are you'll find whatever gear or goods you need. I frequent there myself between watches.
Is there anything else you care to ask?
The Order of the Twin Adder is under the leadership of Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna.

She is the very spirit of our Gridania, and the most benevolent soul in the realm. She listens to all forestborn with love and compassion, and always has the kindest of words to give in return. Through the gifts the gods have given her, she is able to hear the whispers of the elementals, and guides the nation with the benefit of their timeless wisdom.

Do you think Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna will grace us with her presence today? I joined the Order of the Twin Adder solely for the chance to gaze upon her with my own eyes, but I've yet to see her even once.

Join your strength to ours, [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)], and make the Order of the Twin Adder a force to be reckoned with! Take yourself to Adders' Nest in the Lotus Gardens and enlist in the Grand Company of Gridania today!

Greetings, friend. I am Prosperlain, officer at arms of the Gods' Quiver, and I have been charged with the keeping of records concerning the races and clans in the lands of Gridania. The records are open to the public. Should you wish to know something, you need only ask.

text_en: We Wildwood are descended from the first Elezen to settle in the deep wood. We ourselves have lived amongst the trees for nigh on nine hundred years.
We share the same tall, slender physiques as our Duskwight brethren, but are known for our sharper vision─a trait which lends itself well to our prowess with the bow.

Our clan is also known for its innovative genius. The carpentry of Gridania's immense wooden structures, the tawing and tanning techniques of the leather trade─these and more are the products of Wildwood ingenuity, handed down through the ages.
The Duskwight are cousins to us Wildwood, and the same blood of the first Elezen courses through both our veins.
We are not entirely unlike in appearance, but their kind has spent generations dwelling in the darkness of the caves, which has served to create rift enough between our ways of life.

Mind you, I bear them no ill will. I simply keep the records. And the records state that the Duskwight are generally believed to be...shall we say, unruly, and stubborn. Many turn to thievery and banditry to survive.
Those who do are seen as a disgrace to the nobility espoused by the Wildwood. Should you encounter any beyond the city's boundaries, you had best be wary.
The Miqo'te race has diverged into two clans─the Seekers of the Sun and the Keepers of the Moon. The latter is the more numerous here in Gridania.
Even so, they are few enough. Many and more care not for life in the city.
They possess large, round pupils and long, swaying tails, and I daresay that in comparison to the Seekers of the Sun, they tend to be a bit more reticent and reserved.
Time was, our own Gods' Quiver used to clash with Keepers that would hunt in the Twelveswood. But these days we deal with them friendly enough, trading what crops and hides are to be had.

text_en: The Ixal are the sworn enemies of Gridania─craven birdmen who live in the secluded canyons and valleys of the eastern reaches of Abalathia's Spine.
They oft breach the Hedge and steal into the Twelveswood, foraging for plants or hunting small game. Theirs and ours is a timeless war.

The scholars tell us that the stunted wings and coarse feathers of the Ixal are vestiges of a time when they could fly freely through the skies. But they were not content with their gift, and sought ever greater power to oppose the very winds that bore them.

They learned to build ships full of air that allow them to move in great numbers, appearing suddenly from above to attack the unwary. For the nonce, it is all we of the Gods' Quiver can do to oppose them.

The sylphs are a wee folk of the forest. They seem adorable enough at first glance, but do not be fooled. There is no small number of stories of travelers and gatherers being attacked by little greenfolk in the Twelveswood.

They are not considered an absolute enemy, as the other beast tribes are, but they do possess a morality completely alien from our own. Still, Gridania manages to maintain some exchange with them, though the lack of structure in sylph society lessens any lasting impact.
Sadly, there are times when our hand is forced by unruly sylphs, and units are sent ranging to put them down. I must confess, however, that such endeavors rarely meet with any success.
Perhaps there is some other race or clan which holds some interest for you?
Ten years past, the Empire battled a great dragon here in Mor Dhona. It was around that time that the Garleans called a halt to their war of conquest.
No one knows for sure why they chose to interrupt their march on Eorzea, but it seems likely their encounter with the dragon played a part.
The Empire's fate is deeply intertwined with this land, this much is plain. Why else would they erect such a mighty stronghold here?

That was a fine show you put on, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)]. We've managed to secure yet another victory for the high commander, and it's due in no small part to your efforts.
From the episode with the Ala Mhigan informant to the storming of Castrum Novum, our unit owes you a great deal. It won't be an easy task to repay the debt in full.
Upon receiving word that the Eorzean Alliance lives again, High Commander Flutaint met with his counterparts in the Maelstrom and the Immortal Flames and convinced them to unite in a joint offensive.
If it weren't for him, the three-nation force wouldn't exist, and each Grand Company would be taking it in turns to dash its strength against the walls of Castrum Novum.

The high commander has given us a fighting chance, and we must not squander it. Steel yourself for the coming operation, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)], and see to it you spare no preparation.
There's a favor we would ask of you. We'd be much obliged if you would impress upon your commanding officer the virtues of an alliance.

As an adventurer, you understand the importance of unity better than most. Your eyes are unclouded by national prejudice, and your every endeavor necessitates cooperation. You must see that our three nations have little chance of repelling the Empire unless we stand together.
This scarce needs be said, but the Garleans are no ordinary foes. Only a madman would think to challenge them on his own.
Word has arrived of your foray into Castrum Novum. Those who fought beside you say you cut down imperials as a reaper hews wheat.
That our cause should have so staunch an ally gives me hope. We will have need of you again, depend on it!
They say you had a hand in resurrecting the Eorzean Alliance, and that you also smoothed the way for the establishment of a three-nation force.
You've given us a precious chance at victory, and I do not mean to squander it. Let us go and show those imperial whoresons the power of a united Eorzea!
An adventurer, eh? Well, I used to be an adventurer like you, but then I...decided it was past time I settled down. But gods, I would take an arrow in the knee just to relive those days!

I used to be an adventurer like you. My journeys took me to all corners of the realm, and I beheld wonders untold. At some point during that time, I came upon a tale that claimed Mor Dhona is the center of Eorzea.
Not in the geographical sense, mind you, but in terms of aether. If aether flows through all creation like a river, then deep beneath Mor Dhona lies a great ocean of the stuff...or so it was told.
When first I heard the tale, I quickly dismissed it as claptrap. But seeing this crystalline landscape with my own eyes, I was compelled to change my stance.
If that alone doesn't convince, the Garleans have chosen this very place to erect a stronghold. That can be no coincidence, I tell you, and no good can come of it.

To confirm how long you must wait before reentering, check the Timers tab located under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)].
All items in a player's loot list will automatically be transferred to that player's inventory upon leaving [@SHEET(xtx/raidDungeon,$E8(1),26)]. Items unable to be obtained will be lost.
This being an alliance operation, you are encouraged to join forces with members of the other Grand Companies.
Rewards for mission completion will be greater for parties including representatives of all three Grand Companies.

In closing, I'm obligated to inform you that the operation will be fraught with peril. Even removing the automated defense system from the equation, Castrum Novum fair crawls with defenders. Victory will not be bought without cost.
Make ready as best you can, and once you have done so, you would do well to make ready some more. I pray for your safety and success.

You are a soldier of the [@SWITCH($E8(1),Maelstrom,,Immortal Flames)], are you not? Then I'm afraid I am not authorized to lend you my assistance. Ah, but pray do not mistake my intent─were the decision mine, I would have our organizations working in concert.
Many Twin Adders died to bring us intelligence on Castrum Novum─good men and women whose best days were yet ahead of them.
We do their sacrifice the greatest honor by succeeding in our mission to lay the lunar transmitter to waste.

With the Eorzean Alliance revived, the Grand Companies are now free to cooperate with one another. I should be glad to assist a [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)] from the [@SWITCH($E8(1),Maelstrom,,Immortal Flames)].
If you wish to know more about Castrum Novum, I suggest you speak with Flame Commander Ryder, the officer who heads the operation.
If it's information on the lunar transmitter you desire, I should be glad to assist you. Shall I proceed?
Would you like to hear information on the lunar transmitter?

Our objective is to destroy the lunar transmitter housed within Castrum Novum. In so doing, we deal a crippling blow to the imperial initiative known as Meteor. Given the perilous nature of the mission, only volunteers of proven worth shall be considered for participation.

To enter [@SHEET(xtx/raidDungeon,$E8(1),26)], you must be in a party consisting of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE(45)] or above.
Furthermore, each party member must also have fulfilled the entry requirements for one of the three “United We Stand” quests.

It would seem Castrum Novum is equipped with an advanced automated defense system. Once intruders have been detected, it will trigger after a certain delay. For their own safety, assault party operatives will be extracted via teleportation magicks at this time.
All forays into [@SHEET(xtx/raidDungeon,$E8(1),26)] are limited to [@VALUE(30)] minutes (Earth time).
Upon the conclusion of a mission, regardless of whether it ends in success or failure, our officers routinely assemble in order to deliberate the next move.

In closing, I'm obligated to inform you that the operation will be fraught with peril. Even removing the automated defense system from the equation, Castrum Novum fair crawls with defenders. Victory will not be bought without cost.
Make ready as best you can, and once you have done so, you would do well to make ready some more. I pray for your safety and success.

Do you believe in truth, justice, and the Gridanian way? Then I urge you to join your strength to ours. Present yourself at the Adders' Nest in Gridania, and make common cause with the Order of the Twin Adder.
We of Ishgard hold the Fury as foremost among the Twelve, and our faith in Her lends strength to our lance arms. What is it that lends strength to those who know no law but their own?
There are chambers in the Aurum Vale where massive crystals jut forth from the rocks. Those who have visited these chambers say they are the most beautiful things they have ever seen.
Those that have returned alive, mind you.

There's been talk of suspicious bands traveling in and out of the Aurum Vale. Add that to the rumors of eerie new monsters about the place, and it's no wonder I have trouble drifting off to sleep at night.

When I was fishing near Camp Ever Lakes, I swear on the name of the Fury herself that I saw a pair of men in pitch black armor carrying a large crate in the direction of the Aurum Vale. Don't they know that place is haunted?
'Twasn't till after the Hound waxed crimson that the Rot took both my sons.
Good boys, they were, but you won't see me shed a tear for either. Yes, it won't be long now before I'm with them again.
