The lifeblood spilled in Lord Dalamud's name shall be blessed upon His return...
Many a man and woman have given their lives to ensure the tables of Ishgard do not go without bread.
I may not stand on the front lines of battle with spear in hand, but I ensure the men and women who do, do so with full bellies.
You have arrived in the Falcon's Nest. The hamlet's residents do not take kindly to outsiders nor unbelievers. If you have business here, you had best make it quick, then take your leave.
The end is nigh, and only they who keep faith in the Fury shall know a new beginning.

A friend once asked me if I believed all creatures were born equal. In turn, I told him to look to the sky and tell me how anything living under something so great could consider itself any more significant than another. It is in [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] we are equal.
And in death also. For it shall come to us all, from the proudest of kings to the humblest of insects. Aye, as assuredly as Dalamud makes its descent.
Might you spare a moment to listen to a lay most lovely? No? Very well, then. Mayhaps another time.
Admittance to the Darkhold is restricted whilst the Holy See conducts its investigation of the area. On your way, unbeliever.
The Fury tells us no one need fear death by the dragon's maw, for those who are slain by the fell beasts are granted a place within the heavens.
Yet doubt not that I will soak my shift in poison each morning, that I might send the vile dragon who takes me to the seven hells even as I ascend. Hah hah hah!
No one man can defeat a dragon on his own, but if we stand together, the Fury will guide us to victory. Even an unbeliever may redeem himself in the eyes of the goddess thus.
Are you aware of the airship landing to the northwest, betwixt the rivers Coerthas and Swiftrun? It is a favorite target of the dragons who fly out of Dravania.

The Holy See sends many a knight to ensure the safety of the ships which use the landing, but to little avail. As a result, fewer and fewer pilots are willing to risk the trip, preferring only to stop short in Millers' Glade before continuing on east to Gridania.
The holy Knights of Ishgard will oft visit our hamlet while they patrol the region.
Here they will find succor, as will you, traveler, for we welcome all into our homes.
While the rocky soil and the high elevation are not suited to farming, the surrounding hills and dales make excellent homes for all sorts of different wildlife.
Ofttimes, I see Ishgardian nobles take their chocobos into the nearby hills to hunt fox and deer. What I would not give to have a chocobo of my own...

Dragon activity has lessened recently, leading us to believe that the creatures may be contriving something ill, hoping that we grow complacent in the meanwhile. Until we discover their motives, the Ayerie will remain off-limits to all but those authorized by the Holy See.
Would you pledge your fealty to the Fury, or would you walk the path of the unbeliever─to be cast from the heavens upon your passing, doomed to wander the seven hells for eternity?
A man must gaze not upon the eyes of a dragon.[@CR]A man must hearken not the words of a dragon.[@CR]A man must lay his hands not upon the flesh nor blood of a dragon.
The archbishop, his Holiness, declares thus, and thus is it law.
We are born of our father's seed, and raised on our mother's love, yet it is the Fury who instills our lives with purpose.
As long as we embrace that purpose, we need not fear death, for it is but one of the ways in which we may serve the goddess.
The unbeliever is not to be given succor.[@CR]The unbeliever is not to be given absolution.
Woe betide he who cowers before the lesser moon.[@CR]Woe betide he who lives in thrall to fleshly desires.
The archbishop, his Holiness, declares thus, and thus is it law.
You have no business in Hengr's Crucible. Begone!
Many an adventurer has entered the Darkhold in search of fame and riches. Far fewer have come back...
I wonder what fate Nymeia has spun for you, my friend.

The birdmen in Natalan to the east o' here have been sendin' them bastard war balloons o' theirs this way, hopin' to raid our lands. Can't keep both eyes on the sky, though...or ye'll walk into the big-gobbed beastie that's been sighted down here on the ground.

[@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)]! No disrespect intended, but ye may want to be extra careful-like when ye head out into the wilds. Been reports o' some right unnatural creature poppin' up in the region.
Keep an eye to the sky, friend. Might be ye'll spy some o' them Ixal war balloons. But take care...they might jus' spy ye back.
Birds in Natalan to the east o' here been settin' 'em off o' late.

Keep an eye to the sky, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)]. Might be ye'll spy some o' them Ixal war balloons. But take care...they might jus' spy ye back.
Birds in Natalan to the east o' here been settin' 'em off o' late.
There is something truly unnerving about the creatures brought forth by that great-mawed horror. They possess an aura most foul...
Something must be wrong with my eyes. I could swear the beasts roaming the hills here have grown larger as of late...
If you plan to continue along Thordan's March to Ishgard, be forewarned─the archbishop has closed off the city and has forbidden all but the holy knights passage through the Gates of Judgement.

Do as you will, but know that you must needs retrace each step you take. Aye, and when you do, be wary of sudden rises in the wind. It may well be the primal Garuda, guardian deity of the Ixal, come to relieve you of your life.
Even should the sky come crashing down and lay Ishgard to waste, our faith in the Fury shall live on for all eternity.
The Fury judges the souls of all those who stand before these gates. None may pass until Her voice is heard.
The water here runs clear as the hearts of the men who work these mountains. May it quench your thirst and wash your spirit clean.
But ware the foul waters of Ashpool and Banepool far to the northwest. The taint of the dragon runs deep in those lakes, making them poison to man and beast alike.
We've had more than our share of strange visitors as of late. They seem to be drawn to the aetheryte, and I don't only mean this one. My fellow Scarlet Lancers all report these ominous gatherings.
The Aurum Vale is strictly off-limits to all without the Holy See's blessing...and that includes you, unbeliever.
In my three score summers, I've seen far too many of our men leave the shire.
It is the archbishop who summons them hence, and the dragons who ensure they never return.
I know not which I loathe more deeply...
From what corner of Eorzea do you hail, traveler? The shadowy reaches of the Black Shroud? The sun-baked sands of Thanalan? Or perhaps the wind-swept shores of Vylbrand?
Yes, they all are impressive. But step into the Darkhold, and you will witness wonders unimaginable.
We have little here in Falcon's Nest but our faith.
Even the towering cliffs which surround the hamlet cannot belay those beasts who claim dominion over the skies. Nor can they stay the advance of the lesser moon.
The mountains are littered with hunters' traps, set and forgotten by poachers who would dare defy the archbishop's edicts. Ware that you not stumble into one yourself.
I had my doubts about that prophecy...but after the things I've seen, I'm inclined to start taking it a mite more seriously.

No dragon sightings today, I am afraid. But I did come across a queerly dressed bard who sung an off-key ballad foretelling such rubbish as the falling of the Heavens and the rising of bloodthirsty colossi. If you ask me, I should have sliced out his rotten tongue right then and there.
Ne'er till land consumes sun can sea bear moons,[@CR]Heavens spew crimson flame, hells seep...black dooms.[@CR]I wonder if that monster the rumors speak of is one such doom...
Ne'er till land consumes sun can sea bear moons.[@CR]Heavens spew crimson flame, hells seep black...er...[@CR]Hells seep black... Blast! I can never remember that line.
Begone, unbeliever! Not I nor my brethren shall grant your like access to this holy place.
I long to see the faces of my children back in Ishgard. Alas, the archbishop's recent sealing of the Gates of Judgement has robbed me of the means to send so much as a word to them.
I pray daily that they remain safe behind the stone walls of the cloud keep.
...Yet no matter how stout, no wall shall avail us should the lesser moon continue along its present course.
I've been given specific orders to prohibit all access to the Fesse...using all necessary force. If you value your life, unbeliever, I suggest you withdraw at once.
My brothers and I are knights of House Dzemael. The count has ordered us to stand guard over the Darkhold and prevent any unauthorized entry by persons of suspicious intent.
This includes you, adventurer. Begone, or I shall have you removed.

I am, what you might say, a different type of merchant, for I place little value in coin.[@CR]“Parley” is [@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] preferred method of trade. Perhaps one day you and I can partake in a turn or two.
I don't know if I'll be able to manage a trip all the way back to the mainland. I'm feeling sick just watching the ships bob up and down...
<yawn> What with levequests, crafting, and umpteen bazaars, I've had little time to rest. If only I had enough coin to hire someone to lend me a hand...
<snore>
What sets my dishes apart from those made by other chefs? Why, blood, sweat, and tears, of course! I make sure to add a dash of all three to each and every creation!

Why break ground on a settlement so far from the protection of the Yellowjackets? Therein lies your answer, adventurer. Good is like a lodestone for evil. It is drawn to it, for it is destined to destroy it. Keep your distance from that which is light, and one need not fear the darkness.
Hah hah! I was right! A hidden port right here in the middle of the damn cit―
Who in the seven hells are you―sneakin' up on an honest man takin' in the sights of this here fair polis!? Now make yourself scarce, afore I call me the Yellowjackets!

The assessors at the custom-house finally approved my goods for import...but not before charging a hefty fee and forcing me to hand over a third of my cargo for “further inspection.” I had heard that getting shipments through Mealvaan's Gate was difficult, but I never imagined it would be this [@1A(1)]taxing[@1A(0)].
This area is off-limits.
My business has been yielding good returns of late, and so I decided to take my family on holiday. Making up for lost time, as it were.
Work takes up much of my life, you see. Though it shames me to admit it, I've been a less than attentive father to my young daughter. Speaking of whom...you haven't seen a little girl, have you?

Oh [@1A(1)]why[@1A(0)] did Father convince me to enlist in the Maelstrom!? What was he [@1A(1)]thinking[@1A(0)]!? I've only seen nineteen summers. I don't want to die. I don't belong here. I don't belong heeere! <sob>

Oh [@1A(1)]why[@1A(0)] did Father convince me to enlist in the Maelstrom!? What was he [@1A(1)]thinking[@1A(0)]!? I've only seen nineteen summers. I don't want to die. I don't belong here. I don't belong heeere! <sob>
We adventurers wouldn't get very far without airships and chocobos, but the costs empty one's coinpurse faster than a sailor empties his tankard.
Truth be told, there're times when I wonder whether I'm paying for airship flights to go adventuring, or going adventuring to pay for airship flights. <sigh>

Beyond this point are stored countless crates containing items which could prove deadly if they were to fall into the wrong hands. Access to the warehouse is strictly off-limits to all without the Admiral's consent.
Ain't a city[@1F]state in the realm what could stand 'gainst the Lominsan fleet! Take that from a smitty who helped build every last ship in it!
One might think a city overrun with pirates could fall into chaos at any given moment, and if it were any other city, I would agree.
But this is Limsa Lominsa, and the Knights of the Barracuda have an iron grip upon her neck, ready to squeeze the moment she threatens to get out of hand.
[en]
Every morning I flood the ponds with fresh water, skim off any new greenbloom, and check the fish for gillblight...because if I didn't, we could lose everything.
They say the Twelve do the same for Eorzea's rivers and seas... Does that make me the god of this fishery, do you think?
Dunno how it is in the outlands, but if I was you, I'd watch who I was speakin' to. Not everyone's hells-bent on bein' your mate, savvy?
Congratulations, scrag! Ye've managed t' drag yerself into th' Drowning Wench.

We've everythin' an 'onest-lookin' [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)] like yerself might need t' make a livin' in this rat-infested 'ole. An' if ye're jus' lookin' t' forget the fact ye're livin' in a rat-infested 'ole, well, we got somethin' fer that an' all.

Most o' me patrons be tight-lipped bastards, but a flagon or twelve o' me cheapest ale, and they'll tell ye everythin' from their secret 'untin' grounds t' th' color o' their ol' lady's unmentionables.
If ye've time enough to loose yer tongue, spend it scourin' the caves instead. Show me Mistbeard's treasure, [@1A(1)]then[@1A(0)] I'll be all ears.
The Kraken's Arms'll appraise any treasures brought out o' Shposhae, and see the fine ones to market for a handsome price.
I am not allowed to let anyone pass without the permission of the Admiral herself. Move along.
I reckon th' Astalicia's got 'erself a rat problem...an' I'm starin' one in its beady eyes right now.
Us Salthounds eat vermin like ye fer dinner, so if ye ever see the Rusty Claw flyin' 'er jet-black flags, ye'd best turn yer rat tail and start runnin'.

Ain't nothing like a cool breeze off the open sea to help set a man to slumber─which is why there ain't no better place to catch a few winks than right here, see? 'Course, if ol' Syntberk ever caught me dozing, he'd sling me in the drink afore ye could blink, but that's one of the benefits of being a Lalafell! I could be sleeping right at his feet and the oaf'd never even know I was there!

Most men here'll tell you there's nothing like fishing the Deep. Once you've sailed past where you can't see the shore no more, the bottom drops off so steep, it's like the sea herself's turned to pitch. Heard a puller once say he tied a thousand yalms of rope to his anchor, but ne'er did it touch the sand. That be the true abyss―Sahagin territory.

Should the imperials breach the city's defenses, I'd wager the Drowning Wench would be a safe place to take refuge. But even a tavern full of adventurers won't be able to do much about it if Dalamud comes down...
I should familiarize myself with my escape routes. So...the aetheryte is just beyond those stairs... And the Drowning Wench is next to the weapon store...
You heard of my sister? Private B'nmanbi Ena, Thalassocratic Navy First Squadron, Fifth Levy Infantry, Seal Rock Provisional Unit.

There once was a time her unit was the most talked about in town. What I wouldn't have given to be out there with her! Floating islands, hidden treasure, giant sea serpents... What more could a marine ask for!?

Well would ye look at that, laddies―another fearless adventurer wanders into the forge. Ye like playin' Knights 'n' Dragons with the other kiddies, eh? We can play if ye like. Just let me warm me poker first. Gahahahaha!

Or maybe ye thinks ye got iron in yer veins? Maybe ye thinks ye can hammer life into lifeless steel? Maybe ye thinks ye can build a whole ship with yer own two hands. Hah! And maybe I thinks the Navigator'll invite me down to her bedchamber for a night o' poundin' the anvil!

Ye thinks ye got iron in yer veins? Ye thinks ye can hammer life into lifeless steel? Ye thinks ye can build a whole ship with yer own two hands. Hah! And I thinks it may be the Navigator'll invite me down to her bedchamber for a night o' poundin' the anvil!
Ye'll keep yer 'ands off the crops if ye know what be good fer ye.
We lose enough o' th' 'arvest t' tempests, insects, kobolds, Sahagin, and the occasional pirate raid to let each an' ev'ry passin' 'venturer fill [@IF($E9(4),'er,'is)] belly with our bounty.

Ain't naught sweeter than the smell of ripe dodo dung on a [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),clear night,sunny morning)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),sunny afternoon,clear night)])]─or a cloudy one, for that matter. 'Tis what makes our crops the most sought-after in the land.
Why, our produce even lines the larder shelves of the world-renowned Bismarck. The chefs themselves will oft frequent the Stead to select their own vegetables.
You blind, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]!?
Talk to me again while I'm swinging my axe, and I may just lop off your head!
Buburoon so hungry... Pirates swinging slicies, pirates snatching sparklies, pirates forgetting tasties...
Dalamud keeps on growin', but I ain't seen the 'Cudas lift a finger to stop it!

The beastmen keep sendin' raiders, same as always, and now they say a giant monster's turned up, and all. It's been scarin' the breeches off travelers! How's a person s'posed to focus on spottin' sparklies with all this goin' on!?
No. Time. For. Talk. Must. Concentrate. On. Work.
The custom-house and their tariffs are bleeding me dry... My wife tells me to lodge an official complaint, but I know that will only make things worse... What should I do?
You've come here after talking to Hasthwab, too, yes? Aye, all have.

It may be the Bloody Executioners have no interest in Mistbeard's treasure, though it makes no matter either way. We Sanguine Sirens will find it first. And if they should beat us to it? Why, we'll just beat [@1A(1)]them[@1A(0)] and take it! Hahaha!

Once-timid beasts have grown bold, assaulting travelers without provocation. The beast tribes' raids encroach ever deeper into city[@1F]state territory while men claiming to be holy Archons defile the sanctity of our aetheryte camps by preaching of impending doom. There are even rumors of silver-clad imperial knights lurking about the island.
Now I am certain the balance between man and nature has been disturbed, and it is all due to that ever-growing canker in the sky─Dalamud, our [@1A(1)]once[@1A(0)] lesser moon.
The denizens of the wilds have grown violent, making journeys for lonely weavers such as you and me something of an ordeal.

Without coin to hire escorts or purchase unguents, we are left with little choice but to remain behind the protective walls of the city. However, we are not powerless. There are many who would pay handsomely for our clothcrafting skills.
And the best way to locate them is through levequests. If you haven't already, I suggest you speak with the man in the back about offering your services to someone in need.

Not enough bells in the day for all the levequests? I know how you feel. In a port city, a weaver's talents will always be in high demand, so long as there are ropes to be spun and sails to be mended.
However, if you wish to expand your skills beyond simple repairs, then may I suggest you consider a journey to the Weavers' Guild in the desert city of Ul'dah?
A ferry to the mainland leaves regularly from Limsa's docks. Once you have landed on Aldenard, your final destination is only a short walk to the east.
Welcome, connoisseur, to the world-famous Bismarck!
I see that fear of the lesser moon falling from the sky hasn't kept you from our fine establishment. Might I interest you in one of our moonlight specials?
Limsa Lominsa must constantly deal with threats from without, as well as from within.

While ridding our waters of the Sahagin is―and always will be―our number one priority, we cannot ignore the gangs of pirates infesting the city and preying on her honest citizens. Until they can be brought under control, I'd suggest you watch your back when walking the streets, or you just may find a knife in it.
Chichiroon see the sea! Waves go up and down and up and down and up an― Urglg... Chichiroon close eyes now...
Seen the two beacons lighting the waters off Gods' Grip? Llymlaen's Ring and Oschon's Torch, they're called, and they're both maintained by candlekeeps sent from this very guild.
Trouble is, not many pullers'll volunteer for the job since the Sahagin started raiding the shores of La Noscea. Can't say as I blame them, either.

Last time I complained to me wife 'bout how much work I had here at the forges, she said I was welcome t' come home and rear our four kids instead. As ye can see, I was wiser 'n t' take her up on her generous offer!
Oh, how I long to be rid of this place... One more day wading through alleyways knee-deep in rotting fish entrails and I may just jump in the sea and start swimming.
Greetings there, my friend! I have everything I need for my forthcoming sea voyage! Have you everything for yours?

Or perhaps you crave a different sort of adventure from the sea than merely travel? If so, then might I be so bold as to direct you to the Coral Tower? There you will find the headquarters of the Knights of the Barracuda─the thalassocracy's standing navy. Join their ranks and experience the thrill of battle as you had never thought possible! That is, if they accept you, of course.
Ofttimes, Laniaitte won't answer when called upon. You don't think she's sleeping now, do you?
You 'ave quarrel with any o' the Astalicia's patrons, you take it outside.
We may be pirates, but we ain't uncivilized, and that means we don't tolerate any bloodlettin' 'ere in the 'all.
Keep that in mind, outsider.

Not a day goes by without at least one vessel attempting to smuggle in some sort of contraband, whether it be illegal herbs, outlawed weapons, or forbidden tomes. It is the duty of the custom-house not only to locate and confiscate those items, but to see to their proper disposal as well.
Once the internal assessors have completed their inspection and identified an item as hazardous, it falls to my team to clean up the mess.
When the seas roil, me brothers and I offer a cask of our finest rum to the Navigator. Though some say it be a waste, I'd far rather face the loss of grog than the wrath of a goddess.
And it is far more civil than what the original settlers of Aleport used to offer. Twelve be good...
As flattered as I am by your unsought attention, stranger, I have no business with you. Why not occupy yourself browsing the wares at that shop over there?
Ain't seen no Reavers or no fishbacks this far up in the mountains, but we get more'n our share o' bandits an' kobolds, that's for bloody sure.
Not a day goes by without havin' t' chase one or tother out of our vineyards or our pressin' vats...or our wizenin' cellars...
It is my task to process and dispose of any and all hazardous materials confiscated by our field assessors.
Unless you have reason to be here, might I ask you step back and allow me to concentrate?
[en]
Oh, I do hope she is alright...
Hm? Oh, I apologize. I was simply worried about a young adventurer I spoke with earlier today. I was giving her advice on what to hunt near Bearded Rock.
However, what I forgot to tell her was what to avoid. I don't believe that she would last very long if she were to accidentally invite the ire of a delinquent dodo or peeved puk.
Well met, traveler. An archer is a rare sight in this place.
Yet you look as if you still have much to learn. I could show you a few things, if you have the time. Free of charge, of course.

Let me begin with the most important of lessons─distance. To ensure your attacks are truly effective, avoid wandering too near or too far from your target. Not only will this maximize the amount of damage your arrows deal, but lessen the chance you might be injured.
And there you are. There is no need for thanks. I am just happy to pass on what little I know to those who are eager to learn.
Ah, a fellow archer! It is truly a delight to cross paths with one who shares my passion.
I would offer you advice to better your skills, but perhaps you have reached a level where the mutterings of an errant barterbow can no longer sate your appetite for new knowledge.

For one such as you, I recommend a voyage to the city of Gridania, far off to the northeast in a primeval forest known as the Black Shroud. There you will find a guild which will provide you with the knowledge you seek.
Ferries to the mainland leave regularly from the docks. The journey is a long one, so I suggest you make thorough preparations before setting off.
If you are waiting for companions, I ask that you do so outside the plaza. This area can become quite congested at times.
O merciful Llymlaen, may your winds guide my prayers safely across the endless seas and to your realm.
Increased Imperial activity to the north has prompted us to cancel all flights to Aldenard until the threat can be properly assessed.
You smell that? No, not the flowers. Something more sinister. Smells of blood, it does.
Another poor soul from Camp Bald Knoll sent to the Seventh Gate before his time, I'd say. And with the Empire drawing ever closer, he'll soon have more company.

Welcome to the Pullers' Guild...the only official Fishermen's Guild in Fisherman's Bottom. All those other guilds you see in the area? Imposters! Yes they have bait, and yes they have tackle, and yes, some of them even call themselves pullers―but just because you call yourself a fisher[@IF($E9(4),woman,man)], it don't make it so. And just because you can fish, it doesn't mean you can [@1A(1)]fish[@1A(0)].

Limsa Lominsa's a heaven for fishermen from around Eorzea...if heaven were in the sea...and let me tell you, the seas around Limsa Lominsa are quite heavenly. Whether you be catcher or farmer; baiter or monger; novice or master; Fisherman's Bottom is sure to have that which your heart desires...provided your heart desires fish.
Sometimes I stand here and pray to the Navigator, Llymlaen. And when a gentle breeze blows in off the sea, I know she's heard me and answered my prayer.

Lookin' for Shposhae, are ye? Well, ye've found it. Aye, an' I reckon I know why ye're here an' all. I've seen many an' more o' ye 'venturers o' late, an' pirates besides, all come for the selfsame thing─Mistbeard's treasure.
What's a Mistbeard? Bloody hells, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]! If ye don't be knowin' that, ye don't have no business here! Scamper on back t' th' Astalicia, an' hear it from Hasthwab.
I's just a lowly guide here at Shposhae. But ye'd do well to hearrr what I's got t' say all the same.

Too many bloody fools go divin' in headlong, soon as they reach that spot ye be standin' on. Ain't got a mind t' listen t' th' likes o' me, see─which be why they don't know what's hit 'em when they get inside.
But ye be differrrent from all them. Aye, ye're a patient soul, ain't ye? I respect that. So come, then, what'll ye know o' Shposhae?
Ohhh, it be nasty, an' no mistake. All manner o' beasts just waitin' to make a fine feast o' whatever wanders in.
No place to go mistakin' brashness for brrravery, that's for sure. Don't even [@1A(1)]think[@1A(0)] o' headin' in there on yer own, savvy?
If ye be dead set on explorin', then ye'll need a party o' mates─an' not just any ol' scrags, neither.
Ye'll need fightin' lads 'n' lasses─proper mean bastards. An' at least one o' them magi as can weave healin' magicks. A bit of everythin', an' a plan of attack t' boot.
So the noble 'venturer reveals [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] true colors! Hehehe! Aye, aye, aye, there be treasure chests within. Most think 'em to hold treasures stashed by ol' Mistbeard.

Now don't be thinkin' ye'll find no sword o' the ages in any ol' box ye happen t' stumble on. Hells, even openin' the things is a bloody chore. Every last one o' the buggers be locked up, good 'n' tight. An' where be the damned keys? Now [@1A(1)]there's[@1A(0)] the question what needs askin'.

An' it just so happens I's got the answerrr, though it ain't a happy one. They're nestlin' deep in the bellies o' the nasties roamin' about within. So if ye're plannin' on openin' the chests, ye'll need to be slayin' beasts─and then fishin' through their entrails.

What godly business has a monster got eatin' keys? Well, I's been thinkin' on that. Strikes me ol' Mistbeard might've got his crew to feed 'em to the beasties. Either that, or Mistbeard fed the keys t' his crew and then fed [@1A(1)]them[@1A(0)] t' th' beasties. Wouldn't put it past the black-hearted bastard.
Ah, 'fore I go forgettin', there ain't no one key. Bloody mess o' the things, there is─all shapes 'n' sizes.
So don't be thinkin', just 'cause ye found one, that ye can be openin' any chest ye damn well please. Ain't naught ye can do but find a chest, find a key, an' then pray to the Twelve.
Keys obtained within Shposhae can only be used on treasure chests within the same area.
Locked treasure chests can be found all over Eorzea. Keys can be obtained by defeating nearby enemies.

Ye'll see for yerself when ye go in, but the cave's teemin' with dancin' flames. Can't miss the bloody things. Always flittin' about, they are, to gods know where. But they light the place up, and make gettin' around a deal easier.

Always wondered where ye'd end up if ye followed the li'l buggers for a spell... Hells, who's t' say they ain't trying to lead ye t' some secret nook? Or failin' that, into the jaws o' whatever terror 'twas as made Mistbeard quit the place...
Any hells, that's all I's got to say on that. If ye'd know more, it'll have t' be by yer own learnin'.
[@1A(1)]Eh?[@1A(0)] Ye're havin' me on, right? Ye didn't just ask that, did ye? In earnest, like? Expectin' an answer an' all? <sigh>

Ye daft bloody sod! All that's “known” o' Mistbeard's treasure comes from rumors o' rumors 'o bleedin' rumors. Aye, there may be an old sultan's gold somewhere in that cave, but no bugger knows where.
By the by, did Hasthwab happen t' tell ye 'bout the first treasure as turned up after the huntin' craze took hold?

Poor bastard what found it weren't never the same after. When asked o' the caves, he'd just speak the same two words o'er and o'er─[@1A(1)]the depths...the depths...[@1A(0)]─an' start shudderin' 'n' murmurin' to hisself─[@1A(1)]no, no, no...[@1A(0)]

Must be like a scene from one o' the seven hells down there, though I ain't about to go 'n' see it for meself. Serpents, giant crabs, demons? Worse? Don't bloody know and don't bloody care to, neitherrr.
Hmph, suit yerrrself.

Mistbeard, Smokebeard, Shitebeard─bugger the bloody legends! If there's treasure to find, we Salthounds'll find it. We'll wine and wench our ways to early graves! The bards'll sing of our deeds for ages to come! Our ships'll sink beneath the weight of our plunder! The realm─ Wait, wait... No, never mind that last one.

You think chefs have it easy, eh? I had to scrub floors for five years before I was even allowed to touch a frying pan―and that was only to wash it. Another three years of doing that and they finally let me use the stoves. And don't even ask how many stoves I had to light and tend before I was permitted to actually [@1A(1)]cook[@1A(0)] something over one.

You hear the legend of how this city was born? Well, years ago, there was this mighty kingdom far to the south―so far, they say it would take a man half his life to sail to her shores―and it had an invincible armada of twenty score times ten unsinkable battleships. They conquered nigh on every city for a thousand leagues, and were the unchallenged masters of the sea...until, that is, an armada just as invincible as their own invaded their waters.

Both sides fought with the courage of lions and the ferocity of sharks, but the kingdom's fighters, so used to doing the attacking themselves, were unsure about how to defend against onslaughts of a similar nature. And so their fleet was nearly destroyed and their cities were completely razed. Only a small fleet of their fastest dromonds was able to escape the carnage under cover of nightfall. It pained the crews to abandon their lands, of course, but they knew flight was the only way to ensure their people lived on.

And so they sailed and they sailed, until one day a terrible storm―some say sent by Llymlaen herself―picked up the few remaining ships and tossed them down upon the rocks of La Noscea. The ships were too badly damaged to be rebuilt, though by this time the men were weary from their journey, and no longer wished to run. And so they salvaged the remnants of their ships and built a tiny settlement on the rocks. Over time that settlement grew...and transformed into the city you see here today.
Stare at me much harder and I might turn to stone. Something you want, eh?
You thinking 'cause I have an awl in my belt and lime stains on my hands that I can teach you the secrets of leatherworking? I have nothing for the likes of you, [@IF($E9(4),girl,boy)].

Fetch yourself a knife and have a go at scraping hides day and night, like I did when I was just a sprat. Then, once you've properly got your hand in, might be there's a leve or two you could manage, at a push.
Can't a man drink his ale without every damn outlander tapping him on the shoulder, asking him this and that?

You thinking 'cause I have an awl in my belt and lime stains on my hands that I can teach you the secrets of leatherworking? I have nothing for you, or the scores of other adventurers come my way this day.

<sigh> But it looks like you won't leave me be unless I give you something, so...buy your way onto the first ferry that'll take you north and east to the city of Gridania. There you might find someone who can slake that stubborn thirst for knowledge of yours.
A city surrounded by the sea! What more could a fisher ask for? Well, bait, I suppose.
Me da brews ale, but he drinks more'n he makes. When he ain't sleepin', he's lookin' fer an excuse t' give me a strappin', so I spends me time out here on the beaches, searchin' fer seashells.
Bubusha says there's beaches far to the east what're so big, the people livin' on 'em ain't never seen the sea! What I wouldn't give t' see a beach that big. Think of all the shells there'd be!

Not a day goes by when we don't catch some bottom-feeding pirate attempting to worm [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] way into our ranks in the guise of an honest adventurer. Sadly for them, the greed-addled brutes fail to take our information-gathering network into account. We have extensive files on almost every soul that passes through our ports.
Why, we even know [@1A(1)]your[@1A(0)] true identity, you conniving...er...adventurer. Oh. Well...on your way, then.
Since the guilds began opening their doors to every vagrant adventurer off the street, the quality of their goods has been...questionable at best...
Some of us ain't got time t' play games with you adventurers. Now leave me be!

After the Sahagin sunk the last ferry, sending her passengers and crew to the bottom of the abyss, the Admiral ordered that each line be closed until the Knights of the Barracuda could guarantee the safety of the seas. Now that they have guaranteed us that safety, the ferry lines are open once again.
A busy chef often has little time to eat... There are even times I become so hungry, I catch myself drooling over my own dishes! <slurp> Oh, now look at all the spittle on my hand!
There was a time I couldn't stand this stinking city and its equally odorous inhabitants, but lately, with the Sahagin attacks increasing in frequency, there has never been a dull moment!

Ah, but an adventurer of your...type...would have little interest in such matters. Perhaps you should simply retire to your bed, where you can dream about valiantly slaying fanged ferrets with pointy sticks.

Or if you are feeling especially brave this [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),evening,morning)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),afternoon,evening)])], you might try your hand at the real thing. There is a gate to the east leading to the La Noscean fields. You will find more than enough rodents gallivanting about there to test your prowess with...that unsightly excuse for a weapon.
<sniff> <sniff> Why, your soul bears the mark of a thaumaturge―a rarity here in this primitive town. Many days and nights have passed since last I encountered one of my own.

Yet, I sense a lack of focus...a lack of polish. You still wander aimlessly through the darkened labyrinth of the art. And so I shall bestow upon you a priceless morsel of advice─take care not to drown in illusions of power you are yet to possess. Knowing your limits is key to survival on the battlefield.

Return to me when you have had sufficient time to ponder the truth of my words. If from them you have gleaned so much as might lead your aimless soul into the light, then―and only then―shall I reveal more unto you.
Well, it would seem you have matured into quite a thaumaturge. Yet...I still perceive a trace of your old lack of focus. Even now, the aether flows but erratically through your veins.
What do your brothers at the Arrzaneth Ossuary have to say of this? Or perhaps you are of the Milvaneth Sacrarium?
You belong to neither!? Well that explains it! Bereft of such guidance, it is truly miraculous that you have not lost yourself entirely in the ineffable warrens of your mind.
I would highly recommend traveling to the desert city of Ul'dah and joining the Thaumaturges' Guild...before your soul is lost for good!
You would do well to avoid the ship known as the Astalicia. It is a rotten den of miscreants and rabble-rousers, hells-bent on thwarting everything the Barracudas try to achieve.
They prey on ignorant adventurers and use them to obtain that which they want, tossing away those who are no longer of use.
Damned adventurer... Got me swabbin' the deck for the next three moons.

'Twas simple. Toss a scrag over the side, he makes it back up the hull, me purse's a little heavier. But no... Bugger didn't even make it halfway t' th' ship. How was I t' know we was in shark waters?

If you're looking to stimulate your palate with something more refined than the standard Lominsan fare of blackened merbeast and watery ale, you'll be pleased to know that the world-famous Bismarck is but a moment away.

Not another step! [@CR]Ah, I seem to have mistaken you for one of this city's overenthusiastic guards. The so-called Knights of the Barracuda have been harassing me day and night, simply because I was unlucky enough to be caught up in an assault on a cargo ship bringing goods to the island.

Alright, “caught up” might not be the most accurate description...but I was under the impression that the Barracudas―being of a recently piratical persuasion―wouldn't mind a bit of honest brigandry, if only for the good of the thalassocracy's economy.
Does anyone truly believe that Limsa Lominsa grew to its current size on the export of rotten fish and lemming charms?
Leave me to my drink. I am in no mood t―[@CR]You! Though faint, I sense the unmistakable residue of magicks on your soul. Did the elders from the Stillglade Fane send you?
No...they would not be foolish enough to send one so unskilled, knowing what secrets I possess.

Ah, but how it would upset them if I were to divulge the secrets I possess unto another. Hah hah! The Spinner smiles upon you today, friend, for I am about to reveal to you one of the most guarded pieces of knowledge in all the realm...

The key to living a long life as a conjurer is...avoiding the pointy end of a sword! Gah hah hah hah! And remember, that which I have taught you is certain to bring you great fortune...but only if you use the knowledge wisely. Hah hah hah!
The mark of the conjurer grows ever more prominent upon your soul, yet I sense that you still lack focus.
I would aid you myself if I could, but I am not an instructor. I am merely an outcast who left his guild for...reasons I'd rather not go into.

But perhaps you will succeed where I failed.[@CR]Very well, if you seek further training as a conjurer, travel to the Black Shroud―a sprawling forest of towering giants and hoary spirits. Deep within the ancient wood you will find the city of Gridania, and within it, the Stillglade Fane. Offer them your services and they just may accept you into their ranks.
A ferry can be taken to the Aldenard mainland. From there you will have to continue on foot, but I'm assuming the wilderness holds no fears for an adventurer such as yourself.

In exchange for this information, I ask of you only one thing: that you do not tell the guild of my whereabouts. I wish to remain here, unknown and unregarded. I trust you understand the delicacy of my position.

Now ye may be thinkin', why call a village Wineport if there ain't no sea for malms? Well, some say back in the day of the first settlers, the oceans was higher than they is now, and that over a thousand thousand turns of the sun, the water's been sucked back up by the sky, leavin' the hamlet dry as a bone.

Welcome to the Bismarck. Rather than drowning your sorrows in a flagon of lukewarm ale over at the Drowning Wench, why not dine in style? We offer only the finest dishes made with the finest ingredients. You deserve that much, do you not?

Welcome to Mealvaan's Gate. Hundreds of ships arrive at our docks every year, and to prevent the unlawful import of hazardous materials, we inspect all cargo, crew, and passengers before granting them entry into our fine city. If you arrived via a sea route, then you will have already met one of our upstanding assessors.
Our biggest problem at the moment happens to be accomodating all the frightened smallfolk seeking passage from Eorzea to...well, anywhere.
There have been reports of beastmen using the weapons of the poor men and women they've slain. Stay alert, adventurer, or the next report will be of a fishback wielding yours.
Ye 'eard the tale behind this ol' galleon?
The decks, they be stained with the blood o' more men than there be in all o' Limsa. Ain't a nook in the ship what 'asn't drunk of the red stuff...and yet she craves more withal.
You couldn't be more in the right, Sosoze. Doesn't matter whether you're a smitty or a shipwright, there's no escaping the bad blood 'twixt the 'Cudas and the pirates.
I'm sorry, Mother, Father... I don't think I have what it takes to be a chef anymore. I just want to go home!
Bilge! If the waters was truly that high when them first settlers landed on the rocks what now be Limsa, how come the city o' today ain't ten score yalms above the breakers?
I seen the way you been glarin' at the ratboys on deck. Well, let me warn you: lay a hand on 'em, and their prickly hide'll be the last thing your meaty digits ever touch.

Qiqirn have their place on a ship, as does a helmsman or a cook. Them sniffers they got can tell when trouble's brewin', and them claws o' theirs'll rip clean through a fishback's fins. That, and they make for decent fare when a ship's larder's spent. Heheheh.
When you've seen as many summers as I, past events eventually lose their weight, until what seemed like major turning points fade to little more than nostalgic bumps on life's long and winding road.
I guess what I'm trying to say is, no matter how terrible a memory, it is only as significant as you choose to make it.
The ash-rich soil of O'Ghomoro is perfect for growing the grapes we use in our famous sour red.
We just have to make sure and keep an eye out for the kobolds who call the mountain home.
Why, if it isn't the kind [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)] who fetched me this ink! One of these days I'll make it a point to remember yer name. Gah hah hah!
Have a nice rest!
Ye can come and go anytime ye please. Our beds are the softest in the land, and I guarantee ye'll sleep like a babe at [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] mother's warm teat.

Entering an inn room grants a [@COLOR(#ffff7b1a)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]resting[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] status. This indicates that you are gradually accumulating a [@1A(1)]rested bonus[@1A(0)]. This continues even while offline if you logged out from inside an inn room.
While rested, experience points earned through combat, synthesis, and gathering are increased by 50%. How rested you are is shown in green on your experience bar.
If your experience point bar is highlighted in red, then this indicates that your rested bonus will continue beyond your current level.

Rules? I've just [@1A(1)]one[@1A(0)] rule in me establishment, and that's no craftin'. Me patrons don't want to be kept up all night listenin' to you waxin' hafts, burnishin' brass, or poundin' steel.
Synthesis, repairs, and materia melding cannot be performed inside inn rooms.
Let me tell ye, though, I'd be right tickled were ye t' pick the Mizzenmast Inn as yer return destination.
It is possible to set an inn room in the Mizzenmast Inn as a secondary home point. Doing so will ensure that you are teleported there when using the Return command.
Another adventurer looking for an easy way to line [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] pockets with shiny coin, are we?
Well then, you came to the right place. Smithing's dirty work, but it'll fill your purse and your belly too, so long as you put your back into it.
You are on the first floor of the Coral Tower, the official headquarters for the Knights of the Barracuda.

The Barracudas are Limsa Lominsa's acting city garrison and are charged with the protection of her citizens...which does not include you. If you'd prefer not to sample the hospitality of our brig, I suggest you take care.
A terrible blight has taken the lives of nearly all my poor chocobos... I simply cannot rent out the remaining few for fear the sickness may strike them as well.
Any cargo a field assessor confiscates and brings back to the custom-house will then be inspected by a team of internal assessors, of which I am a member.

Ships from strange lands all across Hydaelyn find their way into our ports, often carrying items no one on Eorzea has ever laid eyes upon. I consider myself blessed to have the opportunity to hold such wonders in my hands, without ever having to leave the city.

Greetings, traveler. They call me Jainelette the Honeysong, for my melodies are said to ring as sweet as rose nectar. I am a beauty among savage beasts, but one must brave the den if she would soothe its denizens.

Another wide-eyed adventurer come to Limsa looking for fame and riches, eh? I don't know what you heard about this city before you came, but if you're not careful, Limsa will chew you up and spit you out into the sea, like it has countless others who wandered through its gates unprepared.
Welcome to us smittys' guildshop. How may I help ye?
Jojoroon carry good goods. Good Jojoroon [@1A(1)]good[@1A(0)] at carry goods. Good Jojoroon carry your goods?

Welcome to the Adventurers' Guild, traveler. There's one of these in every city[@1F]state in Eorzea, and they'll be your lifeline during your journeys throughout the realm. You may forget the face of your dear old ma, but you'd better not forget the location of your local guild.

And I'm not just talking about this one. There are hundreds of guilds in this city alone, though only a few allow adventurers to join. Last I heard, the marauders and the smitties were open to the idea of new recruits, in case you're interested.

Before rushing into anything, it's worth remembering that there are a lot of guilds you won't find here in Limsa Lominsa―like the Carpenters' Guild. You'll have to make it all the way to Gridania to find that one.
A fellow woodworker, are you? Well met! Might you have come to Limsa Lominsa to learn to be a shipwright?
I left the Carpenters' Guild in Gridania to learn shipbuilding from the city's armorers at Naldiq & Vymelli's. I never believed iron could float until I saw it with my own eyes.

Now, while I cannot deny the skill required to breathe life into lifeless steel, there are few who can manipulate that which is already alive. You have a rare talent, friend. May it bring you good fortune.

If you have not already, I suggest paying a visit to Hawkers' Alley and equipping yourself with the proper woodworking tools. Saws are not the only means a carpenter has to create [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] masterpieces.
Ah, if it isn't my fellow carpenter. I am pleased to see you have continued your training. I have mentioned you to my companions in Gridania, but they tell me you have yet to join their ranks.

There are ferries which leave regularly from the Lominsan docks. Find one which will carry you to the western coast of Aldenard. From there you must travel over land through the parched deserts of Thanalan and then finally through the ancient forest known as the Black Shroud. The city[@1F]state of Gridania lies near the Shroud's center.
Once there, seek out the Oak Atrium, a haven for all who would work wood.
Good luck and good travels, friend. May the Navigator guide you.
Greetings! Might you be in need of supplies? We stock a wide variety of ingredients from all four corners of Eorzea!

My name is Bango Zango, junior archivist with the world-renowned Brugaire Consortium. When I was littl― Er, when I was young, I dreamed of opening a store which employed only kobolds. Kobolds are quick and they have sharp minds, and they used to be friendly to us here in Limsa.

I say “used to” because in the past few years they've changed... It seems my dream will never come true... Ahem! Now, if it is an appointment you seek, I must ask that you proceed through the proper channels. You can start by checking the local guildleve counter.
Serpents, sirens, specters, stars... This stinking cesspit is swirling with unsavory scuttlebutt, I say!
Everywhere's abuzz with word of an enormous sea serpent at the moment. I swear they never stop whispering about it, yet when I raise the topic in conversation, all I get is sullen scowls.
As far as I can make out, the Lominsans seem to think it may be connected to some sort of legend. Hmph! Nothing but superstition, if you ask me!
Those meddlesome old misers at Mealvaan's Gate have made it their mission to take the secrets of the Alchemists' Guild for themselves.

Hah! Good luck, I say. Knowledge is power, and power should never be simply given away. Just think: the more people who know the secrets of our trade, the fewer opportunities we have to use those secrets to raise ourselves above the rabble!

Alchemy is a noble craft, granting its practitioners the power both to preserve life, and take it. The last thing it needs is to have its clear waters muddied by those who do not appreciate its subtleties.
Ah, my fellow alchemist. I have been meaning to ask you, have you already joined the guild?
Oh, no no no. That is not acceptable! Are you content with distilling water and extracting herbs? Do you not wish to expand your horizons?
Why hesitate? A whole new wonderful world of wondrous wonders awaits you in Ul'dah!

Hurry to the ferry docks and book yourself passage to Aldenard. Once you've landed, you need only make a short journey east to arrive at the magnificent markets of the desert rose. There, you will find Frondale's Phrontistery, where your future as an alchemist awaits!
Beyond me lie the laboratories of those assessors residing here at the custom-house. It is strictly off-limits to those not granted access.
Get yerself an eyeful o' that monster with the great big gob, did ye? They say it spits out nasties if ye stray too close. Best keep yer distance, I reckon!
Say the monsters is growing larger, do ye? Well ain't that rich! Might be 'tis you what's growing smaller, eh?

O Navigator, I am floundering in a sea of ineptitude! Make of Thy light a beacon, that I might find my way safely into the port of gustatory inspiration, there to concoct the mouth-watering recipes that will sate the appetites of my slavering clientele!
On your feet, adventurer! This is no place for napping!

<sigh> The last thing I expected I'd be doing when I enlisted with the Barracudas was babysitting adventurers...especially while my fellow knights are exploring mysterious islands and waging epic sea battles with the Serpent Reavers.
[en]
Only a pirate would permit the establishment of a pub right below the legislative offices of a city[@1F]state.

You didn't know? We're standing beneath the “Bridge,” thalassocratic headquarters and office of Limsa Lominsa's ruler, known as the Admiral―though she's no more than a pirate with a fancy title, like all her predecessors for as long as anyone can remember.
Though, this Admiral has her work cut out for her, what with the Garleans breathing down our necks and that infernal moon growing bigger and redder with each turn of the sun.
Ah! This one carries a sword! Perhaps [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] thinks [@IF($E9(4),she's,he's)] a gladiator like Kokoto the Bloodied!
Yes, yes... The blade maketh the gladiator, but a good one it maketh not.
To excel in the art of swordplay, you must watch your opponent and take advantage of his weaknesses.
And once you can prove that you have mastered my words, come back and I may tell you more. Good day!
Ah! Another mediocre adventurer with a blade in [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] hand and fire in [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] eye.
Though, I will never understand why your kind waste that fire on empty chores, when you could be using it to temper the skills that would rescue you from your mediocrity.

How, you ask? Why, by joining the Gladiators' Guild, of course! They will sharpen your reflexes, hone your senses, strengthen your body, and feed your mind. The Coliseum will change your life; will make you a [@IF($E9(4),warrior,man)]!
Head to the docks, find a ferry, and begin your journey to Ul'dah! You will not regret heeding my words!

Well met. I am Chief Storm Sergeant Kurtz Nolan of the Maelstrom. What brings you to this gods-awful place? And don't tell me it's for the scenery. The wind-swept stones and spindly trees here are no different from the ones in Skull Valley.

I, myself, have been assigned watch over the U'Ghamaro Mines located just to the northeast of this camp. A nasty place, if you ask me; overrun with those filthy kobolds and their terrible machines. Take care if your travels take you in that direction.

A pleasure to lay eyes, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)]. I am Chief Storm Sergeant Kurtz Nolan. If you do not mind me asking, what brings you to this gods-awful place? I somehow doubt it's for the scenery. The wind-swept stones and spindly trees here are no different from the ones in Skull Valley.

I, myself, have been assigned watch over the U'Ghamaro Mines located just to the northeast of this camp. A nasty place, if you ask me; overrun with those filthy kobolds and their terrible machines. Take care if your travels take you in that direction.
I have never been so insulted in my life!

I simply wish to have my pet lemming, Scuttles, accompany me on my trip to Ul'dah, but the cold-hearted brutes here at the custom-house have the nerve to insist I leave her behind! How dare they! Who is in charge here!?

When I requested a table with a view of the bay, the steward had the nerve to seat me next to a pair of the most hideous commoners I have ever set eyes upon―doubtless ripe from a sordid back alley near the docks! Naturally, I asked if a small [@1A(1)]consideration[@1A(0)] might persuade him to escort them from the premises...and he simply laughed and walked away! I have never been so insulted in all my life!
They say the more you learn of the arcane arts, the less you truly know... I wonder if the opposite is true as well...

To the north of La Noscea, deep in the mountains of O'Ghomoro, lives a tribe of beastmen made up of dirty little creatures known as kobolds. It is rumored they worship a terrible primal formed from mud and stone.

This primal is thought to live deep beneath the ground, and people say that his frequent fits of rage cause the tremors that plague the region. I can't imagine why the Brotherhood of the Broken Blade doesn't send a party of its best warriors to deal with the creature once and for all.

Maybe they are waiting for the Garleans to come and do it themselves. I hear the Empire is planning their own assault on the primals―or “eikons,” I think they call them―because they believe the creatures to be nothing more than lesser demons posing as false gods.
Ah, what is that I smell? The musty aroma of loam? You must be a botanist, like me!
Just as Nophica's bounty helps Her children to grow, so too does the blessing of experience help young men and women grow into noble servants of the land.

If you wish to expand your horizons, you need only look outside these stifling walls, for the whole world is a garden, her crops ripe for the harvest. Your journey awaits, my friend. This fine guild will guide you, and the leves provided will unlock the gates, but the rest...is up to you.
And may I suggest your first step be in the direction of Hawkers' Alley? There you will find a modest selection of botanical equipment, including scythes to assist you in your endeavors.
In this city of fishermen and women, it is a pleasant surprise to meet one who has chosen to toil upon the land, rather than the sea.
Perhaps it is time you visited the Botanists' Guild. There, you may learn some of the natural world's most intimate secrets.
The guild can be found in Gridania, a city encircled by the majestic trunks of the Black Shroud. You will need to secure passage on a ferry to reach it.
The journey is long, but fear not: the Matron [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] watch over you, for you are her child, and what mother forsakes her own?
A good warrior is always prepared, but I need not preach such fundamental truths to an adventurer, am I right?
There are those who may mock my routine, but when their muscles lock up on the battlefield, the last laugh shall be mine.
I've been assigned to a small trading vessel hailing from Garlemald which is due to arrive in less than five bells.

Until then, I must review assessor logs pertaining to goods recently confiscated from imperial soil. We would not have any of their unauthorized technologies falling into the hands of unscrupulous individuals...and this city has more than its share of those.
Who was I talking to, eh? Why, me plump, sweet grapes, that's who.
Ain't a farmer in the realm what don't know the good a few kind words can do her crop.

All ferry routes had been closed until the Knights of the Barracuda were successful in neutralizing the Sahagin threat. However, an official announcement was recently made deeming it safe for the lines to be reopened.
Welcome to our honest guildshop. Feel free to browse our quality wares.
I don't know yer face, which means you ain't worth more'n the mud on me boots.
Watch yer back, scrag, if ye know what's good fer ya.
Ye fixin' t' be an armorer, eh? Then ye might try speakin' with a kobold─if ye can find one what'll listen t' three words afore tryin' t' claw yer bleedin' 'ead off, that is.
Word 'as it, they be right skillful with an 'ammer an' anvil. Think o' the sweet coin ye'd make if ye could convince 'em t' part with a few o' their secrets.

Our spawnin' ponds be the biggest in all o' Eorzea. In fact, you won't see nothin' like 'em nowhere else on Vylbrand [@1A(1)]or[@1A(0)] Aldenard. 'Tis why fishers from all across th' realm drag their dinghies t' Limsa Lominsa hopin' to learn 'em our secrets.
There be some religious types what says we're interferin' with Llymlaen's work, but I ask, why would a “navigator” e'en mind?
From behind these walls can oft be heard the screamings and moanings of the innocent souls lured into eternal torment.
If you remain in Limsa long enough, perhaps one day you will be drawn in yourself... Mwahahahahaha!
I know all there is to know of Limsa's Southern Islands. Where is it you mean to go, dearrr?
Them damned shipwrights think themselves somethin' special, they do. And why? 'Cause they got a slab o' lead, nailed it to a piece o' driftwood, and coaxed the bloody thing t' float?
Hah! One o' these days I'll forge a sword that'll slice right through their rusty boats. Then maybe the 'Cudas will learn t' fear ol' Martiallais and his hammer o' the gods! Ahah hah hah!
Heard there were another starshower o'er the seas not but a few days past. Hm? Ye say ye seen one yerself?
That don't bode well... They say them as seen a starshower go missin'. Gods come down to Hydaelyn an' snatch 'em up, jus' like that. Heh, 'twas nice knowin' ye...
If I ain't mistaken, and I never am, ye've got the looks of a pugilist. Ye here t' train, mayhap?

While Limsa's got its share o' brawlers, ain't many trained proper, like. Ain't many...but me, o' course. Here's a bit of advice─always aim for the back, and don't worry none about honor. There ain't no honor in bein' dead on the sand.
When ye've added a couple more notches t' yer belt, come back an' see me. I might show ye a few moves I picked up on the docks.
Well, what do ye know, the bruiser's still standin'! Startin' t' look like ye can hold yer own in a fight.

But that don't make ye nothin' more'n the nothin' ye was before. Ye want t' live long enough in this world t' make a mark in it, ye'd best get on the next ferry east to Ul'dah an' join the Pugilists' Guild.
Start by findin' the Platinum Mirage, then speak t' one of the bouncers. They'll point ye rightwards.
Ah, that was undoubtedly the most delectable meal I have ever eaten!
If I weren't a merchant, I'd be here every day...but then again, if I were here every day, I'd need a good job to pay for my meals...and being a merchant is the best job there is!
Here to sign up for a place in the 8th Levy? Then you'd best speak with Isaudorel at the recruitment desk.

Been a lot of shady types trying to wriggle their way into our ranks of late. Ever since we caught the first one, the major has personally overseen the enlistment of all new recruits...and as a result, the number of candidates accepted has dropped off significantly. I'd wish you luck, but I'd more than likely be wasting my breath.
Here to sign up for a place in the 8th Levy? Then you'd best speak with Isaudorel at the recruitment desk.

See them unsightly ladies drinkin' th' ship dry o'er at yon table? They calls 'emselves pirates, but they ain't nothin' more'n salt wives what've added wanderin' the five seas t' their list o' dainty things fer a girl t' do.
Not that me and me Kraken brothers couldn't find [@1A(1)]some[@1A(0)] use for 'em on th' [@1A(1)]Misery[@1A(0)]! Gaaah hah hah hah!
Sea not for me, no, no. Fishbacks have big teeth, serpents―big, big teeth! Mimiroon want to go below!
The ocean breathes salty, and it be her briny whispers what give our salt ale its temper.
There ain't many men from the mainland who can stomach the brew, but then again, there ain't many [@1A(1)]men[@1A(0)] there of any sort! Heh heh heh.

Being a nation of mariners, most Lominsans would sooner ride a ferry and feel the spray of the sea on their faces than take to the skies. With you adventurers, though, it's whatever gets you to your destination the fastest.

What am I doin'? What does it look like I'm doin'? A good knight keeps his weapon cleaned and polished at all times. The salt air and sea spray gnaws away at the metal, causing parts to jam and lives to be lost. I seen many a friend fall to the treachery of his own weapon.
Think of it this way: a firearm ain't much different from a lady. Pay her attention, she'll be loyal as a starvin' hound. Rub her the wrong way, she'll blow up in yer face.
Used to be the whole coast was littered with villages and hamlets not unlike this one, but the Reavers put the torch to each and every one of them.

Every one, that is, 'cept Aleport. Where the other villages laid down their weapons and accepted their bloody fates, our men and women stood in defiance and drove the foul beasts back. The fishbacks haven't paid us a visit since.
Welcome to the Mizzenmast Inn!
Next to my forgemate, I may look smaller than a dwarven dormouse, but there ain't another woman, or man for that matter, in this city who can bear the brute force o' Pfynhaemr's poundings like I can.
Though, even after the hammering stops, my hands still buzz like I went an' stuck 'em in a hornets' nest.
[en]
Some say that adventurers have it easy, but having to live day[@1F]by[@1F]day is anything but simple. Above anything else, adventuring requires coin, and coin is not always easy to come by.
Yes, there are ways a resourceful [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)] can fill [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] purse―selling a defeated enemy's possessions, pursuing a craft, or undertaking levequests―but which is best?

As a craftswoman, I prefer to earn my living catering to the needs of others. Adventurers will always need armor, weapons, accessories, and the like, which is why I spend most of my time at the markets. You can find almost anything...in addition to a good living!
Good [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),evening,morning)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),day,evening)])], adventurer. You wouldn't happen to be a goldsmith, would you?
What a coincidence! I happen to be one myself.

Before I came to Limsa Lominsa, people warned me it might be difficult to ply my trade here in the absence of a goldsmiths' guild―but that is exactly why I wanted to come! Fewer goldsmiths means less competition, and sure enough, I've made a hefty sum of coin from levequests alone. Perhaps you should try some yourself!
Ah...many summers have passed since I first took up goldsmithing. How many, you ask? Why, that's tantamount to asking a lady her age! Let's leave it at “many”!

Anyway, I've been here long enough to tire of Limsa's ceaseless hustle and bustle. Perhaps it is time I returned to my native Ul'dah. I hear there is a new guildmaster at Eshtaime's Lapidaries whose acquaintance I should very much like to make.
You mentioned that you were a goldsmith yourself. Are you also a member of the guild?
No? That is unfortunate. You cannot excel in any trade without a hand to guide you. Perhaps a journey to Ul'dah is in your best interests, as well!
The Sanguine Sirens are nothing more than wanton wenches and feculent fishwives brandishing their blades as they beat their breasts like jilted jezebels.
Mark my words: Carvallain and his Krakens will put these vulgar vixens in their proper place!
See that over there? The Krakens and the Sirens at it again... Well, I doubt anyone's surprised. It's not as if they're the best of friends.

Still, as long as it's only words they're exchanging, I suppose Limsa'll live to see another sunrise. It's when they shut their mouths and draw their knives that people should worry. That'll be the day this city burns.
Sod off, outlander. I haven't time for the likes of you.

The next Trident approaches, and every pirate gang in the city is at its worst, scheming up ever more devious ways to take first in that godsforsaken race. It's my job to make sure they don't...by any means necessary.
The brig lies below, and trust me...you do not want to see what is inside.
Another shipment lost! If I ever get my hands on one of those dirty beasts, I'll wring its neck and throw the corpse to my hounds!
Those who believe the Sahagin pose the biggest threat to the island need to open their eyes to the [@1A(1)]real[@1A(0)] threat―those godsdamned kobolds!

Yes, yes. You find yourself in the Pullers' Guild; the Fishermen's Guild; the guild of those who cast nets and lines and then pull and pull them in to collect the delectable offerings of that spectacular, sprawling sea stretching all the way to the shimmering sky.

But, but...there are many creepy-crawlies with a taste for those selfsame tasty tasties who pose a threat to those whose only wish is to fish the wide-open waters in peace. And that is why we must stand united! What say you, fledgling fisher[@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]? Join us in our crusade to protect the seas...and grab some grub in the process!
They say that truly exceptional cuisine comes from the heart. However, I only believe that to be half true.
It also comes from the soul...
And if you happen to have neither, you can always come to the world-famous Bismarck! For truly exceptional cuisine, I mean―not a heart or soul. You'll have to look elsewhere for those.
Away with you, scrag! No one is allowed past this point!
The 'Cudas gone an' writ theirselves up another one o' them fancy legal laws they likes.
I swear there'll come a day as an honest pirate won't be able t' piss wi'out a license 'n' a measurin' jug.
All airships will remain in port until further notice. We apologize for the inconvenience.
The tradin' ship me husband's workin' on is late returnin' to harbor. That foul red light o' Dalamud has led them off course, or I'm a Sahagin's slime scrubber.
No matter how skilled your sword arm may be, such martial strength pales in the face of celestial wrath. The magnitude of the Seventh Umbral Era dwarfs us all.
Young [@IF($E9(4),lassie,laddie)] 'ere lost [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] way in the big city, now? Or maybe [@IF($E9(4),she,'e)]'s 'ere t' dine with us pirates.
Prick up yer shell-likes, ye bilge-swillin' bottom-feeder. Best take yer fineries and scurry off 'fore I call me boys and we 'ave ourselves some fun, savvy?

We are always searching for new employees, though we only accept those who exhibit a natural grasp of the arcane arts―a skill essential to the efficient examination of the many ships that frequent Limsa Lominsa.

Though it takes many years of training to become a master arcanist, those who are recognized as possessing the Gift will be invited to the guild and trained by the finest mages in Eorzea. Upon completion of that training, the adepts will be accepted into our ranks, and given a position within the custom-house.
What are ye gawpin' at, outlander? [@IF($E9(4),Ain't never seen a man swing a sledge?,Get them winkers off me forgemate's dugs, fore I renders ye black an' blue.)]
I have been charged with the distribution of guildleves.
Wench! Bring me another ale! Eh? What's that? Ye ain't a wench!
Wench! Bring me another wench!
I paid me fees in full, now why can't I see me cargo!? I got buyers waitin', and most of 'em ain't th' type what like waitin'.
I welcome all the new adventurers to Limsa Lominsa. Without their business, I'd never be able to feed my five sprats!
Look at this! You call this a vegetable? It's little more than a weed.

How am I supposed to provide my peckish patrons with perfectly poached produce when all I have to work with is this...this provender!? I may be known as a goddess in the kitchen, but I cannot work miracles!
You are well come to our restaurant and guild, [@IF($E9(4),milady,fine sir)]. Might you be interested in learning the culinary arts?

The Bismarck is renowned throughout Eorzea for its exotic cuisine, making it a popular destination for those whose travels bring them to Vylbrand. Unfortunately, we seem to suffer from a constant shortage of chefs, and are accordingly never less than willing to accommodate any who would lend a hand in our kitchens.
Look like a smart one, you do. But ye know the diff'rence 'tween a smitty an' an armorwright? How 'bout 'tween an alloy an' an ingot?
Might be a piece o' piss willin' a rock from a crag, but 'tain't easy willin' iron from out that rock, let me tell ye.
Ye thinkin' 'bout learnin' our ways, ye'll have t' become one of us. Jus' don't expect me t' hold yer hand while ye sign yer name on our ledger.

What brings you to Halfstone, adventurer? We are but a tiny colony of botanists, working the land we were given. We have little for ourselves, and even less for visitors. It is a life filled with hardships, but it is enduring those hardships that makes each day more rewarding than the last.
My husband and I became separated from our little girl! We've since been in contact with her via linkpearl, but precious good that does when she refuses to stay in one place!

We arrive at where she's supposed to be, our hearts in our mouths, only to learn she's hopped aboard another vessel and vanished over the horizon! Oh, what could've possessed us to let her keep that lifetime airship pass? The Twelve strike us down for fools!
The commodore is a very busy man. The last thing he has time for is to listen to the whinings of each and every scurvied adventurer newly washed up on shore.
That is, unless you're carrying the head of Imperial Legatus Nael van Darnus in your pack there. No? I didn't think so. Now off with you!
There must be some way to unite the pirates and persuade them to assist the Admiral in her campaign against the Sahagin... Though, if I knew what it was, I expect [@1A(1)]I'd[@1A(0)] be Admiral.

You want to stay afloat in this here city of bandits and brigands, best you learn to make an honest living. Every pirate dreams of plunder, but truth be told, there's not much to be had, what with the 'Cudas and their patrols. And even if you do lay claim to a ship's cargo, by the time your captain has taken his cut and the leavings have been divvied up however many umpteen ways amongst your shipmates, you'll be lucky to buy yourself a half-mug of salt ale and a couple of pieces of stale bread.
That's why I chose the life of a puller. I won't be living like a noble, but at least my belly'll be full...and my head still attached to my shoulders!
One bream, two breams, three breams, four...
Halt! Ain't no one waltzin' into th' Captains Ward wi'out first payin' the Barracudas' toll!
Uh...oh, an adventurer, are ye? Bah... On ye go, then. Don't need no more trouble wi' your lot than I's already got.

Being a chef on a ship can be depressing sometimes... Why, a couple of big waves and half the food you serve ends up splashed across the deck. One of these days, I hope to invent a dish so delicious, it will taste even better going down the second time.
Yes, I understand you have clients waiting, but your vessel will not be given special treatment. A field assessor will survey your cargo bay in three days; an internal assessor your cargo in five.

If you wish, you may submit a petition requesting the expedition of the assessment process, but I am legally required to inform you that any such petition would require a minimum of five days to process, and a further two days to invoke.
Some say a man o' th' sea ain't truly become a man 'til 'e 'as a ship t' call 'is own.
But I says it ain't th' ship what makes th' man―it be th' man what makes th' ship. Same goes fer ye adventurers an' yer weapons o' choice.

Over the past several moons, the Empire has shown signs of increased activity in this area, with air and ground patrols becoming ever more frequent. And now we have reports detailing the appearance of a dire-looking beast. Perhaps it would be wise to double the guard...
The Empire has begun showing signs of increased activity in this area, with air and ground patrols becoming more frequent over the past several moons.
'Tweren't all smiles 'n' handshakes when they first let you adventurers into the city. Lot o' me mates lost their jobs, and I reckon it won't be long afore I meet the same fate...
Nigh on ten years, folks been sayin' them imperials be readyin' 'emselves t' take what's left of Eorzea. Why I took up the smitty's hammer, it is. Can't well gut a Garlean wi'out a gutter, eh?
An' now it looks as the blighted hounds have finally mustered the courage to crawl out their holes and bite. Won't be long afore me blades finally get 'em a taste of imperial blood. Heh heh heh!
Now if I could only see me way into the Maelstrom... <sigh> Ain't nothin' for it but to drag these ol' legs down to that new recruitin' station they's set up in the Sailors Ward.
I used t' sail the five seas with the League o' Lost Bastards, but I packed it all in when me ma came down with the Green Rot.
I now gather herbs for the local medicine women, hopin' that while I'm at it, I might find a cure...
Heh heh heh. Bet you never been as far as Shoshoma!
Once, I walked all the way to the east coast on a clear day, and when I looked out across the sea, I caught a glimpse of Aldenard! Top that!

Journey far enough to the north, and you will find the land crawling with those terrible kobolds. It is said that they have dug caves throughout the fiery mountain of O'Ghomoro to house their metal forges...but what ever could they be making!?
'Ow's business on yer end? Be glad ye ain't standin' in these sodden boots─the seas 'ave been so bloody rough, me ship's done naught but wallow at the docks.
Not that dry land's much better. They say glowin' monsters are prowlin' the wilds, now. Navigator guide us all!
What I wouldn't give t' hook me one o' them boats an' row out 'cross th' Navigator's realm, not stoppin' till I seen what's waitin' on tother side...

Ye be a long way from Limsa, now, [@IF($E9(4),lassie,laddie)]. What business brings ye to our 'umble 'amlet? Might ye 'ave come t' fight the Reavers? Or may'ap t' seek a sip of our fine salt ale. Put 'air on yer chest, it will. And maybe grow ye a pair o' bollocks t' boot[@IF($E9(4),─or not! Gahahahahaha,)]!
I'd suggest stepping aside, stranger. My aim is not yet that good, and we wouldn't want any...accidents now, would we?
Should you see anything which might pose a threat to the camp, you are to inform one of the guards immediately.
Never understood the constant bickering back and forth 'twixt the blacksmiths and the armorers... As if one were any better than the other!
Ain't a day goes by wi'out some soap-scrubbed 'venturer come waltzin' in 'ere lookin' t' play pirates...an' by the smell o' ye, yous ain't no diff'rent.

Well then, let me give ye some sound advice, free o' charge. Find yerself a frippery, trade some pennies fer an eyepatch an' a bottle o' rum, then jump off any one of our fine cliffs into th' Rhotano. When yer bloated, crab-nibbled corpse washes up on shore, maybe th' country sprat who finds ye will tell 'is mammy 'e saw 'im a pirate.
<cough> <cough>
Oh, stop yer fussin'. I ain't got the Green Rot. This cough's been with me since I were a sprat and first went down the mines with me father.

If I did have the Rot, I wouldn't be here chattin' with you now, would I? They say there ain't no cure, and once it's grabbed hold of yer soul, there's no escape. Ye keep coughin' 'til yer lights turn t' jelly, then ye drown in yer own blood. Now, if [@1A(1)]I'm[@1A(0)] t' drown in anythin', it'll be the swill in this mug!
<cough> <cough> Carryin' the tools of a miner, are ye? Looks more like they be carryin' you.
You could bury me twenty yalms deep, I'd dig me way out before ye could blink thrice.
Thick arms and a strong back, that's what makes a miner.
Ye want to make yer livin' poundin' rock, eh? Well, ye'll have to do somethin' about that scrawny body first.
Thrash a few fishbacks, complete a few leves, then come back t' old Stephannot.
<cough> <cough>
Well, ye're finally startin' t' look halfway miner-like. Ever since I first saw ye walk into the Wench, I knew ye were diff'rent.
And now it's time I told ye about the Miners' Guild. Oh, don't look at me like ye've heard of it, 'cause if ye had, ye'd already be an initiate.
If ye want t' truly make a livin' from the land, ye need to leave this forsaken city behind and travel to Ul'dah. There ye'll find Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern. Tell 'em old Stephannot sent you.
<cough> I ain't got long in this world, but at least now I can die knowin' I pointed another young [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)] in the right direction before I went.
This is a high traffic area. I have been stationed here to ensure that no suspicious persons...or items find their way into the plaza. It is my duty to maintain the safety of all therein.
Pshhh... Shkohhh...[@CR]Has uplander no busydeals with Sweetnix? No busydeals, no tongueflaps, no excepting!
You see any suspicious types, let us know. The place has been swarming with pirates trying to sneak their way onto ships bound for Seal Rock.
