I come from a long line of armorers, back to my great-great-grandfather...though he was known more for armoring ships than men.
Since the day the Galadion and its crew first washed up on these rocks, it's been the shipwrights who've kept Limsa afloat, and forged her into a force to be reckoned with.

The city[@1F]state may be rife with rabble, but it is run by the Knights of the Barracuda. If you encounter any problems during your stay here, inform me or one of my brothers-in-arms and we shall do our best to see to your needs.
Would ye believe me if I told ye this well be filled with wine and not water? I did not think so, but it be true nonetheless.
They say we make so much sour red here in the hamlet, that it seeps down into the soil and mixes with underground lakes. Honest to gods!

Pirates in an uproar over the new Admiral? Hah! If they don't like her, then all they have to do is beat her in the next Trident. If they can't do that, then they should crawl back into their holes and keep quiet until they grow the stones to stand up to her!
The Indigo Deep has become a battlefield, the Sahagin and their primal refusing any attempts at peace.
All the more reason why the Knights of the Barracuda should make a stand and drive the accursed creatures back into the abyss.
Beyond me lie the Southern Islands, and on them the Sailors Ward and the market wards.
For every item we confiscate, there is sure to be a complaint to follow. I cannot blame most of these poor folk, though.

Since taking the Admiral's chair, our new leader has doubled the number of items on the restricted list, and more are added every day. One cannot expect every trader and ship captain to stay current on the latest amendments.
Adventuring is much like one's life―we are born alone, and it is by the hands of those we meet that our destinies take shape.

There is still much haze on the road which you have chosen, but your journey has only just begun. There will soon come a time when you shall fight alongside others, and they will come to rely on your skills.
But will you be able to play your part? Is there a trade you can truly call your own, be it that of the culinarian, armorer, or blacksmith?
Adventuring is not solely the trade of those who claim mastery of the sword or the staff. Disciples of the Hand and of the Land enjoy epic exploits all their own. Forget this not, my friend.
Why, you have the look of a fledgling lancer. How are we enjoying the salt-scoured sights of the Navigator's Veil?

This being a city of seafaring men and women, the spear―while used for fishing―is oft frowned upon as a weapon for battle. One need only spend a moment in the close confines of a ship to understand why, as a weapon's reach can all too easily become a hindrance rather than a help.

Which leaves few to teach those who [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] wish to learn the ways of the lance. I am far from a teacher, but I did train when I was younger, and I would be delighted to share with you what I know.

The foremost advantage to wielding a lance will be your ability to inflict damage on multiple enemies with a single thrust. When combined with attacks from your adventuring companions, the results can be deadly...for your opponent, that is.
Greetings. I can see by the blisters on your hands that you have spent many a day wielding the lance.
But perhaps it is time you hardened those blisters into calluses. One can train alone, but never excel, for one cannot teach oneself that which one does not know.
In the forest city of Gridania is a place where you can learn the secrets of the lance. Visit the Wailers' Barracks and join their ranks.
A ferry will take you near the city, but the remainder of your journey will be on foot. Take care not to get lost in the Black Shroud.
Adventuring is much like one's life―we are born alone, and it is by the hands of those we meet that our destinies take shape.

There is still much haze on the road which you have chosen, but your journey has only just begun. There will soon come a time when you shall fight alongside others, and they will come to rely on your skills.
You do not have the look of a warrior. Nor a mage. Are you a crafter, then? A gatherer, perhaps? Perhaps you think your rightful place is in the guild, away from the clamor of battle?

Do not let these false perceptions dissuade you from pursuing a fulfilling career. Your talents are just as welcome on the front lines as they are behind the protective walls of a city. Forget this not, my friend.
Corporal Totoruto of the Knights of the Barracuda...and what fresh hell did this ugly, [@IF($E9(4),shovel-faced cow drag herself,misshapen little turd drag himself)] up from!?
There's no place for such as you in the Tower, outlander. Now begone, 'fore I fill your backside with lead!
While I must say I've never tasted anything so sublime, there's a limit to the number of courses a woman can eat! It's been six bells since I arrived, and still no sign of dessert!
I've never seen anyone eat so much. And this with the Empire threatening to attack the city[@1F]state at any moment!
Why, I'm so frightened, I can barely keep the peas on my fork!
It's not often I find myself in Limsa Lominsa these days, what with the Sahagin raids and all, but when I do come, I never miss a chance to dine at the Bismarck.
Not only is the food outstanding, but it is a wonderful place to meet other travelers and hear tales of their exploits.
Captain Rhoswen says she'll let me choose our next target, and I've already got my eye on a pleasure boat run by the Krakens.

What? You think I'm afraid you'll reveal my plan to one of them? Ha! I'm betting that you will! The more prepared they are for us, the more bloodshed there'll be...and there ain't nothing a Sanguine Siren likes more than a boatload of bloodshed! Hahahahaha!
Whether ye be buildin' the boats or sailin' 'em, any good man knows ye'd best be payin' yer obeisances t' Llymlaen, lest ye incur the Navigator's wrath.

Welcome to Red Rooster Stead, traveler. Feel free to have a look around, but try not to worry the livestock. Too much excitement, and they all run off into the hills, and it's ol' Tutumoko that has to go and round them up.

There was a time when the farm'd stage cockfights, and pirates from all across the island would come to bet on their favorite bird. Problem was, each cockfight would end up in a pirate fight, no matter which rooster prevailed, so we put an end to the matches for the safety of me and my hands.
Brawn o'er brain, 'e says, eh?
Hm? Oh, didn't see ye there, titch.[@CR]Lookin' for the 'eaviest tackle goin', I am. Only way t' land the really big buggers―an' they don't come much bigger'n the sea serpent I'm after!
If you've any queries regarding retainers, feel free to ask.
Back before the Admiral won the Trident, she would often spend time with recruits like me, teaching us how to use our firearms. That's why I'm one of the sharpest shooters this side of Vylbrand.

I dunno what tales yer mammy told ye, but bein' a pirate ain't somethin' ye can jus' sign up fer. It be a way o' life. Reavin' and pillagin'; drinkin' and whorin'; puttin' the wind up all them posh bastards in their shiny towers and townhouses―[@1A(1)]these[@1A(0)] be the noble pastimes what'll earn ye the title, and sooner 'n ye can say “Arrr!” like as not.
And if ye be cravin' a little o' this an' that, then I might jus' be able to help ye. Ye'd be startin' from the bottom o' the bottom, mind.

Reavin' and pillagin'; drinkin' and whorin'; puttin' the wind up all them posh bastards in their shiny towers and townhouses―[@1A(1)]these[@1A(0)] be the noble pastimes what'll earn ye the title o' pirate. Heh heh heh!
Move along, move along. I've no time to chat with each and every ruffian that stops to tap me on the shoulder. Can't you see I'm busy?
The people of Wineport are wary of outsiders, and they have good reason to be. The hamlet's inland location off the Eastroad makes it an attractive target for mountain raiders seeking easy plunder.
Even regular traders like myself are met with cold stares and sidelong glances. It is best you conduct your affairs here in a timely manner and then continue on with your journey.
If you're keen on avoidin' the untimely displacement of that poxy mug from your shoulders, you'd best refrain from sullyin' the name Merlwyb when in the esteemed company of our good cap'n.
This talk of mutiny has Hyllfyr in a mood most foul.
Let me first congratulate you on making it this far into the Astalicia without losing any of your limbs. I fear, however, that your preservation may owe as much to luck as judgment.

Should you wish to entrust the retention of your extremities to something more tangible than good fortune, I suggest you limit your meanderings to the ship's main hall. Should the pull of Nymeia take you to the lower decks, not even the push of Oschon will see you out alive.
Allow me to repeat your order...again.
An eggless omelette. A bowl of three-bean soup, minus all three beans. And...er...an apple tart without the pastry case...with pears substituted for the apples.
Have I forgotten anything?
Ye likes th' fishies, do ye? They says a woman, she's like to a fish. All smelly an' scaly, wi' glassy eyes an' a mouth what won't stop waggin'.
Eh? Think I'm wrong, do ye? Might be as you never clapped eyes on me ol' lady, then! Gahahahah!
Another adventurer, eh? Ain't been no shortage of your lot in the hamlet as of late. As long as yer coin is good, we won't turn ye away.
Begone, filthy adventurer. Can't you see I'm trying to take in the scenery? Just look at the size of that moon!
[en]
The Admiral has restricted all admittance to the upper levels of the Mizzenmast.
Move along before I call for reinforcements.
The Adventurers' Guild makes some high and mighty claims about how no problem is beyond their solving─so I went ahead and requested they restore Dalamud to the way it was.
And can you guess how they responded? “A task of that magnitude must be accompanied by a sufficiently substantial reward.” Who could offer such riches after paying the tariffs imposed in this city!?
Been a fisherwoman half me life, I have. Ridden the worst o' the Indigo Deep's furies in that time, an' all. But nowt could've prepared me fer that infernal “turbulence o' the airs.”
An' it's so bloody [@1A(1)]cold[@1A(0)] up there! One bloke told me he damn near froze his knackers off on the flight from Ul'dah. Makes me glad I don't have a pair!
Eat up, my darlings...
The fatter you are, the more we can sell you for.
The immaculate symmetry of the design, the purchase of the trigger, the crack of the hammer, the aroma of sulphur, the taste of lead―a firearm has something to titillate all five senses!
Now if my supervising officer would only let me have one!
My charge is to ensure that no ill-intentioned individuals slip on board. The last thing we want is for an airship to be seized by pirates.

It's yet to happen, but I wouldn't put it past those covetous scoundrels to try. To them, I expect an airship seems like a lavish prize─but in their untutored hands, such a vessel would be more like to bear them to their swift and fiery doom than the skies.
The Southern Islands are a myriad of tiny, wind-blown rocks connected by hundreds of wooden and rope bridges.

On some of the rocks are built the homes of the city's citizens. These islands are called the Sailors Ward. Still, on other rocks, you'll find the ateliers and laboratoriums of countless different trades. These make up the market wards.
On nearly half of the Southern Islands you'll find nothing but street after street of tightly packed houses, built up, rather than out, due to the lack of space on the rocks.

You'll still find your share of sailors living in the area, but don't think that because it's named after them, that's all you'll find there. This is where most [@1A(1)]all[@1A(0)] of the city[@1F]state's laborers come home each night to eat a hot meal and sleep away their hurts before trodding off to work the next day.

Crafters and merchants, mongrels and mongers, those who cannot afford to set up shop in Hawkers' Alley all congregate in the many islands of the market wards. Once, each island housed shops and workshops of separate professions, as you can see by looking at the names of the wards.

However, the recent influx of adventurers buying up empty stalls and selling their random bits of plunder wherever they please has changed how the islands look...whether for better or worse, I cannot say.

Shhh! Not so loud! You wouldn't want our enemies to hear you now, would you? The location of Maelstrom Command must be kept a secret if we are to emerge victorious in our fight against the Garlean Empire.

If I told everyone who walked by that the Grand Company's headquarters were two streets down from the Frippers' Ward on the easternmost leg of the Southern Islands, why then, what sort of Barracuda would that make me?
Why, you're standing in it! All the important locations are right here. From the Bridge, the Admiral rules the thalassocracy. From the Coral Tower, the Knights of the Barracuda maintain the peace.
You'll also find Hawkers' Alley, the Ferry Docks, as well as several of Limsa's better-established guilds, including Naldiq & Vymelli's and Mealvaan's Gate.
But if you're looking to make some coin, well...I think you'd have a better chance behind me.

There's always Hawkers' Alley here in central Limsa Lominsa. Though, the taxes the Admiral puts on the goods sold there would make even a noble lord weep... No, those with any wits about them will see they make their purchases in the market wards. That is, if ye have the time. I've known a man to get lost in those warrens.
Is there anything else?

Helmin' the Maelstrom is none other than the indomitable Admiral Merlwyb Bloefhiswyn herself─aye, the woman that outlawed piracy an' enacted a host of other darin' policies besides. Might be as this Admiral's got naught down her britches, but she's got guts enough t' fill a whole fleet o' galleons. A leader worth followin', she is.
'Course, the pirates ain't best pleased with her more radical reforms, but the vast majority o' folk are behind her. An' now, more'n ever, is the time fer all Lominsans t' stand united.

Oh gods, am I really up to this? I enlisted in the Maelstrom thinking to don the livery with head held high...but now everyone's looking to me for reassurance! [@1A(1)]Me![@1A(0)] What have I ever done!?
The time has come for all Lominsans to unite under the banner of the Maelstrom! If you've yet to learn of our noble cause, proceed to the recruiting station at the Southern Islands without delay!

Well met. My name is Merewina, and I am traveling across the realm documenting the various characteristics of the races and clans who live in Eorzea. I one day hope to compile them all in a tome similar to the Raimdelle Codex, but of the [@1A(1)]people[@1A(0)] of Eorzea rather than the fauna. Perhaps you would enjoy listening to what I have collected so far?

text_en: Midlanders do not possess the endless stamina of the Roegadyn, nor the hawk-like eyes of the Elezen, nor the hound-like noses of the Miqo'te, nor the deer-like ears of the Lalafell, nor even the muscle-bound builds of their cousins, the Highland Hyur.
Then how, you ask, is it that they became the most prevalent race in the realm?
Why, I believe it is their creativity and craft, combined with their intrinsic ability to adapt and borrow from other cultures.
The Plainsfolk are the descendants of the Lalafell tribes who lived on the massive expanses of grasslands covering a stretch of islands far to the south of Limsa Lominsa, across the Sea of Merlthor.
While their bodies are small, their ears are markedly large and developed─a trait thought to have been once necessary to locate food, as well as detect enemies in the wide expanse of the steppe.

One of the theories as to why many of them have green hair is that the color helped them blend into the tall grasses, making them more difficult to find by avian predators such as the giant rocs known to hunt the region.

Every child has heard frightening bedtime tales of fearless, bloodthirsty vikings who would stalk the five seas in their longboats, mercilessly reaving and pillaging coastal villages until the ship holds were overflowing with plunder, and the villages with their bastards.
Several hundred years ago, this was most certainly an accurate description of the Sea Wolf clan; however, now only a fraction of those characteristics remain.
They still are recognized by their remarkable gait and girth, booming voices, and quick tempers, while many follow (albeit loosely) in the steps of their ancestors and exceed in the art of sailing.
I suppose many of them feel right at home here in Limsa Lominsa.

text_en: The kobolds are stout, mole-like creatures who live inside the fiery mountain of O'Ghomoro situated in northern Vylbrand.

Because of the way they are built, it can appear they run on four legs, which leads people to believe they are closer to animals than they are the five races. However, this could not be farther from the truth, as the kobolds are devoid of most any barbaric traits.

They are, for one, known to be extremely pious, and consider ores and metals to be the carnal manifestations of their patron deity, Titan. They also possess advanced knowledge of smelting and armoring, utilizing techniques to rival even the renowned smiths of Naldiq & Vymelli's.

In my three summers here on Vylbrand, I have yet to see one of the aquatic beasts the locals refer to as “fishbacks,” and the rumors gathered from the people of Limsa Lominsa are, well...let us say “inconclusive.”

For example, people claim they can only breathe underwater, wear armor made from shells and seaweed, have no eyelids, can survive without food for six turns of the moon, can swim faster than a two-hundred-oar galleon, have a three-sided head with a mouth on each side, and kidnap babies from fisher villages to sacrifice them to their deity, Leviathan...amongst other things.

However, one thing is known for certain─there are many former citizens of Limsa Lominsa who have, for reasons unclear, given up their lives in the thalassocracy to [@1A(1)]join[@1A(0)] the beastmen. The worst of these dissenters are known as the Serpent Reavers.
The Garleans are an enigmatic race of people from a massive empire situated to the north and east of Eorzea, and despite coming from a realm so large, remarkably little is known about them.

As few have ever seen them without their armor, rumors about their physical makeup are many, some of the more “colorful” claims being that they implant machina in their bodies to improve agility and strength, and that they possess a third eye allowing them to see in all directions at once.
Though, I would assume there is little truth to these sailors' tales...
Is there anything else?
No need t' worry, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]. We'll see ye safely across the roilin' seas.
A number of ancient-looking tomes and treatises adorn the shelf.

text_en: Penned by Lewphon of Sharlayan, master theologian and astrologist, in the Year 233 of the Sixth Astral Era, to weave together the disparate histories of the nations of Eorzea with a common thread─the thread of time.
For through its inevitable march the hours turn into Suns, and they into Moons, and they into Years. And from the Years come the Ages of Man. And ever eclipsing those is the eternity of Gods.

By the unit of a sole Sun we mean that period which lasts for the duration of four cycles of the six elemental hours─those of Ice, Water, Wind, Lightning, Fire, and Earth. And so is the Sun twenty hours and four, and so shall it ever be.
The life of a single Moon spans four cycles of eight Suns, and is thus the sum of thirty and two.
The eight deriveth from the elements six, Ice, Water, Wind, Lightning, Fire, and Earth, and the polarities two, Astral and Umbral.
The Year is made when the Moons go round the two Astral and Umbral poles, fluctuating between the six elements, and that in turn. In this, the Year can be said to be the length of twelve Moons.

The first and second Moons of the Year are the first Astral and first Umbral, and together they share an affinity with Ice. On their watch, all is frozen, and breath of life sloweth to near silence beneath.

The second Astral and second Umbral Moons come third and fourth in turn, and they are the Water of the melting Ice, and with their flowing slaketh the thirst of life again. Fifth and sixth are the third Astral and third Umbral Moons, and the Wind bloweth over the Water, carrying its heavenly boons near and far.

The fourth pairing of Astral and Umbral Moons come seven and eight, when the heavens rageth with the furies of Lightning, and sendeth them below with godly terror to test the faith of men.[@CR]The ninth and tenth Moons are the fifth Astral and Umbral, as the Lightning turns to Fire, and it charreth growing life with the colors of its flames, bleeding blade and leaf with brilliant hues of crimson and scarlet.[@CR]Year's end cometh in the eleventh and twelfth Moons, the sixth Astral and sixth Umbral, in which Earth consumes all, for out of the ground we are taken for the dust we are, and to the dust we shall return.

The wisdom of the Twelve saw fit to grant man with the cycle of years, and in turn the reverence of man bound them to his gods─the Year of the Navigator, of the Wanderer, of the Builder, of the Destroyer, of the Warden, of the Traders, of the Matron, of the Keeper, of the Fury, of the Lover, of the Scholar, and of the Spinner.
The turning of these Years twelve is a sacred thing, and together they comprise one epoch of man, by which the histories of his endeavor are measured.
The constancy and eternity of time derive from the pulse and breath of the Twelve.

And by their divine will the brilliance of the Astral Eras which see man flourish and prosper, and the shadows of the Umbral Eras which see man falter and doubt, are visited upon him in equal, and neither the greatest good nor the greatest evil may escape their purview.

Since the peace among the Twelve was broken and life was created to wage their wars, six cycles of the Eras have come to pass in keeping with the elemental order. The Sixth Umbral Era belonged to the waters, as heavy rains fell and the seas rose high, submerging and cleansing all in a great deluge. With time the waters receded, ushering in the present Sixth Astral Era, during which man has again rebuilt his halls and tilled his lands.

Naught save the ken of the Twelve themselves knoweth when the Seventh Umbral Era shall come and end our days. The sole certainty what resides within man is the selfsame as it has ever been─ours is the power to make of our Era what we might.
A cursory examination reveals that the volume is comprised of four chapters dealing with the elements and creation.

text_en: The spark of Lightning ignites when it strikes, and thus Fire is born.[@CR]The heat of Fire renders to ash all that it touches, and thus Earth is born.[@CR]The density of Earth shuns Sun and harbors cold, and thus Ice is born.[@CR]The armor of Ice melts away, and thus Water is born.[@CR]The moistness of Water mists and rises, and thus Wind is born.[@CR]The gusts and sighs of Wind gather the clouds, and thus Lightning is born.
Earth grounds Lightning.[@CR]Water erodes Earth.[@CR]Lightning boils Water.
Fire is extinguished by Wind.[@CR]Ice is melted by Fire.[@CR]Wind is obstructed by Ice.
The six elements are manifest in all things great and small, and their polarity deriveth from the Astral heavens above and the Umbral depths below.

Hello, and welcome to the Coffer & Coffin, my own humble port of call for travelers such as yourself. A favorite haunt of the folks from the Jolly Raptor, too. You'll often see their chocobo coaches putting in here.
Have you ever viewed the games from above, in the stands? Noticed the handrails, perhaps?
Placed there for safety, they were. More than one spectator has fallen to their death, what with all the jostling that goes on up there.

The Immortal Flames have been reformed, and under their banners the Ala Mhigans now have a chance to strike back at the Empire. It is true, relations between Ul'dahn and Ala Mhigan are strained, but gods grant us the tolerance to unite against a common foe.

The Immortal Flames have been reformed, and under their banners the Ala Mhigans now have a chance to strike back at the Empire. It is true, relations between Ul'dahn and Ala Mhigan are strained, but gods grant us the tolerance to unite against a common foe.
I'll get out of this bloody hellhole someday. If for no other reason than to spite all the Ul'dahns looking down their noses at us.

Did you know that Highwind Skyways owes its existence to the toy dirigible of a wealthy entrepreneur? As a matter of fact, it is after that selfsame craft─the good ship “Highwind”─that the company is named. Quite an interesting morsel of trivia, no?
Ah, but to imagine that a rich man's plaything would give rise to such a lucrative business venture! It is truly as they say: “coin begets coin.”

Have you heard? The goblins have returned from their great pilgrimage. We might all have made a fortune trading with them, but for the law passed a decade ago that forbids all beastmen from entering Ul'dah. <sigh> Being a merchant, I can't help seeing it as a missed opportunity...
Only ever worked the Nanawa Mines after joinin' the Miners' Guild─'til I heard there was good ore to be found out here. 'Twas 'cause of that that I asked to join this crew.

No matter the place, no matter the danger─if there's ore to be dug, I'll be there with pick in hand. We can't all answer the call to adventure like you. The gods've cursed me with a greedy wife and a starvin' daughter to feed.
You have come to Milvaneth Sacrarium. Here is the temple of Nald, imbuer of life. Would you care to make a donation to the faith?

With the lesser moon looming nigh, more and more people are forsaking Nald, resigned to the belief that their lives will soon be lost to them. But so long as there is life, there is cause to hope. Being an adventurer, I trust you appreciate this sentiment.
Only the great Nald, purveyor of life's currency, can bestow salvation in this dark and dismal era! We must pray! All of us as one!
Ask yourself─of which are there more in this world? Those who wear armor, or those who wear cloth?
The answer, of course, is unspeakably obvious. Yet consider it in the context of our clientele─people from every walk of life, male and female, young and old, rich and poor.
You can imagine how far our spheres of influence extend. Quite far. To every corner of Eorzea, in fact.
The walls of Ul'dah are some way off yet. You'd do well to rest here before setting out again.
As much as I might like to, I'm afraid I cannot let you by. Give it time, friend, give it time.

Mayhap you've heard how the Empire blasted a passenger vessel out of the sky? Aye, well, the incident prompted the rich folk to start insuring themselves against aerial mishaps, and at exorbitant rates.

Overnight, the thaumaturges went from swimming in coin to [@1A(1)]drowning[@1A(0)] in the bloody stuff. Leave it to those bastards to profit from a tragedy! Call it envy if you will, but something about all this strikes me as a little [@1A(1)]too[@1A(0)] convenient.
To me, there's as much thrill in parleying over a price as there is in any combat. And the folk around here are more than happy enough to oblige me. Care to try your luck?
I tell you this─there's more coin to be had in placebos than in all the alchemical agents in this damned place!
What concerns us Ul'dahns most is changing the world to suit our needs, and how we might go about it.
Not like those [@1A(1)]foreigners[@1A(0)]. They're too busy changing themselves to suit the world's needs─poor fools! Can you think of anything more pathetic?
Gathering places like this are the loam in which the seeds of business take root─and I, for one, am eager to see what sort of shoots spring forth here.
Come to look down on us like all the others, have you? Have a good laugh, perhaps? Go on, get it over with. You'll get yours someday!
We [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] persevere. Bear children, build homes, live on. Even in such desolate lands as these.
Ala Mhigo may be broken, but the spirit of her people is not.
Legend says that in the mountains of Bluefog lurks a Twelve-forsaken beast with the head of a lion, a ram, and a dragon.

There are even some who claim that it makes its lair in a cave known as Cutter's Cry. I reckon the Immortal Flames would pay a handsome reward to the man[@IF($E9(4),...or woman, mind you,,)] who brought back even one of them heads.
There is a small shrine near here, dedicated to one of the eastern gods─Thal, if I remember rightly.
Those that follow him come to pray often enough. I thought a shop here would do quite well, but they've no desire to buy from an Ala Mhigan.
I ain't no Ala Mhigan. You should say as much yourself, truth or no.
Them Ala Mhigans been flockin' into the poor quarters, over there by the Quicksand. Turned the place into a bloody breedin' ground for maladies, they have.
There was once a wayside inn on this very spot. But with the Amalj'aa summoning their foul gods, and growing ever more warlike, the region was lost and the outpost abandoned.

Aren't we frightened, you ask? Well, it's true that you can see traces of the Amalj'aa all around if you know what to look for. Hells, after a while, you can even [@1A(1)]feel[@1A(0)] them. Sets your hair on end, it does. Still, it's not like we're wholly incapable of defending ourselves. We knew the risks when we came.
New to Ul'dah? Perhaps you have yet to hear of the Syndicate. Just a small council of wealthy leaders, really, but they oversee the majority of the city's events and affairs.
Most are owners of Ul'dah's most profitable institutions─the Coliseum, the Platinum Mirage, Eshtaime's Lapidaries.
You are in a city of merchants now, friend. And here, all answer to the almighty gil.
A fledgling cook, are you? Aye, you remind me a bit of myself when I first donned the apron.

I remember the days when I had yet to learn of a culinarian's secondary tools. I was studiously stirring away for fully three moons before I even noticed they existed. You can find them for yourself at P'sonjha's culinarian shop at the Ruby Road Exchange.
What I have just told you was imparted to me on my journeys as well. I was young then, foolish and proud, and paid it no heed. Do not make the same mistake.
A talented culinarian can do very well here, catering to the rich. But truth be told, their palates are dull, and you will tire of them quickly.
To learn the widest variety of recipes, there is no place better than the Culinarians' Guild.
The masters can be strict, I grant you, but the facilities and talent to be found at the Bismarck are second to none.
The path of the culinarian leads west of here, friend─across Vesper Bay to Limsa Lominsa. You can find a ferry to take you there at the docks west of Ul'dah.
The heat... Gods, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)], the [@1A(1)]heat[@1A(0)]... I swear I feel it tenfold as much with that great red moon looming over me.

I cannot let the end find me still stuck at this posting. The Order teaches us it is our labors in this life that determine our lot. I must redouble my efforts to deceive the unsuspecting and amass greater wealth.
An Ul'dahn airship was shot down by a Garlean battle cruiser to the southwest of here. We've bolstered the watch here at Camp Black Brush.
From youth, Ul'dahns are taught to see others. Not just look at them, but truly see them for what they are.
We are unmatched as judges of character. And rightly so. Survival here means knowing who you can mark, who you should mark, and who means to mark you.
If it a tale you seek, then let me tell you whence I came.
Beyond the Sea of Clouds, rising like angry fists pointed in defiance to the heavens, lies Ablathia's Spine.

Within these cursed mountains reside my people, chosen long ago by the Twelve to guard the ancient gates of the seven hells. And from the undying flames of the pit do we forge the steel with which we hew our cities from the unrelenting rock.
I see your will continues to strengthen. For me, my journey has just begun.

For my brother, as well. His wounds were severe, but I believe, in time, he will recover fully. Until then, he has agreed to assist me in the deciphering of the chronicles. If I find anything of interest, I will be certain to let you know, my friend. Until then, godsspeed!
And what is it you are looking for today, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)]? A gift perhaps? Or a little something for yourself?
Might I inform you that the guild is waiving all delivery fees on, shall we say, [@1A(1)]generous[@1A(0)] purchases?
Well met. I am an alchemist come from Frondale's Phrontistery in Ul'dah. I've been sent to see to it no outbreaks occur among the Ala Mhigans.
Yet none here believe me when I say as much. They suppose all Ul'dahns driven by the selfish love of wealth, not the selfless love of healing.
Anything you could ever want, you'll find for sale here─though the quality might not be up to Ul'dahn standards.
Still, we have good wares, and the prices are fair enough. Most passing merchants are happy to deal with us.
A day in the mines, and only this to show for it. Well, me mum said there'd be days like this. Reckon I'll drop it on the tables at the Mirage and see what comes back.
None shall pass. Begone.
We here at Camp Black Brush hurried to the aid of the vessel set upon by the Garleans. Sadly, there were no survivors.
This workmanship is quite exquisite. They say the best pieces bring out the appraiser in us all. I believe this may be a case in point.
Heehee, the guildmaster has more than his fair share of lovers, that's no secret. They say he only employs women he means to bed. Purrr, heehee!
Nowadays, the Silver Bazaar's nothing but a refuge for Ala Mhigans.
And so what if it is? All the better, I say. They work bloody hard and barely complain. Not like [@1A(1)]Ul'dahns[@1A(0)].
You... Were you too guided here─brought, led, guided? Or...no?
You... Yes, yes, could it be?
Yes, I sense it. You are the one we seek─look, search, seek.
It is good you are safe─unhurt, well, safe. The black magic has awoken within you. Yes, yes, it has. When you learn to command it, Dozol Meloc will tell you what you must do next.
The Black Shroud─forest, wood, Shroud? What kind of place was it? You must tell me sometime. Yes, yes, you must.
The [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)] truly exists! Yes, yes, it does! [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], you must come see me again after you have gather the first four artifacts!
I understand now why my ancestor Da Gu left La Noscea. Yes, yes, I do. Seeking new things with new friends is most exciting─amazing, inspiring, exciting.
I will stay here in Thanalan a bit longer. Yes, yes, I will. I wish to see more of the Thanalan that my great-grandfather saw.
Ah, a customer. Oh, an adventurer besides, from the looks of it.
Tell me, have you an interest in textiles? A keen eye for quality warp and weft? Then, by all means, the Weavers' Guild welcomes you.

How fare your efforts to nurture a keen eye for quality warp and weft? Remember always that our charge is to better the appearance of folk Eorzea over. For in so doing, we better their sense of self-worth.
You're not supposed to be back here, you kn─ Hey! Where do you think you're looking!? Gods, you're just as bad as [@IF($E9(4),the men,all the others)], you filthy [@IF($E9(4),hussy,devil)]!
I am not an object to be ogled! I am a performer. An artist!
Shall you buy a gem?
Wouldn't you prefer a good piece of chert?
Such brilliance. Such beauty. Such perfection.
I know now why you cry.
That garb is agreeable! That garb is agreeable!
Take medicine with meals.
No more than thrice daily.
Side effects may include death.
Reading... Moon phase... Star lines... Guardian favor...
A moment, please. A moment, please.

<mumble>
A moon made massive and a mystery monster make for an era both exciting and enthralling.

One could easily distinguish a Sunsilk patron even if they were to disrobe. There's just something [@1A(1)]different[@1A(0)] about them─elevated, refined, [@1A(1)]better[@1A(0)]. They even [@1A(1)]smell[@1A(0)] divine!

Thank you for using Highwind Skyways. We wish you a pleasant voyage!
One of the thaumaturges in there once told me to come to him in my darkest hour. For a price, he'd exact whatever revenge I saw fit, he said. Tempting, no?
Eshtaime's Lapidaries welcomes you. Here we cater to the jeweling needs of Eorzea's opulent.
Do not hesitate to let me know if there is anything I might help you with.

Please, do not bother me with your idiotic blathering. I need to concentrate! I am working on my latest theory. I should not even have spared the time to tell you that just now. Or [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)], just [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)]! Leave me!

I confess, I believe great things lie in store for you. A curious thing, considering how painfully stupid you are.
If and when your name does become known throughout the realm, be sure to tell everyone that it was I who taught you everything you know!
Time to put as much distance as possible between myself and the Mirage before they come asking for their gil. Take care, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! And do try to read me. Right, then!

Master Mutamix belongs to a fraternity of goblin scholars known as the [@1A(1)]Illuminati[@1A(0)], but over time found himself at odds with their secretive ways. Ferry's the only way you're gettin' to Limsa, [@IF($E9(4),lassie,laddie)]. Though I s'pose you might try an' swim it. Hah hah!
You one of them wandering types? Been out slaying dragons and saving maidens and all that faerie tale shite? [@IF($E9(4),Woman's,Man's)] got to earn coin for [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] ale somehow.
Come to think, why not cast your lot in with the Immortal Flames? That's Ul'dah's Grand Company, case you weren't aware. I heard it said they've set up a base over in the Dunes.
Used to be we'd have all manner of beast shipped down from the mountains to the north. Trade with Ishgard ain't what it was, though.
I'd like nothing more than to see things go back to the way they were, but it seems less likely with each passing moon.
What do you think? It's beautiful, is it not? Sunsilk Tapestries certainly deserves its reputation.
Arrzaneth Ossuary is the temple of Thal.

His aspect is that of death and darkness, that which we shall all come to know in time. Many of the poor and destitute worship here. For it is they who seek a better place in death than they knew in life.
Be welcome to the Platinum Mirage! No doubt you've heard of our gambling halls, but our contribution to the economy of Ul'dah does not stop there.
Gil from all over Eorzea makes its way here. We lend that gil to others, and in doing so earn even more for ourselves.
The heat worsens with each passing year. Some say it is the burning fury of men, reflected in the heavens.
Has our fury sundered the very heavens? The red moon burns with hatred, poised to punish the land with fire and ruin. We have brought this violent purification upon ourselves...
Aye, they let criminals take to the bloodsands now an' again─them what's caught murderin', thievin', piratin', an' whatnot.
Ain't winnin' what gets 'em turned loose, though─'least not directly. Fight's got to turn enough profit for them to buy their freedom, see. And that ain't no modest sum.
You stand before Ul'dah, traveler. May Nald'thal smile upon you during your stay.
<sigh> The world as we know it may be about to end, yet here I am spouting the same tired old line, day in, day out...
Ul'dah welcomes you, traveler. Enter, and discover what fortune awaits you!
Journey elsewhere, adventurer. This way is not open to you.
These are the famed ferry docks of Vesper Bay─the only place you'll find safe passage to Limsa. Of course, these ferries ain't free...usually.
Tell me, how does a girl like me make her way into high society? Oh, just imagine it, the dresses, the banquets, the wines!
If only I could catch the eye of one of those Syndicate fellows. Or better yet, a young bachelor in the royal family!
The realm of Thal is a paradise of Man─unplagued by decay and disease, free of pain and the pangs of hunger, unmatched and eternal in its beauties.
In recent moons, even they who ordinarily pay their dues to Nald have come to give offering to Thal. That is well, that is well.
The chief engineer is known to appear at the boarding lounge on occasion to oversee airship safety inspections.
In the event that he is present, we kindly ask that patrons refrain from such conduct as would impede his work.
Lost your way? I'd not think there'd be much to bring an adventurer out here.
I have need of rubies. [@1A(1)]Rubies[@1A(0)], you lackwit! Red as blood! Peridots!? No, I'll not settle for peridots! Green is as dead as your head is dense!

<sigh> Gods... My apologies, [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)], placing orders by linkpearl can be...stressful. I am Roarich. Roarich of Ashgana's Exporters, if it please you. If your business is not pressing, might it not wait until later?
Spices! Get your spices here! Cinnamon and laurel! Paprika and marjoram! Dragon pepper and more! Spiiiiiices here!

Oh, [@1A(1)]welcome[@1A(0)], dear. Are you from the Seventy-seven Caravans? Well then, I'm afraid we have no [@1A(1)]business[@1A(0)]. I'm authorized to deal [@1A(1)]only[@1A(0)] with Caravan members.
Next moon on the bloodsands! Franz the Fair-faced versus Georg Galleongut!
A match the bards will sing of! Pay now for the entire seat─though ye'll only need the [@1A(1)]eeedge[@1A(0)]!
Ul'dah greets you as a friend. Pass, and may victory attend you beyond these gates.

I make frequent use of airships for business purposes, and my other half has taken to accompanying me on every single trip. While I negotiate deals, she passes the time shopping and doing whatever else takes her fancy.

Now, I'm grateful for her presence, truly I am...but it's costing me a small fortune to keep her entertained. Oh, if only she'd consent to remain at home upon occasion! <sigh> I've been meaning to broach the subject, but gods know I can't bear to see her disappointed...
Such luster, such luminosity... Truly, this is a tangible token of the Twelve![@CR]...Hm? You wish a word with me, adventurer?
I am Havak Alvak, a self-styled student of sundry subjects. Though I am best known, perhaps, for putting pen to parchment for a popular paper, [@1A(1)]The Mythril Eye[@1A(0)].
So you too were seduced by the scintillation of this striking stone?
I hastened here as soon as the rumor reached me that the base of Nald's statue had suddenly started to sparkle.
It is a sacred stone, touched by the Twelve, and more of its like lie across the land. Legend says that their brilliance will brighten when disaster draws nigh.
Suffice to say, I am delighted to discover that this was no mere myth!
You desire a discourse on deities? If you possess the patience, I should be overjoyed to oblige. Shall I launch into my lecture?
Ahem! As the empyrean entities of Eorzea, the Twelve receive reverence from the realm's residents. Allow me to acquaint you with all.
Halone, the Fury. This goddess governs glaciers while contemplating conflict. She is especially esteemed in Ishgard, where people pray for Her well wishes in war.

Menphina, the Lover. Monitoring multiple moons─well, two─this divinity is dotingly disposed. She is the preferred personage of the Keepers of the Moon. If your love life is lacking, you might consider calling on Her cooperation.

Thaliak, the Scholar. This god rules rivers and reads ravenously─or so one would assume. He is held highly by the Sharlayans and those to whom enhanced erudition is the object of every endeavor, yours truly included.

Nymeia, the Spinner. This deity determines destinies while supervising the stellar sphere. In directing the dance of the stars, She weaves the fates of men. Those given to gambling are oft heard petitioning Her partiality.

Llymlaen, the Navigator. Warily watching the waves, She succors sailors and facilitates fishing. Not surprisingly, She is the guardian goddess of Limsa Lominsa, where the tavern-goers toast Her twelve times daily─though that may merely be a means to defend their drinking.

Oschon, the Wanderer. He presides over peaks and is patron to travelers and transients. People pray for His protection prior to peregrinating. It is said He used to indulge the inhabitants of the immemorial city of Nym.

Byregot, the Builder. As His style suggests, this divinity is an ardent advocate of architecture and the arts. Small wonder, then, that those who carve a career out of crafting have a high opinion of Him.
Rhalgr, the Destroyer. This deity deals in destruction, and was widely worshiped in Ala Mhigo before the fall. Symbolizing strength, He breaks all barriers that presume to prevent one's passage.

Azeyma, the Warden. Standing in steadfast surveillance of the sun, this goddess favors inquisitive individuals. The Seekers of the Sun of the Miqo'te are among Her most fervent followers. She consoles all who would confess to their crimes.

Nald'thal, the Traders. This dual-aspected divinity administers the afterlife and commerce, a curious combination. Eminent entities in the sand-girt sultanate, Nald looks after the living, while Thal deals with the dead.

Nophica, the Matron. This good-natured goddess is the personification of plenty, fecundating the fields, and gathering the growth. A motherly figure in Gridania, She is fawned over by farmers, foresters, and so forth.

Althyk, the Keeper. This deity is dedicated to the dimensions of space and time. He receives praise from people who passionately pursue the particulars of the past, as well as those who fumble to fathom the future. Sadly, He seldom seems to satisfy supplications for His succor.
...These, my most attentive adventurer, are the guardian deities of Eorzea. Now, nary a soul can say what the Twelve will do to avert the approaching apocalypse. Verily, only the gods know.
Whenever my husband travels on business, he always brings me along, and while he works to close new deals, I'm left to my own devices to occupy the time until his day is done.

Now, at risk of sounding an ingrate, I'd much prefer to wait for my husband's return in the familiar surrounds of our home. <sigh> I've been meaning to broach the subject with him, but I'm loath to hurt his feelings. Gods know how sensitive the man can be.
Those who worship the word of Nald value achievement over all else. Pray to him, and be rewarded in the here and now. Through him, salvation lies in the affirmation of life, friend.
My rounds've become a deal easier since this place sprung up. See there, even me chocobo's chipper. Ain't nothin' better for a coachman's spirits than seein' his bird happy.

The reestablishment of Ul'dah's own Grand Company is well under way. Soon the Immortal Flames will lead our nation to peace once more. And how could they not? The former champion of the Coliseum, Raubahn Aldynn himself, has been appointed Flame General.

Raubahn was always held in the highest regard, and not just by those in his own Gladiators' Guild. Hells, even the pugilists couldn't help but respect the man for his prowess on the bloodsands. I tell you this─those bloody Garleans are in for the fight of their lives.
If those Amalj'aa scum so much as show their tails anywhere near this hamlet, by the Twelve I'll lop them off an' make me a bloody necklace of 'em!
Weak thing, you are! Be gone! Squaaawk!
Squaaawk! Air around you... Strange, it is.
Squaaawk! Perhaps you. See it, Dozol does.
Squuuawk! Strong, you are. But be stronger, you must. Use black magic. Learn to control. Then come see Dozol.
Good, good! Squaaawk! Almost true black mage, you are. Almost! Something missing, there is.
[@1A(1)]Solace[@1A(0)]? [@1A(1)]Solace[@1A(0)]!? What means [@1A(1)]Solace[@1A(0)]!? Squaaawk!

Cutting and polishing, hours hunched over a tiny rock, muscles tensed, barely breathing. Before long, you turn into a rock yourself. I─I'm sorry. That wasn't funny.
The gates of Ul'dah are open to you, adventurer. I pray you find what you seek within.
...Such as medicine for afflictions caused by the lesser moon! Suffering from a Dalamud-related complaint? Never fear, for the remedy is surely to be found here in Ul'dah!
For years, I've wanted nothing more than to open a shop here. But the taxes! Gods take Ul'dah and its taxes! You can't so much as piss around here without someone demanding a share of it.

With folk taking to hoarding supplies out of fear of the swelling lesser moon, goods are changing hands at breakneck pace. But the wealthy secure all the choice plots, and I'm left to peddle my wares from a common stand.
If you ever find yourself in need, please, come to my bazaar in the market rows. You won't be disappointed!
For years, I've wanted nothing more than to open a shop here. But the taxes! Gods take Ul'dah and its taxes! You can't so much as piss around here without someone demanding a share of it.
I thought for sure my skills would fetch a pretty gil─carpenters are rare enough in the south. I was so sure, I even went so far as to have a ledger bound of the finest paper.
Please, if you know any worthy investors, tell them of me. I-I'll even let you in on one of my trade secrets.
Have you learned all there is to know of secondary tools? I suggest you do. You can find them at Barryn's carpentry shop at the Sapphire Avenue Exchange, I should think.
It's not just the taxes that have crippled me. It's the corruption as well. The bribes you have to pay would eat up even the vastest of profits!
I knew things would be different here than in Gridania, but this... Perhaps I should return to the Oak Atrium.
Do you know of the Atrium? It is home to the Carpenters' Guild. The woodworkers there are as skilled as any you'll ever meet, and wise, too. Wise enough not to come here at any rate...
Gods, the bribes... If only I had enough gil to placate these vultures, I might actually get my wares seen!
Been to the miners' alehouse yet? You know, over at Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern. The place is pure heaven!
Where they find them ladies I have no idea. But they got the curves, voices, and moves to drive a man to madness─or at least to penury!
Toil the days away. Save every gil you can. Buy yourself a fancy grave. Such is the life of an Ul'dahn─and a grand one it is!
Ala Mhigo lives on in the hearts of her survivors. But what are we to do now? How do we regain our former strength?
The ever shifting sands of Cutter's Cry have claimed more than their share of victims. It is as if the caverns have an insatiable hunger for living flesh...
The ever shifting sands of Cutter's Cry have claimed more than their share of victims. It is as if the caverns have an insatiable hunger for living flesh...
Most Ul'dahns are obsessed with their insurances. Sad to say, there's none I can recommend for a traveler such as yourself.
You and your kind care little for stability. You'd rather leap into an unknown tomorrow than linger in a known today, would you not?

Lovely to have you back, [@IF($E9(4),gorgeous,handsome)]. Oh, before you head off, I must inform you that the front entrance to the inn rooms is inaccessible at the moment─building inspection and all that.
We're terribly sorry for the inconvenience, but in the meantime you'll have to make use of the back entrance, over in the Gold Court. The doorman, Kopuru Fupuru, will be pleased to assist you.

It takes most goldsmiths a lifetime to master the touch. Some cuts need an arm like an aurochs's, strong and sure─others, a feather-touch, gentle as a lamb.
It's a damn shame, is what it is─how far this hamlet has fallen.
Did you know it started out as a bustling waypoint on one of the major trade routes of the day? Time was, every good from across the sea would pass through here.
You must be heading south. Were you heading north, you'd be coming from Ul'dah, and most who visit there never want to leave.
Slash! Gouge! Maim! [@1A(1)]Kiiillllll[@1A(0)]!!!
I am Jandonaut, of the Immortal Flames. I have been dispatched here to carry out an investigation of Zahar'ak─the Amalj'aa encampment to the east.
I am Jandonaut, of the Immortal Flames. I have been dispatched here to carry out an investigation of Zahar'ak─the Amalj'aa encampment to the east.
