Whether it graces an Ul'dahn lady of the Fronds or a common tablemaid of Ishgard, every fashion worth knowing in Eorzea bears the Sunsilk name.
Come, and be welcome to the Gold Court. It is open to the public for the moment, at the behest of the Syndicate.
It is to be hoped that you will find a measure of peace here, even in these troubled times.
The Sultansworn are bound to defend Sultana Nanamo Ul Namo, even to the death. Such is the solemn oath that we have taken.
A true paladin is one who bends his knee to a higher cause, and offers his sword and shield without promise of reward.

Of all those sworn to protect the sultanate─the soldiers, the mounted guards, and the knights─the Sultansworn are the elite of the elite. Our conviction unwavering, our hearts true, our sword skills without peer.
The Sultansworn are bound to defend Sultana Nanamo Ul Namo, even to the death. Such is the solemn oath that we have taken.
The Monetarists will not rest until the Sultansworn are destroyed. But I shall take up Solkzagyl's torch, and together with General Raubahn, I will restore our honor and might.
Go on, leave us be! We ain't botherin' no one!
If you happen to see any Amalj'aa, I suggest you keep your distance. Consider yourself warned.
The wealth and belongings one amasses are not without meaning. They are glorious in their own right.
But for all their worth in life, in death they are mere fetters─chains which bind our souls to baseness.
Think on it, and you will see the truth of what I say.
Success lies in secrecy. I am part of a greater whole. I shall not cause undue disturbance.
Introspection is the only path to true knowledge. Ask none but yourself what it is you must do.
The time we all wait for approaches. When it comes, I shall be ready.
You must temper yourself. Make yourself a vessel for the black magic to enter. Once you have done so, Dozol Meloc will have a new task for you.
The Glooms seeps forth from the Voidgate, drawn to the black magic awakened within you. Little time remains to us.

You have done well to gather the first four artifacts, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. For my part, I have searched for answers as to this [@1A(1)]Solace of the Gods[@1A(0)], but fear I have learned nothing.
Such a strange turn of events... Could Ququruka truly have orchestrated this all those years ago? Or... Could it be that Nald'thal truly spoke to him?
Pore as I might over the writings left by my great-grandfather, I have yet to find any knowledge that may serve to aid us.
Pay no mind to any harsh words you hear around here. Most of the bitter ones are born of losing runs at the Mirage─nothing personal.

Dalamud the lesser moon growing angry and immense, stars falling in all directions and tearing holes in the sky... If there's an iller omen, I've not seen it. More than a few took it for a fireworks show─gazed right into it, they did!
Word is, any caught near them falling stars been cursed something awful. If I was one of them, I'd give every gil I'd got to the Ossuary. If anyone can save them, it's them thaumaturges.
You have the look of a marauder, that much is certain. Come to swing that axe of yours in the Coliseum, have you?
You'd best pray you don't draw me on the bloodsands. All the same, what say I give you some friendly advice, one marauder to another?

A marauder can be a shield of sorts to those around [@IF($E9(4),her,him)]. But you've got to learn to let your pain drive you, to let each blow your enemy lands harden your resolve. Learn that, and you'll never want for allies─loyal ones, too.
Now there's a true axe[@IF($E9(4),maiden,man)]. I've had my eye on you for a while now.
Whenever I saw you, couldn't help but wonder if you knew of the Marauders' Guild. Met plenty of you axe-fancying adventurers who haven't.
There's ferries at the docks of Vesper Bay what will take you clear across the sea to Limsa Lominsa.
You'll find a boat there, put in at the docks, name of Astalicia. Bloody nest of whores and vipers, but home to our guild all the same.
I wager I can guess how much gil you've got in that bag by the weight alone. What say you, stranger?
Not interested, eh? Fair do's, smart arse! But mark my words─you'll need a line of your own if you ever want to claw your way out of the Dunes.

This camp has been named Mythril Pit T[@1F]8. We are mythril miners by trade, dispatched here by the Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern to prospect the area. Our orders are to find every last scrap of ore there is to be had, to help the nation make ready.
Ye wouldn't believe the demand for dark matter. Hells, the stuff's nearly as popular as ore! Its discovery's changed the face o' minin' as we know it, an' that ain't no word of a lie.

Greetings, good [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)]. You stand before the rearward-facing entrance to the inn rooms of the Hourglass. Pray avail yourself of this ingress should access not be possible via the front.
Any pugilist worth [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] piss'll tell you─flexibility is key to mastering hand-to-hand combat.
All fees must be paid in advance. This is a place of healing, not a charity.
Without sufficient coin, there is no treatment for you here.
I ain't at liberty to disclose the nature of my mission here. Suffice it to say I'm keepin' a close eye on the Amalj'aa to find when and where to best strike.
Master foretold of one who would usher the return of an ancient power. It is for that soul's coming that I wait.
Master will not be seeing you. His meditations are far more important than such mundane meetings. I shall speak in his place.
More of Master's words await you. But you are not yet ready to hear them. Return when the black magic is stronger within you.
There is not much time left. You must see the Voidgate sealed anew, and soon.
There is not much time left. You must see the Voidgate sealed anew, and soon.
There is not much time left. You must see the Voidgate sealed anew, and soon.
I...I was foolish. I craved guidance. A mentor. I see that now. I never should have believed Ququruka's words.
Even now, I cannot say what of Ququruka's words is truth, and what is falsehood. But you are indeed the one destined to guide this power. Of that alone am I certain.
Master ordains the time has come. You are to visit Arrzaneth Ossuary. Go, now.
Hmph, from the looks of you, I'd say you have no business on this coach. Go on, now, and stop wasting both our time.
You adventurers have always done well by me. Your travels take you far, and often put you in great company. Send any business my way, and I'll see to it you're well rewarded.
I could offer you a trinket. Or...a good polish for your family jewels, perhaps? Should you have any, that is. Anything you'd like.

It is the thaumaturges of the Order of Nald'thal who write Ul'dah's laws. You had best not breach them, or you may see the “other side” they preach of sooner than you wish. Guard your tongue at all times, lest you mean to be chased out of the city as the sylphs once were.
And be especially wary when speaking of the Garleans or the beast tribes. These are both sensitive subjects to the thaumaturges.
It may not be too much to say that getting on with the thaumaturges is the secret to success here in Ul'dah, such is their influence. You'd do well to remember that.
As a leatherworker, you may think your affairs far-removed from those of the thaumaturges, but that is not so here in Ul'dah.

The wealthiest of the wealthy have the Order in their pockets, and it is the Order who make the laws. You had best not breach them, or you may see the “other side” they preach of sooner than you wish.
Gods know what will come of the guildleves should they take power over their issue. If I were you, I'd earn what gil I could, and stock up on some secondary tools.
That, and learn where to exercise caution─around the Garleans, the beast tribes, the sylphs... Unpredictable foes, all.
I must say, just to survive down here, your talent as a leatherworker must be rivaled by your cunning as a merchant.
Dedicate yourself to bettering your skills, and they'll serve you well. Speaking of which, have you considered a sojourn at the Leatherworkers' Guild?
To the north of here, in Gridania, you will find Atelier Fen[@1F]Yll. There, you may learn under the realm's finest.
If your path does lead you there, do us a favor and spread word of the horrors and hedonism of Ul'dah. Anything to deter a competitor from taking an interest, yes?

Welcome to the airship landing, good [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)]. If you wish to book passage on an airship, please seek the attendant stationed at the counter situated behind you, on the right-hand side.
Welcome to Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern─proud miners of Thanalan, from the Copperbells to the Nanawas.
We've even some shafts open to the public, seein' as how they're picked clean an' all.
Hah! I can see it now. Me, in this, strolling the Fronds, Ruby Road, the Gold Court. The women will flock to me in droves!
Are you aware of the mercenary band known as the Darklight Raiders? Surely you have heard the famous lay? Well, to the east of here lie the caverns of Cutter's Cry, where they met their untimely end.

They say 'twas the fearsome chimera that brought them low. Me? I think I'd like to be remembered as the one swallowed whole by the monster of the distended maw. 'Twould make a fine tale... A fine tale indeed...

Don't mind ol' Yuyuhase. He ain't all there, if you grasp my meaning. Anyway, the city asks that you take care not to use the aetheryte too freely. They have been known to break, after all. And these days, there are none left capable of restoring them.

Welcome to the Coliseum, the place where legends are forged and felled, our own Flame General Raubahn Aldynn being one of the few who've managed to avoid the latter. Most 'round here call it the bloodsands. Name don't matter much, though─if you're fighting for your life, especially.
You'll come to love it here. All who come do. Watching the fights is entertainment enough, but nothing roils the blood like a sizeable wager.
There is more to fighting than mere victory, friend. You must respect the opponent who treads the bloodsands with you, and earn your glories together.
If you are going to spend some time in Ul'dah, remember this─return that which you borrow, with all haste.
Interest here accrues at the rate of a percent a day─and that tends to be the bare minimum.
Go on, stare if you will. Make japes if you must. But I been doing this for eighty-odd years, and I know what a miner needs─booze! Not those bloody grape wines, neither─I'm talking spirits!
There was a time when I wanted nothing more than to be a bard. Now? Now this is my lute. And I weave cloths instead of songs.
I offer guidance in the Dunes to any in need of it. Seek you the market rows? The Hall of Flames? Where would you care to go, friend?

Many and more townsfolk fear that there may already be imperials spies in our midst. But I give you my word as a sister of the Sultansworn, no Garlean shall pass through the city gates so long as I draw breath.
Pshhh... Shkohhh...[@CR]Airyself lives in objects. When full of airyself, object changes to stonyshine, name of [@1A(1)]materia[@1A(0)].
What do you think of our Ul'dah? Quite a sight, is she not?
We toil to keep her beautiful, lest visitors take less-than-flattering reports home with them.
You are not permitted to pass. Begone.
Beyond this arch lies the district known as the Dunes. No, no, it's just a name, not the bloody desert. You'll find the Merchants Ward and the market rows there.
There's a saying in Ul'dah─it's not what you got, it's who you know. My grandmother said that to me just before she died.
The Order teaches us that we cross over to another realm after death, but I don't think that makes the people we meet in this one any less important. Words to live by for an adventurer, no?
I can see you walk the path of war. And what of the bonds you have forged on that path? Crafters? Harvesters? They can serve you as surely as you can serve them.
But be wary of those who plead and claim their purses empty, for I assure you they do not always speak true.
As I've said before, it is not what we have, but who we know. And I would very much like to know a blacksmith such as yourself.
Ul'dah is a ruthless city. Lower your guard for a moment and you risk all─your gil, your reputation, your very life. I will let you in on a secret...

A true blacksmith must temper [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] off hand just as diligently as [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] main. Doesdornn's blacksmith shop at the Sapphire Avenue Exchange has the secondary tools you'll need.
And that, friend, is all you need know to succeed here. Now, what say you return the favor someday, eh?
My grandmother's dying words have become the axiom by which I live out my days─that what matters most is not what we have, but who we know.
You would do well to make those words your own. There is no treasure more valuable than that of companionship.
Start at a guild, if you must. The Blacksmiths' Guild in Limsa, say.
You need only take the road to the west, to the ferry docks. The ships there will see you safe across Vesper Bay to Limsa. After that, just follow the din of hammer on anvil to Naldiq & Vymelli's.
There's a saying in Ul'dah─it's not what you got, it's who you know. My grandmother said that to me just before she died.
The Order teaches us that we cross over to another realm after death, but I don't think that makes the people we meet in this one any less important. Words to live by for an adventurer, no?
Tell me, do you feel intimidated at times in the presence of your brethren? Around those who walk the paths of war and magic?
Many and more of them are lackwits, thinking of naught but battle. Be crafty, be clever, be cunning─and take them for all they've got!
To be seen and tended to is cheap enough, I grant you. It's the medicines what run you a pretty gil.
The stuff comes in all manner of potencies and doses, but don't let that confuse you─it's always the costliest what works the wonders.
Thing is, the costliest medicines are dearer than ever these days, what with the near endless lines of folk who come seeking cures for the “afflictions of Dalamud,” bloody fools.
Ah...a hard-earned ale after a long day's labor! Is there any greater pleasure? Well, other than [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)], o' course!
Come on, love, get 'em out! This hundred thousand gil here says get the rest out, as well! Bwahahaha!
What'll it be, then? Don't tell me you just happened to wander into my Quicksand not knowin' what you wanted.

Well, even if you don't know where you are, I suppose you're in the right place. You see, I make a point of tryin' to help your kind. Travelin' merchants, travelin' adventurers, plain old travelers...

This is Ul'dah, after all. We see types from all over Eorzea in here. Makes it a ripe spot for hearin' talk, gettin' your bearin's, that sort of thing. Gods know it's hard enough to get your bearin's these days, what with folk so wrought up 'bout the lesser moon comin' down on us all.

Ya've heard of the old mines─those open to all folk? Well, now every lackwit with a pickaxe is cloggin' the shafts. Any of them strike it rich, and I wager the miners'll have a hard time swallowin' it.
You have not been granted audience with the Syndicate. Leave.
Twelve be with you, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)]. Might you spare some gil for a Lalafell down on his luck?
Got a bout o' pre-flight nerves, eh? Well, ye can set yer mind at ease, friend, 'cause me an' the lads are standin' by t' clean up the mess if the airship falls out o' th' sky.

If that ain't enough reassurance for ye, I suggest ye make an offerin' t' that lot over at Arrzaneth Ossuary. Jus' be prepared t' leave the place with a light coinpurse. Hmmm...now that I think on it, I reckon the loss in weight might well help keep the ship in the air!

Most don't know it, but Ul'dah was once ours─the Lalafells'. Till the promise of gil brought in all the others, that is. Now I can't talk to half these leeches without looking up. Ruined my bloody neck, it has.
This city is ours by rights. There ought be a tax, if you ask me. Aye, all non-Lalafells should pay for the privilege of living here─or at least for being so godsdamned [@1A(1)]tall[@1A(0)]!
What's that? Might not my neck complaint actually be caused by gazing up at Dalamud? Well, if it be so, we will need to find a way to make that vexatious hound pay as well!
You flatter me, dear. If it's a touch you want, might be your coin'll buy it. Shall I wait for you 'round the back, then?

Good [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),evening,morning)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),day,evening)])] to you, [@IF($E9(4),miss,sir)], and welcome to Frondale's Phrontistery. You will find the finest alchemists and healers in Eorzea within these halls. Our treatments are second to none.

While I have your attention, I feel I should warn you that remedies of dubious utility are rampant on the streets of Ul'dah of late, peddled by swindlers who seek to profit from the spreading fear over the lesser moon's...engorgement.
Well look at this one, Gairbert. Swaggerin' right down our very own avenue. Not lackin' for balls, is [@IF($E9(4),she,he)]?
Lucky for you, I still owe me mum a good deed for the day. Now run along, or I [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] cut you.
Ul'dah seemed a pleasant enough place to live...'til I heard about the horrifyin' creature all the ale dens are buzzin' about.

Ul'dah ain't half as scary as most outsiders'd have you believe. Folk 'round here are friendly enough, so long as you don't cross them. A bit tighter with their coin than most, but that goes without sayin' in these parts.
Receive what potions and salves you can, but do not seek a bed here. I know not what ails you, but the costs of a room will do you far more harm.
Gather 'round, gather 'round! Behold a most tragicomical musing on the Trials of Life, delivered via the timeless medium of juggling by the wan and lonely Ococo! Donations hungrily appreciated!

I've mixed this selfsame concoction more times than I'd care to count. Yet whenever I do, I still find myself praying to the Twelve to guide my hand, lest one reagent prove too potent, or another too weak, and the whole batch spoiled for it.

I swear by the Twelve this damn city gets hotter every time I come. Ul'dahns like tellin' anyone who'll listen it's all because of them Amalj'aa. Meant to be big─proper [@1A(1)]massive[@1A(0)], by all accounts. Strong as hells, and with brains enough for words, too.

If that alone don't make you piss your britches, the creatures have their own god what they summon at will─named Ifrit or some such. You'll see naught of me but my backside when their lot comes callin'.

Itchin' to catch yourself a glimpse of 'em? Thought you might. Bloody adventurers... Well, I ain't about to stop you. Head north out the Gate of Nald. If you don't spot 'em, they'll spot you soon enough.
<sniff> <sniff> You... You got a whiff of the sea about you─and fish. You an angler?
Don't see many of our kind in this part of the realm. What the hells are you doin' in the middle of the desert?
The trick to good fishin' is bein' able to find the best spots to cast your line. No secret there. Hells, you can even spearfish in shallow waters─with the proper secondary tools, o' course.
I fish with both feet on dry land. I'll never cast from a boat again. Not after last─ Bah, never you mind about that! You just come on back if you find any good spots, you hear?
You're quite a [@IF($E9(4),fisherwoman,fisherman)] yourself, I can see that─and smell it. How's castin' your rod from a rollin' deck tickle your fancy?
'Less you came to Ul'dah lookin' to get away from boats, I'd say you're best off makin' for Limsa.
There's a whole damn guild of pullers over at Fisherman's Bottom. Any fisher worth [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] spit got [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] own private tank there.
Good many Ul'dahns ain't pleased none at all by this influx from Ala Mhigo. Best not to say as much 'round here, though─if ye value yer life.
Mirage here is one o' the few places willing to give the poor bastards a bit o' work. Hells, my own parents were among some o' the first Mhigans to come here.

Even here, the winds find us. Gods know how, but they do. They make the heat of day bearable enough. We see beasts from time to time, as well, drawn to the water. But they are no match for an Ala Mhigan blade.
The greatest dangers come with nightfall. Fearsome things prowl the darkness. I do not envy the traveler caught out past sundown.
Hello there, [@IF($E9(4),gorgeous,handsome)], and welcome to the Hourglass. If it's respite from the heat and hot sands you seek, you need look no further.
<sigh> Good ingots are rarer than good women[@IF($E9(4),─or men, in your case,)]. There [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)] be a better way to go about finding them. Hmmm...
If you're after the cheap wares this hamlet's known for─bad luck. Market's closed for now.
The Amalj'aa rarely venture this far from their lands, though it is not unheard of.
It's said they summon forth their foul fire god, and feed it the captives they take in battle.
You wish to view the games? Please, do not embarrass yourself with such brazen requests.
You'll not find a soul selling tickets to the likes of you. They are reserved for the wealthy, as all things are here.
Well met, friend! Have you a riveting story you'd like to share with me?
If you wish to take issue with how Ul'dah is ruled, you need only make your voice heard at the Heaven's Shard. All are free to do so.
But if it is the law itself you wish to see changed, that will cost you gil─and a good deal more than you look to have.
They do not suffer us to grope these dancing wenches, no matter how much coin you throw their way. But suppose one were to make a gift of a necklace, or a brooch?
One would naturally ask for the honor of placing it on her. And then perhaps one's hand slips? Stranger things have happened.
I was told to drill this over and over until I could do it in my sleep. My limbs ache and my muscles burn, but I'm no better than when I started.
My orders are to let none pass beyond this point. That would include you, by my understanding.
There have been beast tribes in the region of late, searching for crystals. And not just Amalj'aa─Ixal, too.
The Brass Blades no longer patrol the mines. That task falls to we Stone Torches, now. But I wonder how long we can keep them safe...
This is our bloody corner. If you ain't got no food or gil to give us, then piss off!
Welcome to the Platinum Mirage, where the sands turn to gil!
Are you feeling lucky [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),this evening,this morning)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),today,this evening)])], friend? Come, and receive a free reading from our mammet here.
See anything you like, adventurerrr? Don't be shy, sweetling, [@IF($E9(4),even two ladies can have fun together,I won't bite. Unless you want me to)].
Was me what said we should start ropin' in beast tribes for the games.
Y'know, bloody great Amalj'aa, an' them vicious little...little...shites. Bugger it, the name's gone. Ah! Sylphs, that's it! Amalj'aa an' sylphs! Now there's a fight I'd pay to see!
Oh, and I damn near forgot them Ixal! Aye, I'm told them an' the lizardmen're goin' at it like...well, [@1A(1)]beasts[@1A(0)] in the wilds─might as well have 'em do it for our amusement!
The journey here was wrought with perils. We suffered hardships beyond imagining. But we have arrived.
This war with the Garleans, the fall of Ala Mhigo─this is the end of nothing. Mark my words!
No need to say it, I know what you're thinking. Only a bloody fool would spend her days spinning wee little threads. Still, I love the stuff. Always have, always will.
Come on, give us a hundred gil.
Give us a hundred gil or I'll scream thief! Honest I will!
We are bound by no allegiance here, either to the Seedseers or the sultana. For Gridania and Ul'dah alike fail to claim us as their own.
I do apologize, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)], but I'm afraid my shop and services are reserved for a...particular clientele.

Eorzea has seen six Umbral Eras in the past. There's no reason to think it should stop there. I have my doubts about these doom-spouting “Archons,” but it doesn't mean the seventh Umbral Era isn't coming.
The only question is when... I've pored over every text, tome, and treatise on the subject and haven't been able to find a single clue!
Aye, I hear ya. You and every other adventurer. I know only too bloody well that you want to rent a bird. But there just ain't enough of 'em to go 'round.
The Brass Blades say the beast of Cutter's Cry has awoken.
Perhaps a new generation of heroes will succeed where my brothers and I failed... Or perhaps they are all doomed to the same fate...

Might you have heard of the [@1A(1)]Illuminati[@1A(0)]? It's a goblin fraternity which has long been the marvel of the scholarly world. Why do I mention it? Master Mutamix is an inducted brother. See to it that you accord him the proper respect.
It is truly beyond belief. Even with the shadow of the Seventh Umbral Era darkening our very doorstep, there are yet fools who concern themselves with securing a seat in the Syndicate.
What worth such worldly concerns when Ul'dah teeters on the brink of oblivion...?
This is the exit for those arriving in Thanalan.
Excuse me, [@IF($E9(4),lady,mister)]. How am I supposed to see when the monster comes with you standing straight in my way!?
The last time he was here, he hit me daddy and stole all me mum's bread.
But not next time! Next time, I'll show him! You'll see...if you get out of my way, that is.
Not again! Why does everyone stop right in front of me? I won't be able to see when the monster comes!
I wouldn't have to stand guard like this if that other big man came back─that one who helps keep the birds out.
I wish I hadn't have called him a monster, too. He looked so sad. Da was right sore with me after that. Said I had to apologize if I saw him again...but he hasn't been back since...
Oh, would you please stay out of my way! I won't be able to see when the brothers come back!
Ever since I apologized, the two agreed to come back and watch over the town.
And it's a good thing I did, too, because until I'm done training to be a warrior, there's no one to stop the bad birds.
That's right. Soon, I'll be the one watching over the Silver Bazaar. Just you wait!
The sentries posted here can't seem to be bothered. I'm not sure I blame them. Do you have any idea how little coin they are paid?
The head of the Golden Bazaar is always being ridiculed by the head of the Silver Bazaar for being too sparing with his gil.
My vessel carries only distinguished passengers. Them posh sods from Ul'dah toss around more coin in one trip than most folk see in their entire lives.
So tell me, traveler, what of our Ul'dah here has surprised you the most?

I must say, I myself was astonished by the lack of violence in the city, given all I'd heard of the struggles for power and money. We Ala Mhigans may not be welcomed by all, but I've not seen so much as a single stone thrown here in the name of hatred.
They are called the Twins, Nald and Thal. Or at times, the Traders. All of reality is governed by their two aspects, and they hold a ceaseless vigil to ensure order is maintained.

Long ago, our city itself was split into two great sections, to mirror this truth. As an honored teacher of mine once said, microcosm recapitulates macrocosm. We have since merged, and prospered for it. Perhaps the gods will someday mirror us.
All seeking entry to the Coliseum, present yourselves here. Fame! Wealth! Power! Come, and know the true meaning of victory.
Hahaha! Not you, sprat. You've too few winters under your belt.
Please! You haven't happened to see a ferry pass anywhere, have you? I-I swear it was just here! Gods, I'm ruined if I've lost it!
Don't take much nous to work out most of Eorzea's gil's right here in Ul'dah. Hells, just look around you!
Goes without saying the bloody desert ain't got the resources of the other nations. But the merchants here got minds sharp as swords. And Ul'dahns are nothing if not perseverant.
Still, this place is a pale shadow of what it once was. Merchants and travelers used to come from all over Hydaelyn till the Garleans blocked the trade routes.
It might look a sight, but the Ul'dah you see's a shadow of its former glory. Merchants and travelers came from all over Hydaelyn till the Garleans blocked the routes.

No airships launching now, though. All trade goes by boat or wain, and the seas and snows claim more freight than the skies ever did. On the upside, the folks doing the shipping seem to love having archers around.

Not a bad way to earn. Start out knowing where you're heading, and you'll get there a deal faster. If you remember anything, let it be this─a good archer is ever aware of the distance to [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] target.
Find yourself a sturdy ally. One who knows how to keep the enemy's eye on him and off you. One who'll take the blows while you line up the reply. Find such an ally, and never let them go!
Well, judging by that gear, I'd say you were guard to some wealthy merchant or other.
An adventurer? Come, let's have a look at you. Is this what passes for an archer these days?

Gods, Ul'dah's quite a city, ain't she? Looks like she's sullied yet another fledgling archer. Best get to Gridania, 'fore it's too late. The Gods' Quiver'll set you straight. Teach you the proper use of that bow, too.
They run the Archers' Guild, right there at the Quiver's Hold. Make that your next stop if you mean to be a [@1A(1)]true[@1A(0)] archer─'stead of a [@IF($E9(4),princess,dandy)] with a pretty bow.
Lord Lolorito is the official proprietor of Eshtaime's, but he has left all of his dealings to Yuyune, the current guildmaster.
When the last guildmaster was stripped of his position, the entire upper echelon of the guild was replaced. Such dramas make this city what it is.
The Mirage has its appeal, I grant you that. But there is something to be said for a fight─for a single spectacle whose every act commands the eyes and cries of so many.
Hedonism, gluttony... Hah! Let the other nations call it what they will. We Ul'dahns live for the things we love! Give us a hot sun, a spicy meal, and a bloody fight, and we'll give you true passion!
The ferries had been docked for some time, but now, they sail again.
These cliffs serve to channel in winds off the sea. Damn saltspray'll rust every scrap of metal in sight if you let it.
I've been following the gladiators for some five years now. I've even had a few scuffles of my own up here. We ladies can be quite...territorial.

This route was navigated and mapped by the Lominsans. But the Ul'dahns and their famous greed didn't take long to seize upon it. Have you any idea how much gil they make from all the shipping and passage fees?
Might you be seeking a retainer to see to your bazaar affairs? If so, allow me to assist you in your search.
All Ul'dahns have a price, however dark the deed. I myself have done things...terrible things. Too terrible to speak of, even.
But never have I forgotten why! To reclaim my homeland─to take back the soil and sky of which my people have been robbed!
When it comes to work, the Platinum Mirage has no eye for races and clans.
Appearances? Personality? Upbringing? These things have no value here. What is truly needed is an eye for an opportunity, and the ability to take it.
East of here lies Milvaneth Sacrarium. Within its halls, the exaltations and praises of life are sung.
The aspect of Nald governs this side of existence─passions and possessions. Many who worship there are the wealthy and privileged─those most grateful for what they have.

In contrast, the aspect of Thal governs the realm which begins where life ends. There, comfort is to be had for those who believe no joy awaits them in this mortal coil. Such souls wax ever more common in these dark times.
If you would walk these halls, you must know of Nald'thal of the Twelve, and his two aspects. It is Nald who rules over this world of the living, and Thal who keeps the realm of the dead.
All which lives must die, and to cross over one must be devout of mind─a true follower of Thal.
I suggest you stay sober. You won't want to forget what you might see here.
Once the show's in full swing, you won't even [@1A(1)]remember[@1A(0)] the name of that big red thing in the sky.
We had heard that Ala Mhigo's armies were more than enough to fight off the Garlean invasion from the northeast. Tidings of her demise were...disheartening, to say the least.
And now there is word that Garlemald has made a stronghold of the ruins. It is from there that they launch their winged monstrosities, such as the one which destroyed our own airship.

Their juggernauts have been spotted in the skies over every part of the realm, and their silver-clad soldiers are becoming a regular sight in the borderlands. Aye, it would seem the Garleans mean to unleash their full wrath on Eorzea.
After Ala Mhigo's fall, the Garleans' path through Eorzea would surely lead them to Gridania next. Or so we all thought.

Gods know I did─'tis why I fled here to Ul'dah. Yet many moons have passed, and still there is no sign of attack. If this is to be the way of things, I had best return to the Twelveswood. This desert is no place for a botanist.
Yet my travels have taught me something of people. And I can see you have an honest air about you. So allow me to offer you this counsel.

Any fool with a hatchet can log, but harvesting is a bit different. Some don't even know the necessary tools. Fortunately, you can find everything you need at Tataroga's stand in the Sapphire Avenue Exchange.
Garlemald could well nigh blot out the sun with all the airships they command. Aye, they are massing their strength, biding time. Before long their fell fires will consume these lands.
If you wish to learn the ways of botany, best make for Gridania while there is still life there to be seen.
You will find our beloved Greatloam Growery there, home of the botanists. Among gardens, there is none finer.
Make haste, while the forest still stands. The pounding of war drums echoes from the north. The fires are coming, friend.
Drinks! Cold drinks here! 'Cause baying for blood's murder on the throat!
Gambling is a gentleman's endeavor, dear [@IF($E9(4),girl,boy)]. It is not about winning or losing. It simply serves to make the games that much more exciting!
Royal order─none are to pass beyond this point. Now make your way back from whence you came.
Working at the airship landing, you hear all sorts of tales from all kinds of folk. Adventurers, merchants, sellswords─everyone has something fascinating to tell.
The finest part of this, though, is how people now flock to me wishing to hear the anecdotes of individuals they've never once met. Mayhap I can fashion a career for myself as a taleteller! Heh heh!
I've heard so much about the beauty of Silvertear Falls, and I'd hoped to see it for myself. Sadly, the sun would be the end of me if I tried to go on foot─assuming the Amalj'aa didn't get me first.
And I haven't the coin to ride that damned bird there, either. Hmph, for that kind of gil, you'd think Ishgardian chocobos laid golden eggs.

The Coliseum's been popular of late, bustlin' with folk who seek a diversion from the woes of everyday life. There ain't nothin' like watchin' blood bein' spilled to take the mind off doomsday prophecies and oversized moons.

Matches what pit gladiator 'gainst beast always draw the largest crowds. And when it comes to them monsters, people only know one thing─the bigger and bloodthirstier, the better. It's the death folks come to see, ain't no mistakin'. But think on this─which side you reckon they'd rather see die?
The path of the thaumaturge is an arduous one─for both mind and body. More than a few have succumbed to its demands.
Oh gods, wherever have I wandered to now? Tell me, dear, is this the other side? Has Thal taken me in my sleep?
Oh, let it be so! My grandbabies─just little ones, taken in their cribs by the fever─are they here? Have you seen them?
All praise be to Rhalgr the Destroyer. He guided we Ala Mhigans to Gyr Abania. There we built a great city.
Our country was a gift from Him. It was divine will that we have it. The Garlean invasion that took it is a dire blasphemy. Soon His wrath will find them.
Change is slow. But it will come. The path before me is clear.
My garb? These are not true monk's vestments. They are only made in their likeness. I never took the trials.
It may be wrong of me to do so. But I feel a strength when I wear them. A bond with my brothers and sisters.
Place your trust in Nald. Give your life over to him, and we shall help you however so we might.
Bloody shopkeep thinks just because he has coin, he can push good people around.
I've half a mind to open his throat from ear to ear and show the bastard his blood runs red as mine!
I s'pose you might get by, if you were to kill me first. But that ain't bloody likely to happen.
Many Ala Mhigans have flocked here since their nation's fall. And in such a short time. There have been...undesirable consequences.
Visitors are being swindled in the streets and at market in no short order. The rumor that the lesser moon will fall and destroy us all serves only to compound the chaos.
It is the alchemist's duty to try all things, lest the truth of them remain hidden. The results may sometimes be tragic, but such is the price of progress.
I'm such a fool... I took an advance on next moon's wages and put it all on this fight. I...I think I might have a problem.

All life culminates in the birth of death, so say we all. Greetings, and welcome to the Arrzaneth Ossuary. As Dalamud's shadow threatens to devour the realm, ever more souls come to us seeking to learn the truth of life transcending.
Do you desire to see the other realm through the eyes of a thaumaturge? Do you wish to know the limits of this mortal coil?
Even as we proffer guidance to the uninitiated, with newfound fervor must we strive to free ourselves from the limits of this mortal coil.
The red moon falls towards us? Hah. I place no faith in such rumors. If you would peddle doom, I suggest you speak to someone with a little less sense.
Ul'dahns believe great dangers prowl the lands beyond the city walls under cover of darkness. Cold fiends, come from the realm of the dead to stalk the living.
The miners tell of how they claw their way up from deep below ground when the moons begin their ascent.
And if you don't tell this story to six other people within a week's time, they will come for [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)], and no city walls will keep you safe.
Ul'dahns believe great dangers prowl the lands beyond the city walls under cover of darkness. Cold fiends, come from the realm of the dead to stalk the living.
Ah, forgive me. I see you are a conjurer. You are asking yourself whether or not I am some apparition summoned forth by the sylphs, perhaps?
I know, I know, the spells of conjury have means of assaulting several enemies at once. Yes, yes. Tell me, was the promise of such power the siren's call that lured you?
Great strength breeds great enemies, friend. Heed that. Still, I must admit, the sight of a conjurer bringing down nature's wrath on a pack of fell beasties can be rather entertaining! Hahaha!
Ul'dahns believe great dangers prowl the lands beyond the city walls under cover of darkness. Cold fiends, come from the realm of the dead to stalk the living.
They say a miner went missing, his screams echoing from unknown depths─a miner who failed to tell six others what I have just told you within a week of hearing it.
If you do not intend to spread this tale to six others, I suggest you head for the safety of Gridania to the north.
Perhaps you could beg the conjurers at Stillglade Fane to rid you of your curse. You might even consider joining their cause to show your gratitude.

New face, eh? I can tell. Too clean by half. Anyway, found aught worth the showing? Dug up, stolen, or otherwise, it makes no odds to me. I warn you, though─put a dodgy rock in my hand and I'll bury my pickaxe between your eyes. Don't think I won't know, neither.
Halt! Thou must needs swear a solemn oath before gods and man to seek naught but wealth and riches by yon aetheryte! Wilt thou!?
The thought that the Amalj'aa might come a-raiding at any moment has always set me trembling. But that's nothing compared to the terror I feel just looking up at the moon these days...
It's an odd thing to shiver when you spend every waking hour beside a fire like I do.
I cannot permit you to enter here. Please, seek your adventures elsewhere.
Fools being named by others as the newly come Archons have been heard spouting nonsense about the end of the world. Pay them and their empty words no heed.

...Hm? Does not the swelling lesser moon suffice as proof, you say? N-Naught could be further from the truth! If the sight of Dalamud fills you with disquiet, you need but direct your gaze to the ground─though I daresay an “Archon” would have us see doom in a cobblestone...
I warn you, try and thieve from me and you'll be one hand the worse off for your pains.

Ah, you are not one of them, that's plain enough. Forgive me, I've acquired certain...habits during my stay here in Ul'dah. The city has become a veritable haven for crooks and cutthroats of late, owing to the mounting fear over the lesser moon.

Let me set things right. I have nothing but my word, but perhaps it still has some value. There are foes best avoided beyond these walls. Antlings, for one. They're known to make short work of lesser folk.
You carry a polearm. But do you know how to wield it, I wonder?
You wear it well enough. Aye, and your hands tell me they are no strangers to its haft. Forgive me, suspicion and doubt can often be your only allies in this city.
Mayhap a few words from an old lancer might right the wrong? Aye, well, it is an oft overlooked fact that your polearm can serve your allies as well as yourself. Remember that.
And pay no heed to these mummers you see dancing left to right like maids at a ball. A strong thrust requires a strong stance. Get your legs under you, and your thrusts will be the better for it.
Well met, lancer─and a fine one at that by the looks of it!
Can never be too careful in these parts, y'hear? I make it my business to know every member of the Lancers' Guild. Who can you trust if not a fellow Wailer?
Leave this foul city. Travel to the Twelveswood─to Gridania. Take that weapon of yours to the Wailing Barracks, and the Lancers' Guild will welcome you.
I pray you give me reason to remember yet another face. Hahaha!
These are the Nanawa Mines, property of Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern. The shafts have been opened to the public, but visitors are asked not to venture too deep.

The Dunes, is it? Yes, well, it is the common area of the commonfolk, and lies just beyond here. There you will find both the Merchants Ward, comprised of the homes and workshops of both crafters and merchants, and the market rows, where peddlers and traders gather to sell their wares.

The Merchants Ward lies on the far side of the Dunes, and serves primarily as a residential district for both craftsmen and traders. There are educational and religious centers, as well. Aye, it's quite a bustling little area, and has a charm to it.
The market rows lie on the near side of the Dunes, and are host to the most lively bunch of shops and bazaars you're like to find in Eorzea.
It is the only place you need visit if you have a mind to spend your gil─well, there and the pillowhouses, of course.
You as well!? Gods, are there none left who [@1A(1)]haven't[@1A(0)] heard? Yes, Ul'dah's Grand Company has established itself in the Dunes.
The Hall of Flames welcomes all who would serve. They are not so demanding as we Brass Blades.
The Fronds? Look no further─you're in them, friend. The richest of the rich live here, counting the gil in their mansions on Emerald Avenue and Ruby Road.
It is also home to some of Ul'dah's greatest architectural feats, and is located directly below the royal palace.
There's water to be had, and even plants to be seen. Quite lovely, actually.
If it's goods you want, the market rows are where you need to be. You're like to find anything you fancy in the shops and bazaars there─and a few things you don't.
Is there aught else? Ask what you will. And be quick about it.
The great Raubahn Aldynn leads the Immortal Flames, and there is no finer warrior in the realm.

He was the greatest champion of the Coliseum in his time─perhaps of all time. There was not a soul in Ul'dah that didn't rejoice at his return, and we mean to follow him wherever he leads. Gods, I would like nothing better than to see him wield a sword once more!

Come, look upon my uniform. Have you ever seen such armor? The mere sight of it instills fear and dread in your enemies, and courage and purpose in your heart. Make a name for yourself in the Immortal Flames, and one day you too could don such armor. As for me... Well, I borrowed this set... But you get my point.

We have need of you adventurers. Ul'dah's Grand Company rises again! The Immortal Flames have come to Eorzea once more, and we will end all evils with our purging fire! I urge you to travel to our halls in the Dunes, friend, and learn more of our cause.

Greetings, traveler. I am Healer Vavaki, of Frondale's Phrontistery. I have been entrusted with the task of researching the genealogies of Eorzea's races and clans, that we might better our methods of developing new medicines.
Is there anything on the subject you would care to know? I find reciting my data to be ever so helpful in remembering it.

text_en: Very well! Ahem! The Highlanders are a clan of Hyur whose name derives from their long tradition of building strongholds in the mountains. Long years at high altitudes endowed them with a stamina that lent itself well to physical activity, and both the men and women are trained in the arts of combat from childhood, which accounts for their thick musculature. They are truly beautiful physical specimens─from a purely scientific point of view, of course.
They have become increasingly rare, however, since their homeland of Ala Mhigo fell to the Garlean Empire─the females in particular. A pity, that. It makes it exceedingly hard to study them.

I myself am a Dunesfolk, as you may have noticed. Our kind is a feisty little bunch, with a long history of life in the desert. From an early age, we are made to drink a traditional herbal concoction to raise our resilience to poison, as nearly all the plants and animals in our native lands are venomous.
But since migrating to Eorzea, this resilience seems to have absolutely no effect─an interesting fact of Eorzean toxicology! And please, take note of my eyes.

There is what appears to be a thin layer covering the pupil, yes? That too is an evolutionary response to the environment─our bodies' way of protecting the eye from the harsh rays of the sun and errant grains of sand. Unfortunately, it limits detailed ocular research to Dunesfolk cadavers.

There is no mistaking the Hellsguard among the Roegadyn. Their skin is as fiery red as their name implies. They hail from the northern mountains of Abalathia's Spine, where generations among the volcanoes have endowed them with rugged bodies and steely resilience.
Here in Ul'dah, they can oft be seen working as mercenaries and sellswords, or armorers and blacksmiths for those with no taste for violence. I suppose the forges remind them of home...

The greatest hindrance in studying the Hellsguard is that they have no patience for Phrontistery members. They regard the alchemical trade as dark and sacrilegious sorcery that spurns the Twelve. I must find a way to study them closer. If only I could somehow procure eight live specimens... <sigh>

The Seekers of the Sun are a true miracle of evolution at work. Though lean and flexible, they possess immense strength and stamina, and excel at near any physical act─be it bounding amongst the treetops or swimming in rough waters.
Above all that, their powers of expression are also second to none. Yes, Seekers of the Sun make fine study specimens─fine study specimens [@1A(1)]indeed[@1A(0)].

Still, it is the males of the race which remain a near complete mystery. An effective medicine requires detailed study of both the male and female of a species, but male Miqo'te are simply nowhere to be found.
Rumors say that some reside right here in Ul'dah, but they must avoid people like the bloody plague, because I've yet to set eyes on a single one!

text_en: The Amalj'aa are a lizard-like race of nomadic beastmen who inhabit the environs of Paglth'an to the north and east of Ul'dah, where they subsist by hunting the region's wildlife.

They are comparable in size to even the largest of Roegadyn, and possess near-inexhaustible stamina as a result of their crueling and rigorous way of life. They could be an immensely valuable ally─if only they could be trusted...

But there is certainly no hope of that in the near future. There has been widespread talk of the Amalj'aa amassing their forces for an assault on Ul'dah. My research to develop a drug to counter their─ Oh... Oh dear. Best forget I said that.

The Qiqirn look, for all intents and purposes, like rats. They are known to have tremendous appetites, which they will sate by feeding on nigh anything─from rotten meat to hot trash. More than once I've tried taking them back to the Phrontistery, only to have them steal away to the storerooms and gorge themselves on medicines until their stomachs burst or their hearts stop or some such ridiculousness.

All the same, they [@1A(1)]are[@1A(0)] exceedingly clever things. They know their numbers as well as any scholar, and have a gift for merchant trade, as well. The Phrontistery even employs some to keep their books. In fact, there's a funny story about that.
For no more than a dodo egg, the gluttonous things will even let me stick a─ Oooh! Never mind that last part. Well... This is awkward.

The goblins are short little monstrosities, though amicable enough. Time was they could oft be seen throughout the streets of Ul'dah peddling wares. You will certainly know one if you come across them. They never take off their distinctive masks, and always bear seemingly unbearable packs on their backs.

Some say they only make one great pilgrimage every hundred years to the cities of man. Perhaps now is that time. With every passing sun I hear more and more talk of people claiming to have seen a goblin, or that they've now come back to us.
Is there some other race or clan about which you care to ask?
Ah, you must be the adventurer of whom Haurtefert sent word. Greetings and well met.
I am Ser Alberic Bale, knight of Ishgard. The Holy See is much obliged to you for your aid.
Time being of the essence, I shall proceed straight to the heart of the matter. The Eye, an Ishgardian relic of immeasurable worth, has been stolen. We require your assistance in its recovery.

The thief has been identified as a man named Estinien, a dragoon sworn to the service of the Holy See. Aye, you heard true: the crime was perpetrated by one of our own; an individual in a position of trust and no little honor... You may be assured that a fate worse than death awaits him upon capture.

Estinien was last sighted in the vicinity of Camp Nine Ivies, in the East Shroud. It is believed he chose the place in the hope that the fell creatures who inhabit it would hinder the efforts of his pursuers. And indeed they would...were we able to approach them.
We had not anticipated that the man would be so reckless as to flee into the Black Shroud, and this oversight has necessitated our reliance upon you.

We know better than to cause a disturbance in the forest without the elementals' consent, but have not the luxury of time to observe the protocol. It is imperative that the Eye is recovered, and with the greatest of expedience.

To this end, Ishgard desires your cooperation in purging the area of hostile creatures, that the fugitive might be apprehended without causing undue disruption. At the risk of presuming too much...we would [@1A(1)]also[@1A(0)] have you identify the precise whereabouts of the one we seek.
We know full well that this is no small thing we ask of you. As such, you can expect to be recompensed fittingly for your kind assistance.

A dragoon clad in black, you say!? Tell me all that transpired!
By the Fury... That the Eye would choose another...
I had not thought it possible. In light of recent events, it would seem an explanation is in order.
The Eye is no ordinary relic. It harbors the power of the dragon, which it bestows upon a single chosen soul─the strongest and wisest dragoon.

He who is chosen is possessed of the power to fight our mortal foes, the dragons of Dravania, on equal footing, soaring the firmament as if it were an extension of the land. That man is known as the Azure Dragoon.
The Azure Dragoon is the light of hope for all Ishgardians, and the paragon of all dragoons.

...For this reason, you may imagine how it pains me to have to confess that the man you encountered, the [@1A(1)]thief[@1A(0)], is none other than the Azure Dragoon...and that [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] was once his teacher.
Needless to say, I acknowledge myself accountable for Estinien's misdeeds, and mean to do all in my power to find him and recover the Eye. But I cannot do this alone.
I require your help, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─you, who have received the power of the dragon.

You may labor to believe it, but there can be no mistake. The Soul of the Dragoon I bear glows in your presence─irrefutable proof that you are chosen. What I can ill explain, however, is the why of it.
Never before in Ishgard's long history has the Eye roused to more than one individual in a single generation. But it avails us naught to cudgel our brains about it.

The fact of the matter is that you are now a vessel for the power of the dragon. That dragon lies yet in slumber, however, and you must needs possess the means to wake it: the Soul of the Dragoon. I would entrust you with mine, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Like Estinien, I once ruled the skies as the Azure Dragoon, although that power has since become lost to me. It was simply by force of habit that I have hitherto kept the soul upon my person.
I have no inkling as to why the Eye has seen fit to choose a second, and an outsider at that.
Yet one thing is clear: none can challenge the Azure Dragoon and conceivably prevail save another Azure Dragoon.

You are our only hope of bringing Estinien to justice and reclaiming the Eye. Of course, I do not ask that you do this unaided. I may be a dragoon no more, but what knowledge I have, I shall gladly impart to you.
For indeed, when the time comes that you must face the Azure Dragoon, naught less than complete mastery over the power of the dragon will avail you.
That a perilous road lies ahead of you, I shall not deny. Knowing this, if you would still lend me your lance, I will teach you to harness the power that has chosen you.
Go forth, my young dragoon, and rouse the dragon within. I look forward to your return.
The next dragoon quest will be available from Alberic upon reaching level 35.
Ah, I daresay you might just be the right [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] for the job. The guild has urgent need of a capable lancer for a mission beyond our nation's borders. Hear me out, if you will.
You there! You have the bearing of a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] who can see a task through to the bitter end. We have urgent need of one such as you. Hear me out, if you will.
I've received word from an Ishgardian friend to the effect that he requires our aid. I would have you go and provide that aid.

As you may already know, due to her ongoing conflict with the dragons, Ishgard has kept her gates closed to outsiders for some time. The occasional dragoon on patrol duty is about all folk see these days.
In spite of her self-imposed isolation, however, the Holy See has never failed to honor her obligations to her allies.

It is only fitting that we answer the call and lend what assistance we can. To this end, we offered to dispatch a contingent of Wood Wailers with all haste─but were politely informed that they would not be welcome, much to our initial confusion.

It was later explained that we are dealing with a matter of some sensitivity, best handled by individuals who are capable and trustworthy, yet unbound by allegiance─and who fits that description save adventurers?
Secrecy being paramount, I can provide no details as to the nature of the task. All you need to know will be revealed at the rendezvous point.
Should you accept the mission, you must take yourself to the Gates of Judgement. A knight called Ser Alberic will receive you upon arrival.

Gridania thanks you, friend. Now then, as I have mentioned, your contact awaits at the Gates of Judgement, at the base of the ascent to Ishgard. To get there, first take yourself to Camp Glory in Coerthas, and thence follow the road west then north and west. May the elementals watch over you.

I shall not feign surprise at your reluctance. Truth be told, I might have questioned your sense had you blindly volunteered without a moment's hesitation. Well, should your spirit of adventure get the better of you, I shall be here.
The petitioner, Ser Alberic, awaits your coming at the Gates of Judgement, at the base of the ascent to Ishgard.
To get there, first take yourself to Camp Glory in Coerthas, and thence follow the road west then northwest. The Gates of Judgement will appear in sight before long.
You must be a level [@VALUE($E8(3))] [@SHEET(xtx/text_jobName,$E8(2),1)] and level [@VALUE($E8(5))] [@SHEET(xtx/text_jobName,$E8(4),1)] to begin the quest “[@SHEET(xtx/quest,$E8(1),2)].”
As part of your training, I would have you put down a monster called the bomb baron. The creature inhabits Cassiopeia Hollow, a short distance east of Camp Bloodshore in eastern La Noscea.

Not only will vanquishing the menace serve to hone your lance arm, it will also prove a great boon to the region's residents. And you may be assured that the experience will serve to stir the dragon within.
It is pleasing to see how readily the dragon stirs within you. You show great potential, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─a potential that may well prove the difference between victory and defeat.

Estinien is no ordinary dragoon, this you well know. Even among the lauded ranks of the Azures, however, the man is considered peerless. Such is his prowess, in fact, the day he was chosen by the Eye, it was proclaimed that Haldrath the Dragonseye had been reborn.

As promised, I shall train you in the way of the dragoon, that you might face Estinien as an equal. Before we commence, however, it is only fitting that you are edified regarding our origins. It all began a millennium past, when our forebears resided in the southern plains in humble circumstances.

The Fury, impressed by the spirit of our ancestors, decided it was meet that She make them Her own. So did She appear before Haldrath's sire, a man of courage and integrity named Thordan, and bade him lead Her people to the Promised Land─to what would become the great nation of Ishgard.

Their journey brought them to a wide chasm, whereupon Thordan and his people set to building a bridge. It was then that a dark shadow descended upon them─the great wyrm Nidhogg. Heedless of his own safety, Thordan fearlessly charged at the colossal beast. Alas, he was pushed into the chasm by one of his own, a man seduced by the wyrm, and fell to his death.

Taking up his slain sire's lance, Haldrath hurled himself at Nidhogg, even as tears streamed down his face. The confrontation ended when the young man, his hand guided by Halone, landed a mighty thrust that prized out Nidhogg's eye. With a terrible roar of pain, the great wyrm took wing and fled, while jubilation reigned below.

Ishgard's priceless relic is none other than the eye taken from Nidhogg that day. It is a veritable wellspring of dragon power─even so removed from its owner, it can exert control over the hearts of men.

Haldrath himself felt its malign influence, but his love of justice brooked no corruption, and he prevailed over the power, claiming it for his own. And so it was that the first Azure Dragoon was born.
Being derived from our foe, the power of the dragon is a thing to be loathed. But as Haldrath proved to us all, so long as our hearts burn with justice, we need not fear being taken in its thrall.

Ah, but what is justice, precisely? Justice assumes many shapes and forms, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and none can say that one is greater than another. So long as you hold fast to your beliefs and stay true to yourself, you leave no room for the power of the dragon to master you.

But enough of history─let us return our attention to the present. For reasons yet undetermined, the dragons have been stirring of late, those that had lain in deep slumber rousing themselves to wakefulness.

But a few days past, word arrived that a dragon had been sighted over La Noscea, a region well outside the creatures' habitual range. While no casualties were reported, the scent of a dragon has agitated the local fauna.
As part of your training, I would have you put down one such creature: the bomb baron. The monster inhabits Cassiopeia Hollow, a short distance east of Camp Bloodshore in eastern La Noscea.
Not only will vanquishing the menace serve to hone your lance arm, it will be a great boon to the region's residents.
The experience will surely help to stir the dragon within, and you will be one step closer to standing upon even ground with Estinien.
The set of your face attests to your resolve. Let us speak again once your task is accomplished. Take here this linkpearl, and may the Fury grant you strength.
None but you can decide for whom you wield your lance. Yet know that the Soul of the Dragoon answers not the call of the unworthy.

A young dragoon has been slain in the latest dragon attack. While the creature responsible has long since departed the scene, a spriggan known as Spitfire, presumably drawn by the scent of death, has set about desecrating our comrade's resting place. This cannot be tolerated─the creature must be vanquished.
Once you have seen to the vile beast, pay what respects you will to your comrade─to a fellow of the path who gave his life in the name of justice. In so doing, the dragon within you will surely stir.

You grow ever stronger, and I speak of more than just the flesh. Aye, you are slowly but surely realizing your potential as an Azure Dragoon. It is heartening to look upon...though I must confess that my presiding feeling is one of relief. You must understand, the mere thought that the Eye would choose an outsider─one who ill comprehends the threat posed by the dragons─filled me with the gravest of misgivings. Yet you have... Ah, but I shall say no more, lest flattery impede your improvement!

Now, during our last lesson, I enlightened you regarding the origins of dragoons. You will recall how Haldrath heroically triumphed over the great wyrm Nidhogg, and Ishgard came into possession of the Eye.

Tell me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─do you believe that these events truly transpired? Or are you inclined to think them faerie tales? I ask you this because few folk have seen dragons in the flesh besides we Ishgardians, and most would as soon dismiss them as products of the imagination.

Alas, dragons are no less real than you and I, with Nidhogg perhaps the most real of all. In the course of its history, Ishgard has suffered under the creature on eight separate occasions. Each time the great wyrm rouses, the blood of countless Ishgardians is spilled.
Let us revisit the past once more, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. The time is fifteen summers past, and the place Dravania.
After a century in slumber, Nidhogg awakened once more to resume his reign of terror. Entire villages were razed to the ground, their inhabitants reduced to ash.
Sensing the great wyrm's unbridled rage, others of his kind began to rouse, and in such numbers as to blot out the sun with their wings. A deep, foreboding darkness swept over Ishgard.

Raging infernos painting the belly of the sky an angry red... The agonized screams of innocents fading into deathly silence...[@CR]In my station as the Azure Dragoon, I was there through it all─bore witness to all the horrors.

But there was no time to offer even a silent prayer. Nidhogg lingered in one place only long enough to lay it to waste, and when he took wing, so too did I pursue him, a man possessed. This game of cat and mouse continued for what seemed an eternity before I was able to force a confrontation upon the great wyrm.

The battle unfolded in a tiny settlement on the edge of Coerthas, raging on for three days and three nights with neither side able to gain a decisive advantage. Remaining on my feet by sheer force of will, I realized that it must end now else it shouldn't end well. So, marshaling my last onze of strength, I wagered all on a single thrust.

My lance struck home, burying deep in the ruin of my opponent's empty eye socket. Yet before I could withdraw my weapon, the wyrm lashed out wildly in its agony, dealing a blow that left me sprawled upon the scorched earth, nigh insensate.

In that instant, I thought myself surely doomed...but Halone was not finished with me. Having lost the taste for battle, Nidhogg let loose a bloodcurdling roar before fleeing to the sky. The battle was over.

While I did not perish from my injuries, they rendered my body unfit to bear the power of the dragon, and I was Azure Dragoon no more. Lying bedridden, my thoughts wandered to all the innocent lives that had been lost─the people I had failed to protect.
That last conflict with the dragons of Dravania left countless orphans in its wake. Estinien is one of them, the sole survivor of Ferndale, the final village to suffer Nidhogg's wrath.

With none left to care for him, I did the only thing I could: I took Estinien as mine own son, instructing him in the way of the dragoon when he was of an age to learn. Yet I would not have you think me noble. My actions were born not of compassion but of guilt. My guilt at having failed him. And now I have failed him as a father─for what manner of man did I bring him up to be? A thief who would endanger the life of every one of his countrymen.

Aye, you heard me right─all of Ishgard may suffer for his crime. Though we know little and less of the minds of dragons, it is conceivable that the disturbance surrounding his stolen eye will cause Nidhogg to awaken once more. That his kin have been stirring to life serves as fair warning of that.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I fear yet another dragon attack has been reported, this time in the vicinity of Millers' Glade in the eastern lowlands of Coerthas.

Alas, this time, a casualty has been confirmed: a young dragoon dispatched to deal with the creature. While it has long since departed the scene, a spriggan known as Spitfire, presumably drawn by the scent of death, has set about desecrating our comrade's final resting place. Needless to say, this cannot be tolerated.
We dragoons hold comradery as sacred, and the least we can do for our fallen is to ensure them peace. To this end, I ask that you make for Millers' Glade, and there slay this Spitfire.
Let us give prayer, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─a prayer for those poor souls taken fifteen summers past.
See to the vile beast, and pay what respects you will to your comrade─to a fellow of the path who gave his life in the name of justice. In so doing, the dragon within you will surely stir.
There is no shame in being afraid, for that is the only time a man can be brave. There is shame, however, in running from one's fears.

Estinien would trade words with us, and bids us meet him in the foothills southwest of Skyfire Locks. The southbound highroad will take us near to there.
Let us go and discover what it is the man would propose.
Estinien...
F-Forgive me. I was deep in thought. Now then, as to acquiring the armor of which Estinien spoke...
Were you a dragoon of Ishgard, it would simply be a matter of requesting it of the armory. Alas, that option is unavailable to us, and we must needs take the circuitous route.
As Estinien explained, ancient custom decrees that, at the end of his fighting days, the Azure Dragoon must seal away his armor at those places where he shed his blood in the name of justice.

We will help ourselves to that armor─the drachen mail─using the Soul of the Dragoon to open the way. Given the dire circumstance, I have no doubt that our forerunners will be obliging. Now, lest you forget, allow me to recite the location of each piece.
The Aurum Vale, in the central lowlands of Coerthas. The cave north of Camp Brittlebark, in southeastern Mor Dhona.
The U'Ghamaro Mines, at the northern edge of upper La Noscea. And lastly, the cave north of Camp Bluefog, in northern Thanalan.
Once the mail is in your possession, we shall see to it that your inner dragon achieves perfect awakening. Go well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and may the Fury grant you strength.
The swiftness with which your inner dragon rouses is a sight to behold. If there is a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] who can end Estinien's madness, it is surely you.
It is imperative that we recover the Eye before Nidhogg senses the disturbance and stirs to life. To this end, you must endeavor to realize your potential as an Azure Dragoon.
The next dragoon quest will be available from Alberic upon reaching level 45.
Impeccable timing, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. A message arrived from Estinien but moments ago, much to my astonishment.
He would trade words with us, and bids us meet him in the foothills southwest of Skyfire Locks. As to his true intentions, I cannot say.
It may well be a trap, but we must go nonetheless. I trust I can count upon your company.
That is well. Let us go and discover what it is Estinien would propose.
I shall not press you if you are disinclined, but there may not be a better opportunity to take the measure of your opponent. I urge you to reconsider.

You must take yourself to Camp Riversmeet, in the western highlands of Coerthas, and thence strike south till you come upon the place whence the camp took its name. Once there, seek out and slay the drake known as Stollenwurm.
By locking wills with this adversary and prevailing, you will prove yourself worthy to champion the cause to which your lance is sworn. The dragon within you shall then awaken with a mighty roar.
So you return bearing four pieces of the drachen mail. That leaves us with the fifth and final item.

Aye, there exists one more piece to the set. However, it cannot be worn save by those dragoons who have achieved perfect awakening of the dragon within. This is something you must attend to presently.

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]...I would hear something from your lips. As a fellow Azure Dragoon, will you join your strength to Estinien's, that Ishgard might forever more be free from the rage of the great wyrm?
I see...
Then I shall honor my promise to Estinien. You shall have full use of your powers by the time we are done.

Before we begin, there is something I must needs confess. You will recall the tale of my battle with Nidhogg fifteen years past, how the power of the dragon left me on account of the injuries I sustained.
What I said was an untruth. The power did not abandon me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. It was I who abandoned it.

Being derived from our mortal enemies, the power of the Azure Dragoon is a double-edged sword. Even as it lends us the strength we need to smite dragons, it heightens our communion with the creatures, rendering our minds more susceptible to their seduction than ordinary men.

Even as I buried my lance in Nidhogg's flesh, our gazes locked, and mine eyes met then with a look that would fair impale a man. In that instant, I found myself assailed by a torrent of emotions not mine own...

Sorrow... Rancor... Pity... They threatened to drown the man in me and leave behind a dragon. Fearing that I might turn traitor, I chose to purge myself of the power that the Eye had bestowed upon me.
Thus regaining lucidity, I was able to rout the grievously wounded Nidhogg.
Alas, countless of his brethren yet remained. As if to mock me, they fell upon Ferndale with a vengeance. Bereft of my power, it was all I could do to save but one child.
Nary a soul knows of this. Nay, not even Estinien...but I can keep him in the dark no longer.
At our last meeting, Estinien said that protecting Ishgard and exacting revenge upon Nidhogg are as one to him.

That frame of mind, I fear, may well lead to his demise. The desire to protect and the desire to avenge are opposing forces that can ill be reconciled. Worse, the latter serves only to cloud his sense of self.

When next Estinien and I meet, I intend to confess all, though it mean the loss of his good opinion. The outcome of the coming battle─and his very life─may well depend upon his readiness to relinquish his powers.

Never allow yourself to forget the origin of your strength. Ever does the dragon lurk behind your eyes, biding its time, ready to claim you for its own. Aught less than complete conviction, and you will find yourself in its vice-like grip.
So forewarned, let us return to our present endeavor.

You must take yourself to Camp Riversmeet, in the western highlands of Coerthas, and thence strike south till you come upon the place whence the camp took its name. Once there, seek out and slay the drake known as Stollenwurm.
Being close kin to dragons, drakes also hold sway over the hearts of they who wield dragon power.
Lock wills with this adversary and prevail. In so doing, prove yourself worthy to champion the cause to which your lance is sworn. Then the dragon within you shall awaken with a mighty roar.
I expected no other answer. We have come far─let us not rest till we achieve full awakening of your inner dragon.
Only by confronting our weaknesses can we grow strong. I shall be here when you are ready to confront yours.

Estinien awaits at the Griffin Bridge, southeast of here.
Let us go and finish this, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
When the being of darkness closed upon us, you appeared to me a spitting image of Haldrath the Dragonseye as he is depicted in the holy scriptures.
I thought that mayhap the years had taken their toll on my mind, but behold─the Soul of the Dragoon shines as it never did in all the years I bore it.
It would seem you have achieved that which was thought impossible: you have awakened to the ability that none but the first Azure Dragoon possessed.
I-I can scarce believe mine eyes─the selfsame armor worn by Haldrath! To think that it had been sealed within the soul crystal all this time...
I have borne witness to many and more wonders over the years, yet none compares to you, my young dragoon. Could it be that you are...?

Ahem. Mark not my mutterings. I should rather have said that your indomitable sense of justice resonated with the spirit of the first Azure Dragoon, prompting him to bestow the armor upon you. Yes, that is doubtless what happened.

As the being of darkness faded, so too did Nidhogg's aura subside. And now his kind have ceased their stirring. Whether this was compelled by your awakening, I cannot say. I suspect we will learn the truth of it eventually.
Estinien, my dear boy... Whatever becomes of him, he will ever be as a son to me.
I pray that he is somewhere out there still...and that he has not wholly forgotten the great man he once was.

When that darkness brushed against me, the selfsame torrent of emotions swept over me as those I experienced fifteen summers past. But there was something else besides. There was a voice, and it lamented the rift that divides dragons and men.
You will come to comprehend what I speak in due time. Till then, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I pray that you will ever use your newfound strength in the name of justice.
Nidhogg is a lord among his kind. Aught less than complete conviction, and you will surely fall under his thrall.
Before you can master your foe, you must needs master yourself. Hone your lance arm till it can bear no further honing, and then present yourself to me.
I look forward to our next meeting, my young dragoon.
The next dragoon quest will be available from Alberic upon reaching level 50.

Ah, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! An urgent message arrived from Estinien in your absence. He bids you come at once to Griffin Crossing, southeast of here. It would seem Nidhogg is on the move─and rather sooner than we had anticipated.
We are racing against time, I fear, and the final piece of the drachen mail must wait. Are you ready to face Nidhogg, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]?
Then let us away. Estinien must know the truth of Ferndale, lest he fall for the great wyrm's seduction.
Every second we tarry could be costing lives. Whatever it is you must do, pray do it quickly and speak with me once more.
