You're an adventurer, if these eyes aren't mistaken. I hear you lot never turn down a chance to make quick gil. Well, I happen to have just the task for you.
Not more than a few suns past, as I was making my way back from Gridania, I came upon a peculiar carriage being pulled by chocobos.

It was all I could do to hide my astonishment when a [@1A(1)]goblin[@1A(0)]─the first I'd seen in these parts in well over a decade─sprang out and hailed me. As if to compound my amazement, he turned out to be rather an agreeable fellow, and we were soon chattering like old friends.

When I told him I was a merchant, the little chap's eyes─such as they were─twinkled with delight. Excitedly, he asked if I might be able to procure some dark matter for him, before grabbing me by the wrist and thrusting a handsome amount of coin into my palm.

I could scarce believe my good fortune...until he added that ordinary dark matter wouldn't do─only a specific variety, riddled with impurities. Now, I had my doubts as to why anyone would want impure dark matter, but I'd already taken the man's coin, and a merchant's only as good as his word.

So it was that I commenced to combing all four corners of the realm in search of the blasted stuff. And, after much painstaking effort, here it is: dark matter fused with fossil. All that remains for the bargain to be fulfilled is to see the merchandise safely delivered to my client, the goblin Mutamix. And [@1A(1)]this[@1A(0)], my friend, is the task I need you for.
Mutamix and his crew have set up camp north of Ul'dah, halfway up a sheer cliff. Keep an eye out for a mysterious cloud of smoke, and you'll soon find the place.
What's that? Why don't I make the delivery myself? A fair question, and it's only right I answer, lest you worry that I'm playing you false.

The fact is, the Brass Blades are concerned about the sudden resurgence of goblins in the area, and have been keeping them under tight surveillance. Being an Ul'dahn merchant, of course, it wouldn't do for me to be seen in the company of beastmen, so I've been forced to turn to outsiders like yourself.

Do me this favor, friend, and I'll see to it you're more than fairly compensated. I am promised the remainder of my payment upon delivery─that entire amount will be yours to keep. A veritable windfall, even if I say so myself.

My thanks, adventurer! I knew you had more sense than to let this opportunity pass you by.[@CR]Now then, you must see to it that the merchandise is delivered intact to Mutamix. My good reputation rests upon your shoulders!

Good coin for performing the simplest of tasks? Such opportunities are rare indeed. Take it from me: you'll do far worse work than this, my friend, and for far less. Anyway, I'll be here should you have a change of heart.
Mutamix and his crew have set up camp north of Ul'dah, halfway up a sheer cliff. Keep an eye out for a mysterious cloud of smoke, and you'll soon find the place.
Pshhh... Shkohhh...?[@CR]Who is uplander come to tent-ring of Mutamix Bubblypots?

Uplander bring [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,10013008,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,10013008,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] from goodsbearer Aistan? Ahee-hee-hee! Now catalysts are complete!
Pshhh? Uplander wants to know about sweatytime of Mutamix? Mutamix gives uplander tongueflaps. Uplander stand ears to attention now.

Fighty-tool drinks in airyself. When full of airyself, fighty-tool changes to stonyshine, name of [@1A(1)]materia[@1A(0)]. Uplander makes materia join with other fighty-tool, then...bigeyes! Fighty-tool gains power of airyself!
What materia will airyself of uplander become? What power will uplander gain? Imagining fills Mutamix with many heartthumps![@CR]Here, uplander take jinglyshine of wordbond!
Gods damn it, what in the seven hells was this materia, again? Was it fire...or fire veil? Gah! They both look the same!
Oh, beg pardons, friend. I'm prone to the odd outburst, though it does me no credit. Now then, like so many others, you've no doubt come here seeking the secrets of materia.
Come now, there's no call for shyness! It is Master Mutamix's wish that materia be made to benefit one and all.
I would be glad to initiate you into our mysteries, after which you will have a chance to demonstrate what you've learned.
That is well! Without further ado, let the lesson commence! Ahem!

Materia, strictly speaking, is a kind of crystal. It is created by reducing equipment into its aetheric constituents and then crystallizing them. Not just any old equipment will serve, mind you, only those pieces that have sufficient [@1A(1)]spiritbond[@1A(0)]─that being a measure of how fully an item has been imbued with its owner's spirit.

Now, you're no doubt wondering how it's possible that objects of varied shapes and sizes can be rendered into materia. The answer, my friend, is [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,2001001,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,2001001,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], a most subtle and ingenious device conceived by none other than Master Mutamix himself.

[@2B([@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,2001001,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,2001001,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)])] operates by transitorily sublimating objects into a form not far departed from dark matter. That is to say, an astral substance possessed of the faculty of metaphysical resonan─
...I see from your blank expression that I've confused you. If it's any comfort, you're not the first. Allow me to put it in layman's terms.
See my axe? Well, since the day she was forged, she's been brimming with the aetheric energy of a cleaving weapon, right?

Right! But through many long years of faithful service, she now holds another kind of energy, too─that of her wielder's desire for victory. And the accumulated concentration of that stuff is what determines her aetheric alignment with her owner, yours truly.

[@2B([@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,2001001,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,2001001,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)])] works by crystallizing these two kinds of aetheric energy into specific varieties of materia. In the case of my axe, gods bless her, it'll be one that grants enhanced strength.

Well, if it ain't a fellow Disciple of the Land. I s'pose ye already know about dark matter─aye, the stuff folk use t' mend every bloody thing nowadays.

Accordin' t' Master Mutamix, dark matter comes from rocks what fell from the sky. Stuff's older'n Eorzea, he says, and landed here gods know how long ago─but owin' to its habit o' bondin' with anythin' it touches, it's remained hidden from sight...'til recently, that is.

I don't know the why of it, but lately dark matter's been separatin' off again, allowin' keen-eyed Disciples o' the Land like usselves to spot it. Queerly, though, there's some dark matter what don't quite separate fully, leavin' it part-melded to its host material.

This impure stuff's worthless for repairs, but as it turns out, there's another use for it─as a catalyst for meldin' materia. Without catalysts, there ain't no way t' attach materia to gear, see. An' materia what can't be attached to gear's about as useful as nipples on a breastplate.

Now, I reckon ye can appreciate that catalysts spell good coin for us gatherin' types. Only thing is, they're a deal harder t' spot than yer ordinary dark matter. There's a trick to it, t' be sure, an' bein' the charitable bloke I am, I'm willin' t' teach ye, provided ye're willin' t' learn.
But o' course ye want t' learn how t' find catalysts! An' seein' as ye're so eager, let's get on with the lesson, shall we?
Now, there're three common types o' catalyst: carbonized matter got through minin', germinated matter got through harvestin', and calcified matter got through fishin'.

The type ye get depends on the method o' gatherin' ye're usin'. But before ye go reachin' for yer favorite pickaxe, hatchet, or rod, ye'll recall I mentioned there bein' a trick to findin' catalysts, an' so there is─an ability, more specifically, taught me by Master Mutamix hisself.
“Fingerprints o' the Gods,” 'tis called. Without it, ye might as well be searchin' for a needle in a haystack what don't have no needles in it─usin' naught but yer sense o' smell.
Now, clean the wax out o' yer ears, 'cause I'm gonna teach ye how the ability works.
Catalysts can only be gathered by Disciples of the Land for whom the Fingerprints of the Gods ability is active.
Here, lend me yer map. I'll mark a choice gatherin' point or two where ye can put theory t' practice.

Use an ability such as Lay of the Land, Arbor Call, or Gulleye to locate a grade 1 gathering point. Upon finding a suitable spot, ensure that Fingerprints of the Gods is set, and then commence gathering.

...An' that about sums it up. Now run along an' give that ability a try. Oh, an' have a flick through the tome over there if summat ain't clear.

The only answer I expected! I mean, what self-respecting Disciple of the Hand wouldn't be thrilled at the prospect of learning new ways to enhance equipment? But without further ado, let the training commence!
First, a review of the properties of materia. As you may have heard, materia is a synthetic stone born of the aetheric energies that reside within equipment.

Although each individual piece of materia holds tremendous power, that power remains dormant until such time as the stone is attached to a suitable host item. However, conventional methods of attachment─meaning a hammer, nails, and toil─will not serve.
Materia is formed of both physical and astral matter, you see, and as such, a special substance known as a catalyst is required to stabilize and meld it to equipment.

Catalysts occur in nature, but can only be gathered by Disciples of the Land. If you want for an acquaintance who can supply you with some, you may want to save yourself a few gil and do the procuring yourself. In which case, you'd do well to speak with my fellow Carrier of the Cauldron, Kokosamu.

Now, this next part is important, so heed my words well. The type of catalyst required for the melding process varies with materia. Similarly, you can attach specific materia only to certain types of equipment.
Of course, even assuming you pair everything up correctly, if you lack the skills needed to craft the host item, you can forget about attaching any materia to it.
The requirements for melding, such as class level and compatible equipment and catalysts, can be reviewed by examining individual pieces of materia inside your inventory.

You should know also that certain gear can't host materia. I speak of age-old articles whose contact with countless souls has rendered their aetheric alignment permanently unstable. Such gear, referred to as “soul-worn,” is unsuited to bearing materia, and neither skill nor ingredients can remedy this.

It shared its rations with her, loosened her bonds to allow her sleep, and spared her the tortures of its comrades. Were it not for that one Amalj'aa, she believes she would certainly have died.

Of course, we knew naught of this when we attacked the Amalj'aa camp...and the beast was among those that fell during the ensuing battle. Wounded grievously, it bled to death before her eyes as she lay bound and gagged, powerless to help. She blames herself for its death─and it seems it was this thought which drove her wits from her.

As for the ring you've recovered, Theda told us that it was a gift from that same Amalj'aa...though I suppose it is more of a keepsake now. You may leave it with me. I will see that it makes its way to her hand once more.

That trust is then manipulated to obtain what they truly seek─in this case, knowledge of our thaumaturgical arts. A case of good Amalj'aa, bad Amalj'aa, as it were. Near every hamlet in the region has such a story, and many and more end with smallfolk turning to the side of the Amalj'aa.

Whether it was yet another instance of this, or a truly compassionate Amalj'aa, perhaps we shall never know. But I for one am certainly not about to abandon my mistrust nor hatred for the race at large given the possibility of one gentle soul.

No, it ain't my place to speak ill of the dead─mine nor no one's. All that concerns me now is that the girl is sent over proper. We'll make offerings of treehollow brew and say our prayers, as we do for all our departed.

But there are foul souls in the forest these days, angering the elementals something fierce. I'll not wager a guess as to which is more dangerous─but I can say as there won't be no Hyrstmill folk leaving the safety of the camp with things as they stand.

That being so, might be as a [@IF($E9(4),sturdy lass,strapping lad)] like yerself could lend Hyrstmill a hand. If ye'd bring us [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000162,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000162,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], we could honor the girl's memory in our way, see. It's pungent stuff, made by the lemurs near Treespeak, 'case ye're wondering.

The lemurs near Treespeak are surly buggers, an' won't shy from a fight. Hells, 'tis a struggle for Hyrstmill's finest to lay 'em low. No doubt ye fancy yerself more'n capable, but don't go letting yer guard down, alright?
Show some bloody compassion! Have ye no respect for the dead?

[@2B([@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000163,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000163,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)])]! You've brought them! As you may have gleaned from my relief, all efforts to reach the elementals since your departure have yielded nothing.
I shall make use of the stones right away. A moment, please.
...By the gods! Th-The stones! They've all cracked in two! Just as I felt the whispers of the elementals taking form, they simply...shattered!
This is surely an omen─a dark portent of things to come. The Seedseer Council must be informed! It is they who interpret the will of the Twelveswood. They will know what to do.
Here, payment for the stones. Use it to prepare yourself─for I fear the coming darkness will soon be upon us...

Please, bring me [@IF($E5(5,0),[@IF($E2(5,10),[@SWITCH(5,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(5)])],[@VALUE(5)])] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000163,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000163,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] as quickly as you are able. You will have no choice but to slay them, yet their sacrifice will at least serve a higher purpose.
Then go now, with all haste. Time is of the essence. I shall continue my attempts to commune with the elementals in your absence.
You have heard my words, yet fail to understand their significance. I pity you. Really, I do.
Our scouts tracked the Ixal as far as Quarrymill before losing the trail. They're like to be somewhere near there still. Find those damned vultures, and end their days of preying upon forestfolk.

Words travel fast in the wood, friend─faster than you by far. Our scouts found the corpses of the Ixal you sent to meet their maker. Let us pray it is enough to quench the vengeance of the elementals.
When their fury is on them, there is no safety to be had in the wood─not even for those of us who fight to protect it.
The beast tribes are as different from us as night from day─plain and simple. There's no sense trying to understand them, much less live side by side.

And a swift exile from Gridania awaits any who hold otherwise. Aye, we had a healer years ago who found that out to his cost. Seemed a good enough sort...until the day he tended to the wounds of an injured bloody Ixal, citing “the healers' oath” or some such nonsense. What could possibly bring a man to take pity on that filth? <spit>
But I've kept you long enough. No doubt you are eagerly awaiting your reward. Very well, here you are. Continue to fight the good fight, friend.

I've neither the time nor the stomach to bandy words, so I'll say this straight─I need your help, adventurer. One of the Quiver's new recruits came across a band of Ixal that had stolen into the Twelveswood.

They clawed the poor bastard to within an ilm of his life before they were chased off. We and the Wailers are scouring the wood for them now, but we don't have the numbers to be everywhere at once. These fiends must be put down before another of our own meets the same fate...or worse.

I need a brave soul to hunt down these damned vultures, and end their days of preying upon forestfolk. Our scouts tracked them as far as Quarrymill before losing the trail. They're like to be somewhere near there still.
Then make what preparations you must and be off. There is no time to waste.
You would risk the wrath of the elementals before that of the Ixal? I'll never understand you outsiders.

Noticed something off about the stalls today, friend? Aye, not so lively as normal, are they? Ain't no surprise, neither. None among us was able to come up with what Fafajon was looking for, see, and he weren't too happy about it.
He's one of the richest men around these parts, and new to them as well. Just came up from Ul'dah, where he made his fortune.
He had a mind to set up some new dealings with the Knights of Ishgard, selling them Mun[@1F]Tuy brew. Hell of a drink, that. Puts you flat on your back and feeling it for a week.
But brewing it ain't no easy thing. You've got to get your hands on a waspwing stone─a bloody rare thing. And [@1A(1)]that's[@1A(0)] what Fafajon was 'round here looking for.

Now every merchant in Gridania's running about like an opo[@1F]opo with its head chopped off. Can't blame them, though. Being in the good graces of Fafajon'll get damn near anyone damn near anything they fancy.
Me? Hells, I ain't the type to dive headfirst into a blooming ruction without a damn good reason.
So what I'd like to know first is what them Ishgardians think of the brew Fafajon's already sent. Don't see no point in tracking down the nectar if they ain't pleased with the product.

Why get your knickers in a twist if they don't even like the bloody stuff? So how's about doing ol' Lefwyne a favor? Head over to Owl's Nest in Coerthas and ask the Ishgardians face[@1F]to[@1F]face how the Mun[@1F]Tuy brew sits with 'em.
I owe you a debt, friend. Now, things can get a bit hairy out that way, so be sure and steer clear of danger, you hear?
I suppose it doesn't sound like the most interesting quest in the world... Can't say I blame you.

Bugger the bloody nectar for now. I want to know what the Ishgardians think of the brew Fafajon's already sent first. Hurry to Owl's Nest in Coerthas, and ask them yourself. I'll be waiting right here.
Things can get a bit hairy out that way. Be sure and steer clear of danger, you hear?
Have you business here, traveler? Mun[@1F]Tuy brew? You speak of the drink sent us by the merchant Fafajon, yes?
Truth be told, we had our doubts. That Lalafell is not the most reputable looking fellow, but in the end he was as good as his word.

This drink, this Mun[@1F]Tuy─I am told it is brewed by fermenting a bean mash of some sort. Drinking it seems to have an immediate effect on a man's vigor. It is rich in nutrients, and keeps easily besides. It must be consumed in moderation, to be sure─lest we have a drunken army─but the same could be said of all such draughts. Still...it does have one...minor drawback.
The stuff reeks! Urgh, gods, just thinking about it is enough t─ <heave> ...I swear by the Twelve, it's the most revolting bloody smell your nostrils will ever have the misfortune to know! <heave>

“Invigorating,” eh? Well, leave it to Fafajon. The man's a true merchant, he is. Bloody hells, if this deal is made, he'll have extended his influence from the Sea of Ash to the Spine.

But they've no stomach for the stink of it, have they? Well, ain't no surprise there. Without sourleaf nectar, Mun[@1F]Tuy brew reeks like a latrine in a smokehouse. Gods know how they managed to down that.

Well then, it looks as if I still have need of you, friend. Go and gather me [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000202,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000202,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. When that day comes, rest assured, you'll never have to pay full price. Hells, you're practically my partner! For now, though, take this, and my thanks along with it.

East of Camp Tranquil! That is where you shall find the goblins who made off with my [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000221,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000221,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]!

My precious [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000221,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000221,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], come home to me!

During your journeys, you will likely come across moko grass and cotton bolls; feathers of this bird and that.
Do not toss them aside, or sell them for quick coin. Don the weaver's mantle, and seize the chance to practice your craft.
You'll not hear more sound advice this day.
And here's a little something to help set your hands to the loom. Purchase a needle from the merchants here, and before you know it, you'll be well on the way to sewing yourself a new wardrobe!

My beautiful...my exquisite...my irreplaceable [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000221,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000221,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]!

Away with you, then. Do not return without my [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000221,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000221,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], oh mighty hero!

I shall remain here and watch over my flock until you have slain the foul dreadwolves roaming the hills nearby. I would venture that the death of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] would put fear enough into the hearts of the others that they would think twice before attacking even a shepherd such as myself.
Adventurer! You have slain the dreadwolves and returned unharmed! These are good tidings, indeed!
I, myself, bear good tidings as well. You see, my missing sheep were found by a fellow shepherd scarcely a bell ago. It seems they had joined his flock when they could not find their own.
Ah! Prithee do not think your efforts this day were for naught. The dreadwolves have plagued our hamlet for many generations, but for now they are gone. Your valiant deed will not be soon forgotten.

Ah...but grateful though I am, I find my heart is yet troubled by the strange events which first caused my flock to take flight... I recall a dark shadow passing overhead, followed by a terrible howl and a rumbling that shook the birds from their trees.
My first thought was that it must be a dragon, but the form and size of the thing were unlike aught I had ever seen. And never before has a dragon caused the land to tremble...
Which can only mean the apparition was an airship. But this cannot be possible, for there has yet to be word of the recommencement of flights to the Holy See and its outlying landings.

I suppose there is always the possibility that it was an [@1A(1)]imperial[@1A(0)] airship, but that would mean... No, such thoughts are foolish. What would the Empire want with Coerthas? It [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)] have been a dragon.

Ah, but I have wasted enough time on idle speculation. I have sheep to tend, and I am sure you are eager to return to your travels. You have my thanks once again, adventurer. Here, a reward for your kind assistance. Farewell, and may the Fury give you strength.
An adventurer in Owl's Nest! This is most certainly a sign from the Twelve. Might I ask of you a favor?

My name is Patrick, and I am but a humble shepherd making his living here in the mountains of Coerthas. I take my flock to pasture each morning, and lead them back here to their pen each night, as my family has done for seven generations.

However, last night, as I was gathering the animals for the journey home, two of my ewes took fright and ran off into the hills. I was tempted to give chase, but the sun had already passed below the nearby peaks, and I knew there was not nearly enough time to both find the sheep [@1A(1)]and[@1A(0)] guide my flock back to safety before darkness fell in the valley.

And so...I did what I knew I must. Yet it pains me to know that a pair of my poor children is still out there in the hills, lost and cold...and in grave danger. You see, this area is home to a pack of bloodthirsty wolves, and if not found quickly, my ewes have little chance of survival.

As I said, I am but a shepherd, unlearned in the ways of war. Though I might have strength enough to stave off the jaws of a single wolf, I fear I would not last long against a whole pack. A well[@1F]traveled adventurer, on the other hand, would surely fare rather better. Might you consent to cull the beasts, that I may search for my stray sheep?

You are a Twelvesend, good [@IF($E9(4),lady,sir)]! I shall remain here and watch over my flock until you have slain the foul dreadwolves roaming the hills nearby. It is impossible to know just how many of the creatures there are, but I would venture that the death of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] would put fear enough into the hearts of the others that they would think twice before attacking again.
You have my apologies. It was unmeet to ask of a stranger such a boon.
My patient will be most pleased when he learns you have agreed to help us. It was he who revealed to me the recipe of the sheepbur poultice.

And to think that a common weed could possess such healing properties! <sigh> There is so little we know of the forest, and so much [@1A(1)]they[@1A(0)] could teach us, if only we would put aside our differences...
You found the seeds! And not a moment too soon, I may add. The Ixal's wounds have begun to supp─
<gasp> I mean the, uh... I-I mean... Oh dear. I apologize for not saying anything earlier, but you must believe me when I tell you that my intentions were pure.
I cared only of my patient's well-being, and did not wish something as trivial as bigotry to prevent him from receiving the treatment he deserved.

During my apprenticeship as a healer, I learned the importance of never denying a man succor. However, in Gridania, where I used to provide my services, the people grow up being taught that the Ixal are foul beings who do not belong in the forest. My willingness to offer aid to those deemed outsiders often put me at odds with my colleagues.

Which is how I ended up here. Though not a few score malms from the Black Shroud, the people in this sleepy hamlet adhere to a completely different set of values─those established by the Holy See of Ishgard. And while I wouldn't go as far as branding one set wrong and another right, I find my work better tolerated in Owl's Nest. That's not to say the villagers don't have their misgivings about accepting me...

Yet one thing is certain─it matters little how others perceive me and my actions, as this is the path I have chosen to follow. The Spinner may see fit to nudge me one way or another, but it is I who determine my own destiny. Nothing is set in stone, my friend. Change is but a step away, if you are only brave enough to take it.

Good adventurer, I find myself in something of a predicament and would appreciate any assistance you could provide. Late last night, I stumbled upon a man lying half-conscious outside the main gate. Seeing at once that he was grievously wounded, I resolved to carry him back to my hovel─where he now rests.

I cleaned and bandaged the cuts the best I could, but due to a lack of [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000177,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000177,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], I have as yet been unable to prepare the herbal poultice necessary to ensure the wounded areas do not fester.

I cannot stray far from my patient, for there is still the possibility that his condition may worsen, yet I cannot ask others in the hamlet for assistance for reasons that remain rather...complicated. Which leaves me no other choice than to place the life of this man in the hands of a stranger.

Sheepbur is a plant native to Coerthas, but it is tiny and wont to grow in the shade of larger shrubs, making it a nightmare to find. However, its barbed seeds have been known to snag on the furry hides of antelope does that graze in the region, and remain entangled there for many moons. In short, your efforts might better be spent hunting antelope than the plant itself, especially given the relatively modest quantity required for the poultice. I need hardly add that time is of the essence.

You have my thanks, adventurer. I require no fewer than [@IF($E5(5,0),[@IF($E2(5,10),[@SWITCH(5,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(5)])],[@VALUE(5)])] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000177,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000177,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] to complete my patient's poultice.

Scouring the hills for the tiny plant and its seeds would almost certainly take too long, which leaves us with no other option but to hunt doe antelopes in the hope of finding burs entangled in their fur. Antelope are known to graze near the stretch of Thordan's March south of Camp Glory, so I suggest you start your search there.
I see that you are no different from the heartless churls I left back in Gridania.
You hear a rustling behind you...
Y-You're back!? This is... This is most unexpected. Then I presume my wife...and the cultists are...dead?
Hm? I don't seem very upset? Ah, well, there is a reason for that. You see...
...this is even better than I ever could have imagined!
The blood of loyalists slain in His service will please the Hound far more than that of a nonbeliever.
You have served us well, adventurer, as did my wife!
Yes, she was one of the first to give herself to the Hound when we began to see signs of His return.
You see, the Lambs of Dalamud do not fear death, for it is written that the Hound will remember the scent of the blood of those who offered themselves to guide Him back to the corporeal realm.
And He will descend to the Gates of the Seventh Hell to bring our souls back to Eorzea, where we shall serve Him in the seventh and final Umbral Era.
Ah...my words kindle the flames of vengeance in your heart... Good. Let them engulf you!

We already have an agent aboard the Astalicia operating under the guise of a crewmember. His name is Hasthwab. You will take this bottle of vintage rum to him and make it seem as if you are bribing him for information on Shposhae. He will, in turn, aid you in gaining access to the caves.

The task will most like prove a difficult one, but you must not flinch in the face of danger. To do so would be to concede the future of the thalassocracy to those who would see this city[@1F]state fall into chaos. Good luck, and godsspeed.

Seek out Hasthwab on the Astalicia. He may appear a pirate, but he is actually one of us, as loyal as a hound and as sharp as a fox. Give him this bottle of vintage rum, and play along with his charade until he chooses a time to reveal to you what he has learned of Shposhae.

Gah hah hah hah! What do we 'ave 'ere!? Another wharf rat come sniffin' 'round th' deck fer an 'unk o' cheese, is it? Well, ye'll get less than bugger all from me─'cept a bloody nose an' an 'earty kick [@IF($E9(4),up the arse,in th' bollocks)], o' course!
Hm? What be this, 'ere? Vintage rum? Vintage...rum...? Oh!
Radz[@1F]at[@1F]Han reserve! Well, I'll be! Seems some folk in this town still 'as proper manners. Aye, I suppose I can tell ye what I know o' the Sahagin den.

(Greetings! I was told someone bearing vintage rum would be along soon. You must forgive me for the brash display I put on earlier. I must wear that facade at all times, lest the crew here learn my true identity.)

(As for information regarding the treasure of Shposhae, I will relay all I have learned anon, but you must forgive me for doing so in character. Now...ahem, accost me again as if I were lost in a rum-induced reverie!)
We'll need all the heroes we can muster to restore the Immortal Flames to their former glory. Go now, and find whatever word there is to be had of warriors fit to champion our cause.
So you seek to recruit heroes for the Immortal Flames? Curious...

Now, as in times long past, the Immortal Flames serve the sultana. The finest souls in the realm are being rallied to our banners. We shall know victory, whether you adventurers cast your lot with us or no.
Still, the efforts of the Gladiators' Guild are reassuring, to say the least. Very well, I shall give you the names of several strong, sure warriors.
The Coliseum does Ul'dah a great service by amassing this information. Thank you.
Champions to enlist in the Immortal Flames, eh? Wouldn't that fall under the thaumaturges' jurisdiction?

Bah, bugger the Order. This is hardly the time for formalities, what with sightings of Garlean airships increasing by the day. If we do nothing but continue to watch, we'll soon be watching our city walls come down around us!

To be sure, nothing would do more for the morale of the nation than the gathering of heroes under the banner of the Immortal Flames. Allow me to give you a few of the more respected names mentioned here at the Adventurers' Guild.
To be sure, nothing would do more for the morale of the nation than the gathering of heroes under the banner of the Immortal Flames. I pray you find us many great souls.
Gathering great warriors to join the Immortal Flames of Ul'dah, is it?
By fire reborn! The Immortal Flames burn again! As we speak, Ul'dah is already undergoing a vast restructuring.
There will be new opportunities for all─rich and poor alike. [@1A(1)]That[@1A(0)] is what has the people so excited.
Aye, I know a number of able men and women─just the type you seek. Here, their names. May the Twelve see them into the service of Ul'dah.
There are those empowered in name who are powerless. And those who wield true power with no name. Travel the city and learn what you will─but know truth from falsehood.
Hm? What is it, dear [@IF($E9(4),girl,boy)]? I'm [@1A(1)]frightfully[@1A(0)] busy, you see.
Searching for heroes? Is that so? Well, I will [@1A(1)]always[@1A(0)] lend my support to any initiative offering opportunities to the gladiatorially gifted!
Enlistment? Then the Immortal Flames have begun building their army of heroes. It seems the rumors have turned to truth.
This means it will be open war between Ul'dah and Garlemald. And if the wheels are already in motion, it must be that Raubahn Aldynnn has returned to us, as well.
Raubahn Aldynn was once a great champion of the bloodsands, and former owner of the Coliseum. In all my years, I've yet to see any match his prowess in battle.

There is an entire generation of young warriors who train day in and day out, aspiring to repeat Raubahn's past glories─gifted swordsmen and women all. Here, this is a list of their names. Please, take it─and Twelve watch over Ul'dah!
You have what you came for, yes? Please, I've been looking forward to this match for some time. Allow me to savor it in peace.
Fine warriors from across the realm? Gathering in Ul'dah? It could only mean the Immortal Flames are seeking recruits!

They say lineage and lands will stand for naught in the Flames. Any and all proven warriors will be welcomed into its ranks. I myself have often dreamt of the honor that would come with pledging my allegiance to such a banner, should it fly.

So, it's great heroes you want, is it? Well, since you ask, the companions that accompanied me on a recent journey were warriors of the first order, all. Here, I shall write down their names if you wish─along with my own, of course!
How goes the hero hunting, friend? Don't go and find none [@1A(1)]too[@1A(0)] mighty, now, lest they make me look bad.
How did you fare? Were you able to discover the names of any possible recruits?
What's that? So you heard Raubahn Aldynn has returned to Ul'dah, did you? Aye, it's true. Though as to why he left in the first place, none can say.
Still...a good few of the names on those lists you gathered were fans of his. If they caught wind that he were with the Immortal Flames, they'd no doubt come flocking to join.
Thank you, friend. You've done more than I hoped. Please, take this as payment.
Oh, and consider devoting a bit of time to training, you hear? If you've enlisted to serve in the Immortal Flames, you just might find yourself sparring with Raubahn one day, hahaha!
The Garleans grow bolder by the day. They'll launch an assault on Gridania before long, mark my words.
But they're not the only ones busying themselves. The three nations have stirred, and the Grand Companies have been reformed.
The annals say the Grand Companies were the forces of old─the union of the free peoples in all the nations, formed to confront the threat that faced Eorzea long ago.
Here and now, in our own lifetimes, the Immortal Flames of Ul'dah have been rekindled.

No doubt the call will go out to the great men and women of the realm. No small feat, though, unifying the masses. The royal family, Syndicate, and all the rest of them have got quite a job on their hands.
We've been called upon to take stock of our realm's warriors─and what better place to start? We've certainly no shortage of them here at the Coliseum.

But we've need of all the heroes we can muster. What say you to lending a hand, friend? Might you be willing to roam the city and find word of any warriors? Must be [@1A(1)]some[@1A(0)] smallfolk in this bloody town what know of a good sword arm.
Good, then. Come, let's see that map of yours. I'll mark a few places you're like to find someone in the know. You're on your own from there.
You adventurers best not be thinking none of this concerns you. The Garleans have begun their attack, and it could well mean the end of the realm─and all in it. There ain't no time to lose.

See the five [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000172,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000172,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] delivered safely to the hands of Nald's devout followers. We must do what we can to allay their fears, that they might swiftly return to more profitable endeavors.

[@2B([@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000172,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000172,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)])]? You've brought me [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000172,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000172,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]!?

I [@1A(1)]knew[@1A(0)] some good would come of giving all that money to the Order! And all while I meant only to buy forgiveness for pushing that old lady to her death from the Coliseum stands...a-accidentally. Oh, but it [@1A(1)]was[@1A(0)] exhilarating! The match, that is...

Still, news of the airship attack was simply terrifying. I've heard rumors that the nations' leaders mean to resurrect the Grand Companies to oppose the Garlean threat. Is the Syndicate truly moving to do so?
If they mean to raise banners against the Empire, every gladiator at the Coliseum is prepared to march under them!

You have my thanks for delivering this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000172,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000172,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. It is [@1A(1)]so[@1A(0)] choice. If you have the means, I highly recommend picking one up.
A talisman, for me? From Brother Peneli Zuneli, you say?
Why, thank you very much. I shall hang it in the Phrontistery where it may watch over all within her walls.

I confess, we attempted to keep word of the airship tragedy from our patients. It is all we alchemists can do to battle disease and illness. Worrying about an impending war is hardly conducive to recuperation.
Yet despite our best efforts, news of the Garlean attack reached them all the same. Now the entire patient ward is gripped by fear. You could not have delivered this token to us at a better time.
Now if you'll excuse me, I must get back to my duties. If the Garleans [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] launch an assault on Ul'dah, the Phrontistery will be busier than ever. We must make ready for the worst.
Our patients are not the only ones troubled by recent events. The more tokens from Milvaneth Sacrarium, the better.
Twelve watch over me...

I have not moved from this spot since the Garlean attack on our airship. Someone must offer prayers to the Twelve. We mortals think highly of ourselves─but few realize that we are little more than the pawns of the gods.
Hm? A talisman from Milvaneth Sacrarium, you say? Given only to those who make the most gracious donations?
Then in the name of Nald, I humbly accept this gift.
Spare me your accusatory looks. Your eyes betray your suspicion. I am aware of how things appear, but I can assure you that I acquired my wealth honestly.
And now I must bid you farewell. Leave this pauper to his prayers. Surely you have other trinkets to deliver, no?

Why, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)], this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000172,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000172,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]... Is it truly...for [@1A(1)]me[@1A(0)]!?
Thank you a thousand times over! It is for just such unexpected acts of kindness that I continue to give selflessly to the Order of Nald'thal.

I recently purchased for them an elaborate statue of Nald for some ten billion gil or so, I don't recall the exact figure. No doubt such a gift moved Nald to imbue this talisman with his complete graces.

It is a true shame about the people on that airship... Men of means like myself often travel on such vessels. And now I hear that a band of scavengers has taken to pilfering valuables from the wreckage site. Dear me.
No doubt the bereaved families of those lost will blame the Sacrarium for any further grievances.
Were there any others who were given a talisman? I am not fool enough to think only I give to the Order, but there would be a certain comfort in knowing I was the sole recipient of such a token.
What's this, then? A talisman from the Milvaneth thaumaturges, is it?

Well, I sure as hells haven't given so much as a bloody gil to the Sacrarium. Suppose that means it's meant for Master. Gods know he's always sending those charlatans more coin than most Ul'dahns see in their lifetime.

Since the Garleans filled that Ul'dahn airship full of smoking holes, Master's been nowhere to be seen. Always been a gambling man, he has─and it looks as if he put all his bets on turning tail and running this time, hehehe!
But a trinket like this might be just the thing to set his tattered nerves at ease. I'll be sure to pass it on when I see him next.
Wouldn't mind hanging on to it myself...though I doubt the gods will favor me enough to keep Master away forever.
Have you completed the task? Hm...? You have a rueful look about you. What troubles you, friend?
What!? Bandits rifling through the remains of the vessel destroyed by the Garleans? But the Order is supposed to lay claim to─ Errr, I mean...
This is most grievous news! If word of this were to get out, the Milvaneth name would be irreparably marred!
I'm afraid I have another task to ask of you, friend. Travel to the site of the wreckage, northwest of Ul'dah, and kill these accursed brigands.
Kill them all, and let the gods sort them out.
Travel to the site of the wreckage, northwest of Ul'dah, and kill these accursed brigands.
You handle yourself well enough, friend, but it would be unwise to linger here. Those scouts were nothing compared to the real Garlean infantry─who may well be on their way.
An adventurer, are you? Well, you have our thanks─for killin' them bandits, I mean.
An adventurer, are you? Well, you have our thanks─for killin' them bandits, I mean. Come to think...we've met before, have we not?
We come from the Ironworks─the Garlond Ironworks. Sent to survey the wreckage, we were, but fled for cover when them bastards turned up─pardonin' my language.

Made them for common thieves at first, but they ain't like no thieves I ever seen─too organized for that. Had linkpearls, even, and was reportin' back to somewhere 'bout not findin' what they was lookin' for.
I'd wager the forge they was Garlean agents, that I would. Won't be long before they're missed. Best put as many malms as possible between yourself and here─and quick.
Tell me, have you done Nald's work? Are the fiends no longer of this world?
Garlean agents!? Twelve be good, that is far worse than mere scavengers...

It is fortuitous you arrived in time to save the Ironworks' engineers. They are an invaluable lot at this point in time. The Syndicate has commissioned their order to furnish the mysterious cogs and pistons of our machinery, and maintain our airships.
It seems the essential elements of the wreckage have already been reclaimed. Most likely they were conducting their final survey of the site.

I've heard their master at the Ironworks has been paying visits to the sultana's palace of late. They say he is a prodigy when it comes to wheels and cogs. But many wonder, can he match the magitek machinery of the Empire?
But the point is moot. There is none more gifted than he in his field, and so rely upon him we must.

Perhaps it is time we began accepting donations in the name of a new cause. Something to inspire the people to oppose the Empire and instill morale. A monument, perhaps? Yes, a building, I should think. We could call it the [@1A(1)]Sepulchre of Garlemald[@1A(0)]. Quite a nice ring to it, no?

If you harbor anxieties about your own future, perhaps you would care to make a contribution? I have here your reward for services rendered to the Sacrarium. Shall I make a gift of it to the Order?[@CR]...No? Very well, then. [@1A(1)]Take it.[@1A(0)]
An Ul'dahn airship was shot down by the Garleans no more than a few days past. It seems the imperial gauntlet has been thrown down.
Terror is spreading amongst the smallfolk─and justifiably so. Many of our own devotees frequently use the airships on their travels, and all now fear for their safety.

To those generous enough to make [@1A(1)]particularly[@1A(0)] sizeable donations, we present [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000172,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000172,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]─a talisman imbued with the power to ward off calamity and disaster.

I wonder, friend, would you be so kind as to deliver these [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000172,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000172,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] on behalf of Milvaneth Sacrarium? There are five charitable souls who must be visited in all. You will be compensated for your trouble, of course.
Nald welcomes your service. I pray these talismans bring peace to the hearts of our dear friends, and hasten their return to more profitable endeavors.
Very well, but know that by refusing this duty, you have refused Nald himself. Some might consider that...sacrilege.
Well done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! It does me good to see both you and Little Ala Mhigo safe.
I see. That's quite a tale... So, this craven told you all this, did he?

S'pose you deserve the truth, having put yourself in harm's way. Aye, I serve Raubahn Aldynn, as you've likely gathered by now. The forces behind this latest plot mean to see both him and the sultana toppled from power.
I daresay they were tryin' to lure us into the open. Mayhap they meant to capture some o' those who serve Raubahn, that they might turn their tongues to learn more o' his comin's and goin's.

And so I asked you to go. You're an adventurer[@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),, and an Immortal Flame besides,)],)]. You're as like to succeed in such an endeavor as any. I'm sorry for hidin' the truth, though I swear it was for all our safety.
If you've learned anything here, let it be this─there're forces other than the Empire threatenin' Ul'dah. Such evils plague us even within our own city walls.
Not even Raubahn, the great Bull o' Ala Mhigo, can hope to defeat all our enemies alone.
We'll have need of you again, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I pray when that time comes, you're willin' to answer the call once more.

Raubahn ruined me with the purse he won that day. I lost all standing in the city, and was forced to sell him the Coliseum. In time, I was reduced to doing anything for gil─cleaning privies, begging in the streets, selling off my...my... Even now I cannot bring myself to say it.

What do you know of my despair, stranger? Hm? You who are not even Ul'dahn. If you value your life, I suggest you pry no more into matters that do not concern you. I'll spare you this once, if only because there is no money to be made from your death.
But know that my masters do not take kindly to interlopers. Interfere again, and they are like to send a piece of you to each of the seven hells.
What do you want[@IF($E9(4),, woman,)]? Are you another of Raubahn's lackeys?
Hmph, so you claim not to be. But is that the truth, I wonder? Well, bugger you if you are, and bugger you if you aren't.
And bugger that bastard Raubahn most of all! Just who in the hells does he fancy himself, anyway!? As if taking my Coliseum weren't enough, he seems intent on tormenting me even now!
I was [@1A(1)]someone[@1A(0)] in Ul'dah. I had everything─money, power, position. And Raubahn took it [@1A(1)]all[@1A(0)] from me that day with a single swing of his damned sword!

Raubahn ruined me with the purse he won that day. I lost all standing in the city, and was forced to sell him the Coliseum. In time, I was reduced to doing anything for gil─cleaning privies, begging in the streets, selling off my...my... Even now I cannot bring myself to say it.

What do you know of my despair, stranger? Hm? You who are not even Ul'dahn. If you value your life, I suggest you pry no more into matters that do not concern you. I'll spare you this once, if only because there is no money to be made from your death.
But know that my masters do not take kindly to interlopers. Interfere again, and they are like to send a piece of you to each of the seven hells.
Oi, been waitin' on you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Had word you'd be by sooner than late, and my master's never wrong about such things.
Had his eye on you, he has. Aye, we both have. There's a task we think you fit for. A task that'll test both your mettle and your mind.

There's a game over at the Platinum Mirage what only caters to the richest o' the rich. Seems the gamblin' tables don't hold no thrill for their like no more. No, it's bloodshed they want, and they'll stop at naught to have it. Hells, some time ago they took to pittin' their debtors against each other.

Raubahn the Bull put an end to those games when he took his seat on the Syndicate. Some two years past, that was. But he set out on his journey a short time after, and without him 'round to enforce his word, the fights were on again afore long.

When he came home to Ul'dah to see the Flames remade, we thought the games would end again on their own. But the bastards runnin' 'em grew bold while he was away, and the games've only gotten more savage...

Mayhap you know of Little Ala Mhigo? Scores of our Ala Mhigan brothers and sisters took refuge there after the fall. These rich devils mean to let a beast loose on the place under the guise of an accident, and wager on the outcome.
And if what we hear is true, they mean to do it soon. The beast's a ferocious thing─one captured for use on the bloodsands. The Ala Mhigans... So many innocents...
Well, it don't bear thinkin' about. The point is, we can't let it happen. The beast must be laid low before it's let loose.
Aye, I knew you'd help us. Master's never wrong about such things, like I said.

Raubahn hails from Ala Mhigo, you know. Started out in Ul'dah as a warrior on our bloodsands, and fought his way to enough purses to earn himself a seat on the Syndicate. The other members didn't take too kindly to that, o' course. A commoner in their midst, and an Ala Mhigan besides.
They ain't like him, see. No, they only care about featherin' their own nests. They're behind all this, like as not. I only pray you can stop 'em, friend.
You'd turn your back on all them doomed innocents? Then their blood'll be on your hands.
That bloody beast'll be set loose on the Ala Mhigans afore long.
Make haste to Little Ala Mhigo, south o' Camp Drybone, and there find and slay this monster. The lives of countless Ala Mhigans are in your hands!
Have a habit of turnin' up at the right time, don't you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? Aye, well, there's news from Limsa─news what might interest you a great deal.
Seems there's a hidden grotto somewhere on the isle of Vylbrand. And in its deepest reaches─a black market!
Aye, a place where pirates from all over flock to trade their plunder. True or not, no self-respectin' merchant of Ul'dah could let such a tale pass without prickin' up an ear.

Think of it. Ill-gotten goods of all sorts bein' bought and sold at a fraction of their true worth, each sale undercuttin' the honest souls here who toil day and night sellin' the selfsame wares to scrape a livin'... If it is indeed happenin', it can't be allowed to go on.
Or at least that's what those very merchants felt moved to come and tell me. They've requested someone be sent to this grotto─Shposhae, they call it─to see if there's any truth to these rumors.
Chances such as this don't come often. You'd do well to put yourself in the good graces of these merchants. Do right by them, and might be they'll put in a good word for you with the Immortal Flames.

Take on the task or don't─matters none to me. But if you mean to see it done, travel first to Limsa and pay a visit to the Astalicia. There's a bloke there by the name of Hasthwab you'll want to talk to.
What? Too [@1A(1)]far[@1A(0)], is it? Are you a bloody adventurer or ain't ya!? Aye? You are? Then bloody well [@1A(1)]adventure[@1A(0)]!

Gods, I've half a mind not to tell you this now, dirty ingrate that you are, but the merchants've laid on transport for any souls willin' to make the voyage. Bloody [@1A(1)]air[@1A(0)] transport, no less.
If you can't be bothered to go by land and sea, then take to the air. Don't know what else them airships is good for, if not cartin' around lazy [@IF($E9(4),wenches,bastards)] such as yourself.
The Wellhead Lift in the south of Ruby Road Exchange'll see you to the airship docks. Off you go, then. I'll be prayin' that airship o' yours don't crash and burn.
This ticket'll get you passage on the airship. You'll be neck-deep in fish guts and cockles before you know it.
That's my [@IF($E9(4),girl,boy)]! The Wellhead Lift in the south of Ruby Road Exchange'll see you to the airship docks. Off you go, then. I'll be prayin' that airship o' yours don't crash and burn.
Like I said, matters none to me. There'll be another adventurer along before that door closes behind you.

I'm sure there's a map in that bag o' yours. You might think about─oh, I don't know─[@1A(1)]lookin' at it[@1A(0)] every once in a while. <sigh> The Wellhead Lift in the south o' Ruby Road Exchange'll see you to the airship docks.
Be sure and make for the Astalicia once you're in Limsa. Pirate there by the name of Hasthwab'll tell you what needs knowin'. Off you go, then.
Greetings, [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)], and welcome to the airship docks of Highwind Aeronautics.

We are happy to announce that since the re-establishment of the Grand Companies, the city[@1F]states are seeing to the constant surveillance of Eorzea's skies, rendering it safe for us to resume flights. And not a day too soon, what with all of the men and materials that need transporting!
We are currently offering passage between Ul'dah, Gridania, and Limsa Lominsa.
Our airships were built at the famous Garlond Ironworks, and their safety and speed are second to none. If you have not flown with us before, I strongly urge you to do so. It is quite an experience!
Take the airship to Limsa Lominsa?
Your ticket please, [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)].
Very well. Please come and see me whenever you wish to make flight preparations.
Take the airship to Limsa Lominsa?
Passage to Limsa Lominsa, I see. Very well. Your vessel will arrive shortly.
I am told there are two things in Limsa best avoided─the pirates and...everyone else. Ahem. Just a little joke, that. [@1A(1)]Do[@1A(0)] take care, though, [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)].
Take the airship to Limsa Lominsa?

Bugger me... What bollock-brained business could drag the likes o' [@1A(1)]ye[@1A(0)] in 'ere? Eh? Whassat? Th' black market o' Shposhae, ye say? O, aye! The famous black market o' Shposhae! [@1A(1)]That[@1A(0)] black market! Gah hah hah hah! Come all th' way from Ul'dah to ask me that, 'ave ye?
Well, me trustin' friend, I dunno which sly sod poured that bilge into yer braincase, but there ain't no black market in Shposhae. Nay, not so much as a single stall.
Aye, there's a cave near 'ere by that name, that much be true. But it ain't nothin' to no one, save a few cunnin' 'Cudas.
A black market run by sea dogs? Word'd get out soon as th' first sale was made. Secret port? Underground tunnels? Gah hah hah hah!

Ye been too long in Ul'dah, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]. Mere mention o' gil an' off ye go! Too many fairy tales from yer wet nurse, I reckon. Aye, an' that be why I don't never believe aught I 'ear at a woman's teat! Gah hah hah hah!
...Still 'ere, eh? Can I take it that ye ain't rightly inclined to believe me, neither?
Well, I sure as 'ells ain't stoppin' ye from goin' there, ye daft bugger! Follow the cave as far it bloody goes an' see fer yerself!
I tell ye what─'ave a little think on it, an' let ol' 'Asthwab know if ye be dead set on explorin'. Jus' don't go blamin' me when ye ends up just plain dead! Gah hah hah hah!

Aye, aye...jestin' apart, though, it might be as I've a secret t' share wi' ye. One I ain't never told another soul... An' if [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] don't get yer adventurer's juices flowin', I dunno what will!
Did your foray bear fruit of a faceted fashion?
Fascinating. So the tales telling of a titanic terror are true...
And this is the curious crystal you acquired after annihilating one of its coruscating companions?
The elements within appear to be unnaturally aligned, but more than that I hesitate to hypothesize.
It seems I shall have to speak with a specialist in such substances.
What the manifestation of this massy monstrosity means I cannot imagine, but at least I possess proof of its presence.
Your assistance has accorded me the ammunition I need to author an arresting article! It is only fitting that you are furnished with a finder's fee.
Slay the strangely shining monsters spawned by the big-mouthed behemoth, and bring me one of the crystals created, if you could!
The massively mawed monster appears in the area of aetherytes. Pinning down its position may prove problematic unless you exchange experiences with others of your proud profession.

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! What a splendid surprise to chance upon our paper's champion! It is I, Dural Tharal! ...Renowned reporter? ...Of [@1A(1)]The Mythril Eye[@1A(0)]? You [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] remember me, don't you? Ah, but of course you do, you wicked wag!
A hearty hail to you, adventurer. I am Dural Tharal, renowned reporter for [@1A(1)]The Mythril Eye[@1A(0)].
Have you heard the rumors recently running rampant? Many have mentioned a mysterious monster appearing in the area of aetherytes.
This curious creature purportedly possesses a monstrous maw. It appears with amazing alacrity, and then, within a wee while, it slips away like smoke on the sea breeze.
This monster of mouth most massive was first witnessed with wary wonderment in the region of Mor Dhona.
But the tales of tangible terror have more to tell: the monstrously mawed monster is said to summon separate entities enveloped in eerie light.
The glowing ghouls are my primary preoccupation. By all accounts, the incandescent imps expel a curious crystal upon expiration.
And the crystals collected from the bodies of beasts often bear invaluable information...
I assume you see the significance! Discerning the identity of the luminous life-forms will nudge us nearer to the nature of the jumbo-jawed giant!
So then, will you best the brilliantly blazing beasts on my behalf, and collect one of the crystals they carry?

I was [@1A(1)]convinced[@1A(0)] I could count on your cooperation! The location of the gargantuanly gobbed ghoul and attendant glowing ghoulies may best be unburied by cooperating with your colleagues─by which I mean your adventuring associates.
And please, neglect not to collect a crystal from your fulgent foes after felling them.
Your reluctance is regrettable. Could you at least communicate my conundrum to your capable companions?
Oooh, an adventurer, and one who looks capable besides! The Matron Nophica must be smiling on me today to bring you herrre in my moment of need!

Or─herrre's a sudden thought─have you just come to stay at our humble inn, the Roost? Are you an adventurer seeking work, or a travel-weary guest? At first glance, I say adventurer. At second...who knows?
Ah, but what does it matter! 'Tis an emergency, a crisis, a time of strife! I need help, and to you I turn, whatever you might be!

A guest checked out and left [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000224,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000224,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] in his room. He is making his way to the Gridania airship landing, or so I was told. Descend those steps─aye, the ones over by Miounne─and do hurry before he leaves!
Once he boards the airship, not even Nophica herself will be able to find him. Go, go, go, run like a chocobo, like you have never rrrun before!
Oh, thank you! I knew I could count on you. Such a well-used bag must be much loved by its owner. Reunite them, master and pouch, and bring a little joy into their lives.
Oh... You are a cold-hearted one, [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)], to forsake the plight of such a fine bag. <sob>

You seek the Gridania Landing, down those stairs over by Miounne. Hurry now and restore [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000224,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000224,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] to its owner, a burly man in a black straw hat.
What's that, you say? I left somethin' behind at the inn? I don't know about that. I've got everything that belongs to me, I reckon.
Hm? Aye, that's my bag all right...
Truth is, I meant to throw it out. I left it in the room, so's the maid could clean it up.

Look at the thing, will you? It's got a bloomin' big hole in the bottom. It served me well, 'tis true, but now it's worn and no good to no one. What's the point of a bag with a hole in the bottom, I ask you.
Is that so? The little missy at the inn thought it important and sent you after me, eh?
...Hm. Here, let me tell you a story. I'm a merchant hailin' from Limsa, and I came to Gridania to buy up vegetables. The folk here grow the best leafs and legumes in all of Eorzea, you know.

But some of the produce I bought wasn't up to par. Bruised, too small, that sort of thing. So I started throwin' away the rejects...but as I was doin' so, who comes up to me but some Gridanian bloke frothin' at the mouth. The man laid into me, sayin', “Oi, that's good food you're tossin' out!” Right peeved, he was.

So I told him I wasn't doin' it for my own gratification, and I thought it was a waste, too, but my customers are the cream of Lominsan society with uncompromisin' tastes, and they wouldn't take too kindly to me tryin' to fob off inferior cucumbers on them.
Well, that just poured oil on the flame, let me tell you, and we got into quite a heated discussion. I came away thinkin' folk hereabouts are all bull-headed and stubborn.

But then I thought on it some, and came to realize somethin'. Obnoxious though he was, that man had the right of it─we shouldn't waste things. Gridanians're 'specially passionate on this, and that bloke simply couldn't bear the sight of me tossin' decent food.
You know what? I'm gonna fix up this here bag, make it as good as new. And then I'll use it for as long as I can. It'll be my little way of showin' respect to the good people of Gridania.
It's done my soul good talkin' with you. I owe you one, friend. If our paths ever cross in Limsa, I'll be sure to feast you on the finest vegetables the land has to offer!
I owe you one, friend. If you see little missy back at the inn, do pass along my thanks.
Ah, you're back, and without the bag! I take it your quest has met with success!
If I might be allowed to grumble, though, it's always outsiders who leave things behind. We forestborn know better than to treat our belongings callously.
Take a simple bag, for instance. Making one requires hide─hide that comes from creatures of the Twelveswood. Such creatures give their lives that we might be able to carry our possessions about.

It would be wrong to treat their sacrifice with any less than the utmost respect. ...But then, I have no need to tell you these things. [@1A(1)]You're[@1A(0)] the one who returned the bag to its owner, after all.

Which reminds me! You came herrre as an adventurer, but perhaps you would like to stay as a guest? We just need to enter your name in the registry, and our inn shall be your home. Now, let's see. [@STRING($EB(1))], is it?

Excellent! Now that it's official...[@CR]Ahem! Greetings, good [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)], and welcome to the Roost. Herrre you may rest your weary limbs and restore your vim and vigor. Drop by whenever the adversities of adventuring begin to take their toll.

You begin [@COLOR(#ffff7b1a)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]resting[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] the moment you enter your room. The longer you stay in your room, regardless of whether you are logged in or not, the more [@COLOR(#ffff7b1a)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]rested[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] you will become.

Now, this goes without saying for persons of quality such as yourself, but we do not allow synthesis on the premises. Our guests expect peace and quiet, and we endeavor to provide it.
In addition to synthesis, equally cacophonous actions such as item repair and materia melding are also strictly prohibited.
You're now registered in the book. Remember, you will always have a home away from home at the Roost. Palliation for the mind and body is what we do best.
What's this I hear? Did you happen to misplace that wanted notice for Gauwyn the Gannet?
Rumor has it Gauwyn the Gannet has left Ul'dah. I'll give you a new notice to take with you. If you must lodge at an inn outside the sultanate, pray remember to exercise all caution.
Nobody knows where and when Gauwyn the Gannet will strike next. Be sure to keep the wanted notice with you at all times.
The suspect is said to be in the Acorn Orchard at this very moment. Do hurry, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─there's no guarantee he'll be there for long!
The man standing over by that tree? He's been here for [@1A(1)]ages[@1A(0)].
He's got a lot of friends, and they visit him sometimes. You can tell it's them because they always wear the same red clothes.
They were here again just yesterday. One of them said something about meeting at “heck waters.” Maybe that's where they play together?
The man standing by the tree has lots of friends. They always wear the same red clothes.
If you ask me, though, that big man over there is [@1A(1)]much[@1A(0)] scarier!

So we meet again. I do grow weary of this game. Well, you may question me all you like, but my answer will ever be the same: I've been at this very spot the entire day. Ask any of the locals, and they will tell you as much.

Not convinced? All right. You recall the oaf who was hired to shadow me, yes? Well, I will make no comment on his, ahem, [@1A(1)]unique[@1A(0)] new pastime, and say only that he too will most assuredly testify in my favor. I trust that will be sufficient? Good.
Hmmm... In spite of my infallible disguise, I fear the suspect may not yet have taken me fully into his confidences... I must endear myself still further if I am to─

Uwaaah! Wh-What business have you with me, a law-abiding carpenter of nondescript appearance, here to inspect this excellent facility!? R-Rest assured, I am satisfied that the apparatuses here are assembled from the finest woods! No child shall suffer from unpleasant splinters here! C-Carry on, citizen!

Oh, where could the inspector be? When last we spoke, he said he had a mind to go deep undercover for the case. But his disguises are [@1A(1)]perfect[@1A(0)]. If he's already in one, I shall never find him... <sigh>
Well, I see only children here. I suppose I'd better try looking elsewhere...
Hahaha! What in the world is that man doing? That's the most ridiculous thing I've ever seen!
Is that strange man your friend? He [@1A(1)]isn't[@1A(0)]? Then shouldn't we summon the Wood Wailers?
I've eagerly awaited your returrrn, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Tell me, were you able to locate our suspect?

...So Gauwyn had been there for some time, had he? He must have known he was being followed─I can't say I'm entirely surprised. At any rate, it's heartening to know that you, at least, were able to learrrn something new.
So our thief has accomplices and a secret lair besides... That certainly explains why he never fails to have an alibi.
But I do wonder, why go to such pains to steal individual weapons? Instead of the occasional adventurer, wouldn't it make more sense to target weaponsmiths and merchants?

Well, if I knew the answer to that question, I suppose I'd be on the way to becoming a crrriminal myself! Anyway, with you on the case, I'd wager it's only a matter of time before their operrration is exposed and the case duly closed!
First time staying with us at the Mizzenmast Inn? Then I'll need ye to sign the ledger proper. I've some ink for the quill right he─
Seven hells! It's that damned Qiqirn again! I swear to the Fury, if I ever catch that slippery rat, I'll skin his arse and boil his bloody bones down to glue!
Normally, I'd ask for yer help...but the last time I had an adventurer...er...[@1A(1)]dispose[@1A(0)] of someone, Baderon had me scrubbing soup pots in the galley for a fortnight.

I guess I'll have to settle with simply havin' ye fetch me some more ink. If it ain't too much trouble, could you hie yerself down that flight of stairs o'er yonder and speak wiv a wee goblin peddler what goes by the name of Sweetnix?
That's me [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]. Didn't ken a 'venturer what weren't willin' to lend a helpin' hand.
Now, don't ye worry about the goblin. He won't bite ye none. Hells, the bugger's always wearin' that queer mask, so might be he doesn't even have a maw to nip ye wiv.

Truth be told, there ain't much can be said about the stocky lot, 'cept that they like them the jinglyshine─that be gil to you and me─and that they'd sell naught less than their own kin to get a handful of the stuff.

What are ye to buy the ink wiv? Oh, ye need not fret o'er that detail, me [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]. Wee Sweetnix owes me a favor or two, and I reckon it be right time to call one in. You jus' tell the gobbie that ol' Mytesyn sent ye. Heh heh heh.

Wivout any ink, yer name ain't goin' on this here ledger. Wivout yer name on this here ledger, ye ain't settin' a single stinkin' foot in one of me fine rooms. I don't care how much gil ye've janglin' in yer pockets.
Sweetnix sells his ill-gotten wares to those what frequent the Drownin' Wench. He's set up shop in that stairwell o'er yonder. Ye cannae miss him.
Pshhh... Shkohhh...[@CR]Has roomgiving rainlander need of undry wordpaint?
Sweetnix has much undry wordpaint! Undry wordpaint good for writing gobbietomes. Good for writing backwords!
Roomgiving rainlander trade many tongueflaps with Sweetnix. Has wideheart and widepurse!
Sweetnix gives all wordpaint to roomgiving rainlander. Ninety and ten claypots, all for rainlander!
Ohohoho! Sweetnix is unremembering that uplander has only tinypack upon backchest, not widepack like gobbiepack. Ohohoho! Ninety and nine claypots must hurryback to gobbiepack! Ho ho ho!
Sweetnix aftertimes makes busydeal with lustyeyed uplander. Now, uplander walks with fastness to roomgiving rainlander before undry wordpaint is redrying!

Ye have a chat wiv Sweetnix? Quite a character, the bugger. Cannae comprehend a bleedin' word what spills from the gob's gob, but he's a good listener when he wants to be, and is quick to give his cullies a fair price when bargainin'.
Me? I's been in his good graces since he walked in one day wantin' to hear the tale of the Mizzenmast.

I told him what I'd heard from me mum when I was a wee sprat, and the gob, he sat there ears pricked up like a cur at a feast, waitin' for that first scrap to fall from the table. Scribbled down every last word, he did, but for what purpose, I cannae say.
What exactly did I tell him? No scrap of lore every last Lominsan doesn't already ken.
That the city of Limsa Lominsa was built from the wreckage of the mighty [@1A(1)]Galadion[@1A(0)], which ran aground on the rocks of this very bay some seven hundred years past.

This tower we stand in now─the Mizzenmast─is called such because it was built by hollowing out the [@1A(1)]Galadion[@1A(0)]'s actual mizzenmast. That should give ye a good idea of jus' how massive the original ship was.
Ah, sorry there, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]. Ye didn't come here for an 'istory lesson, did ye? Let me jot yer name down in the ledger, and I'll have one of me boys ready you a room straight away.
Ye can come and go anytime ye please. Our beds are the softest in the land, and I guarantee ye'll sleep like a babe at [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] muvver's warm teat.

Here for the Gannet, are we?

We were able to apprehend one of his dogsbodies, but even our patent brand of [@1A(1)]persuasion[@1A(0)] has yielded naught.
