You are welcome to continue the search on your own, if it suits you. One of my men spotted a set of tracks heading northwest, but the trail disappeared after half a malm.
Another Yellowjacket? Ye'll not get nuffin' outta me, ye piss-drinkin' sod-pot! <spit>
You discover what appears to be some sort of notebook...
“Opportunity[@CR][@CR]I have been assigned the Dalamud story. This may prove a most fortunate opportunity─when it comes to the red moon, the citizenry is afire with equal parts fear and curiosity.
“If I can pierce this veil of mystery, my name shall be on the lips of every last nobleman and tavern-dweller in Eorzea.
“Interviews[@CR][@CR]Taking to the streets, I conducted interviews with members of the populace.
“When asked for their thoughts on the changes that Dalamud has undergone in recent days, a notable majority responded that the moon seemed to them to be growing larger.
“If my own senses are to be credited, I too would swear that Dalamud swells with each passing day. My chest tightens at the thought of what may betide Eorzea when it reaches 'maturity'...
“Research[@CR][@CR]A scholar of Ishgard termed an authority on the movements of celestial bodies answered my queries with her theory that Dalamud grew [@1A(1)]nearer[@1A(0)] rather than larger.

“Such a possibility seems fanciful, to say the least. As if to confirm my doubts, the scholar was unable to support her claims with anything approaching solid evidence. I fear she may be courting controversy in an attempt to win fame.
“As things stand, I shall consider myself fortunate if my article makes page three. Days of groundwork, and so little to show for it...
“Defeat[@CR][@CR]Exhausted and footsore, I paused to rest outside the Arrzaneth Ossuary. That is where I encountered a most unusual character reciting a most peculiar poem.
“Though I listened with but half an ear, one phrase in particular lodged itself in my mind and now refuses to depart. 'Heavens spew crimson flame...'
“Could this 'crimson flame' refer to the red moon? The words evoke catastrophic images...almost as if the end of days were upon us.
“Dear me. Am I a child to be affrighted by a stranger's grim bedtime stories? Shall I next pray for a hero to deliver us from our ghastly fate?
“Perhaps my senses are muddled from too much pondering and too little sleep. Though it pains me to admit defeat, I believe it is time I cease this fruitless search for answers and make my way home.”
The remaining pages of the notebook are blank.
Allow me to show you to the room in question. Do try to be discreet!
Ah, [@IF($E9(4),my lady,my lord)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Might you be interested in a mutually advantageous proposition?
Allow me to explain. A short while ago, our establishment was graced with the patronage of a reporter investigating the mystery of Dalamud.

Hardly newsworthy in itself, I concede, but listen on! After pursuing his story for some days, the fellow was observed to stumble from his room and quit our establishment, leaving his notebook behind!
Now, I should imagine an adventurer would be more than a little curious to peruse this reporter's findings─curiosity being a quality common to the members of said profession.

And if an adventurer were to come looking for the forgotten notebook─declaring [@IF($E9(4),herself,himself)] to be acting upon the reporter's request─then I would be obliged to grant [@IF($E9(4),her,him)] access to the vacated room.
Good [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)]! How fortunate it is that I chose to confide in you! The reporter's chambers are just as he left them. Simply say the word, and I shall take you there.
And should the secrets you find within happen to be worth a gil or two to the newspaper peddlers, well...I should not be averse to pocketing precisely half of the profits!
Good [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)]! You mean to say you have no interest in Dalamud and its crimson mysteries!?
You seem distraught, [@IF($E9(4),my lady,my lord)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Would I be correct in assuming you have lost your copy of Hildibrand's memorandum?
If so, then worry no longer! The inspector was kind enough to furnish me with a generous number of spares. Yes...very generous. Please, take one. Take several!
Quite how the arcane ravings written thereon will help you, I cannot imagine. The inspector assured me, however, that they are pivotal to cracking the “case of the century.”
Why the long face, [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)]? Might you perhaps be searching for a copy of Hildibrand's memorandum?
As fortune would have it, the inspector entrusted me with a sizable pile of them. You are more than welcome to take one!
I confess their usefulness is not apparent to me, but Inspector Hildibrand spoke at some length about how these notes would assist him in cracking “the case of the century.”
Ye've the face of a [@IF($E9(4),maid,man)] what's dropped [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] coin purse in the chamber pot. Has somethin' happened, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]?
If it's Hildibrand's memorandum ye're lookin' fer, the good inspector left me a pile o' spares.
I dinnae ken what use this scrap o' paper might be t' ye, but he seemed convinced ye'd be needin' it if ye was to solve “the case o' the century.”
Leave the sowing of the pumpkin seeds to yours truly! I may be adept at digging up the truth, but burying things also happens to be one of my myriad skills!
Pumpkins sort of remind me of...um... No, it's gone.
Like I said, mind you keep that ash away from open flames. Wouldn't want you losin' a finger, would we? Heh heh heh.

Hello there, [@IF($E9(4),gorgeous,handsome)], and welcome to the Hourglass.[@CR]...Well, I say welcome, but we're actually not accepting guests at the moment. We've got a commotion on our hands, you see.

If you must know, we were hosting a rather wealthy couple, and things were proceeding uneventfully─just the way I like it. But come the morning they were due to leave, the husband storms up to me and says that someone had stolen his rather pricey wedding ring from within these very walls.
That's not the worst of it, either. The couple has the ear of an individual of─shall we say─considerable influence in the Mirage Trust, which happens to own the Hourglass.
And now, at the good lady wife's bidding, the inn is to remain closed until the culprit is found and arrested. If we don't crack this case soon, it might be me who ends up in irons.
Of course, I'm not just standing around with a finger up my nose. I've already hired an independent investigator, a man who specializes in difficult cases, to look into the matter.

But this is Ul'dah, and if there's any place in Eorzea more infested with charlatans and scoundrels, I'd like to know where! The investigator reassured me that the case is in good hands, all the while patting me on the head. But for all his pomp and pageantry─or perhaps because of it─I don't find myself feeling reassured at all.
I need more people on the case. Safety in numbers, you see. So...um, would you care to help a poor innkeeper out?
The husband, Mister Josce, claims he didn't set foot outside the Hourglass the night the ring went missing. And so we've been scouring the premises from cellar to attic.

But I can't help but wonder whether we're overlooking clues outside. And that's where I could really do with some help. I would appreciate it if you could go to the alley out back─Pearl Lane it's called─and ask around for Judithe.

Judithe has ears in alleys and alehouses throughout Ul'dah, and little happens here that she doesn't know about. She's a wary little rascal, though, and doesn't easily take to strangers. But just maybe she'll be willing to open up to a kind adventurer like you.
Wonderful, wonderful. Frankly, I have serious doubts about that investigator fellow. I feel better knowing you're on the job, too.
The culprit is somewhere close, I'm sure. At least, I hope so─my livelihood depends on it!
<sigh> Well, that's your right, I suppose. I just hope that that investigator is everything he claims to be.
Try to find Judithe in Pearl Lane. She has ears all over Ul'dah, and perchance the culprit's name was whispered into one of them.
Cor, we been gettin' all sorts o' nutters 'round 'ere recently. That goes for ye, too, [@IF($E9(4),lady,mister)]. Ye're an adventurer, ain't ye? Why don'tcha go do some adventurin' an' leave us be?
Ah, there you are. I do thank you for agreeing to help, but the inspector I engaged recovered the missing ring after all. He came by with it just moments ago.

Do you know where it was? At the Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern! Under...er, quite rigorous questioning from his wife, Mister Josce confessed everything. Apparently, he had dropped it while heavy in his cups. It was never stolen in the first place.

In the evening in question, Mister Josce somewhat insistently asked Miss Momodi to accompany him to dinner. When she refused, he went to the alehouse at the Mineral Concern and over-indulged his fondness for the stronger spirits. At some point, the ring slipped from his finger and fell to the floor.
Well, Missus Josce has a sharp tongue and sharper temper. Mister Josce had no illusions as to what would happen if his good wife found out he lost the ring at a common tavern.
And so he made up the story about the theft, and claimed not to have left the Hourglass that evening.

Of course, his deception was in vain and the tongue-lashing took place anyway. Nevertheless, the case is closed, I still have my livelihood, and the inn is open to guests once more. All's well that ends well.
So, if you're interested in a room, we can add your name to the registry. It'll also be my pleasure to tell you about the services we provide.
The Hourglass is proud to offer the latest amenities and conveniences available to modern hostelry. We trust you will have a comfortable stay with us.

In addition to synthesis, equally cacophonous actions such as item repair and materia melding are also strictly prohibited.
Your name is [@STRING($EB(1))], yes? I've added you to the guest registry, and you are now free to make use of our facilities at any time. We look forward to serving you!

Good [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),eve,morn)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),day,eve)])] to you, [@IF($E9(4),gorgeous,handsome)]. Do keep an eye to your valuables should you put in here at the Hourglass.
Many green adventurers have seen their weapons go missing of late. And the manner of the thefts are all the same.
An urgent pounding is heard at the door, and someone without shouts “Dalamud! The red moon falls from the sky! Run for your lives!”

Frantic, the adventurers throw open their doors to escape. At that instant, the thief takes them unawares, wrestling them to the ground and forcing their weapons from them before escaping in the chaos.
What craven would employ such a tactic─stealing from weary adventurers seeking the comfort of a warm bed?
We have heard testimony from several of the victims, and suspect the culprit to be a man by the name of Gauwyn.
He is known as a traveling arms dealer, but many say he only poses as such. They say his true trade is dealing in stolen goods.
These days see high demand for the so-called relic weapons favored by certain adventurers. He's like caught wind of their value.
Still, we have only our suspicions. Here, take this wanted notice. It shows Gauwyn's likeness. Should you see him, best keep a hand on your hilt or haft.
Who knows when or where the thief will strike next? Were I you, I'd keep that notice with you at all times. If you lose it, just come and see me again for another.
Gauwyn has made a habit of watching the games at the Coliseum around this hour. Please, go and find out if he was there at the time of the crime.
What is it you want of me? Must you interrupt me in the midst of a bout? If you seek a weapon, I shall accommodate you anon, but if it is mere words you wish to trade, let us trade them later.

Ah, but I can tell by the look and smell of you that you are no more than a hapless adventurer sent by the Hourglass. Oh yes, I know very well that they suspect it is I who am responsible for their recent spate of thefts.

I take it another weapon has gone missing? Well, I have been here all the day, friend. Go on, ask that clod of a shadow that has been following me─the one hiding behind that pillar. He will tell you that I speak the truth.

A word of professional advice, if I may be so bold─stick to dreams of slaying dragons and rescuing maidens. Harassing suspects in the service of imbeciles who run a kennel for adventurers does not become you. Run along, then.
The man has been watching the games for hours now, 'tis true. Still, he has a suspicious air about him. The posture of ostentatious repose... The look of studied disinterest...
Inspector, how long must we stay here? I'm so tired I can barely keep my eyes open.
As I told you before, I have been here all the day. Go on, ask that clod of a shadow that has been following me─the one hiding behind that pillar. He will tell you that I speak the truth.
What have you learned of Gauwyn, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]?
So, he claims he was at the Coliseum all the while...? And that the inspector can speak to the truth of it?
Well what bloody good is a shadow when Gauwyn knows he's being followed!? Hildibrand will hear of this, that I promise you!
Still... Where does this leave us? Could Gauwyn truly be innocent? Or... If it was not Gauwyn himself, perhaps he has an accomplice?
We will have to investigate more thoroughly, and increase security at the Hourglass. For now, let me thank you for what you've done.
It may be that the thief visits the other cities of Eorzea, as well. Take care wherever you might go, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
If Waekbyrt saw something in you, then I suppose you cannot be all that bad. The dog has an eye for talent and there's not a man on the Astalicia who'll deny that fact.

Still, you'll rue the day you chose the Executioners over the Kraken's Arms. Once Captain Carvallain takes the Admiral's chair, there won't be room enough for the scrags of rival factions. Though, he may show mercy if you were to experience a change of heart and reconsider your allegiances.
Ye fixin' t' help yer cap'n in the Trident?

Executioners spendin' too much time on the seas, I reckon, 'cause it'd take a goodly dose o' brine on the brain t' make a savvy seaman think a scrag like yerself would survive the first quarter bell o' that race.
The 'ells-damned schemin's of our noble Admiral 'as every flat-footed, land-legged 'venturer in the realm beatin' down the Astalicia's doors.

And then there be those what think they can waltz unmolested 'twixt our guild and that of the 'Cudas. Mark me: right gay be the babe what suckles at both 'is mother's paps at once─but where will 'e be when the fountains run dry?
Fellow scrag, eh? Well, you're welcome to my congratulations on that grand achievement. But that's all you'll be getting from me.
Just be careful you don't find yourself stuffed into a rum barrel and thrown brinewards. Waste of a good rum barrel, that'd be.
Swabbin' the bloody deck...that there be a job for a scrag, I tells ye.
If only the tide'd wash us up a new bright-eyed 'venturer, I could bet on her jumpin' ship the first sight o' danger... Then come the first sight o' danger, I'd toss her brinewise and collect!
Listen scrag, there's only one thing you need to know about the Trident─that the winner takes all. All of Limsa Lominsa.
And the losers? Well, let's just say the Navigator'll be guiding the wretched souls of those caught in the crossfire to the bottom of the abyss...those still in a fit state to be guided, mind ye.
Chichiroon spy the skies. Spy the skies for tasty lemming eyes. But Chichiroon spy no lemming in skies...
Mimiroon spit on some 'Cudas. Mimiroon punch and kick on some 'Cudas!
Jojoroon port good goods. Jojoroon see only sparkly goods. Jojoroon see no 'Cudas.
Ain't got time fer the likes o' ye, scrag. I's got bigger─an' better smellin'─fish t' fry.
That damned drunk Rostnsthal's made it his mission t' prove the bane o' me rosy existence.
Well, if it ain't [@IF($E9(4),Lady,Lord)] Scrag. Find time 'twixt memoir-writin' an' embroidery t' pay us unworthies a visit now, did ye?

Well then, let me give ye some o' me sound advice, free o' charge. Ye ain't got the ballast or the brains t' be a pirate, nor e'en th' scrag o' one. Ye're softer'n a dead rat ripe wi' maggots an' mold, and stink thrice as worse. If ye know what's good fer ye, ye'll march straight off this ship an' not never look back.
You looking to be a pirate?
Then have your fun while you can. If I was one to wager, and there's no man who'd say I ain't, I'd put my gil on you lasting no longer than a fortnight.
The scrag fancies [@IF($E9(4),'er,'im)]self a pirate, eh? Hah! One 'as t' be a rare type of desperate t' take on the likes of a land-legged 'venturer. Oh, 'ow the mighty Executioners 'ave fallen.
Still, ye'd best tread lightly and 'eed what ye're told, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)], or ye'll find yerself paddlin' in a pool o' yer own gore.
Ye're our newest scrag?
Hmph. Just 'cause Waekbyrt gave ye 'is blessin's, it don't make ye one of us.
Ye'll 'ave t' prove yer worth in blood afore ye can bear the brand of Executioner.
Ah, our new lemmin' 'as crawled out from [@IF($E9(4),'er,'is)] burrow. I tip my 'at t' Waekbyrt for findin' an adventurer with the, er, [@1A(1)]qualities[@1A(0)] t' take on this mummer's task.
Since swallowin' the 'Cudas' bloody terms, the Executioners've been the laughin' stock o' Limsa.
Heard the Executioners hired you to do their dirty work. Question is, how long will you last?
As of today, my sisters from the Sanguine Sirens have no quarrel with your new crew. However, one can never know when a war may break out.

There are no laws preventing a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] from becoming a pirate if that is what [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] truly desires. Though, some [@IF($E9(4),women,men)] are far more suited than others. And then there are those who have no place within fifty malms of the sea─some like a certain sottish Sea Wolf.

This town has her fair share of lackwits, but not many are so sorely bereft of brains as to waltz aboard the Astalicia and strike up a conversation with her crew like [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] was holding audience with the Admiral.
Only way our cap'n'll make Admiral is if the guild takes the flag in the next Trident─a three-pronged race t' rule the seas.

Unlike the other townships whose leaders are chosen by bloodlines, Limsa leaves its rule in the hands of its people. Every man bleeds red the same, so we don't see how one man's blood can be deemed better than another's. Anyone can join the Trident, and the victor and his crew are granted full reign over the realm...that is, until the next race.
The Trident is where us pirates can cock our leg t' the city, and piss on what we please. There ain't no rules─least none worth followin'─and the winner takes all.
And, like the bards sing, if ye ain't got the stones, then ye ain't gonna make a splash. Heh heh heh! So, there a fire under yer arse what needs lightin'?
You in?
Take this here map. It shows the course for the first leg of the Trident.

What? Ye thought ye'd be runnin' an actual race? Ha! There be more t' the Trident than just traipsin' from hither t' thither. A crew has t' prove they've got what it takes t' run a realm. Handlin' pest problems be one o' them duties.
Head o'er t' the X marked on that map an' collect me the heads o' the vermin infestin' the place. If ye can do that, then ye may be of some use come the Trident.
I could have a blade in yer belly in a gull's wink...
You in?
Well, ain't we th' lucky scrag! Not every day fresh scum off th' pond gets a go at runnin' the Trident.
Jus' don't go forgettin' th' one rule─dyin' gets ye disqualified. Gahahahahah!
Still here? I'd suggest ye move swift-like. Them lemmin's breed quicker'n rabbits, they do.
Now off t' Swiftperch Tower near Aleport and get t' guttin' the ruttin' rodents 'fore I'm inclined t' inform Waekbyrt and the cap'n of yer insolence.
Jus' don't forget to bring us all back some souvenirs.
Where in th' seven hells is that accursed drunk hidin'!?
Ah!? Ye've rid the tower o' them rats, ye say? Well then, it jus' goes t' prove that e'en a scrag of a 'venturer's worth more'n that bottom-feedin' bastard Rostnsthal.
Go an' tell Nunuba what ye've been up to. I've a drunk t' drown.
Took a stroll out t' th' 'Cuda tower, did ye?
'Eard yer job was originally promised to a sot named Rostnsthal...but that we was forced to 'and ye th' reins when th' scurvy bugger never turned up.
Then get outta me face 'fore I rip yers off and wipe me shite-caked boots with it.
Hah. Didn't last long as a Bloody Executioner, did ye?
Consider yerself fortunate the cap'n didn't pickle ye in a barrel an' toss ye to the sharks. And people say he ain't got a soft spot fer adventurers.
Heard us Bloody Executioners took on a new scrag, but I ain't seen none o' th' like on my watch. Someone be pullin' me peg leg, I say. That is, if I had me a peg leg t' pull, mind.
The Executioners are legendary. If ye join the crew, an' live long enough, some silver-tongued bard's sure t' end up singin' yer name one day.
Heard both Krakens and Sirens have their eyes on ye.

[@IF($E9(4),Ye'd be a fool not to sign on with the Sirens. Some say pirating is a man's calling, but I'll tell ye now, Rhoswen has more stones than them kobolds have hidden up in O'Ghomoro,A ship of wanton wenches brandishing cutlasses and drowning in rum may seem a paradise, but only a fool of a man would sign on with Rhoswen. The vixen has a taste for young meat, and it would not be long before ye found yer manhood bitten off and spat out to the sharks)].
Chichiroon left behind. Nobody see Chichiroon. Nobody love Chichiroon...
Fishbacks love Mimiroon. Love tasty Mimiroon... Love [@1A(1)]eating[@1A(0)] tasty Mimiroon...
Seems as yer two best choices did th' decidin' fer ye. An' where might that leave [@1A(1)]ye[@1A(0)], now, eh?
Reckon ye still might find a few stragglers up in the lounge, if ye don't mind drunks an' cowards!
Can't very well play pirate without a ship to call yer own, now can ye?[@IF($E9(4),, And ain't no one countin' that dinghy danglin' 'twixt yer legs.)]

Serpent Reavers, ye say? Best burn that name in yer bilge-soaked brain. Them be th' worst o' th' worst. Was pirates like you an' me─well, like me, at least─that is, 'til they gone an' sold their souls t' th' fishbacks. Now the monsters'll cut yer throat afore ye've time t' scream.
Heard ol' Waekbyrt put his barnacled boot to your arse and kicked you to the rocks...but here you are. Thought you'd have learned your lesson.

Then again, when did an adventurer [@1A(1)]ever[@1A(0)] learn [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] lesson? If you're that intent on waking up in a gutter with a knife in your back, then may I point you in the direction of one Rostnsthal─the sot over yonder staring into the depths of his cup. He'll sort you out. Sort you out good and proper, he will! Heh heh heh.
Ev'ry ship 'as its share o' rats, 'tis true, an' th' 'Licia ain't none diff'rent. Why, I spy me a right fat one just o'er there, a-paddlin' in a pool of 'is own puke.
Cannot fathom why Waekbyrt suffers the likes of ol' Rusty Steel, knowin' all th' grief 'e caused th' Executioners back in th' day.
They say...
...ye toss good steel in with that what's rusted, an' it'll 'ave gone red afore the moon's turned.
Same might be said o' scrags...
Reavers cleared the 'old o' both Krakens an' Sirens without settin' a single foot onshore. Now that be a damn fine trick if e'er I seen one.
'Tis a good thing, too, for if Rhoswen or Carvallain were t' catch wind of [@1A(1)]'im[@1A(0)], the seas 'round the ship'd soon be runnin' red.
Word 'as it th' Reavers bore their fangs in waters not far from Limsa. Would've gone an' bloodied me 'ands wi' th' rest o' the jolly lot, but I reckoned they'd 'ave no need of an extra axe.

Them two crews 'ave more'n enough allies t' warm their beds, an' 'tis only a matter of time afore one or tother takes th' Admiral's chair fer 'is─or 'er─own. That is, unless their ceaseless strugglin' don't see 'em feed each other t' th' fishes first.
Now, why in th' seven hells would a scrag like you want t' know where th' Krakens sharpen their swords?

Decided t' join 'em, have ye? Well, it be high time ye turned that ugly head o' yers away from a certain drunk and tried some proper piratin'. Ye'll find th' Krakens' lair down along th' Sailors Ward docks, o'er on th' Southern Islands.
If ye're quick, might still be a boat what ain't left port yet.
Seems the cup-shotten turncloak finally sobered up enough t' gather 'is wits and make fer the docks. And good riddance, I say.
Would've kicked 'im out meself, but the cap'n says every man what calls 'imself a pirate, no matter 'ow pissed or ugly, 'as a place on the Astalicia...and I ain't one t' quarrel wi' the cap'n.

Saw you talking with ol' Rusty Steel afore he went crawling back out into the gutter. Best watch your back when mixing with the likes of him. More'n a few of me mates wouldn't think twice about slicing his pipes from ear to ear...and paying the same courtesy to any suspected of consortin' with the sot.
Hah! Might the scrag be thinkin' a couple of “arrrs” an' an axe on [@IF($E9(4),'er,'is)] back'll make [@IF($E9(4),'er,'im)] a boney fidey pirate?

Well then, [@IF($E9(4),Lady,Lord)] Pirate, let me learn ye yer first lesson. Me brothers, th' Salt'ounds, don't take kindly t' scrags what go around callin' 'emselves pirates. Consider yerself marked. Heh heh heh.
Ye was warned.
Now 'tis only a matter o' time afore yer name be as rusted as yer rotten cap'n's.
Tread lightly, scrag...
Tempers'll run 'otter than the seven 'ells when Rhoswen an' Carvallain learn they lost face t' the likes of a fledglin' 'venturer an' a drunken 'as-been.
Let the mummers' show begin... Th' main attraction bein' yerself!
Finally back, eh? Was startin' t' think ye might've gone an' got yer throat slit. So, then, what did ye find?
Hm. Not bad, not bad at all. Now all's we got left is t' move the goods.
'Course, try an' peddle them trinkets 'ere in Limsa, an' th' Krakens'll be all o'er us afore we ken it. This bein' so, we must needs undertake a triflin' little voyage t' th' desert.

I've a contact in Ul'dah who'll buy whate'er ye brings 'im, wi' nary a question asked. So, yer second job as me first mate be t' 'op on a ferryboat an' transport our 'ard-won booty somewhere's no keen eyes'll be findin' it.

Them Krakens treat ye proper, like? I only asks 'cause that sot Rostnsthal is upstairs in his cups, an' I was wond'rin' if ye might not rub a bit o' salt in th' scurvy dog's wounds fer us. Tell him all about what it be like servin' under a [@1A(1)]real[@1A(0)] pirate, an' so on. Come now, do it fer yer ol' mate Waekbyrt!
Rumor 'as ye was set on joinin' the Krakens... Ha! Sack o' gelt says they kicked ye back t' th' cobbles where ye crawled from.

'Tis true, there always be th' Sirens, but I'd think long an' 'ard afore stickin' yer [@IF($E9(4),neck,man'ood)] in the maw o' that bloody merbeast. If word slips that ye called on th' Krakens first, the crone Rhoswen might well see it as a slight.
Ye quite sure ye held parley wi' them Krakens? From what I heard, they was good an' wroth upon returnin' from their tryst wi' th' fishbacks, see...

Not only did they lose th' ship what was attacked, but when their reinforcements arrived, cannons a-blazin', th' damned Reavers straightways quit th' scene─leavin' th' Krakens hotter than they was when they left port.
Ye ask me, ye'd be best off pledgin' yer blade t' neither Kraken nor Siren. Any crew that can't catch 'em a Reaver ain't worth spit.
Outta my face, scrag. Unless you'd like a boot up yer arse, which I'd be much obliged to provide.
Lookin' for a way off this rock, be ye? Well, ye won't find no 'elp 'ere, scrag. The ferry ye come in on'll carry yer craven arse back t' th' mainland, though.

I knew the moment I laid mine eyes on yer whore-spawned mug, ye'd not be long for this den o' sea lions. Were it the swearin' or the loud noises what did it in the end? Or may'ap a gil-lender found out ye was in bed wi' Rusty Steel an' came t' collect?
Beware, scrag...
The crews'll be back soon...
And they'll know what ye've done...
Didn't chance t' 'ear whose ship it was what got sunk by th' Reavers, did ye? Krakens'? Sirens'?

Makes no matter, does it? When th' lot of 'em come ashore, there'll be enough drinkin', swearin', and fightin' t' keep th' 'Licia's scrags busy swabbin' blood an' piss for more'n a few nights. The 'Cudas 'ad best stay clear if they value their livers.
HA-hahahahahaha! Rostnsthal sends yet another bearing gifts to humble Rorojaru. And one as naive as the last, it would seem! Very good, very good.

Ah, but before you go, I recommend you ponder long and hard why your benefactor chose the name by which he would have us call him. Though it hinders not the arm that wields his mighty axe, the rust of his past ever corrodes the steel of his soul.
The sot ain't here or hereabouts, scrag. Most like he's lying in a gutter somewhere, wet with his own gore.
I thought we'd rid ourselves o' yer like when th' 'Cudas came an' 'auled off yer piss-soaked patron.
'Cudas can try, but they won't get more'n a belch an' a wink out of ol' Rostnsthal.
Oh, there be a fair few what's done their damnedest─but there ain't none can make use o' steel what's rusted through.
'Specially no scrag of an adventurer.

Me matey says them 'Cudas 'ave a cell in their brigs colder than a dead whore's stare. First, the cold takes yer toes, then yer fingers...then yer member![@IF($E9(4), That is, if there be one t' take in th' first place. 'E didn't say, but I s'pose it'd freeze a maid's paps off, too.,)] Anyroad, 'e reckons none could last more'n a few days down there...
So, if I gets word in a few days that ol' Rostnsthal's seen [@1A(1)]'is[@1A(0)] last down there, drinks'll be on the 'ouse! Gah hah hah!
The day is Cap'n Rhoswen's!
One glimpse of the [@1A(1)]Lady Infernal[@1A(0)] cutting a straight line to the heart of the fishback fleet, and the Reavers turned tail and ran!
Hah! A Kraken that can't shrug off a fishback's bite has no right to be on the sea.

If memory serves, it was a Kraken cargo ship that was sunk, but a [@1A(1)]Siren[@1A(0)] ship that drove off the Reavers... Hmmm, is it just me, or does a certain crew of eunuchs owe someone a debt of gratitude for saving their worthless arses?
Damn Sirens, spreading their untruths as freely as they spread their legs.
Everyone who was out there knows that it was no Kraken ship that was sunk, but a boat full of bawling bitch-hounds.

Sent out our most heavily armed ships an' began firin' all cannons as soon as we got within range o' the beasts. The Spinner's pull saw us land a few hits, but the Reavers seemed to have sensed our comin', and moved off before we could do any real damage.
A good deal o' coin was lost in that attack. Can't no one say Cap'n Carvallain has a tight fist when it comes to ensurin' the safety o' Limsa Lominsa an' her sailors.
You find the watchman's log. It reads:

“Gotte the beste of the captain today. Wyth all the rotten plankes making up the floore, there ain't no reson a man on watch shouldn't be able to do his dutie while drinking grog and tossing the bones wyth his brothers in the reare storeroom. If some sorrie foole even thought of stealing away wyth our cargo, we'd hear him before he got halfway across the room. Anythinge under four creakes, mind, and we won't trouble ourselves. Ain't about to go chasing after another one of those thryce-damned lemmynges what gotte loose.”
You find a bill of sale. It reads:

“For the following services rendered:[@CR] - Repair of damaged floorboards located[@CR]   in the rear center of west storehouse[@CR][@CR]Recompense of 3000 gil shall be paid, half immediately,[@CR]the other half upon completion[@CR][@CR]Amount paid to date: 1500 gil”
You find a tattered piece of parchment. It reads:

“Caught Reymonde sleepinge amongst the cargo agen. Told him I'd have his hede if he did it so much as once more, but we all know he ain't one for lisseninge. I moved the crates over in front of the rotten flooreboardes so the next time he tryed it, I'd heere him. Be sure to lissen in my steade when I am out!”
See the chief?
You! If you happen to bump into a [@IF($E9(4),scrag-cum-adventurer,whoreson of an adventurer)] by the name of [@STRING($EB(1))], be sure and tell [@IF($E9(4),her,him)] this:

Captain Rhoswen of the Sirens doesn't take kindly to those who decline her generosities. The next time the misguided young [@IF($E9(4),lady,lord)] condescends to make an appearance, she'd very much like to have a little chat with [@IF($E9(4),her,him)]...in private.
Scrag! If you happen to cross paths with an adventurer who calls [@IF($E9(4),her,him)]self [@STRING($EB(1))], would you be kind enough to tell [@IF($E9(4),her,him)] this:
Captain Carvallain of the Kraken's Arms frowns upon acts of cowardice and treachery, and condemns those who consort with cowards and traitors. Condemns them...to death, that is.
Ain't a pirate in Limsa what don't know th' dark past shroudin' th' 'Licia. That be why ye won't find none profanin' th' name o' th' Bloody Executioners. None 'mongst th' livin', at least.

Ye find yerself in the presence o' Cap'n Hyllfyr, ye'd best keep yer eyes t' th' deck an' yer gob stitched tight. One wrong word can get ye flayed an' chained t' th' prow fer th' enjoyment o' the gulls.

E'en the Navigator, in 'Er infinite mercy, ain't got no patience fer the pirate what lacks a ship or th' stones to take one. So if ye still 'arbors any 'ope of one day gracin' the waves, ye'd best be ready to dirty yer knees at the feet o' the cap'n, an' beg fer 'is blessin'.
Off to 'is quarters now, ye say? Then I'd best fetch me mop, 'cause there'll be a bloody deck t' swab once 'e's done with ye.
Just 'cause you was a scrag with the Executioners for a few days don't mean you're worth any more'n a stinkin' splash o' gull lime on a lighthouse.

You could do a score and a half o' good deeds, but people only going to remember the one time you caused 'em grief. The bloody world turns thus, scrag. Ain't nothin' you or me can do t' spin her back-wise.
You th' scrag Rusty Steel gulled into joinin' his “crew”?
Heh. Maybe th' wretch ain't three-quarters as stupid as he lets on. I'll hold me hands up, he had wits enough t' find him a scrag what comes runnin' whene'er he so much as passes wind.
Got naught but a sea lion's share of crab offal 'twixt them ears, I reckon. The instant ye locked fates with Rostnsthal, ye slung yer life out with the morning's soil.

He who chooses the easiest path up is always stuck with the hardest path down. If that be what ye wish, then so be it. But when ye be gazing down at an arse-clenching drop, don't expect any help─especially from the cap'n.
Too much talking! Much too much talking and tittering of [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Talking gone soon! [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)] gone soon!
Captain no happy. No happy captain today. Heads be rolling. Mimiroon going!

Jus' 'cause th' Krakens tossed ye brinewise like a bucketful o' night-soil, it don't follow as ye should be doin' th' same wi' yer pride. Sharin' sheets wi' a spent ol' sot'll earn ye naught in th' way o' respect 'mongst us lot, scrag.
But I ain't th' one t' judge ye this day. The cap'n awaits ye through th' doors behind me, an' ye'd best be seein' him soon, or he'll send a couple o' knives t' fetch ye.

Th' Astalicia's been rife with rumors 'bout 'ow ye sold yer soul t' that piss'ead Rostnsthal t' get yerself a ship. There be a fair few brands o' bollock-brained in this town, but if them rumors 'olds one drop o' truth, ye be right on top o' th' pile.

But them ain't th' only rumors flyin' about. Seems boats all o'er th' bay is bein' robbed by someone seekin' supplies. Shippish ones, like. 'Tis but a matter o' time afore some lad wi' wits enough about 'im sticks two an' two together...an' once [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] 'appens... Eh heh heh heh.
Well, would ye look at th' mighty scrag? They says you ain't got no fear in yer belly, brushin' off both Krakens and Sirens like they was lice on yer livery.
Hah! Don't be thinkin' that'll win ye the regard o' Nunuba Nimblenails. Away with ye! I ain't no godsdamned grimalkin with nine lives to forfeit through clackin' with the likes of ye.

Hope you've got a second set of eyes in the back of that head, now the whole city knows you're dancing the pirate's dance with a good-as-dead drunk. Just so's you know, there'll be quite a few lads and lasses who won't think twice about sticking you from behind.

The old Roegadyn earned himself a hold-full of respect back when he was young. Ruled the seas, he did, but ruled them right. Not like those damned 'Cudas. Now, he's using that respect to bring some order to us pirates. Without him, we'd all be at each other's throats. Well...at each other's throats [@1A(1)]more[@1A(0)].
A right stubborn scrag, wi' more lives'n Fortune's own cat, eh?
Then ye won't mind losin' another, will ye? Heheh!

So [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] were the [@STRING($EB(1))] my captain sought... Quite a bold gesture, concealing your identity from me. Such a gesture [@1A(1)]could[@1A(0)] have cost you your tongue, perhaps more... Ah, but that is all forgotten. My master has a message for you.

Captain Carvallain says he, in all his good grace, would be willing to grant you one last opportunity to join him and his noble crew. That is, if you will kneel before him and renounce all ties with Rostnsthal.
Ain't a pirate in Limsa what don't know th' dark past shroudin' th' 'Licia. That be why ye won't find none profanin' th' name o' th' Bloody Executioners. None 'mongst th' livin', at least.
An' now ye seen firsthand what happens t' them cocksure scrags what think t' cross the line.
Might o' seen yer cap'n in th' lounge. Most like he's fixin' t' break his fast on a cup o' swill, if I'm any judge.
Well now, darlin'...might it be true that ye've gone an' lodged yer allegiances with that drunken cur Rostnsthal?
If ye fancy livin' out yer days in Limsa as a minnow, then who am I to stand in yer way? Just beware when a bigger fish comes swimmin' along, hungerin' for a bite.
I consider myself a man of sound judgment...however, your choice to play Rostnsthal's shadow leaves me...perplexed.

Know this: that man cares for naught but himself, and will not hesitate to use another to obtain that which he desires. He is a disgrace to all...[@1A(1)]honest[@1A(0)] pirates in the city, and I suggest─for your sake─that you reconsider your relationship with him [@1A(1)]soon[@1A(0)].
Still breathin', I see...
Th' Twelve grants most but one turn at life 'ere on 'Ydaelyn. Some, like ye, be born wi' two.

Yet instead o' countin' yer blessin's an' puttin' ten score malms 'twixt ye an' th' 'Licia...[@1A(1)]'ere ye be.[@1A(0)] I've 'alf a mind t' cleave yer empty bastard braincase meself, YE BLOODY FOOL!!!
Adventurer or no, 'tis not oft th' Executioners show mercy to a scrag. Ye wasn't feignin' a bane-sore now, was ye? 'Cause if ye was, and th' cap'n finds out, ye'll wish 'e'd killed ye the first time!
Way I sees it, th' Executioners ain't gonna suffer ye t' live more'n a few bells longer. Ye be runnin' out o' choices, scrag...unless, o' course, it be [@1A(1)]runnin'[@1A(0)] ye be set on choosin'.
Executioners roughed you up a bit, did they?
If you were a Siren, then there might have been some pleasure to go with that pain.
So, it was [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] that Rhoswen sought! Ha! Braved your beating like a true pirate, did you?

Before you are reduced to a troublesome stain on the Astalicia's deck, why not take up a position with the Sirens? I can think of a handful of my sisters who would welcome your company, and a handful of [@1A(1)]positions[@1A(0)] you might all enjoy! Aha ha ha!
Th' crew'll be sendin' more men t' stand vigil on th' cliffs, an' more swiftboats t' patrol th' Rhotano. Them Reavers won't likely catch us off guard again.
By the by, we's always in need o' new scrags. Th' cap'n'll pay ye a thousand gil per day fer yer services...an' ye be more'n welcome t' keep all that's left after me an' me mateys takes our cut.
If it ain't me first an' only mate! As chuffed as I am t' see ye─an' I [@1A(1)]am[@1A(0)] right chuffed, 'tis true─I ne'ertheless 'as urgent business what needs tendin' to wi' all due 'aste.
Jus' ye leave th' dealin's t' ol' Rostnsthal, now, eh? Run along an' 'ave yerself an 'ard-earned swig o' rum on th' 'Licia. I'll be wi' ye a few bells 'ence.
Where in th' seven hells ye been, scrag!? Don't recall no one sayin' ye could take leave o' th' ship!
The cap'n ain't finished wi' ye yet, though ye'll be good an' [@1A(1)]finished[@1A(0)] when he is, an' that's fer sure.
Ye say ye got somethin' fer th' cap'n, eh?
Well, it jus' so happens th' chief had his men up on deck lookin' fer ye not more'n a few bells back. Reckon that makes this yer lucky day! Eh-heh-heh-heh.
Th' cap'n seems right taken wi' yer stubborn will t' live. Either that, or 'e's tickled by 'ow ye're too thick t' die... Anyroad, don't go pushin' yer luck. Ye already lost one life.
Won't find the cap'n down here with us scrags. He'll be up top.

And ye'd best not be thinkin' o' tryin' anythin' clever, like. The cap'n may have seen somethin' in ye what pleased him, but as long as ye're wipin' Rostnsthal's shite-caked arse, ain't no one goin' t' trust ye as far as they can spit.
Ain't a pirate in Limsa what don't know th' dark past shroudin' th' 'Licia. That be why ye won't find none profanin' th' name o' th' Bloody Executioners. None 'mongst th' livin', at least.
Cap'n need only say th' word an' there ain't a soul aboard this here ship what'd think twice about slittin' the pipes of a bottom-feedin' scrag like yerself. Best remember that.
I'll give ye this─ye got bigger balls 'n Thal 'imself, showin' yer ugly mug in 'ere after what came about th' last time.
Now, that don't mean I'll be stowin' me mop jus' yet. Chances are, I'll be swabbin' yer gore come the next bell.
H-How in the seven hells did ye─?
Ye slipped 'im a tidy sum o' gelt, didn't ye? He'd never have let ye go fer less...an' wi' only a cut t' yer name.
No, I ain't one t' be questionin' th' whims o' th' cap'n. He knows what he's doin'...I hope.
There be but one way t' learn yerself proper axe-wieldin', an' that be by takin' a few 'eads. Yer favorite drunk used t' be th' best, but ye won't get naught out of 'im no longer.
'Eard th' cap'n lifted th' blade from o'er yer neck.
Seems the Spinner 'as other plans fer ye, an' today weren't yer day t' pass through one o' the seven gates.
As fer the morrow...who can say?
Weren't one among us what didn't 'ear ol' Hyllfyr's applause ringin' through th' 'old...

Me mates say ye fought more like a land-'uggin' 'venturer than a pirate... Won't catch none of us followin' suit, but a victory's a victory. Can't no one take that from ye.
Th' cap'n always welcomes a challenge. 'Tis why 'e takes on adventurers. Says there be not two the same in all 'Ydaelyn, an' that there be no foe better fer keepin' 'im on 'is toes.
Hic! Godsdamned justice-preachin' son of a─ <belch>

If it hadn't come straight from th' good cap'n's mouth, I'd scarcely have credited me ears. Hyllfyr's only gone an' absolved ye of all yer former sins. Seems ye can stay on th' ship wi' th' rest of us dogs.

Cannot fer the life o' me comprehend what ye think ye'll be gainin' by continuin' this farce o' yers wi' ol' Rusty Steel. Then again, only a scrag can scry th' workin's of another scrag's muddled mind, an' Waekbyrt ain't been a scrag since afore ye was a stinkin' seed wrigglin' up yer mammy's undercarriage.

Eh? Lookin' fer th' drunk, now, are ye? Hmph, wait yer bloody turn. The chief has business wi' him, an' all. Trouble is, th' slippery sod's most like sleepin' in an alley somewhere, havin' given his sewer rat neighbors instructions not t' wake him.
Speakin' o' business, what crew'd ye end up lendin' yer pearly smile to, scrag?
Hahaha! A town o' pirates, an' you had t' go an' choose that one!
Hahahahaha! Me gut...ahahahahah!
Oh, ye was in earnest... Well, then...ahahahah...ye'd best go an'...ahehe-HA-hehe...report t' th' cap'n. Y'see, scrag, ain't no one joinin' no crew wi'out [@1A(1)]his[@1A(0)] blessin'. Heheheh.
He's through th' door behind me, scrag. But if I was you, I'd say me farewells t' the dogs in th' lounge afore steppin' in. Might be they'll never see ye again. Gah hah hah hah!
Don't go thinkin' ye've a choice now, scrag. Wouldn't be wise t' put this off fer too long. 'Tis a veritable matter o' life or death, see―more specific'ly, [@1A(1)]your[@1A(0)] life or death.
Accept Rostnsthal's offer?
Can't ye see I'm busy here? Ain't got time fer scrags or their scrag-brained schemes. Now flog off.
Eh? That drunken oaf order ye t' go robbin' other lairs?
Can't say that be a good idea, scrag. Bad blood a-brewin' 'twix th' rival factions lately. All th' gangs been busy settin' traps t' make sure ain't no one gettin' t' their goods.
O' course, Rostnsthall be knowin' all this, an' still 'as the gall t' ask ye t' risk yer life while he be off sottin' an' whorin'.

Now, I ain't one fer stabbin' a man in th' back, even if he ain't no better 'n a boil on me arse, but I'd say it's right time ye start considerin' a change o' allegience. I knows a place where ye might be able t' find somethin'...if yer int'rested.
Accept Rostnsthal's offer?
Alright, but what I'm about t' tell ye ain't public domain. Ye go off blabbin',xxxxx Once in, ye'll figure out what needs t' be done. Now, off with ye, scrag!
Accept Rostnsthal's offer?
A new recruit, eh? Well, remember this--we got only two rules. No fightin' and no lendin'. Got it?
Ye see the woman over there? That's Tiphainia. Talk to her and hope that she's in a good mood...or else. Got it?
Do I look like a chef? Toss the remains in that jar.
You won't be receving any compensation from me. Cacaya's sent your gil to the Astalicia. Now off with you.
Eard ye ruffled a few feathers down at [xxxxx].
No, no. Ye don't need explain yerself t' me, scrag. Ye did what ye were told, and Cacaya ain't the type t' go back on 'is word. Yer gelt's right 'ere.
But if I's ye, I'd spend it quick.
Word spreads 'at ye angered the Lifestealer,/woan walkin'.
Me first mate! Listen ye up, 'cause I gots some ill tidings. Our days as pirates might be numbered.
Lately,yellowcoats..all preventin' me from doin' th' business I needs be doin' t' keep our lil' enterprise afloat-like.
Me face be known t' near on th' whole gods-forsaken city. One wrong move an' I'd be tossed into the brig t' rot.
Ah, but me first mate'll save us,he/sheTaran Give 'im this grog an' he'll do th' rest.
Accept Rostnsthal's offer?
An' don't even think o' drinkin' that, ye 'ear?
We ain't got time t' sniff daisies an' ponder life's lil' mysteries. Our well being's ridin' th' plank an' about t' be shoved t' th' sharks!
Accept Rostnsthal's offer?
First and foremost, and foremostly first, you will find the shortest path to becoming a puller is by earning the respect of your fellow guildbrothers and sisters.

Of course, the shortest path to [@1A(1)]respect[@1A(0)] is via [@1A(1)]gratitude[@1A(0)]; and what better way to make a guildbrother or sister grateful than by offering assistance!? Now, as luck would have it, there [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] a puller in need of assistance, even as we speak. The fair fishwife over yon, poring over the nautical charts, to be precise. Her name is Maisie. Heed her pleas and she may end up helping you more than you help her.

Oh no. Oh no, no. I could never reveal to you the [@1A(1)]exact[@1A(0)] place you will find [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000127,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000127,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. If I were to do so, then you would tell your friends, and they would tell their friends, and before long, every wide-eyed adventurer in the realm would be casting their lines off the cliffs, dreams of fortune filling up their heads. It would then only be a matter of time before every last remora would be gone, and we'd be up to our necks in Sahagin.

And if you are fortunate enough to fish one up, don't, don't, don't─no really, [@1A(1)]don't[@1A(0)]─even consider selling it to the highest bidder. Not only will you invoke the ire of the scholarlies up at Mealvaan's Gate, but you will risk alienating yourself from the pullers down here in Fisherman's Bottom.
And that in itself may be an understatement. Why, the last adventurer who tried something similar went missing...only to be found floating head down off Widow Cliffs.
So you're the new recruit N'nmulika mentioned. Nice to have you aboard.

I can see in your eyes that you are wondering why, if [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000127,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000127,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] are so important to quelling the Sahagin threat, we don't save ourselves some trouble and raise them in our fishery ponds over in the Barrel. Well, these beasties happen to be blind as bats, and will swim straight into the nets surrounding the ponds. Once caught in the weave, they start thrashing about, and will have cut themselves to ribbons in no more than a few bells. In short, it's not nice, and it's certainly not useful.
Done a fair job, you 'ave, but not near as good as we needs.

I reckon no less 'n [@VALUE($E8(1))] more o' the nasty remora'll suffice. Now shut your gob, grab your tackle, 'ead back to the cliffs, an' get fishin'! The longer we take, the more our puller mates cop it.

“Pullers” is a broad term used to describe a band of fishermen and women working together on the seas. There are quite a few of these bands here in Limsa, but Wawalago's is the first, the biggest, and the best. Ask anyone here and they'll tell you the same.

Though each band is technically independent, we make certain to look out for one another. The Knights of the Barracuda, meanwhile, look out for all of us. Without them, many of our brothers and sisters might never have made it back to port.

Maisie has you out fishing for [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000127,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000127,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]? You have my sympathies, mate. Them godsforsaken merbeasts are the worst-tasting things in the sea, and that's including sand, otter dung, and rotting Sahagin corpses.

Not more than a generation ago, you'd never see one on dry land─we'd always throw 'em back─but since the 'Cudas discovered the Sahagin crave the nasty little buggers, there now be pullers who make their livin' solely off dredgin' 'em up from the Deep.
You the minnow helpin' Maisie?

Then ye'd be wise t' 'quip yerself with at least a willow rod. There be some what say a fisher needs naught but th' strength t' pull a devil from th' drink...but t' that bilge, I reply, a fisher ain't like t' do much pullin' when his rod's a-snapped in twain.

There are a hundred things that might kill a man on the sea, from an angry storm to a dim-witted deckhand, but for the most part, those things can be prevented. But the Sahagin... No amount of preparation can ready a sailor for the horrors he'll face if the fishbacks decide it's him they want in their bellies.

And that is why I fear for my fellow pullers' lives each and every time they leave port. If they'd only listen to reason and join me in fishing from the cliffs, they wouldn't need to worry about anything but their footing.
Oh, Bloemerl. Might [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] know of anyone who would be interested in learning under a great fisherwoman? It's simply not fair that Maisie gets her own servant...er, I mean student.

I wouldn't wish an initiate on the worst of my enemies. It's true, they help you with this and that, but who do you think must put up the coin when they complete a task? Not our tight-pursed netmaster, that's for certain.

'Twas not long ago, them brigands from th' Astalicia paid us a visit, in 'opes that we'd rid th' seas of ev'ry last [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000127,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000127,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] for 'em. Why? 'Ow would I know? They're pirates. One of 'em probably saw the fish floppin' on 'is deck and thought 'e was lookin' at 'is mother's pocked arse.
Th' netmaster was mighty wise t' decline their offer. Ye see, if we'd culled the lot, we'd 'ave naught wi' which t' lure th' Sahagin.
I only 'ope 'e's forgotten 'ow 'twas I that said as we should take th' job...

Remember, [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000127,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000127,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] are pretty common in the waters all along the shores of lowland La Noscea. Shouldn't be no trouble catchin' some─providin' you got the right bait.

Let's see, then... I reckon [@VALUE($E8(1))] or so should be enough to coax them fishbacks up from their sea 'oles. And once they show their ugly 'eads, our lads'll be waitin' to smack 'em straight back down again.
Excellent, excellent!

Now, now─before admitting you to our ranks, allow me to intimate one important item of information. We pullers do not let our lives become bogged down by things microscopic, miniature, minute, and or miniscule. We do our damnedest to desist from unduly distressing ourselves about anything deemed diminutive.

To be one of us, you must have a heart as open and free as the boundless blue sky, as deep and wide as the swirling cerulean seas, and as hot and bothered as the blistering rays of the scintillating sun. And if you don't...well, being here can only help you obtain one.
No, no...mere words cannot make you see what your eyes must see, for seeing is done with the eyes, not the ears. Now I see your heart is that of a normal person; a non-puller person.
But perhaps completing a simple job for the pullers will help “pull” your heartstrings in the appropriate direction, no?
Ha ha, ha ha! Wonderful! Speak with Maisie hiding somewhere here in the guild. She has a prickly problem that's positively pleading for some particularly prompt problem-solving!
Oh my, oh my. Needless to say, that is not the answer I was expectantly expecting.
Oh my, oh my. Needless to say, that is not the answer I was expectantly expecting.

If anyone can cure you of this fit of unemployment, it would be that one ever-shining light who brightens our guild with her blistering rays, even during its darkest of days─Sisipu! Inquire with her if there is not something she might have you do.

Oh, do not even think of making Sisipu wait. She is much, much busier than she seems─though perhaps not quite as busy as one might conversely conclude having been forewarned of her deceptive demeanor.

I once met a maiden♪[@CR]Who lived in the sea♪[@CR]With kelp in her hair♪[@CR]And fins on her feet!♪[@CR]What? Oh! You're looking to cross over to the Barrel, are you? Does it have to be today? The waves...they look awfully high. I...I mean, you...could get tossed over the side, and then who would─ Oh, you say you're on an errand for Sisipu? Well, then we'd best be on our way!
Ride with Rerenasu to the Barrel?
Ride with Rerenasu to the Barrel?

Return to Fisherman's Bottom?

Normally, I would feed the hungry herring and starving sturgeon myself, but the netmaster has, in his [@1A(1)]infinite[@1A(0)] wisdom, bestowed me with a bucketful of urgent tasks that require my immediate attention. Enough with the dalliance, and on with dance! These fishes do not need any more food, they require a thoroughly thorough stimulation of their humours!

I spy something suspicious on your person, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. To what could that piece of parchment in your pouch possibly pertain?

Hmmm... Petitioned by a strange mustachioed man to travel off to the far, far desert sands of Ul'dah, there to procure an outfit that will help you better...feed fish? I...don't know what to say...[@CR]...other than bon voyage!
You say you've been sent on a trip to Ul'dah?

Well, the only means of crossing to the mainland is by ship, and unless you own one, which I doubt you do, you're left with a choice between purchasing a ferry ticket or talking your way onto a pirate vessel. Truth be told, I probably wouldn't recommend the latter option, as they'd most like only let you on long enough to steal all your belongings and throw your naked corpse to the sharks.
You look as if you've seen a ghost, mate. Finally spotted the Beast of the Barrel, did you?

You say you saw a strange Lalafell who made you dance a jig and then sent you off on a journey across the Merlthor to fetch him a pair of knickers? Why...who-whoever could that be? Ahem. Well, I have nets to knit. Good day, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Once you've th' knack o' feedin' fish o'er in the Barrel, I'd reckon th' next thing Sisipu'll have you do is dredge the pools...and aye, it [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] as bad as it sounds.

If ye came lookin' fer Sisipu, ye jus' missed the poor lass. Netmaster 'as 'er on another one of 'is “special” missions, see... Which more oft than not entails runnin' down t' th' Bismarck an' fetchin' 'im a bowl o' their tasty chowder.

If ye've 'ad yer fill o' feedin' the fishes, now might be a fine time t' get in some o' that adventurin' your lot seems so fond of─maybe e'en visit yerself a new city[@1F]state. Oh? Already plannin' a trip to Ul'dah, are ye?
Did the fish down in the Barrel appear to be in good health? You did not happen to see any signs of the blight, did you?

They were jumping about, then? Wonderful! And if I am to believe Rerenasu, you were doing a fair amount of jumping as well. Might I ask why? Ah...on second thought, some truths are better let alone, are they not?
Huh. I would never have taken [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] for the type...
But then again, who am I to judge? We're one and the same, friend. Heh heh heh.
Something smells of sand and spice... Might I assume your absence from our halls meant you took that voyage you had planned to Ul'dah?
Ah, and in the nick of time, I would say. Why, just this morning I received a message in a bottle requesting that you come down to the Barrel...alone. Armed with certain...finery.
You look fatigued, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You didn't truly travel all the way to Ul'dah, did you?

Twelve be good! I am always amazed by the resourcefulness of you adventurers. So, was the desert city everything they say? Were the walls made of solid gold? Did the fountains run red with wine? <sigh> I can't imagine what it must be like to be in a place where you can't see the sea.
Would you look what the tide brought in! And where have you been, matey?
In Ul'dah purchasing a “mystery item,” you say? Ahem, well...I, er...I've got hooks to...to...[@1A(1)]polish?[@1A(0)] Yes, that was it─[@1A(1)]lots[@1A(0)] of hooks to polish. So if you don't mind...
Did you hear, Bloemerl? That poor adventurer made it all the way to Ul'dah and back in one piece.
Now that, I do not believe. Why would anyone who actually made it off this godsforsaken island ever feel the need to come back?
Ah, but here that someone is... Let me give you some advice, [@IF($E9(4),lassie,son)]. If you ever find yourself on the mainland again, do yourself a favor and stay there.
Lady Sisipu's been in an' out o' th' guild e'er since ye went gallivantin' off to Ul'dah.
Ol' netmaster must be plannin' somethin' big...and that ain't never good.
If I get my hands on that fool of a netmaster, I'll use his tiny bloody member to hook myself something tasty from the Barrel!

What did he do, you ask? What did he do [@1A(1)]this time[@1A(0)], you mean. Word has it, the chefs down at the Bismarck found a stout, mustachioed man in the scullions' quarters, rifling through the serving maids' smallclothes! Hmph! Not a woman here needs more than one guess to tell you who the culprit is!
Oh! [@IF($E9(4),She,He)]'s back! And in fine fettle, I must say! Now dance! Dance to your heart's content!
Oh! [@IF($E9(4),She,He)]'s back! And in fine fettle, I must say! Now dance! Dance to your heart's content!
Do you delight in doubting all that you do not understand?
Go on, then! Catch one of the creatures circling about the pools and I shall show your mean mistrust to be utterly and undeniably undeserved.
Oh dear, oh dear. I do not believe I have ever seen our dear Sisipu so upset. The netmaster had best be on guard if he wishes to see his next nameday.
Most folk would be properly seething if they found out they'd wandered halfway across the realm for a sackful of sod all, but you seem to be taking it well enough. Ah hah hah hah.

I can understand why Sisipu is so upset, but I reckon her anger's preventing her from seeing what's truly important. This “mystery man,” who none will deny has caused you an ocean of grief, has also provided you with invaluable guidance, whether you realize it now or not. You'd do well not to forget that, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Heh heh. 'Twould seem you truly did tackle th' Beast o' th' Barrel...in a sense.
Times like these, we're best off trustin' to our strength, fer 'tis strength what conquers all...I suppose.

Well, Bloemerl, seems that adventurer did what was bid of [@IF($E9(4),her,him)], ne'er uttering a single protest, even though it meant playing pander to that perverted pip. The [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] must be made of stone and sinew to suffer what [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] did.
Perhaps... You will find that many who join this guild have a certain fire which burns deep in the fathomless depths of their souls. Without it, they wouldn't last a bell with [@1A(1)]him[@1A(0)].
Fret not o'er wee Sisipu. Ol' Xavie'll see t' the poor lass.
Th' ragin' storm what roils within 'er soul ain't no match fer these tender 'ands o' mine. Heh heh heh.

<sigh> Though it pains me to say it, I fear the fiend has escaped with his filthy neck once again... And I was so hoping Sisipu would get him this time. There are a few issues I have been meaning to press him on myself...
<sigh> Why do I even bother?

I apologize on behalf of the guild, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You did a wonderful job with all the tasks you were assigned, no matter how...er...unusual some of them may have seemed. I've already entrusted your reward to N'nmulika. Speak with her to collect it. I do hope this won't discourage you from remaining with the pullers. You are truly one of a kind, and it would be a great loss to the guild if you were to leave us.
Yes, yes. I have already spoken with Sisipu about your reward.
We were all jolly impressed by the grace with which you comported yourself down in the Barrel. A truly memorable display, I must say. Well worth the price of admission, ahaha...ahem.
Let's think of it as another stage in your initiation. Yes, let us think that.
Now hold forth your hand, so that I might fill it with coin!

Fine food for our fine fish! So fine, in fact, that it is fit for a fisher, as well as a flounder! No one here will judge you if you cannot fight the urge to feast on a handful of that fabulous fodder intended for the fishery. If you happen to run out of Sisipu's special blend, you need only ask for more.

Just be certain that you do not overfeed our [@1A(1)]friends[@1A(0)]. Their brains are as small as those of a...well, fish. As long as there is food afloat, they will continue to eat and eat until they explode! And I have yet to meet anyone who enjoys a blown bream.
Most of the fish we raise in the Bottom are gutted, cleaned, and then sold on Hawkers' Alley to the people of Limsa Lominsa. The Bismarck will buy up a fair amount as well.

For those looking for something a little more exciting than haggling with a fishmonger, we allow one and all to come down and fish in the ponds themselves. That is, for a small fee, of course. If you have the time, and the bait, you might just end up going home with a bargain!

You'll find all sorts of fish there in the Barrel, from tiger cod to coral butterflies...even saber sardines. Though, there are some sea-dwellers what don't take to being confined to a corner of the great blue. To catch them, there's nothing for it but fishing the old-fashioned way─with a swift ship, a strong rod, and some sweet-smelling bait.

But lately, there have been queer rumors of a titanic sawfish lurking deep in one of the ponds, though which one depends on who you ask. Many have claimed to have seen him, and more than a few boast of having him on their line, until he breaks free just as they're about to wrench him from the water. Strange thing is, there ain't no record of a puller ever putting one in the ponds. Another fishwives' tale, if you ask me.

Helpin' out Sisipu this time, are ye? That's right decent o' ye. Feedin' them fish down at the Barrel ain't no easy task. The burnin' sun beatin' down on yer back like ye was a slab of iron from the forge, the unrelentin' winds off the sea saltin' yer skin like ye was a pike fit fer picklin'... Heh. Now ye knows why old Undsatz stays in here.

Tell me, Bloemerl, how long do you reckon that new adventurer─[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I think [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] name was─will last? Maisie speaks quite highly of [@IF($E9(4),her,him)], but she cannot truly believe that [@IF($E9(4),she'll,he'll)] stay with the guild long enough to earn a place on one of our ships...can she?

Out of all the guilds in Limsa, [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] had wits enough about [@IF($E9(4),her,him)] to choose this one. That must count for something. Now whether [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] won't just up an' leave the moment the wind changes, like most of them adventurers, well, only the Navigator can tell you that, and last I heard, she ain't wont to converse with the likes of us.
The Navigator's a fickle mistress. 'Tis said th' waves on th' sea be like t' th' waves in 'er 'eart. Them who rides 'em can just as soon move 'er t' mercy as they can t' wroth.

And, if ye're one t' believe th' musin's o' th' netmaster, a man's countenance can also meddle wi' th' goddess's moods. Now whether that be true or nay, I 'onestly could not say...but I'm not one t' question th' ravin's of a madma─er...th' logic of our fine leader.
To reach the Barrel, you will need to ask young Rerenasu to ferry you across in his dinghy.

The boy is so infatuated with Sisipu, he volunteered to help with transport to the Barrel...even though he cannot spend more than five minutes on a boat without his face turning as green as chokeweed. If you value your garments, I suggest sitting behind the lad.
Finally! I was beginning to worry you'd left us high and dry.

Now listen, and listen well─there's a job here with your name on it; clearly marked with the name, “[@STRING($EB(1))],” it is; a job for you, and you alone...unless you refuse, in which case it will no longer be yours. But you won't refuse, because it's [@1A(1)]yours[@1A(0)], right?
Very well, very well. Then you can start by speaking with Sisipu. She's just over there.
Oh me, oh my. You seem to be missing that mite of motivation that might mold you into a mighty [@IF($E9(4),maiden,man)].
Indeed, indeed! You have more than every right to participate in matters such as these, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You are one of us now, one and the same! Now hurry off to the back room!
Everyone dropped what they were doing to participate in the strike. I, for one, am glad of the rest.
We had a vote, and decided to go on strike. Ain't stopped us loiterin' around the guild, though.
Heh. Seems the Beast of the Barrel finally got caught in someone's net.
You come as well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? Can't deny not bein' a bit surprised, what with 'ow a certain little bugger put you through an 'undred 'ells down at the feedin' ponds.

Well, be sure an' speak your mind, mate. Jus' 'cause you takes yourself for a scrod with no 'int of a say in guild matters, don't mean you need keep your gob shut. You 'ave somethin' to say, you bloody well say it.
Twelve be damned! Th' sale o' th' bleedin' century an' fate 'ands me a bucket o' slop an' dumps me on Barrel duty.
Looks like I'd best be findin' me a new scrod t' tend the ponds. Don't fancy 'elpin' ol' Maisie out again, do you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]?[@CR]...Aye, I didn't reckon you would.

A sale!? This folly will see the guild's coffers empty faster than an undarned net at pulling! Why, it seems like only yesterday that the netmaster was telling us we'd have to open our doors to adventurers so that we might save on wages paid!

And I thought this might finally be the day I left me spot here in the guild and spent some time with me wife and sprats... But now...who knows? Maybe they'll come up from the Sailors Ward to see me for a change.
Me missus's been hintin' as she'd like a fancy aqua-box, like the ones they got here in the guild. Who knows, if the sale brings in enough coin, I may yet buy her one.
Hells' bells! Was set t' make me a killin' today, I was...and what happens? Me best rod snaps atwain!
Buggers are [@1A(1)]always[@1A(0)] bleedin' breakin' on me! I'm startin' t' wonder if there [@1A(1)]be[@1A(0)] a rod out there what can bear th' pull o' mighty Undsatz!

Thinking of getting all your fish from the Barrel, are you? Well, that wouldn't be fair now, would it? You'd waltz back to the guild with a basketful of breams, and the other fishers would all cheer and praise you on your prowess as a puller. And then Sisipu would...!
No! No! I will have none of this treachery! You shall not have my help, usurper! Sisipusurper! The only way you will see the Barrel today is if you swim over there yourself! Hmph!
The nerve of that lecherous leech! How dare he use us for his own gain!
Now I must needs find someone I can use for [@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] own gain...and where ever might I fish up such a fine catch on such short notice?[@CR]......Why, what do we have here?

While they might have seemed spontaneous, the netmaster's actions were anything but unpredictable. And that is why this morning I bid the acolytes under my tutelage set out and begin fishing offshore. A few more moons with us, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and you will learn that there is [@1A(1)]always[@1A(0)] a method to Wawalago's “madness.”

'Eard the netmaster, didn't ye? 'Tis all about love, it is. And there ain't a single sod among this lot what's seen more sweet lovin', an' given so freely of 'is 'umble seed, than yers truly[@IF($E9(4),─uh, no offense, milady,)]. Anyway...if it be love that ye seek this fine day, ye need only 'eed th' advice of 'onest Xavalien 'ere.

In times like these, 'tis a common belief that the [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)] what works 'ardest gets the best o' th' kisses when [@IF($E9(4),'er,'is)] day's labors be done. But 'tis lies, I tell ye. [@1A(1)]Real[@1A(0)] [@IF($E9(4),men,women)] lust fer the [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)] what shows calmness in th' very jaws o' th' storm─'cause it be [@IF($E9(4),she,'e)] who they want beside 'em when th' waves o' passion come crashin' at their stern! Remember them words, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I ain't one t' steer ye wrong.

If you wish to take full advantage of the opportunity the netmaster has presented us, it would be wise to first contrive a plan of attack. My advice to you is simple─ignore the smaller fare and concentrate only on the big catch.

Oh, and never let the location choose you. Trust your instincts and select a spot that [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] feel is right, never one chosen by another. I find the same advice useful when choosing a man to bed. A hah hah hah hah!
Well, well. I must say, that was the last thing I expected, but then again, one never knows [@1A(1)]what[@1A(0)] to expect when dealing with our nefarious netmaster.
And soon the Fisherman's Bottom will be abuzz with the buzzing of fishers fishing and fishmongering.

Which leads me to the question: why ever are you still here? Why are you not down by the docks netting me a plump, juicy [@SWITCH($E8(1),[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011213,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,3011213,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011203,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,3011203,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011209,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,3011209,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011217,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,3011217,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011225,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,3011225,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)])]? Bring back one of those beauties and I'll make it worth your while!

I am so, so sorry, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Time has expired! There are some who say the netmaster's generosity is as deep as a well, but we ourselves have seldom found it to be any deeper than his privy.

The guild will be glad to take [@SWITCH($E8(1),[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011213,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,3011213,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011203,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,3011203,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011209,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,3011209,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011217,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,3011217,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)],[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3011225,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,3011225,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)])] off your hands at a good price. But only if you bring it back within [@IF($E5($E8(2),0),[@IF($E2($E8(2),10),[@SWITCH($E8(2),one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE($E8(2))])],[@VALUE($E8(2))])] [@IF($E4($E8(2),1),bell's,bells')] time!
Gil and gil! But there's still more gil for the getting!
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! You come to file a formal grievance with 'is 'orny 'ighness? You've every right, you know! 'Specially after what th' man put you through.
If you'd like, we can go in together. I'll be right there at your side while you give 'im what for!

Why not see if you can convince the netmaster to [@IF($E9(4),grace you with an extension, too,give you an extension of your own)]? Only the Twelve know what he might say...or do, but it can't hurt to ask now, can it?

An extension!? If we continue paying these exorbitant prices for the city's fish, the guild will find itself drowning in debt...and putrid seafood! For my part, rotten fish is not a smell I want our members to be associated with!

How quick they are to forget! Why, it weren't more than a few bells back that every man and woman in this guild had it in their minds to feed the netmaster to the krakens. Yet toss a few coins on the floor, and yesterday's crimes are forgotten...
But what truly boils my bile is that, by some sleight of hand, he has us working even bloody [@1A(1)]harder[@1A(0)] than we were before this farce began!
Turns out, I didn't need me no rod when I got me these here arms.
Slung a few boulders in Iron Lake, I did, an' 'tweren't long afore th' fish came a-floatin' t' th' top, ripe fer th' pluckin'. Gah hah hah hah!
I made enough coin today to court my Sisipu for at least three more turns of the moon, if not four!
It was a fine idea to do all my fishing in the Barr─er...erl...ulp!
No matter how big the wave, a good fisher will never lose his balance. And as you can see, our netmaster is at his most upright when set adrift in an ocean of adversity by mutinous seamen.

However, what the little man has regretfully failed to recognize is that the biggest wave is yet to come... And when [@1A(1)]she[@1A(0)] does, it will only be a matter of time before he finally ends up on his back.
Ye take me advice concernin' the [@IF($E9(4),laddies,ladies)]?
Calm as a summer sea, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]. Calm as a summer sea. Don't ye go makin' waves, now, 'ear?

I've never been so exhausted in my life... I barely have the strength to bear a grudge against the netmaster, though over the past few days, he's done naught but continue to provide us with good reason to remain sore wroth.
And that harlot of a Miqo'te with her honey-tongue hasn't helped a whit! The netmaster's probably locked up in his office polishing the mast just thinking of her.
Could [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] be the reason for the [@1A(1)]unmentionables[@1A(0)]...?
...And [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] is the reason behind the dance?
Ahem! Of course I knew the answer all along! Light clothing and dancing! It's so simple, you'd have to be blind not to see it!
<sigh> Pains me t' say it...but th' netmaster [@1A(1)]does[@1A(0)] have 'is uses...some o' the time, that is.
Aye, I said the netmaster had 'is uses, but don't think I enjoy admitting it.
Your call for an extension went limp, you say? What a terrible letdown. Terrible. Then again, if a sale never ended, one could not very well call it a sale, now, could one?

Ah, but that is beside the point. [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], as always, you have proven an invaluable asset to our guild, and your resilience in the face of...er...irrationality has seen you past another malmstone on your path to becoming a fine fisher[@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]! I would undoubtedly doff my cap to you...were I wearing one...which I am! (But I won't...)
Good, good! You're just in time!

Everyone and anyone who's anyone in the Pullers' Guild─and plenty who aren't─is attending a meeting on how to improve the day-to-day running of our glorious organization. It's the perfect opportunity for you to intimate your innovative ideas, submit your sage suggestions, and contribute your carefully considered comments! Join us!
Yes? Yes! Now off you go! I believe the festivities have already begun, and it would not be meet for you to miss any more of the meeting than you already have missed!
Really? Really? This guild is yours as much as it is mine. You really might want to consider reconsidering. Really.
