text_en: This was not...his doing. He already lay dying...when we found him.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Breathe, Pfrym. Gods damn it, breathe. Gods damn it, you bastard, you never backed away from anything in your life! Now fight! Fiiight!!!

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: What of Pfrymloef? Does he live? Please...tell me...

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Business with Master Cid? Then you are in luck. Both he and Foreman Ebrelnaux are here with us now, though they do not normally attend such tasks.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Every resource we have to spare is now focused on Meteor. So far, all our lines of investigation have pointed us in the direction of a certain remnant of the Allagan Empire─a structure.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: What's more, we've also learned that valuable literature concerning this structure is kept here in Gridania. That is what has brought Master Cid and the foreman.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: So far, all our lines of investigation have pointed us in the direction of a certain remnant of the Allagan Empire. We have also learned that Gridania is home to some uniquely valuable literature on the subject. That is what brings Master Cid and the foreman.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Gods be good, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)], can't you see I'm using my linkpearl? ...What? No, not you─someone here with me. Yes─ That's what I was trying to─ Gah! You! Yes, [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)], [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─go and talk to someone else while I finish my conversation!

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Gods, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], what kept you? Quinquerol said you'd be coming. He didn't say you'd take so damned [@1A(1)]long[@1A(0)]! Come, tell me what you've learned.

text_en: Seven hells... Then the Empire means to recreate the tragedy of ten years past. And now Gaius has joined his strength to the cause...

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: It is no diversion. What the White Raven said is true. But Twelve be good, have they already drawn so close!?

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: I myself played a part in the Empire's Meteor project during my time in Garlemald. I only wish I could work out what it is they've discovered in the years since I left.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: All I know for sure is that this─[@1A(1)]all[@1A(0)] of the Empire's machinations of late─is a grand experiment to recreate the ancient magic known as Meteor.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Decades ago, a Garlean engineer made a remarkable discovery─the ruins of a great Allagan structure.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Within it was a device they believed could somehow send [@1A(1)]waves[@1A(0)] of energy to Dalamud─waves of energy that could [@1A(1)]influence[@1A(0)] the celestial body itself.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Not long after, it was proposed that the device be used to cast Dalamud down upon the lands of the beast tribes. But to do this, a breed of sorcery powerful enough to tear the very stars from the sky was needed─Meteor.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Only Garlemald could devise such an act of villainy. Aye, here was a chance to annihilate the beastman threat in a single catastrophic stroke. And so they gathered every man of science they could to begin work on this grand endeavor...

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: But things didn't go so smoothly for the murderous bastards. In the end, all efforts were called off. That was just ten years ago.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Some elements were beyond their control, others beyond their comprehension. Dalamud could not be harnessed as they'd hoped. My father was among those who... Bah! You don't need to hear about that.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Ruins from thousands of years ago? Ha! To even [@1A(1)]think[@1A(0)] they could make it work is a testament to Garlemald's hubris. And it seems they mean to continue trying.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Were it not for the involvement of van Darnus, I'd laugh at the bastards and be done with it. But the men of his line have long been the keepers of Allagan knowledge. Could that godless fiend have made some new discovery?

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: I pray not. The man is a monster. He kills enemy and ally alike─any who might oppose him. To look upon the son, you'd not imagine his father the hero he was.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: After his death, all his loyal advisors found themselves less a head upon van Darnus's command. Hells, if the whisperings at court are to be believed, he even had a hand in his father's demise.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One

text_en: And this is the maniac into whose hands a weapon of untold power has fallen. Perhaps now you see why I don't believe in the gods.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: We must act quickly. I'll see to it word gets back to Quinquerol. Ah, that reminds me─he asked me to give this to you. The price of your service, he said.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One

text_en: Allag? You're asking me about Allag [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)], of all times?

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: I know only as much as most men, I suppose. It was an ancient civilization that began in the Third Astral and flourished some thousand years─until the Fourth Umbral.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Some say the technology back then was even more advanced than Garlemald's is today, though I don't suppose all the legends passed down are true. Few remains have been found, but there's enough to prove it existed.

quest_names: Two Vans are Better than One
text_en: Allag was an ancient civilization that flourished for some thousand years. It's said their technology was more advanced than Garlemald's is today─but one shouldn't set too much store by legends.

text_en: Quickly, you must tell the High Commander! Oh, and I would advise you not to mention your...[@1A(1)]gifts[@1A(0)] to anyone else─for your own good.
Legend holds that Dalamud is the loyal hound of the goddess Menphina. In art and literature, he is ever depicted protecting his mistress from vile fiends.
One cannot help but wonder, what becomes of the goddess if Her defender should leave Her side?
Well come and well met, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]. The elementals told me that you would come.
I am given to understand you have rendered invaluable service to Gridania as a white mage─a fine path for one beckoned by the elementals. You have my profoundest gratitude.
I am given to understand you have rendered invaluable service to Gridania. It is little wonder the elementals beckoned you to the Twelveswood. You have my profoundest gratitude.
I am given to understand you have rendered invaluable service to Gridania as a white mage. You have my profoundest gratitude.
I am given to understand you have rendered invaluable service to Gridania in the name of the Twin Adder. You have my profoundest gratitude.
As time is of the essence, you will pardon me for forgoing pleasantries. Now, I believe Serpent Lieutenant Fulke has already recited to you this prophecy:
“When white wings hie from distant east, a maid of steel to bear,[@CR]Shall darkling sky shed tears of fire, and veiled ones know despair.”
We are quite certain that the white wings bearing a maid of steel refer to the one men call the White Raven─Nael van Darnus, Legatus of the VIIth Imperial Legion.
Alas, we failed to reach a consensus regarding the nature of the tears of fire, and the identity of the veiled ones is as yet unknown to us.
Be that as it may, this much is plain: Legatus Nael van Darnus comes to the Twelveswood, and chaos and destruction attend him.

Upon hearing the prophecy, I called a council between conjurers and key Twin Adder personnel to deliberate a course of action. There, it was decided that we must needs make another attempt at erecting an Irmin Hedge.
The Irmin Hedge is the most potent magical barrier known to conjury. Even as it rises high to the heavens, it stretches deep into the earth, protecting all within.
Only the most gifted conjurers can erect an Irmin Hedge, and only after having entered a prolonged state of meditation. Needless to say, they are wholly defenseless during the rite.
Should they come to harm while in this state, the bond betwixt their wandering consciousness and the flesh is violently and irrevocably severed, leaving naught but an empty husk behind.
It was not so long ago that we last attempted to erect an Irmin Hedge. Alas, that effort was foiled by the Empire.

Ah, the memories do come back to me. You lent us your aid in our last attempt to erect an Irmin Hedge. Allow me to express my gratitude once more, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)].
You will recall that our previous effort was foiled by the Empire.
With the imperial threat drawing ever nearer, however, failure is no longer an option. I mean to do all in my power to see that, this time, the Hedge rises stout and strong.
In preparation for the rite, I have requested permission of the elementals to conduct a large-scale ranging.

Even as we speak, the Wood Wailers scour the Twelveswood in a bid to rid the area of imperial presence. Your task, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)], will be to aid them.
Report to Swethyna, the Wailer charged with overseeing the mission. She can be found south of Camp Crimson Bark.

Before you take your leave, pray be reminded of one thing: the elementals are as gods to we Gridanians, and the petty quarrels of mortals concern them not. Under no circumstance must they be embroiled in our conflict.
Ah, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]! Thank the elementals for delivering you hither in our time of need!
As you are doubtless aware, the lesser moon Dalamud has strayed from his mistress's side of late. Understandably, the citizens of Gridania are much disquieted by the phenomenon.
While most keep faith with the elementals, fear has driven a wayward few to turn their backs upon the forest and seek what may loosely be termed comfort in the arms of various doomsday cults.

Needless to say, this troubling development did not escape the notice of the Elder Seedseer. Growing ever more concerned for the well-being of her people, she resolved to appeal to the elementals for guidance. They, in turn, whispered to her the following prophecy...
“When white wings hie from distant east, a maid of steel to bear,[@CR]Shall darkling sky shed tears of fire, and veiled ones know despair.”

Cryptic words, to be sure, yet in such troubled times, we can ill afford to let a warning from the elementals pass unheeded. To this end, the Elder Seedseer has instructed me to send her a proven Adder who can be relied upon for a mission of utmost import. I would send no other but you, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)].

Verily, the elementals have guided your steps to us. But let us waste no more time─the Elder Seedseer awaits your coming at Stillglade Fane. Report to her, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)], and do as she bids you.
You would forsake not only duty, but destiny as well? Know that it was not mere chance that brought you hither. Search your heart, and speak with me once you have resolved to do what is right.

Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna is presently at Stillglade Fane, deliberating our nation's future with the conjurers. Report to her, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)], and do as she bids you.
Well met, soldier. I am Grand Serpent Marshal Brookstone. All affairs within the Adders' Nest fall under my charge.
Before you go about your task, I would offer you a word of caution: of those troopers who serve in the VIIth Legion, a great many are sons of Ala Mhigo who have been forced into imperial bondage.
As you well know, the city-state is famed for being home to thewy Highlanders. Should you cross paths with such adversaries in the course of your ranging, you would do well to be wary of their brawn.
Gods, so much armor to make! And [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)] of all times, when our resources are stretched thinnest...

Hm? Oh, you must excuse me. I was merely thinking aloud. You, you look to be a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of the Twin Adder. And a [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)], no less! Well, you couldn't have come along at a better time.
Hm? Oh, you must excuse me. I was merely thinking aloud. You, you look to be a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of the Twin Adder. Well, you couldn't have come along at a better time.
There was a skirmish between our own forces and those of Garlemald near Fallgourd Lake. Victory was ours, but not without a price.

I speak not of the men we lost. Tragic as it may be, they died in service to the realm, and there is great honor in that. No, I speak of the remnants of the fight left on the field of battle. The leather of all that armor, slashed and pierced and torn...and then carelessly tossed aside.
No battle is without such remains. Experience tells me there are more than a few pieces of armor strewn about up there that could be used for scraps, if not salvaged whole.

It would be remiss of us to abandon that which the forest bestowed. Those leathers are gifts from the animals which gave their lives to make them. We must see that they are treated with the proper respect.

You are of the Twin Adder. Surely you feel the same? Should you happen to find yourself near Fallgourd Lake, do have a look around, would you? If you were able to bring me, say, [@IF($E5(3,0),[@IF($E2(3,10),[@SWITCH(3,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(3)])],[@VALUE(3)])] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000401,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000401,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], I'd return the kindness.

Thank you, friend! Just knowing that someone is looking into this will help me to focus on my work here. A word of warning, though─that area is home to dreadwolves, foul beasts with an unslakable thirst for blood.
Should you encounter any, use these hypnotic scales to lull them to sleep. They're not unlimited, mind you, but don't be stingy with them. Just be sure to knock the bloody things out!
...Oh. That is a great shame. <sigh> Had the gods granted me a talent for combat, I'd gladly brave the wilds myself. Alas...

The skirmish took place near Fallgourd Lake in the North Shroud. Search the area and bring me back [@IF($E5(3,0),[@IF($E2(3,10),[@SWITCH(3,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(3)])],[@VALUE(3)])] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000401,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000401,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].

Dreadwolves are known to lurk thereabouts. Should you encounter any, use the [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000402,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000402,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] I gave you to put them to sleep. They're not unlimited, mind you, but don't be stingy with them. Just be sure to knock the bloody things out!
Welcome back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! I am relieved to see you returned safe.
Truth be told, Master Geva scolded me after you departed... It seems that he himself was reprimanded by none other than Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna, Elder Seedseer and head of the Twin Adder.
She thought it was wrong of me to ask you to go to such a dangerous place─and so shortly after a confrontation with the Garleans. I count my blessings that you are safe, truly.
But not all her words were admonishing. Master Geva said Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna praised my efforts, as well!

She explained that when the life of a thing reaches its end, it often returns to us in the form of a gift─be it a hide or lumber. Just so, the items we create from these gifts have lives of their own, and go on to return to the earth.
Yet through all those births and deaths, the essences of things are not changed at all. She said that when we come to know that─[@1A(1)]truly[@1A(0)] know it─then our eyes will be opened.

The leather armor worn by the brave souls who fell at Fallgourd Lake was a case in point, she said. Should it be reclaimed by the forest's soil, it will come to nurture seeds and feed their sprouts, and it will be our duty to protect that new life. Thus, that which once protected us will in turn benefit from our protection.
Her words struck a chord in me, and shamed me at the same time. But then, that is the power of Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna.

I was too intent on my duties to even take notice... I saw the cost of everything, yet the value of nothing. Yet now I see that I am here now because of life's march─its cycle. That I am the same as those scraps of leather, part of a far greater whole.
This terrible danger said to be threatening Eorzea─perhaps it too is but a part of this grand scheme. If so, there is no need to grieve its coming.
I am a leatherworker, and so must do a leatherworker's part to serve the realm in its fight against the Empire, just as you do your part as a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of the Twin Adder.

And so I shall take these precious [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000401,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000401,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you have placed yourself in harm's way to gather, and from them fashion new armor to protect those who fight under our banners! You have my thanks, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Please, accept this as a token of my gratitude.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: You... I know your face. Yes, you are [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)] of the Wailers. The wood's whispers told of a foul beast here, and so I came to put it down. But I see you have already completed the task for me. You have my thanks for that.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: You, there! You are a Serpent of the Twin Adder, are you not? The wood's whispers told of a foul beast here, and so I came to put it down. But I see you have already done it for me. You have my thanks for that.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Ah, so it is another purpose that has brought you. Dhemdaeg? Searching for one of his recruits, you say? A girl named Hilith?

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: I am sorry you came all this way, friend, but Hilith has already returned to the Wailing Barracks. She was with me, yes, practicing her spearwork. But I dared not bring her here. She is not quite ready for such a fight.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Begging your pardon, I know your name but I've yet to give you mine. I am Challinie, conjurer of Stillglade Fane, medium of the Lancers' Guild, and dear friend of Hilith. It was I who put forth her name for recruitment.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: And I would again, despite the worst of Dhemdaeg's protests. I've never known a person of greater convictions or dedication.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: But she also has the pride of youth. She would not let the others see how unwieldy she is with a spear. And yet she has the fears of a recruit, as well, and cannot bring herself to ask Dhemdaeg's leave to train alone.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: She often speaks of the gaze he fixes her with. Cold and steely and filled with loathing, as she tells it, and enough to sap the strength from her knees. All because he sees her as naught but an obstacle to his own petty ambitions. Such a shame.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: It is true her talents do not lie with the spear. But there is more to service than spears. The girl is charismatic and clever. She warms the spirits of those around her, and has a profound love for both nature and nation.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: There is none more fit for service than she. If Dhemdaeg cannot see that, then it is he who is unfit to lead. Who we meet in this life is the work of the gods. But once met, it falls to us to bring out the best in each other.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: I think it high time the truth came out. Here, look at this. It is a drawing of me, done by Hilith herself. Rather good, is it not?

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: She often retreats to the wood and takes to drawing after being chided. I want you to show that drawing to Dhemdaeg, and tell him all I have told you. Perhaps it will help the fool realize that some gifts in this world do not lie at the end of a spear haft.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: I think it high time the truth came out. Here, look at this. It is a drawing of me, done by Hilith herself. Rather good, is it not?

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Ah, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], you're back. It seems Hilith returned not long after you and I departed. Somehow that girl manages to waste my time even when she's not present. I was just on my way to have words with her.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Challinie? Our own Sister Challinie? That is most...unexpected. What did she have to say?

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Drilling on her own? Hilith!? Hahaha, not bloody likely! She's never been anything but slothful in her training.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: She has no mind for fundamentals, and there's been no improvement in her form since she came to us. The girl is all thumbs.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: It is true her devotion to our cause is second to none. But without strength and skill, she is of no use to the Wailers.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: A hard truth, but true nonetheless. If I am to be a commander someday, I must not shy from─

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Hm? What's this? A drawing? Remarkable! The resemblance to Challinie is extraordinary. This is the work of a master, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and I thank you for showing it to me, but I've more pressing matters to─

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Hilith? [@1A(1)]Hilith[@1A(0)] drew this!? Gods be good! The girl [@1A(1)]does[@1A(0)] have talent! But why did she not tell me?

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: As it happens, the Twin Adder has issued a call for gifted artists. They mean to commit the likenesses of suspicious individuals seen in the wood to paper, that they might be recognized by any and all.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: If we replace Hilith's spear with a brush, both she and the Order will be a deal happier. The bloody fool, why did she not tell me of this? Why did she not─ No... No, she was not in the wrong. I was only too blind to see it.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: I owe you a debt, friend. So loath was I to fail in front of my superiors that I neglected to see Hilith for who she is, and what she has to offer. Had I had my way, her talents would have been forever lost to our cause. Gods, and I fancied myself a leader...

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: I was the one in need of guidance, not Hilith. You've helped me to learn a lesson I'll not soon forget, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Here, the payment promised.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Well, if it isn't [@STRING($EB(1))]! I hear you've been made a Serpent of the Twin Adder─though why such a fine force would welcome the likes of you is beyond me. Hah hah!

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: It's always an honor to meet a Serpent of the Twin Adder. You're in exalted company, there. The Order's home to many of the realm's finest.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: We Wood Wailers have been called upon to serve as well, as has the Gods' Quiver under Bowlord Lewin. Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna herself has put to us the task of training recruits. Theirs is the only green this wood has no use for.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Most have never wielded a spear nor donned a jerkin. A far cry from you adventurers, but they mean well enough.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: Even so, there is one among them, Hilith, who is proving most...troublesome. Her passion for the cause is unquestionable, to be sure. Greater than most, in fact. Yet...

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: The woman is hopeless with a spear, and makes no effort to improve. She has little love for drilling, and less for rules. Hells, even now she is off to gods know where without my leave.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: I've put in for her discharge on more than one occasion, but my commander won't hear of it. He says the fault lies in my leadership.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: I mean to make commander myself someday, and I'm not about to let an upstart recruit put an end to my hopes. I must find the [@IF($E9(4),girl,wench)] and make a true Wailer of her!

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: But I can only cover so much ground on my own... Would you help me? If you could search for her near the Rootslake in the South Shroud while I scour Quarrymill Landing, I would consider it a great service.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: You have my thanks now, and payment later, should you see the deed done. Once Hilith is put in her place, she'll be the better for it.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: You have better things to do, is that it? Then bloody be off and about them!

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: How can I train those who would protect the realm, if I cannot even train a green girl? ...Bah! I shall not give in to doubt. Hilith is an unruly mare to be broken and tamed. But first, she must be found.

quest_names: The Pen Is Mightier Than the Spear
text_en: I will look for her at Quarrymill Landing. Please, search near the Rootslake in the South Shroud. If you find her, put the fear of the gods in her, will you?
I fertilized the herbs with a special concoction in hopes of doubling yield, and indeed it had the desired effect. Alas, the monsters came and ate every last─
...Dear gods, what have I done? The concoction is the source of all my woes!

In my desire to maintain my standing at the guild, I commissioned the alchemists of Ul'dah to create an especially potent fertilizer. Knowing that many forestborn abhor the Ul'dahns' materialistic ways, I hid my dealings from my peers.
But now I am reaping that which I sowed: my beloved mentor may well lose his life, and the balance of the Twelveswood is in peril. I am unworthy of the name of botanist.
What do you mean, “Remember the words and actions of Aldous, kupo”?
How could I possibly forget? Why, my every endeavor in botany is based upon his teachings. Take, for instance, his efforts to preserve balance in the Twelveswood.
He would take great pains to harvest such flora as had grown unruly, that the forest might have a chance to─

...By the Twelve, how could I have been so blind? The answer lay before my eyes from the first, just as Master Aldous taught me, but in my desire to increase yield, I lost sight of the most basic principle in botany.
Why, I daresay I never needed the fertilizer in the first place!
If I thin out the weeds that have sprung up, the herbs will have a chance to recover. But...but by then it will be too late to save Master. Oh, whatever am I to do?
What!? A still more potent medicine may be made by blending the odious weed with the roots of the herb!? Where in the world did you come by this knowledge!?
From the moogle, you say? He bade you reveal the information to me only on the condition that I first deduced for myself how best to restore the balance?
So...you can converse with the creatures? Amazing! That certainly explains why the little fellow seemed so worked up before!

I owe you a debt of gratitude, friend. Without your kind aid, I might have remained forever blind to the true needs of the Twelveswood. From this day forth, I vow never again to rely upon profane practices in my work.

By the gods, that the monsters could have multiplied to such numbers in so short a time... And if that weren't bad enough, the infernal things have eaten up all of the herbs that I need! Why, the place has grown thick with odious weeds!
Remember: relay the information to Enie when─and only when─she realizes the significance of the weeds, kupo. Being Aldous's pupil, I have no doubt she'll make the connection before long.
Faugh, kupo! Look what you've done! The monsters are threatening to topple the delicate balance of the forest, kupo!
What are [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] doing here, kupo!? Ah, but never mind that! I have a mind to take your botanist friend to task, and you can deliver my message!
You understand my words!? Perfect, kupo! I have a mind to take your botanist friend to task, and you can deliver my message!

Tell the lass she mustn't sprinkle her strange stuff here! The herbs grew the faster for it, true, but they only served to attract hordes of hungry beasties! The land will be left a barren waste in their wake, kupo!
Hm? Did you say your friend's name is Enie? I thought she looked familiar! Would she perchance be the Enie whom Aldous once mentored, kupo?

She is!? Well then, there is no great cause for worry, kupo! Aldous has always done well by the forest, and I have no doubt that his pupil may yet do the same─if given proper guidance. Now, heed me well, kupo, for I shall furnish you with instructions.
When Enie realizes... <mumble> ...reveal to her this knowledge... <mumble> ...kupo...
Uwaaah! I would thank you not to startle me while I am deep in thought!

Oh, it's only you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Word has reached me of your enlistment with the Order of the Twin Adder. It does the spirit well to see one of ours do [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] part for the greater good. But tell me, have you had occasion to meet a Hyur by the name of Aldous?
...Hm? You are of the Twin Adder, are you not? Tell me, have you had occasion to meet a Hyur by the name of Aldous?

The man is a botanist of great renown, and it was my honor to learn the craft under his tutelage. At the Elder Seedseer's behest, however, he was later put in command of the Blue Badgers and compelled to relinquish his post at the guild.

Oh, in case they are unfamiliar to you, the Blue Badgers are a unit of engineers─Disciples of the Hand and the Land for the most part. They spend half their time building bridges and encampments to aid our forces, and the other half laying traps and erecting barricades to hinder the enemy.

Now, there is a well-known dictum here in Gridania that was first uttered by Master Aldous. It states: “When met with an obstacle in life, step back a pace that you might behold it in full. In seeing the whole, you will surely see the path that leads around it.”

These words of wisdom he shared with me during a particularly trying year at the guild, when I was struggling to meet the quota. He taught me that the answer is ever before our eyes─we need only find the viewpoint from which to see it.

By virtue of this advice, I was able to locate a thriving field of wild herbs, a discovery which allowed me to become the leading harvester in the guild. It would be no exaggeration to say that everything I have, I owe to Master Aldous's sage guidance.

...I tell you all of this because he lies even now on the brink of death. He was set upon by monsters during an expedition for the Blue Badgers, and grievously wounded. The healers at the infirmary say the outlook is grim, but I believe that Master might yet be saved if he were to be treated with a certain medicinal herb.

Alas, there has been a marked increase in the number of monsters inhabiting the only place the plant is known to grow─a tract of land south and east of Humblehearth─and I have been unable to pass near enough to harvest what I need. In a bitter irony, it was these selfsame creatures that harmed Master Aldous.

Had I an aptitude for swords and spells, I might be able to avenge the harm done to my mentor and save his life besides. But the gods did not see fit to bless me with such, and I must rely upon others to handle more [@1A(1)]onerous[@1A(0)] undertakings. And so I turn to you, friend. I would be eternally grateful if you could vanquish the monsters that hamper my efforts to procure the herb.

I'm forever in your debt. Now, as Master's life hangs in the balance, let us see to the task without delay. I also have a mind to uncover what it was precisely that gave rise to the monster infestation.
If none are fain to aid me, I have no choice but to face the vicious fiends myself. With or without help, I must save Master Aldous.
I would gladly give up my standing in the guild if it meant Master Aldous would be saved. Please assist me by vanquishing the monsters that infest the area south and east of Humblehearth.

All the better. I've a task for you.

Tell me, do you know of the dirigibles of the Ixal? They employ two kinds─armored balloons that carry their soldiers and beasts of war, and fleet cargo balloons used to transport felled trees back to their strongholds.

The Ixal lost their wings for their sins, but learned to fly once more. And since regaining the power to escape to the skies, they have proven an even more elusive enemy. Many times now has the Gods' Quiver been thwarted by these damnable contraptions.

Still, they are beastman-made, and therefore far from perfect. We have learned they are made to fly on the steady winds summoned by the airstones of the birdmen shamans. On days when the gods send gusts and gales, their ships are nigh on uncontrollable.

With this in mind, we had the conjurers of Stillglade Fane commune with the elementals of the air. By reading the winds, we thought to predict when and where the Ixal would strike. And predict we did, with near unerring accuracy. However...
Some days ago, a number of trees were felled in the Twelveswood. And this on a day when the winds were blustering.
There is no denying it was the work of the Ixal─their markings and leavings were strewn about the scene. But we are at a loss to explain how they were able to navigate amid such strong winds.
I'd like for you to travel to Camp Dragonhead in the central Coerthas Highlands, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Ask the forces stationed there if they know aught of what took place that day.
The Ixali stronghold of Natalan falls within the area of their vigil. Were anything suspicious afoot, they are like to have noticed it.
I am grateful, truly. But I must warn you─foul things prowl the lands around Camp Dragonhead, and I do not speak of the Ixal alone. Be wary.
Adventurers such as yourself often place their own needs before those of the realm. Unfortunate, yet only to be expected, I suppose.
To have flown a war balloon to and from the Twelveswood in such strong winds, and with allowance enough to load the trees they felled... No. The Ixal must have some new means at their disposal.
It is my hope that the forces stationed at Camp Dragonhead will be able to shed some light on this. The nearby Ixali stronghold of Natalan falls within the purview of their watch.
Visit there, in the central Coerthas Highlands, and ask if they have observed any suspicious goings-on of late.
Anythin' odd about the Ixal on the day the winds last blew strong? Aye, might be there was. Who wants to know? Hm? Alaire o' the Gods' Quiver, is it?
Ixali war balloon...?

So [@1A(1)]that's[@1A(0)] what it was! Aye, I've seen yer balloon. Made it for a cloud, I did, dark as it was. Not that I'd ever seen a cloud like it... Damn near perfect circle with a wee square on its underside. Came driftin' this way from the forest, it did.

But wait a godsdamned minute! Every bugger knows the birdmen can't fly their balloons in gales that strong. Might be they could just about fly [@1A(1)]with[@1A(0)] the wind, but these birds were flyin' [@1A(1)]against[@1A(0)] it.
It'd take nothin' less than a bloody [@1A(1)]magitek engine[@1A(0)] to─ Nooo...can't be. The Garleans would never cast their lot with any o' the beast tribes. [@1A(1)]Never[@1A(0)]. ...Would they?
With the freedom of the skies, there'd be no stoppin' them bastard birds from attackin' wherever they bloody well fancied! Hells, they could be flyin' over Gridania right now for all we know!

Well, look at that... This is... Huh.
Looks to be some sort of leather panel. This must be what they stitch together to form the envelope. I s'pose this is common enough on balloons o' that sort.

See that shine? Brighter than any Ixali airstone, that. Mayhap this is what them birds've been usin'. Aye, I'd wager there's power enough in this stone to push one o' their balloons upwind.
But what I'm more interested in is the blessin'. If Garuda has power to spare turnin' airstones to eyes...

Now, according to the thaumaturges, Ifrit has been gaining strength of late. They've theorized that the changes occurring to Dalamud in recent moons are symptoms of the primal's burgeoning might.

Now, you'll be heartened to know that we've obtained intelligence that should facilitate your mission. Our agents have learned that Gridania was recently visited by a most distinguished personage, an elderly Elezen man hailing from Sharlayan.

This fellow─Louisoix is his name─claims to hold the secret to defeating primals. Moreover, he means to strike at Ifrit, and is seeking capable and willing adventurers to assist him. In short, the circumstances could not be more favorable to our cause.
You are to make contact with Louisoix and befriend him. As I mentioned earlier, he is currently sojourning in Gridania, and is regularly seen near Apkallus Falls.

Learn all you can of how to defeat Ifrit, and use the knowledge you acquire to see the deed done. If all goes well, Dalamud will then revert to its former state, and our mission will be a glorious success.

Now, 'tis not without good reason that primals are worshipped as gods in some circles. Why the additional condition, you ask? To that question I respond with another: would you have Ul'dah share her glory with rivals? I thought not.

That concludes the briefing. Now, this is purely routine, but regulations require you to indicate that you consent to undertake the mission. Only then can I consider the task officially assigned. So, go on─let me hear the words.

Only parties consisting of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE(25)] or above will be permitted to battle the primal Ifrit.

Further, barring exceptional circumstances, we ask that you seek the aid of none but those sworn to the Order of the Twin Adder. If the secret to vanquishing primals is known only to our organization, the other nation-states will be all the more likely to enlist our aid, bringing Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna's dream of a three[@1F]nation alliance that much closer to being.
Now, we are not unmindful that such constraints render an already onerous mission that much more difficult. As such, we are prepared to offer you an incentive by way of further rewards.

Only parties consisting of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE(25)] or above will be permitted to battle the primal Ifrit.

Your mission is a crucial first step towards realizing the Elder Seedseer's dream of a three[@1F]nation alliance. My thanks, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)], and may the Twelve speed your way.

I understand full well your apprehension. It is no small thing to vie with a god. But our number counts none more suited to the task. For the sake of our forest nation and all who call it home, I beg you reconsider.

Ah, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)], impeccable timing as ever. The Maelstrom has need of a dependable operative for a covert mission, and your name was foremost in my mind.

We've received reports that an individual claiming knowledge of how to defeat primals has appeared in Gridania, a man said to be the leader of a fraternity called the Circle of Knowing. As if to confirm our intelligence, the Gridanians have since extended to us an offer of alliance, proposing that we act in concert to eliminate Ifrit, under the direction of the aforementioned third party.

Hah! Those wooden-headed tree fondlers will have to do better than [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] if they hope to play the thalassocracy! All know it was our own Company of Heroes that slew Leviathan, and it's plain the Gridanians seek to supplement their feeble ranks with allies who might feasibly contend with a primal.
Needless to say, we stand to gain little and less by joining hands with such cravens. Yet it cannot be denied that the secrets held by this man─this Louisoix─may prove useful to us.

Assuming he isn't a Gridanian fabrication, of course─bait to lure our trust and thence our resources. I mean, if this Louisoix truly [@1A(1)]were[@1A(0)] the leader of those who advocated the reformation of the Maelstrom, would he not make Limsa Lominsa his first port of call?

And here, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)], is where your services are required. We need you to verify the identity of Louisoix and ascertain if he does indeed know of a means to defeat Ifrit. Should all appear to be in order, you are to [@1A(1)]invite[@1A(0)] him to Limsa Lominsa.
Louisoix has taken up residence in Gridania, and is said to frequent Apkallus Falls. Take yourself there, and be on the lookout for an elderly Elezen man.

In order to discern whether Louisoix is who he claims to be, you will need to encourage the man to talk. And to encourage him to talk, you must gain his trust. Do whatever is necessary to earn his confidence, even if it means offering to fight Ifrit himself.

Should it come to that, you will want to assemble a party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] before facing the primal. Battling the Lord of the Inferno with fewer would be tantamount to suicide.

One last thing. The secrecy of this mission is a matter of national security. As such, if you are able to accomplish this task aided only by sworn members of the Maelstrom─and no outsiders─I shall see to it that you are rewarded more generously.

Only parties consisting of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE(25)] or above will be permitted to battle the primal Ifrit.

Not even the prospect of facing a primal makes you flinch. I'm glad to count you among our ranks, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)]. Now, without further ado, go forth and make the Maelstrom proud!

This mission is of the utmost gravity to the Maelstrom, and I'm loath to entrust it to any other. I would ask you to reconsider, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)].
The man we seek, Louisoix, is said to frequent Apkallus Falls in Gridania. I'm told the place is situated along the path to the Lily Hills, the forest city's most affluent district.

Travel to Gridania and seek out the man they call Louisoix. Upon making contact, ascertain if he is who he claims to be, and whether he possesses credible information on Ifrit. Should all appear to be in order, you are to [@1A(1)]invite[@1A(0)] him to Limsa Lominsa.

Your task, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)], is to assist Louisoix directly. Our guest is an elderly Elezen gentleman. Meet with him at Apkallus Falls, and attend well his every word, that you might arm yourself with the knowledge to overcome Ifrit.
For your mission, you are to make contact with Louisoix and befriend him. He is currently sojourning in Gridania, and is regularly seen near Apkallus Falls.

Learn all you can of how to defeat Ifrit, and use the knowledge you acquire to see the deed done. If all goes well, Dalamud will then revert to its former state, and our mission will be a glorious success. I have every faith that you will not fail us.
[@STRING($EB(1))], I presume. Right glad am I to behold at last the valiant adventurer of whom [@SWITCH($E8(1),Y'shtola,Papalymo,Thancred)] has spoken so oft.
Pray allow me to introduce myself. My name is Louisoix Leveilleur, and it is my honor to preside over the Circle of Knowing.

You are yet unfamiliar with our collective, I think. If it please you, the fellowship was formed in Sharlayan, great seat of learning. Ever since our founding, we have endeavored to archive all extant knowledge, that man might learn of his origin and destiny both.

'Tis our firmly held belief that knowledge is power─specifically, the power to realize a better future. To this end, my fellows and I─your friend [@SWITCH($E8(1),Y'shtola,Papalymo,Thancred)] included─have come to Eorzea that we might enlighten her peoples as to what lies ahead.

Mayhap you have also crossed paths with Urianger, yet another of our circle. In which case, I must crave your pardon if his mannerism strikes you as outlandish. 'Tis not his intent to confound folk with cryptic words. You see, the man has seen much more of tomes than he has of the world. I assure you, though, that his heart is in the right place. Ah, but permit me to return to the subject matter at hand.

Just now I made mention of Eorzea's future. But first I must speak of the past, for that which is to come was ever the product of that which has been.[@CR]Ten years ago, an event took place which shook the very foundation of Eorzea: a tribe of beasts summoned forth a primal. So began the spread of summoning till there was not a tribe in this world to whom the practice remained unknown.

Alas, they paid no heed to the consequences of its use. You see, in order to remain in our plane of existence, a primal must needs devour prodigious amounts of aether─the energy bound in crystals and at large throughout all creation.

Consequently, the land is slowly but surely being drained of its aether, and the day fast approaches when the fount will run dry. Should that happen, what then? Why, all life in Eorzea will end. Even as we speak, the land bleeds, with every passing moment another ilm closer to death. And die it surely will─unless we purge it of its blight. Aye, I speak of the primals.
It is to bring about their downfall that I have journeyed to Eorzea. Ifrit, fell primal of the Amalj'aa, shall be the first. I should welcome your help in this.

Forgive me if I seem brusque or presumptuous, but time is not on our side. I require that you procure an echo crystal for each of the six cardinal elements. These crystals have unique reverberative properties, and are yielded only by creatures possessed of an indomitable spirit in life.

Take from me this receptacle, into which the crystals must be placed. Once all six are present, each will begin to resonate with the others, giving birth at last to a new power whose application I shall explain when the time is right.
Now, I have taken the liberty of identifying your quarries. All are creatures of preternatural ferocity, and none will be bested lightly.
The first you will find northwest of Camp Bloodshore in eastern La Noscea. A roseling known by the name of Barometz, it is aligned with the element of wind.

The second beast also makes its home near Camp Bloodshore, but to the southeast. The people there call it Slippery Sykes, an endearing name for a voracious man-eating slug, I'm sure you'll agree. Its affinity is with water.
Third, we have the nest commander, an especially savage antling that prowls the area northwest of Camp Horizon in western Thanalan. Its element is earth.
Your next quarry is also seen near Camp Horizon, but to the west. A puk called Pyrausta, it is a creature of lightning.
Fifth, we have Queen Bolete, a monarch among funguars, whose element is ice. She holds court southwest of Camp Tranquil in the Twelveswood.
The last is the jackanapes, a fire-aligned primate who prowls the patch of forest southeast of Camp Tranquil.

These are the six creatures you must seek out and put down. It matters not the order in which you hunt them, but I urge you to spare no preparation, lest the hunter become the hunted. To make absolutely certain that naught is left to chance, you might consider forming a party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])].

I require that you procure an echo crystal for each of the six cardinal elements. They are yielded only by creatures possessed of an indomitable spirit in life. I have taken the liberty of identifying six such beasts.

In eastern La Noscea you will find Barometz, a creature of wind that inhabits the area northwest of Camp Bloodshore. Southeast of the selfsame camp is Slippery Sykes, a slug whose elemental alignment is water.

Two more await in Thanalan─one to the northwest of Camp Horizon, and the other to the west. The former is the nest commander, an antling whose element is earth, while the latter is Pyrausta, a puk aligned with lightning.

The last two beasts inhabit areas of the Twelveswood in the vicinity of Camp Tranquil. The first is Queen Bolete, a creature of ice known to hold court northwest of the camp. The second, named the jackanapes, is a fire-aligned primate often seen prowling the forest to the southeast.

All are creatures of preternatural ferocity, and none will be bested lightly. To make absolutely certain that naught is left to chance, you should consider forming a party of [@VALUE(4)] before attempting the deed. Gods willing, I shall see you here again before long─with a receptacle containing six resonating echo crystals, and nary a scratch besides!
It gladdens me to see you returned, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and bearing the echo crystals, no less. 'Tis plain that their power has opened your eyes to the aetherial gate beside me.
You may labor to believe it, but this aetherial gate has always been present─aye, even when you first paid me visit. It was merely veiled from your sight.
There exist objects in the world, you see, that lie beyond the plane of mortal perception. Only by overleaping the boundaries of our senses can such objects be made manifest.

This metaphysical leap may be made via a variety of means, the echo crystals you hold being central to one of them. Indeed, it is they that are responsible for the apparent “appearance” of this particular aetherial gate.
As you are able to see it, so too are you able to traverse it. Ah, but we're not quite ready to step through just yet.[@CR]Would be so kind as to lend me your six echo crystals?

From these, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I shall create for you [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000420,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000420,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. Think of it as a key of sorts for entering the aetherial gate.

With this on your person, you will be able to enter Ifrit's sanctuary, the Bowl of Embers. Ah, but if you expect to find the primal already there and lounging about, I fear you will be met with disappointment.

You must needs first summon forth Ifrit, an act which requires [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000419,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000419,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. It serves to kindle a magical flame, you see, which acts as a beacon toward which the Lord of the Inferno may bend his course.

If there is one among them who holds [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000419,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000419,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], it can be none other than he. You have the means to traverse the aetherial gate. However, you still lack the relic required to summon Ifrit.

Namely, [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000419,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000419,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. This artifact kindles an enchanted flame which serves as a signal for the Lord of the Inferno to descend.

I see you've managed to blunder your way to filling that receptacle. Well, I hate to break this to you, but you've been wasting your time. Me and my comrades here will be the ones who do for Ifrit. Ain't that right, lads?
Fancy seein' the Lord o' the Inferno brought down, [@IF($E9(4),girl,boy)]? Then best leave the fightin' to the experts. Why don't ye fly like a faerie 'fore ye take a tumble an' skin yer knee?

It takes wisdom to recognize when something is beyond one's capacity, and bravery to default on an obligation one cannot fulfill. For your own good, friend, I counsel you to walk away and forget any foolish notion of defeating Ifrit.

The mere thought of facing Ifrit sets my blood to boiling! Gods, it's been a long time since I've had free rein to use my thaumaturgy. Looking at you, though, I'll bet you've never let yourself go in battle, or that anyone would notice if you did! Hah hah!

Your jubilant countenance can only mean one thing: you have returned with [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000419,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000419,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. My congratulations, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

Now naught stands between you and a reckoning with Ifrit. Before you rush headlong into the fiery jaws of danger, however, I would give you some words of counsel, that you might be better prepared for the coming struggle.

Your adversary is a god at best, and a demon at worst. You will want to assemble a band of your most stalwart companions for this encounter, lest you imperil both yourself and Eorzea's precious hopes of survival.

Only parties consisting of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE(25)] or above will be permitted to battle the primal Ifrit.
