Be warned also that primals radiate a malign energy which has a corrupting influence upon mortal minds. For your own safety, I shall employ my magicks to extricate you and yours should I deem the struggle has persisted overlong.
Nor shall I permit you to confront Ifrit again until such time as your body has purged itself of the primal's taint. You must be fully rested and clear of mind to attempt this feat.

The allotted time for the battle with Ifrit is [@VALUE($E8(2))] minutes (Earth time). A waiting time also applies between challenges, and you will not be permitted to return to the Bowl of Embers immediately.
To confirm how long you must wait before reentering, view the Timers tab located under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)].
Commit my counsel to memory, for you will needs abide by it if you are to have the faintest hope of prevailing.[@CR]Make now any preparations you deem needful, then speak with me once more.
Very well. If you find your resolve yet wanting, I shan't begrudge you the time to steel yourself for the coming firestorm.

I see you have chosen to ignore my counsel... Ahem. Allow me to be plain. I will brook no argument in this matter. Make ready as per my original instructions, and this time see that you do so to the letter. Only then shall I give you leave to proceed.

Is...is it true what you say? That the aether spilled forth from the land, and the aetherial gate was severed entirely? Twelve be good...[@CR]I would know all that transpired, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Pray spare no detail.

So Nael van Darnus himself appeared...? That he would so callously sever the flow of aether─no man of sound mind would contemplate such wickedness! More troubling still is the fact that he had the means to do it at all. It would seem the Empire has acquired a terrible new weapon.
Yet we have a more pressing issue to consider: the land has been divested of its aether. If Ifrit was somehow able to absorb that energy, he will grow powerful beyond reckoning.
What? You claim acquaintance with an individual who is familiar with the workings of the crystals?[@CR]Cid Garlond... Yes, I have come across that name on my travels.
And he is in Limsa Lominsa, you say? I should very much like to meet the man. It would seem an outing to Vylbrand is in order, would it not?
We failed to put an end to Ifrit, to destroy the primal's body and soul both that he might never rise again.
But we have not the luxury of conceding defeat. The fate of the world is at stake, and we must fight on until such time as the crystals nourish the land once more.
Ifrit grows ever more powerful, and the scales have tipped far against us. It will take nothing short of a miracle to vanquish him...yet we must try.
I shall return to the tomes, there to search for knowledge that may avail us. In the meantime, I ask that you, too, devote yourself to seeking a means to best this foe.

I shall devote myself to seeking alternate means to contend with Ifrit. In the meantime, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I ask that you hold fast to your resolve. When the hour is ripe, your feet shall surely carry you hither again.
I shall return to the tomes, there to search for knowledge that may avail us. In the meantime, I ask that you, too, devote yourself to seeking a means to best this foe.

Congratulations, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]! That was a fine show you put on against Ifrit. Never for a moment did I doubt that you would succeed.
You are to be commended also for relying only upon your comrades within the Order of the Twin Adder. Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna will be most pleased.
As promised, you will be furnished with an additional sum on top of the standard reward. Once again, well done.

It is unfortunate that circumstance forced you to turn to those not of our number for aid. Yet it could be argued that a hotchpotch band of strangers uniting to overcome insurmountable odds is a manifestation of the ideal world Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna has envisaged.
In no small part due to your exploits, we have taken the first step towards establishing an alliance with Ul'dah. I knew I was not mistaken in assigning this task to you.
Hmm? Are you feeling unwell? You have the look of one who bears a heavy burden. Come, tell me what troubles you.
Legatus Nael van Darnus of the VIIth Imperial Legion!? That the White Raven himself would set foot in Ifrit's lair...
And he gave you reason to believe that Dalamud's blood-red hue is the [@1A(1)]Empire's[@1A(0)] doing?
But...how is that even possible? We're speaking of Dalamud, the lesser moon that has existed on high since time immemorial!

Then again, perhaps it is not so unlikely... The Garleans have long possessed the power to make gigantic masses of iron soar the skies. If any on Hydaelyn are capable of calling Dalamud to heel, it is they.

This recalls to my mind a disquieting report I heard of the Seedseer Council held the evening past by moonlight. The elementals were said to have been in a state of heightened agitation. Some were frightened, others enraged.
At the time, none could shed any light on what may have upset the elementals so. Now I wonder if it wasn't something the Empire did to Dalamud.
But I will not indulge in idle speculation─the Elder Seedseer must be informed of this development posthaste. We can only pray that the time for action is not yet past.

My thanks once more for your outstanding service, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)]. In delivering to us this crucial piece of intelligence, you have gone above and beyond the call of duty. I hope we can count on your loyal support for a long time to come.

Ah, the mighty extinguisher of Ifrit makes [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] triumphant return! There's nary a soul in the Maelstrom who hasn't heard of your victory over the primal. Let me be the first to congratulate you.

You have done a great service for the Maelstrom, and kept our secrets safe from outsiders besides. You've upheld your side of the bargain, and will receive your due reward. Once again, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)], well done. I pray that you'll keep fighting for our cause, and for the continued prosperity of our fair nation.

You are a shining example to all in the Maelstrom, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)]. I pray that you'll keep fighting for our cause, and for the continued prosperity of our fair nation.
Now then, report to me all you have learned. Tell me of this man Louisoix and the knowledge he claims.
A way to prevent the rebirth of primals, you say!?

A pity van Darnus's uninvited appearance rendered all of your efforts void. Still, your account of events suggests to me that Louisoix is indeed the genuine article. In which case...you were supposed to have brought him here.
I thought I had made it abundantly clear what was meant by [@1A(1)]invite[@1A(0)]. <sigh> There's no help for it now.
What's that? Louisoix expressed his intention to visit Limsa Lominsa of his own accord? So the man has taken an interest in Master Garlond's research...

Then this is how we will proceed: you are to maintain contact with Louisoix, keeping the man amenable with the promise of a meeting with Cid Garlond. Besides his conversance with primals, mayhap Louisoix has information that will avail us against the Empire. Speaking of which, what can you tell me of van Darnus?
Great Admiral's ghost! The changes exhibited by Dalamud are the Empire's doing!?
But how is it possible that an object so enormous and distant─that has existed since the dawn of time─can be at mankind's beck and call?

By the Twelve...I find I am inclined to believe it. Gods only know what else the vile Garleans are capable of. I must take word of this to the Chief Admiral without delay. We will need to dispatch reconnaissance squads, the better to devise an effective response.

Owing to your efforts, the Maelstrom has an opportunity to move preemptively. My personal thanks, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]!

'Tis good to see you returned, and none the more scorched for your fiery encounter with Ifrit! Word of your triumph over the Lord of the Inferno long since reached Ul'dah, and the entire sultanate is abuzz with recountings of your exploits.

I'm pleased also to see you were able to fulfill the objective without involving outsiders. You have more than earned your reward, [@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)].

Now, you've done everything that was asked of you...but I'm sorry to say that vanquishing Ifrit did not, in actual fact, affect Dalamud in any discernable way...at all. Ahem. Do you, by any chance, recall anything else of note? Anything at all?

'Tis good to see you returned, and none the more scorched for your fiery encounter with Ifrit! Word of your triumph over the Lord of the Inferno long since reached Ul'dah, and the entire sultanate is abuzz with recountings of your exploits.

Now, you've done everything that was asked of you...but I'm sorry to say that vanquishing Ifrit did not, in actual fact, affect Dalamud in any discernable way...at all. Ahem. Do you, by any chance, recall anything else of note? Anything at all?
Imperial troopers appeared, including one clad in imposing white armor!?
By the Twelve, that could only have been Nael van Darnus─the one they call the White Raven! But...what business could the Legatus of the VIIth Imperial Legion have had within the lizardmen's lair?
And the words he spoke, of the crimson star and the purging of the land...
Could van Darnus have been speaking of Dalamud? In which case, mayhap the lesser moon's transformation is the Empire's handiwork, and naught to do with Ifrit...

I fear it is beyond me alone to pass judgment on this. I must send word to the Garlond Ironworks without delay. I've been given to understand that they've recently made a discovery regarding Dalamud, and I daresay they'll be glad of the information.

...Which leaves us with the thaumaturges. If it comes to light that the Empire is indeed behind Dalamud's changes, you can bet your life the touchy lot over at Arrzaneth Ossuary won't stay quiet. They'll see it as a slight upon their honor that their theory was refuted.

You don't strike me as being given to slips of the tongue, [@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)], but I shall remind you to keep your knowledge of this matter in strictest confidence. This is no less for your sake than ours.
The Immortal Flames will have need of your services again before long. See to it that you're not far away when that day comes. Till next time, may the Twelve keep you.
The Meteor project was a platform for the development of new armaments for use in the Empire's subjugation of rival nations─until the accident at Bozja Citadel ten summers past, that is.
It was on that ill-fated day that we learned which lines the Emperor was willing to cross in order to slake his thirst for power...
That was also the day Master Garlond and the rest of us made our decision to flee Garlemald. As to what progress has been made on the project since then, your guess is as good as any.
It is [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] who have doomed Eorzea? [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)]!? The gall of that man to even suggest that a decade of suffering is somehow [@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] fault!

It is not [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] who kidnaps children and poisons their minds, turning them against their mothers. It is not [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] who razes entire cities upon the whim of a madman whose addiction to power requires a daily sacrifice in blood.
It is not [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] wh─uh, oh. [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I-I'm... You should not have had to witness that. My behavior was...unbefitting.

Allow me to apologize and thank you once again for coming. Preventing the Empire from advancing on our position allowed us sufficient time to restore our airship to something approaching working order.

I suppose you will be heading back to Camp Iron Lake to report the day's happenings to your commanding officer. Well, to show my gratitude for your bravery, let me give you a piece of information that the Chief Admiral is certain to appreciate.

The Empire's Meteor project is far more than it seems. While the initiative itself is fairly new, its origins lie in ancient magicks that legends tell us were used to tear stars from the heavens and send them crashing down upon the land.

However, the Empire's interest centers not only on the arcane, but on a colossal machine created thousands of years ago by a people known as the Allagans. What is this colossal machine, you ask? Why, look up and you can see it for yourself.
Dalamud─the perfect weapon with which to destroy the beast tribes. A pity that it will destroy all the rest of us, as well.
After the incident at Bozja Citadel, I believed that the Empire had come to realize their folly, and abandoned their studies regarding Meteor.
But here they are, scouring every ilm of Vylbrand for the solitary needle, buried somewhere in this vast haystack of a realm, that will bring them closer to achieving their ends.
And House Darnus's role in all of this only serves to deepen my dread. The Empire are getting close.

Make haste back to Iron Lake and inform your High Commander of what I have told you here today. If the Garleans are truly on the verge of completing the Meteor project, then we may not have much time...

What has the White Raven learned? What does he know now that he did not ten summers past? I must ponder this riddle a while longer. In the meantime, you should hurry back to Camp Iron Lake and report to your supervising officer. Godsspeed, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Time is of the essence, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]. Report.
I see... The Chief Admiral must be informed of these developments directly.
Accept that as payment for your work here today. I shall mention your performance in my report to Maelstrom Command. Dismissed!
Many thanks, soldier of the storm.
Your assistance in clearing the area of imperial operatives has saved me and my colleagues a good deal of unwanted trouble, and will allow us to promptly return to our search for Allagan tomestones.
While much has been uncovered about the lost civilization, a great deal remains veiled in the mists of time.

What we do know is that the Allagan civilization was established sometime soon after the dawn of the Third Astral Era, more than fifty centuries past. It thrived in Eorzea for more than a thousand years, its boundaries extending as far as the great continent to the north and east.

The Allagans were remarkably skilled in the manufacture and manipulation of complex machina similar to what is seen in Garlemald today, though it is believed that their knowledge was at a level far in advance of the Garleans.
Though it may sound ludicrous, we believe that a recently discovered device of theirs may have been used to communicate with...and possibly even [@1A(1)]control[@1A(0)] the lesser moon Dalamud.

Yes, I understand this is all difficult to digest, but you must bear with me. That which you and countless other Eorzeans believe to be a star, a god, a divine watch hound, is actually something more...substantial, and the Allagans, in their hubris, found a way to bend it to their own will.

Yet in the end, it was this very power that hastened their civilization to its Doom. You see, for all their knowledge and all their marvelous achievements, their meddling served not to halt the eternal cycle of destruction, but to speed its progress.

And now Garlemald walks the same path. The fact that they still seek tomestones like the one Master Garlond threw to the legatus serves as confirmation that they have not abandoned the Meteor project, or their hopes of controlling Dalamud.
That the Black Wolf is involved... Well, there can be but one explanation─the White Raven now pulls the strings.
That the Black Wolf is involved... Well, there can be but one explanation─the White Raven now pulls the strings.
Consider yourself fortunate. There are few officers who command the respect of their men as does R'ashaht Rhiki.
A veteran of battles on both land and sea, the high commander has earned the name Redwind, for when she walks the fields of valor, the air waxes ruddy with the blood of her enemies.
Yet never once has she allowed the foul stain of pride to color her judgment. Even now, she remains humble in her appraisal of her talents─always striving to work on what few weaknesses she has.

There is much one might learn from observing her, which is why there is a list of names a malm long requesting transfer into her elite unit. More than a few will feel slighted when they learn of your assignment...
Not moments ago I saw the Ironworks' airship rise from behind the mountains and set off for the north and east.
Just watching the infernal contraption makes my head spin and my stomach churn. I cannot begin to fathom the horrors I would face were I to sail on the bloody thing.
Might you be curious as to what it was that Master Garlond threw at the legatus?

We call them tomestones─relics from the Third Astral Era. It is believed that they were once used to store the knowledge of the empire that ruled during that age, but time has rendered them useless─no more than novelties to collectors.

You may be interested to hear that Nael van Darnus, Legatus of the VIIth Legion, hails from a family of just such antiquarians... Moreover, van Darnus's father─a decorated hero of the Empire─famously used Allagan technology to give Garlemald the upper hand in the war which ultimately earned the Empire its independence.

That his son should be so heroic. Upon inheriting the mantle of legatus when his father died, young Nael's first act was to publicly execute his father's entire household guard and replace them with a cabal of hand-picked loyalists.

One would think that such a gratuitous display of ruthlessness would invite the scorn of the Emperor, especially since rumors of patricide were already rife in the royal court. But as it turned out, the opposite was true─Nael's willingness to do whatever it took to achieve his goals was exactly the quality His Excellence sought in his leaders.

And so, despite his murky past, Nael van Darnus has soared through the ranks of the Imperial Army, surpassing even Gaius van Baelsar. Still, his enemies whisper that for all his ruthlessness, the man would never have achieved such greatness if it had not been for his family's study of Allagan technologies.

Maelstrom Command sent you, eh? Well, it's about bloody time. Me and the lads've spent the last gods know how many bells twiddling our thumbs while we waited for the great [@IF($E9(4),adventuress,adventurer)] to grace us with [@IF($E9(4),her perfumed,his dashing)] presence. Anyway, have you reported to the commander yet?

Don't tell me that you thought it was old Myrganmoen who would be leading you on this mission. I may have seen a few more summers than R'ashaht, but when it comes to war, there isn't a finer soldier in the armada.

Rumor has she was the youngest Barracuda ever to make major, and was on course to become general one day, only to resign her post and enlist in the Maelstrom─and in the [@1A(1)]foreign levy[@1A(0)] of all places.

Needless to say, when the scrawny lass arrived, we all had ourselves a good laugh...until, that is, she beat each and every one of us to a bloody pulp. Since then, let's just say there have been no problems.
The commander has more than earned the respect of the men and women under her, and we're more than ready to die in her service. You'd do well to remember that.
You were attacked by the legatus of the XIVth Legion, Gaius van Baelsar, yet you stand here before us with your head still upon your shoulders!?
Thal's balls, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]! You have more lives than a bloody coeurl!
So we meet again, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]. Thank you for coming so far on such short notice.
[@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)], is it? Thank you for coming so far on such short notice.
I would normally give you a proper briefing, but we've little time and every moment spent here lessens our chances of locating Master Garlond and his companions alive.

As Lieutenant Guincum will have told you, an Ironworks airship was grounded while en route to an excavation site here in upper La Noscea. Witnesses living nearby claim that they saw the vessel flying dangerously low, most likely in order to avoid being spotted by the Imperial juggernauts which periodically patrol the area.
We can only assume that the airship came into contact with something on the ground and crashed.

Attempts are being made to contact the Ironworks engineers via linkpearl, but aetheric interference is hampering our efforts. On the handful of occasions when we have gotten through, the link has lasted a matter of seconds.

In spite of this, we have learned that the ship went down somewhere in Oakwood, and that most of the crew, including Master Garlond and his advisors, survived─the bad news being that they are in an extremely hostile area, and unable to move.
I sent scouts to determine if the northern route into Oakwood is safe, yet as I feared, the Garleans have already begun their march towards the wreckage.
Master Garlond's only hope lies in us reaching Oakwood before the Empire, but to accomplish that will mean putting our trust in the very machines our enemies are wont to use against us.

This device was stolen from a Garlean camp and brought back to the Ironworks for inspection. It turns out that it can be made to disrupt the communication signals of nearby imperials. Use it while we engage the enemy today, and they will be unable to call for reinforcements. Understood?

Follow the northern route into Oakwood, slaying any Imperial soldiers you encounter. Do not forget to use [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000423,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000423,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] to prevent them from calling for reinforcements.
It is said that the legatus and Cid's father, Midas nan Garlond, were close friends...though I find it difficult to believe Gaius van Baelsar capable of anything even remotely resembling friendship.

It was about the time that Midas was assigned to oversee the Meteor project that Cid's burgeoning talents came to the attention of the Emperor, and His Excellence invited the young prodigy to work for the crown.

That was how Master Garlond came to be separated from his father at such a young and impressionable age. Separated, and given over to care of those chamberlains and generals who frequented the royal court...
...among whom was one Gaius van Baelsar, Legatus of the XIVth Legion.
Master Garlond appeared full wroth moments ago, but I do not doubt his feelings for the legatus are far more complicated than that.
I suppose we all owe you our thanks for your daring─albeit delayed─rescue effort.

Had you arrived any [@1A(1)]sooner[@1A(0)], we may not have had time to complete our repairs to the airship. However, your belated arrival afforded us [@1A(1)]ample[@1A(0)] opportunity to mend the hull, retune the engine, and apply several coats of stain to the figurehead. And then some varnish. Which is now dry.
Welcome back, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]. As always, your timing is impeccable.
It just so happens there is a matter that requires immediate attention, and as you have served us so well in the past... I trust you see where I am going with this.

Earlier this [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),evening,morning)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),afternoon,evening)])], we received a distress signal from an airship recently departed from the city-state─an airship carrying several senior representatives of the Garlond Ironworks.

From what we could gather, the vessel encountered difficulties somewhere over upper La Noscea, and went down shortly thereafter. I regret to add that we have had no contact with the ship or her crew─Twelve protect them─since that time...
A search-and-rescue party has already been deployed to Camp Iron Lake, but initial reports state that the area is crawling with imperial soldiers preventing the unit from carrying out its orders.
It is imperative we ascertain the status of the passengers on that airship, and secure what survivors there may be─which is why Maelstrom Command has authorized your dispatchment.
You are to journey to Camp Iron Lake, where you will join High Storm Commander R'ashaht Rhiki and her unit of elite operatives and aid them in their search.
Very good, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)]. You continue to serve the armada well. The Admiral will be pleased.
You see, it was not just anyone on that airship...but Master Garlond himself.

Ordinarily, the boy would not set foot beyond the protective walls of the Ironworks, but the recent discovery of a vast network of Allagan ruins in upper La Noscea prompted him to tear himself away from his studies and come here to Limsa Lominsa.

Shortly prior to his departure, rumors began to circulate that Cid believed these vestiges of the ancients to be the key to unlocking the secrets of Dalamud, and preventing the Empire from carrying out their so-called Meteor project. In other words, something best left to the scholarlies. Heh heh.

The Maelstrom owes much to the Ironworks. The engines crafted in their manufactories power our armada. The weaponry developed in their laboratories keeps our enemies at bay. It is in the city-state's best interests that we aid our partners in their time of need, and for that I ask that you please reconsider.
Make haste to Camp Iron Lake. There you will join High Storm Commander R'ashaht Rhiki and her unit of elite operatives and aid them in their search for the passengers of the Ironworks airship.

At ease, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)]. You are wondering why I summoned you. Wonder no more. After witnessing your skills firsthand, I was left in no doubt that you were different from the rest─that I could trust you.
It is for this reason that I would have you present at the signing of the Galadion Accord.
Ah, it seems Lieutenant Guincum was neglectful in his briefing. This has been duly noted.

The Galadion Accord is not unlike the pact recently made 'twixt the Grand Companies, yet though its scale is comparatively modest, I have no doubt that it will prove to be of greater benefit to our city-state than the hollow promises exchanged by the signatories of the Eorzean Alliance.
With the signing of the Accord, Limsa Lominsa takes its final step in preparing for war with the Empire.
As you can see, I have summoned others to this meeting─Commodore Reyner of the Knights of the Barracuda, Grand Storm Marshal Eynzahr Slafyrsyn...
...and finally, Hyllfyr, Captain of the Bloody Executioners, and voice of Limsa Lominsa's pirates.

After several days and nights of deliberation, we have at long last reached a concord stating that for the duration of our conflict with the Empire, the myriad independent pirate crews of Vylbrand and beyond will gather under the crimson standard and follow us into the flames of battle.
That is the Galadion Accord.

With our city-state thus united, we need no longer let the Empire ravage our homeland for lack of strength to oppose them. We need no longer cower behind our city gates because our allies would sooner rain taunts upon one another than cannon-shot upon their oppressors.
If it is a fight the Empire wants, they shall have one! Once the Accord is signed, we will announce our intentions to the realm with a chorus of blood and fire!
As not to flaunt my command and prick the pride of those pirates who have but recently warmed to the idea of the Maelstrom, I have chosen the neutral location of Aleport for the signing.
And I would have you attend as representative of the Foreign Levy.

In these past moons, you have proven yourself time and again an invaluable asset to the Maelstrom. You were cast in the mold of great [@IF($E9(4),women,men)], [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)]. You are the standard against which heroes are measured, a shining example to those yet in the dark.

[@1A(1)]You[@1A(0)] are the Maelstrom, and without you, our cause would be lost. And so I ask you stand with us as the proud armada embarks on her most important voyage─a voyage into the annals of history!
I shall await your arrival in Aleport, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)]. Till sea swallows all.
Hmph. You may have beguiled the Admiral, but you'll not find me so easy to deceive.
Regardless of what Merlwyb believes, the Maelstrom needs you like a privy needs an oven. One misstep and I'll have your head on a pike. Understood?

Why are you still here, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]? The Admiral awaits your arrival in the Coral Tower. She is a busy woman, and will not be pleased if she is made to wait at the whim of an errant adventurer.
A ship must 'ave a compass. 'Tis elsewise doomed t' drift the endless Deep. Yet a compass be worth only as much as the man readin' it.
And Merlwyb be more man than any barnacle-backed scrag for a thousand leagues. Don't ye forget that.
With the signing of the Galadion Accord, the Admiral will have accomplished that which her predecessors could only dream of.
Whether she can maintain order remains to be seen... Yet I have full faith in the woman. She has come this far, and that in itself is an achievement few could claim.

[@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]! I must say, it never ceases to amaze me how you adventurers just happen to pass by the moment we have need of your services. Either you are guided by the hand of the Twelve, or we have a serious security problem... I jest, of course! Ahem.
Great change is upon us, and there is much we must do to prepare, lest we come to grief in the coming storm.

The Admiral and her high council have met every evening for the past fortnight to deliberate over Limsa's course, and it seems they have finally reached a consensus. She has called an assembly to announce the Maelstrom's next move...and has requested that you attend, [@1A(1)]by name[@1A(0)].
Now, why she would want to meet with a member of the rank and file, I cannot say...though it may have something to do with your recent success in dealings with Master Garlond of the Ironworks.
Whatever the case, it would not be wise to keep the Admiral waiting. Make haste to the Coral Tower.
Very good. Perhaps it is this undying loyalty to the Maelstrom that has won you the Admiral's regard. Now hurry along.

Gods, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]! Do you realize what you are doing by ignoring an official summons from the Admiral!? At best, you will be dishonorably discharged and ejected from the city-state. At worst, you'll be tried for treason, keelhauled, and beheaded! We are at war, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]! I strongly suggest you reconsider your answer [@1A(1)]at once[@1A(0)]. If you tarry, I shall have no option but to report you.
I wonder...will it work? Limsa Lominsa, a nest of whores and vipers. Ul'dah, where gil is god.
Can such lost souls truly hear the message Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna preaches?
At the Archon's behest, I have summoned Master Garlond. He awaits you in the chambers atop the steps, there.
I had never thought the Immortal Flames would have the honor nor the cause to beckon the master of the Ironworks. Your heroics do us proud, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
But what could be of such import that Master Garlond himself agreed to come?

You have come so very far, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. To think, you not only fell primals in battle, but hold counsel with the likes of Master Garlond and our own Bull, Flame General Aldynn himself.
Your victory over Garuda with your fellow Flames has placed Gridania greatly in our debt. Rest assured, your rewards will reflect our gratitude.
Keep fighting the good fight, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. In the name of the Immortal Flames, Sultana Nanamo Ul Namo, and the glory of all Ul'dah. By fire reborn!
We gathered for one reason─our belief in the Admiral. Our sails and axes are hers, till sea swallows all.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Hah, I bloody knew it'd be you. And I'm glad it is.

I'd all but resolved to make a ruin of whatever face came through that door─save yours. Truth be told, I've scarce had a moment to myself since Dalamud ripened. There's much to be done, and I don't take kindly to interruptions.
I'm told you have news of the red moon. Well, what is it, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]? Go on.
Is that so? Well, you're not blind. You can see as well as any how large Dalamud has grown in the sky.
Of course, it isn't really growing at all.
It's drawing closer. The closer something is, the bigger it looks. Even the most unlettered Gridanian would concede that.
It's as we feared─if the thing stays its current course, it will fall to Eorzea. What's more, what will fall is no mere rock.

It is a star crafted in antiquity by the hands of man and raised to the heavens by his hubris. As of today, only a few among the Empire and mine own Ironworks are privy to those great technologies of old.
Should it fall... <sigh> Bloody hells.

A [@1A(1)]failed[@1A(0)] attempt to waken Dalamud ten years past wiped an entire city from the face of Hydaelyn─every last stone and soul of it. From that, I daresay Eorzea is not like to survive its impact with more than a crater to show for it.

Mayhaps the land itself will cease to exist... No, even that is mundane for van Darnus. If that prating knave is intent on turning the power of the crystals to the red moon, I fear something far worse. But what...?
Bah, that question will have to wait. For now, what we must rather ask ourselves is this─[@1A(1)]how[@1A(0)] is the Empire controlling Dalamud?
They'd not be toiling to bring it down were there chance of it landing on Garlean territory.

But the lunar transmitter was obliterated in the tragedy of ten years past. It was the only device capable of controlling Dalamud. They [@1A(1)]couldn't[@1A(0)] have built another Allagan transmitter. No... Could they?
Could it all be tied to the crystalline power van Darnus seeks to channel to the red moon? Is there some new Garlean base?
Hm? Bah, my apologies, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I'm grateful for the information you've brought. I'll see to it our studies take it into account.

Ah yes, before we say our farewells, I've been asked to let you know that [@SWITCH($E8(1),Merlwyb,Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna,Raubahn)] wishes to have words with you. [@SWITCH($E8(1),She,She,He)] awaits you [@SWITCH($E8(1),atop the Admiral's Lift,before Stillglade Fane,on the Royal Promenade)].
Hm? No. I've not the faintest idea what it's about, but I can't imagine it'll be all bad.
Caught word, 'ave ye? Aye, the “Barons' Betrayal,” they's callin' it. But by what right, I ask ye? They's bloody pirates, ain't they?

Landlubbers think there's some manner o' pirate code, o'course. But if there's aught I learned in me time among the League o' Lost Bastards, 'tis that the code is more what you'd call guidelines than actual rules.
I hear it told you have met with both Master Garlond and the Bull. Many and more will envy you should you keep such company.
You have done a great service for the Flames, Ul'dah, and the realm. If you wish to claim the bounty for besting Garuda, speak to Lieutenant Aubrey at the Hall of Flames.
Go. We shall tend to the wounded. Hurry, seek out the aid of the Archon in Gridania!
It is said strength must be shown in the face of adversity. Well, never have we faced such adversity as we do now.
And show strength we shall. Our shipwrights will work day and night to forge new vessels to bear the crimson standard─till sea swallows all!
There is the matter of your reward for defeating Garuda. Rest assured it shall be handsome. See Lieutenant Guincum at Maelstrom Command when you wish to claim it.
Welcome back, [@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)]! If it is Master Garlond you seek, he awaits you atop the stairs just there.

Tell me, is he [@1A(1)]truly[@1A(0)] the master of the Garlond Ironworks? I only ask because he speaks in such an uncivi─ Uh, I-I mean...he talks no better than a Lims─ That is to say...his choice of words is very...colorful.

You have accomplished so very much, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Your defeat of Garuda is a task worthy of legend, and you have held counsel with Master Garlond and Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna besides.

Let your deeds be a proclamation to all of the Twin Adders' might and resolve! In victory, you have laid a cornerstone upon which the Eorzean Alliance shall be built─a feat for which you shall be handsomely rewarded.
We will have need of you again, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. For the Twin Adder, for Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna, for all life in Eorzea─the struggle goes on.

We have been expecting you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. As Archon Louisoix requested, we have hailed Master Garlond. He has only just arrived and awaits you in the chambers atop the stairs to your left.
A bold thing indeed, summoning the Master of the Ironworks himself. I pray it is not without good reason.
Victory over the mighty Garuda followed by an audience with the Admiral herself! You have been busy, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]!
The Maelstrom is proud to count you among its ranks. Such loyalty will not go unrewarded.
All Eorzea thanks you. I pray you will answer the call when next we have need of you.
There was nothing I could do. [@1A(1)]Nothing[@1A(0)]! What good is my lance if it cannot reach my enemy!?

There is grim word from the wood, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! We hear that the hamlet of Quarrymill in the South Shroud is being blustered by strange winds. Winds so strong they cannot rightly be nature's doing.
When foul winds blow, it is to our sworn enemy the Ixal that suspicions turn. Should our worst fears be realized...it may be that they have summoned forth Garuda.
Garuda is the primal of wind and matron deity of the birdmen. Beyond that, she is the most dreaded fear of all forestborn.

The Twelveswood is in chaos. Yet again, outsiders have broken through the Hedge and stolen into the wood. And as the forest is ravaged, the grief-stricken cries of countless elementals ring out─so many that we know not how to tend to them.
Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna has taken it upon herself to calm them, and the conjurers, too, do all they can. We of the Twin Adder must also play our part.
We have sent word to Archon Louisoix and asked him to aid in planning a course of action. Please, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], call upon the Archon at Apkallus Falls and follow his guidance.

Would that I were greeting you in less troubled times, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. There are ill tidings from Gridania. Word from the South Shroud is that the hamlet of Quarrymill is being buffeted by winds of a strength never before seen.
The winds show no sign of abating, leading many to suspect that the Ixal are responsible.
Yet the birdmen possess no sorcery so powerful as to summon gusts and gales of such magnitude.
There is only one other possibility...
The Ixal have summoned forth the primal of wind─Garuda!
To make matters worse, Limsa Lominsa's mercenary unit, the Company of Heroes, is busy combating other primals, while the Maelstrom has its hands full seeing to the defense of the nation.
You see what I'm getting at. The defeat of Garuda is a task for you─you who have already proven yourself by felling the primal Ifrit.
Seek out the Archon known as Louisoix at the Apkallus Falls in Gridania. He will guide you.
We have just had word from the Archon Louisoix.
It seems that a hamlet in the South Shroud known as Quarrymill is being...attacked...by the winds. I grant you, it sounds improbable, but this is from no less than an Archon.
The forestborn claim the gales are too strong to be the work of the Ixal. Nor have they found anything in the area that might be causing them.
Left with no other explanation, they have named it the work of the primal of wind─Garuda!
Archon Louisoix himself is of a similar mind, and so has entreated the Immortal Flames to send any brave souls willing to combat the threat.
I would send you, [@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)]. If naught else, it will present an opportunity for you to place an Archon in your debt.
Louisoix asked that we send any souls we might to him at Apkallus Falls in Gridania. Go then, Flame, and burn bright.
Ah, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Right glad am I to─ What is it, friend? You look for all the world as though someone just walked over your grave.
I see... So it is as we feared─Garuda. Then the rumors are rumors no more... Your findings corroborate those of Papalymo. There can no longer be any doubt.

But what of the words she spoke? Of “using the crystals' power to waken the other from slumber”? Does she refer to another primal? We know only of those whom the Amalj'aa and the dark moogles have summoned.
No, to think upon it now will serve no end. We must needs reckon with the enemy before us.
There is but one course open to us. To forestall Garuda's rise, we must send the power of the crystals she feeds upon back whence it came─to the bowels of the earth.

She comes and goes as the storms─sudden and without warning. None know when or where she will show herself. In the long years the Gods' Quiver has waged war against the Ixal, nary a single arrow has found its way to her.
Hm? What is it you carry? There.

Gods be good, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! This is [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000431,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000431,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]!
It is said the plumes which sprout from the body of Garuda carry within them the power of the tempest.

Recall if you will [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000419,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000419,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], mark of Ifrit's coming, the flame of which burns without end. It proved to be the key to facing the primal...

Were I to add my own magic to the power of the tempest housed within this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000431,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000431,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], mayhap I could fashion a device akin to that one...

...There! I have enchanted it to react in the presence of Garuda's powers. I suppose you could call it something of [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000432,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000432,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]... It may be used in much the same manner as the flambeau.
Take it, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. It belongs to you. After all, it would not exist were it not for your efforts.
Go, now. There is a beastman aetheryte in a cave in the northeastern region of Feathergorge. Use it to travel to the Howling Eye.
Garuda commands all the fury of the tempest. Worse yet, she has grown to a power greater even than that of Ifrit. You cannot hope to defeat her alone. You must gather companions to your side.

Only parties consisting of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE(40)] or above will be permitted to battle the primal Garuda.
Furthermore, all party members must have either completed one of the three “In for Garuda Wakening” quests or fulfilled the quest requirements for entering the battlefield.
It is known that being too oft or too long in the presence of the primals wreaks havoc on both the mind and the body. You must know your limits.
Once you have fought Garuda, you will not be permitted to set foot in the Howling Eye again until such time as all trace of her taint is gone from you.

The allotted time for the battle with Garuda is [@VALUE(30)] minutes (Earth time). A waiting time also applies between challenges, and you will not be permitted to return to the Howling Eye immediately.

Rewards for defeating Garuda will be greater for parties made up entirely of members from the same Grand Company.
Have you committed all I have said to memory? If so, make ready and travel to the beastman aetheryte. It is found in a cave in the northeastern part of Feathergorge.

Garuda commands all the fury of the tempest. Worse yet, she has grown to a power greater even than that of Ifrit. A battle the likes of which you have never known awaits you. You must take due time to make ready.
Once you have, travel to the beastman aetheryte. It is found in a cave in the northeastern part of Feathergorge. The way is well hidden, so I urge you to keep an eye to your map.

We must not remain idle while Garuda harries our hamlets and homes. To take her unawares in the Howling Eye offers us the best hope of wresting the power of the crystals from her and restoring it to the earth.
Yet even the greatest of our armies cannot succeed in this. Thus it is to you, the able adventurer, that we now turn for aid.

The gods are good to send us this [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000431,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000431,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. Gather companions to your side, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and set forth for the cave in the northeastern part of Feathergorge. There find the beastman aetheryte that will see you to the Howling Eye. The time to put down the wind primal Garuda is now!
Twelve be good! You look atrocious, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Are you well!? Whatever has happened!?
I see... Dalamud... So the power of the crystals taken by Garuda has been given over to the red moon of Allag.
Hmmm... What could this mean?
The power of the crystals and the power of the aether are one and the same. When the Circle of Knowing first learned of the Empire's designs, we had thought they sought only the primals─nothing more.
Yet if what you have learned is true, it would seem van Darnus harbors aims that differ from those of Garlemald.
What is it the White Raven seeks? Why would he focus the power of the crystals upon Dalamud? Hmmm...
Was that Cid Garlond fellow you spoke of before not knowledgeable in the ways of the crystals? I daresay he knows more of the Empire than any other, having once been counted among its number.
Was that Cid Garlond fellow you met before not knowledgeable in the ways of the crystals? I daresay he knows more of the Empire than any other, having once been counted among its number.
I wonder if you might be able to gain an audience with him, perhaps through your Grand Company ties?
Well, we can but try. [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], hasten to [@SWITCH($E8(1),Maelstrom Command,the Adders' Nest,the Hall of Flames)]. I shall send word ahead of you.
None know more of the crystals and their properties than Cid Garlond. I wonder if you might be able to gain an audience with him, perhaps through your Grand Company ties?
Hasten to [@SWITCH($E8(1),Maelstrom Command,the Adders' Nest,the Hall of Flames)]. I shall send word ahead of you.
...Do you make me for a prattling politician? One who speaks of high ideals, and dreams of unity even as her nation's divisions deepen?
And what of it? To speak of high ideals is the charge of every ruler. As is never abandoning hope.

I saw much in your presence at the signing. It showed there are those among your brethren with a desire for alliances to be struck. A desire to forge a united front. In the end, acts guided by such desire will lead to great things.
Trees put to flame take time to mend, and replanting the lost takes more. It'll not be easy quelling the greenwrath these sins have woken.
But if any can, it is the Elder Seedseer. Already she has gained the forgiveness of the great ones for much of what happened.
I received a letter in the post from an old friend. Just between you and me...
...It seems Gridania and Ul'dah are not having an easy time of things.
It is the unity that Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna champions that will lead this realm to victory. That is my belief.
And once you have your beliefs, there is naught left to do but act. It is the simplest of things, is it not?
We are bound now. Your strengths are mine, and so too are mine yours.
Make use of me as I will you. Let us share our victories, and may they be many.
Eorzean Alliance? <spit> We're not bloody like to reach terms with a commune of treelovers and a fleet of fishermen. Not as if they'd be much use on the battlefield, anyway.
Still, us Flames is paid well to do what we do, and orders is orders. If Raubahn commands it, I'll follow.
It is our born right and responsibility of each of us to seek our own path to freedom.
Yet in the doing, many forget to respect the same right of their fellow man. In seeing one's own path open, one must take care not to close the path of another.

Yet even paths made in the midst of discord are not all in err. Truth lies atop the mountain, 'tis true, but there are many ways to navigate its slopes. Should a path lead to the top, it matters little if its way is winding.
But I have rambled on for far too long... I do hope that which I endeavored to impart will prove useful. Yet should my meaning elude you, fear not. Adventurers were ever wont to find their own way.

It is as I thought, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─a deep bond exists between you and Eorzea. Your fates are inextricably intertwined. Lo, you stand before me as proof. That you have come at this time of great peril to the realm is no coincidence.
You look perplexed, friend. Do not be. You will understand all in time.
Dark words have reached the Adders' Nest. The hamlet of Quarrymill is under assault, though not by the siege-craft of any known army or beast tribe. No, the enemy comes as [@1A(1)]wind[@1A(0)].
There are dark words from Gridania. It seems the hamlet of Quarrymill has been besieged, though not by any army or beast tribe. Nay, the enemy comes as [@1A(1)]wind[@1A(0)].
Given its strength and constancy, we believe it to be the work of Garuda─the primal worshiped by the heathen Ixal.
Garuda is a wholly ruthless being─a harpy among primals. She is as a storm, marked by caprice and prone to violence, and her appetite for destruction is without equal.

She has wreaked ruin upon remote hamlets in the past for naught but her own amusement, and is known to butcher the men last, that they might live to see their women and children tortured and killed before them.
For nigh on a decade, she has been a sworn enemy of Gridania. Know that when forestborn utter her name, they do so with both a hatred and dread far deeper than that they bear any Ixal.
And now Garuda has gained strength enough to extend her presence in Eorzea. We fear she can bring her power to bear anywhere in the realm─Gridania not least of all.
For their part, the other nations have now risen to aid us in our struggle, but our combined victories are too few to warrant mention.
Rare is the soul bold enough to vie with a primal in battle. Those few who would find Garuda wearing the winds as her armor─a contrivance so cunning that most mortals are powerless to do her harm.
Now her reach grows ever more vast, and her acts ever more depraved. The soldiers of our armies will prove no match for her─that much is plain.

It must be you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─you who have prevailed against the primal of fire and the mad moogle king. I beseech you, hasten to Quarrymill and deliver it from destruction at Garuda's hand.
It must be you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─you who have prevailed against the primal of fire. I beseech you, hasten to Quarrymill and deliver it from destruction at Garuda's hand.

Aid us, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. All see that you adventurers possess prodigious gifts. If any can best a primal, it is you and your brethren. I beseech you, hasten to Quarrymill and deliver it from destruction at Garuda's hand.
The lives of men are nothing to Garuda. She kills without conscience─nary a thought. If the gusts and gales that batter Quarrymill persist, I fear there shall be no one left to save.
Travel to Quarrymill in the South Shroud and learn what you can of these ill winds. If our fears are confirmed, and Garuda is indeed responsible, return to me at once.
Your eyes betray you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You do not wish to refuse this charge. I beg you reconsider.
Travel to Quarrymill in the South Shroud and learn what you can of these ill winds.

Victory over a primal and a private audience with the Elder Seedseer. Gods, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], just how am I to greet you now─kiss your hand or bend the knee? Hah!
You are no doubt eager to claim your reward for defeating Garuda. If so, see Lieutenant Fulke at the Adders' Nest. That is all.
We have sent countless messengers and envoys to the other nations, all to strengthen the bonds of the Eorzean Alliance.
Our words are sent, yet no words return. I pray they heed our call this time, before it is too late.
I suffered a grievous wound in the service of the Barracudas not many days past.
Many returned with their lives, but not with their will to continue the fight.
The Flame General comes from humble beginnings, like many of us. He understands those he commands, and that commands our respect.
As do your deeds. Word of your victory over the imperial vanguard has reached the ears of all─smallfolk, Flame, and lords alike. All name you a hero.
The Admiral awaits you in the stateroom.
Take the Admiral's Lift to the stateroom?
You'll not gain an audience any other way. Last I checked, the Crow's Lift in the Adventurer's Guild doesn't go to any staterooms. Hahaha!
Take the Admiral's Lift to the stateroom?
Visit Gridania's Lotus Stand. There you will find the Elder Seedseer, Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna. Hear how it is she proposes to forge this alliance and then report back to the General.
The Admiral has no patience for... Well, the Admiral has no patience. Do see you conduct yourself in a manner befitting your station when in her presence.
Tarry not, here. If your business is done, get you gone. But know that once you depart, you will not be permitted reentry without the Admiral's leave.
Exit the stateroom?
The messenger from Ul'dah left words for you. He bids you hasten to Mor Dhona, to the southwest of Camp Brittlebark. There will be more to hear once you arrive.
'Tis the site of Castrum Novum. Whatever orders await you, I daresay they will be of great import.
Delaying will gain you nothing. See the deed that brings you done, and then be gone.
Exit the stateroom?

So, it's you they've sent, is it? Ha! I had an inkling it would be. Whatever else you might say of the [@SWITCH($E8(1),pirate woman,horned lass,the man-bull)], [@SWITCH($E8(1),she,she,he)] does have an eye for talent.
It's no secret the leaders suddenly feel moved to remake the alliance. Having a Garlean stronghold built on your doorstep has that effect on people.
The place is called Castrum Novum, by the way.
A strategic location, a stalwart fortress, masses of troops to defend it... All of this, and now, of all times.
Their purpose could hardly be more clear. This Castrum Novum was built to house the lunar transmitter, with which the red moon will be controlled.
If it is not destroyed soon, there will be no hope of stopping Dalamud from falling to Eorzea. Should that happen, all the realm will be made a ruin.
Our only saving grace is that the transmitter is not yet complete─hence the Empire's attempt to divert our attention elsewhere with their recent flurry of attacks.
But we have need of more information if we are to destroy it. Scouts sent by the three nations have learned little and less of what must be known.
Most sane observers now realize that no single nation can hope to triumph alone, and that the strength of all three must be combined. Yet each mistrusts the other, and the alliance remains unmade.
We have Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna to thank for what little has been achieved. But for her devotion and goodwill, I daresay the battle would already be lost. If you care to hear more, best hear it from her.

Well then, back to Ul'dah with you! March into the Fragrant Chamber and tell your Flame General to lend a bloody hand while his beloved sultana still has a sultanate not to rule.

An imperial warship was shot from the sky on way for Castrum Novum.
I sent word to the three nations requesting help surveying the wreckage. With luck, there may well be something that will tell us more about the Garleans' activities in Mor Dhona.
And here you are, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─the finest the realm has to offer.

I might have known that you would be the first to arrive. Aye, knowledge is power, and your leader means to make it [@SWITCH($E8(1),her,her,his)] own. With it, [@SWITCH($E8(1),she,she,he)] could no doubt improve [@SWITCH($E8(1),her,her,his)] nation's standing in the alliance.
Each postures, seeking an opportunity to wrest control of the proposed alliance. But if that's what it takes to see it made, so be it.
The fallen warship is to the north and west of here. Go, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and search the area.
Should you find anything of note─anything at all─bring it to me at once!

You've returned! It is good to see you safe. Did you find anything?
Gaius van Baelsar!? So the Black Wolf has shown himself. Tell me everything!
Hmmm... I see plans within plans. It was not luck that brought down that ship, I think. It was van Baelsar.
And we wandered, artless, into his hands... But what choice did we have? We must take what we can get.
So long as I draw breath, Eorzea's fate is not sealed. Together, we shall turn the tide of this war yet.

Let's see... This [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000433,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000433,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you found details how the lunar transmitter functions.
Aye, it's as I thought. The transmitter takes shape at the heart of Castrum Novum even as we speak.
I'll need to study the plans further, but I daresay they will prove invaluable in planning an assault on the stronghold.
There was word that Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna is calling an alliance defense council. The Lominsans and Ul'dahns are dragging their feet, though, as one could expect.

Take news of what we've discovered to the leaders, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Knock some bloody sense into those rock-hard heads of theirs. Tell them the last chance to save Eorzea is upon us, and they'd best not piss it away.
Leave the rest to me. Travel to the Lotus Stand in Gridania and do whatever you must to get those damned fools to pull in the same direction!

Twelve be damned! We're too late...
I was [@1A(1)]sure[@1A(0)] van Darnus lacked the Allagan tomestones he needed. I didn't think that many were even left! Where in the bloody hells did he find them!?

I've finished studying [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000433,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000433,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you recovered. I believe I've identified a way to access the lunar transmitter.
And with the might of a three-nation army, I'd wager we can destroy the damnable thing.
Once we do, Dalamud will be little more than a pretty red spot in the sky!
I don't intend to stand idly by while those bastards make a crater out of this realm! We [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] put an end to Meteor!

Ye'd best behave yerself afore the Admiral, [@IF($E9(4),lassie,laddie)]. She don't 'ave no truck with 'alf-wits.
It is believed Castrum Novum houses the lunar transmitter needed to control Dalamud, though it is not yet operational. Twelve be praised for that.
It would seem the Empire is investing still more of its power in Mor Dhona. More and more we see airships bound in its direction. We were fortunate enough to shoot one down not long ago.

There may have been much on board that can tell us more of the lunar transmitter. If you mean to search the wreckage, do take care─I wager the imperials have already dispatched forces to secure the site.
Gauis van Baelsar...? You mean to tell me the legatus of the XIVth Legion told you of van Darnus's designs? That they were at odds with those of the Empire?
The White Raven is a keeper of the knowledge of Allag. If he has come here to realize his own ambitions...perhaps the Black Wolf would rather he failed.
Welcome, friend. Pray forgive my directness, but tell me, what do you know of the Syndicate?
Our nation has long been a sultanate, yet true ruling power lies in the hands of Ul'dah's six wealthiest and most influential souls. It is this council of six that is known as the Syndicate.

They are seldom of a single mind. Their number includes both Royalists and Monetarists─the former being staunch supporters of the sultana, and the latter desiring self-governance for the merchant classes.
Raubahn himself is a Royalist. When he set about rekindling the Immortal Flames, the Monetarists were less than eager to aid him. I do not think that will be the case in this latest endeavor.
The scouts tasked with Castrum Novum's surveillance will form the core of the unit which assaults the stronghold.
It will comprise forces from all three nations. Their number is not yet great, but reinforcements march to meet them as we speak.
It is happening. The alliance has been made. All thanks is owed to you.
Here, your reward. You've more than earned it.
You must now travel to Jagged Crest Cave in Mor Dhona. There you will find the alliance forces gathering for the assault on Castrum Novum.
They will tell you more of your task when you arrive. You have come this far, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Pray do not stop now. Go, and may the Twelve watch over you.
The three armies allied as one... It will not be easily done.
Even should we see this war won, think of the war to follow. The free nations will vie for hegemony, and the Admiral will be forced to abjure open diplomacy, lest she lose favor at home.
The scouts sent to survey Castrum Novum will form the core of the unit which assaults it.
To their numbers will be added those of a force from the allied army.
A fine place for the Eorzean Alliance to claim the first of many victories!
Your deeds inspire hope not only in the hearts of Lominsans, but the free peoples of all the realm.
I will not lie. Our position is...grim. But we must never forget to laugh, and to smile, now most of all. A broken blade may be reforged, but a broken spirit...
Your reward. Get you next to Jagged Crest Cave in Mor Dhona. There meet with the forces staging the assault on Castrum Novum.
The Elder Seedseer has chosen you as her emissary. She asks that you bear her message to the leaders of Limsa Lominsa and Ul'dah. Please, hurry to the Lotus Stand. She awaits you there.
You are to seek out Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna at the Lotus Stand and hear how she proposes to reforge the alliance. Once you have done so, bring her words back to the Admiral.
A pirate ain't got aught on 'is mind but freedom and loot. Hehehe, ain't so different from ye adventurin' types in that, I s'pose.

With no whispers from the forest, we must turn our ears to the whispers within ourselves. For we are forestborn. Our lives come from the wood, and so we are a part of it.
Your visit means much to us, truly. Allow me to offer these words of counsel by way of thanks─harbor no wicked thoughts nor ill will here, for the elementals see all.
They are the wood, and the wood is they. Honor them as you would the gods. Revere them. Fear them. Strive to know their mind.
The fires of war which now spread through the forest have woken the greenwrath. The elementals now pose as dire a threat to our way of life as the Garleans or the Ixal.
I bid you do all in your power to win the other nations to our cause. That which we propose, we propose not for Gridania, but for all the realm.
I bid you do all in your power to win the other nations to our cause. That which we propose, we propose not for Gridania, but for all the realm.
Given their familiarity with the area, it has been decided that the scouts assigned to surveil Castrum Novum will form the core of the unit tasked with assaulting it.
To their numbers will be added those of a force from the allied army.
Even now, infantry units from each of the free nations march for the front. They will take up positions mere malms from the imperial stronghold.
Your reward is more than deserved.

I have new orders for you, as well. The Twin Adder would send you to Mor Dhona. The forces staging the assault on Castrum Novum gather in Jagged Crest Cave. Go to them, and join your strength to theirs.
You will be briefed upon arrival. You have never yet failed us, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and I do not believe you will fail us now. Such is your reputation─and your responsibility.

The nations have each sent scouts to the stronghold known as Castrum Novum, but to no avail. The imperials guarding it are so many that no man can so much as draw near it, much less learn anything of import.
The Elder Seedseer has told me of your deeds. Your praises will be sung across the realm, of that have no doubt.
I am Teledji Adeledji, head of the Mirage Trust. You may not know of me, but certainly you have heard of the Trust's Platinum Mirage here in town. I sit on the Syndicate, as well.

When Raubahn was jumped-up to a seat on our council for amassing a fortune in blood money, he dishonored us all by leaving the city without a word. Only when he learned of Garlemald's plot to attack did he return.
He has since remade the Immortal Flames of old, 'tis true, but the army is as patchwork as a mummer's motley. What can they hope to do against the might of Garlemald?
And now he would have us cast our lot with the bumpkins of Gridania and the scoundrels of Limsa Lominsa? It is enough to make a lord laugh!

What have we to gain from this, hm? We of the Syndicate have a hand in politics, yes, but we are merchants at heart. Do not forget that. To us, it is plain that the other nations mean to use the chaos as an excuse to tap the coffers of Ul'dah.
Bringing Dalamud down from the sky to obliterate an entire realm and everything within it...
Only the twisted mind of Nael van Darnus would seek to realize such an abomination as this Meteor endeavor. Small wonder he is considered a fiend even within the Empire.
This all began ten years past. Midas nan Garlond was working as the Empire's lead engineer when this brainchild of his came into being.
I have often wondered if it might not be guilt that drives Cid Garlond to toil so tirelessly to destroy it. The son's attempt to right the father's wrongs.
If the red moon falls, the destruction will be utter and complete. Nothing will remain to speak of, nor anyone to speak of it.
My friends and I mean to do anything we can to stop it. I, for one, have grown quite fond of this Eorzea. Would be a shame to replace it with an unseemly void, would you not agree?
Yet there is only so much we can do. Unallied, the free nations have no hope of victory. They must unite.

Are you ready?
Just the words I hoped to hear. I daresay in you we have found one of the valiant blades spoken of in the prophecy.

Your deeds are an inspiration to all. Never forget that. Believe in yourself as you walk your path, and you'll be a beacon to others in this darkness. Heh, play your cards right, and they'll follow you all the way to the victory parade.
The council is set to begin. Best find your way to the Lotus Stand.
Well done, old [@IF($E9(4),girl,boy)]. The alliance the Circle of Knowing has long sought and strived for has been made at last.
I confess I've half a mind to put your heroic deeds to song. You make for an unlikely muse, but a welcome one.

Hm. For all her poise, the Elder Seedseer is at heart a gentle soul. To see her greet your coming with such serenity, you would never suspect she had been praying for your preservation but moments before.
Few are as strong and true as Raubahn. He has absolute faith in his men, never doubting for a moment that they will see their duties through to the bitter end.
You must feel proud to serve under such a fine leader. It has ever been my goal to inspire the selfsame sentiment within my own ranks.
As Chief Admiral of the Maelstrom─and on behalf of the Eorzean Alliance─I hereby issue you the following order...
Lead an assault on the floating isle, and eliminate Nael van Darnus.
It is a man to be feared who can bring down a moon, but that he should offer himself as a beacon to guide its descent, and raise the very land to greet its coming...? Seven hells...
If truth be told, I still labor to believe that mortal hands are capable of such feats.

It was a grizzled old huntsman who found the seventh verse─or rather, stumbled upon it. In pursuit of his quarry, he strayed into the depths of an uncharted cave. And there were the words, etched into a slab of stone.
It would take some time for their true import to become apparent. But let us save that tale for a rainy day─I suspect there will be a few of them before the end.
You're finally here. Good.
Time is of the essence, so I'll forgo the pleasantries.

The White Raven is hiding to the southeast of Camp Glory, in Coerthas.

The city of Sharlayan lies on an island in an archipelago far to the north. It was once a great seat of learning, home to countless scholars versed in the ways of magic.
Alas, it was all but abandoned after Ala Mhigo fell to the Empire.
The men and women of the Circle of Knowing hail from Sharlayan. We must be thankful they chose to come to Eorzea's aid when they quit their home.
You look deathly pale, soldier. What did you see in Coerthas? Report!
...A beam of light like the one seen at Castrum Novum, sent skywards from a floating isle? ...And a shower of red-hot boulders as Dalamud's reply?
Gods be good, the prophecy is coming to pass...
I can scarce believe my ears, yet I know you speak true.
Given what you faced, you did well to come back alive.
And fighting fit at that. 'Tis a blessing indeed in this, our darkest hour.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You've scarce had chance to catch your breath, I know, but I need you back out there. I have another mission for you.
Assault the floating isle, and kill van Darnus.

The poor [@SWITCH($E8(1),woman,lass,)] heaped such praise on you while you were gone, I had half a mind to poach you for the Flames.

Your mission is to lead an assault on the floating isle. Once there, seek out van Darnus and kill him.

Pray accept my apologies for the sudden summons.

The legatus has been discovered to the south and east of Camp Glory in Coerthas.
Urianger of the Circle of Knowing informs us that many Allagan ruins lie in close proximity.
The workings of the legatus's mind are beyond our knowing.
Yet given the historic connection between the lesser moon and ancient Allag, there can be little doubt that the man chose his hiding place with good reason.
I would have you travel to the south and east of Camp Glory. Once there, confirm the presence of our quarry, and survey the surroundings, that we might better understand the legatus's designs.
Perchance you are familiar with Saint Coinach? He is among the revered figures whose images grace guildleves.

Saint Coinach taught us the value of passion─a quality which I am pleased to see you possess in abundance.

A beam of light such as that seen at Castrum Novum, rising towards the heavens...and Dalamud raining down fiery boulders?

quest_names: It's a Piece of Cake to Bake a Poison Cake
text_en: As anyone who has spent any time on a ship could tell you, these are the early symptoms of the dreaded scurvy, a malevolent malady which will drag its victim all the way to the gates of the seventh hell if not treated forthwith.

quest_names: It's a Piece of Cake to Bake a Poison Cake
text_en: And how might one go about loosening the deathly grip of this much afeared affliction, you ask? Why, with the sun's blissful bounty, that's how! But therein lies our predicament. quest_names: It's a Piece of Cake to Bake a Poison Cake
text_en: However, at long last, I believe I have finally developed a biscuit that is not only lightweight, but chock-full of nutrients, its dough being fortified with a special blend of vegetables and lemon peel, dried and ground into a powder. quest_names: It's a Piece of Cake to Bake a Poison Cake

quest_names: It's a Piece of Cake to Bake a Poison Cake

text_en: You see, knowing that after tasting my ambrosial oeuvre, Irongut would be back for a second helping, I baked another batch of suncakes, this time adding Nightbreath, a clear, tasteless poison which I purchased from a shadowy fellow recently arrived on a trading vessel from Radz[@1F]at[@1F]Han. It is said that even a single drop can kill a whole army of men... I added three, just to be safe.

quest_names: It's a Piece of Cake to Bake a Poison Cake
text_en: And wouldn't you know it, but not two bells ago, good Aentfoet over there said he saw the rat run off with his cheeks puffed out like a lemming and crumbs spraying about hither and thither. Now it is only a matter of time...

quest_names: It's a Piece of Cake to Bake a Poison Cake
text_en: Ah yes, I suppose you are wondering about my request for assistance. Well, as I would not dare leave the protective walls of Limsa Lominsa while imperials roam the realm, I require someone to venture out in search of Kikkiroon's venom-steeped body, so that I may have definitive proof of his timely demise. I have reason to believe the thief is hiding somewhere in Cedarwood.

It's a Piece of Cake to Bake a Poison Cake
text_en: Many thanks. And if by some chance the rat is still amongst the living when you find him...well, then do what it is you adventurers do best─cuff him one between those floppy ears of his!
