Greetings, adventurer. You have the look of a seasoned slayer of knaves and ne'er-do-wells. Might you be seeking an opportunity to apply your skills in slaughtery to a cause most noble? Of course you might!

Permit me to explain. A few moons back, our field assessors began to discern a trend in the attacks upon trade ships moored here in Galadion Bay. Now, as you know, random acts of brigandry are hardly uncommon in the city[@1F]state, but this was different─it was...[@1A(1)]predictable[@1A(0)]. It seemed as if someone, or something, was making a concerted effort to raid vessels carrying shipments of sthalite ore.

Sthalite is a dense, crystalline substance used in goldsmithing and armory, but because it is not readily obtainable on Vylbrand, firms like Naldiq & Vymelli's must import it from Aldenard. The ore is plain in appearance and extremely difficult to refine, making it virtually worthless to all but those with knowledge of metallurgy.

Which is why the recent crimes had us utterly perplexed...until we received an anonymous lead pointing us towards the kobold tribes of O'Ghomoro. Quite how they managed to slip into the city, board several heavily guarded ships, and finally make off with what has been estimated at ten score tonzes of ore, all unnoticed, is unimportant. What we need to know is precisely how they mean to use it.

According to reports made by Knights of the Barracuda units patrolling upper La Noscea, kobold activity has markedly increased in the vicinity of a system of natural caves known as the U'Ghamaro Mines. The beastmen have gone so far as to bar the cavern entrance with a heavy iron door.

It is well documented that the kobold tribes of Vylbrand are highly skilled in metalworking, with most of their raw materials coming from the countless tunnels carved through the heart of O'Ghomoro. Rarely do they wander far from their caves, shunning contact with Lominsans unless they feel cornered.

The fact that the promise of sthalite drew them out of their holes and into our very midst has prompted us to wonder if the substance might have uses beyond armory and bauble-making...and if those uses might pose a threat to the thalassocracy.

We have taken our concerns to the Maelstrom, and one Chief Storm Sergeant Nolan assured us that an investigation would be conducted shortly. However, given all the armada has to deal with, I doubt they will be able to devote much time to what certainly [@1A(1)]appears[@1A(0)] to be little more than a case of rogue beastmen doing a spot of raiding.
And this, my good adventurer, is why I must call upon you and your many talents. If the kobolds truly [@1A(1)]are[@1A(0)] up to no good, waiting for the Maelstrom to act may prove disastrous.

Would you travel to the U'Ghamaro Mines, find a way inside, and see if you cannot determine what they are using the sthalite to create? If you are successful in bringing back pertinent information, I shall see to it that your efforts are well rewarded.

Your assistance is appreciated, but I must warn you, the region in which you will be traveling is wild and treacherous, and many of the caves there remain unexplored. I hardly need add that you will not be welcome in the kobolds' domain, so be sure to make the proper preparations before embarking on this quest. You may even wish to employ the services of a few of your fellow adventurers. Oh, and might I recommend that you make Camp Iron Lake your base of operations? You will find it a convenient location to provision your party before entering the Mines.
I understand your hesitation. It was wrong of me to ask you to commit to such a perilous quest without due consideration. My apologies. Please, think upon the matter and visit me again.
I [@1A(1)]highly[@1A(0)] recommend that you and your party visit Camp Iron Lake before entering the U'Ghamaro Mines.
Not only will you be able to purchase supplies, but perhaps learn something of the caves from the local guard stationed at the outpost.

Well met. I am Chief Storm Sergeant Kurtz Nolan. What brings you to this godsforsaken corner of Vylbrand? And don't tell me it's for the scenery. The hills here are no different from the ones in Bloodshore.

Kobolds stealing shipments of sthalite? Let me guess─Mealvaan's Gate sent you. <sigh> I [@1A(1)]told[@1A(0)] them that the Maelstrom would investigate their claims in due course. Honestly, if those thrice-damned scholarlies spent a quarter as much time on basic sword drill as they do worrying about the world beyond their magnifying glasses, they might actually be able to venture out into it.

Alright, alright. Considering you came all this way with every intention to help, perhaps we can find something for you to do. But let me make this clear─you are now working for the Maelstrom, and you will report to me, and only me. Oh, and you need not worry about your precious reward. I will recompense you for any reward promised by Mealvaan's Gate. Agreed? Good.

Now, for your assignment: though we have no concrete evidence, we believe that the kobolds may be using the stolen sthalite to forge a super-hard alloy called cobalt iron. When used in armor, the metal can render a man nigh on invincible, but due to the rarity of the materials required to forge it, and the prohibitive degree of skill required to shape it, large-scale production has long been deemed impossible.
However, if the kobolds are hoarding the materials to make cobalt iron armor, then it could mean they are planning for war...

What I require of you is to ascertain the extent of the beastmen's cobalt iron production. To do that, you are to take this liquid compound created from the humours of a coblyn, and apply it to any metal you find within the U'Ghamaro Mines. If the metal contains sthalite, the liquid will change from yellow to green─just don't ask me how.

Once you have used up all the liquid, return here and report your findings. Oh, and please, [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] be careful. I've lost more than a few good men in there, if not to the kobolds, then to the endless labyrinth of tunnels. Keep your map with you at all times, and may the Twelve watch over you.

A pleasure to lay eyes, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)]. I am Chief Storm Sergeant Kurtz Nolan. If you do not mind me asking, what brings you to this gods-awful place? I somehow doubt it's for the scenery. The hills here are no different from the ones in Bloodshore.

Kobolds stealing shipments of sthalite? Then that makes you the one Mealvaan's Gate has sent. It is kind of you to offer us your aid in this matter. To ensure that we are on the same page, pray allow me to review the situation.

We believe that the kobolds may be using the stolen sthalite to forge a super-hard alloy called cobalt iron that, when used in armor, can render a man nigh on invincible. Unfortunately, we have no concrete evidence, but there may be a way to get some...

This liquid, created from the humours of a coblyn, will change from yellow to green when it comes in contact with sthalite. It would greatly behoove our cause if you would venture into the U'Ghamaro Mines and apply it to any metal you find there.

Due to the rarity of the materials required to forge it and the prohibitive degree of skill required to shape it, large-scale production of cobalt iron has long been deemed impossible. However, if the kobolds are hoarding the materials to make cobalt iron armor, then it could mean they are planning for war...
It is imperative that we ascertain with all haste whether the stolen sthalite is being used to produce cobalt iron. Once you have used up all the liquid, pray return quickly and report your findings.

Oh, and please, [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] be careful. I've lost more than a few good men in there, if not to the kobolds, then to the endless labyrinth of tunnels. Keep your map with you at all times, and may the Twelve watch over you.

As you can see on your map, the entrance to the U'Ghamaro Mines lies but a few malms to the northeast. Oh, and the place is fair crawling with kobolds, so I would strongly advise against venturing in alone.

Once you are inside, locate objects made of metal and apply the liquid I gave you, noting whether or not its color changes to green. Once you have used up all the liquid, return to me and report your findings. Good luck, and may the Twelve be with you.

Apply the coblyn humours?
Apply the coblyn humours?
You have already tested this object.
I am pleased to see you back, adventurer. I was beginning to worry that you, too, had fallen prey to the mines and that which lurks therein. So, tell me, what did you discover?
Giant cauldron-shaped buildings made of metal!? What in the seven hells could those beasts be planning?

But even so, you say you were unable to locate any metal containing sthalite... This is most disturbing... It appears that Mealvaan's Gate was correct in their assumption that the kobolds were planning something sinister, though it seems it had little to do with the stolen sthalite.

...On the other hand, ten score tonzes of ore could not simply have vanished into thin air. Perhaps there are further chambers in the depths below the areas we have already explored? If there are, the kobolds would have little trouble concealing whatever it is that they are slaving over, be it weaponry to sell to pirates or armor for use in a war against Limsa.

At any rate, it appears our survey of the U'Ghamaro Mines is far from complete. I shall inform Maelstrom Command and Mealvaan's Gate of your findings and request more men be dispatched to Camp Iron Lake.
Here is your reward, adventurer. Oh, and you need not bother returning to the customs-house to report. I will see that they are promptly sent word of your safety.

Why, if it isn't [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Last I heard, you had gone and shacked up with them storm bringers. Ah, but that's of no matter. What [@1A(1)]does[@1A(0)] matter is that you're here, and that I happen to be in need of a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of your talents.
One of them storm bringers, are you? Well, it just so happens I'm in need of a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of your talents.
You see, it's the damn smitties again...
To protect our most delicate of creations from salt and rust, we use a rare oil pressed from the seeds of the deadly nightshade─as foul a bit of foliage as you could ever hope not to meet.
The problem is, the smitties─brown-nosed bastards that they are─have tapped the armorers' supply, and gifted it to Merlwyb for use on her pistols, Death Penalty and Annihilator.
And this when the city-state has us working the forges day and night to prepare enough plate for the coming invasion.

Each turn of the sun that our stock of nightshade oil remains empty, the further we fall behind on our orders. And the further we fall behind on our orders, the fewer men will have what they need when the cannons start up.
Normally, we'd send one of our own to gather more seeds, but we cannot risk losing any more of our men to the horrors that dwell outside the city gates.
That infernal Dalamud has the whole realm thirsting for blood.
You look as if you've seen more battles than me and my forgemates combined. I trust you'd fare better out there than any of us.
So, what say you?
Thal's balls! I [@1A(1)]never[@1A(0)] thought you'd say yes!

Now, deadly nightshades are oft found growing along the shore of Iron Lake. You shouldn't have any trouble finding the things. 'Course, extracting the oil from them can be... Well, I reckon it's naught a bona fide storm bringer can't handle! Hahahahaha!
Do I look like a man who'd tell you the fate of the realm was in your hands [@1A(1)]if the fate of the realm truly wasn't in your hands[@1A(0)]?

Deadly nightshades grow like weeds about the shores of Iron Lake. The oil from about [@IF($E5(6,0),[@IF($E2(6,10),[@SWITCH(6,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(6)])],[@VALUE(6)])] of the bloody creepers should do it.
Just be sure to watch yourself. There's plenty of deadly things out that way besides nightshades.
Bloody hells! You're alive─I mean, back! You didn't get the oil, did you!?
This is it! Hah hah hah! This'll show them damnable smitties! Once we deliver our orders, the Admiral'll see who's truly an asset to the city-state.

I know, I know... This probably ain't the best of times for in-fighting, but our lot and the smitties have been at it since back before even I can remember, and I'm not sure we could stop if we tried. 'Tis all we know, see?
Then again, maybe it's that same urge to best our brothers that gives us the kick up the arse we need to push on?

But enough talk. I must get back to the forges. You have my thanks, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Oh, and try not to worry overmuch about the coming of Ralgr's wrath. There's naught the Destroyer can ruin that the Builder cannot mend.
Ah, oh? Yes...er...I am Storm Sergeant Third─no, [@1A(1)]Second[@1A(0)] Class Alain Brooks. I...do not believe we have met. Should I...er...know you?
S-S-Sent by Maelstrom Command!? I...er, well...ah... [@IF($E9(4),Ma'am, yes ma'am,Sir, yes sir)]! Nothing to report, [@IF($E9(4),ma'am,sir)]!

[@1A(1)]Corporal[@1A(0)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]? Oh, well... Ahem! Very good. Er, then you may strike the “[@IF($E9(4),ma'am,sir)].” My apologies. It won't happen again, [@IF($E9(4),ma,si)]─ Oh! Yes─carry on, carry on.

Why do I have nothing to report? Oh, yes... I suppose Command [@1A(1)]would[@1A(0)] want to know that...(damn them)... Ah, er... There is a very good explanation for all of this. Very good. Very good, indeed.

You see, my supervising officer, Captain Zigan Shamagan, was...uh, recently injured...(in a damned [@1A(1)]training[@1A(0)] exercise)...and I have been given command of his unit until his wounds heal...which just so happens to be taking [@1A(1)]considerably[@1A(0)] longer than I was hoping it would...ahahaha... Haha?

Though it pains me to say it, I...m-more than anyone...am aware of my, er...shortcomings as a leader of...ahem, men. T-Truth be told, I'd just as soon sit here and wait for reinforcements than risk marching off into battle only to have the death of some young up-and-comer on my conscience...his restless spirit haunting me until the end of days.

Now...um...if [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] would like to risk life and limb for the Admiral, I will not stand in your way. In point of fact, I will gladly stand somewhere else entirely...behind a rock, let's say. The, er, encampment is just over there to the east...I mean west.

Just do not presume to take any of my unit with you. I shall observe your...er, efforts...from afar, and report them back to Command... That is...um, u-unless you fall. Then, I will be forced to declare that you went off without my consent. I shall not have your untimely demise on my conscience...or my record. Yes.
To complete this duty, slay kobold cragsmen, roundsmen, and bedesmen at the kobold encampment until you earn 1000 War Merit.

Do be quick, though. Once the southern front sees that you have infiltrated the encampment, they will begin preparations for their attack. You must withdraw before they arrive. Oh, and, ummm...do not think that you can go and...er...enlist the aid of any companions. The death of a stranger would weigh just as heavily on my poor soul...oh yes it would.
War Merit cannot be earned while in a party. Should time expire, the duty will be deemed a failure and all amassed War Merit will be lost.

It...uh, goes without saying that...um...the higher the rank of the enemies you...you...how should I put this? Um...dispatch? Yes, the higher the rank of the enemies y-you dispatch...the more favorably your accomplishments will chime with Command. I sh-should add that death never seems to chime with anyone very much, so I'd suggest...er...erring on the side of caution. Yes, caution.
Killing higher level kobolds will yield more War Merit. Should you be KO'd, the duty will be deemed a failure and all amassed War Merit will be lost.

Oh, and, uh... I must ask that you do not...erm...stray too far from the encampment...to, say...somewhere I cannot see you. This is more for my benefit that yours...as I will not be moving an ilm from this location.
Should you leave the instance, the duty will be deemed a failure and all amassed War Merit will be lost.
Ahem...very well. I believe that is...uh, all. Let me know when you are ready, then.
Gods! Look at you! Your weapon, your clothing...your very [@1A(1)]soul[@1A(0)] drips with the blood of...oh...oh my...
I believe I'm going to be ill...
Please, I beg of you! Leave me at once... Yes, yes. You have proven you possess the heart of a coeurl, the strength of a drake, the stuff of heroes, and so on and so forth.
I'll tell Command whatever you want, just...just [@1A(1)]go![@1A(0)]

Oh, and...er...I don't suppose you might...uh...agree to keep the details of [@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] performance...let us say...shrouded in the mists of history? I mean, it is the least you could do for me after I wrote you such a...[@1A(1)]shining[@1A(0)] report, no?
Congratulations, Storm Sergeant Third Class [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]. As of this moment, you are no longer a member of the enlisted masses, but a fully-fledged petty officer.

Know that much more will be asked of you, and that mistakes will not be tolerated. Soldiers will look to you for strength and guidance, so let your light be as a beacon in the darkness─a source of hope to those that are lost.
Till sea swallows all.

Oh, my! The good corporal has returned! Here to lay down your arms, are we? Splendid! Permit me a moment to tear up this evaluation and then we shall sit down like civilized [@IF($E9(4),men and women,men)] and have a nice chat over a cup of hot mulled wine. Yes, mulled wine. Good for the nerves, it is.
Abandoning the duty will result in the loss of all amassed War Merit.

Pity... Though, I suppose I never stood a chance of convin─ Hm? Oh, you [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] abandon the mission!? Why, this is...remarkable! Perhaps I am better suited to leading than I first believed! Now where did I put that bag of cloves?

Right... I suspected as much. Well then, away with you. There is little time before the southern unit begins its advance, and I will not be held responsible for anything which might endanger the lives of my misguided colleagues-at-arms. Away with you, I say!
Welcome back, Corporal. Word of your achievements in upper La Noscea has already arrived.
Once again you have gone above and beyond the call of duty, proving yourself a true asset to the Maelstrom.

Sergeant Alain Brooks? You need not worry yourself with that dithering dolt. He will be dealt with in due time...as will the Coral Tower official who used his influence to see his good-for-naught son rise within our ranks.
Now, let this next salute be your last as corporal.
To perform a Storm Salute, first target First Lieutenant Guincum and then either select Storm Salute from the emote list, or input the /gcsalute text command.
What are you waiting for, Corporal? Salute!
To perform a Storm Salute, first target First Lieutenant Guincum and then either select Storm Salute from the emote list, or input the /gcsalute text command.

That assignment is only available to those who have been awarded [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,2001009,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,2001009,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. And how might one go about obtaining said medal, you ask? Why, in the selfsame wise one would go about obtaining anything in the Maelstrom─Storm Seals.

Oh, no no no no... This will not do. This will not do at all. I do not believe you...er...heard me correctly. I specifically stated that you could only...ahem, unilaterally and entirely without my consent, infiltrate the encampment [@1A(1)]alone[@1A(0)].
Oh... So you truly are going through with this nonsense, are you? Ah, well, I suppose if I could convince you not to go, I'd make a better officer.

Ah, of course. Well, then...off you go. As I stated before, I shall observe your assault and deem whether or not your war efforts are worthy of merit. Return here when you feel you've given the kobolds' noses a sufficient...er...bloodying.

Now, should you happen to come to your senses and wish to withdraw from amid the frankly grotesque bloodletting, speak with me and I will...um...[@1A(1)]see to it that none of this ever transpired[@1A(0)].
Wh-Wh-Wha─!? Have you second thoughts? Th-Th-This is...remarkable! Was it my inspirational speech that melted your resolve and stayed your blade!? Oh, joyous day! If my poor mother could see me now!

By obtaining the prestigious Lapis Cross, you have proven yourself not only brave and loyal, but resourceful─the exact traits we seek in our officers. We must be certain, however, that you are truly ready to face the challenges that will accompany your new position, hence this simple trial.
You have no doubt heard of the kobold encampment located in upper La Noscea. It is a festering canker that must be excised lest it spread to infect the whole.

To do this, the Admiral has ordered a staggered wave of attacks from each of the four cardinal directions. Rather than focusing on eliminating the enemy in one fell stroke, each wave is ordered to engage their targets just long enough to weaken them, before withdrawing to a safe distance. Then, before the kobolds have had an opportunity to fully recuperate and refortify, the next wave advances and repeats the process.
If executed properly, a mere fortnight would suffice in seeing the encampment fall. Unfortunately, it appears we have a weak link in our chain─the eastern front.

Since his promotion to Storm sergeant, certain...questions have been raised at headquarters as to Alain Brooks's suitability to the burden of command. You are to travel to his camp and assess the situation, providing whatever assistance is necessary to ensure the fulfillment of mission objectives.

Excellent, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]. Perform well, and the next time we meet, I shall be pleased to address you as “Sergeant.”
Content with your current position? I concede that not all men may achieve greatness...but I had hoped they might at least aspire to it.
Sergeant Brooks is stationed in upper La Noscea, to the east of the kobold encampment. Speak with the officer and assist him in completing his orders.
Your duty lies to the northeast of Camp Bald Knoll in western La Noscea. Scour the area for the great buffalo and bring the beast down.
Wild buffalo are said to be extinct, and ordinarily I would assume our Mistbeard nuisance to be a domestic animal, escaped and turned feral...

But it appears this specimen is a beast bred and trained for war─there is no telling what havoc it may wreak if left to trample the fields unchecked. It must be slain with neither hesitation nor mercy.

Welcome back, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)]. It goes without saying, but you arrive at a propitious moment─I have just now finished reading the report on your latest success.
Not only have you proven to be a constant thorn in the Empire's side, you have also shown an aptitude for shaping a disparate mob into a unified force.
I see before me the makings of a fine Maelstrom officer.
And it is with great pleasure that I hereby promote you to the rank of Second Storm Lieutenant!
Now, signify your readiness to bear the burden of your rank with a salute worthy of the occasion!
To perform a Storm Salute, first target First Lieutenant Guincum and then select Storm Salute from the emote list. Be sure to select Storm Salute, and not merely Salute.
You can also perform a Storm Salute by inputting the /gcsalute text command.

Congratulations, Second Lieutenant. As an officer of the Maelstrom, you are now a member of an esteemed group.
May your strength and courage inspire our soldiers to greatness!

Once again I offer you my congratulations, Second Lieutenant.
And speaking as one officer to another, it will be my honor to serve alongside you─till sea swallows all.

My gratitude! Indeed, you are blessed with foresight to see that a simple act of charity is in truth a sound investment in future profit. An Ul'dahn through and through!

Amalj'aa are vile beasts, but they ain't stupid. They'll be changin' that convoy route, mark my words. But I'll see to it we know when they do. Don't you worry about me. My orders are to stay on here for a spell and keep up the surveillance. You just get yourself back to the Hall of Flames and make your report.

Welcome back, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)], and congratulations! First Commander Ashdale sent word of your victory.
He is a good man and an able leader─though perhaps a bit obsessed with supplies and logistics, as you may have gathered. Still, we owe this victory to his planning, as well as your bravery.

And now, it is my proud honor to inform you that the Immortal Flames have decided to raise you from the ranks of the enlisted to petty officer. I hereby promote you to Flame Sergeant Third Class. My congratulations, Sergeant [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)].
Your first task as such─to pledge your allegiance to the Immortal Flames anew with a salute befitting a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of your achievements.
To perform a Flame salute, first target First Lieutenant Aubrey and then either select Flame Salute from the emote list, or input the /gcsalute text command.
I couldn't have done it better myself. But I must tell you, with greater rank comes greater responsibility. Still darker days lie before us, and we will expect even more of you when they arrive.
For the Immortal Flames! For Ul'dah! For the sultana!
Come, show me a proper Flame salute!
To perform a Flame salute, first target First Lieutenant Aubrey and then either select Flame Salute from the emote list, or input the /gcsalute text command.

There is work to be done, but the burdens are too great. You are not yet ready to bear them. Come and see me again once you've earned [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,2001011,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,2001011,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].

Well met, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]. It would seem the powers that be here in the Hall have taken note of your deeds.
A task has come down befitting a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of your mettle. As you well know, the number of Garlean attacks rises with each passing sun.
We would like nothing more than to raise all our banners against them, yet they are not our only foe. The Amalj'aa have scented opportunity, and they too now move against us.
If both powers were to fall upon us at once... The Immortal Flames could not repel such an assault. We must strike first. We must arrest the Amalj'aa threat before it gains momentum.

We are already surveiling the lizardmen where we are able, and have learned much of their logistics. We mean to use what we know of their supply routes to launch an assault that will cripple their military in one fell swoop.
First Commander Ashdale leads the mission. Rendezvous with his force in the vicinity of the Amalj'aa altar in eastern Thanalan, and have your orders from him.

It is imperative that we succeed in this, [@IF($E1($E9(52),0),[@IF($E3($E9(52),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(52),12)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(53),0),[@IF($E3($E9(53),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(53),13)],)],)][@IF($E1($E9(54),0),[@IF($E3($E9(54),127),[@SHEET(xtx/gcRank,$E9(54),14)],)],)] [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]. May Halone guide your hand in battle.
You would refuse? Hmph. Perhaps you don't want that promotion after all.

text_en: And so, in recognition of your distinguished service, it is with great honor that I hereby proclaim you Second Flame Lieutenant [@STRING($EB(1))]. By fire reborn!

text_en: If you ask me, those damned Ala Mhigans are cowards for fleeing their homes. Still, you'd best watch your back whenever they're around. They're harmless enough alone, to be sure, but they got nasty tempers on them, and take courage from numbers─and they almost always turn up in numbers.
Coliseum's been more tolerant of the bastards than anywhere else in Ul'dah. Aye, threw our doors wide open, we did. And I don't like it one bloody bit.
The Coliseum exists to entertain! To bring the blood to boil and incite roars from the crowd! Only the most exhilarating of battles will serve.
That is why we must weed out all who are unworthy to set foot upon the bloodsands. Our patrons wish to see only the mightiest of combatants. And should they be pleasing to the eye, all the better.
Make your way within through the door, there. And be sure to give the weaklings a thorough trouncing. It's for their own good. I just pray to the Twelve you aren't one of them.
Almost every Ul'dahn with a coin to their name bets at the Coliseum. There's a fortune resting on every fight.
The sums in the Coliseum's ledgers are so large, the smallfolk would scarcely be able to make sense of them. I myself was taken by a shaking fit when I first saw their like.

The first rule of the Coliseum is [@1A(1)]you do not talk about the Coliseum[@1A(0)]. Others will try to pry words from you, by force or by promises of coin and flesh. You must be strong to resist─of mind and of body.
I don't care what they threaten you with─spill our bloody secrets, and I'll spill your bloody guts!
There's but three ways to make it onto the sands─get accepted, get recommended, or get scouted.
Once you's on 'em, though, gods be [@1A(1)]good[@1A(0)], there's riches to be had! Gil and gifts what would put the sultana to shame.
Might be you'll apply to fight, and might be you'll get accepted. But you'll not even make underling until you pass our trials.
You know what an underling is, you spineless mass of puk shite? Naught but a worm what just offers itself up to be thrashed by the crowd favorites, hoping for a bit of coin.
'Tain't as simple as pittin' the strong against the strong. Makin' the lists is a bloody art. Takes years of workin' in the Coliseum to know what makes for a good match.

Hells, all the sword skills in Hydaelyn won't make for a great fight. An adventurer like yourself must know of all the standard weapons and their uses, though, right? Aye, well...that'll take you far, here.

If pushed, I'd have to say Luzlo Pulazlo is the gladiator of the moment. Luzlo Lowthrust, the commonfolk call him. Before him, there was Melusine the Muse, but she suffered wounds in her last match that have kept her abed ever since.
It matters little enough. The names borne by the cheers will change afore long, sure as sunrise. And all the better. Naught stirs the crowd's displeasure quicker than boredom.
Do you know why it is we seek to employ you adventurers here? I will tell you. It is your potential─potential for connections.
Your ties stretch throughout the realm, and put you in the company of all, highborn and low. So forge your bonds with as many as you may. The Coliseum will be the better for it.
Ala Mhigo long claimed to be home to the finest warriors in the land─far mightier than even our own! Ha!
If that's so, then tell me why is it they were so quick to turn tail and flee before the Garleans. Bloody cowards, the lot of them.
Ugh... Gods...not again... Not like this...
Truth be told, even that last match of yours was open to wagers.
I might have put a gil or two on you myself, if it hadn't been for your opponent. There isn't a soul in Ul'dah who'd risk their coin on [@1A(1)]him[@1A(0)], so there was no profit in it.
You fought... Well, you fought. That much can be said. But you've still got a lot to learn.
If you live long enough, mayhap I'll teach you some of the techniques Master Greinfarr himself shared with me. Deadly stuff, that. And right popular with the crowds, too.
I heard the last tourney champion bought an estate in the Oasis with his winnings. They are even saying he hired some twenty or thirty servants into his employ.

Of course, the Coliseum keeps a watchful eye on its fighters. It'd be bad business to let the lackwit drown himself in wine and women. Aye, we'll keep him fit, so long as he can turn a profit. After that, the bloody fool can do aught he pleases.

I've had it up to here with these false warriors. They come crawlin' out of some stinkin' pit on the outskirts of Aldenard─where they was doubtless one o' the very best sword fighters in the whole village─thinkin' that maybe they can fight their way to fame.

And so they takes to the sands, fancyin' themselves the next Greinfarr, only to get their arses damn near hacked off. At least most got sense or pride enough to relent after that. Only most of them, mind. The worst insist on stayin' and fightin' over and over again.
Can't for the life of me reason why we got us more of these Ala Mhigan cravens than Gridania. Gods know the trees are closer to their home. You'd think they mean to conquer us.
Some think it's the Black Shroud what drives 'em our way. They say that godsforsaken forest would put paid to most of 'em afore they got anywhere near the city.
A few of the Ala Mhigans have claimed a victory or two on the bloodsands. But it was only a matter of time, given their numbers. Still, none have yet won a tourney.
There was a tourney a while back where one of their kind nearly triumphed. It caused quite a stir about town.
I envy you adventurers, truly. You have such wonderful opportunities to meet others like yourself and improve your skills.
Make sure and seize those chances when they come along, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Or you may regret it the rest of your days.
So they will!

Yes, I see in you a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] who understands there is more to glory than mere victory. More than killing. We are entertainers, and so we must entertain. Give the crowd something to remember you by, and they will make your name legend!
There are many others like yourself who work for us here. Some fight themselves, others scout the realm for those who would.
But you are new to us, and must begin at the beginning.
Selections for the next tourney are already underway. It presents an ideal opportunity for us to weed out the...[@1A(1)]lesser[@1A(0)] individuals.

For as the old saying goes, [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] that is base in both skill and face doth not a champion make. Knowing little of your own skill, I think perhaps I will have you participate in this tourney, too. Do try not to die.
Make your way within through the door, there. And be sure to give the weaklings a thorough trouncing. It's for their own good. I just pray to the Twelve you aren't one of them.
That is most unfortunate.
You have broken this little Lalafell's heart, and that is no easy task.
Hah! The only calm heart is one that lies rotting in the breast of a corpse! Now begone, before I ring for the guards!
Aye, the games aren't as thrillin' as they used to be. And what of it? You want to go back to the times when corpses littered the bloodsands after a melee?
Least now most can walk away when the fight is done. To hells with dying, I'm here for the bloody coin. Not to make shite-shoveling smallfolk forget how worthless their lives are.

Time was, the crowds used to get worked into an absolute frenzy at every match. Hells, they used to riot in the streets and damn near bring the city down around them! Not like now. Not like these lackluster times.
You must find us new talent, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. We have received word of promising fighters in the north. Follow the road to Gridania, and scout whomever you can.
There is another of our men already arrived there. Seek him out at the inn. He may be able to aid you in your search.
Years ago, they had to turn away smallfolk at the gates every match, so full were the stands. <sigh> Seems like only yesterday...
Even the din of sword on shield was drowned out by the roars of the crowd. I swear their shouts must have echoed all the way to the halls of the Twelve.
We are gladiators─we live and die by the sword. Fascinating, is it not? This piece of steel. Where in the course of its forging does it acquire these powers over life and death?
Heed my advice─don't go gobbing off about the other gladiators to no one. They're not like to take kindly to it. Most want to remain a mystery.
And who can blame them? Fanatical followers and bankrupt gamblers are common enough in this city, and can be a damn sight more dangerous than the bloodsands.
Hells, you need look no further than Greinfarr to see the truth of it. More than a few of his matches have been...problematic.
When the crowds grow unruly, it falls to us to quell them. I tell you, I know of no pleasure greater than swinging my sword freely about the city!
Doing so serves to anger the Coliseum's owner something fierce, though. It's he who shoulders the repair expenses, after all.
Organizin' a match might seem a bloody simple thing, but it ain't.
Each and every fighter's got their own skills, conditioning, strengths, and weaknesses. You've got to look at [@1A(1)]everything[@1A(0)]!
In simpler times, we had only to arrange matches which were like to bring the crowd to its feet. Cheap thrills, swiftly digested. But no longer.
Now, we must craft battles that last for more than mere minutes. We have learned that fleeting pleasures do not make for happy customers.
The Coliseum still makes a profit, to be sure. But the sums are not as great as they could be.
Our coffers contain a shadow of what they did years ago. And the fault is our own, if you ask me. There are simply no heroes for the people to rally behind as there once were.
I see the Coliseum has sent more fools to woo Helbhanth.
Stop wasting our bloody time, and yours. His duties hold him here, and his honor. All your gil and glories mean nothing next to the safety of the Twelveswood.
Oh my, it is [@1A(1)]such[@1A(0)] an honor to meet someone from the Coliseum. Have you just come from Ul'dah? By the Twelve, you must be absolutely [@1A(1)]exhausted[@1A(0)] from your travels.
Tell me, are there no plans to hold a ladies' tourney? I daresay it would attract quite a crowd. Come, have a look about you. The Wailing Barracks has no want of lovely lancers.
You're free to talk to whom you will. But you'll find those long in Gridania are not likely to leave.
They've come to know in their hearts that to abandon the forest is to abandon the elementals─and it is their favor that makes life good.
The Coliseum, eh? Aye, I've no qualms with the battling itself. It's the false fights I'll have no part of.
If you've a mind to put on a show for the crowds, why not a little music? I'd sing those Ul'dahn fools a tune or two. My singing's as sharp as my spear! Hahaha!

The Wood Wailers are the finest lancers in the land. Together with the archers of the Gods' Quiver, we fight to protect the Twelveswood from all who would threaten it, be they sylph, Ixal, Garlean, or otherwise.
We speak solemn vows, and hold to a strict code. You'll not be convincing any of our ranks to dance the bloodsands. Best try your luck with some snot-nosed adventurers.
What business have you with the Wood Wailers? Speak quickly.
The Coliseum of Ul'dah? Come to try those sorry southron skills against some true warriors, have you? Well the Wailers are always happy to oblige. Pray, proceed! Hahaha!
Spar with the Wood Wailers?
What's this? Craven, are you? Then best mince your way back down south and [@IF($E9(4),take your rightful place with the weavers, woman,join the rest of the eunuchs)].
Spar with the Wood Wailers?
We have no interest in your false battles. Our place is here.
You fight to entertain your people. We fight to protect the lives of ours.
I'd be lying if I said I didn't wish to see the Coliseum for myself─just once.
Warriors from all over the realm come to your bloodsands, do they not? Aye, I'd wager the Wailers could learn much of the weapons and ways of our enemies by watching your games.
The promise of a bulging victory purse might be enough to lure most men from their homes.
But we lancers do not want for coin. The forest provides for us, so long as we protect it. No words will coax us from its shelter.
I trust you enjoyed your bout? There is a great deal of difference between the sword and the spear, is there not?
I know not if you are long for this place, but you would do well to learn all you can during your stay.
What is this talk of Helbhanth having fought in the Coliseum? And why does he not deny it?
All know he has never set foot outside of the Twelveswood...right?

You vultures from the Coliseum keep on coming, no matter how often we refuse you. Faced with such persistence, we soon struck upon the idea of friendly combat as a means to draw what little benefit we could from your intrusions. Surely you gladiators are better with your swords than you are with your tongues.

Our plan seemed infallible. Should one of your number lose, we could brand them a weakling and refuse outright. Should they win, meanwhile, we could profess our own weakness and refuse on grounds of inadequacy. Either way, we would be rid of you, and all the better for the additional training.
The way of the sword is such that all who walk it become lost. A skilled gladiator told me that once─one of your own kind.
The way of the sword is such that all who walk it become lost. A skilled gladiator told me that once─one of your own kind.
Word has come from the Coliseum. A promising new fighter has been found in Limsa Lominsa.
Come, we'd best get back to Ul'dah. There's naught for us here. That much is clear now.
It is a shame the scouting did not go as well as we hoped. <sigh> Perhaps we'll never restore the Coliseum to its former glory...

I simply wanted the Hellfire Phoenix to take to the bloodsands once again, and have her redeem her besmirched name before all of Ul'dah. Gods, we could have paid off all the Coliseum's debts in one fell swoop...
I heard that Miqo'te's an Ala Mhigan refugee. Came from one of them camps outside the city walls, apparently.
Rumor has it the Ala Mhigans have a small fortune bet on this fight. Win or lose, they're like to take to the streets after─be it out of happiness or rage.
Greinfarr don't look to be in top form. That could be trouble... If he loses this fight, there'll be riots the likes of which Ul'dah ain't never seen!
Do I have a gripe with the Ala Mhigans? Damn right I do! They come to [@1A(1)]our[@1A(0)] city playin' the part of the downtrodden, and take work away from honest Ul'dahns!

I've never seen a sword and spear more equally matched. That blade of Greinfarr's has hidden powers, they say, but that polearm is no jape either. Had she a bit more weight on her, that Miqo'te might well have finished Greinfarr already.
Any fool knows you play the odds, not the fighters. I thought to make a fortune betting on the Miqo'te, but too many Ul'dahns were of the same mind. In the end, the odds came out about even.
Greinfarr knows not what to do. Look, it is as if his sword has lost its way. Perhaps he is not his father's son, after all...
My parents always leave me behind when we come to the Coliseum. They tell me to fend for myself while they go off looking for better seats.
My father is always ranting about going from poor to rich with the single swing of a sword. That's all well and good, it's just... I... I just want to be loved. Hold me.
So you are returned to us. <sigh> That is...unfortunate. I had wagered that you would be taken by the elementals of the Black Shroud.
Went to Gridania, did you? Aye, I can guess why. I seen some of the Phoenix's fights myself.
Most are quick to make the Ala Mhigans for fools and cravens, but don't you make the same mistake.
There was a time when Greinfarr used to roam the land with Niellefresne─the heir to the Eshtaime fortune.
<sigh> Were that lad still with us today, no doubt our dealings in Gridania would run a good deal smoother.
Gladiators we may be, but all are free to fight at the Coliseum─not just those with swords. Which isn't to say we're in the habit of letting crafters and gatherers loose on the bloodsands.

Though we did hold a culinarian tourney once. [@1A(1)]Once[@1A(0)]. Bloody comical stuff. There were spatulas, tongs, pots and pans, ladles─you name it. One fool was actually swinging a rotten salmon in his off hand, gods' honest truth.
That near-champion you met hails from Ala Mhigo. Damn miracle, if you ask me, making it safe to Gridania after all that way.
With wounds like that, and being hounded all the way? The bloodsands ain't seen toughness like that since, and I doubt they will again.
That new warrior they found in Limsa is one of the Company of Heroes.
But you didn't hear that from me, savvy? If word were to get back to Bhaldfarr...
If you ask me, the Coliseum is in dire need of a tourney of handsome gentlemen.
It would certainly attract the custom of the realm's ladyfolk, of that you can be sure.
Hells, imagine a veritable stampede of vixens, maids, and spinsters, all in heat and swarming over the city... Just think of the gil to be made!
We must think of a name for our newcome recruit.
The Widowmaker! Or perhaps the Orphaner? Something to do with killing people and making the lives of those they leave behind somewhat the lesser for it...
<sigh> The matches Greinfarr gave us when he was in his prime were the best there have ever been. And don't you let anyone tell you different!

And that technique of his─the old “lost blade” maneuver. It would make his opponents think he'd called it quits, and they'd come charging in to deliver the killing blow...and [@1A(1)]that's[@1A(0)] when he would strike!

Imagine the suspense! Hearts aflutter, the people look on... To everyone's eyes the fight is all but won, and then... Yaaaaaargh!!! Greinfarr cries out, his sword finds its mark, and just like [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)], victory is his. The crowds would go absolutely [@1A(1)]wild[@1A(0)]!
Any clod with a blade can [@1A(1)]learn[@1A(0)] the technique. But it takes a master to execute it in battle. Why not try your hand at it?
It is not every day that we are blessed with a gladiator's debut. Give the bards something to sing of, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)] the Unsung.
Go and speak to Yoyobina if there is anything more you wish to know. I must mop up this spittle.
You aided us before in weeding out the weakest from the lists. But this time you will be fighting in a real match.
This is to be a tourney of warriors. You represent our guild, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and so will be fighting with a sword.
Speak to the other gladiators. Hear their words and heed their advice. Then you will know, and knowing is half the battle.

The other gladiators will share with you what they have gleaned from their own experiences on the bloodsands. Knowledge is a weapon, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Arm yourself well before you go forth to battle.
A [@IF($E9(4),swordswoman,swordsman)] is only as good as [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] sword. Remember that.
Repair your weapon when it's damaged, and buy a finer one should you have the coin. The same goes for armor and shield.
That was abject! Simply abject! The least you could have done was [@1A(1)]die[@1A(0)]. Perhaps then the crowd would have had reason to cheer. Try again, and save your name while you are still able.
You [@1A(1)]lost[@1A(0)]? So that is why the breath went out of the crowd so suddenly. As a gladiator, you must learn to answer their cheers with heroics, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
The tourney has brought more than just gladiators to Ul'dah. I only hope the crowd shares our appreciation for the variety of weapons on display.
Of course, you must demonstrate the sword's superiority, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. And do try to avoid losing. It's just bad business.
I hear this tourney is going to be one to remember!
Any soul stepping onto the bloodsands had best know how to put on a show. I've seen bored crowds turn to showering stones down on participants. They get the violence they come for─one way or another.
The bloodsands are not the battlefield─there is no glory in victory alone. You must entertain the fans. Make their blood boil!
Put on a show. Make it so the crowd cannot look away for a second. Swing your blade with great bravado. Taunt your opponents, toy with them. Like this!
I shouldn't think your opponents will be too dangerous. Not this time around.
Yet your inexperience makes it all the more important that you properly prepare. I'd make an effort to watch the other fights, were I you.
This is what I do to taunt my opponents. Absolutely infuriating, isn't it?
Compared to all the gamblin', the coin made from sellin' seats don't amount to a pint o' piss. But the crowds who turn up for matches are the Coliseum's heart an' soul, they are.
Fightin' safe is one thing, but don't even think o' borin' the crowd. Do that, and they'll turn on you faster than a cornered rat.
You wish to know more of your opponents? Hahaha, what's this? Did Yoyobina not bother to tell you?
You're to fight a pirate scouted from Limsa. Murderous devil with a blade that can cut diamonds, from what I hear.
The bloodsands are no ship deck, aye, but a marauder's axe'll split you from head to belly all the same. Don't make the mistake of underestimating that one─not for a bloody second.
Come, do as I do. This one always seems to please the crowd.
The bloodsands await, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. As I told you, you will fight as a gladiator. Are you prepared to play that role?
Are you ready to play the role of gladiator?
Very well. Then you are ready to descend to the bloodsands.
Head down the stairs and through the door─make your way to the Coliseum, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]─and greatness!
Are you ready to play the role of gladiator?
He is our [@1A(1)]partner[@1A(0)]. Do you have a problem with that? It matters little enough who is chosen to compete against him.
It is [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] who applied for entry in this tourney. And [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] who passed the qualification bouts. All the toil has been [@1A(1)]mine[@1A(0)].
You! It is y-you... F-From the...
You remember me from the qu-qualifying bout? I am as w-weak now as then. P-Please do not expect m-much of a fight from me.
The gladiator fighting in the next match is another adventurer.
Look, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Something about that bloke seems a bit different than before, no?
I've seen him fight with a sword. He's no match for even the most inexperienced gladiator. But perhaps his true prowess does not lie with the blade...
You faced him in the qualifying rounds, if I recall. Was there aught of him you thought odd?
That is the Lalafell you fought not long ago. At the time, I thought him quite hopeless with a sword.
Perhaps he has training with some other weapon... What did you make of him, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? Try and remember whatever you can.
Gods be good...
He was hiding his true might when he faced you. The makers of the lists were deceived─as were we all.

Not an uncommon thing, to be sure. Near all who come to the Coliseum do whatever they can before the fighting begins to gain an advantage. Truth be told, it often serves to make the games more unpredictable and exciting.
Each tourney attracts so many warriors, and so many of them are [@1A(1)]truly[@1A(0)] weak and craven. Amid the multitude, it is not difficult to carry out such acts of deception.
Well, I still lost... I thought my deception enough, but you gladiators are not an easily fooled lot, it would seem. The day is yours.
It is not an honorable thing that I did, but it was not without reason. We Ala Mhigans have a cause for which we fight. And for that cause, we will do all we are able.
J'moldva is a turncloak and a craven! She betrayed all of Ala Mhigo!
We need the bloody coin! Without it, we cannot fund the war to reclaim our lands from those Garlean bastards.
Many of our young have no memory of their homeland. But those such as J'moldva who endured the greatest hardships could never forget. Never...
All the more reason for her to wish to do so, I suppose. But we'll not follow her in her treasons. Let the harlot die a traitor. The gods will sort her out.
Who are you? Are you an Ala Mhigan?
Master Greinfarr went to great lengths to see to it the Ala Mhigans receive special favor here.
But I don't see why [@1A(1)]we[@1A(0)] are obliged to uphold it if he himself is never even here.
Ala Mhigo... <spit> Aye, Ul'dah's seen its fair share of war at those bastards' hands.
Our rulers never had any love for the place, but merchants seemed to like it well enough. There was always a gil to be had there. Till the Empire took over, that is.
Smallfolk tell of how many young daughters were left behind in Ala Mhigo to fight. Turns out most of them Highlander girls swing a sword as well as any adult.
I'd dearly love to see for myself. The Miqo'te known as the Hellfire Phoenix was a sight to behold, that's for sure, but they say [@1A(1)]all[@1A(0)] them Highlanders are possessed of the same fury.
We Ul'dahns are underhanded when it comes to coin, I grant you. That is no secret. But these Ala Mhigan scum are underhanded in [@1A(1)]all[@1A(0)] things.
They are a far cry from the proud and austere souls the stories and songs make them out to be.
More of these damn Ala Mhigan lickspittles in Ul'dah now than a drunk can piss on. And they work for bloody [@1A(1)]scraps[@1A(0)]!
Things went well enough for a while. Till the ingrates started gripin' of being exploited. Now there's hardly a soul around here that doesn't hate them.
You'd think more people in Ul'dah'd mean more people payin' at the Coliseum, no? Aye, well, it ain't that simple.
That what's growing is the lower class─them as got no coin. No profit to be had there.
Ala Mhigans everywhere have banded together in the effort to reclaim their homeland from the Garleans.
I will never understand why people insist on laying claim to a certain plot of land. I have always considered my home to be wherever it is I find myself.
There is merit in studying other weapons, to be sure.
But it seems to me that learning the basic use of all would take a great deal longer than mastering just one. Life is too short, friend.
I watched your bout, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. But the one after was so much more entertaining that I forgot entirely about yours! Do forgive me.
Oh, come now. I never went out of my way to make [@1A(1)]fun[@1A(0)] of the little Ala Mhigan. Even if I did, who could possibly have guessed that such insignificance was merely an act?
<sigh> Perhaps that is why I am such a poor judge of men.
But enough of all that. Here, take your reward. Yoyobina extends his gratitude.
So tell me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], are you not thrilled? Your Coliseum debut has finally come.
Perhaps the gods will see fit to spare your life. [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)] the Unsung, the people will call you! A new hero─come to us as sudden and shocking as a bolt of lightning.
Oh... Oh dear, excuse me. It seems I've gone and drooled on myself. Go and speak to Yoyobina while I mop this up.
Oh, come now. You must not dwell on thoughts of defeat. Envision yourself [@1A(1)]victorious[@1A(0)]! Just think of it all─the gil, the glory, the [@IF($E9(4),gentlemen,girls)]...

The miners are responsible for gathering the precious stones and metals we require from the bosom of Eorzea. Of course, it's not as if we can just use them in the state in which they're delivered to us.
No, no, no. Far from it. Ores must be concentrated and purified into ingots, for example.
Strange and wonderful things, gems. Have you ever chanced to note how their color and brilliance change from wearer to wearer?
Aye, they change their moods as oft as we do. They are as near to living as the unliving can be.
I recommend you acquaint yourself with a miner or three. Or, at the very least, some merchants who deal in ores. Without the right connections, you'll never get your hands on the choicest materials.
The relationship between the miners and we goldsmiths is one of mutual respect. For without one, the other is nothing.
And both parties realize that the greatest coin comes by working in unison. Such friendly cooperation comes as a breath of fresh air in this den of avarice.
A gifted goldsmith never wants for coin, and none is more [@IF($E9(4),admired by the gentlemen,popular with the ladies)]. Of course, that is not what drew [@1A(1)]me[@1A(0)] to the profession.
Trinkets with thaumaturgical properties? Yes, to be sure, there are many and more.
It just so happens that such pieces are my speciality─whether imbued with true magic, or simply made to look as if they might be.
Greetings, adventurer, and welcome to Eshtaime's Lapidaries. Elecotte has told me of your coming. I am Colbernoux, and I will be your mentor during your time as a novice here.

No doubt you are feeling somewhat nervous, yes? That is to be expected, considering the sheer value of the goods with which we work. But worry not. You will be using only base ores to begin, all easily procurable.
Come to think of it, what better way to celebrate your joining than through the bringing of fresh materials with which you might work?
A dear friend of mine is employed at the Nanawa Mines─a lovely Miqo'te lass by the name of Z'ssapa. She may be willing to part with some of her haul for such a special occasion as this.
You will most like find her somewhere near the entrance to the mines. Oh, and be sure to tell her Colbernoux sends you with his regards.
Your journey as a goldsmith has begun. And what better way to mark the occasion than with a fresh batch of materials on which to hone your nascent skills.
Seek out Z'ssapa near the entrance to the Nanawa Mines. A lovely Miqo'te lass, and a dear friend of mine. Send her my regards, and she may be willing to part with some of her haul.
That is no small haul of ores I saw fit to part with, you know. Do be sure and tell Colbernoux where they came from.
I wonder if he'll name one of his masterpieces after me like that brooch he did for F'lhaminn...
Oh, you dear thing, of [@1A(1)]course[@1A(0)] I will pose for you. I'd like nothing more! Oh, I could absolutely [@1A(1)]shower[@1A(0)] you with kisses!

What the bloody hells...? Ain't them eyes o' yers workin'? Can't you see people is laborin' here?[@CR]...Eh? What's that? Eshtaime's Lapidaries? Gods, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)], why didn't you say so!? Let a miner know if there's aught she might do to serve.
A man's name? Given to a piece of jewelry?

It is not entirely unheard of, though the honor is reserved for only the most exceptional individuals. Generally, such pieces are designed to embody the power or might of the person in whose image they were formed. Or sometimes to commemorate the dearly departed.

Hone your skills and excel here, and you may well be commissioned to create such a piece. But first, you must make your name more widely known by fashioning trinkets to endear yourself with the people.
Such as our fair Z'ssapa.
A piece made in the image of the miners, is it? Well, perhaps you had best visit Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern for some inspiration.
The miners can be a rough, crude, and vulgar crowd. Yet the Concern still plays host to some of the most beautiful women in all of Ul'dah.
There was a time when I did naught else but craft fineries for every woman I dared fall in love with, and more for all those who dared return my affections.

To this day, I oft wonder how many of them are still worn, still polished, still looked upon with longing eyes. And how many have simply been pawned at the Platinum Mirage for whatever coin they might fetch.
The miners, you say? Yes, well, visiting the Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern should give you a decent enough sense of who they are.
Now may be the ideal time to call upon them. I heard an enormous wealth of gold ore was just unearthed. I imagine they are all in quite high spirits.
Count yourself lucky that you were not here some ten years ago, to suffer the strife which engulfed Eshtaime's Aesthetics.
In our darkest hour, there was a very real danger that the Order of Nald'thal would seize our name and assets.
The flower-themed brooch that Colbernoux designed was [@1A(1)]truly[@1A(0)] breathtaking. An absolute masterpiece.
I have a sneaking suspicion that he was inspired by some fair lady, but such things are not easily asked.
There is an alehouse at the Mineral Concern. All the loveliest ladies of song and dance grace the stage there─though F'lhaminn is by far the most popular.
The woman herself is a jewel. It is only fitting that her heart be won over by a master jewelcrafter. Hahaha!
You want to use m-me for inspiration? A m-muse? But everyone s-says I am homely of face. And I'm b-barely abed before I'm abandoned, if you take my meaning, [@IF($E9(4),m-milady,m-milord)].
Your kindness has instilled new confidence in me. Perhaps I am not so grotesque after all. Yes, perhaps men wish to bed me because I am [@1A(1)]fair[@1A(0)] to look upon.
Well? Did you capture my beauty, love? Did I get your creative juices [@1A(1)]surging[@1A(0)]?
Might be that little sketch there'll make me a household name. Hah! Think of that!
Oh gods, no, F'lhaminn...
Remember what I have told you, friend. For the warriors, knowledge is a weapon. But for we crafters, knowledge is [@1A(1)]wealth[@1A(0)].

Remember, the mark of a true goldsmith is the ability to impose [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] will upon metal and stone. To do so, you must bind both hand and eye to your will, and let your imagination take full rein.
It is... It was broken... I...
Perhaps things are better this way. Perhaps it is a sign that it is time to move on. Nothing lasts forever...
<sigh> Nielle... I have no wish to suffer another loss such as that...
F'lhaminn has come to pay a visit. Have you seen her? It's obvious that Colbernoux is quite taken with her. It must be difficult for both of them, considering that she was his late brother's lover.

Things were different when Niellefresne was alive. Colbernoux lived in the shadow of his elder brother, as many second- and third-born sons do. But his talents have come to the fore in the wake of his brother's death.
As to whether or not he can win F'lhaminn's heart... Well, I should think that one respect in which he best [@1A(1)]not[@1A(0)] follow in his brother's footsteps.
But you do not come to me for such idle chatter. It is your reward which brings you, is it not? And so shall you have it. Here you are.

I welcome you to Eshtaime's Lapidaries, good [@IF($E9(4),lady,sir)], as would Eshtaime himself were he still for this world, and as would the lapidaries themselves were they not taken with task. And how fare you this [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),eve,morn)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),day,eve)])]?
Goldsmiths who can meet and surpass the expectations of our discerning clientele are few and far between. We are always in need of novices with the requisite potential.
Would you care to try your hand at our craft? You never know, perhaps Byregot has blessed you with a golden gift.
Join the Goldsmiths' Guild?
A most wise decision. I have a feeling in time we shall both profit greatly from it.

Accessories such as ours were once used in the thaumaturgical arts. Of course, they then became fashionable, their design more elaborate, and their price prohibitive to all but the colossally wealthy.

And so we expanded our services to include the crafting of bespoke pieces. Yet, in these troubled times, those seeking the thaumaturgical properties of our works have come to comprise the majority of our custom once again.

That is in part why we seek the aid of adventurers such as yourself. Your perspectives oft prove invaluable in bolstering the reputation of the Eshtaime name, not to mention expanding our client base.
But you must start with the fundamentals. Your mentor will be Colbernoux─a very talented man. Why, just recently he designed a series of brooches that were all the rage in the Fronds.
You can find Colbernoux just over there. Feel free to introduce yourself. But whatever you do, avoid mention of his brother...
I had thought you an aspiring goldsmith come to us from the countryside. But I see I was wrong...
It was wholly unfair of me to group you with the peasantry. A peasant, after all, would not be so unutterably lumpen as to refuse an opportunity to work under the Eshtaime name!
I had thought you an aspiring goldsmith come to us from the countryside. But I see I was wrong...
It was wholly unfair of me to group you with the peasantry. A peasant, after all, would not be so unutterably lumpen as to refuse an opportunity to work under the Eshtaime name!

Tell no one that you come from Eshtaime's Lapidaries.
Off to Gridania, are you? I can't say I've any love for that place in these old bones.
The folks there don't even believe in the realm of Thal, you know. Bloody barbarians! And just what the hells do they think happens when you die!?

Ul'dah is home to a whole [@1A(1)]society[@1A(0)] of wealthy collectors who seek out rare gems and jewelry just like [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000124,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000124,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].
That doesn't mean we should start churning them out, of course. No, no, quite the contrary. By lessening the number available, we raise the demand, and with it the price.
If this second issue is a success, there will be a mountain of coin to be had.
And we aren't the only ones with gil on our minds. Many Ul'dahns would be willing to plunge themselves into debt to acquire one, as such possessions have no taxes levied on them.
You are no stranger to Ul'dah's climate by now. You must see that it is nigh on impossible to grow flowers in this heat.
But in the climate and soils of the Black Shroud, flowers thrive even when neglected. The forestborn are fools not to exploit the realm's demand for them.
Considering how much gil they stand to make, what could possibly be stopping them?
Many in the guild were not pleased to hear that an adventurer would be assigned this task. Your reward will only serve to lessen our profits.
The botanists may give you a hard time, but do not make it easy for them. Allow those tree-lovers an ilm and they'll take a malm.
Leave. There are no flowers for you here. Take that bastard goldsmith at the inn with you and bugger off back to your sandy grave.
I'd take fighting an Ixal or Garlean over trading with a miner or goldsmith any day. I've no stomach for the greed and cunning of the Ul'dahns.
Put it back. Put it back this instant, kupo!
Are you looking for that man again? Colbernoux, was it?
Very well. I suppose there is no use in hiding it. I shall tell you where he is staying.
You've come to see Colbernoux? Very well, I shall summon him for you.

You found one! You found [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000123,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000123,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]! Oh, thank you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], thank you! With this, I can make one last brooch for F'lhaminn.
Please pay a visit to Eshtaime's Lapidaries when next you are in Ul'dah. I will contact Elecotte and see to it your efforts here are generously rewarded.
It is the least I can do. You see, it was because of me that the Growery decided to cease all trade with the goldsmiths.
It was I who ruined the bond of trust between our guilds─a bond that my brother worked so hard to forge...
My records show your [@1A(1)]acquaintance[@1A(0)] Colbernoux has already left us. He was bound for Ul'dah, if I recall. And seemed rather sad.
But he found no pity here. All who torment the elementals as the goldsmiths do deserve to have the flesh ripped from their bones! Raaawr!
It seems Colbernoux traveled to Gridania himself. I thought it a while since last I'd seen him.
I imagine his negotiations did not go well. He has always lacked the gift for words that his brother had. Small wonder he has such trouble with the ladyfolk.
Amazing! You were able to procure flowers from Gridania? Simply amazing!
Awww, just the one? Well, that will certainly serve to raise its value. Though I fear not much will be left after the cost of advertising.
How were you received by the Gridanians? We were rejected again, I assume?
They have seen their own share of adventurers and Ala Mhigans there of late. I only hope such outside influences bring about some change in the Black Shroud. Gods know it's long overdue.
You certainly look refreshed. The forest air did you some good, did it?

But what of the forest people? No doubt you found their, ahem, [@1A(1)]lifestyles[@1A(0)] to be in stark contrast to our own. You should visit Limsa next. Never will you meet such a herd of feckless fools as the Lominsans!
You have failed. The task was to procure ten blossoms, and you returned with but the one. Therefore, you failed.
And spare me your “I did my best” talk. Effort is nothing, results are everything. Profits are either made, or they are not.
Please pay a visit to Eshtaime's Lapidaries next time you are in Ul'dah. I will contact Elecotte and see to it your efforts here are generously rewarded.
Forgive me, I wasn't aware you were aiding Colbernoux in his work. Please, allow me to prepare a more fitting reward.
I heard from the others that you obtained only a single flower. Why not give it to someone you hold dear?
They may appreciate it so much they will grace Eshtaime's Aesthetics with their custom in the future. This is how coin is made, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], could I ask you to give this to F'lhaminn for me? I would do it myself, but it would only cause more rumors.
I suppose you have heard the whispers by now as well, yes? That I am in love with F'lhaminn?

I do not mean to deny it. If nothing else, the rumors have at least been a diversion. My father would see me wed the guild owner's daughter, but word of my love for F'lhaminn gave him pause. Needless to say, I have no intention of marrying to slake my father's thirst for vengeance.
Bah, forgive a fool his ramblings. The brooch─you will see it to F'lhaminn, yes? You will find her at the Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern.
Please, you must deliver the trinket I entrusted you with to F'lhaminn. It is for her and her alone.
It is all a humble fool such as myself can offer.
Thank you. A thousand times, thank you.
I shall wear it ever and always. Until the blossom within withers to naught but a memory.
There is a sadness about it, though, do you not think? For what does the wilting of a blossom signify if not the passing of time?
But Nielle would have wanted me to wear it─and Colbernoux still does. I take great comfort in such thoughts.
It cannot have been easy for him to craft this. No doubt the memory of his brother is still with him, wherever he turns. Perhaps it is time that he, too, moved on.
The march of time is a cruel thing. By demanding we forget, it forces us to remember.
I understand you mean well, but... Please, spare me your words.
I haven't the words to thank you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Here, I've taken the liberty of preparing your reward myself.
I pray the Weaver brings our fates together again sooner rather than later.

So good of you to come, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Rest assured, I would not have inconvenienced you were I not desperate. In fact, what I am about to ask of you would normally require the consent of Colbernoux...
...but I fear we are left with no other recourse. You must aid us, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Please say that you will.
It has been decided that a certain piece of jewelry will be reissued in the near future. Only a limited number will be made, to be sure.

It is known as F'lhaminn's Flower. Perhaps you've heard of it? At its center lies a perfect blossom, encased in glass using a secret method. Its stem, meanwhile, is wrought of exotic coral. And surrounding it all is a veritable sultana's ransom in stunning gems, fashioned in the likeness of flower petals.
The timeless, transcendent beauty of the piece swiftly caught the eye of the Ul'dahn elite, and it soon came to be coveted by the royal families of other nations as well.
It was, of course, Colbernoux's design. None can deny his virtuosity when it comes to goldsmithing. His talent is truly squandered mentoring novices like you─no offense.

To craft F'lhaminn's Flower, only the most freshly cut blossoms will suffice─and those can only be found in Gridania. As you can probably imagine, this is far from convenient, not least because the botanists of the Greatloam Growery have a history of being...less than accommodating.

Belligerent botanists besides, merely traversing the Black Shroud makes the journey a perilous undertaking. Naught to trouble an adventurer such as yourself, of course─and now you see why I have called you here.

I should think ten [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000123,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000123,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] will serve. But you must not mention the intended use. Nor that you are acting on behalf of the Goldsmiths' Guild.
I had thought you might be pleased to be called upon. Perhaps you would prefer to idle away your days at the beck and call of Colbernoux for a task that may never come?
A number of highly valuable goldsmithing materials are gathered here.
The bag already contains that material.
You place the material into the bag.
Now, as I think I mentioned, our owner Lord Lolorito is a Syndicate member─and not the sort of man anyone would want to steal from...

Yet it is he who is responsible for the safekeeping of the relic which was recently targeted─the relic in question being none other than the famed blade Heartstrike. ...Understandably, this has given us all [@1A(1)]great[@1A(0)] cause for concern.
And so we mean to conceal the [@1A(1)]true[@1A(0)] Heartstrike amid a number of duplicates.

You will not want for materials. All that you require can be found in the storerooms within. Procuring it should be as simple as notifying Sence of your needs─though she has been known to require “convincing,” from time to time.
The Eshtaime name has a long and proud history. And the same can be said of the owner's family.

It's no accident, either. Only the most talented goldsmiths are allowed to wed into the owner's house. Sadly, the current owner's granddaughter is so [@1A(1)]revolting[@1A(0)], he's had trouble finding suitors! Of course, you didn't hear that from me.
A goldsmith who doesn't know of Heartstrike is no goldsmith at all. They say that to make it one must put one's own life at risk.
Then again, the guild's histories state that the blade can only be made in a time of great war and strife...so the danger to one's life may be no more than that.
If you are one of us now, perhaps you should know that the last guildmaster angered the owner, and was swiftly deposed.
He was father to Niellefresne and Colbernoux, which makes the latter's staying on all the more interesting, if you ask me.
Lord Lolorito hires only the most accomplished pugilists from the Platinum Mirage to guard his private estate.
Which means the thieves who stole in without being caught must have been even more accomplished. Either that, or they were already intimately familiar with the place...

Who would wish to steal Heartstrike? All know it no longer possesses the magical properties it once did. And even if one [@1A(1)]did[@1A(0)] acquire it, it is far too well[@1F]known to draw coin on the open market.
To me, that makes those treasure-groping fiends of the Company of Heroes all the more suspect. Limsa is nothing if not a nation of lackwits and dullards.
I can't say I've seen you around before. Elecotte gave you leave to the storeroom, did she?
That is all well and good, but you'll need [@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] leave before you see a single rock. And I do not give it lightly.
These storerooms hold mere pebbles that are worth tens upon thousands of gil each. And ores, ingots, and gemstones besides. You must prove yourself trustworthy.
Well, you are a goldsmith, to be sure. And seem to be decent enough. You have your leave.
Gather whatever materials you need, put them in this bag, and then bring the lot back to me. If everything is in order, they will be yours to take.
Gather whatever materials you need, put them in this bag, and then bring the lot back to me. If everything is in order, they will be yours to take.
Well, you are a goldsmith, to be sure. And seem to be decent enough. You have your leave.
Gather whatever materials you need, put them in this bag, and then bring the lot back to me. If everything is in order, they will be yours to take.
Gather whatever materials you need, put them in this bag, and then bring the lot back to me. If everything is in order, they will be yours to take.
Is that [@1A(1)]all[@1A(0)] you require? Truly?
Let us have a look, then. Yes, there seem to be no problems here. Just be careful not to botch any syntheses.

If that is all, then I would appreciate it if you'd leave. I may seem to be unoccupied, but I can assure you that diligently watching over the storerooms and being unoccupied look almost identical to the untrained eye.

Some say we will never see the like of Colbernoux's brother again. Niellefresne's services were coveted by every self-respecting member of Ul'dah's ruling elite. He was without doubt the greatest goldsmith of his day.
But his life was taken in a dastardly act of murder─the assassin never found. For a time, Colbernoux himself was suspected... One can only imagine what he must have endured.
I never like to see Colbernoux visit his brother's grave alone. Erralig's Burial Chamber at the Arrzaneth Ossuary is such a...dark place.
