But his life was taken in a dastardly act of murder─the assassin never found. For a time, Colbernoux himself was suspected... One can only imagine what he must have endured.
I want nothing more than to send my brother's soul to the realm of Thal, where he might find peace. Yet I know not how. I am lost, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
It is all I can bear to stand here looking down at him. Gods, Nielle...
People are saying the thief that stole into Lord Lolorito's estate was a Roegadyn.
Plenty were suspecting Limsa as it was. And all know they have more Roegadyn than anywhere else.
The way I've heard it told, the full power of Heartstrike can only be coaxed forth by a master thaumaturge of the Order of Nald'thal.
But I've seldom found such rumors to be worth more than a mummer's fart.
You visited the grave of Niellefresne? Is it true what they say? That his body still looks as it did the day he died?
Then the power of Heartstrike [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] at work... I like it not. It is unnatural, such sorcery. A soul should cross over to the realm of Thal, and the body should wither proper.
I'd swear by the Twelve that I saw Greinfarr slinking among the alleys not long ago...
He was a close friend to Niellefresne, did you know? Heir to the seat of guildmaster at the Coliseum, he was. Of course, he left Ul'dah when Niellefresne was killed.
Our current guildmaster seems to be getting on well enough with the owner.
It was the previous guildmaster who caused all the trouble. They say he conspired with powers in the other nations to topple Lord Lolorito and take Eshtaime's for himself.
My thanks again, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], for your loyal service. Here, your payment.
I'm sorry, you must excuse me. I...I feel a sudden distemper. It will pass...yet grant me a few moments alone, I pray you.
To be a botanist is to know the Twelveswood in all its majesty. Anyone else is just a...well, gardener, really.
Go and speak to Cicely. She will guide you from here.
Off into the Twelveswood already? My only advice is this─eat before you go.
The only thing that angers the elementals more than stealing from the forest's larder is the incessant growling of an empty stomach.
I've been trying to school the children of Gridania to salute us botanists, as the children of Ishgard salute their knights.
But in the end they just snicker and jeer. <sigh> We truly are the most underappreciated guild.
Here at the Greatloam Growery, we also plant and nurture seeds not native to the Twelveswood.
No doubt we shall call upon your aid, should you remain with us long enough. But first you must learn, as must all botanists, that in the cultivation of plants lies the cultivation of the soul.
The weeds around Quarrymill are starting to get out of hand. The conjurers have requested that we come and clear them.
I can't be bothered to dirty my hands weeding. Think of it this way─twice the work will get you twice the thanks!
Oh, so Cicely can't be bothered with menial weeding anymore, can she?
Gods, she's a bloody blight, that one... Leave her to me and go on ahead. You should be able to find Quarrymill easily enough─just head south from town.
All of us here at the guild are a bit concerned by Cicely's dislike for Gridania.
But it's only natural for a young woman of her age to grow a bit restless. I myself feel the pangs of wanderlust from time to time.
Back from Quarrymill already? How went the grand weed purge? Plenty of spiny turnip leaves, I take it?
The grasses choking the hamlet are typically only found deep within the wood. But the seeds have been carried far and wide by a foul wind.
The wretched flying monstrosities of the Garleans are to blame. They swoop low over the Twelveswood, and disrupt the natural flow of air.
She may want nothing more than to leave the forest, but not even Cicely would malign the moogles.
What!? You overheard a moogle speaking ill of Cicely? I-I don't know what to say... I'm just going to pretend that I never heard that.
As well you should! The Twelveswood can be an unforgiving place to those who don't know what they're doing.

That's why we work closely with the moogles and conjurers. Only they can hear the voices of the elementals, and thence tell us how to best please them. We scratch their backs, and they scratch ours. We've even had botanists saved from certain death by the wood's elementals. Rarely, I admit, but it has happened.

To put it simply, we take what the wood gives us, not what we choose. We prune the branches no longer needed by the tree, the grasses that have grown to excess. Our main goal is to preserve the health of the wood. In return, we are rewarded with the wood's boon, which we distribute to all.

This may all be a touch confusing to one not yet intimate with the forest and its ways. Well, no amount of talking will convey something so profound. You'll just have to go and experience it for yourself. Are you up to it?
As well you should be! The sooner you pay your respect to the wood, the sooner the elementals will warm to you. You'll be able to meet some of the conjurers who aid in our cause, as well.
Go and speak to Cicely. She will guide you from here.
Come now, the title of “adventurer” demands you show a modicum of adventurousness. There is much you might learn from our ways.
Come now, the title of “adventurer” demands you show a modicum of adventurousness. There is much you might learn from our ways.
Remember, now, take the specimen to Frondale's Phrontistery in Ul'dah.
The alchemists will be able to find out if we can derive a more efficient, longer-burning oil from it.
Cicely has the specimen you will be taking. See her before you leave.
Cicely is ever sending flowers and letters and whatnot to a friend of hers in Ul'dah.
It's a shame to send flowers to somewhere so dry, though, if you ask me. Arid climates are terrible for flowers. And even more terrible for a lady's skin!
Tell me, do you think there are elementals even in the oils we burn? It stands to reason that there would be, but the conjurers never speak of elementals complaining about being set to flame.
I asked the young ones their thoughts on the matter, but they snickered and jeered.
I've seen countless plants since joining this guild─more than most people see in a lifetime. And still, not a day goes by without me being amazed by a new peculiarity of some sprout or blossom.
If you wish to excel as a botanist, take note of all you see at the Growery. The wisdom of generations of gifted botanists is at work here.
If you want your precious specimen, you'll have to do as I ask. Oh, I know it's devious, but what would you have me do?
I need to put [@1A(1)]something[@1A(0)] in my next letter.
Go and talk to the bard visiting at the Carline Canopy and see if she doesn't have some tidings from Ishgard or Limsa. And don't you dare come back with news about Ul'dah. That doesn't count.
<sigh> Yes, I suspected Cicely would refuse to hand the specimen over quietly. I had hoped an adventurer such as yourself would have stories enough to regale her with.
But I suppose you have been spending a bit too much time around here to have anything new to tell. Very well, do what you must.
Come, come, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)]! Don't be bashful, now. What's that? A song? Oh, nothing should please me more than to regale your fine self with a song, Azeyma as my witness.

But I've met so many people on me travels, and heard so many tales─'tis all a formless cloud in me brain. I need...something. A light to clear the fog. A compass to get me bearings by. A trinket from a far-off land, perhaps.

If only me voice could follow me thoughts. So many tales to tell, if only...if only... Oh, forgive a rambling bard, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)], me thoughts are so jumbled that the words won't come. Might you lend me a hand, then?
If only there were some spark to light the fire, a sign to show the way. A trinket from a far-off land, perhaps. An estimable heirloom, an arty artifact, a rare relic?
A trinket? I should have expected as much. Bards are such a greedy lot.
A far-off land, she said? Well then perhaps─
Oh, I don't relish parting with it, but if there is no other way...

No doubt you'll think me selfish, but if you would bring me [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000086,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000086,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] and [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000087,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000087,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], I [@1A(1)]suppose[@1A(0)] I could give you what you need. You will find them for me, won't you, [@SPLIT([@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], ,1)]? You simply must!
Why should I believe that you'll bother to bring the trinket back?

Hmmm, I suppose I could be convinced to entrust it to you for a bit...[@1A(1)]if[@1A(0)] you bring me [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000086,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000086,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] and [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000087,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000087,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].
This should do well enough. Take this, then, and hear all that you can from this bard!
Exquisite, isn't it? I came upon it in a traveling Lominsan merchant's wares and bought it at once. I've heard the dancers of Ul'dah use it to paint their skin.
Exquisite, isn't it? I came upon it in a traveling Lominsan merchant's wares and bought it at once. I've heard the dancers of Ul'dah use it to paint their skin.

Oh, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)]! This is precisely what I needed! Thank you, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)], a thousand times over! Ask what you will of this humble bard in return, and it shall be yours. Hm? A story? A small price to pay, indeed. Let me see...

How's this, then? The sailors of Limsa tell of a ship that sails their waters─a ship with no crew. Those few who've seen it by light of moon say the wood is barnacled and decayed beyond knowing. Cracks and gaping holes in the hull. Sails tattered and torn. More a shipwreck than a ship, with no godly business staying afloat.

But then, to those bold enough to board it, they say, the ship transforms before their very eyes. The greens and whites give way to the rich, brown sheen of new wood. The masts stand straight and the sails grow full. The brasses and bronzes shine blinding bright. In every way, the ship takes on its former glory, as new as the day she left the shipyard.

But then, at the very instant of this divine restoration, those on board simply vanish. Gone forever, never to be heard from or seen again. The Lominsans say they are taken by the ship, their souls consumed to keep her afloat, but who knows for sure? Be wary what ships you board, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)], should you find yourself in Limsa.
So, did you get your story?
Well, let's hear it! That damned bard hasn't sung a single song or told a single tale for any of us since she got here! No matter how many tankards of ale we buy her!
By the way, that item you were good enough to bring by─it's the stuff of pirates, it is. Don't know how you came to have it, but it's quite a find.

I'm relieved to have my [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000085,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000085,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] back. All that's left is to make sure that my letter gets to the Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern.
I just know my friend will be waiting for it to arrive. And thanks to you, it's my most interesting letter in months!
It amazes me that Cicely has been exchanging letters for so long. I'd run out of things to─
Well, I take that back. If it's food we were talking about, I suppose I could write a letter a day, at least.
Ul'dah? Bah, not to my liking. Nothing for free in Ul'dah. I hear the shopkeeps there charge you just for browsing!
And when children misbehave, their parents threaten them with “Gridanian” pocket gil! As if we were somehow ungenerous!
The Growery's flowers often end up at market in Ul'dah. Not as much as they used to, though.
Our ties with Eshtaime's Lapidaries were once quite strong. They've a real eye for beauty, those goldsmiths.
A letter? Hmmm... It bears no name. That was careless of someone.
I'm sorry, but I cannot in good conscience accept this letter. The Concern will not be made responsible for the oversights of others.
Greetings, and welcome to Frondale's Phrontistery. How may I direct you?
The laboratory? Ah, yes, yes. You must be the botanist from Greatloam Growery. We've been expecting you. I have been given permission to see to the handling of the plant specimen. If I may?

Everything looks to be in order. I'm pleased to report our studies into this new oil derivative are progressing well. Still, the alchemists are doubtful their experiments will yield a fuel anywhere near as efficient as the ceruleum harvested here in Ul'dah.

But don't merely take my word for it. We propose a demonstration to help persuade your superiors. I'm sure the miners at Amajina & Sons would be willing to part with a small sample. Mention that Nogeloix sent you.
Our tests have yielded nothing that even approaches the power and efficiency of Ul'dah's native ceruleum.
Pay a visit to the Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern and tell them Nogeloix sent you. They should be able to spare a small sample for you to take back to Gridania.
I pray the Twelve grant Nenekko many more years of correspondence with her Gridanian friend.
Did you find Ul'dah to your liking? I hear the bright lights are breathtaking at night, and the city itself never sleeps!
Still, that dry air can't possibly be good for a lady's skin. You'll not see me there unless the climate changes─as if [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] were possible!
I wager some of the more persistent merchants tried to force their needless trinkets on you, no?
Most Ul'dahns are merchants the instant they leave the womb. Selling wares comes as naturally to them as breathing their filthy air.
Ceruleum? Yes, I've heard of it. Some sort of oil, if I recall. Mined in the mountains north of Ul'dah.
Brother Telent of the conjurers says no elementals reside in the stuff. They now think it is most likely produced from the remains of ancient life, long dead.
Perhaps you've come to appreciate what it is we do here at the Greatloam Growery. The cultivation of plants, the harvesting of their bounty, and the careful use of every last morsel.
What is the first use that comes to mind when you think of plants, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? Food, I suspect? Medicine, perhaps?
Essential, to be sure, but only a fraction of what plants are capable of providing. Were you aware that we procure oil from the wood's vegetation as well?

Have you ever wandered Gridania on a starless, moonless night? All is pitch-black, and the darkness so thick it is almost tangible. Our patrols require light, and so we draw what oil we can from the plants, though it is less than ideal as a fuel.

We have been in talks with the alchemists of Ul'dah about developing a new oil. I need someone trustworthy to act as an envoy in this endeavor. And I would like it to be you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Excellent! That's the adventuring spirit I was looking for! Are you familiar with the way? The Lumberline runs south from Gridania. You need only follow it.
Before long, the trees will give way to a vast, barren desert. Even if you don't see Ul'dah immediately, you'll almost certainly hear it─or smell it.

Frondale's Phrontistery is where you'll find the alchemists. I'd like you to deliver to them a plant specimen and report back on their latest findings. I've had Cicely prepare the package you will be taking. Go and see her before you leave.
So the forest has grown on you as well, has it? I understand your reluctance to leave. Still, when duty calls, some sacrifices must be made.

Rychyld may be a conjurer, and a high-ranking one at that, but don't let mention of her office intimidate you. She's as friendly a Hyur as you're like to meet. Our relations with the conjurers are crucial to our livelihood, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Please do all in your power to help her.
Sister Rychyld is powerful, to be sure, but there are many evils in the wood─and more in the world at large. I hope that you will prove a useful ally to her.
Why, hello there, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. If it's Sister Rychyld you are looking for, she was outside just now, I think.
She is versed in mooglespeak, trusted by all...and so beautiful that she would turn heads even in Ul'dah.
Sister Rychyld and Brother Telent are the conjurers assigned to the Greatloam Growery.
Without them, we would have no idea what the elementals in the forest around us were feeling. They say Brother Telent hears them better than any.
There was one among us who could hear the voices in the rocks and soil. But he left without so much as a goodbye some time ago.
I've heard tales... There are some in Ul'dah, they say, who commune with the dead. Is it true?
Sadly, word has gone beyond the Twelveswood of the moogles and their dances─of their powers to bring the rain.
I only pray that word does not travel as far as Ul'dah. A greedy nation plagued by droughts would no doubt attempt to take such power for its own.
I'm told you have spoken with Sister Rychyld. She entrusted you with a task, yes? I suspected as much. She was in council with Cicely for quite some time.
The flower beds south of Camp Crimson Bark? I see. Are you familiar with the way? If not, you should have no trouble finding it with that map of yours.
The flower beds? Those of the moogles?
Hm? Oh, it's nothing, really. Your task doesn't concern me, after all. Do as you will.
Go on, don't worry. We have the moogles' leave to gather seeds here. But take only as many as you need, no more.
Did Cicely not go with you? <sigh> She can certainly be less than helpful at times. Did all go well with Rychyld?
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], you're back! Were you able to gather the seeds?
Superb! Now, you must plant them, and care for them from sprout till blossom. This particular flower is very temperamental, so you'll have to keep a constant eye on them. And─
Well, never mind about that.
Once they begin to blossom, we will replant them in the wild. So bring them back here when they are ready.
They must be planted in the soil quickly once they blossom. Bring them back as soon as they are ready.
Seeds can be cultivated wherever there is soil. And if there is no soil, well...a good botanist finds a way.
Are you actually going to grow those seeds? But that means you'll have to use... Oh gods. Stay away from me. It takes weeks to get the smell off.
You look troubled, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. What is it?
Oh dear, I would like to help, but... I... The stars! Yes, the stars. They have, uh...ordained that Humblehearth is very ill-fated for me today.
Well, what are you playing at? Are you trying to grow those seeds from your hands?
If you don't know what to do with them, ask Opyltyl.
Gods be good, you're a botanist now, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]. What do you mean you don't know how to plant seeds!?
I apologize. I suppose it is to be expected. You have yet to work the soil.
Very well. I will help you as far as I am able. First, we must know what plant we are dealing with. What type of seeds have you gathered?
Ahhh, these... Cicely is quite gifted at growing these herself. But I fear they may prove quite difficult for a newcomer.
And the fertilizer... You will have to obtain the fertilizer.
Beasts known as yarzons lurk near Humblehearth. It is their dung you must procure. They're dangerous things, but nothing you can't handle, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
The dung of the yarzons near Humblehearth stinks to the high hells, to be sure. But without it, you have no hope of growing your plants.
We have a saying when it comes to growing roses─the ranker the shite, the sweeter the sight. Good luck to you.
Well, well, well. I don't envy you.
Nasty stuff, that yarzon dung. The smell seeps into the pores and clings to you for [@1A(1)]weeks[@1A(0)].
You adventurers do a great service to our guild. A garden botanist wouldn't stand a chance against an angry yarzon.
Do be careful, though. Even if they appear to be sleeping, those sensitive legs of theirs can detect the slightest vibrations in the ground around them.
Yarzon dung? That can't be right. Opyltyl must be misinformed.
If anyone were to use that stuff, they'd have Cicely to answer to. The girl can't [@1A(1)]stand[@1A(0)] the smell of the stuff.
Gods be good, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]! How much of the stuff did you bring!?
Come and see! The seeds have budded while you were away.
All that remains is to work this stuff into the soil. Once that's done, we should be seeing blossoms in no time!
I cannot for the life of me work out how Cicely grows these. Given her enthusiastic hatred of dirt, the thought of her handling dung seems...unlikely.
Have you chanced to speak to Cicely, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? You will find her here now, if you wish to do so.
Wh-What are you looking at? I was just tending to the flowers is all. What!?

So, Opyltyl means to [@1A(1)]help[@1A(0)] with [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000123,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000123,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], does he? Don't tell me he means to use that wretched-smelling fertilizer.
Oh well, I don't suppose it matters. Run along and fetch the sprouts from Opyltyl, then.
Come now, there is no time to waste. You must go and see Opyltyl to obtain the sprouts we need. Try not to bring back anything [@1A(1)]too[@1A(0)] foul-smelling.
Ah, there you are! Yeees, I gave these sprouts a healthy dose of fertilizer. They're blooming beautifully, don't you think?
I bet Cicely will resent hearing that. She's not the only botanist with a knack for growing temperamental flowers.
Well done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Growing those flowers is no simple task. Thank you so much for your help!
It would not have been possible had you not brought back the yarzon dung.
Cicely [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)] have another method of growing them. She would never touch that stuff!
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]... They're absolutely beautiful! Thank you...thank you.
Ugh, but they still smell of shite.
Knowing Sister Rychyld, she's already waiting at the place I've marked on your map. Hurry now, and deliver the flowers to her.
Ah, what fortuitous timing. I was just about to contact you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

It seems some moogles were attacked in the wood...again. By whom or by what I cannot say. Sister Rychyld from the Conjurers' Guild is here now. She has been a friend to us for many years. A good woman, trustworthy.

All guilds in Gridania have a conjurer in their service. It's not like we can stroll about cutting down trees and plucking flowers as we see fit. We must have the elementals' consent. And to that end, we need the conjurers. No others are able to commune with the elementals.
Anyway, Sister Rychyld has requested that one of our number assist her with her investigation, and I can think of none better suited to the task than you. Go on, now, and learn what you can from her.

Rychyld may be a conjurer, and a high-ranking one at that, but don't let mention of her office intimidate you. She's as friendly a Hyur as you're like to meet. Our relations with the conjurers are crucial to our livelihood, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Please do all in your power to help her.
Sheepish around conjurers, are you? Gods, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], is there anything that [@1A(1)]doesn't[@1A(0)] scare you?
Go and speak with J'moldva. You will find her within.
She's been looking for some fresh meat to throw at the drudge work. You couldn't have come along at a better time.
Greetings, Wailer, and welcome. It is always good to have a new spear join our cause.
Our code is one founded on peace─peace for the forest, and peace for our people. That is why we fight.
You've witnessed the carefree manner of the Gridanians, yes? It is the result of the peace we Wailers keep.

This is my polearm. There are many like it, but this one is mine. My polearm is my best friend. It is my life. I must master it as I master life. My polearm, without me, is useless. Without my polearm, I am useless.
A skilled lancer always keeps the opponent guessing─if they expect an attack at range, close the distance and strike. If they are prepared for a thrust, swing instead.
The polearm is a versatile weapon. You will quickly learn to wield it, but it will take you a lifetime to master. Luck be with you, Wailer.
It's awful decent of J'moldva to train the likes of us.
She ought to be one of the Wailers' elite by now. It hurts my head to wonder why she contents herself with drilling.
I've heard some of the others say J'moldva doesn't get on well with Swethyna, one of our superiors.
They also say she's not forestborn. I somehow doubt those two things are unrelated.
The botanists at the Greatloam Growery have requested our aid in handling a pest problem.
I've marked the infested zones on your map. Watch yourself out there, Wailer.
When the rains come to Lifemend Stump, it becomes the perfect breeding ground for chigoes.
The conjurers are too busy to hold your hand through a pest hunt. But you needn't worry─the elementals have given their consent.
The vermin themselves are the least of your concerns. You see, when they gather in numbers, the hum of their wings attracts their natural predators...
Don't get reckless. The Wailers won't last long if our recruits start dying on their first ranging.
You may be new, but you are expected to observe the same regulations as all the Wailers. These pests shouldn't give you any trouble, but see to it you do nothing to shame the guild.
How did you fare, [@STRING($EB(1))]? J'moldva awaits you within.
A beautiful assortment of fruits just arrived from the Greatloam Growery.
It is always good to know our efforts are appreciated. Do not forget to take the time to appreciate such kindnesses.
Don't tell me some elemental appeared and sent you running back here with your tail between your legs.
A moogle!? The Twelve must be smiling on you, friend. There's no better omen around these parts.
So you ran into some trouble, did you? Aye, things are never easy in the Twelveswood. And that's not the last we'll see of those troublesome little buggers, either.
Still, you have succeeded in your first task. That alone speaks volumes. We may make a Wailer of you yet!
Never would I have expected the chigoe population to reach such numbers. J'moldva was right to be concerned.
You're a lucky one. Ain't every day J'moldva praises a new recruit. Hells, she ain't never so much as [@1A(1)]spat[@1A(0)] on me.
Remember, the elementals never claimed to give a shite about what we think or feel. Don't start hating them just because you were attacked.
Your payment ought to cheer you up. Go and see Willelda.
Not bad for your first ranging, [@STRING($EB(1))]. Here─your payment in full.
You are now a true Wood Wailer, in deed as well as name.
Know that we may never fully discharge ourselves of our duty to Gridania─and that you will soon be called upon again.
The Wood Wailers serve only true forestborn.
What business brings you? Speak quickly or begone.
Enlist in the Lancers' Guild?
Very well. I shall see to it the registrar is notified. But first, you should know who we are.
We Wood Wailers are the hands of Gridania─the agents of her people's will.
We are the eyes of the Twelveswood─keepers of her peace and protectors of her sanctity.
Harmony in the forest and peace in our nation are one and the same. Only through the efforts of all Gridanians can both be maintained.
From this day forth, you are one of us, Wailer. Are you prepared to accept your first duty?
Good. Go and speak with J'moldva. You will find her within.
Your wail is little more than a whine. Waste no more of my time.
Come back when you are prepared to earn the title you have chosen.
If that is your choice, I am not one to suggest you act otherwise.
What are you jawing at me for? It's J'moldva who sent for you. You know where to find her.
The Lumberline shouldn't prove too daunting for an adventurer like you. Take it straight out of the wood, and then straight to Ul'dah.
Any fool with a map can see the path the Garleans must march to conquer this realm. We will not suffer Gridania to fall as Ala Mhigo did.
An alliance with Ul'dah must be forged before it is too late. We believe our best hope lies at the Platinum Mirage.
The Pugilists' Guild there is known to employ a great many Ala Mhigan refugees. You must find one among them who will rally Ul'dah to our cause!
J'moldva may well be placing the fate of Gridania in your hands. She has a good deal more faith in you than I.
The journey to Ul'dah is long, but straightforward. You need do no more than take the Lumberline south out of the wood. Mind the sun─it claims more lives than aught else in those damnable wastes.
They don't give me none of them talking jobs, seeing as how I ain't too bright. But I'm the strongest Wailer going. And if you ain't strong, ain't nobody gonna listen anyway.
Rallying additional support [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)] is of the utmost importance if we are to repel the Garleans.
I myself would like to help, but our enemies are not limited to the Empire. The beast tribes, too, harass our borders at home. I am needed here.
Our resources are sorely stretched simply patrolling the wood. Were it not for adventurers such as yourself taking up our banners... Well, it does not bear thinking about.
We Wailers see to diplomatic exchanges more often than you would think.
Since the fall of Ala Mhigo, our political ties are more important than ever. Without exaggeration, our ability to call upon the aid of the other nations may ultimately prove our salvation.
The Platinum Mirage? Watch yourself─those fiends hold nothing sacred. They'll empty your pockets, pick the hairs off your arse, and leave you in the gutter, naked as your nameday.
And gods, whatever you do, don't let one of them goad you into a fistfight.
They say the owner of the Platinum Mirage is one of the most influential people in Ul'dah.
An ally like that could do much to bolster our war efforts.
See to it you fulfill your duties, Wailer. I'd best not hear you're down there merrily pissin' coin away at the tables.
I have seen the horrors this war wrought on my homeland of Ala Mhigo firsthand. I would not wish such a fate on Gridania, Ul'dah, or any other nation.
But you waste your time seeking aid here. The Ul'dahns will greet you as a friend with one hand and stab you in the back with the other.
Unless the sultana decrees it, the pugilists will never mobilize. Your friends in Gridania must rethink their approach. Ul'dah will not heed your call.

You've got gumption─I'll give you that. It's no easy task to come in here on behalf of the lancers seeking aid. Perhaps you were unaware, but most Ul'dahns are of the mind that Gridanians can't be bothered to see to the safety of our merchants and traders traveling through the Black Shroud.

I'm a moral man, so I'll not speak ill of other nations, but you'd do well to know just how the outside perceives of the Gridanians and their precious forest. You need hardly take my word for it─simply ask around.
You forget where you are, stranger. I doubt your meager coin would delay my ear long enough to hear you out.
Five million gil for the privilege of asking. Once I hear what you have to say, then we can settle on a real price.

Gridania? <spit> You got any idea how many times we been attacked in that damn wood? The merchants we escort lose faith with every delayed or damaged shipment. Your Black Shroud has cost us no small sum of gil.
You got something to ask, you see to it our trade routes are safe first. And when I'm back in profit, I just might hear you out.

It's all that greenwrath talk what scares me. So much as look at an elemental funny, an' the wood swallows you up, they say. Don't kill you, but don't leave you livin' neither. Just lost in there─forever.
I don't mind gettin' lost every now and then, but an eternity of it? Damned if I'm going anywhere near them bloody trees.
You must be spending a lot of time up in Gridania. What makes you so sure the elementals won't claim you?
I'm sick to death of all this wildling talk. Forest gods, spirits, elementals─whatever the hells they say it is. Bollocks! It's just you bloody Gridanians kidnapping folk!
I'd wager the tip of my tail your lot are ambushing the coaches and making off with the goods. That's what I'd be doing, anyway─except I'd be cat enough to own up.
I'm a proud citizen of Ala Mhigo, and there is naught but hatred in my heart for the imperial scum who laid ruin to my home.
But I am nothing here. A newcome pugilist, that is all. I have no rights and no voice. I fear I have no strength to lend you.
Near all here have naught but gil on their minds. Even under the threat of war with Garlemald, they will look first to where the profit lies.
Welcome back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. J'moldva wishes to see you right away. You know where to find her, I trust?
Glad to be back? Looks as though you got a little sun down there.
So there [@1A(1)]are[@1A(0)] those among the Ul'dahns who fear the elementals.
As well they should. Many in Eorzea still refuse to believe they even exist. And the relations between our nations are the worse for it.
How did you fancy the people of the Platinum Mirage? I imagine them all to be glum of face and hunched over piles of money, counting away.
A tax for simply speaking to someone!? I'd not yet heard that one. Only in Ul'dah...
The owners of Ul'dah's most influential institutions form the Syndicate. Six seats, there are, and all know that it is they who wield true power─not the sultana.
Our own Seedseers are three in number, but six leaders is a bit much, do you not think?
Tell it true─you never even made it past the entrance to the Platinum Mirage, did you?
Hmmm... Then perhaps the rumors were false. I'd heard it told that the owner's bigot of a son wouldn't suffer adventurers on the premises.
Aye, I'll fight the bloody Empire. And why the hells not? Am I to run again should they siege Ul'dah? Where is left for me after every nation falls?

Had a chance to weigh the public opinion on Gridania by now? I wager it's not the warmest talk you've ever heard. You'll find many Ul'dahns of the mind that Gridanians are in sore need of a good conquering─haughty as they are.
But tell your leaders this. We Ul'dahns are people of action─and as good as our word. Should the Shroud be made safe for passing merchants, you will have our aid in the war against Garlemald.
You will find the merchant caravan on the road to the south, beyond the wood's edge.
Guide them to Gridania, and see to it they meet no harm!
It is not unusual for the elementals to be hostile towards those from beyond the forest. They bring evils in with them more often than not.
But this time we must lend our aid. The alliance must be forged. Make your way to the merchant caravan. I will contact Sister Challinie of the conjurers.
Being threatened by the wood can prove a terrifying experience─all the more so for those who have spent a lifetime doubting the elementals' existence.
In their panic, they usually commit some folly that proves to be their end. But this alone does not slake the greenwrath's thirst for vengeance.
The enraged elementals often command great beasts to be the instruments of their destruction─such as the treants.
More than once, their fury has brought them close to our city. At such times, the might of the Wood Wailers is our only hope.
Word has been sent to all Wood Wailers ranging in the forest.
Some among them are making for the caravan now, but if it is elementals that must be dealt with, we will need the conjurers as well.
I'm only saying this because it's what everybody is thinking...
But what in the bloody hells did those godsdamned Ul'dahns go and do now!?
What do you make of those merchants? I can't put my finger on what, but [@1A(1)]something's[@1A(0)] not quite right... You'd think they'd be glad to have been rescued, but they seem...disappointed.
Well done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I am told that you fought bravely to protect the merchants' caravan from a pack of raging beasts.
They are extremely grateful for your service. You should go and look in on them.
Something ain't right... Caravan's cargo was empty, mostly. But to come all this way, they musta been hauling [@1A(1)]something[@1A(0)].
Fortunately, the unconscious moogle's wounds do not appear to be grievous. We have left it in the care of the conjurers.
They have set about calming the elementals, as well. Trade may be vital, but our ties with the forest take precedence over those with other nations.
If you're looking for the merchants, you'll find them there. It seems their cargo was undamaged. Hopefully relations with Ul'dah will not suffer.
One of those sent to guard the caravan was a pugilist of the Platinum Mirage...
No doubt he'll blacken the name of the Twelveswood upon his return to Ul'dah.
A Garlean airship? With that bearing, it is like to have been heading from Ala Mhigo to Silvertear Falls.
The elementals become enraged whenever those monstrosities fly over the Twelveswood, as do the beasts. Something must be done...
We save them from certain death, bring them into our homes, even make them tea─and this is the thanks we get? What passes for manners in Ul'dah?
I heard some talk about dropped cargo and lost profits. Damn ingrates! They don't bother to think of what it cost us to save them.

Ah, the good [@IF($E9(4),lady,fellow)] from the Wood Wailers! A thousand thank-yous for coming to our aid. Through your bravery, our cargo made it through unscathed, and we will soon be able to conclude our business here as planned.
It seems we must add “escort” to your list of talents, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Best go and make a full report to J'moldva.
Bugger this! I took this job because I heard escorting paid well. I didn't sign up for [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)]!
My grudge isn't with you, Wailer. You fought well, and have my thanks for it.
If nothing else, I've seen some exotic wildlife and enjoyed some foreign foods.
My employer is not dead, and I expect to receive payment in full. The gods are good, are they not?
Who, me? I'm fine. I don't believe in those children's stories about elementals, anyway.
We've come through this ordeal unscathed, have we not? All this talk of greenwrath and wildlings is the stuff of faerie tales.
I've always thought this land to be a terrifying one, fraught with danger. But the Gridanians bear a love for it unlike any I have ever seen.
Twelve bless you! How about we put this unfortunate incident behind us, yes? There are still shipments to be made!
Yes, the conjurers have reported that the moogle's wounds were slight. The caravan and their cargo are safe─all told, things could have been worse.
Well done, Wailer. You've done Gridania and Ul'dah both a great service. See Willelda for your reward. Dismissed.
The caravan has already set out for home. I have my doubts as to whether they will make it out of the wood in one piece, though.
I saw naught in their faces nor heard aught in their words to suggest they might have learned anything from the likely consequences of their irreverence.
Well, this was no mere pest hunt. You may well have saved our relations with Ul'dah from disaster, if not improved them.
Here's your reward, in full. You've earned it, Wailer.
You spoke the words, Wailer. Your life for Gridania.
Now is the time to make good on your oath. Go and speak to J'moldva.
The moogle you rescued has returned to the forest in full health. Thank the gods for that. There's no telling how the elementals would react were a moogle to come to harm.
Well if it isn't the burgeoning diplomat who found our friend at the Platinum Mirage. Rumor is, your man was exiled from Ul'dah under trumped-up charges of warmongering.
Hope for Ul'dah's strength is all but lost now. Perhaps it is time we explored our options elsewhere.
They got me escortin' the next caravan in from Ul'dah. Might be this is just the chance I been waitin' for to make J'moldva proud.
Have you heard what good came of our diplomatic talks with Ul'dah? J'moldva saw to it that word went around. No doubt to give us a kick up the arse.
I cannot imagine how we're ever going to prick the Ul'dahns into action. But their strength is too great to ignore.
If trade improves and their profits swell, then maybe... But what really needs to change is their perception of us. We want to be comrades, not customers.
What if the Empire descends on both our nations before our talks bear fruit? That's the thought that has me up nights.
The others will see to it the imperials are stopped. Leave the Hedge to them.
You must do as J'moldva orders and protect the Ul'dahn caravan. Head south and find them, quickly!
Not now! I must get word to the others.
<sigh> The gods must wish us dead for it to come to this again.
Now that was a sight I will remember all my days! Well worth a brush with death.
<sneeze> H-Hells take the elementals. <sneeze> Th-The pollen'll kill me afore aught e-else does! <sneeze>
You are bold to oppose the elementals so openly. Tell me, does the woodsin not daunt you? Do you not fear the greenwrath?
Considering the peril you've placed yourself in, nothing would please me more than to present you with a Wailer's mask. Yet I fear we cannot... I am deeply sorry, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
The wood was well pissed off. Proper seethin', in fact. Don't add up, if you ask me. Them merchants must've done something─they just ain't owning up to it.
I am relieved to hear that all of the cargo has been accounted for.
Your deeds will be known in Ul'dah, of that have no doubt. I shall shout it from the rooftops for the entire city to hear─all trade is safe, so long as the Wailers have the watch!
Come, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Let us return.
Word has come from Ul'dah. The caravan has returned safely.
What's more, J'moldva and the others were able to track the imperials and flush them from the wood.
I done failed again... I just wanted to show J'moldva I wasn't as dumb as everyone thinks. But I... I messed things up real good. Dropped my spear [@1A(1)]and[@1A(0)] got lost...
The Wailers and the conjurers found and dispatched the imperial interlopers almost immediately. Some may call our guilds humble, but when we move in unison, we are a force to be feared.
Thrice-damned Garleans! Rhalgr take their multitudes and their mechanical monstrosities! Hear this!
No fire nor blade shall harm this wood so long as we draw breath!
You there, Wailer. You are the one who saved the Ul'dahn caravan on its journey into Gridania, are you not?

Then I commend you. Your deeds have no doubt helped to strengthen our bonds with the southrons. What's this? Sour to have missed a chance to fight the Empire, are you? Hah! Do not grieve─that day will come soon enough.
Here, as in Ul'dah, we too harbor our share of Ala Mhigan refugees.
I cannot imagine what horrors they've seen. It pains the heart... Such a fate will not befall Gridania. We [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)] rally the aid of the other nations.

To a moogle, Garlemald and Ul'dah are equal evils─as are any with no love for the wood. To us? Different evils, to be sure. But Ul'dah does not pose the threat to our way of life that the Garleans do.
Thank you again for your assistance. We will take our leave of you now. May Nald'thal smile on our future dealings as well!
The road to unity will only prove more difficult from here. But we must not waver.
I foresee that I will have yet more to request of you, [@SPLIT([@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], ,1)].
Ul'dahn merchants and imperial interlopers─the Wood Wailers are needed now more than ever.
Amid all the fighting, one can lose sight of the peace we are fighting for. I'm a simple woman, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], but don't think the irony lost on me.
Again, your contributions have been significant. Take this, Wailer. You've earned it.
For Gridania, always.
You've done well enough up till now, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I daresay you're coming along quite nicely.
But skill alone did not win the Wood Wailers the people's trust. And skill alone will not ensure our survival.
Tell me true, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], would you give your life in the defense of Gridania?
Then you are ready. J'moldva has words for you. She awaits you within.
Bah, run along and enjoy your purposeless adventures. Come back to me when you are ready to risk all for a worthy cause.
<moan>
<groan>
The two seem to be breathing...

text_en: Your life is forfeit should you wander long about the deep wood.
I daresay you still have much to learn before you might justly claim the title of adventurer. Count yourself lucky we Wood Wailers came when we did.

Is that...[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000088,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000088,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]? But that would mean... Did you come across a treant!?
Saved by moogles? To even see a moogle in one's lifetime is rare enough, but to be [@1A(1)]saved[@1A(0)] by a [@1A(1)]pack[@1A(0)] of them? Not many can make such a boast.
Did you see the darkened skies? The streaking lights and the falling comets? I know not what to make of it all...
The two outsiders?

If they are outsiders, I imagine they have made for the Adventurers' Guild. But that is just my guess. The Carline Canopy, it's called. To reach it, you need only take this path. You should pay a visit yourself, if you've not yet been.
Welcome to Gridania. You have undergone much to come this far. Passing through the forest when the elementals are angered is no easy thing.
I will delay you no longer. You must be weary. I urge you to visit our Adventurers' Guild, the Carline Canopy. Perhaps you will find some respite there.

text_en: So, did you make it to Camp Bentbranch without losing your way?
Good. Any adventurer fixing to stay long in the wood should take the time to attune with the camp's aetheryte. Neglect to do that, and you're guaranteed to lose more than just your way out there.
I slipped a little something special into your bag for you, as well. Did you happen to notice it?
It's called a guildleve. The aetheryte throughout the land, and the camps built around them, are the keys to unlocking it and others like it.
That one's just a trivial task. It's up to you whether or not to accept it. Either way, feel free to come back to the Canopy here as often as you like, alright?
So, did you make it to Camp Bentbranch without losing your way?
Good. Any adventurer fixing to stay long in the wood should take the time to attune with the camp's aetheryte. Neglect to do that, and you're guaranteed to lose more than just your way out there.
I trust you can handle things on your own from here. Feel free to come back to the Canopy as often as you like, alright?

Why the moogles would want to help a complete stranger like you is beyond me. Got me wondering if you might not be one of these [@1A(1)]forest-beckoned souls[@1A(0)] the conjurers are always on about.
Ah, you must be the poor soul Fufucha has running all over creation. Come, allow me to guide you to the flower beds.
Understand that we do not wish to see you made the scapegoat in all of this. We seek only to find the perpetrator as swiftly as possible.
For their own safety, as well as ours.

Instances are special areas that are entered upon fulfilling certain requirements, such as progressing in a quest. There will always be a message telling you when you have entered an instance, and your minimap will show its boundaries.
Most instances can be left by crossing those boundaries; however, there are some, such as this one, in which certain objectives must be met before you are allowed to exit.
Impurity's as bad as a curse, I tell ye. Gotta get all them dirty deeds off yer back, else the elementals'll get ye.
I didn't believe it, neither─till some of me own mates were taken right before me eyes. Poor bastards.
You would do well to fear the Twelveswood─and live in awe of it. It is as integral to us Gridanians as the sun and the moons.
She demands your due respect. Never attempt to oppose her, for she is alive and she never forgets.
If you are planning to stay a while, you might want to learn a bit about the elementals.
They reside within all creation, and are the organizing principle at work throughout the world.
The ancient elementals of the Twelveswood are much more powerful and wise than those from other parts of the world.

They are blessed with insight far beyond even the most gifted of mortals, and possess a knowledge more primeval and encompassing than we shall ever know. But such gifts bring with them great responsibility.
You met a moogle!? Well, count yourself among the lucky ones. I haven't even [@1A(1)]seen[@1A(0)] one in gods know how many years!

You spoke to it!? Oh, come on, that's just not fair. I've heard of conjurers who have trained for [@1A(1)]decades[@1A(0)] and still couldn't communicate with them. What did [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] do to deserve such luck!?
As if the breaking of the Hedge wasn't enough, it seems an airship crashed in the forest as well.
Most able-bodied adventurers are deep in the wood now, helping the Gods' Quiver and Wood Wailers survey the wreckage.
In Gridania, there live a chosen few who are blessed by the forest. They are known as the Padjal.
The touch of the elementals causes horns to sprout from their heads. They are an ageless kind, fluent in the tongue of the forest. It is the stuff of faerie tales, no?
The Twelveswood is a sacred place, and runs thicker and deeper than you can imagine. Before entering you had best hear what Mother Miounne would tell you. For your own good, as well as the forest's.
You receive a linkpearl from Miounne.
Linkpearls are a quick and convenient way to communicate with others across Eorzea, no matter where they be.
The NPC linkpearl icon will appear in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]micro menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] when an NPC wishes to contact you.

Open the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] and select NPC Linkpearls to hear what Miounne has to say. The linkpearl message will be displayed in the log.
If you feel the need to ease the burden of getting around, I suggest attuning yourself to the aetheryte at Camp Bentbranch.
Bentbranch is the closest camp to Gridania. You should be able to make it there safely, even if the greenwrath is on you.
How do you get out of the city? If you fancy braving it, there's the eastern path, I suppose.
Well, look who it is! Last Mother heard, the greenwrath was after you something fierce. Been so long, I made you for dead.
But it is good to see you returned safely. I pray you learned something of the forest on your outing to Camp Bentbranch.
By the by, whilst you were gallivanting about the forest, I paid the conjurers a visit. Aye, and asked about the purification rites needed to cleanse the greenwrath from you.
It'd completely slipped my mind, but a great festival is to be held soon. The proper rites will take place then, and you'll be welcome to partake.
Oh, and a dance is involved. You'll need to ask at Stillglade Fane if you'd like to learn it. And mind your manners over there─the conjurers don't take kindly to tomfoolery.

And you might want to think about taking that [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000088,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000088,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] over to Atelier Fen[@1F]Yll. They use those things all the time for repairing airships and whatnot.
Both are recognized guilds, and you're welcome to lay your loyalties wherever you like. Here, let's see that map of yours.
You'll have to go to Stillglade Fane to see about the purification rite. The conjurers will see to it your woodsin is cleansed. That will get the greenwrath off of you.

But it's the Fen[@1F]Yll leatherworkers who'll be interested in that [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000088,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000088,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. I've marked the Atelier on your map. Should be easy enough to find.
Oh, and don't assume all Gridanians to be as nice as me. If you need anything, you use that linkpearl I gave you, alright?

We ain't in this trade to be nice. The masters'll tell you true. [@2B([@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000088,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000088,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)])] may be rare enough, but if they ain't quality, they're of no use to us.
Take your gil and be happy. If the conjurers find some rare elemental within, mayhaps they'll send some more coin your way.

Some quests require you to answer a linkpearl call before progressing. The NPC linkpearl icon in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]micro menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] will notify you when an NPC is attempting to contact you.
Select NPC Linkpearls from the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] to open a channel with the Adventurers' Guild.
Go in silence. We conjurers require quietude for our meditations, lest the din drown out the whispers of the elementals.
You wish to take part in a purification rite?
I take it you are the adventurer who recently eluded the treant in the Twelveswood, yes?
Miounne has informed us of your particular...situation. Proceed to the rear chamber, if it please you.
Miounne has informed us of your particular...situation. Being attacked by an enraged treant is no small ordeal. Proceed to the rear chamber, if it please you.
If Swethyna is involved, it must be a matter of some import. The leader of the Wood Wailers wouldn't waste time dabbling in aught else.
I sense great power in them, that much is certain. And then there is you... I cannot yet see the role that you will come to play in all of this.
The two outsiders brought by Swethyna of the Wood Wailers... There was something strange about them.
Then again, there's something a bit queer about you as well. Why don't you try talking to the others? Birds of a feather, as they say.
I pray a moment, please. Swethyna has important words which must be heard.
Look, Papalymo, he's got [@1A(1)]horns[@1A(0)]! This must be one of those Padjal!
Manners, Yda. Gods, the Gridanians will think us raised in a gutter.
The fury of the elementals is sure to be wakened whenever the Hedge is broken through.
That is why the treant became enraged and attacked. Normally it would never have dared venture so close to the city.
Brother O[@1F]App is a Padjal, of course.
He is the brightest of Brother E[@1F]Sumi's pupils, and favored by the elementals, as well.
We conjurers hear the whispers of the elementals, and see to it that their will is made known to all Gridanians.
That is why many of our order regularly journey deep into the forest. Fortunately for you, Brother E[@1F]Sumi happened to be in the midst of one such visit when you were attacked.
Where are those two outsiders from? We've had dealings with those from beyond the wood before, but never have I witnessed such insolence.
The elementals within the stones tell me there is no need for concern. But that mark they bear upon their necks...
The preparations for the rites often require a good deal of time. Mayhaps you would care to take in the sights of our Gridania here whilst you wait.
Atelier Fen[@1F]Yll in particular is much loved by you adventurers. Your custom would be most welcome, I'm sure.

Some quests require you to answer a linkpearl call before progressing. The NPC linkpearl icon in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]micro menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] will notify you when an NPC is attempting to contact you.
Select NPC Linkpearls from the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] to open a channel with the Adventurers' Guild.
You need worry not, what with the upcoming cleansing rites and all. The conjurers will see to it the greenwrath is quelled. They always do.
Aye, an elegant ritual, to be sure. We forestborn call it the Small Harvest. These days, it's mostly an excuse for the young ones to enjoy themselves.
Well, suppose you'll have to head to Greatloam Growery next. 'Tis there most of the festival preparations are made.
Watch how I do it. You have to [@1A(1)]beckon[@1A(0)] the elementals near. Like this.
Let the younglings teach you the dance. They will be taking part in the Small Harvest with you, after all.
You have to [@1A(1)]clap[@1A(0)] to keep the rhythm. Come on, keep up!
We [@1A(1)]bow[@1A(0)] to show our respect to the elementals. Just like this, see?
You have to [@1A(1)]cheer[@1A(0)] like this! Don't be shy, really get in there and throw your weight around!
We always d-do this, like we've just b-been [@1A(1)]surprised[@1A(0)] by s-something.
You can't forget this part! You have to keep a [@1A(1)]lookout[@1A(0)] for the elementals. Just like an archer on watch!
I wonder if the elementals dance as we do...
I don't even want to be here. My parents made me come.
It's not that hard. The most important thing is to let your heart guide you. The elementals will know if you are false.
You're terrible! You dance worse than my nana, and she's almost dead.
I wonder if any moogles will come and watch this time. They usually don't, but they say if one does turn up, the rite is blessed!
Hey, what are you here for? Me? I was running in the forest and tripped. Scraped my knee.
I don't know if that got me woodsin or not, but I'm going to dance anyway, just to be safe.
Hahaha, that's it!
Now you've got it!
Perfect! You're nearly as good as us!
You look like you've done this before.
H-How did you l-learn it so f-fast?
See how well you did? Aren't we good teachers?
Twelve be good, what are those little brats getting into now?
Hey! Practice, practice, prac― I saw that! Would you mind seeing that they behave themselves for me?
<whisper>
<whisper>
Seek out the younglin's and bid them return. Unless you'd prefer they make a tasty snack for the nearest feral beast? Bloody fool...
Wandered about the Twelveswood with the younglings? Gods save us! It's small wonder you adventurers have a reputation for being dangerous.
Not sure what words Fufucha will have, but common courtesy demands you at least pay her a visit.
The Wailers and the Quiver have been scouring the wood since the Hedge came down.
They're undermanned as it is, and ever looking for able bodies. That might well be why they were looking for you.
Get your arse over to the Wailing Barracks. Just look at your map if you don't know the way. Damn near impossible to miss the place.
You may proceed. Commander Burchard and Commander Nuala await you within.
Bugger it! I lost my bloody polearm. I really [@1A(1)]liked[@1A(0)] that polearm.
To bring down the Hedge is to bring down the greenwrath upon oneself. Such a life is forfeit. All here know that.
Only the outsiders would commit such folly.
Tend the wounded! Staunch the bleeding!
I couldn't get a good look. Elemental, or perhaps a man... I-I cannot say for certain.
The shadows... They came to life...
You, help us! Quickly! We have wounded!
The elementals rage as I've never heard. And I feel great fear among the people, as well―genuine terror. What could have done this?
St-Stop...please... The pain is too great...
<wheeze> I can't...breathe...
What the hells was that?
I can make no sense of it. Dunstan... By the Twelve, but [@1A(1)]why[@1A(0)]?
We have seen our share of adventurers in Gridania over the years─some sure-footed on the path of righteousness, and others not so.
For you to have come to the Wailing Barracks, I think you must be one of the former. I pray I am right. If it was Miounne who sent you, best go and see her again.

Adventurers share a certain bond, I know, but should any of your brethren act suspiciously, you [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)] report them to the Wailers. For their sake, as well as our own─before the elementals see fit to involve themselves.
There you are. I hope you weren't disappointed by the lackluster Gridanian welcome you received.
In time you will come to understand our ways, and we yours. With your help, we will solve these problems before us.
Now take this. The guild has seen fit to reward you.
Don't spend it on anything I wouldn't! Now, it's time you got yourself some guildleves and a retainer and set about adventuring!
And if you need to know more about either of those things, come and speak to me anytime. I've more than a few words I could share with you about getting started.
There are weapons and armor merchants here in the guild as well, always happy to help a fledgling adventurer. Off you go, then. And best of luck to you.

text_en: Hmph. From that blank look in your eyes, I would guess you are not too well-traveled. Best scuttle over to that corner you were cowering in and go back to sleep.
You speak to me as if I have something to say. Well, I don't, so begone.

You say you heard singing? Well, maybe it was ol' Llymlaen laughin' at us mortals seeking to trespass in her fair demesne. Or maybe it were them silky-voiced sirens the people back in Limsa are a-fearin'. <sigh> Guess some places just ain't meant for an honest man.
Unable to sleep, friend? How about a drink to calm your nerves?
I knew I should have taken an inn room... One more bell amongst this rabble, and the smell alone will do for me.
<sniff> It's heartening to know at least one of you practices proper hygiene.
Then it is set! Once we arrive in Limsa, we shall make our way to the Adventurers' Guild and find us a noble quest! (One that will make us rich, of course! Ahahahah!)
Hm? You say you'd like to join us? I don't know... You don't look like the adventuring type...

Have you decided what endeavors you will undertake once you've arrived in Limsa Lominsa? That is, unless you're on a sort of spiritual journey to become one with your inner self...in which case, I assume you won't be doing much of anything.
Remember, only you can give your life any meaning.
I heard Limsa Lominsa's a filthy cesspool overridden with pirates and pillagers, wenches and wastrels... Heh heh, sounds like my kind of town!

text_en: You say you heard a voice singing sweet somethings in your ear now, did you?
Well, I've heard nothing of the sort. Perhaps all this brine has started to pickle your brain.

Rhotano Sea's known for bein' rough with the men who tread on her back. Why, every trip, it seems we lose a few casks to her relentless wrigglin' and writhin'. But worry ye not; I won't be lettin' her make off with our best rum.
A barrel's bounty can't be borne away if it be in me belly!
These seemingly endless sea voyages can truly drain a man's soul of its vim and vigor. Might I offer you a drink to enliven your spirits?
You hear somethin'? 'Cause I hear somethin'. Somethin's goin' on up top. An' that somethin' ain't quite right...
I'd go up an' see myself, but I don't want my adventurin' days endin' before they start! Why don't you see what's afoot?

Pardon me, [@IF($E9(4),milady,sir)], but have you seen that filthy Qiqirn? The one that was shuffling about hither and thither, sniffing everyone's baggage. I have an inkling he might be off getting that oversized nose of his into trouble...
They say the seas around Limsa Lominsa are guarded over by a goddess called the Navigator. If her temper's as bad as this accursed storm, I'd say we're all doomed.
First time in Limsa? Then take this bit of counsel―keep your head down and your blade handy. Talk with Captain Hob if you're looking for a decent place to spend the night.
Step back, [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)]. All passengers must be inspected prior to being granted entry into the city. Quietly wait your turn or I will be forced to call the Yellowjackets.

Ye say ye saw a powerful sorceress weavin' her magicks 'round the ship, and that it's her what saved us from the serpent's minions? I ain't believin' what I ain't seen with me own two eyes, and I ain't seen no magickal wench, nor no serpent's minions.
But that storm we had─[@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] be true enough. 'Tweren't fer our fearless Cap'n Hob, we'd all be rottin' at th' bottom o' Rhotano's belly! Don't ye go forgettin' that now, eh?
We're sailors. A little wind or rain won't keep us from findin' our way to port. Bloodthirsty aurelias, on the other hand...well, those we could do without.
Did you see that light? I hope it wasn't what I thought it was...because if it was what I thought it was, we wouldn't be here. Ah, but here is where we are, and all is well, is it not? Heh heh!
Now, my companion, on the other hand...is not here, and that is definitely [@1A(1)]not[@1A(0)] good. Might you have seen her?

Hah hah! My arrival in Limsa Lominsa marks the beginning of a new legend! Call forth the bards, for my adventures will inspire epic tales that shall be sung in the halls of kings and queens across the realm. You, my good [@IF($E9(4),lady,lad)], are a witness to history!
Is there anyone more reliable than a man of the sea? Perhaps I should have stayed on the ship rather than disembarking into this den of wolves.
Last night...I believe we were witness to something well beyond our comprehension, and I believe it is best to leave it at that.

As a merchant, it is never wise to ponder over that which can not earn one a profit...such as that [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000001,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000001,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you carry. A fine specimen, albeit a tad ripe.
Ah, and our adventure on the seas comes to a close, only to make way for a new one upon the shores of this quaint island.

Perhaps our paths will cross again...and if you are planning on a visit to the Adventurers' Guild, then perhaps they will cross sooner than we think. I hear the good Captain Hob is heading there himself.

Welcome t' Limsa, younglin'. If ye're lookin' for an apology for the rough ride, ye won't find one from me or any o' me crew. Ye're here in one piece, and that's more than ye were guaranteed when ye boarded me ship.

I lost more'n a few good lads to that infernal storm, yet here ye be without so much as a scratch. I'd say ye've someone watchin' over ye...and that ain't no bad thing, 'specially if ye're thinkin' o' seekin' adventure out in the wilds.
I'm bound for the Mizzenmast, where me fill of ale and a soft bed await. Ye can follow me so far if ye please.
Accompany Hob to the Mizzenmast Inn?
Then away we go!
Ain't no need t' be timid, now. I ain't schemin' t' swindle ye none.
Accompany Hob to the Mizzenmast Inn?
Venture above deck?

text_en: A strange voice, ye say? Sure it weren't [@1A(1)]sirens[@1A(0)]?
Their song'll tug an' tear at yer very soul, leavin' ye drained of all life, but beggin' fer more. An' them sultry devilets ain't even th' worst o' what's lurkin' in Limsa's waters...
You appear troubled. Might anything be amiss?
Voices? I've heard naught but the infernal squeakings of that damned Qiqirn porter since stepping foot on this vessel.
