text_en: It don't take a bleedin' scholarly to divine what be hidin' in these 'ere crates, friend─[@1A(1)]ale[@1A(0)]. A whole bloody lake o' the stuff!

Might ye be lookin' t' drown yer sorrows, or mayhap muster th' pluck t' snare yerself a [@IF($E9(4),bit o' gentlemanly company,tender piece o' flesh)] fer th' night? Our good host Baderon'll gladly oblige, so long as yer purse be heavy!

Forgive my boldness, but would I be correct in assuming that you are newly come to this land? Let us just say your tattered garb and look of disquietude gave me an inkling. Oh, I did not mean to offend. I was much like you when I first set foot in the city[@1F]state. Truth be told, if it weren't for Baderon here, I daresay I'd long since have taken my place with the bloated corpses clogging the docks of the Sailors Ward. You would be wise to speak to the jolly fellow yourself if you wish to survive long enough to see another summer.

Lookin' to put a few malms 'twixt you and this reekin' hells hole? Aye, I was the same when I first arrived in Limsa. Good Baderon set me straight, though. You'd be wise to partake in his wisdom afore flutterin' off too far from the nest.
There be men who shay Sheal Rock ain't always been there. Rumor is, it jusht 'ppeared out of nowheres back one shtormy night.
Hahgh! An' if you believe that nonshenshe, then who's to shay there ain't some marveloush treasure buried shomewhere 'neath 'er boulders?

Not a soul in the city ain't looking to win the next Trident and knock our esteemed Admiral off his perch on the Bridge. But to even have a hope, you need a fat purse, and that's why everyone and their cousins are searching for that damned treasure.
I'd stay out of their way if you want your head to keep your shoulders company.
I been 'earin' whispers of normal folk like you and me joinin' up with them fishbacks. If I ever find one of the traitors, I'll gut 'im, bake 'im, and serve 'im up with a squeeze of lemon.
Damn Knights of the Barracuda. If it weren't for them, I'd have been on that island and found that treasure weeks ago...
Mealvaan's Gate's been sendin' cadre after cadre of mages to Seal Rock to investigate the place... Now, if I could somehow infiltrate their ranks...
I also heard them Sanguine Sirens got somethin' up their sleeves. What exactly is it? Hells if I know, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]─it's up their sleeves!
Ah, a new face. Welcome to Limsa Lominsa. You have arrived at an opportune time.

There is discord amongst the rival pirate gangs, meaning they have little time to meddle in the affairs of adventurers. This leaves us relatively free to step in and take the work the brigands would usually claim by right. Just be sure to avoid biting off more than you can chew. There is quite enough to keep us all occupied.

Lately, the street's been filled with rumors o' some fantasy island brimmin' with treasure, but I reckon there ain't one in a dozen with an onze o' truth behind 'em. Wish the 'Cudas would just raze the damn rock an' put an end t'all this rubbish.
If I was you, I'd pay nary a listen t'any gil-eyed pirate preachin' of easy loot. Stick with good ol' 'onest guild work, and ye'll make yer mark on this city in no time.
Unless you have information on the Empire, you may take your pleasantries elsewhere.
You receive a linkpearl from Baderon.
Linkpearls are a quick and convenient way to communicate with others across Eorzea, no matter where they be.
The NPC linkpearl icon will appear in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]micro menu[@COLOR($EC)] when an NPC wishes to contact you.
Open the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)] and select NPC Linkpearls to hear what Baderon has to say. The linkpearl message will be displayed in the log.

Can't do much 'venturin' whilst cowerin' in a pub now, can we? Time ye step out an' see the world fer what she truly be―a stinkin' maw lined wi' razor-sharp teeth ready t' rip yer arse right out yer trappin's...an' I got jus' th' place fer ye.

There be a 'Cuda camp jus' beyond the Zephyr Gate on th' outskirts o' town. Bearded Rock, they call 'er. Equipped wi' all th' amenities, she be. Why, she even got one o' them aetheryte crystals what let a man jump hither an' yon quick as th' crow flies. Gotta lay yer 'and on it first, o' course. Attunin', them scholarlies call it. Piralnaut can learn ye better'n I.

Where was I? Ah, right. Look fer th' Procession o' Terns leadin' from Bulwark Hall below. Ye can ride th' lift, or, if yer sea legs don't fancy them infernal imperial contraptions, traipse yer way down th' stairs outside. From there, jus' keep walkin' straight 'til ye see the glisterin's. Ye'd 'ave t' be blinder'n an ahriman wi' an eyepatch t' miss the camp.
Tell me, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)], 'ave ye rubbed on th' aetheryte yet?
Right then. No matter where yer travels take ye, always be sure t' attune with the crystals. Save ye time in the long run, it will, an' ye knows what them in the gelt says about time.
Ahem! Now that I 'as yer undivided attention, ye might want t' open yer pack. I slipped ye a keepsake whiles ye were busy makin' yerself at 'ome in me pub.
Called a guildleve. Think of it as th' quickest road t' fame an' fortune...most o' the time. At worst, it'll get ye at least a stone's throw from fortune an' but a few steps short o' fame.

Each leve offers ye a task what we call a levequest. Be a good [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)] an' finish what ye've got t' finish in the time ye've got t' finish it, and ye'll be generously recompensed fer yer kind efforts. If ye be interested, ye can try the one I gave ye by touchin' the aetheryte there one more time, or by havin' a chat with that Didiwai gent, dependin'. Else, ye can always come back t' th' pub where a tall, foamin' flagon[@IF($E9(4),'ll, and a warm wench'll)] be waitin' fer ye.
Tell me, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)], 'ave ye rubbed on th' aetheryte yet?
Right then. No matter where yer travels take ye, always be sure t' attune with the crystals. Save ye time in the long run, it will, an' ye knows what them in the gelt says about time.

Now that that's taken care of, feel free t' roam th' plains as ye please. Or, if that ain't t' yer likin', ye can always come back t' th' pub where [@IF($E9(4),warm company an' a tall, foamin' flagon'll,a tall flagon an' a warm wench'll)] be waitin'.
Twelve take me! Th' [@IF($E9(4),lass is,lad's)] still 'mongst th' livin'! Well, then. If ye still be interested in talkin', I've a few spare words lyin' about. All ye 'ave t' do is ask.
Still sportin' the look of a lost rabbit, I see. Pity.
Perhaps it's time ye took in a little o' the city.
Limsa's got its share o' guilds what'll take in a stray adventurer every now an' again. Quickest way t' learn the lay o' th' town, an' make a name fer yerself while ye're at it.

By the by, from that cloud o' flies what seem set on makin' friends wi' ye, I'd wager ye're still luggin' that bloody [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000001,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000001,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] around. Didn't I tell ye the swillmongers down at the Bismarck would pay ye good coin for it? They're always scroungin' the docks for somethin' to toss in their slop du jour.
Oh, an' 'cause ye look to 'ave a bit o' fight in ye, lemme scrawl ye up a recommendation fer the Knights of the Barracuda. Never say no to fresh meat, them 'Cudas.
Keep a close eye on yer map, and ye'll eventually find the place.
Limsa's got its share o' guilds what'll take in a stray adventurer every now an' again. Quickest way t' see th' city, an' make a name fer yerself while ye're at it.
Why not try startin' with the swillmongers down at th' Bismarck, then the 'Cudas over in th' Coral Tower?

If I ain't mistaken, the Bismarck'll be interested in that fish ye got rottin' there in yer pack. As fer the 'Cudas, just show 'em that recommendation I scrawled ye, and they'll put ye through yer paces.
An' if ye still find yer arse turned about, ring me on that there pearl. Ye never know, I might even answer.

Now just 'cause ye've peddled that stinkin' piece o' sea meat and be smellin' better than th' last time ye was in 'ere, it don't mean ye know the 'alf o' what this ol' town's about! But if ye're still 'ungry t' learn, there be plenty o' guilds what'll take in a stray adventurer like yer rose-scented self.
Got that recommendation I writ ye up? Take it o'er t' th' Coral Tower and show it t' them 'Cudas. They'll learn ye right.

Now just 'cause ye 'scaped th' Coral Tower with yer arse still strapped on, it don't mean ye know the 'alf o' what this ol' town's about! But if ye're still 'ungry t' learn, there be plenty o' guilds what'll take in a stray adventurer like yerself.
I can smell that ye still 'ave that fish festerin' in yer pack. Why not carry 'er down t' the Bismarck an' see if they'll take 'er off yer 'ands?

As any fine fisher knows, [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000001,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,11000001,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] carries with it a terrible curse, for its kind only rise to the water's surface when a sea serpent is close behind.

And what if someone were to slay this horrible beast from the abyssal depths, you ask? Yes, the seas would be safer, and salt wives could sleep soundly knowing their loved ones were in no danger...but then our chefs may never see [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000001,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000001,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] again.
As a culinarian with a conscience, it's hard to know how to feel about the situation...especially when word goes around that the Knights of the Barracuda may be planning to forcibly resolve it.

Some quests require you to answer a linkpearl call before progressing. The NPC linkpearl icon in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]micro menu[@COLOR($EC)] will notify you when an NPC is attempting to contact you.
Select NPC Linkpearls from the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)] to open a channel with the Adventurers' Guild.
Baderon send us another recruit, eh? Let me see your papers...

Very well. I care little for who you believe yourself to be back in “the world,” because here you are nothing until you have proven different. Let us first see how you fare at our aptitude test. You may proceed to the firing range on the lower floor, recruit.
Let us see how you fare at our aptitude test. You may proceed to the firing range on the lower floor, recruit.
Like t' know why I's smirkin', would ye? Heheheh, 'cause ye're lookin' at a Salthound in a 'Cuda's 'coutrements!
Don't ye think o' tellin' a soul now, savvy? One peep out o' ye, an' me brothers back on th' Rusty Claw'll make sure ye don't do no more talkin'...ever.
Which o' the seven 'ells did that damned pointy-eared bastard crawl up from? Ain't never 'eard o' no Merodaulyn, an' if he ain't one of us Krakens, 'e ain't worth piss in a gutter.
The lout gone swingin' 'is shiny axe left an' right an' this way an' that, an' all the 'Cudas goes limp as tickled trout! Not a one 'ad the time t' bat an eye at me an' me laddies.
Merodaulyn, eh? Young scrapper put on quite a show, so he did. Can't say I ever laid eyes on the man before, though―and I been here since I were a sprat.
Cap'n Rhoswen won't be pleased, though. Countin' on me splittin' the ranks, she was. Here's hopin' one of my Sanguine sisters had a bit more luck.
How dare that hells-damned 'Cuda give the final Seal Rock position to Merodaulyn when he'd promised it to me! And after the things he made me do last night!
Bring one pirate down, there'll be two more to take his place, I tell you. They're like bloodbeetles, sucking the life out of the city, and they're hiding under every rock.
I cannot fathom why Commodore Sthalmann would even consider taking up new recruits, knowing we'd simply be making it easier for those vermin to infiltrate our ranks.
I came in here thinking I'd have to impress these lads with my blade, when all they were interested in was my sheath.
Had them all in the palm of my hand, too...that is until my final test. How was I to know one of the godsdamned invigilators was a Miqo'te?
My name is Totoruto, but you can call me Cerberus. I guard the gates of hell and bite off the head of any addle-pated pirate stupid enough to try to infiltrate one of our units.
And that includes you! Enlistment is over!

Welcome to the Coral Tower―headquarters for the Knights of the Barracuda. We police Limsa Lominsa's streets, as well as her waters, ensuring some semblance of order is maintained in this den of pirates and brigands...in whose company I can see you are not to be counted.

We are also known as the Musketeers' Guild, and provide training to those who wish to study the art of marksmanship. While I would normally offer you the opportunity to enroll at this point, I'm afraid resolving the Seal Rock situation must take priority.
I apologize, but we are not accepting new members at this time.

They say that there is very little to separate a pirate from a Barracuda, and in most aspects I would be inclined to agree. However, there is one difference, and that would be the Barracudas' ability to look beyond the scintillations of loot and see the nobler reward of having done one's duty.
And what separates a pirate from an adventurer, you ask? Nothing of note. After all, what proof do I have that you aren't here chasing after rumors of treasure like the rest of them?

I had but a short time to see the enlistees, yet I was left in no doubt as to which of them was the most impressive. I don't believe I've seen a man wield a weapon as well as that Merodaulyn did today. It was as if his axe weighed nothing at all.

Each knight in the Barracudas' ranks is issued a musket of his own and trains for years to become adept with the firearm. However, I don't think half our men would have survived a one[@1F]on[@1F]one battle with that crazed marauder.
Your interest in joining the Knights of the Barracuda is commendable, adventurer. So many of your type are too easily drawn to the promise of plunder preached by our local pirates.

You may not have earned a position with the Seal Rock Provisional Unit, but do not let that deter you from your goal of becoming a Barracuda. As long as our esteemed Admiral rules the seas, Limsa Lominsa shall not fall, and the reach of the thalassocracy shall extend to the horizon and beyond.

As a gatherer of intelligence for the Knights, I pride myself on having at least a cursory knowledge of all but the most unremarkable strangers to pass through these doors. However, I must admit I had never seen or heard of this “Merodaulyn” until today. While he wields an axe with the deftness of a marauder, his mannerisms do not suggest that he hails from the halls of the Astalicia. Perhaps he is no more or less than an adventurer, just as you are.
Might you have heard anything of the Elezen on your travels? I would personally be grateful for any details on his background.

Some quests require you to answer a linkpearl call before progressing. The NPC linkpearl icon in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]micro menu[@COLOR($EC)] will notify you when an NPC is attempting to contact you.
Select NPC Linkpearls from the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)] to open a channel with the Adventurers' Guild.
Leviathan's eye! I ain't never 'eard o' no one bein' turned down by the 'Cudas, 'cept for way back when Seal Rock first rose from the depths.

Must be some sort o' misunderstandin'. 'Tain't as if they don't 'appen every now an' again. Better luck next time, then, right? Ye mark my words: the 8th'll be lookin' fer fresh meat in less time than it takes a seabird t' shit on yer best shirt down in Fisherman's Bottom.

Speakin' o' th' Bottom, why don't ye try the pullers down there next? Why, they ain't much different from the 'Cudas themselves, what wi' workin' on the seas an' all... Wait, now that ye mention it, that's all they 'ave in common. Gahahahaha!
Now off with ye. I got casks to tap.
Ye claim ye've truly seen a mighty sea beast, eh? Hmph. Ain't the first drylander to come in 'ere spoutin' such bilge...

You can no doubt imagine why our organization is loath to place too much trust in errant adventurers. However, in times of growing instability―such as might be caused by various pirate factions―we are forced to forge temporary alliances that can prove to be of mutual benefit. Needless to say, the commodore feels that now is one of those times.
Come along, come along! Sisipu is a busy woman. Speak with her and learn the hand signals so you can be on your way!
<sigh> Not what I was expecting, though I must say I was not expecting much.

I suppose I cannot blame you for your lack of prowess in the field as it was Wawalago who saw fit to reaffirm the age-old adage that one gets what he pays for. And even if I [@1A(1)]were[@1A(0)] inclined to mock the afflicted, it would seem, for the time being, that we are stuck with each other as a rotting head is to a pike―so we might as well make the best of it!
If ye're lookin' fer Steelmaster H'naanza, I saw her o'er near the back door, but ye'd be wise not t' interrupt her while she's attendin' t' business with Sthalmann.
Enter the instance?
Enter the instance?
It seems Commodore Reyner took quite an interest in you. Whether or not that proves to be a blessing, only time will tell.
In any case, he will have informed Corporal Isaudorel of your test results. Speak with him to learn your fate.

Yes, yes. You find yourself in the Pullers' Guild; the Fishermen's Guild; the guild of those who cast nets and lines and then pull and pull them in to collect the delectable offerings of that spectacular sprawling sea stretching all the way to the shimmering sky.

But oh, but no! There are many, oh so many creepy-crawlies with a taste for those selfsame tasty tasties who pose a threat to those whose only wish is to fish the wide-open waters in peace. And that is why we must stand united! United in our hand signals! Have you learned them from Sisipu yet?

We've received word from one of our boats that a Serpent Reaver vessel is anchored off Oschon's Torch. That lighthouse is responsible for preventing people from coming to grief on the rocks off Gods' Grip. If it were to fall into Sahagin hands, we'd no longer be able to cast our nets in those waters...
Day after day the Barracudas send ships to rid the waters of the Serpent Reavers, but it seems the damn pirates are always one step ahead of our city's finest.
Take my advice, and avoid the coasts unless absolutely necessary. The Reavers are soulless bastards who won't hesitate to rip your heart out and toss it to the sharks.
First, try a formal [@1A(1)]bow[@1A(0)]. Oh, but it only seems like a bow! To the trained eye, it's a secret greeting masquerading as an everyday greeting! How cunning is that!?
Next, [@1A(1)]clap[@1A(0)] your hands! With enthusiasm! I said ENTHUSIASM!
Now clap your hands over your head as if you were [@1A(1)]congratulating[@1A(0)] your pet racing tortoise on its thrilling victory over an egomaniacal hare.
And now [@1A(1)]poke[@1A(0)]. Poke poke poke poke poke!
We're almost done. Next, thrust your fist into the air as if you were jumping for [@1A(1)]joy[@1A(0)]. You mustn't actually jump, of course―that would look ridiculous.

And finally, [@1A(1)]wave[@1A(0)] your hand back and forth. Your father's set off on a journey to find the lair of a magical dragon and may never return. Let him know that you will always be with him in spirit! Wave him farewell, my friend! Wave, like you've never waved before!
Very good! Very good!
No, no, no! Must I repeat myself?

Excellent. You might not be quite as bad as I thought. Just remember, if you happen to see a suspicious-looking someone in or around the lighthouse, be sure to give the correct signal, or you might wind up with an arrow through your head.
To reach the lighthouse, follow the south road out of Limsa Lominsa. I'll be waiting for you at Zephyr Gate.
Mastered our signals, have you? Thank the Twelve you're a quick learner. Now off to Zephyr Gate!
You [@1A(1)]have[@1A(0)] heard of Zephyr Gate, right? March back o'er to the Drownin' Wench and head east, 'cross the colossal span linkin' us to the mainland.
Lady Sisipu'll be waitin' for you on the far side, so no dawdlin'!
Wangled yerself a date with a puller down at the Zephyr Gate, have ye? Not bad fer a new-come drylander. But tell me this: do ye even know where the damn gate is?
Inquire about the Zephyr Gate?
Thal's balls! 'Ow long ye been in the city now, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]? 'Tis a mercy Llymlaen ain't navigated yer drylander arse off a cliff an' into the drink!

Now listen close, 'cause I ain't in the 'abit o' parrotin' meself. Jus' ye take th' stairs down a floor an' leave quietly out Zephyr Gate to the east―that's “right-wards” on yer map if ye ain't too bright.
Underestimated ye, did I? 'Tis comfortin' t' know ye ain't completely 'elpless.
<shudder>
As I said before, you are free to return to...whatever it is you do; however, I ask that you do not roam too far from the city while we continue our investigation into the weapon you were lent.
This poor soul has taken his last breath...

Ah, if it ain't me newest ol' mate, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! A certain 'ead puller's been tellin' me 'ow you did 'is guild a grand service! Well, let me be the first t' give ye an 'earty pat on th' back, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]!
But if I was ye, best be swift 'bout procurin' payment fer yer 'andlin' o' the crisis. That wee wastrel be infamous fer weaselin' 'is way out of contracts.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Me mates tell me the fishbacks gone an' wreaked 'emselves some 'avoc over by Oschon's Torch.

Why don't ye venture out t' Naldiq & Vymelli's and see fer yerself? Maybe th' smell o' th' soot an' th' ring o' th' anvil'll set yer blood a-boilin', eh? Pay no 'eed to them scholarlies in th' Alchemists' Guild, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]―only smitties can turn lead into gold, if ye gets me meanin'.
Rumor 'as it, the smitties o'er at Naldiq & Vymelli's be workin' them forges day an' night buildin' some secret iron giant th' 'Cudas plan usin' t' crush th' fishbacks.

They'd do it too, I'd wager, were it not fer all the infightin'. E'er since th' shipwrights opened their doors t' weaponsmiths, see, they've done naught but bicker o'er who be best with an 'ammer 'n' anvil. Still, succeed or fail, 'tis quite a sight. Why not 'ave a look fer yerself?
Lately, the forges been crawlin' with pirates. Every gang in the city's lookin' to secretly commission 'em a shipwright to build a boat quick enough to slip by the Barracuda fleet and onto Seal Rock.
Problem is, even if your vessel's swift enough to outrun 'em on the water, they already know exactly where you're headed, and ain't nothin'll save you in a battle against their levies on dry land.
Barracuda or not, I see one more un-sooted brute run through the forge, I'll thrust his head in the cooling troughs.
You'd think their hands would be better occupied culling fishbacks than warming themselves over our fires.

Did you see Commodore Sthalmann? He's one of the highest ranking members of the Knights of the Barracuda. They say his fists are like lead and his heart as cold as iron. Why, even his name means “man of steel.” No need to wonder why the Admiral made him his right-hand man.
Treasure on Seal Rock? Hah! The pirates, the 'Cudas, the scholarlies―not a one knows the powers they disturb with their meddlin'.

Ye truly want to know what lurks on that forsaken island? Sirens! And no, not those o' the Sanguine variety, though they won't hesitate to drink your body dry. I speak o' those voracious vixens whose silken songs'll drive a man mad. Heed my words, 'venturer! A great evil is upon us!
Fishbacks don't wear armor, but their thick, scaly skin can be a bastard to slice through with your standard axe.
Now, this here creation of mine will cut through their hides like a knife does through butter. Not too bad on Barracudas, neither...hypothetically speaking, that is.

Now I ain't one to shed a tear over no drowned 'Cuda, but they say the 5th never saw th' Sahagin comin'. 'Tweren't their fault, neither. Only yesterday, I heard it was the Krakens that was plannin' on ambushin' th' fleet, not the fishbacks. Slimy bastards took us all by surprise.
Somethin' tells me things ain't transpirin' as planned. I smell an all-out war a-brewin', and it's a good thing I gots me an axe in the forge!
Three times them eunuchs down at Mealvaan's Gate and them 'Cuda brutes done searched that rock, but ain't no one sayin' a word 'bout what they finds.
You don't reckon as it could be that floatin' island o' legend, Swallowtail Roam, do ye? Hahaha! All this talk o' faerie tales got me thinkin' like me sprats!

This is Naldiq & Vymelli's shipyard. We ain't got no rules 'gainst visitors, but you best stay out of our way if you fancy livin' past th' next bell. Ain't no one'll blink an eye if you [@IF($E9(4),go an' tear yer frillies on me calipers,go an' stick yer manhood in the forge)].
By the abyss! Those damn Reavers roam the seas like it was their own!
There are even rumors swirling that the fishbacks have been dealing with honest townsfolk, like you and me.
Another adventurer, are you?

Lately, there have been a number of folk come in here calling themselves that. Any other day I would be inclined to believe you, but after what happened...I'll leave the character judgments to Bodenolf. If you can convince him that you're true of heart, I'll not question his judgment.

I would like to believe that you are nothing more than an adventurer, but after what happened today...I'll leave the character judgments to Bodenolf. If you can convince him that you're true of heart, I'll not question his word.

So, what say ye to the forges? Quite somethin', eh? I doubt there be a ship in Limsa that ain't passin' familiar with the 'ammers o' the smitties down at Naldiq & Vymelli's. Whole city'd prob'ly sink without a trace if it weren't fer them.

Without smitties, ain't no ships. Without ships, ain't no fish. Without fish, ain't no gelt. Without gelt...well, ye gets the idea, eh? This town lives by the sea, an' dies by the sea. If ye ain't got saltwater in yer veins, ye'd best pack up and 'ead t' the mountains, 'cause you ain't got no future in Limsa.
What's that? Th' Reavers an' the 'Cudas buttin' 'eads again? Hah! That ain't news, [@IF($E9(4),lassie,lad)]―it's war!
Why don't ye 'ead back to th' Wench? I gots me somethin' fer ye.
Came, eh? Maybe I was wrong about ye. Ye're still alive, an' that be more'n anyone expected from ye when ye first walked in.

But don't be kiddin' yerself―ye ain't even seen th' top o' th' tip o' th' rotten iceberg that is Limsa Lominsa. Jus' wait 'til one o' them pirate crews takes an interest in ye. Then we'll see what ye truly be made of...though I'd wager me pub it won't be much more'n a [@IF($E9(4),maid,man)]'s worth o' meat 'n' gristle.

...Still, so long as ye've got yer 'ead and th' wits what came with it, there's 'ope fer ye. Now, before them selfsame wits starts puttin' unwise words in yer gob, 'ere's a little somethin' t' eat from me an' th' guild.

If ye be lookin' fer somethin' t' spend yer newfound fortune on, might I direct yer wand'rin' eye towards our fine ale casks? Or if it's adventurin' ye be cravin', best set 'bout clampin' your grubby 'ands on some guildleves an' a retainer.

An' if there's aught ye care t' know concernin' either of them things, just come an' see ol' Baderon. Might be I've marbles enough rollin' 'round in me head to 'elp [@1A(1)]get ye started[@1A(0)]. Ye needs only ask.
Now, if marbles ain't yer fancy, then these two fine 'awkers 'ere can fix ye up wi' somethin' a tad more practical, like.

text_en: Count yourself lucky. This is him in a [@1A(1)]good[@1A(0)] mood. Best move along before he turns foul.
Sorry, friend, you're not quite ready for what lies beyond here. Go and show yourself to Momodi at the Quicksand. She'll set you on your way.
An adventurer, is it? Beggar of the realm, more like. Sod off. Only them as have coin can pass.
I've come to the big city to live the Ul'dahn dream, I have. Got a mind to send me ma back home a small fortune.
A piece of advice, dear, as I can see you are not from around here.
Do try not to appear so easy a target. Keep your nose buried in that map of yours too long and the sharks of Ul'dah will have stripped you naked as your nameday before you know it.
Look here, I purchased a platinum ticket. I'm finally going to see Greinfarr the Great on the bloodsands!
Best put any thought of leaving aside for now, friend. Parade's just about underway. That coach of yours was the day's last, in or out.
Sorry, but this area is off limits until the parade is over. They must be planning something [@1A(1)]amazing[@1A(0)]. I'm so excited, I can hardly keep from wetting myself!
But I'm forbidden to leave my post until all is over. Gods grant me the strength of bladder to last that long!
You'll have to excuse me, but I am not taking requests for the nonce.
I happen to be thoroughly enjoying the company of these ravishing young ladies and, gods willing, will still be doing so come sunrise.
Did you see the pretty lights in the sky? They're called fireworks.
I'd never seen them before. They mark the start of festival. Oh, isn't is all so [@1A(1)]wonderful[@1A(0)]!?
Have you ever been to Ul'dah before? No? Neither have I.
A voice? No, I didn't hear anything. All I heard was fireworks. They're pretty, but loud.
You've come just in time for the festivities, friend.
The parade's set to begin shortly. Were I you, I'd go and find myself a decent spot to watch from.
Sorry, friend, off limits. They're still making ready for the parade. Wait just a bit longer.
I heard the parade goes straight down the main road. But where the hells is that? Straight ahead? Back the other way? Bugger me...
Surely you didn't come all this way to watch the festivities alone, love. Perhaps we could enjoy some festivities of our own?

I'd be happy to take your arm, and more, for a time. You deserve a [@1A(1)]proper[@1A(0)] welcome to Ul'dah, [@IF($E9(4),fair lady that you are. I can please you as well as any man,handsome lad that you are)]. Though, from the looks of it, you don't have the coin. A shame, that.
Your timing is near perfect, whether you intended it or not. The parade will begin in mere moments.
They say the main attraction is the giant beast they've brought to fight on the bloodsands of the Coliseum. To hells with that! I've only got eyes for those young lovelies dancing about up top.

text_en: That's [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000089,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000089,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you've got there. Bloody expensive thing. How'd you come by it? Rifled it from a corpse, you say? Hehehe, you're going to be just fine here in Ul'dah, I think.
Now that was quite the sight to behold!
The dancers, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)], the [@1A(1)]dancers[@1A(0)]! Mine own daughter was among them─and a deal more beautiful than the rest. I'll have the tongue of any who says otherwise.
Ain't no sayin' what'll come to pass in Ul'dah. Aye, any who tells you different is playin' you false.
An' festivals ain't no different. I seen more fistfights an' floggin's than I can count. Hells, even saw an entire family trampled underfoot once.
I've never seen such a fearsome creature! And all those teeth! To think the gladiators of the Coliseum would willingly fight [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)].

Oh, wipe that blank expression off your face. You really must try to look like less of a bumpkin. I daresay it's not the last rampant beast you'll see in the big city. These things [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] happen.
I thought the fireworks explosions at first. I am sure I was not alone─an Ul'dahn festival simply isn't a festival without [@1A(1)]some[@1A(0)] sort of tragedy.
Hahaha, quite a bit of excitement, no? Not like to be a kerfuffle such as that without some fools losing their lives.
They've no need for grief, though. Those who die at festivals are greeted by Nald'thal as friends.

text_en: Have you ever been to Ul'dah before? No? Neither have I.
A voice? No, I didn't hear anything. All I heard was fireworks. They're pretty, but loud.
I heard the parade goes straight down the main road. But where the hells is that? Straight ahead? Back the other way? Bugger me...
You heard a voice, eh? Hells, I hear lots of voices. It's called [@1A(1)]people talking[@1A(0)]. Bloody fool...
A piece of advice, dear, as I can see you are not from around here.
Do try not to appear so easy a target. Keep your nose buried in that map of yours too long and the sharks of Ul'dah will have stripped you naked as your nameday before you know it.
A strange voice? Maybe I heard it, and maybe I didn't. Who's asking and what are you offering?
Well, excuse my language then, dear, but bugger off. If there's no gil in it, then there's no [@1A(1)]me[@1A(0)] in it.

text_en: Instances are special areas that are entered upon fulfilling certain requirements, such as progressing in a quest. There will always be a message telling you when you have entered an instance, and your minimap will show its boundaries.
Most instances can be left by crossing those boundaries; however, there are some, such as this one, in which certain objectives must be met before you are allowed to exit.
No doubt that beast would have been ushered onto the bloodsands of the Coliseum with the greatest fanfare. A true shame that it had to be put down.
I confess my decision to intervene was not wholly altruistic. Notoriety can take you quite far in this city, you see. And perhaps those I saved will see fit to return the favor someday.
Gil, gil, gil. That's what it's all about here in Ul'dah. Everything's got a price―even life.
And the price of that is so high, there's some who'd sell the lives of others to the Garleans.
Were there any casualties at the parade? There's a pretty gil to be made out of funerals, you know.
There's plenty of rich folk around here. If you try and wring a few gil out of one of them, just make sure you ain't the poor sod that ends up with a mark on [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] back.
They didn't get where they are by being gullible, nor forgiving neither, understand?
You've got to be one of three things to survive here―bloody clever, bloody strong, or bloody lucky! If you ain't, Ul'dah'll be the end of you, sure as your poxy-arsed ma was your beginning.
And leaving now won't do you no good. Ain't you heard? The dead rise at night. Come again to feed on the living what's fool enough to wander outside the city walls.
Did you hear!? Greinfarr the Great beat that rampaging beast at the parade to a bloody pulp!
He's the pride of Ul'dah, he is. If there are any Garlean spies in our midst, he'll find them and flay them and geld them besides!
The Garlean presence in Eorzea is no cause for concern.
If you truly wish to worry, ask yourself why is it that the Sharlayans are pursuing talks with the Amalj'aa.
Word is, an extremely valuable mineral vein was found deep within the Nanawa Mines. They say that's why they ain't allowin' none to enter.
Didn't seem to keep that worthless Elezen gaffer from pokin' around. I've half a mind to beat whatever he might know outta that old head of his.
Ala Mhigo has fallen into the hands of the Garlean Empire, and the number of Ala Mhigan refugees here in Ul'dah grows daily.
They work hard without complaint, and for mere scraps. I suppose we have the Garleans to thank for all this cheap labor. Hahaha!
You receive a linkpearl from Momodi.
Linkpearls are a quick and convenient way to communicate with others across Eorzea, wherever they may be.
The NPC linkpearl icon will appear in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]micro menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] when an NPC wishes to contact you.

Open the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] and select NPC Linkpearls to hear what Momodi has to say. The linkpearl message will be displayed in the log.
Best attune yourself to the aetheryte at Camp Black Brush before aught else.
Aetheryte camps serve as both waypoint and haven. Attunin' to them's essential if you're serious about adventurin'.

The west road through the Gate of Nald is the quickest way out of town. Now, there ain't many beasts close to the walls, but don't go lettin' your guard down, hear? Off with you, then, and be careful.
It's Momodi, [@STRING($EB(1))], from the Quicksand here in Ul'dah.
A whisperer of mine tells me they spied you touchin' the aetheryte at camp. Hope you don't mind my keepin' an eye on you.
I saw fit to smuggle somethin' into your bag. Go on, have a look. Got it? Aye, well, that's called a guildleve.
Aetherytes across Eorzea like the one you touched, and sometimes the camps around them, are the key to unlockin' guildleves. That one you got there's perfect for a fledglin' adventurer like yourself.
'Course, you're under no obligation of any sort. You're free as the winds, just the way you adventurers like it. Take care, now, and come back to the Quicksand whenever you fancy.
It's Momodi, [@STRING($EB(1))], from the Quicksand here in Ul'dah.
A whisperer of mine tells me they spied you touchin' the aetheryte at camp. Hope you don't mind my keepin' an eye on you.
The area around the aetheryte might suit a green one like you. Take care, now, and come back to the Quicksand whenever you fancy.
The prodigal [@IF($E9(4),daughter,son)] returns! So, how went the treasure huntin'? Happen upon any more precious little flowers?

Well, I suppose not every outin' can end in a shower of gil. Still, daresay you look a mite more rugged than when you were last here. I...uhhh... Hah! I've gone and forgotten what I was goin' to bloody say! What were we just talkin' about? Come on, speak to me again. Aye, right now.
Ah, yes! I've remembered! Don't expect to find a flower like that last one every time you go traipsin' about. For most folk, a treasure such as that is a once-in-a-lifetime find.
Hells, if it were easy, every mummer in Ul'dah would be at it, and nothin' would be worth a bloody fart. Come, how about I school you on some of the guilds in town?

You can find the goldsmiths over at Eshtaime's Lapidaries. Ul'dahn demand for flowers is always high, so they're like to part with a pretty gil for that [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000089,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000089,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you've got.
Then there's the gladiators over at the Coliseum. Lots of gil to be had there, no mistakin'─so long as you've got the skills to win on the bloodsands.
You'll no doubt lose your way in the alleys, so I'll mark both places on your map. And I'll no doubt regret it later, but take this. It's a pass to gain entry to the games at the Coliseum.
Now get out of here and make some bloody gil, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Use the linkpearl I gave you if you need anything.
<sigh> Gods... Very well, let's try this again. I'll talk nice and slow this time. How's that?

You can find the goldsmiths over at Eshtaime's Lapidaries, and they'll likely pay good gil for that there [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000089,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000089,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], on account of the demand for such fancies here in Ul'dah.

Still with me? Then I'll continue. The gladiators can be found over at the Coliseum. There's a killin' to be made there, if you'll pardon the expression─providin' you've got the skills to win on the bloodsands. You [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] recall me givin' you a pass to get in there, right? Well, I did!
Now get out of here and make some bloody gil, [@STRING($EB(1))]. Use the linkpearl I gave you if you need anything.
Let's begin at the beginnin', then. It'd do you good to hear about some of the guilds around here that take on you adventurers.
Did you bother to head to the Coliseum with the pass I gave you? If you fancy learnin' to use a sword, there's no place finer in all Eorzea.
Let's begin at the beginnin', then. It'd do you good to hear about some of the guilds around here that take on you adventurers.

Did you find Eshtaime's Lapidaries? Those greedy whoresons are always happy to get their mitts on a rare flower. That [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000089,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000089,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you've got might fetch some gil there.

Our commitment to produce the finest in fineries has even attracted the patronage of the royal family. For several generations, our workshop has been commissioned to craft the jewels worn by the sultans and sultanas themselves.

Our peerless craftsmen were also responsible for forging the now legendary blade, Heartstrike. You're certainly not like to see [@1A(1)]its[@1A(0)] rival in the hands of the barbarians on the bloodsands.

Some quests require you to answer a linkpearl call before progressing. The NPC linkpearl icon in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]micro menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] will notify you when an NPC is attempting to contact you.
Select NPC Linkpearls from the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] to communicate with the Adventurers' Guild.
I never studied logic at the Phrontistery, but it seems to me that if Greinfarr put down the beast at the parade...
...he would have ended up winning the tourney of beasts anyway, right?

The tourney...I... I meant to fight to show my dearly beloved the fierceness of my love for him─to fell the foul beast by the light of the sun, and then offer him my maidenhood by the light of the moons.
But he got tired of waiting and simply went off to the gambling halls of the Platinum Mirage.
Select the command which has appeared under the interaction menu.

Do you wish to fight in the Coliseum? Hmph, another bloody [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000126,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000126,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], is it? You damned adventurers and your special favor.
Always fighting the beasts but never each other. Never gives the crowd what they really want to see, if you ask me.
All your kind does is kill, kill, kill. The people don't want a butcher, they want a hero. Remember, you are an entertainer, adventurer. So entertain! Now go and wait within.
I heard in addition to being a fearless warrior, Greinfarr is also the Coliseum owner's son. They say he oft goes on long trips alone─some sort of ascetic training ritual.
Then again, I've only just started working here, so it might be wise to take absolutely no notice of anything I say.
Gods, have you any inkling how much gil went into organizing that parade? And the Coliseum's main attraction was [@1A(1)]killed[@1A(0)].
Rest assured, there'll be some moneylenders and bookkeepers burning the midnight oil for weeks over this.
This will no doubt increase Greinfarr's popularity among the masses. Any pupils of his certainly have a bright future.
They're short-handed for the next match...but I'm not at full strength. Still, I'd be less than a man if I didn't fight, seeing what Master Greinfarr did for us.
That lackwit of a thaumaturge made a right bloody mess of things. The entire faith of Nald'thal should be held accountable for all costs, if you ask me.
I can't believe the tourney of beasts was canceled. You have no idea...
I've been studying the weaknesses of every bloody beast in the Raimdelle Codex for over a year!
The whole parade incident was Corguevais's fault, that accursed thaumaturge.
The bastard should be gelded and marched out the Gate of Thal, naked as his nameday. Let the Amalj'aa spill his blood to their false god.
We expected much and more of the refugees from Ala Mhigo, but they've done naught but disappoint. Just as in their war with the Garleans, all they do is run.
The best of their warriors remain behind to carry on that useless fight. Such a waste!
Master Greinfarr is close friends with Niellefresne, the son of the owner of Eshtaime's Lapidaries.
He lacks Niellefresne's gift for politics, though. His time and talent has been spent on swordplay as opposed to wordplay, you see.
You there, have you seen the owner? I heard that he headed out with the master of the Miners' Guild.
Oh, I wonder if everything is all right. I do hope his employment won't be terminated.
I hear that Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern is takin' on hands for some extra work. Got any interest in diggin'?
Every now and then we get freeloaders who try to sneak into Amajina-owned mines and make off with a haul.
More often than not it's the poor folk from beyond the walls. I'd wager they are lookin' for help keepin' 'em out.

Some quests require you to answer a linkpearl call before progressing. The NPC linkpearl icon in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]micro menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] will notify you when an NPC is attempting to contact you.
Select NPC Linkpearls from the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)] to communicate with the Adventurers' Guild.
Well, I haven't had this much excitement in...in... Oh...oh dear... Perhaps I should lie down.
Please...mercy... I-I meant no harm...
Come to try and lift one of my bottles, have you? Aye, every miner in Thanalan knows Tyago Moui drinks the best wines. Well, lay a hand on aught of mine and you won't get it back, understand?
What were you doing down in the Nanawa Mines? Those are Amajina shafts! Speak! Or by the gods we'll have your bloody tongue out!
And what of the parade? That was your doing as well, was it not? My own sister was injured in the chaos─a broken hip. The healers are saying she's like never to walk again!
<sigh> Gods, not another scuffle. Are all the bloody miners in their cups again?
What the seven hells d'you want? Ain't you never heard there ain't nothin' more dangerous than comin' 'twixt a miner and his drink? Leave me be afore I bury my pickaxe up your adventurin' arse.
Aye, that's it. Take his bloody hands off! That'll make him think twice before goin' in our mines again.
Bunch of bleedin' mummers, the lot of 'em. There's naught to be gained from gettin' hot and bothered here.
Why must these things always happen just before I'm to take the stage?
You hear if that Corguevais got hisself exiled yet? If not, then he's still sworn to the Order. Best not lay a hand on one of them lot, lest you fancy the rest of 'em layin' their hands on you.
I know it base of me, but I do love to see men come to blows. There's something so primal about it, don't you think? Who needs the Coliseum when these brutes bring the fights to me? Hehehe!
Eaaasy there, killer. Rein it in a bit.
You must help me stop them before this goes too far. Do as I do to draw their attention. Come, show them you are [@1A(1)]furious[@1A(0)]!
Yes, just so. Here, I shall teach you another trick I know. Do this to [@1A(1)]beckon[@1A(0)] them to you.
Yes, yes! Well done. Then, of course, you can always simply [@1A(1)]laugh[@1A(0)] at them. No proud miner can bear to be sniggered at.
Alternatively, I suppose you could just [@1A(1)]deny[@1A(0)] them. Condemning the fight outright may serve to end it as well, assuming they find you sufficiently imposing.
Of course, if you can get them to listen, it may be enough just to let them know that you are [@1A(1)]upset[@1A(0)] by their feuding.
I couldn't have done it better myself. Most important of all, though, is to calm them─to [@1A(1)]soothe[@1A(0)] their miner's tempers.
What? You've forgotten already!? Gods...
Now, use all that I have just shown you and calm those two miners down. I've never seen them so angry. I fear something terrible may come to pass...
Who the hells are you? Get lost, sprat.
What are you laughin' at, you [@IF($E9(4),poxy whore,bleedin' whoreson)]!?
I ain't got time for the likes of you.
This ain't no concern o' yours. Piss off!
You got it all wrong. This old sod's the one in the wrong─not us.
Piss off, ye bloody mummer!
Fights ain't nothing new around here. But when them two are around, you'd better not start nothing. They're the last folks you'd want to get on the wrong side of.
Those two are such impressive young men, aren't they? I only hope my boys grow up to be like that!
You don't know how rough we miners have got it. Working our arses off all day, down in them pitch-black mines. This is where we come to relax.
That Elezen whose skin F'lhaminn just saved... I've seen him somewhere before. He's no miner, that's for sure. I think I overheard something about him being a thaumaturge.
Word is they found that Elezen right after the collapse in the shafts. He's lucky to be alive.
Ain't no mistakin', they're their father's sons. Won't never see either of 'em back down from a scrap.

If her belly be empty, I could spare a bit of me bread, such as it is. She ain't gettin' none of me water, though. Whether she be parched or not, we live in the desert, and me charity ain't without limits.
Come, child. What is it? Are you not well? Oh, hello there, good adventurer. Tell me, do you know aught of this child?
Come, sweetling, there is no need for tears. We will take care of you now. Dry your eyes and tell us what has happened.
Why would such a child be out wandering all alone? Where are her parents?
That girl was carrying a map showing the path from Ul'dah to here. I wonder if she was living in the city.
Do you think she was looking for her parents? There's nothing but poor folk around here. Nobody likely to be related to the likes of her.
I wonder if she was abandoned by passing travelers... It's a chilling thought, but having an extra mouth to feed can be a great burden in these parts.
Mayhaps the girl comes from a wealthy house. Could be a handsome reward waiting for whoever sees her back to it in one piece. Don't you even think about it─I thought it first!
Count yourself lucky you weren't chanced upon by one of the waste's many beasts. They like nothing better than the taste of you adventurers. Hehehe!
Corguevais has a good heart. He will see to it that the girl is looked after.
Nothing about that young child suggests to me that she is from Ala Mhigo. Certainly not judging by her appearance, at any rate.
The gods alone know how she came to be out here unaccompanied, though... Perhaps she is a runaway?
I can't for the life of me work out why everybody's still talking about that damned parade.
I can't for the life of me work out why everybody's still talking about that damned parade.
Have you come to see F'lhaminn?
I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but she rarely sings anymore.
Not like the old days, when she use to grace the stage daily for hours at a time.
Enter this instance?
Rumors are all over town, they are. Seems you took a cozy little trip with our very own songstress, F'lhaminn. Tell me, is that the way of it, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]?

Well, if you can't wait to see her again, you can always try your luck at the Concern. She oft takes the stage around this time of day. Could be that she wants to show you her appreciation─though gods know [@1A(1)]how[@1A(0)], hehehe!
Did you hear about the cave-in at the mines? The Phrontistery is full to the rafters with the injured.
If you can stomach those scholarly sods, might be some coin to be made over there. I imagine there's work to be done in plenty.
Scraped a few gil over at Amajina's, did you? Well that's just a taste. It'll take a lot more hard work and dedication to get where you want to go.
Did you hear about the cave-in at the mines? The Phrontistery is full to the rafters with the injured.
If you can stomach those scholarly sods, might be some coin to be made over there. I imagine there's work to be done in plenty.
Accidents in the mine shafts are certainly not the rarest of things. Still, this latest collapse left a good deal more injured than we usually see.
Master Faustigeant is within. He will assign you your duties. Go down the stairs at the rear of this ward and through the door beyond. He will doubtless be somewhere apparent.
I've never seen wounds like this before. And Master Faustigeant has ordered that any accounts given by patients be considered delusions and not recorded. What is going on in the Nanawa Mines?
No...no! Do not make me open my eyes! No!!!
Master Faustigeant has ordered you to survey the sickrooms? Very well. Pass through that door there and you will come upon them.
I s-saw it. Beyond the b-barrier. Such a t-terrifying sight...
Not many miners were seriously injured, but a lot of them─and I mean [@1A(1)]a lot[@1A(0)]─seem to have suffered mental breakdowns. I wonder if they hit a pocket of poisonous gas down there?
Who cares what caused it? Fact is, it happened. Not like the Concern stands to lose much anyway, seeing as how we were never even using that tunnel to begin with.
Look what the coeurl dragged in! Don't tell me the great adventurer has forgotten where [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] got [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] start.
Maybe [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)] you see why the rest of Eorzea thinks us overindulgent. 'Cause we're malms ahead of 'em in every way that matters! It's jealousy is what it is─plain and simple.
Anyway, here's a little somethin' for you. Consider it Ul'dah's way of sayin' thanks.
It ain't much, but get yourself some guildleves and a good retainer, and I have a feelin' you'll turn it into somethin' big.
Oh, and if you care to know more 'bout either of those, come and see me anytime. I can tell you a thing or two about getting started. Just say the word.
And if you be needin' any sort of weapon or armor, look no further than these merchants just beside me. They're always eager to help out a newcome adventurer. Right, then─best of luck to you.

text_en: I wonder what it is the elementals are after... You might be able to find out for yourself, seeing as how you are able to converse with the moogles, and all.
You have to wash all that woodsin from you before aught else, though. I suggest you pay a visit to the carpenters at the Oak Atrium, and see if they've finished your mask for the purification rite.
A message from the moogle to young Fye...
She will certainly be [@1A(1)]very[@1A(0)] excited to hear that. Exit the guild here, and you will find her in the Acorn Orchard just outside.
The Acorn Orchard? Yes, it is the small playground outside, on the west side of the Atrium.
We built it some time ago for the younglings. Fye ran by not a moment ago. I imagine she was on her way there.

Aye, the dead mask. Its powers have left it. A tragedy, that. It was meant for Fye's elder brother, Dunstan. Only it was unable to save him. When it failed, he... The woodsin upon him was too great. The greenwrath could not be stopped.
Looking for Fye, you say? She's out playing in the Orchard, I imagine, as all the little runts do. Just head west. You can't miss it.
Though if you are thinking to restore that mask of hers, you'd best forget it. You'd need some damned rare materials, and the power of the elementals besides.
There are very few among us capable of making the purification masks. I myself have never even attempted the feat.
The moogles certainly can't repair [@1A(1)]everything[@1A(0)]. But I daresay they have a far greater chance of helping Fye than we do.
Fye's brother Dunstan was a mighty lancer, and one of the Wood Wailers. The two of them were close as peas in a pod, until... <sigh> The gods can be cruel, can they not?
Your mask has been fashioned. That is truly good news. Now the conjurers may carry out the rites, and you will be purified before the eyes of the elementals.
Poor Fye. Khrimm can be such a bully. He really shouldn't pick on girls.
<whisper> Ya know what? Don't tell anyone, but both Khrimm's and Fye's families got turned into [@1A(1)]wildlings[@1A(0)].
Brother E[@1F]Sumi has returned to Gridania to conduct the rites at the festival.
He is at Greatloam Growery, and wishes to meet all of those who will be taking part. You'd best hurry.

Off to find [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000129,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000129,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], are you? I fancy Brother E[@1F]Sumi has taken quite a liking to you. He would not teach you the location of such rare fruits otherwise.
He could teach you a great deal more than that, too. More than you could ever hope to learn, truth be told. He knows every root, leaf, and branch in the Twelveswood.
Just a moment, kupo. I'll try and speak to the elementals of the trees.

The moogles love nothing if not their [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000129,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000129,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. Even so, I'd not thought you like to find one so quickly. Gods, all these exceptional adventurers! How does Miounne do it?
The archers asked that you come to the Quiver's Hold as soon as possible. You'll find an agreeable Lalafell bloke by the name of Nonolato there. Best go and speak to him.
The safety of Gridania is the duty of the archers of the Gods' Quiver, the lancers of the Wood Wailers, and the conjurers of Stillglade Fane.
Long have our guilds sought to defend the lives of those who honor the forest and the elementals─and to cast out those who do not.
We make efforts to learn mooglespeak, but our control of the language is rudimentary at best. Without the conjurers, this endeavor would be completely hopeless.
I know not of such things, but there are some that can use mooglespeak, whether through divine providence or study. And not all of them are forestborn.
You know the mooglespeak? Then you must help us, please! Speak to Bowlord Lewin right away!
If the woodsin upon a soul is too great, the power of the purification mask may collapse under the burden. But I do not think you are in any such danger.
Enter this instance?
Some would call you unlucky for the lot you've drawn here.

Dunstan knows more of the Twelveswood than most. An adventurer newly come to the forest is not like to catch so much as a glimpse of him. You're better off training at arms than wasting your time searching.
I hear the archers sometimes take on recruits for their rangings. It might be worth looking into.
Come and see me once you're able to walk the wood on your own. Until then, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Don't care to count 'ow many o' th' seven 'ells we'd be in if it turned out there was somethin' in them serpent-beast rumors.
Swallowtail Roam? Hah![@CR]I take it ye was lucky enough t' catch ol' Rostnsthal on one o' them rare occasions when he weren't fillin' his gods-awful, bilge-spewin' maw with sour ale!
All is not well... First Assessor J'arhll looked paler than usual...
[@IF($E9(6),She,He)] seems to be knocked unconscious.
[@IF($E9(6),She,He)] seems to be knocked unconscious.

Your petty attempts at thievery will gain you naught, Sirens! Everything here before you has been documented in triplicate! The noble Knights of the Barracuda will have it all back before your rotting bodies are pecked clean by the gulls!

The Sanguine Sirens are infamous for their treatment of men. Rumor has it that all who are captured are made slaves of the female members...and then worked day and [@1A(1)]night[@1A(0)] until they literally collapse from exhaustion. And those who cannot “perform” their duties? It's said they're taken out and hung from the bow of the [@1A(1)]Lady Infernal[@1A(0)]...by their manhood.
Oh, if only I'd stayed in bed and watched the sunrise with that beautiful wench I met at the Wench...
Now it looks as if I may not live to see another...or sunrise, for that matter!
I-I a-ask that you remain c-calm while o-our trained p-p-p-professionals bring matters to a s-s-satisfactory conclusion.

Such occurrences are qu-qu-qu-quite c-c-c-commonplace as we have d-d-dealings with p-p-p-pirates almost every d-d-day...albeit with f-f-f-fewer exp-p-p-plosions. (Oh-gods-oh-gods-Twelve-preserve-us...)
I finally complete my training and earn a position at the custom-house...and look what happens!
Perhaps I should have ignored my mother and become a pirate instead.
Ye heard the cap'n―keep quiet or we'll cut yer tongue out and feed it to the fishes.
Now back over into the corner where ye belong!
Wander about the hall all ye like, drylander. Ain't no one leavin' till Cap'n Rhoswen says so.
Mind yer manners, ye may live long enough t' witness her take her rightful spot on the Bridge. Cross her path, and she'll skin ye alive.
If Emerick manages to live through the night, I shall slit his throat with the cock's crow.
After finding the Coral Tower's brig empty, our captain suspected Carvallain's rat might be stowed away here in the Admiral's vaults instead.
I daresay Carvallain'll be hoping the 'Cudas showed a bit more creativity.
Back from th' scholarlies' already? Didn't 'ave too much fun now, did ye?
What's this? Ye say ye're lookin' fer a lad named Emerick? Emerick... Emerick... Why don't ye give me a few bells t' chew on the name and then ring me up on the aether.
That accurs'd treasure'll be the end of us all! I tried warnin' th' 'Cudas, but ain't no one listenin'.
If ye'd half a brain in yer head, ye'd be on the next ship out of Limsa...though I don't know how far ye'd need to go t' 'scape the horrors that're jus' waitin' to rise up from the abyss.
Heard the Sanguine Sirens got a man into the Barracudas' Seal Rock Unit.
Ye mean that lad Merodaulyn? The one that went an' made the 'Cuda sergeant cry like a whelp at 'is mammy's teat?
The fishbacks launched their attack almost halfway between Limsa Lominsa and Seal Rock.
That's why it took so long for reinforcements to arrive from either area...and why so many of them 'Cudas are now feedin' the sharks.

Them tales 'bout them bloody Krakens reachin' the Seal Rock treasure ain't worth more'n a pint o' piss in a jar. If they truly did get their 'ands on the loot, the Sanguine Sirens would be wrapped around 'em 'fore ye could spit.
An' once them two gangs get at it, ain't no stoppin' 'em, 'Cudas included.
Pirates, fishbacks, 'Cudas... That godsforsaken island's got all Limsa's players at each other's throats.
'Tis 'igh time I sent a man down Astalicia-way t' appraise meself o' th' latest 'appenin's.
I have no more words for you.
What's this? Don't tell me th' thought o' mixin' with a few pirates 'as ye cow'd? Not after all ye've seen!
If ye ain't got th' conkers t' stroll through the Astalicia without sullyin' yer britches, that be all the more reason t' get yer arse down there an' on a crew.
Lay one hand on your weapon, and you'll be in chains faster than you can blink!
You had best not be hiding anything from us, pirate scum. We have ways of...encouraging secrets to make themselves known.
I-I'll shoot! Don't make me sh-shoot, because I will, you know! Shoot, th-that is!
Any of you derelicts thinks they can take me down, fire away! I've seen fiercer mugs on the stray bitchpups down in Fisherman's Bottom.
Hah! Ye 'Cudas ain't nothin' more'n pirates with fancy fineries. Ye can try an' take th' Astalicia, but ye'll fail jus' like ye did th' last time...an' th' time afore that!
Who the hell are you? Ain't got the look of a pirate... Adventurer, maybe?
Consider yerself lucky, [@IF($E9(4),lassie,laddie)]. If it weren't fer the 'Cudas, me and me mates'd be whettin' our blades on yer bones.
Now where'd that scurvy little sod Emerick hide the loot!? He swears on his mother's grave them fishbacks up an' five-fingered it, but no one in his right mind 'd believe that crock o' swill!

After bustin' a gut t' get ourselves on that bloody rock, what be waitin' there fer us? Why, nothin' but a pile o' stones all slipp'ry wi' gull lime. Damn scholarlies must've 'auled th' swag back t' their custom-'ouse.

Every fishback I take down earns me coin fer ale an' women. All's I got t' do is take me a trinket from their cold corpses and trades it in. Don't ask me why anyone'd want that rubbish, but if it fills me tankard, I'm 'appy t' oblige.
An 'andful o' coppers says that damn Merodaulyn be privy t' summat we ain't, an' poor ol' Emerick's takin' the fall fer summat he ain't got the nous t' be doin'.
A wee lass from the Pullers' was up 'ere a few bells back lookin' for you and yours.
Ain't no one goin' t' 'old yer 'and all the way down t' Fisherman's Bottom, so get walkin'!
No, no. Don't know exactly what Sisipu sees in you, but there's not a soul in the guild brave enough to gainsay her once she's made up her mind.

But I warn you, I do―even think of layin' a finger on the wee lass and every puller in the Bottom'll hunt you down. And when they've finished with you, your member'll be stuck on a hook and dangled o'er a mullet's gullet.
No, no. Don't know exactly what Sisipu sees in you, but there's not a soul in the guild brave enough to gainsay her once she's made up her mind.

But I warn you, I do―even think of layin' a finger on the wee lass and every puller in the Bottom'll hunt you down. And when they've finished with you, you'll be stuck on a hook and dangled o'er a mullet's gullet.

Jus' been on th' pearl wi' them scholarlies down at Mealvaan's Gate. Seems they's lookin' fer ye. Now what could that be about? Ain't gone an' brung summat unsavory into port [@1A(1)]again[@1A(0)] now, 'ave ye?
'Course, the scholarlies would've sent the 'Cudas t' fetch ye if ye [@1A(1)]was[@1A(0)] in any bother, so I doubts yer neck be in th' noose jus' yet.
'Ere, take this. Been meanin' t' give it t' ye fer some time now, and now's as good a time as any.

Now about this Emerick. Ye're after th' treacherous sod what went an' sold th' 'Cudas t' th' fishbacks fer an 'andful o' sparklies, eh? Well, if I was th' bettin' sort, I'd wager 'e'd be caged o'er in th' big dromond anchored offshore. Them knights send th' worst o' th' worst out there 'til they be sentenced.

Keep a brigand like that in the Coral Tower an' it won't be long afore some lad wi' the fires o' vengeance burnin' an 'ole in 'is belly scales 'is way up the walls, 'ops into th' cell, an' does the sorry bugger in 'is sleep. 'Twas ol' Sthalmann's idea t' 'ide 'im away in th' ship, it was.

Problem is, gettin' on that vessel ain't goin' to be an easy task, 'specially fer a greenback like yerself. Why don't ye drop by the Wench once ye've a few more notches on yer blade, an' then I might be able t' 'elp ye.

I've heard it told the Garleans occupying the lands of Ala Mhigo dress in strange garb. But why distinguish themselves from us so? They could infiltrate the nations easily enough if they were less conspicuous.
There is a famed room at the Platinum Mirage known as Paradise. Only the most privileged of patrons are allowed access.

Smallfolk say that the famous and wealthy spend night after night there, gambling and indulging in gods know what manner of revelry. I myself have seen Greinfarr the Great and the songstress F'lhaminn come and go...if you take my meaning.
If you ask me, it was the Garleans behind the incident at the parade, and no mistaking. They mean to wreck our economy with acts of sabotage before risking open war, the craven bastards!
I was standing at the front of the crowd when the beast began raging. I would have died for sure had Niellefresne not saved me─with a flower. This flower he picked and gave to me...

I know he had hundreds of them, and gave them out to all─but then he [@1A(1)]had[@1A(0)] to, didn't he? It would have been [@1A(1)]obvious[@1A(0)], otherwise! Of course, [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] knew what that flower meant. Yes, his feelings for me were as clear as a spring morn. Oh, it's all so [@1A(1)]romantic[@1A(0)]! <sigh> My prince of flowers...
Heard the rumors of war with the Empire? Thought we were s'posed to be gettin' [@1A(1)]closer[@1A(0)] to peace─not farther from it.
You've caught me in a gay mood this [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),evening,morning)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),day,evening)])], so I shall share with you this.

I've heard reports that young Niellefresne and his companions have captured the Garlean in our midst...or tried to...or may be planning to try to...or...um... Oh dear, I've already forgotten the details. Niellefresne and his friends were definitely involved, though.
In any event, there is no cause for concern. The future of Ul'dah is bright so long as it lies in their hands.
Word is there's an openin' for a mercenary over at the Platinum Mirage. I daresay they'd welcome an able-bodied adventurer like yourself. Why not head over there and find out what's on offer?
Sounds like good coin to me. You'd regret it if you didn't have a sniff, that much I can promise you.
Welcome to the Platinum Mirage, where the sands turn to gil!
Ah, so you have come about work? Then you had best go and speak to one of the masters.
Reading... Moon phase... Star lines... Guardian favor...
A moment, please. A moment, please.
You are what you love. Not what loves you.
Welcome to the Platinum Mirage, [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)]. Home to all the pleasures in Eorzea─old and new, traditional and exotic!
We strive to provide each of our guests with whatever their heart desires─and their coin commands! Momodi has spoken to you of the work available here?
Very well. I shall make word of your coming known. Proceed through the door at the foot of the stairs within.
Welcome to the Platinum Mirage, adventurer.
If it is work you seek, you will find those you must speak with within. Pass through the door at the foot of the stairs.
Welcome to the Platinum Mirage, where the sands turn to gil!
Ah, so you have come about work? Then you had best go and speak to one of the masters.
Reading... Moon phase... Star lines... Guardian favor...
A moment, please. A moment, please.
You are what you love. Not what loves you.
Are you lost? You seem a little too...impoverished to be wandering the halls of the Mirage.
Ye're here for work, are ye not? Aye, I thought as much. Been here more years than I care to count, meself.
'Nother wayward adventurer come to Ul'dah with naught but the gear on [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] back, am I right?
Welcome, my [@IF($E9(4),lady,lord)], to [@1A(1)]Paradise[@1A(0)]! Within you will find the Platinum Mirage's highest stakes, and every pleasure imaginable besides.
I don't believe this! What have I gotta do to win? And why do I keep losin'!?
I'll win it all back, you'll see. 'Cause I'm special. I was [@1A(1)]meant[@1A(0)] to win. I know it. I can feel it. I'm different from all these lackwits. Gambler's fallacy, my arse!
What are you gawping at!? Get the bloody hells out of my way before I spill your rotten guts.
I locked the door, I'm sure of it... Are you a new employee of the Mirage?
The Platinum Mirage has [@1A(1)]no[@1A(0)] tolerance for cheating. Still, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], you are bound to treat all you have witnessed here with utmost secrecy. Do you understand?
Such luck! The Twelve are smiling upon him this day!
Dirty rotten cheat! Ain't none of them damned bards to be trusted. Not a one!
I have never seen Niellefresne lose... I suppose given the stakes, it is no surprise things became so heated.
Leave. You have no business here.
Chased off, were you? Yes, well, eavesdropping is not exactly looked upon favorably here. Momodi usually sends us more trustworthy adventurers.

We are required to conduct a thorough investigation into your history. Counterfeiters and spies from the other nations have sought to infiltrate the Mirage of late, so every precaution must be taken. Surely you understand.

I hope the Mirage was to your likin'. For now, it's all a hard-up adventurer like yourself can do to get work there. Give it time, though...give it time. In a few years, it may be you sittin' in that Paradise room they've got there.
And gettin' cozy with F'lhaminn certainly don't hurt your chances. Best not keep our songstress waitin'. You're like to find her at Sunsilk Tapestries.
Ah, a customer. Oh, and an adventurer besides, from the looks of it. Have you come to reinvent yourself? To drape your frame in the latest fashions and trends?
F'lhaminn? You are not a...crazed admirer, I hope?
She is off practicing her song and dance, as always. The miners of Amajina & Sons are a very demanding audience, you know?
I suppose I can tell you where she is, but pray do not disturb her long. Come, show us your map.
You can find F'lhaminn at the location I've marked on your map. That area [@1A(1)]can[@1A(0)] be a bit dangerous at times, though. Do take care.
Fortunately, the twins of the Mineral Concern are always good enough to see to it F'lhaminn has an armed escort.
Her name is Ascilia. She lost her father some time ago, and with him all that was left of her family.
We were finally able to hold a proper funeral, but the girl's future still weighs heavily on my heart. Would you believe she says she wants to be a miner here in Ul'dah?

The thaumaturges? Aye, I know a bit of their ways. Theirs is the Order of Nald'thal. Split into two sects here in Ul'dah, it is. And each with its own temple─Milvaneth Sacrarium and Arrzaneth Ossuary.
The Sacrarium's notorious for turnin' away visitors and novices. But the thaumaturges of the Ossuary welcome even lay adventurers into their halls to train.

What with war seemin' more inevitable by the day, I'd imagine the Order's recruitin' anythin' with a pulse to bolster Ul'dah's strength. That bein' so, it might be worth payin' Arrzaneth Ossuary a visit.
I oft wondered what form the funereal rites of the southrons took. Given the weather here, I assumed cremation rather than burial.
Damielliot of the Phrontistery hired me to attend as a mourner. I need do no more than cry. It is an easy way to make gil, should you ever find yourself in financial difficulty.
I had not imagined Master Niellefresne would attend. That reminds me, there was something I wished to speak to him about...

There are certain techniques among the thaumaturgical arts which are more, shall I say...[@1A(1)]esoteric[@1A(0)] than others. I should very much like to attempt one such ritual, but the gemstone components it requires are far beyond my means.
I have asked the Eshtaime goldsmiths countless times to procure the rocks, but have met with no luck.
F'lhaminn has taken quite a liking to little Ascilia. The two are inseparable of late.
Me? F'lhaminn asked me to attend since there were so few to invite. No family, no friends. It is tragic...
<sob> Wabutron! Oh, Wabutrooon! The world is already a darker place without you... <sob>
War-button? Oh, [@1A(1)]Warburton[@1A(0)], was it? Bah, it makes no matter. The gods are cruel! Now let us drink!
It is rare to see so many mourners at so humble a funeral. How much coin are you getting to cry, friend?
You're going to have to conjure up a few more tears if you expect to be paid in full.
Leave me be. I had no hand in this man's death, and will suffer no more accusations to the contrary.
It is a privilege to be able to speak with one as wise as Master Mumuepo. Nald'thal must favor you to bestow such an honor.
But the topic of which you spoke is taboo within the Order. None are to speak of it, thaumaturge or otherwise. Your words will not be without repercussions.
So what did you blather on about over at Arrzaneth Ossuary?
A thaumaturge came by askin' about you not long after that. Told him you were harmless enough, but you can be damn sure the Order's eye's fixed on you now.
You'd better bloody watch yourself, alright? Piss off the wrong person around here and you'll be exiled before you can say necromancy─[@1A(1)]again[@1A(0)].
But enough of that. There's other news, have you heard? A band of gladiators from the Coliseum and pugilists from the Mirage has been sent off on some secret business beyond the city walls.
Don't bode well, if you ask me. Both sets serve to protect the city. For them to be runnin' off on missions and such... Well, I've a feelin' it could mean somethin' bad's on the horizon.
They were seen leavin' the chocobo stables, but the gods alone know where they were headed.

Y'know, I'm startin' to think that [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000089,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000089,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you had might've been an ill omen. Just see to it you don't do anythin' to get yourself exiled from the city, alright?
Why Master Mumuepo does not simply do away with all you heretics who come asking about such sins and sacrileges, I will never know.

text_en: Welcome back, Pathbound [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Your companion should be arriving shortly.

I wish you both all the best. Your journey together has now begun. It goes without saying that the next few days will prove crucial in forming a bond between you. The more time you speak, dine, travel, even fight together, the stronger that bond will become. And it is the strength of that bond that will decide your fate on the Path.
Now hurry to the Quicksand and speak with proprietress Momodi about securing a table for you and your companion. May the Twelve watch over you.
A fine name. I believe I could get used to it.
Interesting... Not what I would have chosen, but...
Hmph.
If it pleases [@IF($E9(4),my lady,my lord)].
A fine name! More than fine. [@1A(1)]Too[@1A(0)] fine for one as unworthy as I.
How quaint.
Hmmm... Aye, I reckon that fits!
Oooh...yes! [@1A(1)]Now[@1A(0)] we're role-playing!
That'll do.
