text_en: Welcome back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I take from your presence that you have had sufficient time to consider my offer. What say you?
Join Minfilia on the Path of the Twelve?

I see... It would be wrong of me to pressure you into making a choice that could well define the rest of your life, but I strongly suggest that you take some time to reconsider. We can help you find your true calling. You need not walk alone.

But if you must, then I pray you heed these words: those with your gift are oft shunned by those who do not understand it. To most, you will be perceived as a kind of voyeur, violating the innermost sanctums of the soul. If you are caught, you will be punished. You may even be killed. And there will be [@1A(1)]no one[@1A(0)] to protect you.
Join Minfilia on the Path of the Twelve?

I too would introduce myself, but...when I chose to walk the Path of the Twelve, I also chose to leave behind the man I once was. It was a chance to start anew. Anyway, I no longer have a name...so you may call me what you will!
As for me...well, I have many names, and I have none. People call me what pleases them, and I find that by allowing it, things go much more smoothly. Feel free to call me what you will.
My name is my own. Call me what you will, if you must call me anything at all.

You must forgive me, but I cannot tell you my true name. I come from a small clan, and we are very protective of our past. Please, do not take offense─I ask but this one secret. To prove I bear you no ill will, you may call me whatever you wish.

I s-s-suppose that you'll now want me to tell you [@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] name... Oh, if only I could, if only I could! But ever since the starshower...I cannot seem to remember! What is a man without a name!? A nameless man, he is. Hardly a man at all! But wait! Might [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] be generous enough to give me a name? Any name will suffice! A nameless excuse for a man has no right to be picky!

And now, I suspect that you suppose I shall make known mine own moniker─namely, my name! Well that cannot be! A name has powers most powerful─powers to corrupt and control! Why, would you have me believe “[@STRING($EB(1))]” is even your [@1A(1)]true[@1A(0)] title? Ha! I thought not! So call me what you like, just don't call me Ri─ Oooh, you almost had me there! Ahahahahah!

I had a name, but I decided to forget it when I started on the Path. I ain't th' man I was before, see, an' I reckoned it wouldn't be right t' use that fellow's name. Anyway, since me new life starts here, I s'pose now's as good a time as any t' pick a new one. Got any ideas, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]?
My name? Why, [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] is a secret! A little mystery will help to keep things fresh. Oh, and you can call me anything you like─so long as it [@1A(1)]pleases[@1A(0)] you.
My name's─ No, you ain't getting my true name. Just as I didn't get yours, [@1A(1)][@STRING($EB(1))][@1A(0)]. Call me whatever you bloody like.
New recruit, eh? All the whispers and sidelong glances pricklin' ye like knives, I bet.

Well, don't go takin' such petty discourtesies to heart. 'Tis the same greetin' every wanderer newly come to the Path receives. Once ye've spoken with Minfilia, ye'll be one of us, and before ye know it, it'll be [@1A(0)]you[@1A(0)] who'll need remindin' of [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] manners.
You saw one, didn't you? A starshower. I can tell from the sparkle it left in your eyes.
It is said that starshowers affect no two people the same. Yet none can deny their power to move the hearts of all.
I beg of you, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)]─you must help me. I am far too old to fight them on my own.

This is madness! I do not see why I must wait around to be assigned a Path companion. My companion is my bow, and it would serve the Path far better if we were given leave to stop lying low in here and start laying low the imperials out there!
You feel the same, do you not?
Leave me be, wanderer. I have much to deliberate, and there are some paths one must walk alone.

Yer pardons, good [@IF($E9(4),lady,sir)]. Though it breaks me heart, I can no longer care for this...er...[@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] child, here. I beseech thee─take her in and provide her with the good home she so richly deserves! It's what her poor mother would've wanted.
What are you talking with this [@IF($E9(4),lady,man)] about?

I've not woken, and therefore cannot hear the Echo as do the others on the Path. Yet I'll not let that prevent me from setting off on my own search for the truth. You see, when the Empire assaulted Ala Mhigo, I alone of all my family was spared, and I consider it my life's duty to return peace to the realm they loved, and I love still.
Another eyesore come a-calling, eh? Might be that only Lady Minfilia can deny a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] the Path, but step into mine and I'll not hesitate to knock you out of it.

The Twelve bless each and every one of their children with talents. Learn to apply those talents, and you may one day rise to greatness. But give in to arrogance, and the world will shun you as the moonless night.
You are well come to the Waking Sands. This is but a humble gathering place for those who seek knowledge.
There are other such places dotted about the realm, but the Twelve, in their wisdom, have chosen [@1A(1)]this[@1A(0)] place to be the start of [@1A(1)]your[@1A(0)] journey.
I might tell you more, but it is best you first speak with Lady Minfilia. You will find her in the Hall of the First Step.
Best keep yer nose out of trouble, [@IF($E9(4),lass,laddie)]. That's [@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] speciality. Heh heh heh.
An audience with Lady Minfilia, you say? Very well. She waits behind these doors.
Those who walk the Path of the Twelve do so in the hope of apprehending not only the mysteries of the benevolent deities, but also the secrets of their own souls.
If it is truth you seek, then to you our doors shall remain ever open.
And who might you be? Nenekani never forgets a face, and yours is one I am quite [@1A(1)]certain[@1A(0)] I would remember. This must, I conclude, be your first time in the Waking Sands.

And if that is so, then I assume Lady Minfilia will be wanting to speak to you of your awakening. Very well, I shall waste no more of your and the Lady's time with my idle ramblings. You will find the Antecedent in the Hall of the First Step.

You lost, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]? This ain't the Adventurers' Guild, you know. Won't find no ale nor [@IF($E9(4),no silver-tongued bards,no saucy ladies)] within these walls. We serve a greater purpose.
And once you've been enlightened to that purpose, might be that I'll listen to whatever it is you have to say. Until then, though, I've no spare words to waste on you.
Hundreds...thousands...perhaps even hundreds of thousands walk the Path of the Twelve. You need not be one of us to see how far our influence extends throughout the realm.
As of late, our guild has seen many newly woken adventurers pass through its doors, and each day seems to bring more.

I first thought the sudden influx might have had something to do with the Fall of the Keeper, ten summers past. However, after speaking with several of those newly come to the Path, I now believe I may have been mistaken.
For a man such as myself, the Waking Sands is a Twelvesend.
Here, I need not don my merchant's mask, knowing that none will judge me by my station, but only by my desire to pursue the truth.
Hah hah! It seems my anger was misplaced. Shortly after you entered the Hall of the First Step for your audience with Lady Minfilia, I was introduced to my new Path companion.
The marauder brooding over yon. Yes, she seems a touch somber for my tastes...but after a few cold nights on the road, I'm sure she'll warm up to me!
Got myself a partner...but I can't say I like the looks of him. Something to do with the way his eyes barely leave my bodice.
Truth be told, though, I'd rather they stayed there than went peering into the murky depths of my past.

Alright, alright! I cannot tell a lie. This young lass is [@1A(1)]not[@1A(0)] my daughter, and I apologize for leading ye to believe that she was. The girl is the trueborn child of a noble family who lives nearby my tiny hovel. Late one night, not long after a starshower, I saw her wandering the streets alone.

When I asked her where her parents were, she said she hadn't seen them since they kicked her out of their home─this was after she told them she'd been having visions. I am a poor man and have five children of my own to feed, but I could not bear to see her on the streets. Now do you see my predicament?
Please, sir. When can I go home?
I miss my mummy and my daddy. Why won't you take me home?
I bid you accept my apologies. I was wary of revealing my gift to one I did not know. The truth is, I, too, have been woken to the Echo.

However, the power to live another's past is not the “blessing” some think. I've borne witness to many dark memories... So many, in fact, that it has become difficult for me to place my trust in anyone for fear of becoming a dark memory myself. Not knowing what else to do, I came here looking for salvation. Perhaps one day I will have the courage to find it.
People from across Aldenard and beyond the Strait of Merlthor gather here in the Waking Sands to learn of the Twelve and walk their Path in the search for truth.
Those who have chosen this life are called “walkers,” while those who have yet to make the decision to take that First Step are called “wanderers.”

Though you have traveled many malms over sea and land, and seen more in the space of a few moons than most see in a lifetime, you yet lack a path. Without one, you will ever remain bereft of truth, and bereft of a future─a mere wanderer.
Lady Minfilia is one of the few survivors of the Fall of the Keeper─one of the few who remember the horrors of that fateful night, ten years gone.
I am sworn to protect her, and I will give my life before breaking that vow.
We who walk the Path of the Twelve seek to uncover the mysteries of the benevolent deities who bless the children of Eorzea.
Or so we'd have people think.

Nenekani can see the past no more clearly than any man might if he closed his eyes and pictured his breakfast. However, the gods did see fit to bless me with a proficiency in languages, including those of the beast tribes.
It is an aptitude that has proven not only useful, but also [@1A(1)]profitable[@1A(0)].
With chapters across Eorzea to guide us, walkers need never succumb to temptation and wander from the Path of the Twelve.
For alone, we may be lost, but joined together as one, our gifts will save the world.
I myself was woken ten years ago when I saw me a starshower up in the mountains near Ishgard. Not long after, I started havin' these visions.

Once or twice a year is all, mind ye, but it was enough to put the fear in me belly. Afore long, there weren't no one I could trust. 'Twas enough t' drive me wife into the arms of another man. If it weren't fer the Path, the Echo might've killed me. Luckily, it helped me kill someone else first.
Many here have unique gifts, from the ability to bend the will of a beast with a sword, to the ability to bend the will of a beast with a [@1A(1)]word[@1A(0)].

As for those who hear the Echo and can delve deep into the pasts of others, there are yet but few, though their numbers have been on the rise as of late. Who knows what that might portend? Could the Twelve be preparing mankind for a terrible bale?
Please, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)]...I have nothing...and I've seen too many summers to start anew.
If you'll not grant a man life, then at least grant him the mercy of eternal sleep.

The Antecedent still requires more time to deliberate over your choice of Path companion. Once Lady Minfilia has come to a decision, both you and your new companion will be notified via the linkpearl you were presented. You haven't [@1A(1)]misplaced[@1A(0)] it now, have you?

text_en: Audience! The woken ones must grant audience!
There is little time! Little time!
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! A party of frenzied sylphs has spirited past our sentries and trapped Lady Minfilia in the Hall of the First Step!

They have gathered in the Hall, shouting in their strange tongue; however, there are few here who can understand them, myself included! Oh, whatever shall we do? If anything were to happen to the Antecedent...
A pack of strange green beasts just appeared out of nowhere! And now they're demanding audience with the Antecedent!
At least I [@1A(1)]think[@1A(0)] that is what they are demanding. I cannot understand a word they are saying!
Was that a sylph I saw fly by? Impossible... For what purpose would a sylph come all the way from Gridania?
Sylphs in Ul'dah!? How did the devilish creatures ever get past the Brass Blades? Nenekani knows not!
Though...I do seem to recall reading that the sylphs were adept in some sort of queer sylvan conjury. Perhaps they cast a glamour upon themselves and walked right through the city gates!
What folly is this, adventurer? Did [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] bring these heathens into our sanctuary?
I am seeing to the doors to ensure our “guests” cannot leave until we are certain of their intentions. You, however, may pass at will.
Yes, it is true I am somewhat versed in the sylph's tongue, but I cannot leave my post. The safety of those I am entrusted to defend must come first!
The woken ones must hearken! Terrible tidings this one brings!
There has never been any indication that the sylphs intend to do anything so rash. Though, if threatened with eradication, who knows what one might be driven to?
Perhaps it would be better if we did not become involved, lest we invite the ire of the Empire.
It is said this grove of the sylphs' lies deep within the Black Shroud, hidden from the eyes of man, and that only the most skillful trackers can locate it.
Many who enter the forest in search of the grove are never seen again─or so the rumors say...
Take care not to end up a rumor yourself, Walker!
The sylphs crossed forest and desert to beg for our help. It would be wrong of us to turn a deaf ear to their pleas.
You and your Path companion have been entrusted with a task of great import. Contact [@2B($EA(1))] using our linkpearl and make haste for Gridania.
And just like that, the green beasts were gone...but at least they used the door this time.
Sahja Zhwan claims they were sylphs─a beast tribe living deep within the Black Shroud... As if that makes what they did any more acceptable!

Sylph sightings are not as uncommon as you may believe. They are friendly and inquisitive by nature, and rarely harbor ill will towards the five races. Their extensive knowledge of crystals also makes them valuable contacts for merchants in the aether trade.
Though, now that I think of it, there [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] seem to be fewer around the sultanate of late.
Imperials in the Black Shroud... This does not bode well for the realm. First Ala Mhigo, now Moonspore Grove. If the sylphs were to fall, nothing would stand between the Garleans and Gridania.

Still, I take some solace from the fact that the Garleans have yet to succeed in subjugating the tribe. Gods know what's stopping them, though. Could it really be that the sylphs possess a power to rival the Empire's machina?
Dreadful little creatures. It is no wonder they are called “beasts.”
Ah, my pardons, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I did not mean to imply that those whom you seek to assist are unworthy of that aid. Not at all!
One used to be able to find sylphs in all of Eorzea's city[@1F]states, and none would pay them any mind.

As a child, I would spend countless bells with my nose in scholarly tomes, trying to learn their language. I dreamed of asking them to tell me all about their hidden kingdom in the Black Shroud, you see.

While it lies on the edge of the protective “Hedge” which surrounds and protects the Black Shroud, Moonspore Grove is situated closer to the imperial-occupied city[@1F]state of Ala Mhigo than it is to Gridania.
If the Garleans continue their push into Eorzea, it is only a matter of time before the Grove, too, is engulfed in a sea of cerulean flames.

Many believe that the Garleans seek to exterminate the sylphs before the tribe can muster enough power to summon their primal deity─which the Empire refers to as an “eikon,” believing it to be naught but a false god.

Were you able to contact [@2B($EA(1))]?[@CR]Ah, so you have chosen to make your preparations separately before meeting in Gridania and continuing on to the Grove together? It is clear you have given this some thought.

Within the confines of the city, you will find many shops and stands where you can provision for the next leg of your journey. I trust an adventurer of your experience will be able to discern the necessities from the niceties on offer.
It is said this grove of the sylphs' lies deep within the Black Shroud, hidden from the eyes of man, and that only the most skillful trackers can locate it.
Many who enter the forest in search of the grove are never seen again─or so the rumors say...
If you cannot trust your map to aid you, it might be wise to seek the assistance of someone with local knowledge before you set out from Gridania.
Ul'dah is still the only city[@1F]state that's closed its gates to the sylphs.
But rumor has it the Gridanians are losing patience with the green demons, and may soon drive them out. Haven't heard what the pirates think, but I doubt many sylphs make it as far as Limsa.

In a town teemin' with pirates, fishbacks, ratboys, and kobolds, I don't think anyone'd notice if a sylph walked right up the Procession o' Terns, took a seat in the Drownin' Wench, and ordered itself a mug o' salt ale.
But the Garleans'll notice...if they haven't already. And they won't forget where the sylphs went, or who agreed to help them. And soon it'll be too late, even for Limsa.
Sylphs and the Garleans, eh? Naught good'll come of that.
There is some wisdom in ignoring the noble urge to confront those greater evils which loom over us. Men are weak by nature, and as long as we remember that, blood need not be spilled unnecessarily.
I'll be lookin' t' tickle some information on th' Empire out of a couple o' their scouts, I will. I have me ways o' makin' 'em talk. Heh heh heh.
This one will hide woken ones!
This one will blind metal ones!
This one will use magicks! Woken ones will save podlings!
Quick! Quick! Rescuing ones must take the podlings! Take the podlings to the one called Flaxio! But beware! The metal ones must not see! Be silent, be swift!
Minfilia is indisposed. If you have something to report, speak with Lady Tataru.
Sneaking about the forest while iron-clad monsters stalk your every move? Don't tell me you weren't afraid!
Then again, I assume such tasks are second nature to an adventurer such as yourself.
This ain't the first time the Empire has sought to invade the Moonspore Grove and uproot the sylphs.

They always seem to get close, but the beastlings' magicks never fail to pull the proverbial wool over the imperials' eyes. Reminds me of another city[@1F]state what hid themselves from the rest of the realm─Sharlayan.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Tell me, is it true more than half of the sylphs' children were lost?
The poor, poor creatures. Perhaps I misspoke earlier. I myself know what it is to lose a child...
And thus will the sylphs' numbers slowly dwindle, till one day none remain.
If only there were something I could do to protect them! Perhaps I could travel to the Grove and help rebuild! Ah, but they would most likely turn me away...
So you say it was the sylphs' magicks that allowed you to slip into the Grove unnoticed? Amazing...
To think that they could have worn off at any time, putting you at the mercy of an imperial juggernaut! Might your guardian be the Spinner, for you most certainly have Her luck!
The Garleans are intent on slaying every last sylph in the realm before the beast tribe can summon forth their eikon.
I, for one, do not know what the Empire is so afraid of. Any deity who would choose to watch over those glorified vegetables cannot be [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] imposing.
After countless rangings, Dunstan remains unfound. Despite their best efforts, none among the archers, lancers, or conjurers have the faintest idea where he is.
Now more than ever, they would surely welcome your help. The search has their resources stretched thin, and every pair of eyes counts. Ask in at the Quiver's Hold.
Our rangings keep us busy. An adventurer of all people should know the significance of what is transpiring here.
Ah, so it is precisely that which brings you, is it? Very well. Bowlord Lewin is within holding counsel with Brother O[@1F]App. I doubt they will be too much longer.
I feel a great disturbance in the forest...as if millions of voices suddenly cried out in terror. The elementals... We must leave at once!
Set forth into the wood?
Set forth into the wood?
I feel a great disturbance in the forest...as if millions of voices suddenly cried out in terror. The elementals... We must leave at once!
Set forth into the wood?
Set forth into the wood?
You mean to go with them? Have you taken leave of your senses!?
If Brother O[@1F]App wishes it, then it cannot be helped. But know that this is one ranging from which you may well not return.
How did you find things at Quiver's Hold? A ranging!? By the Twelve, you have a deal more courage than I imagined!
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], There is word of a commotion over at Stillglade Fane. Haven't been to see for myself, but I've heard talk of [@1A(1)]wildlings[@1A(0)].
Times like this, there's naught for the commonfolk to do but trust that the conjurers and moogles will calm the wood.
Best go and see if you can't make yourself useful. You adventurers are good at that, are you not?

You wish to know more of Khrimm'm past? For that you must speak to the conjurers. I warn you, though─the good brothers and sisters of Stillglade Fane may not be eager to speak of such things as wildlings.
Welcome, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Please, feel free to join the others within.
Brother O[@1F]App has been expecting you.
A wildling within the city... I fear we have all been placed in great danger.
Brother E[@1F]Sumi will know what to do. He always does.
Dunstan was next in line to command the Wood Wailers until he was...taken from us.
My head... It pounds. And my ears scream with ringing. The voices... The elementals are in great distress.
I don't know what to make of all this. I've never seen the greenwrath so fierce.
Truly, my heart goes out to the poor lad, but is it wise to bring one so tainted to the Fane?
What does Brother E[@1F]Sumi mean to do? If there were some way to assist him, we would, but...the truth is, the rest of us don't have the first idea how.
This Papalymo and this Yda... Where in the bloody hells have they come from? They wield powers unlike any we've ever seen.
My gut tells me Bowlord Lewin may be hiding something from the Quiver. But that would mean Brother E[@1F]Sumi is, as well. Could it be?
Calm down, child! You can't see him now. It's too dangerous.
You cannot pass, Fye. Trust us, it is for your own good.
The grand rite is one of conjury's most sacred and powerful acts. It requires all of our order to come together as one.
I must do all that I am able to aid Brother E[@1F]Sumi. We cannot fail!
Brother E[@1F]Sumi plans to hold counsel with the Seedseers. For now, we must send word to the conjurers still within the wood to return.
Let me in! I have to see him! I have to see Khrimm!
You'll help me, won't you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? Find Brother E[@1F]Sumi, or Brother O[@1F]App. Tell them I'm here!
I have to see Khrimm. I have to talk to him. To tell him I...I'm sorry.
Let me in! I have to see him! I have to see Khrimm!
You'll help me, won't you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? Find Brother E[@1F]Sumi, or Brother O[@1F]App. Tell them I'm here!
I have to see Khrimm. I have to talk to him. To tell him I...I'm sorry.
The grand rite is about to begin. I daresay you must be looking forward to getting all that woodsin off your back.
Not that there are any guarantees when it comes to cleansing the stuff. Oh, but I'm sure you'll be alright. Now stop wasting time and run along to Mih Khetto's Amphitheatre!
Afraid you're going to stick out like an Ul'dahn whore in an Ishgardian church? Hah! Don't worry, it will be over before you know it.
Not even the elementals can turn a deaf ear to the festival. They enjoy the music as much as any.
Who can say what will come of all this? The greenwrath is so thick about the city, even [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] can feel it─and I'm not even a bloody conjurer!
Be quiet! I'm looking for moogles!

I bet the moogles would come if we had some [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000129,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000129,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]. Moogles [@1A(1)]love[@1A(0)] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000129,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000129,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]!
Dance! Dance! Dance!
Mother? Mother? Mother!? Moootheeer!? I've lost my mother...
I'm gonna dance as well as I possibly can. Then the elementals will [@1A(1)]have[@1A(0)] to save Khrimm!
The rite will start once the conjurers gather. Since it is to be a grand rite, Brother E[@1F]Sumi and many others have returned from the wood to take part.
This festival has an interesting history. Originally, it had nothing to do with appeasing the elementals. It was simply a harvest festival─as unremarkable as that might sound.

This grand rite shall be the most important in recent memory. We can afford no mistakes─all the woodsin must be purged. And if the children and the rest enjoy themselves in the process, so much the better.
I've thanks to give for the year's bounty, and prayers to give for next─if it isn't too late...
The woodsin may fall from you, but take care [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] don't fall from the stage. Hahaha!
Ohhh, I can't wait for things to get underway. Me own grandson's goin' to be up there dancin' his little heart out, the adorable lit'l bastard.
They are saying that Khrimm has drawn the greenwrath. But could it truly be? I've not seen him out and about of late...
The lad whose parents went wildling? Hmmm...can't help wondering if a bit of their woodsin didn't get passed on to the boy. I've heard stranger tales told.
From the look of things, this rite is going to be quite large. I'm beginning to wonder if those rumors I heard about a wildling attending might be true after all...
When the elementals rage, there is naught we can do but pray for their forgiveness.
What strange and ridiculous dancing! We have nothing like it back in Sharlayan─thank the gods for that!
They put on joyous airs, to be sure, but there is a sick desperation in their dancing. They fear this greenwrath─that much is obvious.
And our presence here isn't making things any easier for them. Regrettable, that, though I suppose it can't be helped. We must see our work done, after all.
We like to think that even the elementals are soothed by the laughter of innocent children.
But I fear that Khrimm's treachery in the wood may have placed the rest of our younglings at the greatest risk. I pray the conjurers are able to keep them safe.
You are no forestborn. What right have you to take part in this...er...rite?
Brother O[@1F]App, you say? Hmph, I will look into this, I assure you. Twelve save you if you have told me false.
If Dunstan flees, Khrimm's life would be forfeit. No, he will not run. Not Dunstan. He was─ He [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] a man of honor.
Once all are onstage and the rites begin, the forest takes on a very solemn air. And when all is done, that is replaced by an air of peace.
So you are to be cleansed too, are you? Don't remember seeing you around before. An adventurer, I take it? Try not to make a mess of things.
Hello to you, forest...
How in the bloody hells did we get [@1A(1)]here[@1A(0)]!?
Travel to Ul'dah's Merchants Ward by way of the market area. There the hermit of the wood awaits you.
After reaching level 18 with any class, travel to Ul'dah's Merchants Ward by way of the market area. There the hermit of the wood awaits you.
What news from the west Hedge? Is aught amiss? What has come of Brother O[@1F]App? What in the bloody hells is going on!?
You are searching for Brother O[@1F]App? Have you come to ask after Khrimm?
You certainly seem to be coming into your own around here. Though you may not be aware of it, you're quite the talk of the town. But there will be time enough for praises later.

For now, Dunstan is still to be found. The rangings of the guilds' patrols are growing larger and longer, and more frequent besides. No doubt they would welcome the aid of an adventurer such as yourself.
If you've a mind to help, I suggest you head over to the Quiver's Hold. The archers will see you put to good use.
I have need of you. Take this ward and cast its magic over all here. It will protect against the element to which it has been attuned.
The ward is ready! Bless all with its magic!
Which element do you wish to ward against?
I am attuning the ward! A moment, pray!

Ah, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Was about t' send one o' me boys t' fetch ye, I was. 'Eard that lad Emerick's caught yer attention, and ye be keen on payin' 'im a visit o'er on th' 'Cudas' warboat.
Ain't no small feat, that...yet I reckon I knows me a man what could 'elp ye─one Cap'n Hob.

Sound familiar? 'E bloody well should! Th' good cap'n's grace be th' sole reason ye made it t' Limsa in one piece. Like t' be found somewhere down by Fisherman's Bottom, 'e is, 'case ye were wonderin'.
A good many 'ounds been by lately on th' trail o' one Emerick.
But if I told 'em once, I told 'em a thousand times─the bastard be dead an' rottin' at th' bottom o' th' abyss; the Navigator scratchin' 'er arse wi' 'is bones.

Still don't believe me, eh? Then 'ave th' good Cap'n Hob ferry ye 'cross t' the 'Cudas' boat so ye can stare Truth in the eye─jus' don't be surprised if she spits in yours fer disbelievin' 'er faithful servant 'ere! Now off t' th' Bottom wi' ye!
Me bastard son's wed to the daughter of the dromond captain's brother's steward...'s cousin......in-law, so I's as much right to board the ship as the next man.
Perhaps, we should look in on me son...er, steward. Ah... What say ye?
Sail to the dromond?
Sail to the dromond?
You the [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)] Baderon sent?

Good. But we'd best not speak here. Can never know who's listenin' in on that what should be privy. The walls have ears, and them ears has ears of their own. Meet me at the pier in Fisherman's Bottom where we can continue our...business undisturbed.
Open your eyes, 'Cuda! There be Serpent Reavers makin' straight for the dromond!
If I was you, I'd be readyin' me blade for battle...but I ain't [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)], so I'll be waitin' here! Captain's honor! That is, unless ye want to leave now.
Return to Limsa Lominsa?
Return to Limsa Lominsa?
What are you doing out of uniform!? The commodore will have your head if he sees you in those rags!
The fishbacks had best not try anything or the seas will run red with Sahagin blood!
Keeper fend, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]! Th' five seas ain't big enough t' 'old all th' trouble ye've got yerself into.

Not t' mention poor Cap'n Hob! Ye'd best not be ponderin' lettin' 'im rot in the Coral Tower after the kindness 'e showed ye. But if ye still be itchin' t' learn o' that key ye was yappin' on about, might be ye take a detour t' the Gods' Grip afore ye go a-rappin' on the 'Cudas' gates.
Keeper fend, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]! Th' five seas ain't big enough t' 'old all th' trouble ye've got yerself into.

Not t' mention poor Cap'n Hob! Ye'd best not be ponderin' lettin' 'im rot in the Coral Tower after the kindness 'e showed ye. But if ye still be itchin' t' learn o' that key ye was yappin' on about, might be ye take a detour t' the Gods' Grip afore ye go a-rappin' on the 'Cudas' gates.
What in th' seven 'ells are ye doin' 'ere, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]!? Cap'n Hob be down rottin' in the 'Cudas' brig while ye be takin' strolls about the city.
I don't claim t' 'ave an 'eart o' gold, but turnin' th' blind eye to a man what 'elped ye...that ain't right, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

Now, after ye're finished takin' that detour t' th' Gods' Grip, ye get yer arse o'er t' the Tower an' turn yerself in t' the curs. They might jus' grant ye mercy. Wait any longer and ye might wake up one mornin' t' find yerself in shackles.
A...disquieting tale... Yet there is little evidence with which to convict you.
But do not think that I will hesitate to toss you in the brig if I hear you've paid another unannounced visit to one of our ships. On your way, adventurer.
Send a unit to the cliffs off Bearded Rock? And why would we do that?
There hasn't been a Sahagin sighting in that area for nigh on four score turns.
What is this place?
Where is Sthalmann?
Travel to Ul'dah's Merchants Ward by way of the market area. There, Blackburn awaits you.
After reaching level 18 with any class, travel to Ul'dah's Merchants Ward by way of the market area. There, Blackburn awaits you.
Been hearin' naught but bad rumors of late. Dark talk of cursed magicks bringin' the dead back to life─proper nasty stuff.
Not sure if it's connected, but a guard of gladiators and pugilists left the city from the chocobo stables around the time the rumors started. And in quite a hurry, too.
Can't for the life of me put together where they were headed. Somethin' stinks, though―stinks of coin and death.
F'lhaminn's in danger? Where!?
Gods, not again... What the bloody hells is goin' on?
Help us, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Take this gold powder. The beasts will be drawn to it. You must keep them away from here.
The beasts will be drawn to the gold powder. Use it to keep them away from here.
Use the gold dust I gave you to lure the beasts. You must not let them come near here.
Lure the bloody things to me. I'll see them all dead!
Bring them to my blade.
Have you come to visit a patient?
F'lhaminn? Yes, she is being treated here.
The door at the end of the corridor will lead you to the sickrooms. You are free to pass.
I have been ordered to care for Damielliot. There are now some twenty of us tending to him.
Ow! Quit it. Ow! Quit it. Ow! Quit it.
Are you here to visit a patient?
I thought the rumors of F'lhaminn's accident were just that─rumors. But then I saw a gaggle of Ul'dah's most prestigious personages pass by as if they were visiting someone. Could it be true?
Please, you must help us. If you happen to see the bard Thancred, tell him to come with all haste to Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern.
There's been sightin's of an exile wanderin' close to the city. Damn bold, whoever it is.
The laws of Ul'dah don't leave much room for interpretation on that score. Exiled is exiled. And it's best to steer clear of the poor buggers what are. Most think 'em cursed in one way or another.
Still, if you were able to capture this trespasser and serve 'em up to the authorities... Let's just say the sultana can be [@1A(1)]very[@1A(0)] generous to protectors of the peace.
So they'd already found the exile, eh? Shame, that. Still, say what you will of the city guard, them gladiators and pugilists do get things done.
Wouldn't happen to have been that bard who was askin' around about some threat to Ul'dah, would it? I made him for dead at the hands of a thaumaturge by now.
Somethin' ain't right, that much is certain. The city guard's been busy of late. They've even sent a unit of gladiators and pugilists on some sort of secret mission outside the city.
Only reason I know that much is 'cause folks saw 'em settin' out from the chocobo stables. Gods know where they were headed, though.
'Course, it's my business to know these things, so you can be sure I'll be askin' around. I smell trouble, and my nose ain't often wrong.
Travel to Ul'dah's Merchants Ward by way of the market area. There Minfilia awaits you.
After reaching level 18 with any class, travel to Ul'dah's Merchants Ward by way of the market area. There Minfilia awaits you.

text_en: Lady Minfilia has informed me you will be providing assistance to the Ashcrown Consortium.
You [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] be providing assistance, won't you?
Very good. The Consortium's headquarters are located in the Peasants Ward in Gridania.
Your Path companion, [@2B($EA(1))], has already left for the city and will meet you there.
I trust that after your last foray into the Black Shroud, you will no longer require directions...but if you should for some reason, feel free to ask.
That...is most unfortunate. The Antecedent sets great store by your abilities. For you to shun her... Dear me.
Welcome back, Walker. Lady Minfilia has been expecting you. You will find the Antecedent in the Hall of the First Step.
Your assistance is much appreciated...if somewhat unexpected. I had always thought adventurers to prefer a life of freedom over one of service.
I continue to ask myself, can any good come of aiding the sylphs? They claim they mean us no harm, but when all is said and done, how are they different from the other beast tribes?

How can peace ever come to a war-torn realm? Why, Nenekani knows! We must look past our differences and work together to forge a better tomorrow! Fighting amongst ourselves will earn us naught but pain and suffering!

Every man, woman, and Lalafell on the Path has their own opinion regarding which direction we should all take. It is the Antecedent's task to consider each one of those opinions, and then choose one. 'Tis not a job I envy one whit.

There has been much talk of punishing those who stray too far from the Path and betray their fellow walkers. Nothing of that nature has ever happened here, of course, but I worry it is only a matter of time. Only a few moons ago, a man belonging to our Gridanian chapter was banished after it was discovered he was selling information to the Empire.

The Antecedent has many ties with Ul'dah's ruling class, including the Syndicate. However, those ties will not shield us from everything, so we must take care not to violate any of the city[@1F]state's edicts.
Another task for the Path?[@CR]The Ashcrown Consortium? A noble endeavor, indeed.
Crystals form the backbone of Eorzea's economy. By aiding the Consortium, you are contributing to the well-being of every man, woman, and child in the realm.
As of late, it has become nigh on impossible to maintain civilized dialogue with either the Ixal or the Amalj'aa.
But then again, what can one expect when dealing with [@1A(1)]beasts[@1A(0)]?
Lady Minfilia told you the Ashcrown Consortium wants “peace in Eorzea”? Well, of course it does!
Foul blood betwixt buyers and suppliers can only work to hamper the crystal trade. This, Nenekani knows!
Why do I reckon the beast tribes are hoarding all the crystals? 'Cause they ain't the lackwits we imagine 'em to be, that's why.
The livelihoods of many and more of the realm's crafters depend on them crystals. Cut off the supply, and...well, a quick-witted adventurer like yourself can work out the rest.
I hear you will journey again to Gridania. If you mean to go there on foot, you would be wise to pay extra heed to your surroundings.

I have lost count of the number of reports of travelers going missing. Some say it is the wild beasts growing ever more bold, while others say it is the Empire kidnapping Eorzeans to indoctrinate them into their cause.
Going to the Ashcrown Consortium, are we? Say what you will of their practices or their motives, there is no denying that the traders are...[@1A(1)]unique[@1A(0)].
There was once a chapter in Ul'dah, but recent [@1A(1)]events[@1A(0)] have forced them to consolidate their resources in a single location.

The Ashcrown Consortium can be found in Gridania's Peasants Ward. To get there, travel east along the Royal Sunway. Once you have passed the Burning Wall, the road will turn north and become the Lumberline. You need only follow its timeworn path to reach the gates of the forest city.
Your Path companion instructed me to ask you to wait for them at the Consortium's headquarters.
You need not look so surprised. The sylphs have as much right to be here as you or I.
The last thing we need is another outsider calling in the Holtwatch.
For decades, the Ashcrown Consortium has seen to the realm's crystal trade, ensuring that matters run smoothly.

By acting as intermediaries between the beast tribes and the guilds, we have been quite successful in preventing a number of...shall we say, [@1A(1)]unsavory incidents[@1A(0)] between the two parties.
Ahem! I am fluent in over twenty dialects of both Amaljic and Ixali.

I might add that learning the barbaric tongues was anything but simple. Both languages contain sounds that are all but impossible for members of the five races to reproduce. It took many years of rigorous training to acquire the knack, but the rewards for my efforts have made it all worthwhile.
Many of the sylphs you see in Gridania can speak the language of the free cities. Perhaps that is why they have been accepted by the people here.
Words allow us to paint the picture of our soul. Without them, we are a blank...and as you are no doubt aware, men are wont to fear the unknown.
Even in Gridania, whose denizens preach harmony betwixt man and nature, there are those who would look down upon the beast tribes simply because they are different.
That is one of the reasons the Consortium was forced to seek premises on the outskirts of the city. Out of sight, out of mind...

You have our thanks, Walker [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)]. You are not the first we have approached about assisting in inter-tribe negotiations. You are, however, one of very few to accept the task.

Ah, but do not allow me to take up any more of your time. Your Path companion awaits your arrival in Camp Drybone. If you have not already attuned with the aetheryte there, you need only travel due south on the Lumberline, and when the forest thins to desert, you will be close.

Once you have arrived at the outpost, make for the excavation site; but take care not to engage the beastmen before meeting up with the party we dispatched earlier. They will inform you of the situation and your role in the negotiations.
This one wishes only to return to the Grove, but Troxia demands this one stay. Troxia says metal ones will hurt this one...
The grove of the walking ones has many wonders!
Many wondrous happenings to warm this one's heart. Help this one forget podlings lost.
These ones come to this grove to study the ways of the walking ones. So much to learn, yet so little time.
Troxia scolds this one for playing tricks on the walking ones...
But this one means no harm! This one only seeks to make friends. To make friends to play tricks with to make new friends!
The scaled ones and feathered ones once lent their hands.
Those ones would play the tiles, those ones would trade their crystals─but no longer...
The scaled ones have always been proud, but have always been fair. Respect there was for these ones. Respect there was from these ones.
Now, scaled ones respect none but crystals...
The feathered ones have always been loud. Squaaawk! Squawawawk! Squeeeaaawk! Always loud. Always made this one laugh.
Now, feathered ones only scream “crystaaal.” This one misses squawks...
You have our thanks, Walker [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,2)].
Now hurry to the crystal excavation site in eastern Thanalan.
There you will find a party of three Consortium members awaiting your arrival.
The scaled ones cannot be allowed to prevail...
The feathered ones cannot be allowed to prevail...
If it is in battle that you excel, join the fighting at the van, and try to weaken both sides into submission, taking care not to hand victory to either one.
Yet if you abhor violence, as I do, speak with the shamans, and convince them to play the tiles.
If you can best them at parley, they may lay down their staves.
Woken ones must weaken both sides! Neither must emerge victorious!
Attack the feathered ones with drubbings and clubbings! Attack the scaled ones with lashings and thrashings!
The little one spoke of a visit by the shadowless ones. Woken one should feel fortunate [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] soul was not stolen!

What is the Path the woken one walks? Does the Path run north to south, or south to north? East to west, or west to east? The little one says it is a Path these ones cannot see. This one asks, how does one know where the Path is, if the Path cannot be seen?
The scaled ones and feathered ones harbor much anger. Anger born of ignorance.
To quell their anger, both must learn of the other. Only then might there be peace.
These ones are fortunate the scaled ones did not perform a summoning. From the primal comes only flame. Comes only anger.
These ones are fortunate the feathered ones did not perform a summoning. From the primal comes only storms. Comes only fury.
[@STRING($EB(1))]! You must forgive me. I simply could not wait for your arrival, and told everyone of our grand adventure.

While they were understandably disappointed to learn of the failure of our negotiations, and more than a little concerned by the subsequent appearance of the Ascians, the Interlocutors were ultimately satisfied with your efforts. And...well, the fact your keen-eyed companion found that bag of crystals didn't hurt matters, either.
Though they are an integral part of our everyday lives, there is still much we do not know about crystals.
For example, what fell power transformed Silvertear Falls into the crystalline wasteland we know today, and why has the scene of this unknown atrocity so captivated the Empire's attention?
Your efforts in Drybone will likely help stabilize the market for now...
But I believe it is only a matter of time before the price of crystals begins to rise again.

Yes, yes, I see you were successful in bringing back a sizeable sack of crystals─but, from what I hear, [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] was more a matter of luck than judgment. If I recall Nananoby's account correctly, your negotiations with the beast tribes were nothing short of a complete and utter disaster.
Perhaps if you had bothered to study the intricacies of their languages and cultures─as I have─you might have been better prepared for your little adventure.
I am beginning to wonder at the wisdom of persisting with these fruitless negotiations. The beast tribes simply will not compromise.
Perhaps it is time we considered more...[@1A(1)]aggressive[@1A(0)] tactics.
Nananoby says that you did not flinch when faced with even the most terrible of odds.
You have made quite the name for yourself.[@CR]...What was it you said your name was, again?
The woken one is more capable than [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] appears. This one must watch the woken one more closely.
This one hears of adventures from the little one. This one finds the tales hard to believe!
This one shall accompany woken one on [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] next journey. Then this one shall discover the truth!

We have been expecting you for some time, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. The sylphs will be delighted to see you have brought them the remaining [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000096,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000096,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].

text_en: [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], there is something I must ask Lady Minfilia.
You had best hear this as well.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], there's something I wish to ask Lady Minfilia.
I would appreciate it if you accompanied me...in that you [@1A(1)]are[@1A(0)] my Path companion.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]...I have words for the Antecedent.
I would have you hear them.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I wish to pose a question to Lady Minfilia.
Would you be so kind as to accompany me?
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], there is something I feel I simply must say to Lady Minfilia.
I was wondering...if you did not have any other more pressing matters...if you would consider accompanying me? I am not sure I can say what must be said without you there as well.
There is an important issue which I wish the Antecedent to address, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
It would be apt if you accompanied me.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], there's somethin' I need t' speak with the Lady about.
An' I'd be right grateful if me Path companion'd join me when I do. Hope it ain't askin' too much...
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I have something important I wish to ask of Lady Minfilia.
I would be [@1A(1)]very[@1A(0)] grateful if you could be there with me when I do.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], there's something that's been gnawing at my gut since I first joined this guild─and no, it ain't all the extra wine I've been quaffing over at the Quicksand.
Point is, I've got a few words for Lady Minfilia, and I'd be...er...grateful if you were there when I said them, you being my Path companion and all.

text_en: You say the sylphs contacted you on the Consortium linkpearl? You have my condolences, friend.

As long as the Amalj'aa and the Ixal are at each other's throats, we here at the Consortium are left with a mountain to climb when it comes to negotiating for crystals. That is not to say the summit is unreachable, however. Why, as long as there are agents such as myself, who are fluent in over [@1A(1)]thirty[@1A(0)] dialects of beast tongue, there will always be hope for the realm's crafters.

I once urged the sylphs to look for crystals in Mor Dhona, near Silvertear Falls. Suffice to say, they didn't think much of [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] suggestion. How was I supposed to know that the Garleans stationed there had been ordered to kill all sylphs on sight?

Many of our agents employ the “parley” tiles when negotiating with beast tribes. Since the rules are known throughout Eorzea, the game is especially convenient for those of us who do not speak the Amaljic or Ixali tongues.
This one has a riddle: How can one crystal which is not a crystal turn into a bag of many? This one knows! This one knows!
Bury a crystal here?
Bury a crystal here?
Other ones have left the Consortium, but this one shall stay. This one enjoys Ashcrown grove almost as much as Moonspore.
This one hears the lake in the center of Eorzea is a giant eye watching over the realm. This one has not yet seen it, but has [@1A(1)]it[@1A(0)] seen this one?

The Consortium has fallen into debt! Or that is what the interlocuting ones say... This one doubts it is wholly true, for the interlocuting ones have attempted such trickery before. Yet...this one has seen very few crystals in recent moons...

The feathered ones are in the mountains, the scaled ones in the deserts. Now, the metal ones are above the lake with their scoutings and searchings. This one has no place but the forest...but the metal ones want that, as well!
This one dreams and dreams of meeting the Paragons, who the tribal ones say will grant wishes. This one would wish for bigger wings to fly to the skyey realm.
If this one could write the words of the walking ones, much trickery could be achieved. Much, much trickery. Tee hee hee!
It appears the sylphs have taken a liking to you and your Path companion. [@1A(1)]Some[@1A(0)] may consider that fortunate...
I understand this is all quite sudden, but the sylphs mean well. They, as much as any of us, only seek to mend relations between the Amalj'aa and the Ixal.

Collecting [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000096,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000096,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]? How interesting... Though it just might work. While such crystals are practically useless to a crafter who seeks to harness the elemental aspect of the aether, many of the beast tribes consider [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000096,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000096,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] to be of a “purer” state, and therefore better suited to their rituals.

Unfortunately, there is only one place you can obtain [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000096,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000096,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], and that is in the heart of Mor Dhona. The land there has the mysterious quality of draining the element from anything with which it remains in contact for an extended period of time. If you were to bury [@SWITCH($E8(1),a fire,an ice,a wind,an earth,a lightning,a water)] crystal there, I don't suppose it would take long for it to transform into the item you need.

Mor Dhona is an old, old place that is mentioned in the myths and legends of the beast tribes and the five races alike. While the stories vary, all contain references to a great force that slumbers there─though whether it be a force for good or evil depends on whom you ask.
Could it be this force that draws the elemental aspect from crystals?

You say it is [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000096,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000096,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] you seek? Then you were wise to come to Cenmin, for I speak over thirty dialects of beast tongue.

Now, which dialect would you have me translate “[@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000096,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000096,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]” into first? And fear not, I am equally adept at all of them.

I [@1A(1)]knew[@1A(0)] I wasn't wrong to suggest traveling to Mor Dhona, merely wrong in my choice of audience. If it is [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000096,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000096,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] that you seek, there is no better place, or should I say, no [@1A(1)]other[@1A(0)] place.

You need only take several [@SWITCH($E8(1),fire,ice,wind,earth,lightning,water)] crystals, and bury them at certain special locations there. Which special locations, you ask? Oh, if you search about a bit, you're sure to uncover them. Adventurers have an uncanny knack of finding that which needs to be found.

I assume you found Mor Dhona as terrible a place as everyone says. You must be exhausted after such a perilous journey, but Minfilia awaits your arrival. Certainly you have the time to speak with her before retiring to an inn for the night.
The Path of the Twelve has recognized my uncanny talent with dialects, and employed me to assist them in translating several archaic works on the myths surrounding Mor Dhona and Silvertear Lake.

You need not worry, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You have done nothing wrong. Several recent events have given the Antecedent cause for concern, and she would like to discuss them with some of our newer members who may be unfamiliar with the issues at stake.

The others have already gathered in the main hall and await your arrival. Speak with those here in the atrium if you must, but do not take long. Lady Minfilia's patience may seem inexhaustible, but she must not be made to wait unnecessarily.
It is at times such as these that I do not envy the Antecedent. I fear I would be unable to resist the urge to thrash any who stepped out of line.
A lack of strength or wit may lead a man toward his undoing, but it is solitude which sees him undone. This is why we must cling together.
Might you already have an imperial linkpearl? No? Garlean airships have been showering the free cities with them. Perhaps you will find one in the gutter with the night-soil. Nenekani did.
Or perhaps it is better that you did not have one at all...
No blade can cut as deep as fear, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]. To survive, we must steel our wills so they can protect us.
Being an adventurer, I have little doubt that you have willingly faced danger on countless occasions.
May that courage aid you, and inspire those who look to you for guidance, in the dark days to come.
Please, if you would make your way into the main hall. The Antecedent is about to begin.
I knew you would not let me down.

Ah, but there is something else that we might use to our advantage. You see, I overheard on the Ashcrown linkpearl that one of the Paragons was sighted in Thanalan, presumably on his way to see the Amalj'aa. If we can find him, we may be able to convince him to help us in our negotiations with the tribes.

Though, whether we find him or not, I am not so foolish as to go rushing into Paglth'an unprepared. The wounds I suffered in the mesa caves still smart. I will be making my preparations in the city before traveling to the stronghold. You should do the same, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. As always, I'll meet you there.
Splendid! I knew I could count on you!

Now, I have made it a point to listen to the sylph chatter on the Ashcrown linkpearl every day, and I was rewarded for my efforts just this morning when I overheard one of them say that a Paragon has been sighted near the Amalj'aa stronghold of Paglth'an.

And so that is where I think we should begin our quest to convert the tribes! If all goes as planned, not only will we gain ourselves a new ally in the Amalj'aa, but also the knowledge of the Paragons![@CR]Now, I must be off to make my preparations. Shall we meet at the gates of Paglth'an? Good!
Very well.

I have learned from the Ashcrown Consortium linkpearl that the sylphs have sighted one of the Paragons making his way towards the Amalj'aa stronghold in Paglth'an. If fortune smiles upon us, perhaps we can find this traveler and enlist his aid.
Make your preparations and meet me in southern Thanalan, at the gates of Paglth'an. We shall deliver our entreaties together.
Huzzah! May the Twelve smile upon our endeavors.

I should probably take this opportunity to mention that I have overheard mutterings among the sylphs of a Paragon sighting in the vicinity of Paglth'an. If we could find him and somehow sway him to our cause, he would surely be an invaluable ally at the negotiating table.

Of course, we must not allow such thoughts to distract us from our primary objective. Even if the sighting is real, there is no guarantee that the Paragon in question would assist us. No, for the time being, I suggest we focus on the Amalj'aa alone, and make the necessary preparations. I will meet you before the main gate of their stronghold. Godsspeed, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

I understand. It was foolish of me t─ Wait. Did you say yes? You [@1A(1)]did[@1A(0)], didn't you!? Yes to my idea! [@1A(1)]YES![@1A(0)] Hah hah! [@1A(1)]You[@1A(0)] actually said yes to [@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] idea! Mother isn't going to believe this!

Oh, speaking of Mother, I have her to thank for a rather intriguing piece of information. You see, when I'm at home, she rarely lets me out past the eighteenth bell, so I have lots and lots of time to sit in my room listening to my linkpearl collection. Oh dear...I'm boring you, aren't I? I-I'm sorry! The point is, I've been listening to the Ashcrown pearl nonstop, and that is how I came to overhear the sylphs talking about a Paragon sighting in Paglth'an!

And that is what started me thinking...what if we, meaning you and I, were to travel to the Amalj'aa stronghold, find the Paragon, and have him help us convince the beastmen to join us in our fight against the Empire!? It is a brainchild so brilliant, I have rather begun to doubt that I am truly its father! Yet father it I almost certainly did! So, shall I meet you there? Of course I shall! Ta-ta!
A most appropriate answer!
But that is far from all! While listening in on a lately acquired linkpearl, I intercepted an item of interesting information... A Paragon has apparently appeared in the proximity of Paglth'an!
We must make haste into the hot and dusty wastes before our window of opportunity has closed completely!
I knew I could count on ye, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Hey, an' while we're there, we might even run into a Paragon. Been followin' the sylphs' chatter on th' Ashcrown pearl, see, an' from what I gathered, one of 'em's been spotted in southern Thanalan!

Still, 'twouldn't be wise to go pinnin' our hopes on the preservin' powers o' what might be naught but tittle-tattle. From what I know o' the Amalj'aa, there won't be no warm welcomes when we arrive at their gates─'least not the nice kind. We'd best be ready fer th' worst. Meet me at the stronghold entrance once ye've made yer preparations.
Ah hah hah. You truly would do [@1A(1)]anything[@1A(0)] for me, wouldn't you?

Ah, but though we will be acting alone in this, I have recently been given reason to hope that our pairing will soon be joined by a third. Oh, don't be jealous! I mean a [@1A(1)]Paragon[@1A(0)]. You see, I happened to be listening to the Ashcrown linkpearl─the lives of others [@1A(1)]interest[@1A(0)] me─when I overheard some sylphs discussing the reported appearance of a Paragon near the Amalj'aa stronghold.

If we could convince him to join us, imagine what a difference he might make to our relations with the beast tribes! text_en: Alright, listen carefully. When they ask, we will tell them only that we wish to join them in their fight against the Empire, nothing else. No mention of crystals or primals, as we saw how well that worked last time. We can also tell them of the Path and the Echo as well, if you believe it will provide us extra leverage.

If the chance presents itself, we must assure them that we are here not to fight, but to request their assistance in standing against the Empire. I believe we should tell them of the Echo, as well, as proof we are not without our own strengths.

If they prove willing to listen to us, we must choose carefully what we say, for our lives may rest on those words. I believe a simple explanation of who we are and the cause we represent will suffice. We must then assure them that standing with us against the Empire is the only viable means of securing the peace of the realm.

Once the opportunity presents itself, we must convince them of our desire to join in their struggle against the Empire. I believe that if we also mention the Path and the Echo it can only lend credence to our claims.

I was thinking...before a beheading... Yes, I know it's not good for morale to be discussing beheadings, but please, hear me out. Before an “execution,” let's say, the captor always allows the condemned a chance to say a few last words. Well, what better time to tell them who we are, and why we've come!? They are certain to listen! ...Aren't they?
Once they've led us to their leaders, I suggest that you stay silent as I exhort the elders to accept the Antecedent's offer of an alliance. Agreed?

If they ever get 'round t' draggin' us off t' see their elders, we'd best decide on what story t' tell 'em. Keep it simple, I say. State Lady Minfilia's plan, an' allow 'em t' chew on th' proposition. Too much talk won't do us no good when dealin' with these buggers.
Should they do so, we must waste no time in explaining Lady Minfilia's proposition. The sooner we can demonstrate that we come in peace, the better we'll all get on.

Now, here's what we'll say if they allow us a few words. First, we tell them that we have no quarrel with their kind. Then, we tell them about Lady Minfilia's plan to stand against the Empire. If that doesn't get a reaction out of them, well, we can consider ourselves supper, because I ain't got any ideas beyond that.

text_en: [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),Good evening,Good morrow)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),Good day,Good evening)])] to you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. My apologies for making you come on such short notice, but I've been thinking about what Lady Minfilia said─about joining the beast tribes to defend the realm against the Empire.

What if [@1A(1)]we[@1A(0)] were the ones to convince them to join us? We possess the Echo, so communication won't pose a problem, and we have already proven ourselves capable enough when faced with a challenge. Yes, it would most likely be more difficult than our previous missions, but it wouldn't be impossible.

But I do not think I could accomplish this alone, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. As my Path companion, there is no one I would rather have at my side than you. Will you accompany me to the Amalj'aa stronghold of Paglth'an?

Thank you for coming.[@CR]Over the past few days, I've spent a lot of time pondering what Lady Minfilia said about joining the beast tribes. At first, I couldn't help thinking that it would be downright folly to even contemplate such a drastic course of action...

But after considering the alternative...the tribes began to seem more and more inviting. So, I began to wonder how I...how [@1A(1)]we[@1A(0)] might play our part. And that is when I had the most amazing idea!
[@1A(1)]We[@1A(0)] could visit the beast tribes and convince them to join the Path!
[@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),Good evening,Good morrow)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),Good day,Good evening)])], [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I have a proposition for you.
I have spent many a turn of the sun contemplating Lady Minfilia's words regarding a possible alliance with the beast tribes. And I have come to a conclusion.
I believe we should use the Echo to conduct our own negotiations with the Amalj'aa.
Thank you for coming, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I apologize for the mystery, but this plan to join forces with the beast tribes is a matter that requires a certain amount of discretion.

Needless to say, I have considered the matter very deeply. In doing so, I came to wonder if we might not be the perfect candidates for such a mission. With the Echo granting us our talent with languages, who else is better equipped to treat with the tribes?
What say you? Will you do the honor of joining me, your Path companion, on this duty of paramount importance? Shall we stride side by side into Paglth'an, the very stronghold of the Amalj'aa?

You came! Oh, I was beginning to worry that I might never see you again! And then what would I have done? I could not hope to accomplish what I have planned without the aid of my wise, kind, patient, and [@IF($E9(4),surpassingly beauteous,exceedingly dashing)] Path companion.
And what is it that I have planned, you ask? Oh, trust [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] to show an interest in the trifling ruminations of a man as tiny as I! My noble companion truly does have a heart of gold!

Sorry? What [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] my idea? Oh! I haven't told you yet, have I!? Right, yes, well, I propose a journey into the deepest depths of Paglth'an to parley with the Amalj'aa and win them to Lady Minfilia's cause!

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I have carefully considered the comments made during the course of our conversation with Lady Minfilia, and have come to a conclusion concerning our next course of action.
You and I have been gifted with a glorious gift that gives us the capacity to converse with anyone, anywhere. Why, even with the Amalj'aa!

And so why, I ask with much wonderment, would the Antecedent not want us to wield that wonderful power with which we have been so wondrously endowed? Why would she not wish us to pay a visit to Paglth'an and entice the Amalj'aa into accepting our offer of an alliance?

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Ye have me apologies fer makin' ye come all the way out here, but I wasn't keen on speakin' o'er the aether. Cannot know who'll be listenin' in, and the matters I mean t' discuss are o' the utmost import.
I suppose ye recall what Lady Minfilia said about joinin' the beast tribes. Well, I've been givin' the idea a good deal o' thought as of late, an' I reckon I've come up with a solution o' me own.

We've both been touched by th' Twelve an' can understand th' beast tongues, right? So, why can't it be us as convinces th' tribes t' join Minfilia's cause? We can start with the Amalj'aa in Paglth'an.

Ah...[@1A(1)]there[@1A(0)] you are! I was beginning to imagine life without you. Needless to say, it didn't seem anywhere near as pleasurable. Anyway, to come directly to the point─since last we met, I've found myself thinking about Lady Minfilia...

Specifically, her mention of a union with the tribes. Now, aside from our more [@1A(1)]obvious[@1A(0)] qualities, you and I have been blessed with a gift which enables us to converse with whomever we choose─male or female, man or beast.

Are we not, therefore, precisely the kind of people to convince the tribes to join Lady Minfilia's cause? I know it may seem unusually forward, even for me, but I propose that we throw caution to the wind and travel to Paglth'an, there to parley with the Amalj'aa.
I see you finally made it. I'm sorry about all the secrecy, but I don't trust those linkpearls. You can never know who may be listening in.

Now, as to why I called you here: ever since Lady Minfilia told us about her plans to ask the beast tribes for help, I've been doing a pirate's worth of drinking, and a scholarly's worth of thinking, and I reckon I've finally come up with a way for us to help.

You and I, we're both touched by the Twelve, which means we can communicate with the tribes just as well as any bugger on the Path. Hells, after all that practice with the sylphs, I'd even say we were better than most. So, why not put that talent to use? Why not go and parley with the beast tribes ourselves?
I knew you would not let me down.

Ah, but there is something else that we might use to our advantage. You see, I overheard on the Ashcrown linkpearl that one of the Paragons was sighted in Thanalan, presumably on his way to see the Amalj'aa. If we can find him, we may be able to convince him to help us in our negotiations with the tribes.

Though, whether we find him or not, I am not so foolish as to go rushing into Paglth'an unprepared. The wounds I suffered in the mesa caves still smart. I will be making my preparations in the city before traveling to the stronghold. You should do the same, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. As always, I'll meet you there.
Splendid! I knew I could count on you!

Now, I have made it a point to listen to the sylph chatter on the Ashcrown linkpearl every day, and I was rewarded for my efforts just this morning when I overheard one of them say that a Paragon has been sighted near the Amalj'aa stronghold of Paglth'an.

And so that is where I think we should begin our quest to convert the tribes! If all goes as planned, not only will we gain ourselves a new ally in the Amalj'aa, but also the knowledge of the Paragons![@CR]Now, I must be off to make my preparations. Shall we meet at the gates of Paglth'an? Good!
Very well.

I have learned from the Ashcrown Consortium linkpearl that the sylphs have sighted one of the Paragons making his way towards the Amalj'aa stronghold in Paglth'an. If fortune smiles upon us, perhaps we can find this traveler and enlist his aid.
Make your preparations and meet me in southern Thanalan, at the gates of Paglth'an. We shall deliver our entreaties together.
Huzzah! May the Twelve smile upon our endeavors.

I should probably take this opportunity to mention that I have overheard mutterings among the sylphs of a Paragon sighting in the vicinity of Paglth'an. If we could find him and somehow sway him to our cause, he would surely be an invaluable ally at the negotiating table.

Of course, we must not allow such thoughts to distract us from our primary objective. Even if the sighting is real, there is no guarantee that the Paragon in question would assist us. No, for the time being, I suggest we focus on the Amalj'aa alone, and make the necessary preparations. I will meet you before the main gate of their stronghold. Godsspeed, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

I understand. It was foolish of me t─ Wait. Did you say yes? You [@1A(1)]did[@1A(0)], didn't you!? Yes to my idea! [@1A(1)]YES![@1A(0)] Hah hah! [@1A(1)]You[@1A(0)] actually said yes to [@1A(1)]my[@1A(0)] idea! Mother isn't going to believe this!

Oh, speaking of Mother, I have her to thank for a rather intriguing piece of information. You see, when I'm at home, she rarely lets me out past the eighteenth bell, so I have lots and lots of time to sit in my room listening to my linkpearl collection. Oh dear...I'm boring you, aren't I? I-I'm sorry! The point is, I've been listening to the Ashcrown pearl nonstop, and that is how I came to overhear the sylphs talking about a Paragon sighting in Paglth'an!

And that is what started me thinking...what if we, meaning you and I, were to travel to the Amalj'aa stronghold, find the Paragon, and have him help us convince the beastmen to join us in our fight against the Empire!? It is a brainchild so brilliant, I have rather begun to doubt that I am truly its father! Yet father it I almost certainly did! So, shall I meet you there? Of course I shall! Ta-ta!
A most appropriate answer!
But that is far from all! While listening in on a lately acquired linkpearl, I intercepted an item of interesting information... A Paragon has apparently appeared in the proximity of Paglth'an!
We must make haste into the hot and dusty wastes before our window of opportunity has closed completely!
I knew I could count on ye, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Hey, an' while we're there, we might even run into a Paragon. Been followin' the sylphs' chatter on th' Ashcrown pearl, see, an' from what I gathered, one of 'em's been spotted in southern Thanalan!

Still, 'twouldn't be wise to go pinnin' our hopes on the preservin' powers o' what might be naught but tittle-tattle. From what I know o' the Amalj'aa, there won't be no warm welcomes when we arrive at their gates─'least not the nice kind. We'd best be ready fer th' worst. Meet me at the stronghold entrance once ye've made yer preparations.
Ah hah hah. You truly would do [@1A(1)]anything[@1A(0)] for me, wouldn't you?

Ah, but though we will be acting alone in this, I have recently been given reason to hope that our pairing will soon be joined by a third. Oh, don't be jealous! I mean a [@1A(1)]Paragon[@1A(0)]. You see, I happened to be listening to the Ashcrown linkpearl─the lives of others [@1A(1)]interest[@1A(0)] me─when I overheard some sylphs discussing the reported appearance of a Paragon near the Amalj'aa stronghold.

Of course, should the reports turn out to be false, we still make a formidable team in our own right. Nevertheless, I daresay things [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] get a little hairy in Paglth'an─and possibly somewhat scaly─so I suggest we go and make careful preparations, and meet before the entrance to the Amalj'aa stronghold with suitable protection.
