Right, well, now that you're on board, I'll tell you the best bit. See, these past few turns of the sun, I've made a point of listening in to the sylph chatter on the Ashcrown pearl. Most of the time, it ain't naught but those oversized gourds yattering on about how they tricked some poor sod of an adventurer into doing something menial, but last night, I finally caught something useful... Seems a Paragon has been spotted in the Amalj'aa stronghold of Paglth'an!

Now, I say we head to Paglth'an ourselves and see if we cannot find this Paragon. Could be that he's willing to help us negotiate with the tribes, or at least tell us how best to go about it. The beastmen obviously listen to him. What do you say, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? Meet me there in a few bells? Good [@IF($E9(4),on you, lass,lad)].
Worry not, my [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]. You will soon grow accustomed to your new home.
Once you have been tempered in the flames, you shall be born anew. As was I.

It has been long since I saw you last, Walker. Oh, you need not worry, I never forget a face. Some of these others, though...well, you may have to visit the Waking Sands more often if you wish to gain recognition amongst them.
For every new walker who steps onto the Path, there is another who steps off, never to be seen again. I often wonder what cruel fate befalls those errant souls.

There have been fell rumors of the beast tribes abducting normal citizens and brainwashing them into joining their ranks, only to use them as fodder in their petty wars. Let us hope they are but rumors...
Though many say that the Serpent Reavers of Vylbrand are made up of traitors and brigands who betrayed their own kind, could it be that they, too, are simply victims of this brainwashing?
I am from Gridania where the spirits of the wood ensure that the Ixal do not defile the forest.
However, the spirits cannot be everywhere at once, and so there are still those who lose their lives to the beastmen.
The message on the imperial linkpearl states we are not to be fooled by the appearance of the sylphs, for they, too, are beastmen like the Amalj'aa and Ixal.
If that is so, then why does Lady Minfilia insist on aiding them? Perhaps it is time I left the Path...
The Sahagin and kobolds continue to summon their primals as well.

We hear little about Titan and Leviathan on Aldenard, but on Vylbrand, reports of terrible tremors tearing down buildings and towering waves washing away entire fishing villages are supposedly quite common.
You went to Paglth'an!? Have you taken leave of all your senses!? You could have been killed!
Then again, your bravery will more than likely earn you the praises of the smallfolk. There is no love for the Amalj'aa here in the sultanate.
Step lightly, Walker. Parties most unsavory are starting to take notice of your actions.
I'm not one to stop you from smashing in a few heads every now and then, just don't go mentioning the Waking Sands. There are those here who do not revel in the attention like you do.
There are many amongst us who are not skilled in sorcery or swordplay, and many more who have lost loved ones to war, be it with the Empire or with the beast tribes.
While the Lady Minfilia may speak for all of us, she does not speak with our voice. Reflect on that when choosing your next step on the Path.
You [@1A(1)]spoke[@1A(0)] with Ifrit!?
This gift of ours is truly amazing...though I am not sure I [@1A(1)]want[@1A(0)] to hear what a terrible fire-breathing deity has to say.
You truly believe the bilge Minfilia's been spewing about us saving the world with our godly powers? Hah! Then you're as naive as she is.
Those who linger in the past can never grasp their place in the future. Mark my words, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]. Use the Echo to save others, and who'll save you?
Chatted with a primal, did ye? Did them ones from Limsa turn up brandishin' their blades?
Please, [@IF($E9(4),milady,milord)]. You say you saw others who were captured by the Amalj'aa? Were there any who looked like me?

You see, I am searching for my sister. She was traveling through southern Thanalan when her chocobo coach was attacked by beastmen raiders. They never found any bodies, so I still hope that she may simply be in a cell somewhere in Paglth'an. Yet I worry for her safety. Please tell me you saw her!
You... You are [@2B($EA(1))]'s Path companion, are you not? I knew it! Nenekani never forgets a face.
Your friend was here when the mysterious message arrived...but went dashing out of the Sands even as it finished. I wonder why?

text_en: Who ever could have sent that spine-chilling plea for help?
If anyone would know, I suppose it would be Lady Tataru, as she keeps the Path register.
Linkpearls are given by Lady Minfilia to all who walk the Path. There must be thousands of them in circulation.
When a walker abandons the Path, they are asked to return the pearl. However, there are many who have left on assignments only to vanish in the field. [@1A(1)]Their[@1A(0)] pearls could be anywhere.
With the Empire breathing down our necks and beast tribes hammering at our gates, the last thing the Path needs is any more reason to panic.
Which is why the Lady Minfilia needs to start considering a little more carefully who she passes out them pearls to.
Lady Tataru's summons sounded awfully urgent, but from the looks of things here, one would not know it.
Of course, it may simply be that we have all grown numb to the urgency of such pleas, so common have they become over the past few moons.

Little is known about linkpearls, other than that they somehow manipulate the planet's aether, allowing us to project our voices over long distances, in a similar way to how aetheryte enables bodily transport.

Yet the system has many quirks, and missent or missing messages are an everyday occurrence on most linkshell channels. There is a good chance that the message which arrived earlier wasn't even intended for the Path.
We still do not know the precise identity of the person who sent the message, but Lady Minfilia has narrowed down the possibilities.
You say you assisted the Ala Mhigan Resistance in rescuing one of their scouts?

Will they be visiting the Waking Sands? If so, we must make the proper preparations. They will require food, ale, and beds. They will also desire an audience with the Antecedent, and possibly─ Oh, I am sorry, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I did not mean to ramble.

Rumor has it that after taking Ala Mhigo, the Empire constructed a massive wall to prevent the people of the fallen city[@1F]state from escaping back into Eorzea; yet no one has been able to draw close enough to learn if this is true or not.
No one, that is, except the Ala Mhigan Resistance. Perhaps if the chance presents itself, you should make an inquiry.

Heard you helped the Resistance, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. For nigh on thirty years, those men and women have refused to give up the fight to reclaim their home, though they face incredible odds.

Under normal circumstances, I'd embrace you and offer you my thanks...but Lady Minfilia looked less than pleased when she learned of your triumph, so I will keep my appreciation of your deed to myself. Don't want to go incurring the ire of the Antecedent now, do I?
So the call for help was from a scout being hounded by the Empire.

While I am sure it was your lack of hesitation in making the decision to join the search that ultimately saved the woman's life, you must try and understand why Lady Minfilia cannot wholly approve of your actions. You have been fortunate thus far, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], but you cannot win every battle. One day, your ambition will prove your downfall.
This is not the first time the Path has aided the Ala Mhigan Resistance.
But since seeing off the ones who visited before, there have been no reports of their whereabouts. I hope nothing ill has befallen them...
Listen to these brave men and women and you'll know why my Path is set in stone.
These men and women have been through so much. I only ask that you listen to all of their tales before passing judgment.
I have naught to say to you until you have heard the voices of my brothers and sisters of the Resistance.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Before you ask me my opinion, I plead that you first lend your ear to the tales of these brave men and women.
Oh, you needn't speak with me. My insignificant opinions are but motes of dust in a sandstorm compared to those of the brave men and women here in this Hall. Why not see what they have to say?
Still not spoken with all these strapping soldiers? Then why are you wasting your time tittering away with yours truly?
I ask that ye hear th' words o' these brave lads an' lasses. Their tales'll open yer eyes an' ring true in yer soul.
Not spoken with the others yet? Well, what are you waiting for? Or did you think I might get jealous?
I see you still ain't talked to all the Resistance members. Well then tell me how you expect to make any sort of rational decision if you ain't privy to all the facts, eh?

text_en: During my time as Antecedent, I have seen many like that one. Their intentions are good, but they are ever at the mercy of their emotions. And once they have found a cause to latch onto, they blindly follow it where'er it would lead them─most...never to return.

Your companion understands my fears and knows them in [@SWITCH($E8(2),his,her)] heart to be true, just as I understand why [@SWITCH($E8(2),he,she)] will follow [@SWITCH($E8(2),his,her)] own path, regardless of what I say.
Your Path companion seemed to be in quite a hurry. I believe I overheard something about traveling to Silvertear Falls.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Is aught amiss?
Your Path companion seemed distressed when leaving with the Resistance captain. Won't you be joining [@SWITCH($E8(1),him,her)]?
Ungh... This wound may be worse than I thought. I should have someone at the Waking Sands attend to it before it starts to fester. Let us go, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Ngh... These hurts may be worse that I thought... I'm beginning to feel light-headed. Come, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Ngh... I must see my wounds tended to. Let us leave this place.
<wince> I fear my wounds are more serious than I first supposed. Come, let us go.
Ow! Owww... I-I fear I may be about to take a turn for the worse... Might we go somewhere more...medicinal?
Ngh... Are you ready yet? I require rest and respite to heal my hurts, and here I will receive neither.
Gah... How about we head back, eh? I could do with, say, eleventeen flagons o' wine t' calm me nerves...

Oh...oooh...ow. I think the afterglow is finally wearing off... I'm starting to feel like I did after that time at the Gladiators' Guild... Never again will I agree to take on all comers. Ow! Uh, anyway, let us go somewhere more civilized, shall we?
Ngh... We need to get back to the city so I can find myself a skin of wine to pour on these cuts...and another dozen or so to help me forget them.
Your Path companion's wounds are...grievous. Yet I do not believe they will prove fatal. [@SWITCH($E8(1),He,She)] will live to fight another day...
...unlike those brave men and women from the Resistance. May the Twelve watch over their souls.

text_en: Minfilia is currently in the Hall of the First Step giving audience to an important client.

You have been granted permission to join the dialogue, but only if you first give your word that you will never repeat what you hear behind those doors. If the Empire were to learn of our pl─ Ah, but my tongue has already betrayed me.
The Antecedent and her guests await you in the Hall.
We cannot allow the plight of the Ala Mhigans to be ignored.
The Waking Sands has been gathering food, medicine, and other essentials for the Resistance to take back with them to Ala Mhigo.
Nenekani never forgets a face, and therein lies my problem. The faces of these recent guests from Ala Mhigo are haunting my dreams!
I do not even want to think of the torments one would have to endure to acquire such a turned, twisted, and altogether terrifying visage.
I ain't sure I agree with what the Antecedent has planned for the Path. It all seems so sudden.

What if something were to go wrong? What if we were to be betrayed? Think of all the lives that would be lost then. Lady Minfilia is quick to talk about always moving forward on the Path to Truth, but when danger lies ahead, I say there ain't nothing wrong with taking a few steps back.
To ensure that our guests are not disturbed after their arduous journey, I have been instructed not to allow anyone beyond these doors without the express permission of the Antecedent.
After all they went through to get here, a brief gift of respite is more than well deserved.

Many of our newer walkers have been sent on smaller tasks to...shall we say, keep them occupied while the Antecedent and the Resistance flesh out their plans. It is not that we do not trust them with the information... Alright, it [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] that we do not trust them with the information. With enemies on all sides, one can never be too careful.
For every man and woman you see here standing before you, there are a thousand more who remain trapped in Ala Mhigo, suffering under the weight of the Empire's rule.

Since the day the Wall was built, there has been only one way out of the city─a single road which stretches north into the Garlemald wastes. Unless something is done, a whole generation of children will grow up never knowing Eorzea. Never knowing freedom.

The Empire is using Ala Mhigo as a breeding ground for new soldiers. Once children reach a certain age, they are taken from their parents and sent into the north for training...never to be seen or heard from again.

The road leading south from Ala Mhigo is the road to freedom, barred to us by the Empire. We dream of one day reopening that road to all, and we will gladly pay any price to make that dream a reality.
We have many men and women stationed in city[@1F]states and hamlets across Eorzea collecting vital information on the Empire's movements.
The scout whom you and your companion saved was to be stationed in Gridania before her injuries... Now, we can only pray to the Twelve that she recovers enough to take up her charge.

Many lives were lost ensuring that those of us you see here could make it beyond the Wall. My brother was killed, as was someone dear to your Path companion. And while my heart wells with sorrow, so too does it well with pride, knowing that they died for a greater good.

Which is what makes the success of this mission so important. Since our escape, the Empire has increased the number of guards who patrol the city[@1F]state, and were we to fail, this might very well be the last party ever to make the journey south from Ala Mhigo.
I was born in Ala Mhigo after the fall, so until now, I knew naught but the scarred city's walls.

This is the Eorzea that my mother and father walked when they were young; this is the boundless sky they gazed up at, faces aglow with the warm light of freedom. I will see to it that they walk here again...even if it means giving my life.

I ask that you be not hasty, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], but weigh your decision with the utmost care. Great peril awaits those who accept this mission. Answer not until you have listened to the words of the captain, and then, if you would still stake your life on this endeavor, I shall not stand in your way.
As you know, Lady Minfilia is treating several very important guests in the Hall. They have risked much in their traveling here.
Did you make it a point to listen to each and every one of their tales?

You have heard the words of the captain and his men and women. You have also heard my concerns. However, the Path you walk is your own, and you must make your own decision on the direction you take. Just remember, there are some gates through which one might pass that admit no return.
I know of the operation the Ala Mhigan Resistance has planned, for I was invited to take part myself.
And, as much as I would have liked to, I knew my talents would be better put to use here than on the battlefield. I doubt there will be much need of a translator once swords begin clashing.

During my time as Antecedent, I have seen many like that one. Their intentions are good, but they are ever at the mercy of their emotions. And once they have found a cause to latch onto, they blindly follow it where'er it would lead them─most...never to return.

Your companion understands my fears and knows them in [@SWITCH($E8(2),his,her)] heart to be true, just as I understand why [@SWITCH($E8(2),he,she)] will follow [@SWITCH($E8(2),his,her)] own path, regardless of what I say.
Mama...
Please... I'm so tired...
Where are we going?
Where are you from? I'm from Ala Mhigo.
Even the discipline and determination of the Resistance was not enough to withstand the sheer power of the Empire's machina...
From what I hear, the legatus alone slew half of their force...and suffered nary a scratch to his stygian armor.
Nenekani will never forget the faces of those who died at the hands of the Empire. I shall see personally that their names live on!
Born on a battlefield, and died on a battlefield.
That ain't no life for a man... No...
No matter how many imperial soldiers the Resistance slay in battle, there will always be another airship from Garlemald to bring replacements.

It would take the citizens of every city[@1F]state and hamlet in Eorzea standing together as one to make the Empire so much as pause for thought...and even then, their machina would probably annihilate us anyway.
To ensure mission details were kept secret, I had the doors to the hall barred for the duration of the Resistance members' stay.

Many of the people here did not even notice our guests' presence...and so when the Resistance was defeated in Mor Dhona, there was no reason to inform them...sparing everyone a great deal of unnecessary pain.

Accidents in the shaft ain't as rare as most think. Everyone knows about the cave-ins, but most don't hear o' the floods. A slower death, but just as certain. Respect the rules and reduce the risk─that's what we say 'round here. And it's all the advice I got to offer.
Fifty years, I've worked these mines...and in all that time, I've had but three finds worth mentioning. The first, a diamond cluster. The second, a virgin vein of precious ores.
And the third, and by far the sweetest, is this fine, fine mead that finds its way into my belly on a daily basis. Hahaha!
As the mines age, it becomes difficult to keep track of what connects to what. Don't go gallivanting around down there, lest you end up starving or worse.

Haha, look at the peach-soft palms on this one. New, eh? I know what you're thinking. Is it safe for a little lady like me to be in a mineshaft? Well don't you worry about me. Underneath this gear, I'm built like a brick privy!
If you're new to the Concern, might be best to start working out in the wilds rather than down in the shafts.
If you're going to the Nanawa Mines, make sure to say your hellos to the brothers, Seserukka and Popokkuli. They are the guildmaster's twin sons. One of them stands to inherit the title, someday.
Make your way to the Nanawa Mines when you can. It is Amajina & Sons' main base of operations.
There will likely be a Miqo'te at the mine's entrance. Her name is Z'ssapa. Speak to her to learn what you must do.
<sigh> Always the same with those two─competing over the most infantile things. I fear for the future of this guild...
But you'd best do as they say. Just be wary of any beasts─the outlands have their share of them. And bring me back anything you find. Meanwhile, I'll...stand here. Gods, I'm so borrred.
Are you mocking just me, or the entire guild? This is worthless. I've seen finer [@1A(1)]coprolites[@1A(0)] than this!
<purr> And [@1A(1)]just[@1A(0)] when I thought I might die of boredom, you turn up with [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)]. Let's have a look!
This...isn't all bad. There is something about it... Something that makes me...sleepy...
But it still won't be enough, knowing the twins. It will take something truly extraordinary to impress them. Keep looking, and bring me anything you find.
<purr> And [@1A(1)]just[@1A(0)] when I thought I might die of boredom, you turn up with [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)]. Let's have a look!
Now this is quite a find for a novice. But I doubt it'll be enough to convince the twins to let you in... Sorry.
But it still won't be enough, knowing the twins. It will take something truly extraordinary to impress them. Keep looking, and bring me anything you find.
<purr> And [@1A(1)]just[@1A(0)] when I thought I might die of boredom, you turn up with [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)]. Let's have a look!
Well, well, this is certainly no stone, but still... Such a strange shard... You may have a natural talent for digging after all.
But it still won't be enough, knowing the twins. It will take something truly extraordinary to impress them. Keep looking, and bring me anything you find.
If she suffers so much as a stubbed toe, gods help me...I will [@1A(1)]end[@1A(0)] you!
That's our little sister. She may not look it, or sound it, or smell it, but she's our blood. If anything happens to her, anything [@1A(1)]at all[@1A(0)]...
There they go again, the territorial oafs. Always the same nonsense... So borrring!
I hate to inconvenience you, but my brothers worry for my safety. Would you be so kind as to see me home? I'd be in your debt.
Met Nenekko, have you? She's the daughter of the Concern's guildmaster, you know, and sister to the twins. Imagine the riches she's bound to come into!
Though she'll not put them to a bit of good, knowin' her. Gods know why she's so taken with those old ruins.
Only privileged members of the Miners' Guild are permitted in the deep shafts of the Nanawa Mines. Adventurers are given leave only to enter the public shafts.
I couldn't tell you what lies in the depths even if I wanted to─which I don't. Who knows? Maybe a city of bloody gold.
So you met Popokkuli and Seserukka? Are they as incorrigible as ever? Aye, they've always been that way.
I've known 'em since they were whelps at the teat. It may look like they don't get on, but they're always at each other's side, thick or thin. They share a special bond, those twins.
Best watch yourself around little Nenekko. Those brothers of hers aren't the only ones with their eyes on her.
She has [@1A(1)]far[@1A(0)] more powerful guardians. Draw their wrath, and you stand to lose a good deal more than your mining rights.
To speak to Nenekko, you'd never know she shared the same blood as her brothers. She wasn't raised for a life around the mines, you see.
Her rearing was that of a lady─playing at house and learning needlework, garbed in fine silks and cloth-of-gold. Her world is not that of Amajina & Sons.
Dug yourself up a little something, did you? Aye, I myself have a curiosity for such curios. Hehehe!
Most Ul'dahns are bloody fools, and don't you forget it. They know the cost of everything, and the value of nothing!
It seems the twins have taken notice of you already. They may come across a bit rough, but they are dutiful, caring boys. You need only see them around their sister Nenekko to know as much.
The surest way to advance in this guild is to have nothing to do with Nenekko. No good will come of it. I apologize, I should have told you when first you came to us.
But, since it seems she has already warmed to you, I suppose there's naught to be done for it. She is a sweet girl, truly, but can be trouble. When she is taken by one of her fits of wanderlust...
Well, you need only endure the drama until you are granted your entry permit to the deep shafts. Then you'll be able to pass the days in a miner's paradise!

Welcome to the Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern, overseers and operators of mines throughout the region. You will no doubt have heard of certain of our better-known sites─the Nanawa Mines, for instance.
There are even mines which we have opened to the public─the quality of their remaining resources no longer being conducive to commercial mining, you understand.
If you wish to gain access to the mines that will yield truly [@1A(1)]valuable[@1A(0)] ores and gems, you will first have to join our Miners' Guild. I assume that is why you are here?
Will you join the Miners' Guild?
A decision you will not regret. You have just taken the first step towards striking it rich!

Ul'dah is a commercial center which thrives on trade and is teeming with merchants, but we boast our own well-developed industries, as well. The materials we miners provide help lay the foundation upon which they build.

The lands around Ul'dah are naught but barren wastes of rock and sand. Look beneath them, however, and things could not be more different. Veins of gold, silver, and copper beyond measure! Near every excavation yields a new discovery.

Our studies show that we have only just scratched the surface. The vast majority of minerals still lie hidden, deep below. And who knows? It may yet be you who finds the next undiscovered vein of precious metal.
Why not have a look around the guild? This is where our miners come to relax. Perhaps you can cajole some of them into teaching you the tricks of the trade.
Make your way to the Nanawa Mines when you can. It is Amajina & Sons' main base of operations.
Oh? That is...unfortunate. I had thought to send you to the mines straightaway. I suppose there is no need to rush things.
Very well. But do not think you can dig wherever you please on your own. The Miners' Guild has eyes everywhere...
Popokkuli and Seserukka have headed north for Gridania. You should depart as soon as you are able, and look for them there.
Try the Roost. It's an inn we've used before. The twins will likely have rented several rooms for their traveling party. Ask after them there.
The twins summoned you by linkpearl? Were I you, I'd make for Gridania without wasting another moment.
Just head north from Ul'dah and you'll see the trees of the Black Shroud sooner or later. Gridania's somewhere in the middle of that lot.
Things aren't like to pass quietly in Gridania. Not with the twins there─and all the adventurers they dragged along with them, besides.
If you go yourself, beware the forest's elementals. The traveling merchants reckon they'll happily curse a southron for so much as looking in their general direction.
The Black Shroud is full of those elemental creatures. The Gridanians worship the bloody things day and night, from what I've heard.
Since the folks over at the Coliseum first caught wind of their power, they've tried more than once to capture one for the bloodsands. Every attempt's ended in failure, though─and sometimes tragedy.
Gridania may well be the poorest nation in all Eorzea. They've none of life's comforts. I'd wager good gil you'll be longing to come back in no time.

Of course, the scenery is no doubt agreeable enough, and the air passably pleasant to breathe─if you go in for all of that out-of-doors stuff. Oh, and there's the Carline Canopy, too. Most travelers speak highly of it. Might be worth a visit─while you're in the neighborhood, I mean.
I'd never have thought the twins would leave Nenekko behind to go so far as Gridania.
I outright refuse to believe it. The two who left must have been imposters or look-alikes sent as a diversion or...or [@1A(1)]something[@1A(0)].
Bloody shame that you're being made to go all that way to Gridania just now, what with the Nanawa shafts literally bursting with riches as they are.
But I suppose you can't well refuse a request from the future guildmaster─whichever one of the twins it turns out to be.
Aye, this isn't the first time the twins have raised hells at Gridania's inn. It seems the impression they've left is a lasting one.
All the same, I passed on word that you were on your way to join them. Gods go with you.

This city among the trees has quite a dull look to it if you ask me. No shine, no sparkle, no brilliance. I'm surprised the wealthier residents put up with it. Hells, who'd have thought they even [@1A(1)]had[@1A(0)] wealthy residents!?

I was shocked to hear it myself─till I learned they all made their fortunes down south and then simply bought up lands there. There's one richer than most, if the smallfolk are to be believed. Fellow by the name of Fafajon, I think it was.
The guildmaster's lady wife often visits the finest shops in Ul'dah together with her daughter, Nenekko. Imagine it...
To be dressed up in the finest silks and linens, adorned with golds and platinums, emeralds and rubies... And to be the object of everyone's attention! I'd give anything for just a day of it!
Nenekko often travels north to Gridania. For her health, she says. Of course, her family always insists she is accompanied by a heavy guard.
Talk to her for long enough, and you will hear how she detests it. The poor girl wants nothing more than to be free of her house and to do as she pleases.
What? Fafajon? Never heard of him. Nope. Haven't an inkling what you're on about.
Raaawr! At this rate, all of my custom is going to pack up and leave... Oh, Amajina & Sons will [@1A(1)]rue[@1A(0)] this day!
This lackwit can parley all [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] wants. [@IF($E9(4),She'll,He'll)] not hear from me that Fafajon paid for a coach to the flower fields near Longroot.
Did I just think that, or did I say that out loud?
Peace at last... It is good to have things back to nor─ What? You're looking for the miner twins?
They ran off into the Twelveswood, last I heard. I only pray they annoy the elementals as much as they annoyed me. They'd make for fine wildlings. Hehehe!
Now, we're looking for something─a box. It should be buried here, somewhere among the flowers.
Put all the soil back where it was. And be [@1A(1)]gentle[@1A(0)]! And don't damage the flowers! There's elementals in bloody everything here, and they're touchy bastards.
Enjoy your time in the Black Shroud, did you? Didn't end up in an Ixal's gut, I see!
Truth be told, I meant to insure your lifeblood with the Arrzaneth Ossuary, but I clean forgot. Seems I saved a few gil there!
Another vein was discovered deep in the Nanawa Mines while you were up north.
All miners on the shift took home all the ore they could carry and made a bloody fortune. Poor you, eh?
<sigh> I see the twins are up to their usual high jinks. Yes, I heard all over the linkpearl─again. Do you think me a complete fool?

You have nothing to gain by speaking to Nenekko. She is set to leave for Gridania at the behest of her parents. A miner just back from Eshtaime's Lapidaries chanced to overhear her and her lady mother discussing the trip while shopping there.
Nenekko's parents are sending her off to Gridania to take in the air and savor the calm.
One of our miners chanced to overhear her discussing the trip with her mother while they were shopping at Eshtaime's Lapidaries.
Seems Nenekko's lady mother has found herself a new favorite pastime─buying up everything in sight that might serve as a wedding present.
She'd just as soon see her daughter wed off to an Amalj'aa were it rich enough, the coin-grubbing old hag. <spit>

Who in their right mind would want to marry themselves off to a Gridanian? The tales one hears of elementals snatching folk up and turning them into wildlings should be enough to keep away anyone with their wits about them.
Lady Shalala started out as a singer and dancer herself, you know, right here in the guild's alehouse. Aye, and she sang and danced herself right into the guildmaster's bed! Hahaha!
As for this wedding business, well, she's only trying to spare Nenekko the life of hardship she had to endure. A parent's love can manifest itself in strange ways.
Coin, lands and titles, fame─to think Nenekko may have to give up all that [@1A(1)]here[@1A(0)] to go and live in the north...
I heard they brew tea from the same leaves over and over to avoid killing too many plants! What folly is that!?
So it was for Nenekko's sake that the twins journeyed to Gridania, after all...
No doubt they are attempting to sabotage their parent's plans for Nenekko, yet again.
Who can blame Nenekko's lady mother if she desires a wealthy husband for her daughter? Love fades, but coin? Coin lasts a lifetime.
No doubt she found a great deal of comfort in that coin when word of her husband's philandering came to light.
We didn't cover our tracks well enough. Mother suspects us...
You turned out to be quite helpful after all...[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], was it? We even made use of the stones you dug up. A good miner throws nothing away. Hehehe!
What exactly did the twins [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] up in Gridania? Do you know?
Well, whatever they did, it seems clear that their parents will be livid if they discover the truth. That said...it would not surprise me if their father had put them up to it.
It seems the twins have set their sights on you. I heard over the linkpearl. They bid you come to the Concern, and so you have. But I fear they have already left.
Yes, they gathered some adventurers and headed north just recently─for the Black Shroud. As boisterous as ever, those two. Always leaping before they look.
No doubt they meant for you to accompany them, as well, but forgot amidst the confusion of their departure. You had best go and find them in Gridania, before they realize you are missing.
Visit the inn in Gridania─a place called the Roost. No doubt the twins have taken a number of rooms there to accommodate their party.
Are you quite certain? They have been known to respond rather...[@1A(1)]violently[@1A(0)] to refusal. You may wish to reconsider.
Nenekko has gone missing, and the twins are tearing the town apart looking for her. At this rate, all our miners will be searching for Lalafell maids rather than Nanawa veins.
Tracking people down is a job for adventurers, not miners. It wouldn't surprise me if the twins had already submitted a request with the Adventurers' Guild...
It ain't a comforting thought, but Nenekko [@1A(1)]could[@1A(0)] have been kidnapped, you know? I mean, stranger things have happened, right?
She'd command a sultana's ransom, see. And if all my years in Ul'dah have taught me anything, it's that Ul'dahns are capable of anything where coin is concerned.
I can't say I'd be surprised to hear that Nenekko had eloped with some young lad or other.
All who know the girl would swear she's destined to fall for some beggarly, realm-wandering adventurer. Only a matter of time.
There is distressing news from the mines. The deepest shafts have hit upon seemingly impenetrable walls of rock.
If the twins were in the mines where they ought be, they'd see those walls down. That they would.
The desert is no place for a flower, and neither are the mines. Think of how dull someone like Nenekko must find life here─let alone the men.
Me? I like dull men. The type lacking in wits as well as words. Aye, their wits can be dull, so long as their pickaxe is sharp...and stout of shaft.
You should have seen the twins searching the guild for Nenekko. And in the most ridiculous of places.
I think I even saw Seserukka look inside an empty wine bottle! Gods, but those boys can be dimmer than a wickless candle.
In time, one of the twins will come to take their father's place as guildmaster.
Nenekko is to be married off as she cannot bear the thought of inheriting her father's fortune. Most like she will have to leave her family and join her husband's house when the time comes.
I think that may very well be why Popokkuli and Seserukka are so opposed to seeing her wed. Though I must admit I have never known either one to plan so far ahead.
Work from the Miners' Guild?
Aye, there was some such business as that. Not as I'd recommend it.
So the little princess of Amajina's gone missin', has she? Well, I like to help the twins where I can, but...
Look, if some misguided adventurer is behind all this, they're like to chase every last one of you out of Ul'dah. And that'd be bad for business. Seriously bad.

Oh, and I guarantee the girl's not eloped or been kidnapped─she's just bloody run away. Still, I worry all the same. Gods know she's naive enough for any fool she comes across to take advantage of her.
So Nenekko has finally run away from home...

I was aware she'd been spending time alone beyond the city, on trips to see the ruins of Sil'dih, but I didn't realize she was planning something like this. I presume you're familiar with the place she went, yes? Whence the ruins can be seen to the south, like a mirage?

The city itself cannot be reached, of course, though many have tried. All tell the same story─that however far they go, the ruins seem to stay on the horizon, never drawing close, as if there were some magic shroud at work. Anyway, as I mentioned, there is a place from which Sil'dih can at least be seen. Sadly, it is crawling with beasts. Not that Nenekko ever seemed to mind...
Oh, by the way, whatever you do, don't use the word “runaway” around the twins. They'd be like to march you to the chocobo stables and have you drawn and quartered!
Did you hear what the twins said? “Name your own reward,” it was!
Coin is well and good, but the chance to save Nenekko and have her fall in love with me is priceless!
It is only a matter of time before this gets out of control. Once word of the reward gets around, even the whores of the pillowhouses will be looking for Nenekko.
If the whole city ends up searching, my gil's on the Order finding her. Those thaumaturges have their ways...
The Concern is ruined.
To think one of those raving lackwits is going to be the next guildmaster... I've got to find a new line of work.
The girl may very well have run away of her own accord. But still...
She could not have disappeared without help. And only an adventurer would be foolish enough to aid the sister of the twins in such madness. Hmmm...
Would you send word to my brothers for me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? I promise I won't let them harm you.
Thank you for everything, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I will wait for my brothers here. You should head back to the Concern now.
I'm sorry for all the trouble I caused you. It was never my intention, you must know that. I do hope you will continue to work for Amajina & Sons.
Thank you for everything, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I will wait for my brothers here. You should head back to the Concern now.
I'm sorry for all the trouble I caused you. It was never my intention, you must know that. I do hope you will continue to work for Amajina & Sons.
Word is, someone finally tracked down Nenekko.
Eh? [@1A(1)]You!?[@1A(0)] Why, you lucky [@IF($E9(4),sow,bastard)]! I wouldn't be surprised if the guildmaster gave you a stake in the Nanawa Mines for this!
So there was no elopement and no kidnapping? Well, that's a mercy. Still...I don't see how Nenekko could have made it all the way to the ferry docks on her own...

Actually, there's talk that someone spotted her and gave chase, but that an adventurer helped her to escape. I wonder if this adventurer friend of Nenekko's─whoever [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] might have been─knew there was a [@1A(1)]massive[@1A(0)] reward for finding her. I daresay we'll never know, eh, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]?
I'm just glad it's all over. Maybe now we'll see the twins back in the mines.
Though I daresay as we'll see them in their cups first. Those fools will drink to damn near any occasion!
To think Nenekko planned this running away from home, knowing all the while what a tumult it would throw the twins and the guild into...
The spoiled little cow needs to stop being so selfish and grow up.
It is good that she was found. I heard that the guildmaster was on the brink of selling off the Concern!

Apparently, he'd resolved to give the Order all his worldly wealth to have the thaumaturges scour every ilm of Eorzea for Nenekko. All I can say is, you wouldn't need to hire a thaumaturge to work out where the twins get their hotheadedness...
If Nenekko was at the ferry docks, she must have been seeking passage to Limsa Lominsa.
The gods are good to see her back to us. I doubt she or her maidenhead would have lasted long amidst all those bloodthirsty pirates and brigands.

It is always good to see you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], but I would advise you to give the Concern a wide berth for now. Nenekko has been missing all day, and the twins are in an absolute [@1A(1)]frenzy[@1A(0)].
They've already dreamed up a host of ridiculous theories─everything from elopement to kidnapping─though they all amount to the same thing, as far as they're concerned.
Gods know, once they get an idea like that into their heads, those two will happily search to the ends of Eorzea. Would you be so good as to help us find her first?
They are like to request the assistance of the Adventurers' Guild, if they haven't already. You do call in there from time to time, don't you? If not, you should.
Ignore it all you want─the twins will involve you one way or another. Nenekko is more dear to those two than anything, and they know you might be helpful in finding her.
Professor Erik's well-being is in your hands. He awaits an escort at the chocobo stables as we speak. Oh, and please do whatever he asks of you. He is an [@1A(1)]extremely[@1A(0)] valued customer.

Ah, my punch-prone [@IF($E9(4),maidservant,manservant)], I presume? You may and shall call me Erik. You are to guard my life, even at the cost of your own, and aid in my revolutionary research whenever and however asked. I endeavor to reconstruct military histories of old through the aetherial analysis of ancient battlegrounds.
I assume the word conjures in your simple mind romantic images of vast plains and open valleys, with armies charging blindly at one another. False!

Your efforts will be rewarded. Look upon my garments. This is the war garb of the monkhood.
It attunes to its wearer. It empowers the chakra. Enables it to realize its full potential.
The cloth is imbued with the power of Rhalgr. Only monks of his Fist may don it. Only those who overcome many trials.
I will make a gift of this to you. With it I offer words. Words of instruction.
You need not enter the Fist. I require you to speak no vows. I ask only that you fight. Give yourself to our cause.
You long for adventure. I understand. But such longings can wait. This cannot. See Ala Mhigo freed. Then enjoy your own freedoms.
What say you, [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]?
You have the heart of a true monk. You are different from the others in this realm.
This is what you must do. See it done, and the garb will be yours. Remember well these words...
Dzemael Darkhold, south and west of Camp Dragonhead in the central Coerthas highlands. The U'Ghamaro Mines, north and east of Camp Iron Lake in upper La Noscea.
Turning Leaf, south of Camp Crimson Bark in the West Shroud. Cape Deadwind, south and east of the city of Ul'dah.
I have hidden your garb in these places. The way to them will not be easy. There are great dangers. This is to be your test.
Each garment rests within a chest. These are no ordinary chests. They sense the chakra of man. At the coming of a worthy soul, they will open. Look to your map should the way be lost.
This trial will yield but four pieces. There is a fifth. I hold it.
But I am bound by tradition. Only after the four are taken can the fifth be given.
I can say no more. I am master of your trial. I am forbidden to speak beyond what I have.
The teacher knows much of the Fist and the monkhood. If you would know more, ask him.
I await the day we fight side by side, [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]. Go now, and go well.
Your decision saddens me. But know that my offer stands. I pray you change your mind.
I will put this as plainly as possible so that even you might understand. Hasten─that's “go fast”─to Silvertear Falls, [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)]! Stop the simpleton monk!
Save your words. None will serve you. The teacher did not come himself. He is a weak, craven man.
Yet his is a brilliant mind. Why does he refuse to see? He has betrayed his country. He escapes into study. Theories will not slay Garleans. Theories will not win our war.
I thought him a fellow Ala Mhigan. One who could be reasoned with. I see now that was folly. He is one of the others. He has chosen the craven's path. He is dead to me.
Hasten to Silvertear Falls. Let us meet there, [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)].
Not long ago, I spoke with a man. An Ala Mhigan. He too was of the resistance. He asked me a simple question. Why do I fight?
I did not hesitate. I did not think. The word came of its own will─[@1A(1)]revenge[@1A(0)].
He said revenge is in all our hearts. That it is the most common of reasons. The easiest. And the most dangerous.
I did not think on it then. Perhaps now I should.
I thought of nothing else. But you thought of me, [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]. You and the teacher. For that I thank you both.
I made a promise. I will keep it. The fifth piece is yours. It is meant for you. For one whose seventh chakra is open.
Ala Mhigo fought to protect itself. To protect all Eorzea from the Empire.
And yet we are despised. Ignored. Worse, we are forgotten.
Even so, the teacher preached peace. For a long time, I did not understand. I hated him for it.
Ala Mhigans are a proud people. This pride is strong in me. And in the teacher. As it was in his son.
He fought in the resistance. Yet it cost him his life. He too cursed his father for being a coward.
I wish I could speak to him. I wish to tell him this is not so.
Farewell, [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]. May Rhalgr watch over you.
Widargelt is stubborn, as most monks are. I do not know if it will be possible for him to change his mind. But I pray he does. For his own sake, and for the world's.
He calls you his [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]. Go now. Speak to him as one.
The simpleton monk awaits you at Silvertear Falls. Go and speak to him as the [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)] he names you.

The class or job required to advance the quest “[@SHEET(xtx/quest,$E8(1),2)]” is [@SHEET(xtx/text_jobName,$E8(2),1)].
Muahahahaha! My theory was correct! Correct, I tell you!
I shall spare you the details of my experiment─as you are not like to comprehend their significance anyway─and proceed directly to the all-important conclusion!
The announcement of my theory before a council of my peers was met with thunderous applause!
And to think I owe it all to a fool adventurer and a simpleton monk! Both you and the Platinum Mirage that sent you are due a debt of gratitude.
Speaking of the monk, where in Eorzea has the semiliterate oaf wandered off to?
I have attempted several times to reach him on the linkpearl and inform him of the grand news, but he will not answer. I left a recording explaining all the details of my theory, but...
What have I done!? [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I fear the words I offered may have driven Widargelt to attempt the insane.

I analyzed the ethereal waves of your bodies, second by second. I was able to isolate and identify those of the final aetherial regulation mechanism─the so-called seventh chakra! From that, I was able to find the land which was most likely to resonate with those waves. Silvertear Falls!
I went to the site myself to investigate, and it was there that I made my great discovery─the discovery of the century!
<sigh> It occurs to me that you shall never accomplish such a feat of the mind, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and I find myself pitying you. But I digress.

News of my findings has already been printed in the [@1A(1)]Mythril Eye[@1A(0)]. No doubt all of the region knows of it by now─and soon all the realm! I used the linkpearl to tell the simpleton monk [@1A(1)]everything[@1A(0)].
Do you not see what I have done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! I told him [@1A(1)]precisely[@1A(0)] where he must go to unlock the seventh chakra!

He has given his life to the fight to reclaim Ala Mhigo from the Empire. More than anything, he desires the power needed to achieve that end─the power to combat the might of all Garlemald. Any fool can see that─ Ahem, [@1A(1)]almost[@1A(0)] any fool can see that he imagines the seventh chakra to be that power!

Yet battling the Empire on such terms will only result in another tragedy like that which befell Ala Mhigo. I pray you do not mean to follow him in this fool's crusade, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
He has gone to Silvertear Falls. I am certain of it! You must go, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! You must stop him!
Will you do this?
My words will not sway him─just as they could not sway my son. Perhaps yours will.
By the gods, [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)]... Surely you don't mean...? Would you have [@1A(1)]me[@1A(0)] go in your stead!?
<sigh> If you fail to see the importance of this, then I have failed as a teacher. Just as I failed as a father...
You! My discovery─the greatest discovery of our lifetime─it is all thanks to you, you beautiful, wonderful fool! All that remains is to publish it.
Ohhh, to see the looks upon my colleague's faces when I revolutionize mankind's very perception of reality!
The next monk quest will be available from Erik upon reaching level 50.
Your trial is at an end. You have passed. I will keep the promise made in time.
Many talk of the teacher's findings. He has made a great discovery. The man knows much. He would be a mighty ally. Speak to him. Try to win him to our cause.
The fifth piece must be prepared. I require time. Leave me for now, [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)].
Well done, [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]. You have claimed the first four pieces. I knew that you would.
Now you must train. You must learn to wear what you have won. To draw power from it.
I will keep my promise. The fifth will be yours. But not yet. Your strength must peak. Ala Mhigo requires it.
I have nothing left to say. If you must see me, I am at Silvertear Falls.
The guild is no longer accepting those items.

Th' Admiral's got us workin' the forges day and night, readyin' the armada fer somethin' big. Left our stockhouses bare as a whore's back end, it has, but the guilds ain't got the manpower t' plenish 'em. 'Tis why the forgemaster started postin' tasks on the wall o' th' Wench. With the Admiral's attention directed northwise, her fleet has not the swords to spend on a pisspot of a town as ours. To fend off the bloodthirsty beast tribes that would see our women dead and our brewin' tanks dry, we smallfolk of Aleport had no choice but to form a militia.

As you can see, though, we ain't much of an army─our ranks filled with naught but saltworn pullers and sotted alemongers. There'll be only so much this motley crew can manage when faced with a slaverin' horde lookin' to rend us like bloody butchers...which is why we's need the hands of them what's better at warrin'.

With [@SWITCH($E8(1),the Maelstrom's,the Order of the Twin Adder's,the Immortal Flames')] attention concentrated on the Garleans to the north, the Grand Company has neither the time nor resources to attend to the defense of remote hamlets such as our own. To protect our livelihoods from the bloodthirsty beast tribes that would see our stock dead and our granaries bare, we residents of [@SWITCH($E8(1),Aleport,Hyrstmill,the Golden Bazaar)] had little choice but to form a militia.

However, as you can see, we are not much of an army─our ranks consisting of farmers and bakers, pullers and merchants. There is only so much we can do when faced with a rabid horde, hells-bent on tearing us limb from limb...which is why we seek those with experience in martial matters to aid us.
With the Immortal Flames committed elsewhere, the threat posed by the Amalj'aa to our outlying areas is greater than ever. Their hordes will not relent.

Our hands have been forced. We common folk have taken up arms to defend ourselves, yet we alone cannot hope to repel the might of the beast tribes. And so it is to you adventurers we must turn to bolster our strength.

We's placed lookouts 'round the hamlet. The minute one of them kobolds is spotted, the lads'll report to me, and I'll sound the call to arms. 'Tis then the time that we'll find ye a place in our ranks.

Oh, and allow me the courtesy of makin' ye privy to our one golden rule─and that be you form a unit proper afore ye enlist. Once ye have, line up here with yer mates so's we can proceed with the formalities.

We have stationed sentries in several key locations surrounding the hamlet. If an enemy is sighted, they will report their findings to me, and I shall sound the call to arms. It is at this time that we welcome volunteers such as yourself into our ranks.
To maintain order, as well as safety, we have but one rule─namely that you form a unit prior to enlistment. Once you have done so, speak with me so that I may record your names in the battle ledger.
We have stationed watchmen around the hamlet borders. Should the lizardmen crawl anywhere within sight, the call to arms will be sounded.

I ask only that you come to our aid in a group of no fewer than eight able souls. Any less, and I cannot in good conscience send you into battle. Find seven companions, and then come to me for your orders.
If the kobolds is aught, they's predictable as a sot in an alehouse. The greedy bastards only has eyes fer the sparkly, and with each wave of attack, they'll head straight fer our supply caches.
The better-stocked the caches, the more keen they'll be to get at 'em...

If the [@SWITCH($E8(1),kobolds,Ixal,Amalj'aa)] are anything, they are predictable. It seems their motives are solely of the material sort, and so with every single wave of attack, they tend to focus their efforts on the occupation of [@SWITCH($E8(1),Aleport,Hyrstmill,the Golden Bazaar)]'s supply caches.
The better-stocked our caches, the more eager they will be to get at them...
It is our supplies the Amalj'aa are after. They mean to pillage and plunder every last store in our holds. Should they succeed, then all is lost.
We have found the way to victory to be twofold. Either we fight for all our worth and exhaust the enemy, or we slay the lizard who leads them and throw their ranks into chaos.
Ain't a kobold in sight as of yet, but them beasts, they run a tight ship. I'd wager me right eye that it won't be long afore they's scurryin' their way down from those crags of theirs.
There have been no enemy sightings of late, but if the punctuality of past assaults offers any indication of what's to come, I would think the beastmen will be arriving quite soon.
There is no sight of the enemy as of yet. Worry not, should our watchmen spot them, I will sound the call to arms.

Right kind of ye, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)], but there ain't aught but naught to cross blades with at the moment. And to tell the truth, if I had me own way, it'd stay like that till I's old and withered.
While your offer is appreciated, enemy activity remains at a low, and thus we do not require your services for the time being.
There is no sight of the enemy as of yet. Our militia can see to the hamlet's safety until the Amalj'aa mobilize.
Hah hah! 'Tis a fine day to gut a beastie! Now line up yer mates so's I can give ye a send off proper-like!
We are in your debt, kind adventurer! Now, there is little time before the next wave of beastmen arrives. Gather your allies and make ready for battle at once!
You are most welcome! There is no time to lose. Prepare yourselves for battle!

[@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),Evenin',Mornin')],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),G'day,Evenin')])], 'venturer. I'm [@SHEETEN(xtx/placeName,2,$E8(1),3,1)] [@IF($E9(8),[@SHEET(xtx/displayName,$E9(8),1)],$EB(3))]. We's currently seekin' hale 'n hearty [@IF($E9(4),lassies,lads)] such as yer kind self to assist in the defense of our here village.
Me men tell me the kobolds is gatherin' in full force jus' to the north of here!
Ye can rest easy, [@IF($E9(4),lassie,lad)]. There ain't a kobold within fifty malms of Aleport. We'll keep our vigil. Ye keep fillin' our caches with them fine goods, like.

Well met, adventurer. I am [@SHEETEN(xtx/placeName,2,$E8(1),3,1)] [@IF($E9(8),[@SHEET(xtx/displayName,$E9(8),1)],$EB(3))]. We are currently seeking brave [@IF($E9(4),women,men)] such as yourself to assist in the defense of our humble village.
Our sentries report that [@SWITCH($E8(1),kobolds,Ixal,Amalj'aa)] are amassing to the [@SWITCH($E8(1),north,west,south)], and in considerable numbers.
There have been no recent [@SWITCH($E8(1),kobold,Ixal,Amalj'aa)] sightings. They are doubtless aware that our stores are nigh on bare.

Good [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),eve,morn)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),day,eve)])] to you, adventurer. I am [@SHEETEN(xtx/placeName,2,$E8(1),3,1)] [@IF($E9(8),[@SHEET(xtx/displayName,$E9(8),1)],$EB(3))]. I seek able men and women to help defend our humble hamlet.
An Amalj'aa horde has been spotted! Make ready for battle!
There is no sight of the enemy as of yet.
Oh, and I'll be takin' these nasty instruments of warfare off yer person. They'll serve us better in the caches where they belong.
Oh, and I will see to it that the instruments of warfare still in your possession from the last wave are properly stored in our supply caches.
You bring supplies! Excellent! We shall store them in our caches and make use of them when we have the need.
Excess amounts of the item will be returned to your inventory.
You contribute [@FORMAT($E8(2),,)] [@IF($E4($E8(2),1),point,points)] to [@2B([@SHEETEN(xtx/placeName,2,$E8(1),1,1)])]'s supply rating.
Select an item to contribute.
What items have you to donate?
Select a materia-enhanced item from your inventory. Remember, once you have donated the item, it will be lost.

I need hardly mention that Sil'dihn civilization is now centuries dead.

Sil'dih was plunged into chaos in the wake of King Lalawefu's demise─or the King of Springs, as he was known. Despite the success of his economic reforms, the tax increases he imposed did not sit well with his subjects. This, coupled with a prolonged sequence of untimely droughts, fomented unrest among the people and in time sparked violent unrest throughout the kingdom.

Sil'dih was not alone in its want for water. Ul'dah, too, felt the effects of the droughts. The sultan at the time, Sasagan Ul Sisigan─ Ah! But perhaps you recognize the Ul name? The current sultana, Nanamo Ul Namo, represents the second Ul dynasty. She is Sasagan's distant descendant. Now...where was I? Ah, yes! Right, so, Sasagan ordered an attack on Sil'dih to claim the water resources discovered as a result of Lalawefu's flood control acts.

But the royalty and nobility of Sil'dih would not remain idle. They mobilized their nation in the face of this crisis, and the people fought with great tenacity against the Ul'dahn threat. The full strength of both nations met in battle, and the end result was an arduous protracted conflict.

Though arguably more desirable than surrender, the ruling Sil'dihn elite took little pleasure in having succeeded in uniting the theretofore querulous citizenry to fight. For despite all they accomplished, every day spent waging war dragged the nation's financial affairs─which you will recall had only just been brought under control─back into the mire.
To bring an end to the long military deadlock, Sil'dih devised and set about implementing a perverse yet ambitious strategy.
It sought to zombify the deceased among its army, that they might fight again.

At first, it appeared to have worked. Yet at the height of hostilities, the Sil'dihns lost control over their necrotic creations. The undead turned on their masters, and before long the zombification had spread to a majority of the population.

Ever knowing an opportunity when they saw one, the Ul'dahns grasped this turn of events to justify their war─now proclaiming it a crusade to send these zombies to Thal. After seeing to the extermination of all zombies outside the city, they then sealed the gates of Sil'dih, entrapping both the living and dead within.
And that, in brief, is a history of the fall of Sil'dih. I only pray that your feeble mind is able to retain it.

I shall tell you yet again of the study of aether.

As I laboriously explained, aether is not only the source of all magicks, but also the fount of all life. Yet despite its ubiquity, it remains imperceptible to the senses of man. If you are well loved, power and money will come. If you wield power, you can take both love and money. And if you have money, you can buy either love or power. Yet lack for any, and you shall never rise high.

The city's guilds were founded upon these tenets. Eshtaime's Lapidaries and Frondale's Phrontistery devote themselves to the mysteries of love. The Coliseum and Amajina & Sons Mineral Concern, meanwhile, are dedicated to the honing of power and might. Perhaps an adventurer like yourself finds our rules quaint, even a nuisance in these troubled times. It has been my fate to be named captain of the Sultansworn in these troubled times. But I have bent my knee to the sultana and sworn fealty, and I am bound to my duty. What choice do I have, but to fight to restore our honor and name?
You wield a skilled blade, and more importantly, you have met the traitor face-to-face. Your great task as a paladin will be to help me bring him to justice.

You must ready yourself, marshal your resources, and hone your skills until the time comes when you are able to discharge your duty. The journey will be long, but you are a paladin now, and honor binds you as surely as an oath.

...[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? A fine name. I bid you welcome, and salute your noble resolve. But if you aspire to paladinhood, you should understand what it means.
A paladin swears allegiance to the sultanate. A paladin shall be the sword and shield of the sultanate. A paladin defends the people of the realm.
Sellswords and gladiators and others of their ilk wield their blades for themselves, but a paladin serves the greater good. Do you understand me?
The battle arts that the paladin learns have been held secret, nurtured, and perfected within the ranks of the Sultansworn elite for nigh on these six hundred years.

As you well know, of all those sworn to protect the sultanate─the soldiers, the mounted guards, and knights─we are the elite of the elite. Our conviction unwavering, our hearts true, our sword skills without peer.

Once, not so long ago, the Sultansworn could walk the streets with their heads held high. When they marched by, the smallfolk would look upon them with reverence and gratitude. And no one was more respected than the captain. My predecessor.

When I first saw him, I was still a child. My father had promised to take me to a local festival, but somewhere he took a wrong turn. We became lost and stumbled into a secluded back alley. Luck was not with us, because the next moment, we found ourselves in the middle of a riot. Drunken hunters were firing arrows into the crowd, and we were caught between them. There was no way out─it was only a matter of time before we would be struck...

That's when the captain saved us from our plight. I'd never seen a sword move so swiftly! It flashed faster than my eyes could follow, and in seconds the hunters were on the ground or fleeing for their lives. The captain was gone down the street, slicing at their heels, before my father had time to thank him. Even today, I can see the captain as he was then, blood on his sword, armor impossibly bright in the sun.

After that, all I ever wanted to be was a paladin. I would practice endlessly with my sword, dreaming of bandits defeated and monsters slain. Even after I became one of the Sultansworn, the memory of the captain still inspired me─I was always the first to arrive in the training yard, and the last to leave.

And so the years passed, and before I knew it, I found myself named captain of the Sultansworn. Yet the triumph was hollow, because by then, the honor of the Sultansworn elite, that very thing that had drawn me to the brotherhood, was a tattered vestige, like the discarded banner of a defeated foe.
There were many reasons for the fall, but the loss of Oathkeeper... Yes, that was the mortal blow.

The sword Oathkeeper was bestowed upon the first captain of the Sultansworn by the then sultan of Ul'dah. In time it became our standard, the symbol of the oaths we had sworn, and it was treasured by each new captain for generations. Possession was proof of Sultansworn command.

But then the unthinkable came to pass─Oathkeeper was stolen by the traitor. It shook our brotherhood to the core. How can we be trusted to protect the sultana if we cannot even hold on to the symbol of our fealty? We have been tarnished, in the eyes of ruler and ruled alike.

If the Sultansworn are to survive, we must find the traitor and recover Oathkeeper. But...the Sultansworn have grown too weak, and we cannot do it ourselves. We've been forced to recruit outsiders to help us in our cause.

I have high hopes for you, my friend. It is a great thing that we ask, and you must learn more of our secrets if you are to succeed. Out in the North Shroud, in the Mun[@1F]Tuy Cellars, hides a fiend known as an alux. A fight with such a monster would be a fine way to hone the skills that I will teach you. What say you?
Yes, you have mettle in your heart. I will carve your next lesson on the crystal, and then you will be ready to battle the fiend.
...It is done. When you face an agile foe, let the crystal be your guide, and master the skills that you have learned.
The fiend invaded the Wailing Barracks, where the elite of Gridania are wont to gather. It was captured and imprisoned after growing drunk on wine and ale.
However, it managed to slip its cell and escape, despite the close attention of the guards. Unquestionably, it is a dangerous foe. Take this linkpearl, that we may stay in contact.
I thought you were ready to learn more. Remember, a paladin must not be afraid to journey into unknown lands.
The man who gave you the Soul of the Paladin was a traitor. He dishonored the name of the Sultansworn, and without it, we are nothing.

You are our hope. If you do as I ask, and succeed, the Sultansworn may yet restore the glory that was once its birthright. So prepare yourself. Hone your skills that you may be ready when the time comes.

Everyone knows that Ul'dah is ruled by the sultana─but everyone also knows that true power lies with the Syndicate. And at the core of the group is a faction that calls itself the Monetarists.

Of the six who hold seats on the Syndicate, only General Raubahn is faithful to the sultana. Most of the others refuse to accord her due rights, and work to establish “self-governance” for themselves and their wealthy cohorts. It is they who are the Monetarists. It is they who run the Ul'dahn economy.

“Self-governance” may sound a noble endeavor, but on their lips the words ring hollow. The faction seeks power, and that is why they plot against the Sultansworn, the sultana's last line of protection. They sowed the seeds of our ruin, and nurture them still. The disgrace of our former captain was their doing, of that I have little doubt.
But with your help, we shall stop them. Go to lower La Noscea, find the giant crab king, Old Six-arms, and defeat him in battle. Master your new paladin skills and make them your own.

Welcome, paladin. You should know that word of your deeds has reached me. Few are those who follow the true paladin path without misstep, but you are one of them. I am proud to call you [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)].
You have kept the faith, and in return, I must have faith in you. It is time that you knew the truth─though it is hard to share, for it is a shame I would rather keep hidden from outsiders.
Perhaps you remember when I told you of the traitor and the sword Oathkeeper that he stole. His name is Solkzagyl, and he was my predecessor as captain of the Sultansworn elite.
Yes, he was the same man whom I had admired as a child, who inspired me to take up the sword and follow the way of the paladin. He was the paragon of paladins─until, that is, he changed.

Some years ago now, there was a struggle for influence between the sultanate military and a faction within the Syndicate known as the Monetarists. The latter emerged triumphant, and the army's authority was diminished dramatically. Although Solkzagyl was still captain of the Sultansworn elite, he knew his position was perilous─so he fled, taking Oathkeeper with him.

In doing so, he went against the words that he had spoken on bended knee before his royal liege. Now it falls to me, as captain, to restore the honor and name of the Sultansworn. If that means cutting down my former mentor and master, I would do it gladly, for his misdeed cannot be forgiven.

But his death will not lift the stain that mars our name. He must be put on trial, in a public court, so that everyone knows his crimes. Then, and only then, can we begin to earn the people's trust again.

He served for over thirty years as captain of the Sultansworn elite, and he is a formidable foe─few can match his skill with the sword. Even together, you and I will find it difficult to take him alive without mortal harm to one side or the other. So you must continue to hone your skills and prepare for the day when we will face him.

Well come, friend. I have important news for you. In my search for the traitor, I have been looking through old records─and discovered something chilling.
Around the time the traitor Solkzagyl was named captain, several famed soldiers of the Sultansworn met with untimely deaths. But strangely, our records do not say how they died.

Curious, I begged the favor of an old friend and received permission to inspect medical records kept by the Frondale Phrontistery. I discovered that the soldiers died in various ways─some in combat, some suddenly at night, in the barracks... But in nearly every case, there were signs that poison had played a role in their demise.

Yes, poison. Carefully, invisibly administered. The more I read, the more I saw the dark hand of Death's Embrace at work─assassins in the pay and service of the Monetarists. A society so secretive that few believe it truly exists.

But no matter how skilled and devious the assassins, they should not have been able to kill so many of the Sultansworn elite without being discovered. Not, that is, without help from within our own ranks.

So I asked myself: who had the most to gain from their deaths? One by one, the former captain, his trusted aides, the most capable of the Sultansworn who might become future commanders─all of them, slain by an invisible hand. And with their deaths, the way was open for Solkzagyl to become the Sultansworn's youngest captain in a century.

The Monetarists were plotting to kill the best and bravest of the Sultansworn, to purge its ranks of greatness, and enervate it so that it could no longer carry out its duty to serve as sword and shield of the sultanate.

Which begs the question: how did Solkzagyl remain captain for thirty long years? How did he avoid the poisoner's kiss, when men better than him had succumbed? There can be only one explanation─he was the Monetarists' cat's-paw, the turncloak in our midst.

Just so. You walk the paladin's path now, and you must follow it where it leads. Go, get the armor. By the time you return, I will have found our traitor.
The trials are not easy, of course─but you will need both the fortitude to endure them, and the armor that doing so confers, if you are to help bring the traitor to justice.

They planted the lie that Solkzagyl was a traitor, and tricked me into tracking him down. I was their puppet, twitching obediently at the end of the strings they pulled.

Solkzagyl was no traitor, as I should well have known. But I allowed myself to be deceived by the whispers of mummers and flatterers, and... No. That was not the way of it. It was not their lies that made me blind, but my desire─nay, [@1A(1)]obsession[@1A(0)] to restore our honor.

Solkzagyl understood what was happening, and that is why he gave you the Soul of the Paladin. It was a remonstration, a message. Look how adventurers live, he was telling me. Where does their honor, their authority come from?

I owe my position to the machinations of the Monetarists. They calculated that a young captain, eager to prove his loyalty, bound by unquestioning fealty, would be all the easier to control. They were right.
I am a sham and a fake. But the world does not know that, and even the illusion of power is a power of sorts. I can use it to fight back.
I will tell my subordinates that I'm fleeing to the wastelands southeast of Camp Bluefog. When the Monetarists hear of this, as they surely will, they will send assassins after me again.
But when they show their hand, I will stand my ground and fight back.

The odds will be against me, that much is certain. But Solkzagyl has taught me much, and if I am brave and vigilant, I know I can triumph.
I am sorry you have been caught up in our own political struggles. But now, as a paladin, it is time you traveled your own path.

Find somewhere safe, go to ground until the battle is done. When I return, I would be honored to meet with you again. I owe you much, and for all my faults, I would never have it said that I do not pay my debts.
I hope we can talk again, when this is all over.

I am going to the wastelands southeast of Camp Bluefog to bait the Monetarists into attacking me. When I strike back, it will be a call to arms for every loyal brother and sister of the Sultansworn. As for you, it is time you traveled your own path.

No, do not be afraid for me. We've unmasked the foe and he cannot hide behind his deceptions anymore. The assassins won't find it easy to reach me. For now, I will bide my time, marshal my strength, and, when the time is ripe, strike hard at our enemies.

Welcome, noble traveler. I hope you will join us in admiring the peach blossoms and celebrating Little Ladies' Day.
Little Ladies' Day is a special festival for young girls that began three hundred years ago. It started with the famous story about Princess Edyva Thorne of Ul'dah. Perhaps you've heard the tale?

Princess Edyva was the only daughter of the sultan. She lived in a fancy palace surrounded by luxury, but she was terribly bored by all the rituals and rules of the court. So one day she traded places with a common girl, clothes and all, and slipped out of the palace to get a taste of life outside the walls. Which was all well and good, but when the sultan heard his daughter was missing...well, that's when Edyva's little flight of fancy took a serious turn.
Baldric―that was the sultan's name―went quite mad with worry. He called his entire army to arms, and under his orders they turned the city upside down and inside out searching for the girl.

At first Princess Edyva enjoyed playing at hide-and-seek―it must have been very exciting to have an entire army looking for you―but when she saw the damage that was being done to the city by the sultan's soldiers, she sheepishly turned herself in and was returned to the palace.

The family that suffered the most was that of the girl who had swapped clothes with the princess―the panicked soldiers had inflicted indignities and worse on the poor folk. Once he calmed down, Baldric felt terrible about the whole affair. He visited the family and delivered that famous quote, “all young ladies are jewels in the sultan's crown─to behold and to treasure.”

After that, the sultan ordered his chief architect to rebuild the common girl's home, and, to make up for what had happened, declared that for a full day, he would serve the girl as her personal seneschal.

The sight of their fierce, despotic ruler in humble service to a commoner─and a child at that─delighted the citizens. In his turn moved by the joy of his people, the sultan declared that one day of each year he would select, via lots, a common girl from the city and serve as her seneschal.
Soon, people were celebrating the day all across Eorzea, and even now, on Little Ladies' Day, we hold lots to choose the Little Lady of the Town and her royal seneschal.
