The process will produce a quantity of ash, which I ask that you bring to me. We Cascadiers have use for Bombard ash, and will offer myriad delightful items in exchange for the substance.
And that is all I have to share. Now, I present to you your very own Cascadier uniform. May it preserve you from torrid heat. Always.
Wh-What? Ye'd stand idly by while yer comrades risked life an' limb t' stop the whole realm goin' up in flames!?[@CR]An' ye call yerself a Cascadier... <spit>

Y-You would forsake your sacred vows!? Why, you despicable oathbr─[@CR]I... I shall forget we ever had this conversation. I have faith in you─faith that you will come to your senses and do what's right. Till such time as you recall the meaning of honor and sacrifice, I shall await here with open arms.

What? B-But...you can't simply abandon us.[@CR]Think of the children! For the love of the Twelve, think of the [@1A(1)]children[@1A(0)]─their adorable little eyes melting in the inferno of the Bombard's unholy flames! <sob>
Pray lend me your ears, adventurer! The citizens of Gridania are in terrible danger, and your help is needed to prevent them from coming to harm!

I know full well that my peculiar attire gives you pause and casts doubt over my credibility, but there is a logical explanation for this. If you'd allow me but a moment to explain the situation, all will be made crystal clear.

As you may already know, at present the people of Eorzea are observing All Saints' Wake, a tradition that originates from an age-old legend. According to this legend, once a year the Twelve show their favor to the saints─aye, the exalted personages who adorn guildleves─by inviting them to a magnificent feast in the celestial realm.
A fine gesture, to be sure, save for one small detail: while the saints are gone, the land is bereft of their protection, and we mortals are rendered vulnerable to evil beings that would do us harm.

Fearing for their lives, the people took to hiding themselves away inside their homes from dusk till dawn for the duration of the celestial feast. Over time, this practice took root and eventually flourished into the tradition we call All Saints' Wake. Ah, but little did anyone imagine that this custom would one day endanger the very souls it sought to protect.

In the course of your adventures, mayhap you've come to know that malicious imps were being held in confinement within the Spirithold. Aye, well, the sly creatures managed to escape from their cells when a crew of credulous prison guards left their stations before the shift was scheduled to change so as to return home by nightfall!

The imps are at large, and it's only a matter of time before their vile minds drive them to perpetrate vile crimes. The Adventurers' Guild has since been commissioned to prevent that from happening, and so I find myself here, beseeching the aid of valiant adventurers such as yourself.
I now repeat my first words to you, friend. The citizens of Gridania are in terrible danger, and your help is needed to prevent them from coming to harm! Please aid us in apprehending the imps!
Truly? You have my eternal gratitude, adventurer! Thank you!
Now, heed me well, for I shall arm you with the information necessary to neutralize the imps.

Firstly, I must warn you that this will be no ordinary hunt. You see, upon gaining their freedom, the imps sent a letter of challenge addressed to the Adventurers' Guild. And the nature of the challenge? [@1A(1)]Riddles[@1A(0)], of all things!

Can you believe the nerve of those accursed little blighters? Naught would give me more pleasure than to throttle them with my bare hands, and I'm sure you share my sentiments. Yet if we are to see them recaptured without risking carnage in Gridania, we have no choice but to abide by their terms.

The rules they have set out are simple: the imps will pose you a riddle, which you must attempt to answer. A correct answer will earn you cookies─yes, you heard correctly─of which a certain amount must be amassed by the end of All Saints' Wake. Should we succeed, the imps will willingly hand themselves over to us. If we fail, however, we must publicly swear not to pursue them.

Know, though, that the imps will not allow themselves to be readily found. They've employed their magicks to conceal their presence among the citizenry, and to compound matters, they appear only between dusk and dawn.

The first order of business will be to seek out the creatures and divest them of their disguise. Of late, sightings have been reported of townsfolk behaving erratically in the vicinity of guilds and shops─I daresay [@1A(1)]those[@1A(0)] are our targets.
Considering the amount of ground you must cover, I recommend you enlist the aid of fellow adventurers for the search effort.

Lastly, any cookies you acquire should be brought to me or one of my counterparts in the other city[@1F]states. By way of gratitude, we will furnish you with any of a selection of fine prizes in exchange.
Prizes can be obtained by offering a set amount of cookies (3, 10, 50, or 99) to your local Adventurers' Guild runner.

Y-You refuse to help!? I beg you reconsider! If not returned to captivity, the imps will wreak such havoc upon Gridania as would make the flood that ushered in the Fifth Umbral Era seem little more than a high tide![@CR]...Ahem. That may be a [@1A(1)]slight[@1A(0)] exaggeration, but I assure you my intentions were pure.

What're ye starin' at, eh? I'll have ye know this outfit ain't for show. A bunch o' rogue imps've broken loose, see, an' we're dressed up like this as part o' the plan t' catch 'em. Ah, the things we do t' make ends meet...

Anyroad, ye've heard of All Saints' Wake, ain't ye? Nay? Well, the saints are the fellas what grace guildleves─an' I'm ruddy certain ye've heard o' [@1A(1)]them[@1A(0)]. As for this Wake business, legend has it that for jus' one night each year, Their Eminences are invited t' join the Twelve in their realm on high for a feast o' godly proportions.
Don't sound too bad, does it? Aye, 'cept for the fact that while the saints are off drinkin' 'emselves silly, we mortals are at the mercy o' monsters an' assorted other nasty blighters.

Ah, but folk found a cunnin' way t' cope without divine protection. That is, by scramblin' home afore sunset an' barricadin' 'emselves indoors! In time, this custom─passin' strange though it is─came to be an annual occurrence.

Thing is, observin' this custom's the very thing what caused our woes. Mayhap you've heard tell, but an especially tricksy bunch of imps was bein' held within the Coral Tower's brig, right? Well, on the night of All Saints' Wake, the wardens there took it into their heads to go runnin' off home a bit early, like, afore they could be relieved by souls what weren't so bloody superstitious. Aye, an' no sooner had they done so, than the wily imp bastards broke free!

This is a proper bleedin' [@1A(1)]catastrophe[@1A(0)]! If the imps are allowed t' roam unchecked, only the Twelve know what manner o' mischief they'll visit upon hapless townsfolk! In the name o' the Adventurers' Guild, they mus' be caught, an' caught quick!
I beg ye─nay, [@1A(1)]demand[@1A(0)] that ye aid us. Think of it as makin' amends for starin' at me outfit with mirth in yer eyes─an' don't ye go denyin' it, neither!

A jolly good answer, [@IF($E9(4),lass,mate)]! There's a stout heart beatin' [@IF($E9(4),beneath that buxom bosom,inside that chest)] o' yers.[@CR]Now then, let me brief ye on the situation as it stands: these imps are as brazen as they are cunnin'─not more'n a few bells after they'd won free, they issued a challenge t' the Adventurers' Guild.
If we best 'em in said challenge, they promise t' turn 'emselves in without a fight. But if we fail, we'd have t' let 'em go. Grrr, jus' recallin' the words makes me bleedin' blood boil!

Hm? What's the challenge, ye ask? That'll be riddles, [@IF($E9(4),lass,mate)]. Aye, blasted [@1A(1)]riddles[@1A(0)]. The detestable fiends'll pose a question, an' ye have t' answer. A correct response'll earn ye cookies, an' in order t' win, we need t' gather enough o' the bloody things by the end of All Saints' Wake.

Truth is, it irks me t' no end that we're playin' on their terms. I'd sooner show them filthy creatures the color o' me steel, but we can't risk the townsfolk gettin' hurt. An' so it comes down t' godsdamned [@1A(1)]cookies[@1A(0)].
Oh, but afore ye go lookin' for 'em, there's two things ye should know: the imps've a penchant for shiftin' shape. What's more, they only turn up at night.
Now, reports've been pourin' in o' shady types prowlin' about guilds an' shops in Limsa. Me gut tells me those characters'd bear a bit o' scrutiny.

What cookies ye get yer mitts on, ye need t' bring to either meself or one o' me comrades in the other cities. An' t' make it worth yer while, we've prepared a goodly selection of prizes to offer ye in exchange. Good stuff, too.
Prizes can be obtained by offering a set amount of cookies (3, 10, 50, or 99) to your local Adventurers' Guild runner.
Wh-What? Ye mock me t' me face, then have the gall t' decline an' earnest plea for aid!? Away with ye, ye cold-hearted wretch!

Let me guess: you saw my bizarre outfit and felt drawn to it like a moth to a flame. Well, you needn't worry about getting burned, because I don't intend to set you on fire. I will, however, talk your ears off, so do brace yourself. Ahem!

I'm here at the behest of the Adventurers' Guild to recruit able individuals for a mission of the utmost import. A heinous band of imps has escaped from an inescapable cell in the Marasaja Pit, you see, and we need bounty hunters keen of eye and keener still of mind to recapture the lot of them.

No doubt you're wondering how it's possible that these winged fiends were able to break free of an “inescapable” cell. Well, the opportunistic devils took advantage of All Saints' Wake, the annual tradition that's currently taking place.
In case you're unfamiliar with the tradition, it was born of a legend which tells that the saints of old would ascend to the heavens at the same time each year to join the Twelve in a lavish feast.

Sounds marvelous, doesn't it? Aye, but only if you're a saint─we mortals get the short end of the stick. For while the saints are gorging themselves on honey-glazed meats and imbibing countless bladderfuls of deity-worthy wine, the world must go without their divine protection. And what better time for evil spirits to run rampant?

Having no choice but to fend for themselves, ordinary folk took to returning home while it's still light out, and confining themselves indoors with kith and kin till such time as the sun rose again. And so it was with some of the rather more...[@1A(1)]credulous[@1A(0)] wardens at the Marasaja Pit. You see, they retired for the day somewhat sooner than they were scheduled to be relieved.

Left utterly unguarded, the imps did what any sensible soul would do─by which I mean, [@1A(1)]escape[@1A(0)]. And now they're out there somewhere, waiting to exact revenge upon the mortals that saw fit to imprison them. We must find and recapture the imps before they have the chance to make mischief! And by [@1A(1)]we[@1A(0)], I mean [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)], adventurer!
Excellent! I had expected no other answer! On behalf of the Adventurers' Guild, I offer you my heartfelt thanks![@CR]Now then, pay close attention, for I shall brief you on your mission.

As is commonly known, imps are impudent creatures by nature. Give an imp even a sliver of a chance to show cheek, and it'll cling to it with white-knuckled tenacity. [@1A(1)]This[@1A(0)], my friend, is the very thing that will prove to be their downfall. Allow me to elaborate.

Blessed with the good fortune to escape imprisonment, even a criminal with half the sense the gods gave a flea would know to lie low. Ah, but that would not do for our imps. No, their wanton impudence would let them do naught else but make mock of their former captors.

In our case, the imps sent a missive to the Adventurers' Guild challenging us to a contest of wits. They will pose to us riddles, which we must attempt to answer. A correct response will earn us─don't laugh─[@1A(1)]cookies[@1A(0)], and if we can amass a sufficient amount by the end of All Saints' Wake, the vile creatures swear to return to their prison cell of their own volition. If we [@1A(1)]fail[@1A(0)], however, we must promise to pursue them no more.

Hah! The fools have practically given us license to send them back to the Marasaja Pit without breaking a single bead of sweat! [@1A(1)]We[@1A(0)] will laugh last, and [@1A(1)]we[@1A(0)] will laugh loudest! Aha...hahaha...hahahahahahahahaha!!!

...Ahem. Beg pardons for that outburst.[@CR]Now, the imps have assumed the form of ordinary citizens, and have been seen in the vicinity of guilds and shops. Being creatures of darkness, however, they have no love for sunlight and so will go into hiding during the day.

Now, let us speak of the most important thing─aye, cookies. All the cookies that come into your possession should be brought to myself or one of my peers in the other city[@1F]states. As these baked treats are central to our success, the Adventurers' Guild is prepared to offer you unique prizes in exchange for their delivery.
Prizes can be obtained by offering a set amount of cookies (3, 10, 50, or 99) to your local Adventurers' Guild runner.
Your answer wounds me more than you could ever know. Ask yourself this: what is the Adventurers' Guild if it can't rely on the support of adventurers? Now, please excuse me while I cry. <sob>

You are an adventurer, are you not? We at Black Rabbit Traders have a proposition, if you would be kind enough to spare a moment of your time.

The conjurers of Stillglade Fane have commissioned us to assist with preparations for a winter festival. Doubtless this seems a joyous undertaking, but I assure you our task is grim and urgent both. Permit me to explain.

Mayhap you have noticed, but winter is late in coming to the North Shroud this year. So much so, in fact, that the conjurers felt compelled to delve into the matter. Alas, all attempts to explain the phenomenon have proven fruitless, and fears are running rife as to how it might affect the delicate balance of life in the Twelveswood.

Word of the conjurers' concerns eventually reached a group of Ala Mhigan refugees, who proposed a possible solution. There is an ancient tradition in their homeland, you see─a festival to usher in the blessing of winter.

Known as [@1A(1)]Winter's Knell[@1A(0)], the festival involves building a giant of snow in a ritual to beckon the cold. Clearly, this presents certain problems of its own, however, given that the warm weather renders it nigh on impossible to keep snow from melting.

For a blessing, the conjurers have ways to create heat-resistant snow, albeit at a rather limited rate. And so they came to Black Rabbit Traders, seeking aid to produce the required quantity─which finally brings me to my proposition.

I would have you bring me ice shards─[@IF($E5($E8(2),0),[@IF($E2($E8(2),10),[@SWITCH($E8(2),one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE($E8(2))])],[@VALUE($E8(2))])], to be precise. Should you agree to assist us, I promise to make it worth your while.
I knew you would not shirk such responsibility. You have my gratitude, friend.

I cannot hide my disappointment. I had prepared a delightful gift especially for you, but now I must needs find another recipient.
Oooh, if it ain't a 'venturer! Prick up yer ears, now, 'cause I've got a proposition fer ye.
The Black Rabbit Traders be lookin' fer sure-armed folk t' help out with a certain festival. What sort o' festival, ye ask? Why, the one what ushers in the winter, [@IF($E9(4),missy,matey)].

T' cut a long story short, we're relyin' on good ol' magic. Aye, but fer it to work, we need a fair bleedin' mountain of ice shards. An' that be where ye come in, [@IF($E9(4),missy,matey)].

I'd be grateful if ye'd bring me [@2B([@IF($E5($E8(2),0),[@IF($E2($E8(2),10),[@SWITCH($E8(2),one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE($E8(2))])],[@VALUE($E8(2))])])] o' the blasted things. Yer services won't go unrewarded, o' course. What say ye, now?

Aye! That's the spirit! Jus' so as we're clear, then, that's [@IF($E5($E8(2),0),[@IF($E2($E8(2),10),[@SWITCH($E8(2),one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE($E8(2))])],[@VALUE($E8(2))])] ice shards we be needin', and not a one less.

Well, there are two types of decorated eggs. We have fancy ones, with beautiful patterns and decorations, and plainer types, that are just painted one color.
There are four of the fancier type. We call them the Archon egg, colored Archon egg, painted Archon egg, and darkened Archon egg.
The ones that are painted in a single color are named for that color―obviously! So we have red, blue, yellow, violet, and green Archon eggs. Five in total.

Magnificent! You truly are a paragon amongst Cascadiers, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I pray you never forsake our cause.
Well met, adventurer. I take it you've come to join in the mirth and merriment of Moonfire Faire, the sultriest of all Eorzean festivals. You need but sign your name here.
Congratulations, [@STRING($EB(1))]. You are now a sworn Cascadier, bound unto death to uphold the cause of our noble organization.
Hm? What of the promised mirth and merriment, you ask?
Oh, you will forgive me, but the whole event is an elaborate ruse. We would not be able to recruit members for our suicide squad otherwise. But I digress...
The fact of the matter is, you are now a member of the Cascadiers, an organization formed at the behest of the Adventurers' Guild to tackle the Bombard menace.

Our previous victory over the Bombards succeeded only in dispersing their physical forms for a time─it seems they were able to regenerate from the small amounts of ash left scattered on the ground. This time, however, our triumph shall be complete!
Feast your eyes upon the new and unquestionably improved Cascadier uniform!

Anyone who agrees to join our determined band will receive one of these much coveted protective garments to wear in the fight against the Bombards. You [@1A(1)]will[@1A(0)] join us in the fight against the Bombards, won't you?
Excellent! I knew you would not break your solemn vow![@CR]Now, as we have precious little time, I shall brief you forthwith regarding the specifics of the mission.

On the outskirts of the city, our Cascadier colleagues have been busy constructing a set of “decoy balloons” in the likeness of Bombards. They are drawn to others of their kind, you see, and will willingly round [@1A(1)]themselves[@1A(0)] up with the proper encouragement─which just leaves the small matter of their extermination!
On the front lines, south of the Blue Badger Gate, you'll find a senior officer who will issue you your orders. Follow them to the letter, and help us neutralize this threat once and for all!
That concludes the briefing. Take this, your Cascadier uniform, and may you never know the searing kiss of the Bombard's nether flames.
Ah, it would appear you already possess that item. Regrettably, Cascadier regulations do not permit me to issue you another.

Y-You would forsake your sacred vows!? Why, you despicable oathbr─[@CR]I... I shall forget we ever had this conversation. I have faith in you─faith that you will come to your senses and do what's right. Till such time as you recall the meaning of honor and sacrifice, I shall await here with open arms and beatific visage.
Well, hello there! Got yerself an eyeful o' the fireworks, eh? It's well ye did, 'cause Moonfire Faire's under way, an' I'm signin' up folk fer th' fun an' festivities as we speak.
Come on, scrawl yer name here!
Ye be called [@STRING($EB(1))], eh? Well, [@IF($E9(4),lass,mate)], as Cap'n o' the Cascadiers, I offer ye a sizzlin' welcome!
What's that? Who the hells are the Cascadiers when they're at home? But didn't I just...? Oh, bollocks, I was supposed to explain that bit first...

Well, er, small help for it now. Like it or not, ye've jus' sworn yer service t' the Cascadiers, a suici─er, [@1A(1)]tactical[@1A(0)] squad formed by the Adventurers' Guild t' deal with the Bombard menace.

Bombards are fiery hellsspawns what reduce all they touch t' ash. Proper nasty pieces o' work, they are. Why, there's some as say they're so terrifyin', only [@1A(1)]screams[@1A(0)] can rightly describe 'em!

Now, strictly speakin', the Bombard threat was s'posed t' have been dealt with a while back. But what with them bein' creatures o' fire rather than flesh, they was able t' rise from the ashes...even after we took pains to scatter 'em far an' bleedin' wide...
We Cascadiers are ready fer 'em this time, though! We've got ourselves a new an' improved method fer keepin' them burnin' blighters from retakin' their physical form!

Which is where reckle─I mean, [@1A(1)]righteous[@1A(0)] young recruits like ye come in! I'll bet ye're [@1A(1)]itchin'[@1A(0)] t' head out t' the front lines, an' pull on yer fancy new Cascadier uniform fer the very first time...
Ahhh, I knew I could depend on ye! Proud t' count ye among me [@IF($E9(4),sisters,brothers)], [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]!

Now, the first step t' riddin' ourselves o' the Bombards has already been taken. Jus' outside the city, our Cascadier comrades have set up balloons what mimic the shape of our foe. Bombards have a tendency t' flock together, see, an' these decoys let us deal with 'em in places of our choosin'.

They also serve t' lure the hellsspawn away from the city proper, where fires have a habit of spreadin' like...well...wildfire. 'Course, balloons ain't a solution in 'emselves. No, it's us Cascadiers what have t' provide that. For more o' the mission particulars, speak with the senior officer stationed outside the walls.
But enough talk─me throat's gettin' raw.[@CR]Take this here Cascadier uniform. May it always keep the heat at bay while [@IF($E9(4),flatterin' yer womanly curves,accentuatin' yer manly physique)].
Ah, you look t' be properly equipped already, and I can't issue more'n one uniform per Cascadier. Don't want some poor bugger goin' without, now, do we?
Wh-What? Ye'd stand idly by while yer comrades risked life an' limb t' stop the whole realm goin' up in flames!?[@CR]An' ye call yerself a Cascadier... <spit>

O-ho! You certainly have the air of a [@IF($E9(4),lady,fellow)] who knows how to [@1A(1)]roister[@1A(0)]! Am I right, or am I right!? And it just so happens that my companions and I are seeking more fun-loving friends to make merry with us in the Moonfire Faire!
No need to be shy, now. Just put your name down right next to ours...
Congratulations, [@STRING($EB(1))], on your induction into the Cascadiers! I am Miette, and it is an absolute pleasure to have you on board!
What? When does the roistering commence, you ask? My, my, not the brightest candle in the sconce, are we? Here, allow me to rephrase my words of welcome...
Congratulations, [@STRING($EB(1))]! You have just been duped into enlisting with the Cascadiers, a suicide squad founded by the Adventurers' Guild to neutralize the Bombard threat!
Don't think ill of me, I beg you. I know full well I told you a big fat untruth, but you can't deny that it was for a good cause─a sordid means to a virtuous end.

Now, the last time we encountered the Bombards, we didn't wipe them out quite as completely as we would ideally have liked. In short, the stubborn beasts succeeded in rising from the ashes...in spite of our best efforts to scatter them.
But fear not! For this time, we Cascadiers have hit upon a plan that can't fail!
All you need is one of our Cascadier uniforms! And a uniform you shall most certainly have─[@1A(1)]if[@1A(0)] you agree to aid us in our cause. Well, what say you?
Hurrah! I knew there was a good heart beating in that [@IF($E9(4),noble bosom,stout chest)] of yours!

As part of our operation, our fellow Cascadiers have placed decoy balloons in the shape of Bombards just outside the city. It seems the creatures crave the company of their own kind─a predilection we mean to exploit.

If one were to find its way into a residential area, the gods only know what carnage might ensue... That is why I would ask you to report for duty northeast of the Gate of Nald with all possible haste. One of our senior officers will issue you your orders.
And that is all I have to share. Now, I present to you your very own Cascadier uniform. May it preserve you from torrid heat. Always.
Hm? It seems you already possess this item. In which case, I'm afraid I cannot supply you with another.

What? B-But...you can't simply abandon us.[@CR]Think of the children! For the love of the Twelve, think of the [@1A(1)]children[@1A(0)]─their adorable little eyes melting in the inferno of the Bombard's unholy flames! <sob>

But you needn't worry. The Ishgardians are known for their stoic composure. They are not quick to anger as the Lominsans are.
Even the longest of queues at Ul'dah's winesinks or Limsa's whorehouses cannot compare to our order ledger.
If the decision were mine, we'd serve Gridanians first. But the masters won't hear of it. The Fen[@1F]Yll tradition is based on equality, they say.
You have an errand to run for now, but you may soon have the time to explore the lands of Ishgard more freely.
Many adventurers go there in search of dragon bones, valuable as they are. Sad to say, all most ever find are the bones of men.
The mountain passes are not safe. If you truly mean to travel to Owl's Nest, I beg you to take companions along with you.
The roads beyond the hamlet are even more sinister. I can only advise you do not venture down them─no matter your numbers or strength.
Well, look who's back! Wasn't sure you'd live to see the inside of the shop again, truth be told.
You've earned yourself a rest, no doubt there. Sad to say though, Lalatta was about lookin' for you. Can't say where she is now, though.

Clearwater Lake... Can the Gods' Quiver make it in time...?

She was quite an accomplished conjurer before trading her wand for a head knife─and has fire in her belly besides.
What is it? What's going on?
Oh, I'd ever so much like to help. But I just can't without permission.
Based on the whispers, it's hard to tell if anything has truly happened or not. But it is best to prepare for the worst.
Fret not, Lalatta is just fine. I'm sure of it. She knows how to take care of herself.
But don't tell her I said that. She'd likely beat me to a pulp if she found out that I'd said anything to dispel her carefully cultivated image of delicate femininity.
Do you mean to let a thug who doesn't know sheepskin from sheep shite criticize your work?

Hehe, tell 'em, Vielle.
We're wastin' time. I oughta just open your throat from ear to ear right now and be done with it.
Might be as we could make us some bags outta them faces. “Facebags,” we'd call 'em. How's that strike ya?
What a bother this all is.
P-Please, you must h-help us. For the love you b-bear the guild!
Don't move! Unless you want me to take your legs off for you.
Thank the gods you're all right. We've all been so worried. You're [@IF($E9(4),an inspiration to us all,a far braver man than I)], truly.

Lalatta and the other lass have returned as well. You have all our thanks for delivering them from harm.
Bloody Faces of Mercy! As if all the killing they do were not evil enough, they meant to sell counterfeit leathers!?
And capturing Lalatta and that other poor leatherworker like that? Why, I've a mind to...to... Oh, what's the use? I'm worthless.

Don't know if you already know, and don't care, but part of what Atelier Fen[@1F]Yll does is make goods for travelers.
Our leather's loved all over Eorzea. Hells, in some places, folks can't even get their hands on any, so high's the demand.
But that means the Fen[@1F]Yll name catches eyes, both good and bad. More than like that's why we seen more and more shipments lost of late─taken on the north roads by bandits in the mountains.

As leatherworkers, there ain't much for it. That's why we want you adventurers to help us outmaneuver the bastards. We mean to send our armor north piece by piece, rather than by the coach load. Will you help us?
Well and good. Let no time be wasted. Take this to Owl's Nest in Coerthas. The Knights of Ishgard'll be expectin' it.
With a bit of luck, any bandits won't pay you a second glance. But if you do meet with any trouble on the way, don't be a bloody fool. Give up the gear and keep your life.
Ain't no piece worth a life─no matter the quality. And them bandits ain't likely to damage any armor they mean to steal.
Well, thank the gods the others I asked were willin' to do their bit. Can't imagine what's become of your backbone, but if you ain't got a mind to prove your worth, so be it.
All the leatherworkers within are pupils of Lalatta, same as you. I encourage you to speak with them while you wait on her.
A rambunctious lot, aren't they? Take no offense, I meant no slight. I was much like them once, and you.
They're adventurers, to be sure. But come to master the leatherer's craft all the same. So, what say you? Be they friends, or rivals?
That Lalatta must have some reason for calling all her pupils together. She's piqued my interest, she has.
Mine own pupils are forestborn─the whole bloody lot of 'em.
The masters will not permit me to mentor you adventurers. They claim my lessons are “rougher than leather,” whatever the hells that means!
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! It has been too long. I haven't seen you since...since the time you spared me a death at the hands of those bandits!
I'll never forget what you did for me. Ah, it does me good to see you again. You look well.
You must be a student of Lalatta's as well. How are you finding her training?
I do well enough when working with the aid of the facilities here at Atelier Fen[@1F]Yll, but my skills alone are still nothing to speak of.
I had my doubts about taking up the head knife. I'm old, and all know you can't saddle a chocobo once it's seen too many winters.

But something happened. This guild helped me to uncover something buried deep within me, and I spit-shined it and put it on the mantel. Some things still worry me, though...Master Lalatta not least of all.
You'd best make for Lifemend Stump, like Lalatta says. We leave wares there when we need the moogles to fix 'em.
It ain't always a question of us lackin' the skill, or even the means, as many think. No, there are times when we leave items we are quite capable of repairin'...
Seems Lalatta's thought up somethin' quite clever. A task that'll help both the moogles and ourselves. See to it you do your best.
Whatever's going on, it's creating quite a stir. Try not to let it distract you. Focus on your work and make your repairs.
You adventurers certainly are quick learners. I wish all our leatherworkers were as receptive.
Still, this latest scheme of Lalatta's... Well, it's a bit outlandish even for her. Just you watch after yourself, all right?
I'll be watching over you throughout. You and Lalatta both, gods help us all.
To avoid any possible conflicts of interest, I won't be speaking to pupils until the task is finished. That should make things more...interesting.
Lifemend Stump was originally a place for us to give offerings to the moogles.
For whatever reason, they started fixing everything we left for them. And as the days and months and years passed, that's come to be the way of things.
The moogles aren't like to mind if you fix everything at Lifemend Stump.
They're a gentle bunch, and not prone to anger. Especially over something as trivial as our damaged cast-offs.
I've had enough of adventurers who don't even know how to respect one another. Haven't you?

Some say it's the way the world is today. That competitiveness is destroying the good in people. I don't know about all that. The opposite may be true for all I know. But the good is going out of people, that much is certain.
Hehehe, it sounds like you're in quite a pickle. Matter of fact, one of your rivals just buggered off, sayin' she didn't have time for these games.
But I wouldn't give up just yet, if I were you. Why not try parleyin' with this sprat who made off with all the goods?
It would take a master years to fix all those things, and a pupil a lifetime. Just pay him no mind. I'm sure he'll tire of his game soon enough.
This is so like you adventurers. Always trying to sabotage or outdo one another in everything.
Useful traits on the battlefield, no doubt. But unchecked, they're like to bring a guild down from the inside.
Lalatta is off in the Twelveswood, gathering materials.
You'd be unlikely to find her, even if you went looking. I suggest you interpret her absence to mean, “Work it out for yourselves.”
It just sickens me to hear it. The bastard should be made to lick the tanning vats clean for a season.

How could you!? Give back the goods you stole!
Stole? I don't recall hearing any rules laid forth.
I feel for you, truly I do. If only you had been there to carry them back with me from Lifemend Stump, I'd have been more than willing to share.
I'm not the villain here. It wasn't I who made off with all the items. And I'll thank you not to throw your accusations around so lightly.
That girl who was just here had the gall to do the same. She even tried to goad me into relinquishing what little I do have, though she left when it became clear I wasn't about to be convinced.

Very well, you have bested me. I suppose I can part with this atrocious pair of damaged Fen[@1F]Yll boots. But don't think it's because of your parleying skills─they are simply beyond my ability to repair.

You've been hard at work, I think... Yes, I see an air of confidence about you that was not there before. If I'm any judge, repairing [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000048,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,11000048,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] should be well within your ability now.

I'm still not convinced he'll be able to repair the remainder of the items. And if he doesn't, I'll be sure to let the masters know.

Gods be good, the elementals reside in those wares! To involve them in such meaningless drama is tantamount to heresy.

Best go and show it to Hereward.
Forgive me, Master Lalatta. To be honest, I didn't take this job for the reasons you just spoke of. Or any of the reasons I've learned in my time here.
I was selfish... I was thinking only of my evaluation...so desperate that I would take anything I could find. I think it is for that reason that the elementals have punished me.
Lalatta didn't have to go so far as to dismiss her. Such a shame...
This is the kind of thing you have to expect when you pit ambitious new recruits against one another.
I thought the bloody thing looked familiar. That's not the first time I've seen a part from an imperial juggernaut. Thank the gods we avoided disaster [@1A(1)]this[@1A(0)] time.
You shame us all with every day you pass in Atelier Fen[@1F]Yll. Save your excuses. Consider yourself dismissed from the Leatherworkers' Guild.
It looks like that fool who snatched up your damaged items wasn't able to finish his repairs after all.
He said he was heading off to return them to the Lifemend Stump. Be sure and give him a piece of your mind the next time you see him.
There is a road in the Twelveswood that leads to the north and east. It goes directly to the Garlean-occupied lands where Ala Mhigo once stood.

If you look in that direction, you'll be sure to see one of those damnable imperial juggernauts off in the distance. I fear the day may soon come when they are not so far away, and Gridania is no longer safe.
So what do you think of our evaluation system? Not perfect, I grant you, but it motivates even those who have belonged to the guild for years.
Of course, when task details are made known to individuals before they should be, it undermines the whole process, as we have recently witnessed.
Those who have been here the longest recall what happened the last time we saw one of those things in here.
Master Lalatta wasn't even a leatherworker back then, but... Well, I only hope the elementals never see fit to punish her like that again.
As if all the bickering wasn't enough! What could have possessed one of you to bring something like that back to the guild!?
But it says something of us teachers as well, not recognizing the threat right away. There's a lesson in this for everyone, I suppose.
Do you think what Master Lalatta said is true? About being used by others for evil...
If the Faces of Mercy really have set their sights on Atelier Fen[@1F]Yll, is it even safe to stay here?

Perfect timin', [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! A meetin's been called, and you ought be in attendance. The others are already gathered inside. Pupils of Lalatta, all, like you. Might be worth havin' a word with 'em while you wait for her to turn up.
The only leatherworker that ain't a friend is the one you ain't met yet. Go now, and have what words you will with the others.
Out of sight, out of mind, eh? Suit yourself. I'll not begrudge you your precious bleedin' privacy.
To train at Arrzaneth Ossuary is to know the full weight of your life's deeds and the sin they bring. Prepare yourself, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Prelate I'llofii will be the first light to guide you through the darkness. She will be expecting you.
Pay no mind to Keeper Yayake. She can be rather...cryptic, on occasion.
You will come to appreciate her in time, as all who train here do. And by then it will be too late to leave, whether you would or no.

Capital is as vital to the Ossuary as any of the other guilds, if not more so. You must know the path it travels. Wealth is formed at Eshtaime's Lapidaries and Sunsilk Tapestries, won and lost on the bloodsands of the Coliseum, gambled and guarded at the Platinum Mirage.
It falls to our Order to cleanse said wealth of the residues of sin acquired during its journey.
Perhaps you have come to know that there are two sects within the Order. There is a reason for this―our god is not Ul'dah's alone.
Wherever man is, life and death are as well. This is providence, and known by all. But what awaits beyond death is known by none.
You came here with the hope of seeing something of the occult. Some dark magic or perverted sorcery, perhaps? We mortals are innately drawn to that which we fear.
But a fascination for the macabre is not all the Order requires of its adherents. You must also have a heart for vengeance.
The hierarchy of our Order is reflected in our vestments.
The most gifted and powerful among us, the exarchs, are those with hoods of gold. It is said they can hear the voices of nine souls at once.
A vengeance will is no trifling matter. The costs incurred tend to be quite large─exorbitant, even, by the standards of many.

The Ossuary waives a portion of the fee when a vengeance order forms part of a last will and testament lodged with the Ossuary. Accordingly, there are many who make use of this service in such fashion.
Once you have dealt what vengeance the will and testament demands, there is no need for further slaughter. You are to travel back at once and speak to Prelate I'llofii.
Go and seek out the death-marked aldgoat that stole our friend's life. Spill its blood as it spilled his. And count yourself lucky that you go forth to kill an animal, and not a man.
That is not to say this vengeance order is to be taken lightly. The peace of a man's soul is at stake. See to it the deed is done─and done well.
Your death-mark is a simple [@1A(1)]aldgoat[@1A(0)]? How...common. I would at least have hoped you would be killing Amalj'aa.

Even so, you will find that killing in the name of a vengeance order has a certain sense of...righteousness to it. Thal watches over those doing his work in this realm, and visits his wrath upon those who would interfere.
A death-marked aldgoat, is it?
Aldgoats are wary beasts, to be sure. To draw them out requires cunning. If it is the parent you seek, I advise you to visit harm upon the child.
Last will and testaments are but one of the many services Arrzaneth Ossuary offers the people of Eorzea.
There is near no act we would deny for them as has coin.
As all know, there is an inner strength in man that shows itself only in the most dire of circumstances.

To gain control over that strength and bend it to your will, you must place yourself in constant peril. The sins you accrue in escaping those perils will be great, but once such strength is yours to command, no enemy can stand before you.
It is the suffering of the heart that separates us from the beasts─compassion, empathy, longing.
Tell me when you begin to experience such pains as pleasures, and I will introduce to you a new pain, the likes of which you have never known.
Only by embracing death can one honor life. Greetings, wanderer, and welcome to Arrzaneth Ossuary.
What brings you to us? Do you wish to gain mastery over this realm of Nald, and thence cast your gaze across to the realm of Thal? Do you wish to know the limits of this mortal coil?
Do you wish to join the Thaumaturges' Guild?
A wise decision, perhaps. Those unprepared to gaze inward may not like what they find when they do.
Head in the direction of the setting sun. You will cross the seas, and beyond them come to the ports of Limsa Lominsa─city of pirates.

There you will spread word of our teachings, and convince the Lominsans to purchase graves here at Arrzaneth Ossuary. Your fellow thaumaturges will have knowledge to guide you. Speak to them before you depart.
If you wish to sell graves, you must carefully outline the many benefits of interment here at Arrzaneth Ossuary.
Vengeance orders, seeing to the needs of the bereaved, execution of the will and testament, and so on. The Order may be relied upon to handle virtually all of one's posthumous affairs.
But you would do well to leave out the...[@1A(1)]finer[@1A(0)] details. Time is money, is wealth, is virtue. Squander it not.
Prepare well for your journey. The voyage itself is part of your training.
And keep in mind that the choicest morsels of information in Limsa are typically to be found among the flagons and wineskins of the Drowning Wench. Be sure and pay a visit.
But perhaps I have said too much. If your training is too easy, my soul will bear the sin for making it so.
Off to sell graves, are you? An admirable endeavor, and required of every novice. You must learn that to amass wealth is to take it from others.
The truth which you must teach is this─to live in plenty in the realm of Thal, we must relinquish all we have amassed in this realm of Nald.
Set no store by verbal contracts. The services you offer concern a person's most cherished belongings.
In such matters, the Order will recognize nothing less than a contract sealed with blood.
So it is to be Limsa Lominsa, is it? Not a very welcoming place, I fear. A fight is never far, what with all the pirates and Sahagin about.
Most there have no need of the Order to execute their vengeance─they would sooner exact it themselves.
Arrzaneth Ossuary? You are well come to Limsa, friend. I trust your journey was a safe one.
But I am afraid if it is the sale of graves which brings you, there is no custom for you at Mealvaan's Gate. We do not permit solicitation on the premises.
What's all this, then? Come all th' way from th' Ossuary in Ul'dah, 'ave ye? Hahaha! Ye needn't say another word, matey─not a bloody one.

So, th' Order's freshest sprat 'as found what passes for [@IF($E9(4),'er,'is)] sea legs, an' come all the way t' Limsa 'opin' t' save us sinnin' sailors from an affordable afterlife, eh!? Them brass-necked, black art-dabblin' bastards've got some bloody nerve, I'll give 'em that.

Still, the mere sight o' ye's served t' put a smile on me face, so I s'pose 'tis only fair I offer ye what wisdom I can spare. Well then, ye'll no doubt be 'appy to 'ear that th' anvil-botherers o'er at Naldiq & Vymelli's 'ave been known t' buy yer graves from time t' time─though I'm buggered if I know why.

Might try yer luck there. But don't think as ye can jus' go swaggerin' in like yer sultana's favorite eunuch. Ye'll need t' curry a bit o' favor wi' them steel-'eads afore they'll 'arken t' yer patter.
Which reminds me...a mate o' mine said 'e'd spied one o' Naldiq & Vymelli's runners bein' chased around by some beast or other no more'n a bell past. 'Tweren't far from the city, neither.

Woulda saved 'er 'isself, 'e said, but was too short o' courage an' too long without wine. Still, assumin' ye've got more balls[@IF($E9(4),─if ye'll pardon th' expression─, )]an' less of a thirst, ye might think o' savin' the poor wench yerself. If she ain't been eaten, that is.
Well, ain't this rich? Come all the way from the Ossuary in Ul'dah, have ye? Had I known ye was plannin' on visitin', I'd have scraped the soot from me face─an' the shite from me arsecrack, too.
Hopin' to peddle graves, are ye? Well, spare me yer words an' save yer breath. Ye'll not find any buyers here this day.
What in the hells is goin' on 'round here!? Either things keep bloody vanishin', or I'm losin' me godsdamned wits!
What's that? One of [@1A(1)]our[@1A(0)] smiths? Killed by a beast? An' so ye think we should buy her a plot in yer Ossuary t' lay her dead bones?

Oi, that's my [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000030,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000030,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]! Where'd ye get yer grubby paws on─ That bloody bitch! She waltzed right in an' stole it!

Gettin' torn limb from limb by a ragin' beast is all the thievin' whore deserves. Still, I s'pose there's some comfort t' be had in the fact she'll soon be dung. And the forge's secrets are safe─the gods are good for that.
That's all ye'll be gettin' out o' me on th' matter. Now bugger off, afore ye find me red-hot poker up that adventurer's area o' yers.

What's that? One of [@1A(1)]our[@1A(0)] smiths? Attacked by a beast? An' ye saved her, did ye? I s'pose ye think that obligates me t' buy a plot in yer Ossuary, do ye? A place t' lay me tired ol' bones once me days of forgin' an' whorin' are over?

Oi, that's my [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000030,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000030,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]! I should [@IF($E9(4),tear yer frillies with me calipers,stick yer manhood in the bloody forge)] for savin' the likes o' that thievin' whore!

What drew ye t' th' Ossuary, anyroad? What free-thinkin' [@IF($E9(4),lass,bloke)] would choose a life o' thralldom t' th' trader gods? If ye ask me, them thaumaturges got lumps o' cold, dead gold where their hearts should be.
Best leave the dead in peace. I've no mind t' hear none o' yer dark talk. Bugger off.
Ye thaumaturges are a bloody queer lot, what with all yer words an' studyin' an' prayin'.
Best leave the dead in peace. I've no mind t' hear none o' yer dark talk. Bugger off.
Arrzaneth Ossuary? You are well come to Limsa, friend. I trust your journey was a safe one.
But I am afraid if it is the sale of graves which brings you, there is no custom for you at Mealvaan's Gate. We do not permit solicitation on the premises.

Ah, by the by, perhaps you would be so kind as to pass word to your colleague for me─the thaumaturge who oft comes to purchase explosives. Tell her that my sums show she stands to save coin by buying in bulk next time.
Did you explain the benefits of burial at the Ossuary, as I advised? The Lominsans are a dense folk. I pray you spoke slowly and avoided large words.
The smiths at Naldiq & Vymelli's oft honor us with their custom. Did you do aught to anger them? Not to worry. You need only grovel, and they will forgive all soon enough.
That shouldn't prove too difficult for you. You are an adventurer, after all─unburdened by pride. Had you any, you would not have returned from Limsa empty-handed.
Do you yourself believe in the journey the soul makes in death to the realm of Thal?

All that we do here is to aid the souls of the ignorant rushing headlong towards their life's end, to spare them an eternity of unrest. That is our work─the work of Thal in this realm. Do you grasp this?
None is more forsaken in the eyes of gods and men than the graverobber. If such a fiend were found in Ul'dah, their end would be an excruciatingly slow and painful one.
The Ossuary offers a number of [@1A(1)]special[@1A(0)] contracts─in addition to the standard ones. The extra options serve to give the soul...greater peace.
To give these contracts a sense of exclusivity, they are offered to very few of our patrons. They are so costly that no smallfolk could possibly hope to afford them.
Ye thaumaturges are a bloody queer lot, what with all yer words an' studyin' an' prayin'.
Best leave the dead in peace. I've no mind t' hear none o' yer dark talk. Bugger off.

What drew ye t' th' Ossuary, anyroad? What free-thinkin' [@IF($E9(4),lass,bloke)] would choose a life o' thralldom t' th' trader gods? If ye ask me, them thaumaturges got lumps o' cold, dead gold where their hearts should be.
Best leave the dead in peace. I've no mind t' hear none o' yer dark talk. Bugger off.
You are returned to us from across the seas. Welcome back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Now, please submit the contracts which you secured.
Not a single one? I am thinking that perhaps you did not even bother to take the ferry from Vesper Bay...
I trust you know the punishment for deception within the Order. We do not suffer lies to be spoken, least of all to the guild's keeper.
So the smiths of Naldiq & Vymelli's have had a change of heart? But why? Tell me everything...
That is...most distressing news. And you are absolutely certain it was this other novice of our Order you witnessed pawning the trinket in Limsa?
I see. Thank you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I will attend to this matter myself.
Still, it does not excuse the fact that you failed to secure a single contract. Go and speak to your fellow novice. She is back from Ishgard. You may stand to learn a thing or three from her.
That which you witnessed at Naldiq & Vymelli's need no longer concern you. I will attend to the matter myself.
Still, it does not excuse the fact that you failed to secure a single contract. The fellow novice you accuse of this crime did exceptionally well during her time in Ishgard.
You would do well to go and speak to her. She may have some wisdom to impart to you.
The Ishgardians' way of life is based on a false myth, in whose name they fight and die. For them, those who serve nobly in life are rewarded with eternal glory in death.

Preaching the Order's word there is tantamount to heresy, and punishable by death. To have done so, and convinced so many to take up graves at the Ossuary...well, that new novice must be [@1A(1)]extremely[@1A(0)] persuasive.
It would seem your rival has widened the gap between you with this latest task.
Be mindful that it does not grow too great. For the difference in your sins will manifest itself as the difference in your wealth.
When I first heard the rumors of graves being robbed, I thought it for bones. But are you saying it was for a piece of jewelry?
To be buried with such a trinket is surely the far greater sin. Nald weighs all creation in this realm, and his wares are forbidden in the realm of Thal. This is known!
Have you spoken with the others? I pray you were able to learn more of our ways from them.
As to your fellow novice, she will not be punished for the crime you claim she committed. Here, the teachings of the Order supersede the laws of this world.
You must experience the reality of such eternal truths to fully grasp them. Acts of hatred, malice, regret, scorn, deception, impulse, lust─all that of which sin is born.

Do not give yourself to despair. Sin is not something to be dreaded. Rather, it is the sin's burden, its filthiness and its pain, that will guide you. Where, you ask? Why, to extraordinary wealth, of course.
Prelate I'llofii is eager to speak with you. Go and hear what she would ask of you.
If you truly wish to rival your peer, you would do well to stop wasting your time on idle banter.

Of course, even should you change your ways, it seems highly unlikely that you will [@1A(1)]ever[@1A(0)] be a match for one as promising as she. I daresay you know as much yourself. When she is in your presence, your hatred for her is plain─as is the fact that you are a slave to your enmity. I need hardly add that such a lack of self-control is unbecoming of one of the Order.
You know of the ferry docks far to the west at Vesper Bay? Where vessels depart for the isle of Vylbrand, and the ports of Limsa Lominsa?

Well, it was en route from there that a chocobo coach met its tragic end. The road itself is treacherous enough, but bandits frequent the region as well. If you plan to visit the scene, go with all caution.
A grand funeral ceremony is to be held for the victims of the recent chocobo coach accident. Many of the Order are busy seeing to the preparations.
I myself have been charged with arranging a first mourning service for the bereaved.
To Ul'dahns, nothing is more important than a funeral rite. Those with wealth have time─and with that time, the freedom to ponder the phenomenon of death.
This rite will be one of the grandest in recent memory. We must take care to make [@1A(1)]no[@1A(0)] mistakes.

The chocobo coach which recently met with disaster carried a number of Ul'dahns. There was even a prestigious merchant on board. His house is loyal to Milvaneth Sacrarium, however, and therefore of no consequence to us.
I imagine the Sacrarium, too, must be busy preparing a grand service.
In the wake of the tragedy near Vesper Bay, we have placed orders for a number of coffins. Yet I fear the goldsmiths may not complete the gilding and inlays in time.
Plain oaken caskets simply will not serve. Nearly all those slain in the tragedy were of high birth or wealthy houses.

You must ascertain the cause of this tragedy, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. If there was indeed a culprit behind it, the vengeance orders must be fulfilled. If it was a simple accident, you need do nothing.
Prepare yourself well before you set out. I sense there will be bloodshed before this matter is behind us. The Order has many enemies beyond the Ossuary walls─and even some within.
Prelate I'llofii has entrusted to you perhaps the most meaningless of tasks. If this were nothing more than a mere accident, the vengeance orders will be void.
The other novice you fancy your rival was given a far more significant duty. It was folly to let the gap between you grow this great.
What? You now believe your rival may have [@1A(1)]caused[@1A(0)] the accident?

There is unspeakable sin in this act. To accuse another without seeing fit to ascertain the truth. And in secrecy, no less. Your suspicions betray an unvirtuous heart, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
It is plain that you are still in need of guidance. So I will offer you these words.
When opponents outwit you, you must turn to [@1A(1)]other[@1A(0)] means to defeat them. Surely as an adventurer you have some such means at your disposal?
You wish to know what justice the laws of the Order levy on the unvirtuous among us?
Why, all of that information is contained within the tomes I urged you to read! Why should I take the trouble to explain that which you cannot be bothered to learn for yourself?
This is not the first novice Prelate I'llofii has seen become lost on our path. She was never fooled for an instant, I'd wager.
Then why does she do nothing to stop them, you ask? Why, I suppose it is because a true thaumaturge realizes that evil is as inevitable as death in this realm.
Travelers on the road who saw the chocobo coach said it was shaking violently just before it sped off the cliff.
I think it clear now that it was the work of that Lalafell's fell sorcery.
It weighs heavy on my heart to look upon the children of those killed in the accident─all the more so now that we know it was plain murder.
But learn from this, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. The services we offer, the wills, the vengeance orders...it is best to be prepared for death, for none may know when it will come.
As the murderer was one of the Order, a vengeance killing could not be called for. But rest assured, she will pay for this treason in blood.
There is a separate ritual for that. Many of the murdered were parishioners of Arrzaneth Ossuary. No doubt their loved ones are eager to attend.
The thaumaturges of our Order train that they may know each of the evils within us all. Evils which are present from the very moment of our birth.
Such knowledge is enough to break weaker minds and drive them to rank madness─as was recently the case.
The Adventurers' Guild provides many services, each with their own counter, as you may see if you take a look around.
Would you care to hear an explanation of any of them?
What would you like to ask about?
Why, this is most unexpected...
But the Path will not deny you the opportunity to set right a mistake you may think you have made.

And now, the time has come [@1A(1)]again[@1A(0)] for you to choose, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Which type of companion would you feel [@1A(1)]more[@1A(0)] comfortable with at your side? Which type of companion will complement your strengths and compensate for your weaknesses?
Excellent. Let us all hope that [@1A(1)]this[@1A(0)] decision is final.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: I witnessed your battle with the antlings, and must say that I was surprised. You have proven yourself far more worthy of this than I could have imagined.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: In your hands lies the Soul of the Warrior─a crystal within which the deeds of a thousand thousand warriors from history are recorded. For countless generations, the Soul has been passed on to those in my tribe who choose the path of the warrior, to guide them and aid them on their journey.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: When your inner beast awakens, the runes will resonate, further empowering your will, and granting you such strength as you never thought possible.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Today, there is cause for celebration, my friend, for through you, I have ensured that my tribe's legacy will endure. This is why I left my home. This is why I joined the Company of Heroes. This is why I am here today.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Yet however hard I try, and however earnestly I pursue my goal, I cannot deny that I believe that my mission will ultimately end in failure.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: While I style myself a warrior, the truth is that I left the mountains long before my training was complete.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: And while I carry with me the chronicles of my ancestors, detailing the ancient arts of war, I lack the ability to decipher the texts.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Yet, there may still be hope, for there is another who fled my village─one who shared my dream of passing on the teachings of the tribe, and [@1A(1)]can[@1A(0)] read the tome... My brother.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Without him, I fear there is little more I can teach you at this time.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: But that will not discourage me from continuing my studies of the chronicles, nor shake my belief that further secrets will soon reveal themselves to me.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Until then, I ask that you use the knowledge I've passed on to you, and continue your training. You must strive to harden your will so that it may endure the strain of future burdens. Good luck, my friend.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: The next warrior quest will be available from Curious Gorge upon reaching level 35.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Well, throw me in the fire and call me Rosy! You're back! What with you taking so long, I naturally made you for an oath-breaking cur, and was planning on sending the lads 'round to gut you! 'Tis lucky there were a few names higher up on me list, eh!? Heh heh!

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Hmm... This warrior lad sounds interesting...which means the cap'n will definitely want to hear about him...which means someone'll be getting extra rum rations tonight! Heh heh heh! Much obliged, scrag! Now bugger off!

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: What? I ain't got words to mince with whelps...unless that is, you're here to become a wolf.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: If that's the case, then I'm Curious Gorge─but one remark about the name and I'll rip that [@IF($E9(4),pretty,ugly)] head from your shoulders and suck the marrow out of your twitching spine.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Ahem. Now, I suppose you've heard the rumors about a bloodthirsty madman who, using lost battle techniques, has left a gruesome trail of carnage from Ablathia's Spine to the Sagolii Desert? Aye, well, they're all true─except for the parts about the carnage. Those have been greatly understated.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: That the techniques are “lost” is also untrue, for my tribe has been handing them down for thousands of years.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Yet though our numbers dwindle with every new summer, the elders refuse to accept new acolytes from outside the village, apparently content to let the art die with us. This is why I left the mountain in which I was raised and came here─to spread the teachings of the warrior in hopes that the techniques will be passed on to future generations.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: If you wish, I can teach those techniques to you, but first I must measure whether your body and spirit have the capacity to bear such a burden. To walk the path of the warrior, one must call upon the primal instincts that slumber within the soul.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: However, without a tempered mind and steely resolve, those instincts would engender such rage as could drive a man to madness.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: To the north of this cave you will find an antling nest. Prove to me that you fear not the cries of battle, nor shun the call of death. Do this, and my knowledge is yours.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: The inner beast awaits. Wake [@IF($E9(4),her,him)] from [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] slumber and embrace [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] power.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Any [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] can take up an axe and call [@IF($E9(4),herself,himself)] a marauder, but to become a true warrior, [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] must prove [@IF($E9(4),she,he)] can tame the inner beast that guides the blade. Slay the foul antlings who make their nest to the north of this cave and prove that your will is stone. Do this, and my knowledge is yours.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Well, if it ain't me favorite scrag. Come to lick the shite off me boots like a good [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)], have we?

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Thought I smelled something rank. Another young whelp fresh from [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] mammy's pap come looking to play pirates, eh?

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Or mayhap you're one of them as have been chasing ill rumors regarding a certain wild-eyed Hellsguard─the same one they say's been making his bloody mark with the Company of Heroes of late.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Don't tell me you haven't heard of the Company. A hard band of bastards and brigands, they be─of the like this realm ain't never seen. Can't visit an alehouse, souphouse, or whorehouse in this town without having your ears crammed full of fanciful tales 'bout stronghold raidings and primal slayings.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: And now folks won't stop going on about their latest bloody recruit─some flame-skinned Roegadyn come down from the forsaken crags of the Farreach, apparently. Few have actually laid eyes on the man, but them as have reckon his veins must course with the blood of the Fury, for none can stay his axe once he takes the field.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Yet there are those who've walked the Lance into Dravania with naught but a knife in their pocket and come back with the head of a hoary drake─only to be denied admittance to the Company. The fact that this stripling won a seat amongst that lot not five turns of the sun after rapping on their gates...well, that there be the true mystery.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: That is, a mystery to them as ain't never heard the legends of the Hellsguard warriors.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Bards still sing of a time when whole cities were leveled by a handful of their kind. Like wild beasts, they were. The sound of their roaring alone would make stout knights soil themselves, and lesser men hide behind their whores.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: And then, one day, they simply up and vanished from the realm, taking the secrets of their success with them.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: More's the bloody pity, too. With the Empire breathing down our necks, we could do with knowing exactly how a handful of men could butcher an army or ten.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Speaking of which...mayhap this lad from the Farreach knows something of how they got the job done...and if he does, might be as someone could persuade him into giving the rest of us a few pointers, like.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: If he was here, I'd grab the scrag by the scruff of his dirty neck and bleed his secrets out of him, o' course! But lo, I've me duties to think of, and the cap'n would tan me hide and use it to patch his codpiece if he learned I'd left me post. So, I suppose that just leaves you, eh? Swear to me you'll seek the lad out and let us know if he's the genuine article, and I'll tell you where to look for him. Sounds fair, don't it?

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: It's settled then. The man calls himself Curious Gorge, and he's said to have set up camp in a cave to the southeast of Camp Horizon. In western Thanalan, it is. I'd tell you more, but that's as much as any bugger knows. Still, you adventurers ain't exactly short of a bit of resourcefulness, so I'm sure you'll manage.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: Hmph. No hair off my arse.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: I ain't never been to Thanalan meself, but I hear it's hotter than a forge, and dryer than a crone's...well, you get the idea[@IF($E9(4), missy,)]. If it be solitude the lad wants, he sure as hells chose the right bloody place.

quest_names: Pride and Duty (Will Take You from the Mountain)
text_en: You must be a level [@VALUE($E8(3))] [@SHEET(xtx/text_jobName,$E8(2),1)] and level [@VALUE($E8(5))] [@SHEET(xtx/text_jobName,$E8(4),1)] to begin the quest “[@SHEET(xtx/quest,$E8(1),2)].”
Sirocco is said to hunt with its mate─the female acting as a decoy while he circles to subdue his prey from behind.

He is an agile creature who will use his speed to dodge the deliberate blows of your axe. But if you can wake your inner beast, it will help you anticipate your mark's movements, allowing you to situate your blade directly in Sirocco's path the moment he arrives.
Welcome back, my friend. Much has happened in the short span since last we spoke.

These past several turns of the sun, my duties with the Company of Heroes have taken me back and forth across the realm in search of a mysterious feral beast that's been terrorizing the smallfolk. People know not whence this monstrosity came, but witnesses say its thirst for blood is unlike anything they've ever seen.
Unfortunately, the time I have spent in pursuit of the beast is time I have not spent studying the chronicles, and I am sorry to say I have made little progress.

However, while on the road, I was able to decipher one passage that may be of interest to us both. From what I can gather, the chronicles tell of an ancient set of armor forged by my ancestors in the flames of the seven hells, and inscribed with the same arcane incantations that adorn the Soul of the Warrior.

Apparently, this mighty armor was passed down from hero to apprentice for centuries, until one man, driven by rage and vainglory, cast all five pieces from Ablathia's highest peak. Since that day, the armor has remained lost...and with it, the power that it harbors.

As far as I can make out, the next passage in the chronicles concerns the whereabouts of the missing artifacts...though I have only been able to make sense of the odd word thus far. Still, I must confess to some excitement. It may well be that the pieces cannot be found, of course, but if they [@1A(1)]could[@1A(0)]...imagine what a warrior thus clad could achieve!
Ah, if only my brother were here... We could decipher the text together and spread the teachings of our people to the entire realm!
Alas, he is not. His whereabouts are as hidden to me as those of the ancient armor. I would have liked you to meet him...if only so that you could have looked upon a true warrior.

Well, perhaps you still shall. Eorzea is not as large as most people perceive. Paths cross, fates intertwine. Such is the will of the Spinner. It may be that my brother has chosen a similar path to mine. It may be that─
Ah, but enough of my rambling. I shall not tire you with my words any longer. You are here to take the next step in your training, and so I shall oblige.

Far to the north, beyond the boundaries of this forsaken desert, lies the Black Shroud. In a corner of this primeval wood can be found an area which the locals have dubbed “Humblehearth,” and it is here that a deadly hunter lurks─Sirocco.

When facing this cold-blooded creature, you will soon realize that the labored swings of your axe are ill-suited to the task of felling such a nimble foe─but do not let this dissuade you from your mission. Wake the slumbering beast within and allow it to guide your hand. Learn to anticipate the movements of your mark, and wheresoever it leaps, be there to meet it with your killing edge.

Excellent. I sense your will growing stronger with every step you take. Here, accept this linkpearl. It will allow me to contact you when I have finished my next round of deciphering. Better that than have you make the long journey here on the off[@1F]chance that my studies have borne fruit. Good luck, and may the Fury be with you.
I understand that you may require more time for preparation. Speak with me again when you have steeled your resolve.
Deciphering the chronicles is proving to be a much more demanding task than I had imagined. I shall continue my work, but ask that you be patient.
The next warrior quest will be available from Curious Gorge upon reaching level 35.
