quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: Once a day, mammoth condors descend from the canyon walls into the Silver Bazaar to hunt for small animals...and even children. The men and women of the village have tried everything in their power to fend off the evil creatures, but to no avail.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: I shall approach the hamlet from the west gates, you from the north, then east. Call upon your inner beast to aid you in slaying each and every one of the cloudkin, that we may liberate the Silver Bazaar's people from fear, and go some small way to clearing my ancestors' names!

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]... Please forgive me for leaving so abruptly earlier.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: It was a hasty reaction to a situation for which I was completely unprepared.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: While both you and I know that I was in complete control of my inner beast, I now realize that to the layman's eye, it may have seemed that...well, the opposite was true.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: Mayhap it was this very misapprehension that lent weight to the lies which led to my tribe's disgrace. And if that is the case, then perhaps I should return once more to the chronicles, and endeavor to reassess their message in light of this discovery.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: Speaking of light─your Soul of the Warrior is sparkling.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: What did the whispers reveal? Anything of import?

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: If only they hadn't forsaken me, as they did my brother...

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: Ahem! Yes, well, I suppose that is that. I must continue my studies, and you your training. I hope to have something new for both of us very soon. Until then, my friend.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: The next warrior quest will be available from Curious Gorge upon reaching level 45.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: Hello again, my friend. It is quite obvious that you have been anything but idle in your training since last we met. Your progress is heartening to look upon, truly...but it also serves to remind me that each hour I spend poring over ancient texts is an hour not spent honing my skills. I fear my worth on the battlefield is diminishing by the day.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: Yet I am certain that my studies of the chronicles will yield something of use. In fact, just last night, I discovered how the warriors of my tribe came to be shunned by the outside world.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: Upon witnessing the prowess of my tribe's warriors in battle, the armies of the city-states began to incorporate techniques similar to those I have taught you into their training regimen─techniques which require the waking of one's inner beast.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: The consequences, of course, were dire. Yes, their soldiers became nigh on unstoppable, but they also became wholly uncontrollable...and both friend and foe fell prey to ensuing carnage. Of course, the heads of the city-states laid the blame for these atrocities solely at the feet of my kind, and promptly banned our ancient art, and imprisoned anyone suspected of teaching it. Or so the chronicles say...

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: What I find hard to grasp, though, is that never once during my tutelage did my instructors hint at this dark history. Nor did I ever see any of my tribe succumb to the rage that the chronicles describe.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: Could it be that the tales are mere falsehoods? Stories concocted by some long-forgotten enemy who conspired to poison our heritage and befoul our tribe's name? Who in their right mind would seek to sully something so pure...and why would my ancestors simply bow their heads and suffer such ignominy!?

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: That my people should be so [@1A(1)]weak[@1A(0)]─so utterly bereft of pride─is inexplicable. I refuse to believe it!

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: It matters not if these claims are groundless─if they prompted my tribe's art to fade into obscurity, then the damage has already been done. Well, I for one will not turn a blind eye to this injustice! If none of my people will give the lie to the stories that have so tarnished our reputation, it shall have to be me!

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: My friend, may I put to you a request? Might you agree to accompany me on a mission for the Company of Heroes?

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: It is a simple affair that requires a dual-pronged assault on a flock of giant, carnivorous condors that has been hunting the children of the Silver Bazaar.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: By showing the hamlet's residents the true nature of the warrior, and the purity with which he fights, perhaps the citizenry may begin to embrace my tribe and our art once more─and put aside the lies of the past.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: Excellent! I knew you would understand the importance of this mission. I shall enter the hamlet from the west side, you approach from the north then east. I will meet you when we have dispatched the last of the cloudkin.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: A [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] who walks into a battle unprepared is a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] who walks to [@IF($E9(4),her,his)] death. I contemn you not for wanting more time to prepare.

Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar

Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: It is good to see you again, my friend, but I hope you have not come in expectation of further revelations from the chronicles. I'm afraid I have made little progress with my translation. You still have the linkpearl I gave you, do you not? Rest assured, I will notify you the moment I discover anything of use.

quest_names: Curious Gorge Goes to the Bazaar
text_en: The next warrior quest will be available from Curious Gorge upon reaching level 40.

You need only locate the four pieces I indicated on your map. If you wish to don them, I shall not forbid it, but do so with the utmost care. You must be absolutely certain that your will is strong enough to bear their burden.
I commend your earnest, but I regret to tell you that I have naught yet to report. I ask that you bear with me a few more turns of the sun.
The next warrior quest will be available from Curious Gorge upon reaching level 45.
Welcome again, my friend. I was wondering when your travels would bring you back this way. It just so happens that I have some exciting news.
I have finally uncovered the clues pertaining to the whereabouts of the lost armor of my ancestors!

As it turns out, after the fallen hero cast the five pieces from the mountaintop, five of his pupils set out to recover them, intending to restore their master's name. What is more, they were actually successful in this search. However, when it came to reuniting the set, the armor's great power began to work upon their minds, and not one could bring himself to relinquish his piece.

Realizing then that their master's fatal pride was born of the artifacts' combined influence, the pupils resolved to keep the pieces separate, and to share between five the power that might otherwise have consumed one. Thus did each of them carve his own place in history. The chronicles go on to say that years later, prior to death, each of the pupils returned to the scene of his own greatest victory, and buried the artifact in his possession in a final attempt to prevent any one warrior from holding the set. And it is there that the pieces still rest.
You may be interested to know that the armor I wear is itself a replica of the set crafted by my ancestors─identical in all respects save for the arcane enchantments that adorned the original.

Now, if we were to find the pieces the chronicles speak of, what would stop us from tracing their runes and adding them to every piece of warrior equipment? That way, there would be no need to worry about a single proud fool becoming drunk on his all-surpassing power, as every warrior in the realm would be possessed of the selfsame might!

You, my friend, have walked with me nearly every step of this long journey, and it only seems fitting that I invite you to play your part in this final endeavor. If you are willing, I would have you aid me in the recovery of the lost artifacts.
You see the benefit they can bring my tribe, the benefit they can bring Eorzea. [@1A(1)]You[@1A(0)] understand the importance of ensuring my mission...[@1A(1)]our[@1A(0)] mission is a success!
I have marked the location of four of the pieces on your map. The fifth, I will see to while juggling my duties with the Company of Heroes and training other fledgling warriors.

The order in which you retrieve the pieces is of little import, but I must warn you: my ancestors laid them to rest in some of the most perilous parts of the realm. You would be wise to enlist the aid of your fellow adventurers before attempting to recover them.
You have my thanks, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. May the Navigator guide you true, and the Spinner see you safely home.
That is unfortunate...but there may be some wisdom in your hesitance. Speak with me again if you have second thoughts.

Audhumbla of Iron Lake is said to have a hide so thick that even the legendary blades of the Allagan Empire could not penetrate it.
But the Allagans looked solely to their weaponry for power, while I may look to the beast within! And thus shall I succeed where they failed!
So, my friend, have you tried donning the armor? Did you sense anything different? Did my ancestors lend you their strength?

The detail of these markings... It will be difficult, but I believe with time, I will be able to reproduce them. The problem now is the final piece that I retrieved. Unlike those on your four pieces, the engravings on the cuirass fade the moment I lay my hands upon it...as if it does not accept me, does not accept my strength.
Perhaps it requires that I prove myself further... That [@1A(1)]we[@1A(0)] prove ourselves further.

Since our foray into the Silver Bazaar, I have sensed that something may be amiss. The Soul of the Warrior which I carry no longer speaks with me, no matter how valiant my deeds on the battlefield. After much thought, I believe the silence may be a message in itself─one telling me that I must not grow content with these petty victories.

I must ever test the boundaries of my strength, as my father and grandfather did before me, and as my brother does even now. To deny the challenge set out by my ancestors would make me no better than the tired village elders who cower behind rock and crag while my tribe's pride fades with each passing day.
I, for one, will not suffer the fetters of fear to prevent me from surpassing my limits!

And I shall help others break free from their own chains, so that we may form a mighty alliance the like of which this world has never seen! An alliance of noble warriors, fearless and strong, trained by me in the ancient ways of my ancestors! No beastman army or imperial cannon will be able to stop us!
But first I must have the power of the armor...and to do that I must prove my worth!

Though it was I who led you to their final places of resting, I will not ask that you give your four pieces to me. Rather, I would propose a contest. A contest to show my ancestors who truly deserves to don a hundred generations of history!
The chronicles speak of a rare battle technique passed down via the Soul of the Warrior to those who have displayed peerless courage in slaying the most monstrous of foes.
I say, let us both seek out such a creature, and declare the first to defeat it and learn the last technique the keeper of the armor.
In the La Noscea highlands, deep within the caves of Iron Lake, dwells Audhumbla─one of the largest land-dwelling beasts in all of Eorzea. This shall be our prey.
Then it is settled. And once I have shown my ancestors I am worthy of their praise, perhaps they will speak to me once more...
Are you afraid? Then you may as well hand over your four pieces now, for they will avail a coward nothing and less.

Ah, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I have something important to give you, but for obvious reasons could not leave it here...lest it tempt me as it did once before. Meet me at the Silver Bazaar, so that I may free myself of its burden.
Come, we must make haste. The creature will not remain in the Silver Bazaar for long, and this may be our only opportunity to subdue it.
As for the armor...we can discuss that issue at another time. For now, let us call upon our inner beasts to grant us strength and courage in the coming battle. My ancestors shall decide the rest.

It may be that the Soul of the Warrior spoke to you upon slaying Audhumbla, but that does not mean my ancestors have deemed you the worthier. Something is missing, and I shall not concede before uncovering the truth.
Until then, the fifth piece remains here. Now leave me be.
The next warrior quest will be available from Curious Gorge upon reaching level 50.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! I know there is much we must discuss, but now might not be the best of times.

Do you recall me mentioning that I had been involved in the hunt for a bloodthirsty creature that had been terrorizing the smallfolk? Well, I just received word from the Company of Heroes via linkpearl that the monster was sighted near the Silver Bazaar less than a bell past.
What is more, according to those who managed to escape the carnage, the creature appeared more man than beast.
If this is true, then our quarry could be far more dangerous than any wild animal. We must find a way to stop it... [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] must find a way.
And by doing so, prove to the people of the Silver Bazaar─nay, to the world─that my tribe and my art have been wrongly judged!
Perhaps [@1A(1)]then[@1A(0)] my ancestors will deem me worthy. I know my brother would... Yes, I am quite certain of that.
There is no time to lose. We must arrive in the hamlet before the other mercenaries rob us of our chance to face this foe alone. Let us leave at once!

The journey has been long, but I finally feel we are nearing its end! When we slay the creature, all of Eorzea will be reminded of the true character of my people, and every nation will beg to learn the secrets of the warrior. Then the lies of the past will be buried and forgotten, and my ancestors will have no choice but to recognize the lone warrior who restored their name!
You would forsake me and my people at the last? And this after I gave you so much? No, this cannot be your final answer.

Do us proud, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. The Carpenters' Guild needs all the able hands it can get.
Visit the Acorn Orchard just outside the guild. You will find your instructors there. <grin>
Wood─simple to say, yet difficult to fully grasp. Have you any idea how many types of timber there are? Each with its own peculiarities. Each with a technique for manipulating it.

More oft than not, it's the moogles who tell us which wood we are permitted to take. I daresay we deal with the moogles more than any other guild. If you have a soft spot for the little buggers, then you're in the right place.

Show me someone who claims not to love moogles and I'll show you a liar. They're so damned [@1A(1)]cute[@1A(0)]! Whenever I see one, I just want to...to...squeeze it to death and gobble it up! Oh... Oh dear. I do apologize.
I'll warn you as I warn all new recruits─mind the tools. Some of them can be quite dangerous if not used properly.
We have more than a few children in our care here at the Atrium, so following procedure is of the utmost importance.
You think it endearing to have all these little vermin running about? With their incessant giggling and insatiable curiosity?
They may seem cute enough at first, but give it time. Before long, you'll be praying to Rhalgr for a few well-placed thunderbolts...or, failing that, a spate of unfortunate tree-climbing accidents.
It was brave of you to come here. Many adventurers tend to shy away from the responsibilities that come with joining our guild.

But looking after the Atrium's children as we do, a certain measure of, shall we say...[@1A(1)]unwavering patience[@1A(0)] is essential. Not a quality one associates with firebrand adventurers, if you'll forgive the generalization.
So, you've been sent on an errand to Quarrymill, have you? Well, you should have an easy enough time of it. Just check your map should you lose your way, and be careful.
If you come under attack, make all haste for the hamlet. The Gods' Quiver and others guard it. You will be safe there.
We may be young, but we've each more woodworking experience than you. So that makes us your teachers.
You'd be a pretty bad adventurer if you couldn't make it to Quarrymill. You [@1A(1)]do[@1A(0)] have a map, right?
Have you ever seen the archers of the Gods' Quiver? We watch them practice at the butts sometimes. Nock! Draw! Loose! It looks like so much fun.
The archers are much more fun than the lancers. The lancers are always so serious, and hardly ever laugh or smile.
M-My name's Ryd. You m-may call me M-Master Ryd.
I'm just as good with a saw as any of the grown-ups. I can make a big waterwheel all on myself if I want.
Perhaps I've been training too much. My shots are true as ever, to be sure, but my bow has certainly seen better days. Please, would you repair it for me?
You should be able to find fallen timber close by. The elementals around here have always been good to me. I'd like to keep them with me in my bow at all times, if possible.
You can only hold one branch at a time. Take this branch?
You can only hold one branch at a time. Take this branch?
A sturdy branch lies on the ground. It might make a strong bow.

A supple branch lies on the ground. It might make a good bow.

I appreciate the effort, friend, but I fear the draw of this bow might be a bit rigid for me. All the training in the world won't grant me the strength of a Roegadyn.
If you'd be willing to try again with some other kind of wood, I'd be much in your debt.
You've repaired it! Gods bless you, I─
What have you done!? How do you expect me to hit anything with [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)]? It has more bends than the Lumberline!
I can't use this. Is there no other wood you might try? Please, do what you can, I beg you!
Splendid! I've never seen such a beautiful bow!
No doubt there are elementals within. I should like very much to have the conjurers listen to their whispers.
You and the younglings have my gratitude, adventurer. Thanks to this bow you've mended and the arrows they've made, those foul Ixal will flee in terror before me!
I trust you saw the arrows safely to the Gods' Quiver.
Your instructors will be glad to hear it. Best go and make a full report, hehehe.
The bow you've made is truly a work of art. I daresay my enemies will die with arrows in their bellies and admiration in their eyes.
With it and the arrows the younglings have made, those foul Ixal will flee in terror before me! You have my thanks, adventurer.
Marcelloix finally made it to the lesson, did he? Between schooling the children during the day and carving at night, it's a wonder he gets any sleep at all.
Hahaha, don't be too harsh on the young ones. They meant no harm.
And lest you forget, as far as carpentry is concerned, you're the babe around here. Gods know they could teach you a thing or two if they had a mind to.
The protection of the Twelveswood is Gridania's highest priority. The Gods' Quiver, Wood Wailers, and conjurers all shoulder this burden.
Those of us who cannot fight work to ensure that those who do are equipped with the finest weapons and armor.

You'd think that sufficient, but try telling the archers and lancers as much. They're constantly complaining that we don't do enough to serve Gridania. I suppose one shouldn't expect anything else from the martially minded. They value prowess on the battlefield above all else, and can see little worth in those who lack it.
Were the archers pleased to receive the children's arrows? Good, good. It warms the heart to know. As a wise woman once said, “I believe the children are our future.”
Still, they need to be told to shut their traps from time to time. Someone has got to instill some discipline in these runts!
Marcelloix was late again, was he? Poor, overworked bastard. He sleeps like a log when he gets the chance─no pun intended.
Maybe he and I could exchange some of our duties─give him something less demanding than carving to do. Gods know, a trained monkey could do my work.
I trust that your endeavors were munificently renumera...meruner...runem... <sigh> I hope you got a good reward. I tell you, this teaching's no fun at all. I think it's time I looked into retirement.
So, have the children had their way with you?
Well of course I knew! Wouldn't be much use to this guild if I didn't know things, now, would I? Oh, don't look like that. No harm was done.

Do you recall what I first told you when you came here? That the life of wood mirrors the life in us all? It was those younglings who made me realize that. Like saplings before a breeze, children can bend their minds to any new thought, and be the greatest of teachers─if only we creaky old oaks would listen.
By the same token, wood can play tricks on us just as children do. I suppose there's some sort of lesson in that as well, but I'll leave it to you to find it. Here you are, then.
You'll come to love our trade. A piece of wood may not seem like much, but its life mirrors our own─it breathes, feels, grows, has potential.

The Twelveswood surrounding Gridania provides us with all we need. The elementals are strongest here, and so our lumber is the finest in the land. Needless to say, we don't take kindly to errors resulting in waste.
But come, it will do no good to worry of mistakes before you begin! We are here to guide you, after all.

Many years and more, the elementals have lent the Oak Atrium their powers and wisdom, guiding our saws and chisels. Place your faith in them, adventurer, and they'll not steer you wrong. Pour your heart into your work and you'll soon be carving with the best of the forestborn.
Now then, it's time you met your first...instructors. Are you up to the task?
You will find a small park next to the Atrium─we call it the Acorn Orchard. I think you might find your instructors there. <grin>
What's this? Methinks the trunk of this mighty oak rings hollow! I'll thank you not to waste any more of my time.
Just leave me alone.
I'm b-being good! Can I g-go outside now?
This isn't even fun.
Is life going to be this boring forever?
The children must be bored out of their minds, poor things. Believe me, I'd like nothing more than to turn them loose in the forest and have them out of the way. But the danger is too great.
See to it they don't stray beyond the city's borders, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Go and speak with Marcelloix when you are ready...and Twelve grant you strength.
Those children are far more clever than you might think. They make their own paper and writing utensils, you know.
Sometimes you can see them in the Acorn Orchard just outside, playing at spears. Again, all arms of their own making.
There's nothing the Atrium's children love more than moogles. They're always plotting to sneak into the wood to find them.
You'd best see to it they don't succeed, otherwise they're as good as dead. And their blood will be on your hands.
Perhaps it's time we invite the Wood Wailers to come and hold another festival for the children.
It must be sheer torture for the poor things, having such an awe-inspiring forest to explore, and no leave to explore it.
Marcelloix spoils those brats. What they need is a good scare. Proper piss-your-britches stuff. You know, to put the fear of the gods in them.
I came across some truly beautiful timber the other day. Thought I'd present it to Marcelloix as a gift.
Turns out he knew more about the stuff than I. Claimed it contained some sort of toxin, but that he had a special remedy to neutralize it.
Boooring...
I can't stand it anymore. I want to get out of here.

The younglings returned and went straight to their studies. All made it back safely─and in time for [@IF($E3($E9(11),12),[@IF($E3($E9(11),4),dinner,breakfast)],[@IF($E3($E9(11),17),lunch,dinner)])], no less.
Our toys should be bringing smiles to children all over Eorzea─not just to those of Gridania.
Visit Frondale's Phrontistery in Ul'dah. You will find a ward there with bedridden and sickly children.
No doubt they are in dire need of both smiles and laughter.
I heard you are being sent to Ul'dah. You must be excited.
You do know the way, yes? Just follow the Lumberline south out of Gridania until you get there. Couldn't be simpler. There are hamlets along the way as well, should you require rest or rations.
They say the healers at Frondale's Phrontistery can cure any disease and reattach any severed limb.
Knowing those Ul'dahns, though, I wouldn't be surprised if they were paying to have the rumors circulated.
It's very good of you to watch after the children. But where could Marcelloix have gone off to...
What's that? You're off to Ul'dah? Well, the guild must have good reason. I'll be sure and look in on the little ones when I can.
Looks like the fresh air did the children some good. They seem to have settled down a bit.
Letting them tire themselves out running about might be the answer─short of lacing their meals with a sleeping potion, that is.
Remember that special timber I was telling you about? Well, Marcelloix has been carving it into some sort of effigy.
Said that he'd like to dedicate it to the conjurers if all goes well. I don't know, though... He made that wood sound awfully dangerous.
Welcome back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I hope you will find time to regale the children with tales of your journey.

If you do, would you mind making Ul'dah sound a bit...scary? Just enough so that they wouldn't want to go. They are still quite impressionable. The last thing we need to worry about is them attempting to sneak off to Ul'dah.
Did you hear yet? Word is the Atrium is haunted. More than one person is claiming to have seen a ghost or spirit or some such nonsense.
Sounds like something those idiots in Ul'dah might believe in. But Gridanians know better. Laughable, if you ask me.
I still haven't seen Marcelloix. Have you any idea where he might be?
The runts haven't been making much noise as of late, for whatever reason.
Peace and quiet at last. It feels so...lonely.

The medicine was supposed to last longer, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], but it... Well, I'm afraid there's been a slight problem and ummm...Marcelloix is still quite busy. Too busy to be seen in the light of day, actually.
I'm sorry, but would you mind covering for him just a bit longer?

In Ul'dah, toys often take the form of decorations─status symbols that parents adorn their children with to flaunt their wealth. But, of course, patients are not allowed to wear such things within the hospital.
Your toys will be put to good use. Thank the carpenters on behalf of the Phrontistery. And make sure Marcelloix receives that medicine!
A ghost in the Atrium, is it? <sigh>
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! You're back sooner than I thought. I half expected you'd be emptying your pockets at the Platinum Mirage.

Well, as you're here, maybe you can help me shed some light on an unsettling little mystery. You see, ever since you left for Ul'dah, the children just haven't been themselves. They've been...good. Might you be able to offer an explanation?

And then there's all this mummer's talk of the Atrium being haunted. Something about a ghost that roams the grounds and eats the eyes and tongues of children who misbehave. It's scared the living daylights out of the younglings, as you can probably imagine.
I'm sure it's just someone's misguided attempt to discipline them, but I haven't a clue whose.[@CR]...It wasn't you, was it?
Did you start the rumors?
No, no, you were in Ul'dah all the while.
Unless you would have me believe you have a twin [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)]?
What the hells is going on? Ah, yes, before I forget─Nogeloix from the Phrontistery sent word. He mentioned entrusting a certain medicine to your care.
I spoke with Marcelloix. He asks that you bring it to him at the Roost. I haven't the slightest idea what he's cooped up over there for.
What the hells is going on? Ah, yes, before I forget─Nogeloix from the Phrontistery sent word. He mentioned entrusting a certain medicine to your care.
I spoke with Marcelloix. He asks that you bring it to him at the Roost. I haven't the slightest idea what he's cooped up over there for.
Did you start the rumors?
Do you still have the medicine for Marcelloix from the Phrontistery?
Some business or other has delayed him over at the Roost, and he asks that you bring it to him. Gods know what he's up to over there.
May I help you? You're looking for Marcelloix?
To call him here would be...less than prudent. There is a chance he might be seen. But if you insist...
Sorry to drop so many tasks on you in such a short space of time, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You did us a great kindness in seeing the medicine delivered.
Before I get to your payment, would you mind doing us one more favor while the children are still settled down?
Hahaha, no, no. You've done more than enough already. Once Marcelloix returns, I'm sure the young ones will be back to their normal selves.
Looks like they need him as much as he needs them, the adorable little demons.
In all honesty, I'm not sure you're the right person to be asking, but... Well, no use dancing around it─would you mind watching the children for a while?
I understand you might still be a bit sour about what happened last time, but will you do us this kindness?
In happier times, we used to let them play in the Twelveswood, so long as they didn't venture too far. But now, with Ixal and Garleans prowling about, the risk is simply too great.
They must be bored witless cooped up in here, day after day. I suppose all their pranks and mischief are their only means of release.
See to it they don't stray beyond the city's borders, will you? Go and speak with Marcelloix when you are ready...and Twelve grant you strength.
I can't say I blame you. If you ask me, those little monsters are far more terrifying than any beast you'll find in the wild.
What are you doing speaking to me? You mustn't leave the young ones unwatched, not even for a moment!

More than like they have ventured no farther than the Acorn Orchard just outside. I hardly need remind you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], that they are under your charge now. See to it they return to their studies.
Awww, you found me. I knew I should have found a better spot.
There is no one here.
All right, you found me, you found me.
But I'm [@1A(1)]still[@1A(0)] not going back to study!
Hmph. I [@1A(1)]suppose[@1A(0)] I'll go back. But only because [@1A(1)]I[@1A(0)] want to. It's boring here without Powle anyway.
Everyone else? Don't ask me. This is hide-and-seek! You never give your best hiding places away!
Hmmm, Ryd [@1A(1)]does[@1A(0)] love the Wood Wailers... Maybe he─ Never mind! I shouldn't tell.
The younglings from the Oak Atrium?
I've not seen them. But I heard what might have been a child's laughter not long ago, coming from just outside.
There are flowers in full bloom here, but no hiding children.
Hahaha! You f-found me.
You ch-cheated! Did S-Sansa tell you where I w-was?
I'm n-not going to t-tell you anyth-thing.
Well, I s-suppose I can tell you a l-little. But only because you f-found me.
Powle is in a b-box. He s-said he found a g-good one for hiding.
<silence>
Knock on the box?
<silence>
Shake the box?
<silence>
Kick the box?
Hey, stop it! That's not funny!
I was sure you wouldn't find me. You're not as stupid as other adventurers.
Did you find the others? Hahaha, you'll [@1A(1)]never[@1A(0)] find them all!
The grown-ups say there's ghosts at the Quiver's Hold. And that they gobble up any children they catch playing hide-and-seek there.
Kick the box?
<silence>
<silence>
<silence>
This is the scariest place in Gridania for hiding!
Maybe this box would have been better. But a ghost could get me easy in there.
Look how beautiful the flowers are! We should play come-into-my-castle right here.
Wh-What? You already f-found me.
Help! I think I may have climbed too high...
It's scary up here. I'm too scared to climb down!
I'm fine. Everything's fine.
I'll be fine. I'll...I'll come down in a bit. Honest!
You still haven't found Aunillie, have you?
Do you really want to know? Hmmm... Well, you might want to look up in that big tree. Hehehe.
There is no one up the tree.
Oh? She wasn't up there? Hmmm...
Maybe I was wrong. Hehehe.
Oh, [@1A(1)]now[@1A(0)] I remember! There's a hiding place under the Quiver's Hold. That's where I saw her go.
There is no one under the building.
Hahaha! For a grown-up, you're sooo easy to trick.
I know where she is. But I'm not telling.
Hahaha! <sigh> Good times... All right, all right, I suppose I'll tell you.
Aunillie's back at the Atrium. She's been hiding there the whole time, silly!
Thanks for playing with us. Here, I want you to have this. I don't need it anymore, anyway.
Oh, and this. You can have it, too. That was fun. Let's play again soon.
So it's to be a trip into the Twelveswood, is it? Yes, I've heard. Marcelloix has already been going on and on about getting all the necessary permissions.
Go and tell the young ones the good news, and keep an eye on them until he gets back.
Those younglings can be infuriatingly picky eaters. You'd best take a little of everything to please them all─bread, noodles, rice, popotoes.
But don't you dare let them go mixing their starches!
Don't forget to gather some fruit at Greatloam Growery. Oh, and be sure to take enough to feed the marmots and birds, as well.
An outing into the forest can be quite an ordeal. And that's assuming you can get the consent of the Wood Wailers and the Gods' Quiver. But leave that to us. You have other preparations to see to.
Turning the little beasts loose in the wild, are we? Does this mean we can bring ale back into the Atrium for a spell?
You're off with them as well, are you not? Do us a favor and pick any edibles that might go with a nice, dark stout.
Aren't you the least bit nervous about venturing into the forest? Even should you keep to the paths, you are near defenseless, you know?
You're one of us now, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Make sure you come back safely.
The archers have asked that we send an able-bodied adventurer to aid in the preparations. Nonolato awaits you at the Quiver's Hold.
I shouldn't think they will ask anything too great of you. And it is all for the sake of the younglings, after all.
You must be here about the outing to the Mirror planned by the Oak Atrium.
Taking charge of the younglings may seem a simple task, but there is great responsibility. Should feral beasts appear... It does not serve to think on it.
I have held counsel with the Gods' Quiver, and it has been decided that this task will fall to our own Wybir. And she asked for you by name.
You can find her at Quarrymill. Go now, and may the gods watch over you.
There is a close bond between Wybir and the younglings. She thinks very highly of them─and they of her. Their affection is a source of great pride for us all.
You should feel much the same. Wybir has asked for you by name, after all. She waits for you at Quarrymill.
It is good to see you again, my friend. The bow which you mended continues to serve me well. It is ever at my side.
I thought this an ideal opportunity to show my gratitude. Now that selfsame bow will see the forest safe for the woodworkers and their young ones.
Leave any beasts we happen upon to me. What I need of you...is arrows. I need all the arrows you can craft me. I pray your hand is steady under pressure.
I'm to tell you to make for the Mirror on your own. See that the way is safe, and wait by the banks for the others to arrive.
The Wood Wailers, Gods' Quiver, and conjurers will be escorting the group there and back. They'll be safe enough.
Some of the leatherworkers from Atelier Fen[@1F]Yll were kind enough to send over some new shoes and boots.
Have you ever worn their work? I don't know how they do it, but none of their shoes ever cause blisters or soreness─even when brand new.
Keep a close eye on the children by the water's edge. Don't go letting any of them drown.
You [@1A(1)]can[@1A(0)] swim, can you not? If not...well, best stay near the shallows.
Arrangements have been made for a number of the Wood Wailers to escort the children on their outing.
The Gods' Quiver will be keeping watch over the children, as well. As will the conjurers, which is most reassuring of all.
Look! Look! I found a creepy-crawly! What's this one called?
Fiiirst!
You were not! I was first!
It's so big... No way can the seas be bigger than this!
My mother told me not to get dirty, but just a little dirt should be all right...right?
Ah! A marmot! Did you see it? Do you think there are any moogles around, too?
With you here, I suppose I might permit myself a moment's repose. It is so nice to have an extra pair of eyes.
I'm going to draw my pet lizard. But...I forget how many tails it has.
No peeking! You can't see it till it's finished!
There's nothing to this art stuff. Just cake your face with mud, press it against a fresh piece of paper, and it's finished!
Look at mine. I drawed the rain with white wax. Isn't it pretty?
I want to draw my dada, but I can't remember what he looks like. He got killed in the forest. I heard a Wood Wailer telling Mummy that an Ixal teared his face off.
I don't know what to draw. Marcelloix is always telling me how I didn't have an active imagine-a-nation.
W-Will you draw something f-for me? I'm not a very g-good drawer.
Make sure you give it to Marcelloix when it's finished.
What will you draw?
Make sure you give it to Marcelloix when it's finished.

The ice age that ushered in the Fifth Umbral Era made the land a barren and merciless place, and man was pushed to the limits of his resourcefulness in the struggle to survive. Yet survive he did, through the discovery of magic as we know it─an event which marked the dawning of the Fifth Astral Era.

At first, man was well pleased just to have the means to keep the cold at bay and compete with the other races. But man is nothing if not an ambitious beast. It was not long before he began to seek mightier magicks, hoping to win greater glory.

And it was this desire that brought forth black magic, the arcane art of destruction. In order that the forces of chaos be kept in check, and balance preserved, white magic, the arcane art of succor, came into being but a little while thereafter.

Emboldened by magic, man went on to reach the zenith of glory. But his hunger knew no bounds. Over time, even they who donned the white began perverting their powers for the sake of personal gain, and in this single-minded pursuit scrupled not to sully the sanctity of the Twelveswood.
In his pride and avarice, man brought down the wrath of the elementals upon himself.

A great deluge was sent to cleanse the land of his wicked presence, in the wake of which the forest rose to swallow up all that was not washed away. Thus did the Six Umbral Era begin...or so it is told.

Beyond the bounds of the forest, rogue elementals remain rampant as ever.
If they are left to their rage, another calamity will surely befall Eorzea. We must do all in our power to ensure that this does not come to pass.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I have need of your strength once again.

If the reports are to be believed, the eyes of this bandit and his minions are steeped in such rage as their mortal flesh could not possibly have begotten.
I trust you already know what is required of you. Aye, you must free the hapless souls from the grip of the rogue elemental that controls them.
I knew you would not disappoint me. You are a true friend to the elementals─to Gridania.
Be heedful that your opponents are ordinary men no more. I urge you to proceed with the utmost caution.
I know not the words to express my disappointment. Search your soul, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and ask yourself whether you do the right thing.

Oh, joy! The elementals have seen fit to let me visit my favorite flower bed again, kupo! Just the thought of spending another idyllic afternoon among the petals is enough to make me shiver and shake! When things settle, I shall go there and nap till I give myself bellyaches─see if I don't, kupo!
Raya[@1F]O told me that people tend to say the opposite of what they mean, kupo. So when they say “no,” it actually means “yes.” Is that truly the way of it?
The rage of the elementals appears to have subsided slightly. I daresay our efforts are beginning to bear fruit, but we cannot allow ourselves rest until the Twelveswood has regained its former calm.

Oha[@1F]Sok has been silent of late...but the unease of her kindred is ever present, kupo.
Raya[@1F]O is cross about how long it's taken you to return─and that makes [@1A(1)]me[@1A(0)] cross as well! Hmph, kupo! Hmph!

No doubt you already know, but your newest spell is kupositively [@1A(1)]awesome[@1A(0)]! One would never suspect that white magic had such an exhilarating application, kupo!

Kupopo!? You're out to find the legendary garb of succor!? Why, should you succeed, that would make [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] legendary by association, kupo![@CR]...Hmmm, would that association extend to me as well?
So these are the artifacts... They are indeed aglow with the light of succor. You are to be commended, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Would that I could say my mission was an equal success. I fear I owe you an apology.
I was unable to ascertain the location of the fifth piece. I have set the archivists of Stillglade Fane to scouring our library, but naught has come of their efforts thus far.
For a blessing, the keening of the elementals has yet to reach such an intensity as would be cause for alarm. There is time still.
I promise not to rest until the whereabouts of the final artifact are known to us.
In the meantime, I would have you apply yourself to honing your abilities. You serve Eorzea and the elementals best by realizing your potential as a white mage.

Dzemael Darkhold, southwest of Camp Dragon Head in the central highlands of Coerthas. Zahar'ak, east of Camp Broken Water in southern Thanalan.
Turning Leaf, south of Camp Crimson Bark in the West Shroud. And Tiger Helm Island, southwest of Camp Bloodshore in eastern La Noscea.
These are the four known locations of the garb of succor. Each artifact is sealed within an enchanted chest that can be perceived by none but a worthy white mage.
While you are afield, the moogles and I shall dedicate ourselves to tracking down the fifth and final piece. I hope to have good tidings to share upon your return.

I have spoken with both the elementals and the moogles. Regrettably, none possess knowledge of how to stop the elemental of nihility. But fret not, for there is a course of action available to us still.

The Wood Wailers have sent word regarding Rowland of the Ninety-Nine Blades, the bandit whom you liberated from the elementals' influence. Upon regaining lucidity, the man revealed that he had been hearing voices.
“Show unto me the face of the sixth sun, that I might weigh the deeds of her children.”[@CR]...Apparently, this phrase echoed in his mind without cease.
Now, this is merely conjecture, but I believe Oha[@1F]Sok was attempting to observe mankind through others of her kind.

Alas, it would seem that those elementals who took possession of folk at her bidding ended up being affected by her inherent wrath. And in their turn, they poisoned the minds of their hosts, who were driven to acts of violence.

If this conjecture holds true, it would go far towards explaining why Oha[@1F]Sok chose to reside within [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000551,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000551,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].

After she merged with the staff, she had creatures of the Twelveswood steal it in hopes that it would find its way into the hands of the common man. Thence she would be able to observe the children of the sixth sun.

By sheer coincidence, however, [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000551,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000551,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] came to be in our possession.
Knowing that we Padjal can readily sense elementals, Oha[@1F]Sok doubtless panicked when you brought the staff to me. And so she burst out as she did and told us an untruth.

This reaffirms my belief that Oha[@1F]Sok has not despaired of us─that she is willing to give mankind a second chance. Yet, comforting though this knowledge may be, I fear the fate of Eorzea hangs in the balance still.
As I related to you before, it is by her keening that the elemental of nihility unleashes cataclysm.
Oha[@1F]Sok sits in forbearance of her final judgment and is silent for the moment. Nevertheless, her presence alone is enough to impel her kind to sustain their keening indefinitely.

In turn, that keening serves to fuel the wrath of Oha[@1F]Sok's existence. And so shall the cycle continue until water and wood swallows all. We must pacify the elementals if this vicious circle is to be broken.
As you well know, however, ordinary means serve not to restore enraged elementals to calm, less so those who derive their rage from Oha[@1F]Sok.
In order to save Eorzea, we must avail ourselves of greater power─we must avail ourselves of the garb of succor, the legendary artifacts worn by the white mages of old.
Ancient chronicles hold that the garb is imbued with the light of succor, and is bestowed only upon those deemed true servants of the forest.
The garb comprises five artifacts, each of which heightens the wearer's affinity with the elementals.
There exist accounts of white mages who successfully entreated elementals to render their essence unto the garb as a show of ultimate favor.
Were we to emulate this feat, I believe it would be of great benefit to our mission.
But first things first. [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I would have you journey forth to claim the garb of succor.
The artifacts are sealed away in different corners of Eorzea, and were thought to have been long lost. But with the moogles' help, I was able to ascertain their whereabouts.
This undertaking will sorely test your faculties as a white mage, yet our need is dire. There is no time to waste─you must depart as soon as you are able.
I knew you would not disappoint me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Now, heed me well, for I shall make known to you the whereabouts of the artifacts.
The first rests within Dzemael Darkhold, southwest of Camp Dragonhead in the central highlands of Coerthas. The second can be found in Zahar'ak, east of Camp Broken Water in southern Thanalan.
Turning Leaf, south of Camp Crimson Bark in the West Shroud, is where you shall find the third. And the fourth piece awaits on Tiger Helm Island, southwest of Camp Bloodshore in eastern La Noscea.
Each is sealed within an enchanted chest that can be perceived only by a worthy white mage. There is no doubt in my mind that you are such.
Should you need to review your destinations, I shall mark them on your map of Eorzea.
...Hm? Puzzlement is writ plain upon your face, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. You wonder about the fifth artifact, I shouldn't doubt.

Despite our best efforts, the location of the final piece eludes us still. Rest assured, however, that the moogles and I shall dedicate ourselves wholly to this endeavor. I hope to have good tidings to share upon your return.
You would forsake Eorzea in her hour of need? Mayhap mankind does not deserve a second chance after all...

Oh, thank the gods you're safe! You were so long abroad, I feared for the worst. But never mind that now. That you have returned to me could only mean one thing─your mission was a success!
Hm? That robe...I do not recall seeing it amongst the artifacts you acquired.[@CR]<gasp> Is this Oha[@1F]Sok's presence I sense!?
What is the meaning of this!? Explain yourself this instant!
That the final artifact of succor would be Oha[@1F]Sok herself...
That certainly explains why we were unable to locate it. Pray forgive my outburst─I would not have believed such a thing possible.
I knew from the first that you possessed the potential for greatness─but that you should realize it, and so [@1A(1)]soon[@1A(0)]... Words fail me.
It is no ordinary white mage who can quell the collective fury of the elementals and win the favor of wrath incarnate besides. You can hold your head up high, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Gridania is fortunate indeed to count you among her allies.
On behalf of the nation, I offer you my deepest thanks.
By the power vested in me, I hereby permit you the use of new white magic.
I once taught you that to walk the path of white magic is to devote oneself to the salving of hurts and lifting of misery.
You have grown into the very embodiment of that ideal, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and I say this without reserve.

The future will be fraught with hardships, but so long as I draw breath, I shall give my all to ensure that peace ever reigns within the Twelveswood. I have no doubt that you will strive to do the same.
Pray keep watching over us, Oha[@1F]Sok. I promise you, the day will come when the Eorzea you have envisioned is made reality...and you need mourn no more.
What's that? You'd like my blessing as well, you say? Happy to oblige, kupo! Ahem!
Kupo... Kupopopo... KUPO![@CR]...It is done. Now you're [@1A(1)]certain[@1A(0)] to succeed, kupo!
<sniff> <sniff> Kupopo? The scent of Oha[@1F]Sok is all over you, adventurer...and that of several other elementals besides. I say, what in the world have you been up to, kupo?
How do you mean to deal with the elementals, kupo? With force...or with compassion?
What took you so long, kupo? You ought to know by now that Raya[@1F]O doesn't care to be kept waiting.
The keening of the elementals is loudest southwest of Camp Bentbranch, and it is thither that you must take yourself.
Go forth, my stalwart white mage, and assuage the anguish of the elementals, that the light of succor might shine throughout Eorzea.
I shall pray for your safe return. May the Matron watch over you.
Can you hear it, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]? The elementals' keening has begun to rise in crescendo, a sound that sends a chill down my spine.
Oha[@1F]Sok has returned to the Twelveswood, I am certain of it. Her presence stirs the rage of her kindred.
Having observed the deeds of men through your eyes, Oha[@1F]Sok forbears passing her final judgment.
However, being the collective wrath of the elementals given form, she cannot help but be swayed by the humours of her kind. It is only a matter of time before her hand is forced.
Hm? Might we try treating with Oha[@1F]Sok directly? Would that the solution were so simple, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Alas, the problem lies not with Oha[@1F]Sok, but her kindred.
Our only recourse is to pacify the enraged elementals, one after the next.
If all goes well, some may be willing to render their essence unto the garb of succor, and our cause will grow stronger for it.
...But here I must needs make a confession. It pains me to say this, but I have failed to locate the final piece of the garb.
I have explored every avenue known to me, exhausted every store of knowledge...yet I could not find so much as a single reference to its whereabouts.
And now our time is spent. The hour of reckoning is upon us, and we must needs act, with or without all five artifacts of succor.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], your final mission is thus: you are to go forth and grant peace unto the elementals.
The time is long past that men honor the oath made in the pact of Gelmorra─the oath to shine the light of succor throughout Eorzea.
I will tell it to you plain: this task would ask much of the most experienced white mage.
Yet it was through your eyes that Oha[@1F]Sok saw hope in mankind. We must pray that her kindred can be made to see the same.
The keening of the elementals is loudest southwest of Camp Bentbranch, and it is thither that you must take yourself. Go with the blessing of the Matron, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
Our journey is almost at an end, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Would you truly forsake our cause now?
Oha[@1F]Sok is somewhere out there, alone with her sorrow. The mere imagining of it makes my eyes rain, kupo... <sob>
Raya[@1F]O hasn't practiced with her staff in quite a while. Instead, she's had her nose buried in musty old tomes, kupo.
For a blessing, the keening of the elementals has yet to reach such an intensity as would be cause for alarm. We have time to act still.

I promise not to rest until the whereabouts of the last artifact are known to us. In the meantime, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I would have you apply yourself to honing your abilities. You serve Eorzea and the elementals best by realizing your potential as a white mage.

My research shows that the sabletooth spriggans live in the south of Gridania, near the Tam[@1F]Tara Deepcroft. You are sure to find plenty of them there. And who knows? With your help, perhaps the mystery behind this peculiar “stone snatching” behavior will soon be solved!

They are named for their black teeth─the result of years spent gnawing on ores and earth. Bring me [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,itemNQ=11000164,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,itemNQ=11000164,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], and the deed will be done. Perhaps we can shed some light on this “stone snatching” behavior.
Gods, look at those beauties! And look! The thick crown, grooving and smoothing, these basins and cones!
This is [@1A(1)]precisely[@1A(0)] the type of wear I expected to see. This proves my hypothesis─the sabletooth spriggans are most certainly feeding on ore!

Look closely─you can just make out the metallic remnants in the black coating with the naked eye. And see, the crown of the tooth has been completely covered with a layer of minerals that have permeated the enamel! There is no denying these teeth have been formed by chewing rocks!
Doing so would enable the sabletooth to chew even harder rocks and ores, thus covering their teeth with an even harder mineral coating, and so on, and so on.

But looking at the roots, it seems the stress placed on the teeth eventually causes them to fall out as the spriggan ages. It must be for [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] reason that they resort to stealing from the miners─to avoid having to prize the ores out themselves!

It rather reminds me of a professor I once had. When the last of [@1A(1)]his[@1A(0)] teeth fell out, his speech became all but unintelligible. Eventually, the university released him, citing an “inability to fulfill contractual obligations.” He fell into poverty after that, and died cold, alone, and hungry...

But how about these spriggans!? Truly remarkable! Such an isolated and unique behavior as this among a single population of a species is a once-in-a-lifetime find! You have more than earned this reward, friend.
You there, adventurer. I wonder, have you not seen any spriggans on your travels? Furry little black things, they are, not altogether dissimilar to a dark-furred coney at first glance.

I'm trying to conduct a study of their behavior in this area─eating and mating patterns, migratory routes, and so on─but whenever I draw close enough to make the necessary observations, the blighters all run off! Gods, what I wouldn't give for a few of those [@1A(1)]teeth[@1A(0)]! Most people don't realize the tales teeth can tell.
Oh dear, I've forgotten my manners. My name is Marcette, and I am a naturalist under the employ of the [@1A(1)]Eorzean Geographic[@1A(0)], a publication which surveys the realm's wildlife.

So far, I've learned that spriggans are gregarious animals. They nest in large groups belowground, digging labyrinthine tunnel networks. I also know they are skilled predators, and that they are even capable of creating fire using flint stones... All of which is jolly interesting, of course, yet there is so much that I still do not know.

By way of example─in addition to the flint stones they carry, spriggans are often seen bearing rocks of some other sort, only I haven't an inkling as to why. Perhaps it has something to do with miners having nicknamed them “stonesnatchers.” They claim the spriggans make off with their ores.

Wait just a moment! You look as if you have a lot of free time on your hands. Go out and kill me some sabletooth spriggans! Bring me [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,itemNQ=11000164,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,itemNQ=11000164,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], and your efforts won't go unrewarded.

The spriggans that interest me most are those in the south of Gridania, near the Tam[@1F]Tara Deepcroft. There are likely some nesting holes in the area. Oh, [@1A(1)]please[@1A(0)] say you'll do it! I couldn't possibly bring myself to kill the little dears on my own!
Oh, I [@1A(1)]knew[@1A(0)] I was right about you!

Bring me [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,itemNQ=11000164,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,itemNQ=11000164,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)], and the deed will be done.
That is most regrettable. And to think I had a mind to award you a lifetime subscription to [@1A(1)]Eorzean Geographic[@1A(0)]!

What is this? Have you lost your way, as the four souls whom you seek? You must find these stray lambs, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Purify their souls through confession, and return them to the Warden's flock.

Journey to the places she has shown me. First, to where the forestfolk break their bread. Then, to a remote village in the Twelveswood. Seek passage to Limsa Lominsa, and there find a place of cargo and tariffs. And finally, in Ul'dah, there is a soul on a street corner in need of guidance.

Confess my sins? What ever could you mean? I am a [@1A(1)]pious woman[@1A(0)]! I offer prayers to the Twelve by day, and make offerings by night. I have [@1A(1)]nothing[@1A(0)] to hide! I say to you, [@IF($E9(4),madam,sir)], that I am ready for Azeyma's judgme─

Oh. Uhhh... I suppose there [@1A(1)]was[@1A(0)] one occasion on which I acquired an Ixal horn via...questionable means. I know it is illegal to possess one, b-but I only wanted to learn more of them. You must believe me!

<sob> O Azeyma, I repent! I repent! It was just so twisted and pointy... <sob> ...and I'd never seen anything like it. <sniffle> I just had to have it. I know I was wrong. <sob> I swear I won't do anything bad again. I'll be a good Elezen, I swear I will. <moan>
Confession!? Bah, you've the wrong lady, stranger. Hear this─my fealty lies with the sun and Azeyma's justice, now as ever. I've naught to hide, least of all from you.

'Course, after seeing them sylphs up to their antics in the wood one day, scaring travelers and whatnot, I thought it might be fun to do something similar to my neighbor. Aye, so I threw a sheet over my head and gave him a bloody good scare! Hee hee hee!
Took some pity on him after the fact, but I had a good laugh all the same. That what you wanted to hear?
Confession? But I have already confessed all of my sins! What more does Azeyma ask of me!? I am an honest man. I practice no deceptions. And I work hard to support my family.

I...I... O great Azeyma, hear me! I have sinned! I have...given in to my [@1A(1)]appetites[@1A(0)]! I have frequented...[@CR]...[@1A(1)]restaurants![@1A(0)] Y-Yes, to the Bismarck I have gone, alone, and gorged myself on all manner of exotic dishes! Sweetbreads...steamed puddings...sausages! Ah, such sausages! <gasp> Please, [@1A(1)]please[@1A(0)], I beg of you, don't tell my wife...
O Azeyma, I beg of you, [@1A(1)]please[@1A(0)] do not tell my wife of my latest dalliance! I'll do anything. [@1A(1)]Anything[@1A(0)]! Just don't tell my wife...

I've seen naught but hardship since the fall of Ala Mhigo. Many are the times I've lapped filthy water from a chocobo stable's trough. And now the Warden demands my confession? I'm a sheep lost from the Twelve's flock, you say? <spit>

Where was Azeyma when the walls of Ala Mhigo fell? Where was Rhalgr when our enemies closed in around us? Where were any of the bastard Twelve!? With the Garleans, perhaps!? Because they sure as hells weren't with us!

I've had many moons to ponder the fate of my land. The only way I can make sense of it is to think we Ala Mhigans were punished for a lack of faith. And that drives me to find sleep in the bottle most nights, rather than a bed.
I'm a weak man, and not without faults. A part of me knows I must find my faith again, buried deep as it is. I... I'll make efforts, I swear it─Azeyma as my witness.
Now is the time to offer thanks and rejoice in Azeyma's blessings. For you have seen the deed done, and she is eternally grateful. This, she has spoken to me in your absence.

Worry for the lost souls no longer. For they are returned to Azeyma's flock, and shall henceforth be tended to by her humble servant, Swaenhylt. See how those who repent are greeted by the Warden with love, while those who wallow in their sins invite only the swift justice of her blade.
This world is rife with the lies and deception of man. Yet even they will come to fall under the light of Azeyma's brilliance.
Fast approaching is the judgment of all things at the hands of Azeyma. It is my task to save as many souls as possible before that day comes.
But I have spoken too long. You are no doubt eager for your reward─and you shall have it. Go now, and may Azeyma go with you.
Praise be to Azeyma, great Warden in the sky, beacon of righteousness! By her light, our paths are lit. By her providence, our way is known!

I am her humble servant, Swaenhylt. For nigh on twenty years have I lived in the seclusion of Abalathia's Spine. I come back to you now, at the turn of the tide. And yet I am taken with sadness as I gaze upon Eorzea's children. Far too few live with fear of Azeyma's judgment in their hearts.
Still, I shall not give myself to despair. For salvation awaits us all through Azeyma, and it is to that end that she has brought you to me this day.
Swear yourself to her, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Pledge your being to her service and name, and carry out her work in this realm! Will you vow to do so?
Hark, then! Your first deed awaits. You are to seek out four lambs who have strayed from the Warden's flock. Find these lost souls, and hear them confess their sins.

Truly, your unwavering dedication is moving. In recognition, I shall tell you what I can of the locations of these misguided brethren, just as Azeyma has shown them to me. Here, in Gridania, I see...a place where the hungry break bread. And...there is a village, remote and secluded.

Another is...across the sea. I see the ports of Limsa Lominsa, and a place of much cargo and freight, and busy hands counting the coins of tax. And now sands, vast sands... The walls of Ul'dah! On the corner of a street, I...

That is all the Warden has chosen to show me. The remaining adversity must be overcome by you and you alone. Hear these souls confess their sins, and gaze long into their eyes. Then you shall know, for under the brilliant light of Azeyma's justice, the misguided can do naught but repent.
There is no nook nor cranny where you may hide that the Warden's light does not shine. Your heresies shall be exposed!
Gods, if only there were more [@1A(1)]time[@1A(0)]!

Oh... Why...hello there. I, errr...I suppose you caught me muttering to myself there. How embarrassing. <sigh> This latest development has left me rather flustered. Oh dear! And now I've gone and forgotten my manners.
I am Eugenaire, of the Trappers' League. I've just received an urgent request from a sentry at Buscarron's Fold─an Elezen fellow by the name of Chamberliaux─asking that we deliver a quantity of oil.
But our oil reserves are pitifully low─far from sufficient to fulfill the order. Ordinarily, I'd set about producing more, but I've drawn patrol in the wood. And so you see my dilemma.
Tell me, do you seek work, adventurer? If you'd be so good as to bring me some scarlet oil, I'd be in your debt. It can be obtained from the orifices of oilbugs.
[@2B([@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])])] dollops of the stuff will serve, I should think.
Excellent! Then allow me to furnish you with the knowledge you will need.
Follow the road south of Gridania and you will soon see Buscarron's Fold. From there, head further south still, and you will come upon the area inhabited by the oilbug.

Swinging a sword takes a moment to learn, but a lifetime to master, I always say. And the single most important secret to mastering the blade is─ Oi! Have you been struck deaf, [@IF($E9(4),lass,lad)]!? Or is listening too much effort?
You wish to know my battle philosophy? Well...I suppose it's quite simple, really. I set aside all respect for life and try to hack my opponent into bloody chunks.
Of course, as a performer in the Coliseum, I do try to give the fans what they want. It wouldn't serve to run a man through without letting him get a couple of swings off first, now would it?
Now, if you don't mind, I'd like to get back to my drills. I've a match to prepare for.
Don't keep me in suspense. How'd you fare with Lyngwaek?
Aye, aye, that is [@1A(1)]precisely[@1A(0)] the kind of talk I was hoping to hear. The man is more like Ahldbhar than I'd imagined!

They say Ahldbhar was the mightiest of the twelve Archons. Rhalgr the Destroyer himself, taken form in Roegadyn flesh─a bloody mountain of a man, and a fearsome warrior, besides. Not unlike our friend at the Coliseum, eh?
You must've seen renderings of Rhalgr at some point─in paint or stone. Looks like a bag of angry muscles in a mage's robes, right? Aye, well, those are done in the likeness of Archon Ahldbhar.

Ahldbhar fought relentlessly against a clan of wicked sorcerers that sought only to wreak havoc on the world through their dark powers. But then, something happened... Something that threw Ahldbhar into deep despair. And in the end, he turned and took up with the enemy, though none can say as to why.

What came of him after his betrayal? Well, I confess I haven't heard the end of the tale myself. That bard's a wily bugger, see, and he only ever gets part way through before his throat dries out. Meaning I have to give him yet another bloody ale─free of charge, of course.
But never mind all that. I've yet to pay you for the deed. Here you go, then.

Caught wind of all this Archon talk yet? Some folk make them for the very incarnations of the Twelve, come to Eorzea. Old prophecies and wives' tales say they descend from their heavenly seat whenever disaster threatens Eorzea, see.
Needless to say, many believe the Archons to have otherworldly powers─both of mind and body.

According to the loremasters' books, there was an age of shadow and calamity some fifteen hundred-odd years ago, when a great flood drowned the world─the Sixth Umbral Era, they called it. Believers say it was the twelve Archons what came to fight the darkness then.

Last I heard, he was looking for some sort of muse to help him put his characters to song, or some such nonsense. But I ain't about to leave my bar unattended to go chasing muses.
You adventurers go in for that sort of thing. How about you lend us a hand, eh? There's a famous gladiator over at the Coliseum─name of Lyngwaek.

I reckon he's as good a bloke as any to inspire that addle-brained bard to sing the praises of the Archon known as Ahldbhar, mighty and fearsome as he is. What say you, then? Are you willing to go and have a few words with this warrior?

Ah, now that does me good to hear. Go and talk to Lyngwaek, then, and ask him to share his thoughts on battle. See if you can't find out what makes him so great─straight from his own mouth. You'll know the lad when you see him─big as an aurochs, he is. Most like he's training at the Coliseum as we speak.
No stomach for it, eh? I don't bloody blame you. I'd do the same in your shoes, had I not given my drunken worrrd.

Ah, and yes, look here! See this silver spike? A most ingenious device. The Amalj'aa have actually developed a sort of needle-based self-therapy! The point pierces just beneath their scales, stimulating a pressure point in the neck.
By adjusting the angle and applying various ointments to the tip, their warriors are able to stave off hunger and drowsiness, suppress pain, trigger the release of adrenaline─truly fascinating stuff!

But it is not without its weaknesses. It is quick to rust. Look at this arrowhead. I came across it not three months ago. Never has it graced the end of an arrow's shaft, nor been exposed to the elements. And yet it reddens nonetheless.

I believe this to be reason for the Amalj'aa's custom of applying a mysterious yellow solution to their blades and points. Pretty pungent stuff, to be sure, but it serves to stop the steel from rusting.
I trust I needn't explain the significance of all this. Imagine the advantage in our war against the Amalj'aa if we could cut off their supply of this solution!

Help me, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], now as before! [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Thank the gods you've returned safely! <retch> Ugggh, what is that [@1A(1)]smell[@1A(0)]!? It smells like...a turd covered in burnt hair. <heave> I trust you gathered the vials. <gag>
But there is something there... Just the faintest soupçon of...asparagus? No, it's...it's... Gods be good!

This can only be Arrzaneth holy oil! There are other elements mixed in, to be sure, giving it this abhorrent odor. But the presence of the oil is unmistakable! So [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] is what they've been using to coat their steel!

Scarlet oil is taken to Arrzaneth Ossuary where it is blessed by the thaumaturges. I've seen the prelates then use it to coat the bodies of the deceased in preparation for their funerary rites. It is said to be able to hide the stench of decaying flesh.
Still, we must discover where the Amalj'aa are obtaining the oil. I only hope they are not─ Gods, I dare not even speak it, lest we find it to be true.
But I haven't the time for idle conjecture. I must complete my report and submit it to my superiors!
You have served me well yet again, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Please, take this as a token of my appreciation. And let us pray the Amalj'aa do not have many more secrets of this sort.
Go and meet your mentor Chuchumu at the Golden Bazaar. It's one of the hamlets of Thanalan, where many of the Ala Mhigans have made their home.
The way is a bit far. See to it you are well prepared before you leave. I will notify her of your coming by linkpearl.
It is not only the needs of women we must meet here. Ul'dahn men can be just as demanding when it comes to articles of beauty.
Finely woven cloths of every fiber, brilliant dyes from all corners of Eorzea, feathers from across the seas that change color in the light...
Ul'dahns like nothing more than to drape themselves in the most luxurious and extravagant finery money can buy.
You will have to come to know the hearts of your clients if you wish to be a successful weaver.
That is one advantage you adventurers have over us. Your journeys lend you insight into the fashions and tastes of faraway places. But surely none are as finicky or as demanding as the Ul'dahns.
Deaustie is a good lass. She treats all who come through those doors the same─be they poor or rich, highborn or low.
The Sunsilk's owner'd not have it any other way. He's a fair man, and insists his shop be run as such. I can't do it myself─I despise the poor and downtrodden far too much.

Having just joined us, I wonder if the dilemma we face has occurred to you. You see, we seek to dress our clientele in layers and layers of the most extravagant fabrics, knowing all the while that the desert can be rather...[@1A(1)]hot[@1A(0)].

And so I designed [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,8050521,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,2,8050521,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]! Flaunt the flesh and beat the heat─all in the best possible taste!

I suppose there may be some passing adventurers with coin enough... Anyway, be a good [@IF($E9(4),girl,lad)] and aid Chuchumu as best you can.
A red riding hood? Why on Hydaelyn would you want to make something like that?
Ah, I see now. There's little doubt that Ouvielle would switch her bloody if she were to find out. Very well. Here, you will need this.
Once you have completed the red riding hood, you must deliver it to Chuchumu in all secrecy. Do you understand?
I only pray she is still at the Golden Bazaar when you have finished...
So Chuchumu has gone and lost something [@1A(1)]again[@1A(0)], has she?
Gods know how the girl came to be so forgetful. She once left a row of pins in the crotch of a pair of breeches. Lucky for her they were sold to a eunuch!
<sigh> I am just waiting to play my part for the guild.
My time to shine will come soon enough.
Poor Chuchumu... Despite all she is made to suffer at the hands of her stepmother and stepsisters, she is still such a cheerful, sweet little thing.
Promise me that you will do all you can for her. Truly, none is more deserving than she.
Chased by a wolf!? In the desert!? Chuchumu must be bloody cursed...
But there must be a guardian watching over you. The last adventurer that tried to help her was torn limb from limb by the Amalj'aa!
Where is the wine, the fine red? We must prepare it for Lady Ouvielle.
She will be parched after having been outside...and craving strong wine after having to deal with Chuchumu...
I heard that Lady Ouvielle had another of her fits at the Golden Bazaar.
The woman is an absolute terror when her fury is on her. All here at Sunsilk Tapestries know to stay well away from her at times like that.
Just so! Your name? [@STRING($EB(1))], you say? Well, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], allow me to begin by acquainting you with Sunsilk Tapestries' presiding philosophy─beauty, over all else!
